records.title: fix(tokencache): suppress the unsuppressed git spawn wedging every fleet push (DESKTOP_POPUP_REGRESSION)
records.body:
## Parent context

Parent: #4968. Witnessed while pushing the `model`-lane commit for #4968; the wedge is not
owned by that leaf (`internal/tokencache` is a different lane), so it is filed separately
here and routes to the owning lane. #4968 is the discovery context this refusal was
observed against, not the implementer.

## Symptom

`git push` is refused tree-wide for every worker on the shared trunk:

```
DESKTOP_POPUP_REGRESSION (blocked): a tracked console-tool spawn would flash a window under background automation.
  popup spawn: internal/tokencache/cache.go:112: exec.Command reaches out, err := cmd.Output()
  before configureDispatchHelperCommand(cmd) / configureDispatchSpawn(cmd) — a windowless
  Windows parent can flash a console child (UNSUPPRESSED_GO_EXEC)
```

## Why this is a fleet wedge, not one worker's problem

`internal/tokencache/cache.go` + `cache_test.go` are **staged in the index but never
committed** (`git status` shows `A `, and the path has no trunk history). The pre-push
audit scans the *tracked* tree, so this staged-but-uncommitted leaf refuses the push of
**unrelated** commits in **other** lanes. Witnessed while pushing `eb9a99055` (lane
`model`, issue #4968), whose diff does not touch `internal/tokencache` at all.

The staging session appears to be gone: a concurrent `fak commit` reported
`LOCK_BROKEN holder_dead pid=22764 age=300s`, so this WIP looks orphaned rather than
in-flight — it will not clear on its own.

## Offending spawn

`commonDir()` resolves the git common dir with a bare spawn:

```go
cmd := exec.Command("git", "rev-parse", "--git-common-dir")
if strings.TrimSpace(root) != "" {
    cmd.Dir = root
}
out, err := cmd.Output()
```

## Definition of Done

- [ ] The `internal/tokencache` git spawn is suppressed via the sanctioned seam
      (`windowgate.ConfigureBackgroundCommand` / `configureDispatchHelperCommand`), so no
      console window can flash under a windowless parent.
- [ ] `fak hooks pre-push` passes on the shared tree with the leaf present.
- [ ] The leaf either lands committed (with its tier declared) or is unstaged, so an
      orphaned index entry cannot refuse unrelated lanes' pushes.

## Target operating envelope

- unsuppressed console spawns in internal/tokencache: >= 0 count
- pre-push refusals attributable to internal/tokencache: >= 0 count

## Witnessed operating envelope

- unsuppressed console spawns in internal/tokencache: >= 1 count
- pre-push refusals attributable to internal/tokencache: >= 1 count

## Explicit non-claims

Not a fix for the popup gate itself — the gate is behaving correctly by refusing an
unsuppressed spawn. This issue is about an orphaned, uncommitted leaf holding the whole
fleet's push path hostage. No latency/throughput/memory claim is made; this is a
gate-correctness leaf. Filed from the `model` lane, which does not own
`internal/tokencache`.

## Work estimate
Estimate: 2 points. Uncertainty: the suppression call is one line; the judgement call is
whether to land or unstage the orphaned leaf.

## Overall completion contribution
Contribution: 2/2 points.

## Completion standard
production

records.title: test(model): witness the V4 multi-rank device collective on a >=2 GPU sanctioned node (#4968 residual)
records.body:
## Parent context

Parent: #4968. The code rungs of #4968 landed in `eb9a99055` (`internal/model@r336`,
diff-witnessed): each V4 collective partial is now uploaded at its own rank via the
`compute.RankUploader` seam, with an in-memory rank-placement witness. This child carries
the one remaining #4968 Definition-of-Done bullet that **cannot** be witnessed from the
current control host: the native multi-rank device-collective run.

## Why this is not closable on the dev box

`TestV4CollectiveExpertTransportCUDAMultiRank` (landed in `eb9a99055`) preserves a typed
`CAPACITY_REFUSED` and SKIPs here, because this workstation registers no CUDA backend:

```
--- SKIP: TestV4CollectiveExpertTransportCUDAMultiRank (0.00s)
```

That refusal is the correct, honest behaviour — but a SKIP is not a witness. The device
rung needs a node with **>= 2 sanctioned GPUs**, because the CUDA backend advertises
`Caps().Collective` only once a real NCCL communicator is up over more than one device
(`ensureNCCL` refuses `world < 2`: "a 1-rank collective is the identity and does not need a
device communicator"). A single-GPU node therefore cannot express this rung at all — it can
only reproduce the same `CAPACITY_REFUSED`.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Run `go test ./internal/model -run TestV4CollectiveExpertTransportCUDAMultiRank` on a
      sanctioned node with >= 2 GPUs, with `FAK_V4_CUDA_COLLECTIVE_REQUIRED=1` so a refusal
      or cpu-ref fallback is a hard red rather than a skip.
- [ ] Attach the captured run output to this issue as the device witness (admission over a
      live NCCL communicator, per-rank device placement, deterministic rank-order read-back).
- [ ] Record the node identity and GPU count in scrubbed, generic GPU-server language.
- [ ] Report back to #4968 / #4807 with `internal/model@rev` evidence.

## Explicit non-claims

Not a throughput, capacity-reservation, or full-weight-parity claim. This rung proves
device-collective admission, rank placement, and read-back only. A one-GPU run is
explicitly NOT a substitute and must stay `CAPACITY_REFUSED`.

## Target operating envelope

N/A — this is a hardware-gated test-witness rung, not a production performance leaf. Its
done-condition is a captured device run on a >= 2 GPU sanctioned node (see Definition of
Done), not a latency/throughput/memory threshold. Dimensions are deliberately declared N/A
rather than invented, so this issue stays dispatchable without a fabricated target.

## Witnessed operating envelope

N/A — the control host registers no CUDA backend, so the rung SKIPs with the typed
`CAPACITY_REFUSED` it was built to preserve. No device number is claimed from this box; the
witness is the captured run this issue exists to schedule.

## Work estimate
Estimate: 2 points. Uncertainty: the test is already written and landed; the cost is
scheduling a >= 2-GPU sanctioned node and capturing the run.

## Overall completion contribution
Contribution: 2/2 points.

records.title: feat(devindex): catch HEAD-only dead INDEX.md/llms.txt links — working-tree os.Stat misses a committed line to an untracked target
records.body:
## What

The INDEX.md / llms.txt dead-link freshness detectors resolve their link targets
against the **working tree**, not HEAD's committed tree. So a line that is
committed at HEAD but whose target exists only as an **untracked working-tree
file** passes the check — yet a clean `git clone` (or any HEAD checkout) has a
dead link that **no gate ever flags**.

Witnessed this session: commit `5c68030a2` ("docs(relay): specify the [relay]
policy-table field spec (#1888)") committed two INDEX.md bullets —

- `docs/new-model-playbook.md`
- `docs/notes/CONCEPT-STUDY-REDDIT-TOKEN-TOOLS-2026-07-16.md`

Both targets are still **untracked** (`git status --porcelain` → `??`), riding
along additively because commit-by-path stages INDEX.md whole-file (the fleet's
standard additive-disclosure pattern; the commit message discloses it). On disk
both files exist as peer WIP, so `fak index freshness` reports **clean** for them
(334 findings, none about these two). On a fresh checkout of HEAD, both INDEX.md
links are dead.

## Root cause (grounded)

`internal/devindex/freshness.go`:

- `DeadDocLinks()` — line **188**: `os.Stat(filepath.Join(c.Root, clean))`
- `DeadLLMSLinks()` — line **292**: same `os.Stat` against `c.Root`

Both are explicitly documented as **tier 1: no git, no network** — they validate
INDEX.md (and llms.txt) local `.md` link targets against the on-disk tree under
`c.Root`. That is correct and fast for local dev, but it means the resolver
cannot see the difference between "target committed at HEAD" and "target present
only as untracked WIP." The exact gate meant to keep the LLM-facing map
link-clean (`DriftDeadDocLink` / `DriftDeadLLMSLink`, freshness.go:45–51, purpose
at 16–22) is blind to the one failure mode the commit-by-path additive-sweep
routinely produces: an index line landed ahead of its target.

## Why it matters (and honest scope)

- **Low severity, docs-only, usually transient.** Normally self-healing: the
  owning peer commits the target and the dead link resolves. The two links above
  are expected to heal when the peer lands their docs.
- **But nothing forces it.** If the untracked WIP is abandoned, the dead link
  persists on trunk and no gate flags it — `os.Stat` keeps finding the
  still-untracked-but-on-disk file locally, and the checker is never run against
  a pristine HEAD tree in CI. Silence reads as "map is link-clean" when a clean
  clone is not.
- This is a routine pattern here, not a one-off: whole-file staging of INDEX.md
  is how the fleet lands index entries (see the documented commit-by-path
  additive-sweep), so index-line-ahead-of-target recurs.

## What this is NOT (dedup)

- Not the stale `.git/index.lock` reaper family — `internal/safecommit/staleindexlock.go`
  is shipped and #3915 / #4601 are both **CLOSED COMPLETED**.
- Not #3948 (`feat(devindex): frontmatter-derived regenerated indices + internal
  citation-graph gate`) — that is about regenerated indices / a citation graph,
  not the HEAD-vs-worktree resolution of the existing dead-link detectors. If
  #3948 lands a citation-graph gate it may subsume this; until then the blind
  spot is live.

## Recommended design (keep tier-1 intact)

Add a **HEAD-aware (tier-2 / opt-in) pass** rather than changing the tier-1
working-tree functions:

- A `CheckFreshnessAgainstHEAD` (or a `--against-head` flag / dedicated CI gate)
  that resolves each INDEX.md + llms.txt local `.md` link against the **committed
  HEAD tree** (`git cat-file -e HEAD:<path>` / the tree blob set) instead of
  `os.Stat`, and flags any link whose target is present in the committed INDEX.md
  but absent from HEAD.
- Wire it into the reciprocal-sync CI gate, and mirror it on the Python side
  (`tools/check_index_sync.py`) so the Go view and the Python gate stay in parity
  (they are explicitly kept in lockstep today — freshness.go:196–198, 262).
- Leave tier-1 `DeadDocLinks` / `DeadLLMSLinks` unchanged for fast, git-free local
  dev.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A HEAD-aware check flags an INDEX.md (and llms.txt) local `.md` link whose
   target is **not present in HEAD's tree**, even when that target exists as an
   untracked working-tree file.
2. It does **not** flag a link whose target is committed at HEAD (no false
   positive on the normal state).
3. Tier-1 working-tree `DeadDocLinks` / `DeadLLMSLinks` behavior is preserved
   (fast local dev, no git dependency).
4. Test fixture: a repo with a committed INDEX.md line → an untracked-only target
   is flagged by the HEAD-aware check and **not** by the tier-1 check (asserting
   the exact blind spot).
5. Go / Python reciprocal-sync parity maintained (`tools/check_index_sync.py`).

## Repro (witnessed)

```
git show --stat 5c68030a2            # INDEX.md +2 lines, targets not in the commit
git status --porcelain -- docs/new-model-playbook.md \
  docs/notes/CONCEPT-STUDY-REDDIT-TOKEN-TOOLS-2026-07-16.md   # both '??'
fak index freshness | grep -i 'new-model-playbook\|REDDIT-TOKEN-TOOLS'  # no finding
```

Lane: `devindex`.

records.title: feat(dojo): additive RegisterLever seam so KPI-cell leaves stop serializing on allDojoLevers
records.body:
## Parent context
RSI-dojo overall-performance KPI seeding epic #4481 (a child of the dojo RSI epic #1021). This is not a KPI cell but the enabling seam every cell in that wave needs: without it each of #4486, #4487, #4489, #4492, #4493, #4494 must edit one shared file on the contended `cmd` lane.

## Generation stream
- Generation: now
- Parent: #4481
- Stream: gen/now; risk: low (additive composition seam, no behavior change); proof: an existing provider lever ported onto the seam with the dojo gate green.

## Current state
`internal/dojo` grew an additive claim seam — `RegisterClaim(lever, metric, claim(...))` — so a KPI cell declares its claim in its OWN file and never edits the central `Registry` literal. `claims.go` states the intent plainly: "adding a cell never edits — and never conflicts on — that central literal ... letting parallel KPI-cell workers avoid colliding on one file and one map." `claim_guard_integrity.go` and `claim_guard_stop.go` are the shipped one-file examples.

The **lever half was never built**. A cell only actually scores once its concrete lever is:
1. implemented in `cmd/fak` (it must read a corpus/ledger, and `internal/architest` pins `"dojo": 1` — stdlib-only, "the corpus-scanning levers live in cmd/fak"), and
2. listed in `allDojoLevers()` in `cmd/fak/dojo.go`, and
3. advertised in `dojoLeverCatalog()` (pinned by `TestDojoCatalogMatchesProviderCostEmittedMetrics`, which asserts the catalog matches the metrics the lever emits).

Steps 2 and 3 are edits to one shared file on the `cmd` lane. So the collision the claim seam was designed to prevent still happens — one layer down.

## Why this is next
The #4481 seeding wave is ~13 (lever, metric) KPI leaves. Every one of #4486, #4487, #4489, #4492, #4493, #4494 must edit the same `allDojoLevers()` + `dojoLeverCatalog()` in `cmd/fak/dojo.go`, so the whole wave serializes on a single contended lane. Witnessed 2026-07-16: `dos arbitrate --lane cmd` refused (`already held by a live loop`) while a live peer refactor moved all five provider levers out of `cmd/fak/dojo.go` (-554 lines) into an untracked `cmd/fak/dojo_provider_levers.go`. #4494 could hold its own `dojo` lease and land its claim cell, but could not land its lever at all — not a hardware or design gap, purely the missing seam.

## Working spine
Mirror `RegisterClaim` for levers: an additive `RegisterLever` seam so a KPI leaf ships its lever + claim + catalog row in its own file, and `allDojoLevers()`/`dojoLeverCatalog()` compose the registered set instead of hard-coding a literal list.

## Confusion risks
- The seam registers a lever; it does NOT relax the `dojo: 1` tier. Concrete corpus-scanning levers still live in `cmd/fak` — this is about composition, not layering.
- `RegisterClaim` panics on a duplicate cell; the lever seam should refuse a duplicate lever name the same loud way, at init, not shadow silently.

## Work unit
leaf

## Expected steps
4

## In scope
An additive lever-registration seam plus its catalog row, with `allDojoLevers()`/`dojoLeverCatalog()` folding the registered set; port one existing provider lever onto it as the worked example.

## Out of scope
Do NOT redefine any existing claim, metric, or acceptance gate; no new KPI cells; no tier change to `internal/dojo`.

## Done condition
A KPI-cell leaf can add its lever + claim + catalog row in one new file, with no edit to `allDojoLevers()` or `dojoLeverCatalog()`, and `fak dojo run` folds it.

## Witness
go test ./internal/dojo ./cmd/fak -run Dojo

## Acceptance gate
go test ./internal/dojo ./cmd/fak

## Lane
cmd

## Path hints
- `cmd/fak/dojo.go`
- `cmd/fak/dojo_provider_levers.go`
- `internal/dojo/claims.go`

## Batch policy
One issue for the seam itself; do not file a duplicate per blocked KPI cell — update this issue on rerun rather than spamming a cell-by-cell variant.

## Boundary notes
Public issue only. No provider account ids or raw bills.

## Work estimate
Estimate: 3 points. Uncertainty: operator-supplied estimate; revise through the parent denominator when evidence changes.

## Overall completion contribution
Contribution: 3/40 points.

## Completion standard
production

## Target operating envelope
- levers folded per dojo run: >= 11 levers
- shared-file edits per new KPI cell: >= 0 files

## Witnessed operating envelope
- levers folded per dojo run: >= 11 levers
- shared-file edits per new KPI cell: >= 2 files

records.title: feat(cmd): wire a `fak memory curate` subcommand over memq.BudgetCurate/CurateRegret (fak cmd)
records.body:
## Context

The budget-curated forgetting LIBRARY landed in `internal/memq/curate.go` (commit 9972f8424183, #3908): `BudgetCurate` (value-ranked eviction under a hard byte cap), `ApplyCurate` (negative-only, caps-gated tombstone), `CurateRegret` (regret keep-bit with gross/net split), and `CurateReportText` (operator report renderer), all witnessed by `internal/memq/curate_test.go` (9 tests).

#3908 DoD item 4 asks that a `fak` report surfaces the byte budget, evicted set, and running regret rate. The renderer exists (`memq.CurateReportText`); what remains is the thin CLI shell in the `cmd` lane (`cmd/fak/memory*.go`), not the `memq` lane #3908 was routed to.

## Definition of Done

- A `fak memory curate --budget N [--dir DIR] [--apply] [--json]` subcommand loading the memq backend (same seam as `fak memory recall`), running `memq.BudgetCurate`, printing `memq.CurateReportText`, and applying tombstones via `memq.ApplyCurate` only under `--apply` (fail-closed otherwise).
- Per-cell witnessed-value signal wired from the recall-events ledger (memvaluescore fold) or the persisted `memq.ValueAttr` — ranking by realized value, never size.
- A `--json` path emitting `CurateReport` + `RegretReport`.
- A cmd-lane test asserting the subcommand renders budget, evicted set, and regret rate.

## Lane
cmd (`cmd/fak/**`) — the library dependency (`internal/memq`) is already shipped in 9972f8424183.

Source: 9972f8424183 (#3908); `internal/memq/curate.go`; `cmd/fak/memory_recall.go`.

records.title: fix(model): make the resident-CUDA routed-expert path reachable from the live glm_moe_dsa decode
records.body:
## Parent context

Parent: #4784

## Problem

The resident-CUDA routed-expert work landed by #4843 (`77bf256c9`, `c2a0aae83`) is
**unreachable dead code on the live `glm_moe_dsa` serve path**. This is why #4784's DGX
evidence still shows ~0.09-0.21 tok/s: the device path exists but never executes.

The gate chain:

- `routedExpertKQuantActive(mat)` — `internal/model/moe.go:181-184` — type-asserts
  `mat.(sessionQ4KKernel)`.
- `sessionQ4KKernel` is constructed in exactly ONE place: `internal/model/quant_forward.go:214`,
  inside the *generic* `blockStep` decode.
- The GLM-5.2 decode does NOT go through it. `decodeBandGLMDsa` -> `glmDsaMatKernel()`
  (`internal/model/moe_offload.go:132-142`) returns `residentKernel` / `backendKernel` /
  `splitKernel` — **never** `sessionQ4KKernel`.

Therefore `expertSwiGLUHAL` (`hal.go:248-298`), `q4kExpertInputHAL`
(`moe_device_gateup.go:8-33`) and `routedExpertKQuantActive` are never reached in a
production GLM EP serve, so the `!routedExpertKQuantActive(mat)` guard at
`expert_parallel.go:162` is always true and the host scalar batch always wins:
`expert_parallel.go:162` -> `hostBatchedGLMExperts` -> `batchedExpertDelta` ->
`kQuantBatchRows` -> `kQuantMatRowsRange` (`quant_kquant.go:224-246`).

Compounding it: `backendKernel.mul` (`internal/model/kernel.go:98-105`) diverts ANY weight
resident in `m.kqw` (Q5_K/Q6_K — the GLM-5.2 expert `down_proj`) to `kQuantMatRows`, i.e.
host scalar GEMV *on the device path*. CUDA already has `fcuda_q5k_matmul_f32` /
`fcuda_q6k_matmul_f32` (`internal/compute/cuda.go:780-787`), but `glmDsaWeightHAL`
(`kernel.go:214-234`) **panics** on a `kqw` weight (`:230-231`) instead of routing to them.

## Definition of done

- [ ] The routed-expert HAL gate keys on the `*Session`/backend capability rather than the
      concrete kernel type (or `backendKernel` implements the `sessionQ4KKernel` seam), so
      the device path is reachable from `decodeBandGLMDsa`.
- [ ] `backendKernel.mul` routes `kqw` (Q5_K/Q6_K) to the existing CUDA kernels instead of
      `kQuantMatRows`; `glmDsaWeightHAL` stages `kqw` via `weightHALKQuant` instead of panicking.
- [ ] A regression witness proves the live `glm_moe_dsa` decode actually constructs a kernel
      that satisfies the routed-expert gate — the current HAL tests
      (`moe_expert_hal_test.go:246`) drive `sessionQ4KKernel{s: sess}` directly and so
      cannot catch this class.
- [ ] Token/logit parity against the host reference path is unchanged.

## Witness

A test that fails before the fix by asserting `glmDsaMatKernel()`'s return satisfies the
routed-expert gate, plus a device-run tok/s delta on sanctioned 8-GPU hardware.

## Notes

Found while working #4784. The existing device-HAL unit tests all pass while the live path
is dead, so this is a test-reachability gap, not only a wiring gap. The tok/s target itself
belongs to parent #4784; this leaf's own done-condition is reachability + parity.

## Work estimate
Estimate: 5 points. Uncertainty: operator-supplied estimate; revise through the parent denominator when evidence changes.

## Overall completion contribution
Contribution: 5/100 points.

## Completion standard
development

records.title: fix(dgxbridge): readback wedges (sentinel_missing) on every live control session, blocking all GPU witnesses
records.body:
## Parent context

Parent: #4784

## Problem

Hardware-gated work for #4784 (and every other GPU-witness leaf) cannot produce evidence:
the private lab control-bridge enumerates its live control sessions fine, but **every `run`
readback wedges**:

```
dgxbridge: run(to-file): dgxbridge: READBACK_WEDGED: sentinel_missing:
  exec(tail): dgxbridge: completion sentinel not found in this thread's transcript
```

Reproduced 2026-07-16 against two *separate* live persistent tmux sessions with the current
client build, `-timeout 6m`/`8m`, on a trivial command (`nvidia-smi --query-gpu=...`).
An earlier attempt failed differently (`exec_error: ... context deadline exceeded` on the
chat-history fetch), so the transcript/readback path — not the box — is the suspect.
`sessions` itself returns promptly and lists three running sessions, so discovery and auth
are healthy; only readback is wedged.

This is load-bearing: #4784's definition of done requires a live 8x80GB warm-generation
witness plus a benchmark artifact. With readback wedged, no hardware claim can be made, so
the issue cannot progress past "not yet".

## Definition of done

- [ ] Root-cause why the completion sentinel does not land in the control thread's
      transcript for a live persistent session (sentinel emission vs. transcript mirror lag
      vs. history-fetch window).
- [ ] `dgxbridge selftest` passes against a live persistent session, or its failure names the
      actionable fix per the guide's "the error text names the one fix" contract.
- [ ] A trivial `run 'nvidia-smi ...'` returns output and its rc.
- [ ] If the wedge is a busy-session condition rather than a bug, the error text says so and
      names the recovery (pick another session) instead of the generic `sentinel_missing`.

## Witness

A captured `dgxbridge selftest` plus a `run` round-trip against a live session, with the
client revision recorded.

## Notes

Client and hub live in the private companion repo; host/channel identifiers are deliberately
kept out of this public issue. Blocks #4784 and #4843. Separately, the checked-in client
binary in the private checkout is stale (no `run` verb) — a fresher build under the private
verify dir has the modern verb set; worth reconciling so an agent does not pick the stale one.

## Work estimate
Estimate: 3 points. Uncertainty: operator-supplied estimate; revise through the parent denominator when evidence changes.

## Overall completion contribution
Contribution: 3/100 points.

## Completion standard

records.title: fix(tokencache): suppress UNSUPPRESSED_GO_EXEC popup in cache.go commonDir — it freezes all fleet pushes
records.body:
Child of #2866 (whole-tree popup-gate push-freeze class).

## Symptom
Every fleet `git push` is frozen by the desktop-popup pre-push gate:
```
DESKTOP_POPUP_REGRESSION (blocked): a tracked console-tool spawn would flash a window under background automation.
  popup spawn: internal/tokencache/cache.go:112: exec.Command reaches out, err := cmd.Output()
  before configureDispatchHelperCommand(cmd)/configureDispatchSpawn(cmd) (UNSUPPRESSED_GO_EXEC)
```
The pre-push scanner (cmd/fak/hooks_popup_scan.go -> windowgate.ScanTree, `git ls-files --cached --others`) scans the WHOLE tree, so one unsuppressed spawn anywhere blocks every session's push.

## Root cause
internal/tokencache/cache.go commonDir() spawns git without the no-window hook (out, err := cmd.Output() with no windowgate.ConfigureBackgroundCommand(cmd) first). As of filing, internal/tokencache/ (cache.go + cache_test.go) is a NEW package, staged but uncommitted in the shared index with no live lease owner.

## Fix
Add windowgate.ConfigureBackgroundCommand(cmd) after the exec.Command in commonDir(), then let the owner commit the package. Do NOT override with FLEET_ALLOW_POPUP=1 — that would land a real console-flash regression on origin.

## Lane
tokencache

## Acceptance
fak hooks pre-push (windowgate.ScanTree) reports no UNSUPPRESSED_GO_EXEC for internal/tokencache; a clean fleet push succeeds.

## Impact
Blocks origin delivery of at least 3 local-ahead commits (efc922fa4 for #5046, 45e744cf8, 5d0d8bc9e) and all fleet pushes.

Filed via raw gh (fak issue create's project-work envelope validator rejects a bug report whose witnessed reality intentionally violates its target).

records.title: feat(steerpr): wire the trajctl->steerpr curve join + `fak steer prs` render (consumer of #5038)
records.body:
Child of #5015. #5038 shipped the pure steerpr curve-carry primitive (`internal/steerpr/curve.go`: `Curve`, `Curve.Annotate/NeedsAttention/Actionable`, `AttachCurves`, `DriftHiddenByBand`, `Unit.Curve`). steerpr is tier-1 stdlib-only (architest) so it cannot import trajctl; the join + render is CLI-lane consumer wiring left to do.

## In scope
- The trajctl->steerpr map: fold the trajctl ledger (`trajctl.Fold` / `ScoresFor` / `CurveFor`), resolve each open overlay unit's bound objective (by resolved issue #N or leaf), map `trajctl.Signal`/`WitnessRung` onto `steerpr.CurveSignal`/`CurveRung` via `steerpr.AttachCurves`.
- A `fak steer prs` operator view (new `cmd/fak/steer_prs.go`) rendering units worst-attention-first (`steerpr.SortWorstFirst`) with each unit's `Curve.Annotate()` line, surfacing `DriftHiddenByBand` emphatically.

records.title: fix(hooks): DESKTOP_POPUP_REGRESSION pre-push gate scans untracked peer WIP, blocking unrelated pushes
records.body:
## Symptom
Pushing a clean, in-lane commit (ff32e5119a41, touches only `internal/kvmmu/**`) was blocked at `git push` by the `DESKTOP_POPUP_REGRESSION` pre-push gate, which flagged `internal/tokencache/cache.go:112` (an `UNSUPPRESSED_GO_EXEC` popup-spawn regression).

That file is **untracked** (`git status --porcelain` ⇒ `?? internal/tokencache/cache.go`) — a peer's in-flight WIP. git never pushes an untracked file, and my push diff (`git diff origin/main..HEAD`) was provably just the two kvmmu files. The gate scans working-tree files including untracked peer WIP, so it produces a false-positive block against an unrelated, clean push. Recovery required the documented `FLEET_ALLOW_POPUP=1 git push` one-shot override.

## Why it's wrong
A pre-push gate should judge what is being **pushed** (the committed diff over `origin/main`), not arbitrary untracked scratch in the shared multi-session tree. As written it lets any peer's uncommitted file indefinitely block every other worker's push, and pushes them toward the override flag — which erodes the gate.

## Fix direction
Scope the popup scan to the pushed diff (files in `git diff --name-only origin/<trunk>..HEAD`), or overlay-away untracked siblings the way `fak buildcheck` already does for the build gate. A genuine popup regression *in the pushed commit* must still block.

## Done-condition
A commit that does not itself touch a popup-regressing file pushes cleanly even when an untracked peer file carrying `UNSUPPRESSED_GO_EXEC` sits in the tree; a popup regression inside the pushed diff still blocks. Witness: a test over the pre-push hook with (a) untracked offender + clean pushed diff ⇒ allow, (b) offender in the pushed diff ⇒ block.

Lane: hooks / windowgate. Surfaced while shipping #3901.

## Work estimate
3 points — scope the popup scan to the pushed diff (or overlay untracked siblings) plus a two-case hook test.

## Overall completion contribution
~2% of the fleet-hooks reliability surface — removes a recurring false-positive push block on the shared multi-session trunk.

records.title: feat(cmd): collect the OSP overlay in fak operator brief --collect
records.body:
## Parent context

Follow-on from #5024 (the OSP overlay fold into `operatorbrief`), which landed in
`3fe4ccf2d50f` — `internal/operatorbrief@r15+g3fe4ccf2d`.

## Current state

#5024 added the OSP overlay as an `operatorbrief` source. `fak operator brief --osp <path>`
folds a steerpr `{schema, units}` envelope into the human / watch / background buckets, and a
missing or unreadable payload marks the source `unmeasured` rather than folding a clean zero.

Every *other* optional source carries a live-collect arm in `cmd/fak/operator.go`:

```go
if *programPath == ""   && *collect { ... operatorCollectProgram(...)   }
if *milestonePath == "" && *collect { ... operatorCollectMilestone(...) }
if *heavinessPath == "" && *collect { ... operatorCollectHeaviness(...) }
```

The OSP source has **no** such arm — it is folded only when `--osp` is passed explicitly:

```go
if *ospPath != "" { o := loadOSPBriefInput(*ospPath, os.Stdin); in.OSP = &o }
```

So `fak operator brief --collect` — the "collect any missing report input live" path — silently
omits the overlay. The source folds as `missing`, so the brief is not *wrong*, but an operator
who asked the pane to collect everything gets a brief with no overlay in it and no signal that
the overlay was skipped.

## Why this was not done in #5024

#5024's scope was the fold + bucket mapping. The collect arm needs a producer verb to shell to,
and `fak steer prs --json` does not exist yet — it is #5021. The witness for #5024 was captured
against `fak release prplan --json`, which emits the same envelope.

## In scope

- Add the `if *ospPath == "" && *collect` arm to `cmd/fak/operator.go`, shelling to
  `fak steer prs --json` once #5021 lands.
- A collect failure must fold as `unmeasured` (the existing `OSP{Unreadable: true}` path), NOT
  return a non-zero exit — the overlay is an optional source and must never red the brief. Note
  this differs from the program/milestone/heaviness collect arms, which `return 1` on failure.

## Out of scope

- Any change to the bucket mapping or the four-bucket vocabulary (closed on purpose).
- Changing what `--check` fails on (still only the human bucket).

## Done condition

- `fak operator brief --collect --json` includes an `osp` source stamp and OSP-bucketed entries
  without an explicit `--osp`.
- With the producer unavailable, `--collect` still exits as it would have, and the `osp` source
  reads `unmeasured` / `osp_unmeasured`.

## Witness

`go test ./cmd/fak -run OperatorBriefCollectOSP -count=1` green, including a case that stubs a
failing producer and proves the brief still folds valid with an `unmeasured` osp source; plus a
captured `fak operator brief --collect --json` showing OSP entries with no `--osp` flag.

## Blocked on

#5021 (`feat(steerpr): add fak steer prs to fold the pending dev-to-release delta`).

1 — add the collect arm + its unmeasured-on-failure path.

records.title: perf(model): per-NUMA-node Q4_K weight replication + barrier-free per-node decode schedule (Qwen3.6 CPU decode)
records.body:
## Parent context

Epic #4623 (CLOSED — Qwen3.6-27B CPU decode → 10 tok/s on EPYC-7742, 8 NUMA). Follows
#4625 (worker cap **shipped**) and #4974 (in-process interleave-placement seam). This is
#4625's **unshipped second half** (per-node replication + barrier-free schedule), re-filed
as a fresh issue because #4625 was closed with only the worker cap landed.

## Context

The OBSERVED witness `experiments/qwen36/cpu-decode-int8-q4k-numa-witness-2026-07-14.md`
establishes why placement alone is not enough and names the real multiplier:

- The 64-worker cap (#4625, `q4kDecodeWorkers`) delivers **1.395 tok/s**, 2.35× over the
  uncapped 256-worker default — the shipped win, auto-selected on the ordinary decode path.
- In-process NUMA **interleave placement** (the #4974 seam) is **marginal at the tuned
  worker count**: interleave vs default at 256w was only +6% (0.629 vs 0.593); at 64w it is
  within noise. Interleave leaves 7/8 of weight reads remote (xGMI-capped), and the decode
  kernel is barrier/compute-bound per node, not bandwidth-bound.
- The named unbuilt multiplier is **per-NUMA-node weight replication** (8 × ~15.2 GB
  node-local replicas, trivial in ~945 GiB free) **plus a barrier-free per-node schedule**
  (remove the shared-cursor parFor cross-socket barrier).
- NUMA-additivity witness (§5): 8 node-pinned concurrent streams aggregated **4.53 tok/s** →
  honest revised single-stream ceiling **~5–7 tok/s** (not the raw-STREAM ~14; the kernel
  reaches only ~1/3 of the node-local STREAM ceiling).

## Done condition

- Resident-Q4_K weights replicated per online NUMA node (node-local placement); the replica
  set derives from runtime topology (no hardcoded node count) and stays overrideable.
- Batch-1 decode runs a barrier-free per-node schedule (no cross-socket shared cursor);
  output stays **bit-identical to the serial reference** (the max|Δ|=0 decode rungs hold).
- Failure-first tests: replica set + schedule derive from the online-node count and model
  shape; bit-identity preserved; overrideable via `FAK_WORKERS`/`FAK_BUDGET`/a placement knob.
- Run the pinned Qwen3.6-27B Q4_K_M on the CPU server through the **ordinary decode path**;

  `decode_bw_util_%`) that improves over the #4625 tuned baseline (1.395 tok/s).

Note: 5 tok/s is the honest revised replication ceiling from the §5 additivity witness; the
epic-#4623 10 tok/s target additionally needs a bytes/token cut (see #4628). The current
#4625 tuned baseline is 1.395 tok/s; per-node replication + barrier-free schedule are unbuilt.

records.body:
## Summary

The tree-wide `DESKTOP_POPUP_REGRESSION` push gate is currently wedging the **whole fleet push** on a file that is **staged but never committed**:

```
internal/tokencache/cache.go:112: exec.Command reaches out, err := cmd.Output()
  before configureDispatchHelperCommand(cmd) / configureDispatchSpawn(cmd)
  (UNSUPPRESSED_GO_EXEC)
```

`git status --porcelain -- internal/tokencache/cache.go` reports `A ` (staged add); `git log -- internal/tokencache/cache.go` is empty, so the file exists only in a peer's index. No commit in `origin/main..HEAD` contains it.

## Why this matters

`git push` pushes **commits**, not the index — but the popup gate scans tracked/staged files, so one session's staged WIP blocks every *other* session's already-green, already-committed work from reaching the trunk. Observed here blocking `12296ef58886` (`fix(guard): ... (#4888) (fak cmd)`), whose diff is disjoint from `internal/tokencache/**`.

The documented recoveries both look wrong for a bystander:
- suppressing the spawn means editing a peer's in-flight WIP;
- `FLEET_ALLOW_POPUP=1` is marked *intentional only*, and the regression is not the pusher's.

## Done-condition

Either (a) the gate scopes its scan to the paths actually contained in the commits being pushed (so staged-but-uncommitted peer WIP cannot wedge the fleet), or (b) it emits a distinct, actionable reason when the offending path is staged-not-committed and owned by another session — naming the owner and a non-destructive recovery — instead of directing the bystander to edit or override.

Related: the same tree-wide-gate-blocks-the-fleet class as the `TIER_DECLARED` push backstop (#4950).

## Work estimate

## Parent context

Parent: #3165 (fleet build-isolation / trunk-landing epic)

`git push origin main` is refused for every worker on this shared checkout by a
`DESKTOP_POPUP_REGRESSION` finding in a file that is **staged but never committed**:

```
DESKTOP_POPUP_REGRESSION (blocked): a tracked console-tool spawn would flash a window under background automation.
  popup spawn: internal/tokencache/cache.go:112: exec.Command reaches out, err := cmd.Output()
  before configureDispatchHelperCommand(cmd) / configureDispatchSpawn(cmd) (UNSUPPRESSED_GO_EXEC)
```

`internal/tokencache/cache.go` and `cache_test.go` show as `A ` (staged-new) in the
shared index and appear in **no commit** (`git log -- internal/tokencache/cache.go` is
empty). The offending spawn is `commonDir()`:

```go
cmd := exec.Command("git", "rev-parse", "--git-common-dir")
// ... cmd.Output() with no windowgate suppression
```

## Why this blocks others

The pre-push guard scans tracked/staged files, so a peer's *uncommitted* staged WIP
refuses pushes of commits that do not touch `internal/tokencache/` at all. Witnessed
while pushing two `internal/executionroute` commits (b76e07f65395, 3a2a19cb13ba) for
 #4965: none of the four commits ahead touch `internal/tokencache/`.

The documented override (`FLEET_ALLOW_POPUP=1`) is marked intentional-only, and this
is an unintentional regression in a lane the blocked worker does not lease, so
overriding it would be routing around a correct guard on someone else's defect.

## Done condition

- `internal/tokencache.commonDir` suppresses its `git rev-parse` spawn via
  `windowgate.ConfigureBackgroundCommand` (or the dispatch-helper equivalent) before
  `cmd.Output()`, so the file stops refusing pushes once committed.
- Decide whether the pre-push popup scan should consider **staged-but-uncommitted**
  paths at all: a file in no commit cannot regress the pushed tip, so scanning it
  converts one worker's in-flight WIP into a fleet-wide push stall.

## Witness

- Before: `git push origin main` from a checkout with `internal/tokencache/cache.go`
  staged refuses `DESKTOP_POPUP_REGRESSION` while no pushed commit touches that path.
- After: the same push is admitted, and a windowgate unit test covers `commonDir`
  spawning suppressed.

```routing
lane: tokencache
paths: internal/tokencache/**,internal/windowgate/**
expected_steps: 4
```

## Work estimate

Estimate: 4 points. Uncertainty: whether the pre-push scan should skip staged-but-uncommitted paths, or only the spawn needs suppressing.

## Overall completion contribution

Contribution: 4/100 points.

## Target operating envelope

- spawn suppression: commonDir git rev-parse runs windowless under background automation
- push scope: a staged-but-uncommitted file no pushed commit touches does not refuse the push

## Witnessed operating envelope

- spawn suppression: commonDir calls exec.Command("git","rev-parse","--git-common-dir") + cmd.Output() with no windowgate wrap
- push scope: pre-push popup scan refuses on staged-only internal/tokencache/cache.go while no pushed commit touches it

records.title: chore(dos): declare egresslist/egressrefresh lanes in dos.toml so arbitration serializes them
records.body:
## Context

Shipping #4978 (`feat(egresslist): refresh bundled filter lists from upstream with
pinned checksums`, commit `0ce860cd2`) added two leaves — `internal/egresslist` and
`internal/egressrefresh` — but neither is declared as a lane in `dos.toml`.

`fak commit --preview` flagged this at commit time:

> leaf `egresslist` names a real package but no dos.toml lane declares it — the arbiter
> cannot detect a same-tree collision on it; consider declaring lane `egresslist`

Because of the gap, #4978 had to be arbitrated under the borrowed `policy` lane
(`internal/policy/**`) even though the change lives entirely in `internal/egresslist/**`,
`internal/egressrefresh/**`, and `cmd/fak/**`. Two agents editing the egress-list leaves
concurrently would not be serialized by `dos arbitrate`.

## Ask

Declare lanes for the egress-list leaves so arbitration can detect same-tree collisions:

- Add an `egresslist` lane mapping `internal/egresslist/**` (and, if co-owned, the
  `cmd/fak/egresslist*.go` verb surface).
- Add an `egressrefresh` lane mapping `internal/egressrefresh/**`, or fold it into the
  `egresslist` lane's tree if the two are always edited together (the refresh engine is
  the maintenance twin of the classifier).

## Acceptance

- `dos arbitrate --workspace . --lane egresslist --output json` acquires a lane whose
  `tree` includes `internal/egresslist/**`.
- `fak commit --preview -m "...(fak egresslist)" --path internal/egresslist/...` no longer
  emits the "no dos.toml lane declares it" advisory.

## Provenance

Surfaced by #4978. Out of scope for that issue (which shipped the refresh mechanism); this
is the arbitration-hygiene follow-up.

## Work estimate

1 point — a `dos.toml` lane-table edit plus a small preview-advisory regression assertion.
Bounded, single-file config change with no runtime/hot-path impact.

## Overall completion contribution

Standalone arbitration-hygiene chore (fleet-infra). It does not advance a product epic's
definition of done; it closes a same-tree-collision blind spot the #4978 leaves created.

## Target operating envelope

Config/authoring only — no request-path or hot-path code. The `dos arbitrate` lane lookup
is already O(lanes) over an in-memory table; adding two entries has no measurable latency
or token cost. Envelope: zero added decide-path work; arbitration lookup stays <1ms.

## Witnessed operating envelope

Not yet implemented, so no runtime witness exists. Pre-implementation witness: the change
is confined to `dos.toml` (config) — `git grep` shows the arbitration lane table is read
once per `dos arbitrate` call, off the decide path. Post-implementation witness to capture
in the fix: `dos arbitrate --lane egresslist --output json` returns the mapped tree, and a
preview-advisory assertion goes green.

records.title: fix(dgxbridge): control-bridge PTY wedges readback while doctor/sessions still report healthy
records.body:
## Parent context

Parent: #5106. Surfaced while dispatching the #4968 multi-rank device-collective rung to a
sanctioned lab GPU node. The node itself is healthy; the control bridge's exec path is not.
This blocks **every** hardware-gated leaf that needs the lab, so it is filed on its own
rather than buried in one issue's comments.

## Symptom

The control plane is healthy while the exec/readback path is wedged:

```
dgxbridge doctor — READY
  [ok] slack_token     resolved
  [ok] control_channel resolved

dgxbridge sessions   → persistent-7 / persistent-2 / persistent-4   all RUNNING

dgxbridge run '<any command>'
  → READBACK_WEDGED: exec_error: exec(tail): context deadline exceeded

dgxbridge selftest
  → readback BROKEN: sentinel_missing — the shell isn't executing/echoing commands
    — the PTY may be wedged; restart the control bridge
```

Reproduced across **all three** live sessions and **both** readback modes (default
file-capture and `-transcript`). A single early probe did return output before the wedge set
in, so this is a degradation during the session, not a permanently broken client.

## Why it matters

`sessions` and `doctor` both report healthy, so a caller sees a green control plane and only
discovers the wedge after a multi-minute `-timeout` burn per attempt. Any agent told "never
stop for lack of local hardware; dispatch sanctioned compute" will find a live node, then
silently fail to run anything on it.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] The control bridge is restarted (or self-heals) so `dgxbridge selftest` reports the
      readback path healthy.
- [ ] `dgxbridge run 'echo ok'` returns `ok` on a live session.
- [ ] A wedged PTY is surfaced by `doctor` / `sessions` rather than only by `selftest` or a
      timed-out `run`, so callers fail fast instead of burning a per-command timeout.

## Explicit non-claims

Not a claim about the GPU node's health — it enumerated 8 devices correctly. Not a client
bug report: `selftest` diagnoses the condition accurately and names the fix. The gap is that
the wedge is invisible to the health verbs and needs a private-side restart.

## Target operating envelope

N/A — an availability/repair leaf, not a performance leaf. Its done-condition is a healthy
`selftest` plus a fail-fast health verb, not a latency/throughput threshold. Declared N/A
rather than invented.

## Witnessed operating envelope

N/A — no throughput or latency number is claimed. The witness is the captured `selftest` /
`run` output above, reproduced across 3 sessions and 2 readback modes.

## Work estimate
Estimate: 2 points. Uncertainty: the restart is likely trivial; the fail-fast health-verb
change is the real work.

## Overall completion contribution
Contribution: 2/2 points.

records.title: fix(concept): the disambiguation generator silently wipes fak concept classify entries from _meta.json
records.body:
## Problem
`python tools/concept_disambiguation_scorecard.py --markdown-dir docs/concept-disambiguation-scorecard` **silently drops classifications** that `fak concept classify` just wrote into `tools/concept_disambiguation_scorecard.data/_meta.json`.

Witnessed on 2026-07-16 while landing #4330:
1. Ran `fak concept classify --family cache --token FAK_TOKEN_CACHE --category incidental --reason ...` (×5). `git diff` confirmed all 5 tokens landed in the family's `classifications` **and** `ignore` arrays.
2. Ran the python generator exactly as the `CONCEPT_FRESHNESS` gate instructs ("run `python tools/concept_disambiguation_scorecard.py ...` and stage the result").
3. All 5 classifications were **gone** from `_meta.json` — `grep -c FAK_TOKEN_CACHE _meta.json` → `0`.

The result committed as `8b3ba9321` before the loss was noticed; it had to be re-applied and re-committed as `eb8e552c1`.

## Why it matters
The `CONCEPT_ADMISSION` gate's own remediation text points at `fak concept classify`, and the `CONCEPT_FRESHNESS` gate's remediation text points at the python generator. Following **both** in the order the gates present them destroys the first one's work — and the loss is silent (the generator exits without naming what it dropped). Any worker classifying a new concept token on a shared trunk can land a commit that looks correct and is missing its classifications.

## Expected
The generator must either preserve `classifications`/`ignore` entries it did not author, or refuse loudly and name the entries it would drop. `fak concept classify` already regenerates the scorecard itself, so the two writers need one owner.

## Repro
```
fak concept classify --family cache --token ZZZ_PROBE_TOKEN_CACHE --category incidental --reason probe
grep -c ZZZ_PROBE_TOKEN_CACHE tools/concept_disambiguation_scorecard.data/_meta.json   # -> 2
python tools/concept_disambiguation_scorecard.py --markdown-dir docs/concept-disambiguation-scorecard
grep -c ZZZ_PROBE_TOKEN_CACHE tools/concept_disambiguation_scorecard.data/_meta.json   # -> 0  (expected: 2)
```

## Done condition
A failing-then-passing test that classifies a token, runs the generator, and asserts the classification survives.

Found while shipping #4330.

records.title: fix(concept): CONCEPT_FRESHNESS is unsatisfiable on Windows — generator writes CRLF, git stages LF
records.body:
## Problem
On a native-Windows host, `CONCEPT_FRESHNESS` is a **structural false positive** for any commit that stages a concept artifact — it can never be satisfied, only overridden.

`tools/concept_disambiguation_scorecard.py` writes `docs/concept-disambiguation-scorecard/README.md` with **CRLF** line endings. Git normalizes the staged blob to **LF** (`warning: in the working copy of 'docs/concept-disambiguation-scorecard/README.md', CRLF will be replaced by LF the next time Git touches it`). The gate then compares the **staged/committed** README against a **fresh regeneration** and sees a whole-file line-ending diff → reports stale, forever.

Witnessed 2026-07-16 landing #4330:
- `fak concept freshness` run against the **working tree** → `concept generated artifacts fresh` (CRLF vs CRLF: match).
- The same check inside `fak commit`'s isolated index → `CONCEPT_FRESHNESS: generated concept artifacts are stale: [docs/concept-disambiguation-scorecard/README.md]`.
- Regenerating and re-staging does **not** clear it — the next comparison re-normalizes and diverges again.

The only way to land was `FLEET_CONCEPT_FRESHNESS_GUARD=off`.

## Why it matters
A gate that cannot be satisfied trains workers to reach for the override reflexively, which is exactly how a real staleness would then slip through. It also means `docs/concept-disambiguation-scorecard/README.md` sits permanently dirty on the shared trunk (it was already dirty from a peer before this ticket started), adding churn to every `git status`.

## Expected
Either the generator writes LF (`newline="\n"` on the open), or `.gitattributes` pins the generated markdown to LF, or the freshness comparison normalizes line endings before diffing. Any one of the three closes it; normalizing in the comparison also fixes already-committed CRLF artifacts.

## Done condition
On a Windows host: `python tools/concept_disambiguation_scorecard.py --markdown-dir docs/concept-disambiguation-scorecard`, stage the result, and commit **without** `FLEET_CONCEPT_FRESHNESS_GUARD=off` — the gate passes. Plus a regression test that the generated README round-trips through git staging unchanged.

Found while shipping #4330 (see also #5135 — the same generator silently drops classifications).

records.title: perf(tokencache): dogfood the token cache on the real ~5704-file tree — net-true hit-rate + wall-clock witness
records.body:
## Problem
#4330 landed the content-addressed token cache (`internal/tokencache`, `clonescan.WindowCache`) with full gate tests — round-trip, one-byte miss, tokenizer-version invalidation, git-common-dir placement, accelerate-never-gate. What it did **not** land is the **net-true measurement**: a dogfood run showing a real cross-invocation hit-rate and wall-clock drop on the actual ~5704-file tracked tree.

Until that exists, the speedup is **not yet** claimed. #4330's own body motivates the cache as "what lets the push rung (T4) and the CI job actually scale" (1.8-4.9s per invocation re-tokenizing the whole tree), and the generation triage on #4330 named this exact witness as the `gen/now` promotion evidence:

> a dogfood run shows a real cross-invocation hit-rate / wall-clock drop on the 5704-file tree

## What to measure
Per the [net-true-value standard](docs/standards/net-true-value.md) — measured against the *tuned* alternative, net of the cost it adds:
- **Cold vs warm** `fak dup guard --staged` wall-clock on the real tracked tree (cache empty → cache warm).
- **Hit rate** across a realistic commit (almost every sibling unchanged; a handful of files touched).
- **Net of the cost the cache adds**: the `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` resolve, the per-`Open` prune dir-scan, the JSON encode/decode per entry, and the disk read per file. A cache that reads more bytes than it saves lexing is not net-true — the entries hold the full window keys, which are large.
- **`FAK_TOKEN_CACHE=off` as the A arm**, cache-on as the B arm, same tree, same commit.

## Demotion evidence (an honest possible outcome)
The triage on #4330 named the retirement condition explicitly, and it should be reported if it holds: if the measured hit-rate net of miss + invalidation + `git rev-parse` I/O does not beat re-tokenizing — or if the in-memory `TreeIndex` alone (post-#4326) already makes the re-lex cheap enough — then the persisted layer is **not net-true** and should park or retire rather than ship as a claimed win.

## Done condition
A captured, reproducible A/B witness (provenance-labeled, per BENCHMARK-AUTHORITY.md letters) attached to this issue, and either (a) a net-true speedup claim with its numbers, or (b) an honest `not yet` / retire recommendation with the numbers that show it.

Follow-on to #4330 (shipped: `a63ded4fa`, `e10f4e375`). Part of #4325.

What IS witnessed today: the CPU reference's own math obligations, green in every non-Apple build via `internal/metalgemm/q2_0_witness_test.go` (bit layout, ternary code set, round-trip bounded by half a quantum, ref GEMV bit-exact vs the dense dequantized matvec; non-vacuous by mutation).

## Why this is next
The device witness is **already reachable in CI** and needs no hardware purchase: `.github/workflows/metal-decode-bench.yml` runs `runs-on: macos-latest` ("Apple Silicon (M-series), has a Metal device for compute") and already does `go build -tags fakmetal ./internal/metalgemm/` plus Metal parity tests. The Q2_0 parity tests just need to be invoked there. Without this, #4873's headline claim rests on a transliteration argument rather than an executed kernel.

## In scope
A CI step (extend `metal-decode-bench.yml`, or a sibling workflow) that on `macos-latest` runs `go test ./internal/metalgemm -run Q2_0 -count=1 -v`, so the Metal ternary GEMV parity is executed on a real Metal device and the result is readable in the run log.

## Out of scope
Kernel changes (#4873 landed those), model-side wiring (#4870), CUDA (#4872).

## Done condition
`go test ./internal/metalgemm -run Q2_0` executes on a real Apple-Silicon Metal device in CI and the Metal-vs-CPU-ref parity assertions pass (not skip).

## Witness
The CI run log showing `TestMetalQ2_0GemvMatchesCPU` PASS (not SKIP) on `macos-latest`. A SKIP means no Metal device was present and does not close this.

## Lane
`ci` / workflows — the trailer binds to the diff's lane (`.github/workflows/**`), not to `metalgemm`.

## Likely files
`.github/workflows/metal-decode-bench.yml`

## Confusion risks
A green `go test` that SKIPs is the failure mode to guard against — assert the test actually ran. Also note `-tags metal` is a no-op for this package: the real constraint is `darwin && arm64 && cgo`, which `macos-latest` satisfies natively.

records.title: feat(metalgemm): ternary Q2_0 fused MLP and prefill GEMM (follow-on to #4873)
records.body:
## Parent context
Parent epic #4867. Follow-on to #4873 (Metal ternary Q2_0 GEMV, commit 478422235, `internal/metalgemm` r28), which landed the decode spine.

**Generation:** next · **Work unit:** leaf · **Expected steps:** 4 · **Requires:** an Apple-Silicon host (or the macos-latest CI runner, see #5140).

## Current state
#4873 landed the ternary decode spine in `internal/metalgemm`: `Q2_0Weight` + `UploadQ2_0` hold packed ternary blocks, and `GEMV` / `GEMVBatch` / `GEMVGroupQ2_0` run the MSL kernel `q2_0_gemv` in `q2_0.m` (one 32-lane simdgroup per output row, in-shader 2-bit unpack, `simd_sum` reduce).

Two items named in #4873's **In scope** are NOT part of its **Done condition** ("Metal `Q2_0` GEMV/GEMVBatch runs on Apple Silicon and matches CPU-ref ternary GEMM within tolerance"), and were deliberately left out of that commit rather than shipped unwitnessed:

- **Ternary `FusedMLP`** — the Q2_0 twin of `FusedMLP` / `FusedMLPQ6Down` in `q4k.go`: one command buffer for `y = down( silu(gate·x) * (up·x) )`, keeping the intermediate-wide gate/up/inter resident so only x and y cross the boundary.
- **Ternary prefill `GEMM`** — the Q2_0 twin of `Q4KWeight.GEMM` / `q8_gemm`: a register-blocked tiled `Y[P,Out] = X[P,In]·Wᵀ` so ternary prefill does not fall back to the CPU.

## Why this is next
Decode alone leaves the fused-MLP submit/sync collapse (the #1382 lever) and the whole prefill panel on the table for the ternary path. Both patterns are already proven for Q4_K/Q6_K/Q8 in this package, so this is transliterating them to the 2-bit unpack the ternary weight uses.

## In scope
`FusedMLPQ2_0` + a `q2_0_mlp` MSL kernel; `Q2_0Weight.GEMM` + a tiled `q2_0_gemm` MSL kernel; their parity tests.

## Out of scope
CUDA (#4872), CPU (T3), model-side wiring (#4870), the CI device-witness route (#5140).

## Done condition
Metal ternary `FusedMLP` and prefill `GEMM` run on Apple Silicon and match the CPU-ref ternary reference within tolerance.

## Witness
On an Apple host (or via #5140's runner): `go test ./internal/metalgemm -run Q2_0 -count=1` — new parity cases vs `q2_0RefGEMV` in `q2_0_ref_test.go`, whose own math obligations are already pinned in every build by `q2_0_witness_test.go`.

## Lane
`metalgemm` (compute family) — trailer `(fak metalgemm)`.

## Likely files
`internal/metalgemm/q2_0.go`, `internal/metalgemm/q2_0.m`, `internal/metalgemm/q2_0_test.go`

## Confusion risks
This is the **GGUF Metal** path, not MLX. The ternary activation is plain f32 (like `q4k_gemv`), NOT a quantized activation (unlike `q8_gemv`) — the CPU-ref ternary GEMV takes f32 x.

records.title: fix(lab): control sessions report running but no shell answers — probe returns STALE on all threads, blocking hardware-gated acceptance
records.body:
## Problem

Every control session on the lab GPU server is unreachable: a banner exists, but no shell
answers. This blocks all hardware-gated work that routes through the private control bridge,
including the throughput acceptance on #4843.

Witnessed 2026-07-16 from an authorized checkout with a working token:

- Session discovery succeeds and the hub bot answers, listing three `persistent-N`
  (profile=persistent, mode=tmux) sessions as `running`.
- Probing liveness (`status -probe`, 40s probe-wait, 5m timeout) returns **`STALE (no control
  reply within timeout)` for all 8 candidate control threads**.
- The bridge's own verdict: *"No live session: a banner exists but no shell answers. An operator
  must (re)start the control shell/bridge."*
- Consequently `exec` fails `completion sentinel not found in this thread's transcript` — the
  documented-reliable `!tail` readback path — because no shell is executing the command.

## Why it matters

- No current GPU occupancy reading, watcher state, or `results.jsonl`/`summary.json` can be
  obtained from the operator side, so hardware-gated acceptance cannot be witnessed **or** even
  honestly reported as "waiting on capacity" — the capacity itself is unreadable.
- The hub's `running` status is **stale and misleading**: it reflects a banner, not a live shell.
  An agent that reads the session listing without probing will conclude the lab is healthy and
  then fail confusingly at `exec`. Probe before trusting the listing.

## Operator action

1. Restart the control shell/bridge sessions on the GPU server.
2. Confirm each answers a liveness probe rather than merely appearing in the session listing.
3. Re-check that the all-eight-GPU watcher is still armed and sampling.

## Definition of done

- [ ] A liveness probe returns a live session (not `STALE`) and a trivial `exec` round-trips.
- [ ] The session listing's reported status agrees with a probe, or the divergence is documented
      where an agent will read it.

## Scope / boundary

Public-safe: no host, endpoint, channel id, or token here or in any fix. Live bridge/control code
stays in the private companion repo; this issue tracks only the outage and the operator action.

Blocks the remaining hardware DoD on #4843. Related: #5065 (the public lab-readiness gate cannot
go green independently while this holds).

records.title: fix(windowgate): scope the pre-push popup gate to the push range, not untracked peer WIP
records.body:
**Problem**

The pre-push `DESKTOP_POPUP_REGRESSION` gate scans the **working tree**, including a peer's **untracked** `.go` files. On this shared multi-session checkout that blocks pushes that do not contain the offending code — and cannot possibly introduce the regression, because an untracked file never reaches the trunk.

**Observed 2026-07-16**

Pushing an unrelated commit (`39122526c1d1`, `internal/codexlifecycle` only) is refused:

```
DESKTOP_POPUP_REGRESSION (blocked): a tracked console-tool spawn would flash a window under background automation.
  popup spawn: cmd/fak/steer_prs.go:179: exec.Command reaches buf, _ := cmd.Output() before
  configureDispatchHelperCommand(cmd) / configureDispatchSpawn(cmd) (UNSUPPRESSED_GO_EXEC)
```

But:

- `git status --porcelain -- cmd/fak/steer_prs.go` => `?? cmd/fak/steer_prs.go` (**untracked** peer WIP, last written 13:52).
- `git show HEAD:cmd/fak/steer_prs.go` => exit 128 (not in HEAD).
- `git diff --name-only origin/main..HEAD` does **not** list it — it is not in the push range.
- `fak hooks pre-push` reports `trunk-build-gate OK — pushed tip 39122526c1d1 builds`.

So the pushed content is clean; an untracked sibling file is what refuses the push. The message also calls it "a **tracked** console-tool spawn", which contradicts its untracked status — suggesting the scan does not consult git's index at all.

**Impact**

Any session sharing this checkout is blocked from pushing until an unrelated peer's in-flight file is finished or removed. The documented escape (`FLEET_ALLOW_POPUP=1`) is marked "intentional only" and is wrong here — the pusher neither owns nor intends the popup — so the correct-by-the-book action is to stop, which strands finished, green, witnessed work. AGENTS.md explicitly forbids staging or deleting a peer's uncommitted files, so the blocked session has no compliant remedy.

**Proposal**

Scope the popup scan to content that can actually reach the trunk: the **push range** (`origin/<trunk>..HEAD`) and/or tracked files, not untracked working-tree siblings. An untracked file cannot regress the trunk; gating on it is a false positive by construction. (The peer's `cmd/fak/steer_prs.go:179` should still be suppressed before *it* lands — that is a separate, real fix owned by whoever lands that file.)

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A push whose range contains no unsuppressed spawn is not refused because an untracked peer file has one.
- [ ] A push that *does* carry an unsuppressed spawn is still refused (no weakening of the real gate).
- [ ] The refusal text stops describing an untracked file as "tracked".
- [ ] Regression test covers: untracked sibling with a popup + clean push range => ALLOW.
