records.title: feat(gateway): typed loop-progress observer on the owned loop → structured native SSE events (#2388)
records.body:
Part of #2388 (harness-native program #2387). The **net-new** half of #2403.

## Thesis
The native owned-loop stream (`runNativeArmStream`, `internal/gateway/native_serve.go`)
hand-builds **text-only** Anthropic SSE. Everything the owned loop does between
`message_start` and `message_stop` — turn boundaries, per-call adjudication verdicts,
tool dispatch, result admission/taint — is invisible until the terminal `ArmMetrics`
witness on `message_stop`. An operator or client cannot watch *what the loop is doing*
mid-flight; it can only read the prose and the final counters.

The interrupt/command half of #2403 is already substantially built (the session control
plane — `POST /v1/fak/session/{id}/{verb}` run/budget/pace/priority/wall/throughput
verbs, plus the steer route with `class:"now"` boundary-interrupt semantics and the
`#2758` terminate signal). What is genuinely missing is the **outbound** half: the stream
carrying the loop's *typed state*, not just its prose. This issue ships that spine.

## Distilled inspiration (never copied)
The reference harness's stream carries provenance-tagged loop-state events (each tied to
its originating call), not only text. fak's version additionally carries **kernel
verdicts** — the adjudication reason classes a client can gate on — drawn from the same
closed vocabulary the rest of the kernel refuses with. Every emitted event is a witnessed
fact about a real lifecycle transition, never narration.

## Design
1. **`internal/agent`** — a typed, nil-safe loop-progress observer (a pure additive
   `RunOption`, in the family of `WithSessionGate` / `WithSpeculator`):
   - `ProgressEvent{Kind, Turn, CallID, Tool, Verdict, Reason, Taint}` with a
     `ProgressEventKind` closed set: `turn_started`, `call_adjudicated`, `tool_started`,
     `result_admitted`, `turn_done`.
   - `WithProgressObserver(func(ProgressEvent)) RunOption` sets `runConfig.observer`.
   - `runArm` calls a nil-safe `cfg.emitProgress(...)` at each lifecycle point. When no
     observer is wired the emit is a no-op, so the historical loop stays **byte-for-byte
     unchanged** (the same guarantee every other `RunOption` carries).
2. **`internal/gateway`** — `runNativeArmStream` wires `WithProgressObserver` to emit a
   typed **custom SSE event** per `ProgressEvent` (`send(kind, payload)`), interleaved
   with the existing text deltas, each tagged with the session trace and originating
   call id. The observer runs on the same request goroutine as the text sink (the loop is
   synchronous within `CompleteStream`), so no cross-goroutine send race is introduced.

## Acceptance (witnessable, on-box)
Golden SSE test `TestNativeStreamStructuredEvents` in `internal/gateway`: a multi-turn
`serve --native` stream in which one tool call is **denied** and one is **executed**
emits the full typed event sequence **in order** — `turn_started` →
(`tool_started` → `call_adjudicated{verdict}` → `result_admitted{taint}`)+ → `turn_done`
per turn — interleaved with the text deltas, terminating on `message_stop` carrying the
`fak.native_arm` `ArmMetrics`. Runs under a deterministic mock streaming planner (no model
serving), witnessed via WSL `go test` against the committed tip.

## Out of scope (tracked follow-on)
- The **inbound** command half of #2403 (`TestInterruptLandsAtTurnBoundary`) — the session
  control plane already carries the mechanism; a boundary-lands witness test is a sibling
  follow-on, filed separately.

## Seams
- `internal/agent/loop.go` (runArm lifecycle points), `internal/agent/loop_session.go`
  (`runConfig`, `RunOption`)
- `internal/gateway/native_serve.go` (`runNativeArmStream` SSE synthesis)

## Parent context
Part of #2388 (harness-native program #2387).

## Current state
`runNativeArmStream` emits text-only SSE; loop lifecycle state is invisible until the
terminal ArmMetrics on `message_stop`.

## Why now
This is the outbound half of loop ownership — streaming that carries the loop's state, the
precondition for any client that watches, gates on, or reacts to a running native loop.

## Expected steps
1. Add the typed observer + `WithProgressObserver` `RunOption` in `internal/agent`.
2. Emit at the runArm lifecycle points, nil-safe.
3. Wire the observer to typed SSE events in `runNativeArmStream`.
4. Add and green the golden test `TestNativeStreamStructuredEvents`.

## Batch policy
Single coherent slice, landed once — no spam of per-event commits.

## Done when
`TestNativeStreamStructuredEvents` is green on the committed tip and the native stream
emits the typed event sequence with the historical (unwired) loop byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Work estimate
Estimate: 3 points. Uncertainty: operator-supplied estimate; revise through the parent denominator when evidence changes.

## Overall completion contribution
Contribution: 3/3 points.

## Completion standard
production

## Target operating envelope
tests: >= 1 golden-test

## Witnessed operating envelope
tests: >= 1 golden-test

records.title: fix(nightrun): fleet-outcome-health.jsonl is an orphan ledger — no producer, frozen CRIT
records.body:
## Problem

`docs/nightrun/fleet-outcome-health.jsonl` is a loop-health telemetry ledger with **no producer anywhere in the tree**. It was committed once (`26b055b60` "land new fleet documentation from WIP", 2026-07-09) and has never been regenerated. Its last row is dated **2026-07-08** and still reads `status: CRIT` — so anyone who opens it (or a future consumer that folds it) sees a frozen, months-old CRIT verdict presented as if it were live loop-health.

## Evidence

Exhaustive search finds no writer — only the data file itself and two non-writer mentions:

```
$ grep -rln "fleet-outcome-health" --include=*.go --include=*.py --include=*.sh --include=*.ps1 --include=*.yml .
(no code writer — only docs/nightrun/fleet-outcome-health.jsonl itself)
```

- `internal/sessionaudit/feed.go:10` names "fleet outcome health" as a *sibling signal* in a comment — it does not write the file.
- The cross-ledger loop-health fold `internal/loopfleet/loopfleet.go` (adapter table `:166-173`) reads `collected.jsonl`, `docs/dojo/history.jsonl`, `docs/cadence/history.jsonl`, `.dispatch-runs/progress.jsonl`, `.fak/loops.jsonl` — **not** `fleet-outcome-health.jsonl`. So nothing consumes it either; it is inert frozen data.

Contrast: the observability map `docs/observability/durable-artifacts.md` §3 documents live writers for the other nightrun ledgers, but has no entry that produces this one.

## Why it matters

A committed, frozen `status: CRIT` ledger with no writer is a trap: it looks like a live health signal but reflects 2026-07-08. It either (a) should have a writer and silently lost one (a dead loop), or (b) is dead weight that should be retired. Either way an audit reader can't tell without grepping the whole tree.

## Fix (pick one, whichever matches intent)

- **Retire** it: delete the file (and any stale reference), OR
- **Wire** it: if `fleet-outcome-health` is meant to be a live signal, add the writer + a cadence and register it in `docs/observability/durable-artifacts.md` §3 next to its siblings, and fold it into `internal/loopfleet` like the other loop ledgers.

## Repro

```
grep -rln "fleet-outcome-health" --include=*.go --include=*.py --include=*.sh --include=*.ps1 --include=*.yml .   # -> only the data file
git log -1 --format='%ci %h %s' -- docs/nightrun/fleet-outcome-health.jsonl                                       # -> 2026-07-09, single commit
```

Surfaced by a background-loop audit. No existing issue covers this ledger (searched open+closed for `fleet-outcome-health`, orphan/dead-ledger).

records.title: fix(feeds): bench-feed & backlog-feed dead channel gate — post to CICD channel before the #1005 channel is provisioned
records.body:
## Problem

`bench-feed.yml` and `backlog-feed.yml` document a "dry-run until the operator provisions the channel" contract (backlog-feed calls it "the #1005 blocker"), but a hardcoded fallback in the `env:` block **defeats the channel half of the post gate**. Once `FAK_SCOREBOARD_TOKEN` is set, both feeders POST to the CI/CD report channel `C0BGQ411TCJ` **before** the intended `#bench` / `#backlog` channel exists — contradicting their own headers — and their "posting was skipped" branches become dead code.

## Evidence

### `.github/workflows/backlog-feed.yml`
- `:59` `FAK_BACKLOG_CHANNEL: ${{ vars.FAK_BACKLOG_CHANNEL || vars.FAK_CICD_REPORT_CHANNEL || 'C0BGQ411TCJ' }}` — the literal fallback makes this **always non-empty**.
- `:151` post gate `if: ${{ env.FAK_SCOREBOARD_TOKEN != '' && env.FAK_BACKLOG_CHANNEL != '' && ... }}` — the `FAK_BACKLOG_CHANNEL != ''` term is **always true**, so posting gates on the token alone.
- `:163-166` skip-note `if: ${{ ... || env.FAK_BACKLOG_CHANNEL == '' }}` + `if [ -z "$FAK_BACKLOG_CHANNEL" ]` — **dead code** (never reached).
- Header `:17-28`: "Without either ... the job runs in --dry-run"; "Until both exist the feeder runs dry-run only." Contradicted by the above.

### `.github/workflows/bench-feed.yml`
- `:66` same `|| vars.FAK_CICD_REPORT_CHANNEL || 'C0BGQ411TCJ'` fallback.
- `:104` post gate `env.FAK_BENCH_CHANNEL != ''` — always true.
- `:110`,`:117-118` skip-note channel branch — dead code.
- Header `:20-21`,`:30`: "the bench channel id has NO built-in default, so without it the post has nowhere to go." Contradicted.

### Intent is "default to the CI/CD channel" (so the fix is to reconcile bench/backlog to the family)
The sibling feeds `cachevalue-feed.yml` (`:49`), `capacity-feed.yml`, `dojo-feed.yml`, `node-usage-feed.yml`, `blockers-feed.yml`, `scoreboard-feed.yml` all use the same `|| FAK_CICD_REPORT_CHANNEL || 'C0BGQ411TCJ'` fallback **and their headers/gates match it** (they document the CI/CD default and gate on the token only). bench-feed and backlog-feed are the outliers whose headers + `!= ''` gate term + skip-note branches were never reconciled. `product-feed.yml` (`:70`) has the same fallback with reconciled *logic* but a **stale header** (`:20-25` still says "no built-in default").

## Impact

An operator who reads the bench-/backlog-feed header believes nothing posts until they provision `#bench`/`#backlog`. In reality, as soon as the scoreboard bot token is present, bench rollups and backlog-triage digests post to the shared CI/CD channel `C0BGQ411TCJ`. That's a surprising, undocumented destination for two status streams, and the dead skip-note branches mean the run summary never warns about it.

## Fix

Reconcile bench-feed.yml, backlog-feed.yml (and product-feed.yml's header) to the family default:
- Update the headers to state the CI/CD channel default (matching cachevalue/blockers).
- Drop the always-true `FAK_*_CHANNEL != ''` term from the post gate (gate on the token like the siblings), and remove the now-dead `== ''` / `-z` skip-note branches.

*(Or, if the intent really is "no default for these two," remove the `|| FAK_CICD_REPORT_CHANNEL || 'C0BGQ411TCJ'` fallback so the gate/headers become true again. Given the whole family defaults to CI/CD, reconciling to the default is the lower-surprise fix.)*

Related but distinct: #1005 / #1006 track *provisioning* the missing Slack channels + adding feeders — not this header/gate drift. Surfaced by a background-loop / feed-workflow audit.

records.title: feat(operator): loop-audit signal feed — turn 'fak loop health' DARK/SPINNING read into deduped issues on a cron (score-signal analogue, child of #4954)
records.body:
## Problem

The fleet has a rich **read** of loop-fleet health but **no feed** that turns it into tracked work. `fak loop health --json` folds the loop ledger + registry into a `loopmgr.HealthReport` with a per-loop `dark` verdict, an OS-scheduler reconcile to avoid false-DARK (#4989, `os_fired_no_ledger_row`), and the witness/keep signal for SPINNING (`keep_rate`, `runs`, `witnessed`; the SPINNING-as-debt read is #4956). `fak loop health --check` even exits 3 when any loop is dark.

But that verdict only exists if someone runs the command and reads it. Nothing turns "a rostered loop went DARK (or is up-but-SPINNING)" into a deduped GitHub issue the dispatch loop can pick up. The internal-feeder pattern that does exactly this for other reads is already shipped and proven — `score-signal.yml`/`tools/score_signal.py` (scorecard regression → issue), `bench-signal.yml`, `gate-signal.yml`. There is **no equivalent feeder for the loop fleet's own liveness/progress**:

```
$ ls .github/workflows/ | grep -iE 'loop|roster|operator|health'   # -> (none)
$ ls tools/*loop*audit*.py tools/*loop*health*.py                  # -> (none)
```

So a background loop can go dark and stay dark indefinitely with no ticket — the loop fleet is the one signal source in the repo that watches everything except itself.

## Proposal — `loop-audit-signal`, the score-signal analogue for the loop fleet

A durable, always-on feeder that runs the loop-health read on a cron and files ONE deduped, scoped issue per loop that is DARK (and, once #4956 lands its keep-rate cut, per up-but-SPINNING loop):

- `tools/loop_audit_signal.py` — pure planner over a `fak loop health --json` payload (`--from` for a captured fold). Emits, for each `dark` row (excluding `os_fired_no_ledger_row`, which #4989 already explains), one planned issue. Dedup exactly like score-signal: against the tool's own label only, by a stable per-loop marker `<!-- fak-loop-audit: <loop_id> -->` — at most one OPEN issue per loop, re-fileable after a close. Worst-first `--max-issues` cap bounds a storm. Dry-run by default; `--live` is the explicit opt-in (`gh issue create`). Exit 0 = clean (incl. nothing to signal), 2 = infra error.
- `tools/loop_audit_signal_test.py` — proves the pure plan/dedup core over synthetic `HealthReport` JSON (a filed issue is only meaningful if the planner is proven), run FIRST in CI like `tools/score_signal_test.py`.
- `.github/workflows/loop-audit-signal.yml` — daily, off-the-hour cron clear of the other scheduled jobs; self-test → `fak loop health --json` → plan (always, to step summary + artifact) → file. Start dry-run-on-schedule with a `workflow_dispatch live=true` arm (the blockers-/cadence-feed posture) so the operator can soak one run before flipping to autonomous — same trajectory `score-signal` took to #980.

## Relationship to the operator epic #4954

This is the **FEED rung** of #4954, distinct from its existing children:
- #4955 (canonical roster) and #4956 (verified-progress read) are the *source* — this feeder consumes them (and works today off `fak loop health` before they land).
- #4957 (orphaned-follow-on witness), #4958 (in-process meta-walker under `tend`) are the *in-process walk*.
- This ticket is the *externalizer*: turn the walk's DARK/SPINNING verdict into a tracked, deduped issue — the loop-fleet counterpart of `score-signal.yml`.

It can ship incrementally on today's `fak loop health --json` (DARK only), then subscribe to the richer #4955/#4956 fold as those land.

## Done when

- `python tools/loop_audit_signal.py --from <fold>.json` plans exactly one issue per DARK loop, deduped by the `fak-loop-audit` marker against its own label, capped worst-first; `--live` files them.
- `tools/loop_audit_signal_test.py` proves plan + dedup + cap over synthetic folds and is green in CI.
- `.github/workflows/loop-audit-signal.yml` runs the read on a daily cron, surfaces the plan every run, and files (live-armed) with the storm bounds above.

Surfaced by a background-loop audit; this is the durable mechanism that makes that audit recurring.

records.title: docs(integrations): "embed fak in your product" guide — the app that makes a direct API call, not a coding agent
records.body:
## Problem

Every integration surface fak ships today assumes the caller is a **coding agent / harness
that proposes host tool calls** (Bash/Read/Edit/…). The integration index is literally
titled "Put fak in front of the agent you already run", and all ~13 first-class guides plus
the 47-row compatibility matrix are harnesses, IDEs, or agent frameworks
(`docs/integrations/README.md`). The value narrative is written for that reader: *"every
tool call your agent proposes is adjudicated."*

That leaves a large, common adopter with **no front door**: a product/SaaS feature that
already makes a **direct model API call** and wants fak in front of *that call* — e.g. a
job-application/ATS screener, a support-reply drafter, a résumé field-extractor,
a content classifier. This developer is not running a coding agent; they own their own
loop and call `client.messages.create(...)` / `chat.completions.create(...)` directly.

Two things break for them today, and neither is addressed:

1. **The `guard` vs `serve` category error is never headed off for this persona.** A
   product developer's natural instinct — the one this ticket originates from — is *"can I
   use `fak guard` instead of my API call?"* But `fak guard` is a **child-process
   launcher**: it injects a base URL into a child `claude`/agent process and exits with it
   (`cmd/fak` guard path). A long-lived server product has no child agent to launch. The
   right answer is "keep your API call; put `fak serve` (the gateway runtime) in front of
   it" — but no doc says this to an *application* developer. The runtime-vs-client explainer
   (`docs/explainers/runtime-vs-client.md`) and the planned `fak runtimes` verb (#3257)
   frame the decision around *runtimes*, not around the "I have a product feature that calls
   a model" persona; the adopter playbook's Shape A
   (`docs/integrations/adopter-playbook.md#a--front-a-model`) is the closest, but it too is
   written entirely for "your agent's tool calls," not a product feature.

2. **The default floor allow-lists Claude Code's tools, so an app's own tools default-deny
   and the product breaks.** Verified: `cmd/fak/guard-default-policy.json:4-14` allow-lists
   `Bash`, `Read`, `Edit`, `Write`, `Grep`, plus read-only `allow_prefix` families. A
   product's own tools (`screen_candidate`, `send_offer`, `reject_applicant`) are unknown to
   that floor → fail-closed DENY → the feature stops working the moment fak is in front,
   unless the developer hand-authors a full policy first. And a very common product call has
   **no tools at all** (classify / extract / draft) — for which the current docs never
   explain what the floor/audit/redaction even buys.

## Why this is distinct from epic #3256 (not a duplicate)

Epic #3256 (agent-runtime) productizes the case where **fak owns the agent loop**
server-side — an embeddable runtime (#3260), client SDKs to drive it (#3261), multi-tenant
isolation (#3263), streaming loop events (#3264), gateway governance parity (#3280). That is
"let fak run your agent." This ticket is the **opposite and more common** shape: the product
**keeps its own loop / its own direct call** and just wants the gateway in front. It maps to
the *gateway runtime* row of #3256's own table, but the missing artifact here is a
**persona-shaped front door + worked example**, not the runtime. File as additive to #3256's
Workstream A (disambiguation), which #3257 already touches but from the runtime angle.

## Direction

A new guide `docs/integrations/embed-in-your-product.md` (linked from the integration index
"Which agent do you run?" section with an explicit "I'm not running an agent — I have a
product feature that calls a model" row), covering:

- **The one-paragraph decision** for this persona: you are neither wrapping a CLI (`guard`)
  nor handing fak your loop (`serve --native` / agent runtime) — you **keep your API call**
  and point its base URL at `fak serve`. State the `guard`-is-a-child-launcher fact plainly
  so the category error is closed. (Feed the same intent into #3257's `fak runtimes` tree.)
- **A worked example built around a non-coding-agent product** — a job-application screener
  is the canonical one from this ticket's origin. Show (a) a **tool-less** completion
  (classify/extract) and what fak adds even with zero tools: audit row + `X-Trace-Id`,
  budget accounting, prompt-side PII/secret handling (ref #3280); and (b) an **app-tool**
  call (`screen_candidate`) that the default floor would DENY, and how to author a floor that
  permits the app's own tools — which needs the scaffolding tracked in the sibling ticket
  (`fak policy --from-tools`) to not be a wall of hand-written JSON.
- **The honest fence:** fak is not the token engine; for a plain product completion the win
  is the governance/audit/redaction band, not throughput (mirror the README fence).

## Acceptance

- `docs/integrations/embed-in-your-product.md` exists and is linked from
  `docs/integrations/README.md` with a persona row that is clearly *not* a coding agent.
- The guide explicitly resolves `guard` vs `serve` for a server-side product (no child
  process) and cross-links #3257 / the runtime-vs-client explainer.
- It contains a runnable example for both a tool-less product call and an app-defined-tool
  call, and states the default-floor-denies-your-tools fact
  (`cmd/fak/guard-default-policy.json`) with the fix path.
- Cross-referenced from epic #3256 as the "keep your own call, front it" companion to the
  agent-runtime work.

Provenance: originated from the question "what if a product (e.g. a job application) wants to
route its direct API call through fak instead of calling the model directly?" — a persona the
current integration docs do not serve.



---

## Correction — the enforcement seam (added after grounding guard vs serve internals)

An initial reading of this ticket risks implying a product that keeps its own loop and fronts
it with `fak serve` "loses fak's loop-level enforcement." That is too strong and the guide
must not say it. Grounded in code:

**What `serve` already enforces on your own loop, over the wire (no harness, trace-keyed):**
- Per-turn admission — each `/v1/*` call is the turn boundary; run-state + turn/token budget
  refused *before the model runs* (`internal/gateway/session_admit.go:54`, `cmd/fak/main.go:1246`).
- Hard spend cap — 409 kill that "works on any served path (serve / guard-as-client) … by the
  kernel, never by asking the model" (`session_admit.go:242-247`; #3273, wired to serve by #4859).
- Pace shaping, budget/coherence session resets, operator control + steer at the next
  boundary, and the per-request confirm-token / reversibility gate (`internal/adjudicator/decide.go:629`).

**What genuinely needs process ownership (does NOT transfer to a direct-API product):** the
Stop-hook trio (deny-all auto-continue, task-handoff gate, operator-directed gate), PreCompact,
and supervised restart — they fire on Claude Code lifecycle events the model-API wire does not
carry (`cmd/fak/guard.go:1266`). The guide should key the product's own loop-exit off fak's
**structured refusal reason** instead, and must send a stable `X-Trace-Id` to be
operator-addressable. The wire mechanism to receive guard's give-up/continue disposition
without owning the process is tracked separately in #5161.

**Do not cite cache-break as a working gateway signal.** The per-session cache-break gate is
inert today — no live producer; the #2915 prefix-mutation detector never landed
(`internal/metrics/cache_break.go`). Leave it out of the value narrative until it ships.

records.title: feat(policy): scaffold a starter floor from an application's own tool schemas (`fak policy --from-tools`)
records.body:
## Problem

To get any value from the capability floor, a caller's tools must be on the allow-list.
The default floor is authored for **Claude Code** — verified at
`cmd/fak/guard-default-policy.json:4-14` it allow-lists `Bash`, `Read`, `Edit`, `Write`,
`Grep`, plus read-only `allow_prefix` families. That is exactly right for a coding harness
and exactly wrong for a **product embedding fak in front of its own model call**: an app's
own tools (`screen_candidate`, `send_offer`, `reject_applicant`, `lookup_order`) are not on
that floor, so fail-closed → every one of the app's tool calls is DENIED the moment fak is
in front, until the developer hand-authors a policy.

Today the only documented on-ramp is `fak policy --dump` → hand-edit → `fak policy --check`
(`docs/FAQ.md`, `docs/integrations/adopter-playbook.md#a1`). But `--dump` emits the **Claude
Code** floor — the wrong starting point for an application, whose tools it has never heard
of. The developer must delete the harness tools and hand-transcribe every one of their own
function schemas into `allow` / `deny` / argument rules by hand. There is **no importer**
from an application's own tool catalog to a starter floor — verified: no `--from-tools` (or
any tool-schema→policy scaffolder) exists anywhere in `cmd/` or `internal/`.

This is the concrete blocker that makes the "embed fak in your product" persona
(#5152) a wall of JSON instead of one command.

## Direction

Add `fak policy --from-tools <schema.json>` (thin `cmd/fak` shell over an `internal/`
generator): read a tool/function catalog the developer **already has** — an OpenAI
`tools: [{type:"function", function:{name, parameters}}]` array, or an Anthropic
`tools: [{name, input_schema}]` array (both are what they pass to the model already) — and
emit a **starter `policy.json`**:

- Each app tool listed by exact name (default a conservative stance: read-ish names into
  `allow`, everything else into a commented/`deny`-leaning section the author must promote —
  fail-closed by default, matching the floor's discipline).
- For string-typed argument fields, emit **placeholder `deny_regex` stubs with `TODO`
  reasons** drawn from the closed refusal vocabulary, so the author tightens rather than
  invents structure.
- Deterministic, offline, no model/key/GPU — pure schema→manifest, so it is CI-checkable and
  round-trips through the existing `fak policy --check`.

This gets a product developer from "here are my tools" to "here is a reviewable floor I can
tighten" in one command, instead of hand-writing the manifest from the wrong (Claude Code)
starting point.

## Why this is distinct from epic #3256 (not a duplicate)

#3256's children productize fak **hosting** an agent loop and driving it via an SDK; none of
them import a *client application's own tool catalog* into a policy — that work assumes fak
supplies the tools. This is a policy-authoring ergonomic for the "keep your own call, front
it" persona, upstream of and enabling that guide. It also composes with `fak policy --check`
/ `--dump` that already exist.

## Acceptance

- `fak policy --from-tools tools.json` reads an OpenAI-shaped **and** an Anthropic-shaped
  tool array and writes a starter `policy.json` whose every tool name comes from the input.
- Output passes `fak policy --check` unchanged and is fail-closed by default (unknown/verb-y
  tools are not silently allowed).
- Deterministic and offline; a golden test fixture asserts a known tool schema → known
  manifest.
- Referenced from the "embed fak in your product" guide (#5152) as the step that
  turns the app's tools into a floor.

Provenance: same origin as the "embed fak in your product" persona — a product routing its
direct API call through fak hits the default-floor-denies-my-tools wall immediately, with no
scaffolding to get out of it.



---

## Scope note (added after grounding guard vs serve internals)

`--from-tools` targets the **request-granular adjudication seam** — the capability floor /
per-request confirm-token gate that `fak serve` already enforces over the wire, decoupled from
any process ownership (`internal/adjudicator/decide.go:629`, `internal/gateway/session_admit.go`).
That is exactly the half of fak's enforcement a product embedding via `serve` gets on its own
loop, so this scaffolder is well-aimed. It does **not** by itself confer loop-level
(stop / continue / handoff / restart) enforcement — that is the separate gateway-seam gap
tracked in #5161. The starter floor here is the per-request
layer; that ticket is the turn-boundary layer.

Mean acceptance length >= X at `quality_parity = verified`, where X is taken from the measured external mtp-vs-off scorecard rows. Interim floor 1.5 (drafting must buy >= 50% extra accepted tokens per verify pass) — replace with the measured X once an engine that exposes the acceptance counter is chosen.

- Native DeepSeek-V4 MTP (NextN depth-1) draft head on the pure-fak decode path.

records.title: feat(loop): structured mid-flight session verbs — interrupt / drop-pending-call / set-budget at the turn boundary (#2388)
records.body:
## Summary

Split from the write-half of #2403 (parent epic #2388). The **read half** —
typed loop-progress SSE (`turn_started` → `tool_started` → `call_adjudicated` →
`result_admitted` → `turn_done`) emitted by the owned loop and projected into
structured native SSE — is delivered by **#5148**. This ticket tracks the
**write half**: structured *mid-flight* session verbs that let an operator steer
a running `serve --native` loop, landing their effect at the next **clean turn
boundary** with a tamper-evident journal witness.

Now that the loop's state is legible (the read half), an operator can finally
act on it. Today the native loop is drive-able only at the request boundary
(run-state / budget / pace via the session table); there is no way to reach into
a turn that is already in flight.

## Scope

Three structured verbs, each landing at the next turn boundary (never mid-tool,
never mid-adjudication):

- **`interrupt`** — stop the loop at the next boundary with a closed-token
  witness, distinct from a hard cancel/terminate. Reuses the existing
  terminate seam + `ArmMetrics.StoppedBySession`.
- **`drop-pending-call`** — skip a specific queued tool call by `call_id` before
  it is dispatched. This is the **net-new** piece: the loop has no per-call skip
  consult today. *(design risk — flagged below.)*
- **`set-budget`** — adjust the live token/turn budget the loop reads each turn
  (the session table already carries budget; this is the mid-flight setter).

## Acceptance

`TestInterruptLandsAtTurnBoundary` (and per-verb siblings): an `interrupt`
issued while turn *N* is dispatching tool calls does **not** cut a tool or an
adjudication short — the loop completes turn *N*'s admitted results, then stops
at the boundary carrying the closed witness token; the journal records the verb,
its arrival, and the boundary it landed at. `drop-pending-call` skips exactly the
named `call_id` and nothing else. Byte-for-byte invariant: with no verb issued,
the loop is the historical loop (the same guard the read half honors).

## Reuse targets (verified against the tree)

- **Boundary-drain seam** already lands operator input at the clean turn boundary:
  `internal/agent/loop.go` (after `cfg.gateTurn`, ~L463–505). `interrupt` reuses
  the terminate seam + the `ArmMetrics.StoppedBySession` closed token.
- **Closed op/witness vocabulary already declared** in
  `internal/sessionctl/vocab.go`: `OpPause/OpResume/OpCancel/OpTerminate/OpBudget`,
  `OpSpec`, and `WitnessBoundaryStop`/`WitnessSafePointStop`. A new interrupt verb
  registers an `OpSpec{Witness: WitnessBoundaryStop}` — no new vocabulary invented.
- **Durable write-through** for a persisted verb: `applySessionControlDurable` →
  `mirror.writeThrough` (`cmd/fak/session_durable.go`).
- **Observer seam (read half, #5148)** gives the write half its acceptance
  witness: an `interrupt` should surface as a `turn_done`-then-stop in the same
  structured SSE stream, so the operator sees their verb take effect.

## Design risk

`drop-pending-call` is the only piece with no existing seam: the loop must
consult a per-`call_id` skip set *before* dispatching each queued `tc` in the
tool-call loop. Needs a small, nil-safe skip-consult (same additive-RunOption
shape as `WithProgressObserver`) so the historical loop is unchanged when unused.

---
Part of #2388 · write half of #2403 · sibling of read-half #5148

records.body:

<!-- fak-guard-complaint-key: guard-complaint/over-broad/require-witness/bash/require-witness-preview-confirm-fires-on-plain-single-file-r -->
# Guard complaint (agent appeal)

An agent governed by `fak guard` judged a guard decision wrong and filed this appeal. This is the **subjective** channel: a false-positive refusal is byte-identical to a correct one in the decision journal, so `fak guard-verdict-rsi` cannot surface it — only the agent that made the call knows it was legitimate.

- kind: `over-broad` — a gate that refuses more than its stated danger class — collateral denials
- appealed reason: `REQUIRE_WITNESS`
- refused tool: `Bash`
- occurrences: `1`
- stable key: `guard-complaint/over-broad/require-witness/bash/require-witness-preview-confirm-fires-on-plain-single-file-r`

## Why the agent thinks the guard is wrong

The irreversible-delete confirm gate fired on 'rm internal/agent/zz_tmp_compile_shim_DELETE.go' — a plain single-file rm, no -r, no -f, no glob, targeting an UNTRACKED file this same session had just created seconds earlier. Blast radius is one recreatable scratch file; there is nothing to witness. The recursive/forced case is already caught separately by the POLICY_BLOCK rung (rm -rf/-f), so escalating a bare single-file rm to a confirm-token round-trip is over-broad: it taxes the safe common case (deleting a just-created temp file) with the ceremony meant for irreversible bulk deletes. Recovery wanted: admit a plain 'rm <single-path>' of an untracked or session-created file without a confirm token, or scope the REQUIRE_WITNESS confirm to recursive/forced/glob deletes only.

## Evidence

_No journal verdict attached — this appeal rests on the agent's rationale alone. Re-file with `--from-journal` after the refusal to attach the witnessed verdict._

---
Filed by `fak complain`. Re-running it for the same class updates THIS issue in place and bumps the occurrence count rather than opening a duplicate. A confirmed false positive is a floor bug to fix; a rejected appeal is closed with the reason the refusal was correct.

# Guard complaint (agent appeal)

An agent governed by `fak guard` judged a guard decision wrong and filed this appeal. This is the **subjective** channel: a false-positive refusal is byte-identical to a correct one in the decision journal, so `fak guard-verdict-rsi` cannot surface it — only the agent that made the call knows it was legitimate.

- kind: `over-broad` — a gate that refuses more than its stated danger class — collateral denials
- appealed reason: `POLICY_BLOCK`
- refused tool: `Bash`
- occurrences: `1`
- stable key: `guard-complaint/over-broad/policy-block/bash/recursive-rm-rf-on-a-session-authored-untracked-scratch-dir`

## Why the agent thinks the guard is wrong

The recursive-delete hard block is correct as a default and should stay. It over-fired on 'rm -rf tmp_seorun' — a directory I created this session, untracked by git, holding only a throwaway Go scoring harness (bounded blast radius, no tracked/durable content). Recovery via 'mv' to the scratchpad worked, so the block cost a command rewrite, not data. Request: soften recursive deletes confined to session scratch/tmp paths (e.g. the harness scratchpad) to a confirm-gate rather than an operator-only hard block; keep POLICY_BLOCK for recursive/glob/multi-path deletes on tracked or out-of-scratch trees. Adjacent to #4983 (rm -f single-file) but distinct: this is the recursive case, scoped to session scratch. Witness: harness-hook POLICY_BLOCK is not written to guard-audit.jsonl, so this files rationale-only (args-digest sha256:b0fd20fed4…).

## Evidence

_No journal verdict attached — this appeal rests on the agent's rationale alone. Re-file with `--from-journal` after the refusal to attach the witnessed verdict._

---
Filed by `fak complain`. Re-running it for the same class updates THIS issue in place and bumps the occurrence count rather than opening a duplicate. A confirmed false positive is a floor bug to fix; a rejected appeal is closed with the reason the refusal was correct.

records.title: feat(serve): loop-boundary enforcement over the gateway wire — return the give-up/continue disposition to a product driving its own loop
records.body:
## Problem

`fak guard` and `fak serve` both govern an agent, but they draw the enforcement boundary in
different places, and one class of enforcement is welded to `guard` owning the child process
in a way that a product driving its **own** loop cannot get today.

Grounding (verified in code):

- **`serve` enforces at the request-arrival boundary.** Each proxied `/v1/*` call is treated
  as the turn boundary: `beginServedSessionTurn` → `decideSession` debits `TurnsLeft` and
  refuses paused/draining/stopped/budget-exhausted turns *before the model runs*
  (`internal/gateway/session_admit.go:54`, `cmd/fak/main.go:1246`). The control-plane spend
  cap is a hard 409 kill that explicitly "works on any served path (serve / guard-as-client)
  … by the kernel, never by asking the model" (`session_admit.go:242-247`; #3273 shipped,
  #4859 wired into serve). Pace shaping, budget/coherence session resets, operator
  control/steer, and the per-request confirm-token / reversibility gate
  (`internal/adjudicator/decide.go:629`) are all already delivered over the wire, trace-keyed,
  with no harness. So a product that points its own `client.messages.create` loop at
  `fak serve` already inherits substantial turn/session-level enforcement.

- **`guard` additionally enforces at boundaries the model-API wire does not carry.** The
  Stop-hook trio — deny-all auto-continue, task-handoff gate, operator-directed gate — plus
  PreCompact fire on Claude Code lifecycle events (`Stop` / `PreCompact` / `SessionStart`),
  installed into the child's merged `--settings` (`cmd/fak/guard.go:1266`,
  `cmd/fak/guard_stophook.go:22`, `cmd/fak/guard_stops.go:53`). These require guard to **own
  the process** — the gateway cannot observe "the agent decided to end its turn" (the absence
  of a next request) or "the harness is compacting," so it cannot actuate them over the wire.

The load-bearing detail: the **state** the give-up needs already lives gateway-side. The
deny-all-consecutive counter is computed inside the gateway on any served wire
(`internal/gateway/metrics_observe.go:586-597`); only its **actuation** (exit 2 + child
`--settings`) is harness-welded. A product driving its own loop against `serve` therefore has
no way to (a) read back "fak has refused your last N proposals identically — stop trying," nor
(b) signal "my agent just ended its turn / asked a human / hit a handoff point" and receive a
structured `continue` / `standdown` / `handoff-required` verdict.

## Direction

Expose the loop-boundary enforcement on the served wire, so a caller's own loop can consume
the same disposition guard's Stop hook consumes out-of-band — **without** guard owning the
process:

- On the served **response path**, surface the already-computed give-up signal (the
  deny-all-consecutive / structured refusal reason) so a direct-API product can key its own
  loop-exit off it in-band, instead of looping forever against a floor that keeps refusing.
- Add an explicit **turn-end / stop / handoff marker** a product can POST for its trace (or an
  `end_turn`/idle annotation on the response path), and return a structured disposition drawn
  from the existing closed `guardStopDisposition` vocabulary
  (`cmd/fak/guard_stops.go:53-90` — clean / continue / standdown / failopen / shadow / off).
- Ride the addressable-session plumbing already shipped for fak's own sessions —
  `GET /v1/fak/session/{trace_id}/subscribe` (#2767, shipped) and the SSE/long-poll attach
  (#4310) — rather than inventing a new transport. Requires the product to send a stable
  `X-Trace-Id` to be addressable.
- Scope to the **enforcement seam** only. Supervised restart / process relaunch
  (`guard_child.go:924`) stays out — that genuinely needs process ownership and can be a
  follow-on or remain guard-only.

## Why this is distinct (not a duplicate)

- **Not #3256.** The agent-runtime epic names only two ends of the seam: guard-as-client that
  **wraps a child process** (`docs/explainers/runtime-vs-client.md:52,88`) and
  fak-as-agent-runtime that **owns the loop** (#3258 spine, #3260 embed — POST a goal, fak
  drives `agent.RunArm`). The third model — the product keeps its **own** loop and fak
  enforces the loop-boundary gates over the wire — is never named. #3256's guard row
  ("framed as local-dev client only; it should also run server-side") states the gap but
  leaves the mechanism unresolved and reads as still child-wrapping.
- **Not #2847/#2915** (cache-break) — that pushed *one* gate onto the wire, is scoped to
  prefix-mutation, is **inert today** (no live producer; the #2915 detector never landed —
  `internal/metrics/cache_break.go`), and lives under the #2834 track.
- **Not #4859** — that wired the *spend* governor into serve (a session kill on budget); this
  is the stop/give-up/handoff disposition, a different slice.
- **Not #5152/#5153** — those are a persona doc and a per-request policy scaffolder; this is a
  code seam on the gateway, a different layer.

## Acceptance

- A product driving its own loop against `fak serve` (stable `X-Trace-Id`, no child process)
  can read back a structured give-up / continue / handoff disposition from the existing
  `guardStopDisposition` vocabulary, over the wire.
- The signal is sourced from the gateway-side counter that already exists
  (`metrics_observe.go`), not a new harness dependency.
- Restart/process supervision is explicitly out of scope (documented as guard-only or a
  follow-on).
- Cross-referenced from #5152 as the mechanism behind its "what needs process ownership" row.

Provenance: surfaced by asking, conceptually, what coupling is built into `fak guard`
relative to `fak serve` — the residual weld after grounding is exactly this loop-boundary
give-up/continue disposition, which the gateway already has the state for but does not expose.

records.title: docs(explainers): make the guard/serve enforcement boundary a repo artifact (request-arrival vs turn-end) — extend runtime-vs-client.md
records.body:
## Problem

The guard-vs-serve **enforcement boundary** keeps getting re-derived from source (most
recently while framing #5152/#5153/#5161), because it lives nowhere durable in the repo. The
one doc that should carry it — `docs/explainers/runtime-vs-client.md` — names the three
*loop-ownership* roles (gateway runtime / agent-application runtime / client) but is **silent
on where enforcement actually lands**. As a result the single most load-bearing question for
an adopter who keeps their own loop — *"what does fak enforce on MY loop, and what do I lose by
not letting it own my process?"* — has no canonical answer, and every agent/human re-reads
`internal/gateway/session_admit.go` + `cmd/fak/guard*.go` to reconstruct it.

Concretely, the doc frames "your own backend" as a pure model-traffic client:
- Row 3 (`runtime-vs-client.md:52`): *"the harness or app that calls a runtime … or repoint one base URL yourself."*
- "Which do I run?" (`runtime-vs-client.md:97`): *"I have my own backend/SDK and want to **govern its model calls** → `fak serve` + repoint the base URL."*

Neither says what that client actually *gets* at enforcement time, nor that one class of guard
enforcement does not transfer without process ownership. That gap is the thing worth making
structural.

## The map to capture (grounded)

**serve enforces at the request-ARRIVAL boundary — over the wire, trace-keyed, no harness:**
per-turn admission (run-state + turn/token budget, refused before the model runs —
`internal/gateway/session_admit.go:54`, `cmd/fak/main.go:1246`); hard spend cap 409 that
"works on any served path (serve / guard-as-client) … by the kernel, never by asking the
model" (`session_admit.go:242-247`; #3273, wired into serve by #4859); pace shaping;
budget/coherence session resets; operator control + steer at the next boundary; the
per-request confirm-token / reversibility gate (`internal/adjudicator/decide.go:629`).

**guard additionally enforces at boundaries the model-API wire does not carry:** the Stop-hook
trio (deny-all auto-continue, task-handoff gate, operator-directed gate), PreCompact, and the
supervised restart loop — installed into the child's merged `--settings` and fired on Claude
Code lifecycle events (`cmd/fak/guard.go:1266`). These require guard to **own the process**.

**The one-line spine:** the axis that actually matters is **request-arrival vs turn-end**. The
gateway can refuse/throttle/reset/charge/kill anything that *arrives*; it cannot compel a
request the caller's loop decided not to send. The only residual weld to process ownership is
the automatic **give-up/continue** — and its counter already lives gateway-side
(`internal/gateway/metrics_observe.go:586-597`); only the actuation is harness-bound
(this is exactly the seam #5161 proposes to expose).

**Caveat that must ship with it:** the per-session cache-break gate is **inert today** — no
live producer; the #2915 prefix-mutation detector never landed
(`internal/metrics/cache_break.go`). Do not present it as a working gateway signal.

## Direction

Add the enforcement-boundary map to the repo as a reviewable artifact, in the indexed
explainer spine:

- **Primary (recommended):** extend `docs/explainers/runtime-vs-client.md` with an
  **"Enforcement boundary — what a client gets on its own loop"** section: a small table with
  columns *enforcement · request-arrival (serve, over the wire) · turn-end (needs process
  ownership)*, plus the request-arrival-vs-turn-end one-liner and the cache-break caveat.
  Slot it after "Honest scope" (`runtime-vs-client.md:122`), since it is a completion of that
  doc's own thesis, not a new topic.
- **Alternative:** if the section outgrows the page, land a sibling explainer
  `docs/explainers/enforcement-boundary.md` and cross-link both ways. Prefer extending the
  existing doc first to avoid spine fragmentation.
- **Register it** in the docs index so it is discoverable rather than tribal: keep
  `fak index freshness` clean (no dead INDEX.md / llms.txt links), same as any explainer.

## "And similar" — the reusable shape

The **enforcement-boundary table** (per-mechanism: which boundary it fires on, whether it
needs process ownership) is the reusable structure for future seam findings, not a one-off.
It gives these architecture maps a durable in-repo home instead of agent-local memory, which
is where this one currently sits. Adopt the pattern: when a fan-out establishes a
cross-component enforcement/authority seam, the finding lands as (or extends) an explainer with
this table shape, and the driving tickets cite it.

## Acceptance

- `runtime-vs-client.md` (or the sibling explainer) carries the enforcement-boundary section
  with the request-arrival-vs-turn-end table and the cache-break-inert caveat.
- The doc is registered/indexed (`fak index freshness` clean; surfaces via `fak index docs`).
- #5152 (persona guide) and #5161 (loop-boundary seam) link to it as the canonical rationale,
  replacing the ad-hoc explanations currently duplicated in their bodies.
- No claim in the section outruns the code (each row anchored to a file:line, as above).

Provenance: the map was derived by a grounded fan-out over guard/adjudicator/gateway and
currently lives only in agent memory; this ticket makes it a first-class repo artifact.
Related: #5152, #5153, #5161; epic #3256 (names the loop-ownership roles this section
completes with the enforcement axis).

records.title: feat(gateway): durable CAS for dropped media (image) restore bytes, not RAM-only
records.body:
The `fak_context_restore` stash (`internal/gateway/ctxrestore.go`) holds a dropped turn's verbatim bytes in an **in-memory** per-Server map (`s.ctxRestore`, `restoreEntry.bytes`). For a media (image) turn this is the only copy of the image, and it is:

- **non-durable** — lost on gateway process restart, so a resumed session's `fak_context_restore(id)` handle returns `ErrRestoreMiss`.
- **capacity-bounded** — `maxCtxRestoreEntriesPerSession = 8` (`ctxrestore.go:46`); the 9th dropped turn evicts the oldest → `ErrRestoreEvicted`. On an image-heavy session, early images become un-restorable well before the session ends.

Text context has an out-of-band recovery story (the excerpt is orientation, and text is often re-derivable); a pasted image has **no** other copy — once evicted or lost across a restart it is gone.

**Proposal:** back media restore bytes with the durable recall CAS (`recall.PersistIndex` / cas.json neighborhood) keyed by the same sha256 digest, so an image handle survives restart and eviction. `ctxplan` already persists only a `Digest` (`image.go:27`), so the durable byte store is the missing half.

Context: surfaced during the image-compaction audit that shipped the flat image token cost and the media restore-handle (`ced954bca`, `f992aa051`).

records.title: perf(gateway): don't hold full base64 image bytes verbatim in the restore stash
feat(agent): geometry-aware image token cost instead of the flat imageTokenCost constant
records.body:
`imageTokenCost = 1600` (`internal/agent/anthropic_token_estimate.go`) is a deliberately conservative **flat ceiling** — it stops the two-orders-of-magnitude estimator error in both directions (base64-byte over-count in the compaction path, `[image]`≈2 under-count in `count_tokens`), but a small thumbnail and a full-page screenshot are charged identically.

Anthropic's real per-image cost is ~`(w*h)/750` capped ~1600. When the image `source` carries dimensions (or they are cheaply derivable from the base64/PNG header) price the image by geometry for a tighter budget estimate.

Strictly a **precision follow-up** to the shipped flat-cost fix (`f992aa051`); the flat cost is correct and safe as the floor.

records.title: fix(agent): count_tokens double-counts the [image] placeholder on top of imageTokenCost
records.body:
`EstimateAnthropicTokens` (`internal/agent/anthropic_server.go`) now adds `imageTokenCost` per image **and** still counts the decoded `"[image]"` placeholder (~2 tokens) in the text `len(m.Content)` sum. That is a ~2-token double-count per image — negligible, filed for completeness.

**Fix:** subtract the placeholder length, or skip image placeholders in the text walk. Follow-up to `f992aa051`.

records.title: feat(ctxplan): first-class media span descriptors (signal/noise, durability) for images
records.body:
A `ctxplan.Span` carries a content-address `Digest`, not content (`internal/ctxplan/image.go:27`), and the signal/noise + durability classification (`signalnoise.go`, `layout.go`) is token/role-based — built for text. An image span has no descriptor tokens, so it cannot be scored, aged, or durability-classed like text: the planner is effectively **blind to media**.

**Proposal:** give media spans a first-class descriptor (media type, size class, alt-text/caption if present) so image context participates in the same recency/durability layout instead of being opaque. Larger design item; parent of the durable-media-CAS work.

Note: `internal/ctxplan/image.go` is confusingly named — there "image" means a persisted *index snapshot*, not a picture. This issue is about actual media assets; a rename might be worth considering.

records.title: feat(provenance): trace-scoped post-execution write receipts for safe self-disposal
records.body:
## Problem

Guard complaint #4999 can safely bypass preview-confirm for a plain single-path `rm` only when two independent facts hold: the path is git-untracked and the current guard session/trace authored it. The adjudicator currently remembers some script-shaped paths process-globally, but that table is not a trustworthy general write receipt: it is not trace-scoped, does not cover arbitrary files, and has no execution-success readback. Treating "untracked" alone as ownership would let one session delete peer WIP on the shared trunk.

## In scope

- Add a bounded, session/trace-scoped ledger of successfully executed local write effects: canonical path, trace/session identity, operation id, and observed completion.
- Populate it from the post-tool execution/result seam, not from command intent alone.
- Expose a read-only query that proves `path P was authored by trace T and remains eligible for self-disposal`.
- Expire entries at the run boundary and cap storage so this does not worsen #3482.
- Fail closed on absent/ambiguous trace, failed execution, path aliasing, ignored/external targets, or ledger eviction.

## Out of scope

- Relaxing deletion policy. #4999 consumes this witness once shipped.
- Inferring ownership from git-untracked status, a held lane lease, or the model's narration.

## Done condition

A real write tool call creates an independently read-back receipt only after successful execution; another trace cannot claim it; failed writes create no receipt; canonical-path aliases cannot cross ownership; reset/eviction removes eligibility.

## Witness

A table-driven integration test through the tool execution/result boundary covering same-trace success, cross-trace denial, failed write, alias normalization, run reset, and bounded eviction.

## Dependencies

- Unblocks #4999.
- Coordinate with #3482 so the authored-path state has one bounded lifecycle rather than a second leaking map.

## Lane

adjudicator / gateway execution receipts

## Work unit

leaf

## Closure binding

Close via one commit carrying `Closes #<this>` in the body and a captured integration witness.

records.title: epic: Policy Amendment Classes — explicit who-may-amend-what model for the guard floor
records.body:
## Epic: Policy Amendment Classes — an explicit "who-may-amend-what" model for the guard floor

**Track label:** `policy-amendment` · **Class:** class:dev (kernel/guard) · **Kind:** epic (decompose, don't dispatch)

### Problem

`fak guard` already enforces a rich, per-knob mutability discipline — but it is **implicit**: encoded in scattered doc comments (`decide.go`, `guard_allow.go`, `policy_reload_widen.go`) and enforced by scattered clamps (`sanitizeProfile`, `sanitizeAdvisoryReasons`, `AdvisoryEligible`, `mustRun`, `diffPolicyWidening`, `protectGuardPolicyConfig`). There is no single model that answers, for any policy knob: **who may change it, in which direction, and through which channel.** That makes it hard to (a) reason about what an autonomous run can and cannot loosen, (b) safely add new flexibility on the axes we *want* to be flexible, and (c) prove the core protections stay frozen.

The user ask that motivates this epic: *classify policy so we know which parts can be (1) self-modified by the agent, (2) online-modified by an external process, (3) the current heaviest/immutable setup — so the floor is flexible where it should be, yet the core protections never move.*

### The model — amendment classes (NOT a linear clearance)

This is deliberately **not** an ordered "rung/tier/level" (those words are already taken: adjudicator sub-`rung`s = evaluation order; architest/dispatch `tier`s; risk/lock/reversibility `class`es; repo-guard severity `level`s). And per `docs/notes/EXPLAINER-least-privilege-across-fak-2026-07-02.md`, *least privilege wants capability checks, not level comparisons.* So a knob's amendment class is a **capability = (direction it may move) × (set of channels authorized to move it)**, aligned with the lock-class ladder in `docs/notes/CONCEPT-CORE-SOFT-LOCKS-2026-06-30.md`.

**Four amendment classes:**

- **FROZEN (core).** Compiled-in floor; **no channel may weaken it**, and it is self-protected (the policy + overlay files are injected into `SelfModifyGlobs` by `protectGuardPolicyConfig`, so the wrapped agent cannot edit its own guard config). Members: the hardwired cloud-metadata SSRF egress floor (`egressfloor`, `mustRun` for every class), the reversibility preview-confirm gate (#2156), the structural genuine-danger arg-rules (rm -rf / RCE-pipe / out-of-tree-write / shell-dialect / fork-bomb), the write-class self-modify rungs (`rungSelfModify/CmdSelfModify/SynthTool/LintWrite`, `mustRun` on `classWrite`), the `AdvisoryEligible` clamp (POLICY_BLOCK / SECRET_EXFIL / EGRESS_BLOCK can never soften), and the gitgate hazard table.
- **RATCHET (tighten-only).** Any channel may *strengthen*; none may *weaken*. Members: `EgressExtraDenyHosts`, `EgressBlockHosts`/`EgressBlockLists`, `SecretPatterns` (unioned, extend-never-replace), `ArgPredicates` (restrict-only), added `SelfModifyGlobs`, the `fak guard deny` overlay.
- **GATED-WIDEN (out-of-band only).** May loosen the *convenience* surface — but only via a channel the wrapped agent cannot reach, and every widening is journaled (and, proposed here, optionally TTL'd). Members: the `fak guard allow` overlay (Allow/AllowPrefix), `POST /v1/fak/policy/reload` under `FAK_POLICY_RELOAD_ALLOW_WIDEN`, `Complain`, `AdvisoryReasons` (clamped to heuristic reasons), `Posture` fail_closed→admit_and_log, the read-class `RungProfile`, `AutoRepairSidestep`, `FAK_ADVISORY_REASONS`.
- **SELF-AMENDABLE (frontier — empty today).** What the agent may amend about its *own* policy. Today: **nothing** — self-modification is refused by design ("an agent can never grant itself a capability"). This epic opens a provably-safe envelope: **monotone-tighten only** (a self-write admitted only when `diffPolicyWidening` is empty) and/or **propose-only** (the agent queues a widening request that an out-of-band operator ratifies).

**Five amendment channels** (the "how"):
1. compiled-in / shipped (`guard-default-policy.json` embed, `DefaultPolicy`/`DevAgentPolicy`) — the current, heaviest baseline;
2. on-disk operator overlay (`.fak/guard/allow.json`, `.fak/guard/deny.json`, env→user→repo layering; `--policy`) — out-of-band;
3. live gateway reload (`POST /v1/fak/policy/reload`) — gated + journaled (`AppendConfigSwap`);
4. operator escalation (Slack operator-question / `OPERATOR_GATE`) — the human residue of a held decision;
5. agent-self — closed today (the frontier).

### The three questions, answered by the cross-product

| Question | Amendment class | Channel(s) |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Self-modifiable?** | SELF-AMENDABLE (empty today; frontier) | 5 (agent-self) — via monotone-tighten or propose-only |
| **2. Online-modifiable by an external process?** | RATCHET + GATED-WIDEN | 2 (overlay), 3 (reload), 4 (operator) |
| **3. Current setup / heaviest / immutable?** | FROZEN + shipped `DevAgentPolicy` | 1 (compiled-in) |

### Invariants this epic must preserve

- No channel weakens a FROZEN knob (enforced by a red-team amendment matrix).
- A RATCHET knob only ever tightens; a GATED-WIDEN loosening is never reachable by the wrapped agent and is always journaled.
- Every new knob must declare its amendment class (a reflection conformance test fails the build otherwise) — so the model can't silently rot back into scattered comments.

### Children (tracks A–F)

- **A. Make the model explicit:** PolicyKnob classification registry + conformance test; `fak guard policy explain`; `fak guard policy diff` (drift-from-heaviest).
- **B. Harden FROZEN:** red-team amendment matrix test; `fak guard --core-lock-all` maximal-strictness launch.
- **C. Complete RATCHET:** extend the deny overlay to carry arg_rules/secret_patterns/block_hosts; reload delta auto-applies the tighten direction, gates only widen.
- **D. GATED-WIDEN safety rails:** journaled capability-grant provenance; TTL / expiring operator widenings; explicit per-scope precedence in `policy explain`.
- **E. SELF-AMENDABLE frontier:** design spike for the monotone-tighten envelope; `.fak/guard/self-tighten.json` tighten-only self-write; propose-only → `fak guard allow --from-proposals` ratification loop.
- **F. Docs/observability:** committed concept note (`docs/notes/CONCEPT-POLICY-AMENDMENT-CLASSES`); per-session amendment-posture in the guard exit summary.

Anchor files: `internal/adjudicator/decide.go` (Policy struct + rung sequence), `internal/adjudicator/rungprofile.go` (`mustRun`/`sanitizeProfile`), `internal/policy/policy.go` (manifest schema), `cmd/fak/guard_startup.go` (floor assembly + precedence), `cmd/fak/policy_reload_widen.go` (widening gate), `cmd/fak/guard_allow.go` / `guard_deny.go` (overlays).

records.title: feat(policy): add a PolicyKnob amendment-class registry + reflection conformance test
records.body:
## Parent context
Epic #5170 — Policy Amendment Classes. Track A (make the model explicit).

## Problem
The guard floor's per-knob mutability discipline is enforced by scattered clamps (`sanitizeProfile`, `sanitizeAdvisoryReasons`, `AdvisoryEligible`, `mustRun`, `diffPolicyWidening`, `protectGuardPolicyConfig`) and documented only in doc comments. There is no single, machine-checked source of truth stating, for each `adjudicator.Policy` field, its **amendment class** (FROZEN / RATCHET / GATED-WIDEN / SELF-AMENDABLE) and the channels authorized to change it. A new knob can be added without declaring how it may be amended — silently re-scattering the discipline.

## In scope
- Add a `PolicyKnob` classification table (suggested home `internal/policy/amendment.go`) mapping every `adjudicator.Policy` field → {AmendmentClass, Direction, authorized channels}.
- A conformance test that reflects over `adjudicator.Policy` fields and FAILS if any is absent from the table (adding a knob forces classifying it).
- Cross-check invariants: FROZEN knobs declare no widening channel; RATCHET knobs declare tighten-only.

## Out of scope
- Any behavior change to `decide.go`. Classification + test only.
- The `policy explain`/`diff` verbs (separate children).

## Done condition

records.title: research: design the monotone-tighten self-amendment envelope
records.body:
## Parent context
Epic #5170 — Policy Amendment Classes. Track E (SELF-AMENDABLE frontier). Research/design spike.

## Problem
The SELF-AMENDABLE class is empty by design: the agent can never grant itself a capability, and its guard config is protected by `SelfModifyGlobs` + `protectGuardPolicyConfig`. The first-cut plan was "self-tighten is safe, self-widen is dangerous — allow only monotone-tighten." **That framing is wrong and this spike must correct it.** Safety is NOT monotone in restriction:

- **Over-restriction relocates capability out of view.** A denied structured tool doesn't stop an autonomous agent — it routes around (via `Bash`, a helper script, an encoded arg). The repo already decides the RCE-pipe rule structurally because a regex "misses a one-character launder," and force-admits `ToolSearch` because denying it "bricks the wrapped agent." A denial you can't enforce is worse than an allow you can observe.
- **Refusing to act has consequences too.** A blocked commit loses work; a blocked idempotent read stalls a run; a stall under autonomy becomes a doom-loop or a half-applied migration frozen mid-flight.
- **Tighten-only self-DoSes.** An agent that can only narrow can deny its own required tools and then be unable to recover (un-denying is a "widen"), hanging instead of safe-stopping.

## The corrected model this spike must specify
Danger lives in the **FROZEN core** (egress SSRF floor, structural danger arg-rules, self-modify-core globs, reversibility gate), which adjudicates EFFECTS downstream regardless of the convenience surface. So permissiveness on the convenience surface (which tools are allowed) provably cannot reach genuine danger — the core still catches it. That yields a precise, checkable safety envelope: the **shipped baseline (`DevAgentPolicy`) is vetted-safe by construction.** "Widen" therefore splits into two very different operations:

1. **widen-to-baseline (RESTORE):** the proposed floor is still ⊆ the shipped floor — checkable as `diffPolicyWidening(shipped, proposed).Empty()`. Adds nothing the shipped policy didn't already deem safe. Should be **self-amendable and permissive, no ratification** (this is the anti-stall / anti-wedge direction). New child — see the restore ticket.
2. **widen-beyond-baseline (GRANT):** a genuinely new capability the shipped floor never granted. The ONLY case that needs the out-of-band operator (child E3).

And self-tighten (child E2) is allowed but NOT unconditionally: it needs an **anti-wedge floor** — a minimal operating set (Read, ToolSearch, the un-tighten path) it may never narrow below, mirroring the default floor's forced `ToolSearch` admit.

## In scope (design only)
- Specify the three sub-operations (restore / self-tighten-with-anti-wedge / grant-beyond-baseline) and their exact proof obligations, all expressed against `diffPolicyWidening` and the shipped `DevAgentPolicy` snapshot.
- Define the anti-wedge minimal operating set and the un-tighten guarantee.
- State the governing principle — prefer observed, reversible, baseline-bounded permission over blind denial — and reconcile it with the existing `PostureAdmitAndLog` / `Complain` (observed-permission-for-reads) posture.
- Threat model: what a permissive restore CANNOT reach (the FROZEN core), blast-radius/reversibility of session-scoped grants, and the self-wedge hazard of tighten.

## Out of scope
- Implementation (children: restore ticket, E2 self-tighten, E3 grant-beyond-baseline).

## Done condition
A design note enumerating the three sub-operations, their `diffPolicyWidening`-based proofs, the anti-wedge set, the observed-permission principle, and the threat model — reviewed and marked ready-to-implement, with the child acceptance criteria derived from it.

## Witness
The design is captured and linked from epic #5170; the restore / E2 / E3 acceptance criteria cite it.

## Lane
