records.title: fix(agent): responsesPromptCacheKey folds mid-conversation system/developer turns into the codex prompt_cache_key — key churns instead of pinning the head
records.body:
## Problem

`responsesPromptCacheKey` (`internal/agent/adapters.go:578-602`) is documented (adapters.go:558-566, 583-585) as deriving the key from the *cacheable instruction head* so it stays constant turn-to-turn and shareable across sessions with the same harness prefix. The implementation hashes **every** `RoleSystem` message at **any** position — the loop `continue`s on non-system but has no head anchor and no `break`:

```go
for _, m := range messages {
    if m.Role != RoleSystem { continue }   // adapters.go:586
    _, _ = h.Write([]byte(m.Content))       // adapters.go:589
    _, _ = h.Write([]byte{0})
}
```

For the common case (all system/developer content leads the array) this equals hashing the head. It silently diverges the moment a `RoleSystem` message appears **after** a user turn — which is reachable:

- **Public wire.** `POST /v1/responses` walks the input array in order (`internal/gateway/responses.go:416`) and `responsesRole` folds `developer` → `RoleSystem` (responses.go:512). A `developer`/`system` item placed after the first user turn — a standard mid-conversation steering pattern — becomes a mid-conversation `RoleSystem` message that flows through `completeServed` → `openAIResponsesAdapter` (responses.go:291) into the key.
- **fak-internal.** On a budget/coherence reset, `spliceSeed` inserts a `RoleSystem` carryover seed **after** the leading system block (`internal/gateway/session_admit.go:199-211`; carryover content per `session_admit_test.go`), injecting per-reset-dynamic bytes into the key.
- **Composition hazard (latent).** `GLMCoherenceShaper.ApplyBreakToMessages` actuates a break by inserting a synthetic `Message{Role:"system"}` whose content is per-turn-**volatile** (`internal/agent/glm_coherence.go:97`; marker content rebuilt per turn from refuted world keys, `internal/cachemeta/prefix_coherence.go:128-143`). The shaper runs in `prepareUpstream` (`internal/agent/stream.go:372-373`) **before** `MarshalRequest`, so if a `CoherenceShaper` is ever installed on a Responses planner (its doc says the live wiring is "ONE line in the loop"), the volatile marker re-keys the request on every break — collapsing the exact warmth the key exists to pin. No live code installs a shaper today, so this arm is latent.

Effect (all silent — a miss only costs latency, never errors): a mid-session steering note flips the key from that turn on; two sessions sharing the fixed head but differing in a mid-conversation note never co-locate; a per-turn-dynamic note re-keys every turn.

## Why it matters

This seam exists to keep a large constant Codex/harness system prompt warm on ONE upstream node across turns and sessions (adapters.go:558-566; `cmd/fak/guard_managed_cache.go`). Folding non-head system bytes into the key defeats that for the mid-array-`developer`, post-reset, and (latently) coherence-break cases. It is untested for non-leading system content: the arms in `internal/agent/responses_prompt_cache_key_test.go` only ever build a single **leading** `RoleSystem` message, and a grep for `prompt_cache_key` under `internal/gateway/` returns zero matches — no test observes the outbound key through the real decode fold.

(Possibly related to the observed symptom in #30425, though that reports a *stable* key with zero hits — a different failure mode; and distinct from the prefix-stability *guarantee* tracked in #6528.)

## Suggested fix / acceptance

- Anchor the hash to the **leading contiguous** `RoleSystem` block: `break` at the first non-system message so only the true prefix head enters the key (matches the doc and what the automatic prefix cache keys on). This also excludes the mid-conversation coherence-break marker by construction.
- Unit regression (`responses_prompt_cache_key_test.go`): a transcript with a mid-conversation `RoleSystem`/`developer` message must yield the **same** key as the same transcript without it; a `spliceSeed` carryover must not perturb the key.
- Gateway-level regression (new, co-located with the `internal/gateway` handler tests, capturing the outbound body): two sequential `/v1/responses` turns of one session marshal to an **identical** `prompt_cache_key`; changing only the top-level `instructions` (and, separately, a `developer` message) **does** change it — proving the head reaches the key via the fold rather than being dropped. Keep `TestResponsesPromptCacheKeyPresentAndStable` green (len==32, under the 64-char Codex/ChatGPT cap).

---
*Filed after an adversarial review of the recent wire-aware `prompt_cache_key` / managed-cache work; every anchor above was re-verified against the current source.*

records.title: fix(agent): openAIResponsesAdapter silently drops the ExtraBody escape hatch (FAK_PROVIDER_EXTRA_BODY_JSON / top_k / guided-decode) on the Codex/Responses wire
records.body:
## Problem

`prepareUpstream` builds one `adapterRequest` and threads the merged `ExtraBody` into every adapter's `MarshalRequest`, regardless of wire:

- `internal/agent/stream.go:412` — `extraBody, err := mergeGuidedDecodeExtraBody(p.ExtraBody, sp.GuidedDecode)` folds the operator's `FAK_PROVIDER_EXTRA_BODY_JSON` (`p.ExtraBody`) with per-request guided-decode fields (`guided_json`/`guided_regex`/`guided_grammar`).
- `internal/agent/stream.go:429` — that `extraBody` is passed uniformly into `adapter.MarshalRequest(adapterRequest{... ExtraBody: extraBody ...})`, including for `ProviderOpenAIResponses`.

But the Responses adapter never reads it:

- `internal/agent/adapters.go:543-555` — `openAIResponsesAdapter.MarshalRequest` does a plain `json.Marshal(openAIResponsesRequest{...})` and maps only `r.ResponseFormat` (`:551`, via `responsesText` → `text.format`). It does **not** read `r.ExtraBody`.
- `internal/agent/adapters.go:355` — `marshalWithExtraBody`, the only ExtraBody-merge helper, is called **only** by the chat `openAIAdapter` (`adapters.go:213`), never by the Responses adapter. `openAIResponsesRequest` (adapters.go:441-470) has no field carrying extra top-level keys.

Documented contract this violates:

- `internal/agent/chat.go:798` — "OpenAI/xAI/**Responses** have none [native top_k], so a top_k for them must go via ExtraBody."
- `internal/agent/adapters.go:67-74` — the guided-decode carriers "ride on the wire ONLY where the provider has a native field ... other providers omit them (their path is **ExtraBody**)."

So on the Codex/ChatGPT-subscription Responses wire (and any OpenAI-compatible local server addressed via `ProviderOpenAIResponses`), a request that used the sanctioned `ExtraBody` mechanism — a `top_k`/`chat_template_kwargs` body, or a `guided_json`/`regex`/grammar — is marshaled with those keys silently absent. No error, no typed signal; the model runs unconstrained/untuned while the caller believes the knobs are active. The asymmetry is the trap: the wire *does* honor `ResponseFormat` (→ `text.format`), so partial honoring makes the extra-body path look wired too.

No test guards it: `TestPerRequestTopKForwarding` (`adapters_test.go:1691`) only asserts `top_k` is *absent* from the Responses core body and defers the escape hatch to `TestOpenAIAdapterMergesProviderExtraBody` — which exercises the chat `openAIAdapter`, not `openAIResponsesAdapter`. The comment at `adapters_test.go:1655-1656` claiming the Responses ExtraBody path is "covered by" that test is stale.

## Relationship to #4272

#4272 (open — *"assert per-adapter structured-decode capability at MarshalRequest — fail-fast or map-to-native"*) covers the *structured/guided-decode* capability at this seam and may subsume the guided-decode half. This ticket is the broader **`ExtraBody` escape hatch** — the operator `FAK_PROVIDER_EXTRA_BODY_JSON`, `top_k`, `chat_template_kwargs` — not just structured decode. If the maintainer prefers, fold it into #4272; filing separately so the arbitrary-extra-body drop isn't lost.

## Why it matters

`ExtraBody` is the documented escape hatch for this wire (chat.go:798, adapters.go:70). A caller who followed the docs to pin `top_k`, a chat-template kwarg, or a guided-decode grammar on a Codex/Responses seat gets free-form, untuned output with no signal — a real correctness surprise for a headless fleet that then parses the result.

## Suggested fix / acceptance

- Route `openAIResponsesAdapter.MarshalRequest` through an ExtraBody merge (the Responses analogue of `marshalWithExtraBody` at adapters.go:213) so `r.ExtraBody` top-level keys reach the body — **or**, if the wire cannot accept arbitrary extra keys, return a typed *"ExtraBody unsupported on the Responses wire"* error at the seam rather than dropping silently (aligns with #4272's fail-fast option).
- Add a `TestPerRequestExtraBodyForwarding`-style test for `ProviderOpenAIResponses` asserting a set `ExtraBody` (e.g. `{"top_k":20}`) reaches the marshaled body (or produces the typed error), mirroring `TestOpenAIAdapterMergesProviderExtraBody`.
- Fix the stale comment at `adapters_test.go:1655-1656`.

---
*Filed after an adversarial review of the wire-aware Responses adapter work; anchors re-verified against current source (`MarshalRequest` at adapters.go:543-555 reads only `r.ResponseFormat`).*

records.title: fix(gateway): managed-cache posture reporting is provider-blind — codex ACTIVE session renders false "ACTIVE but inert" / POSTURE_MISMATCH on /debug/vars, fak info, and sessionaudit reconcile
records.body:
## Problem

The recent `bannerLine()` wire-awareness fix (`cmd/fak/guard_managed_cache.go`) taught the startup banner that on the OpenAI Responses (codex) wire the managed-cache lever is the pinned `prompt_cache_key`, not the Anthropic 1h-TTL upgrade — so an ACTIVE codex session no longer reads as "on but doing nothing." That fix was **not** applied to the other surfaces reporting the same posture. Each still judges ACTIVE-ness by the Anthropic-only 1h-TTL upgrade counter, which the guard code itself says "can never move on that wire" (guard_managed_cache.go:106-109).

The chain (verified end to end): `fak codex` normalizes an empty managed-cache mode to `on` (`cmd/fak/guard_cache_posture.go:48-49` via `codex_launcher.go:111,216`); `resolveGuardManagedCache("on")` returns `active:true` for **any** provider without consulting the wire (`guard_managed_cache.go:76-77`) → `CacheTTL1H` (`guard.go:1000`) → `s.cacheTTL1H=true` (`gateway.go:1808`). On the codex wire `anthropicPassthrough()` is false, so `maybeUpgradeAnthropicCacheTTL1H` returns early (`messages.go:814-816`) and `CacheTTLUpgraded` stays `0` forever. Affected surfaces:

- [ ] **`/debug/vars`** — `managedCacheVars` takes no provider input and sets `Inert: active && sum.CacheTTLUpgraded == 0` (`internal/gateway/debug.go:847-857`) → `{Active:true, Inert:true}` on every codex session.
- [ ] **`fak info`** — `guardInfoManagedCacheText` renders `mc.Active && mc.Inert` as the bare `"managed cache ACTIVE but inert (0 upgrades)"` (`cmd/fak/info.go:1161-1176`) — the line the `fak codex --split` pane shows.
- [ ] **sessionaudit reconcile** — `ReconcileManagedCachePosture` derives `wireUpgraded` solely from the 1h counter (`internal/sessionaudit/posture.go:116`) and treats `claim.Active && !wireUpgraded` as `POSTURE_MISMATCH` "behaved PASSIVE" (`posture.go:132`). `ManagedCacheClaim` (`posture.go:60`) and its producer `guardvars.ManagedCacheVars` (`internal/guardvars/guardvars.go:85`) carry no wire field. Latent today (no non-test caller), but **#4386** is the feature that wires this verdict into `fak cachevalue status` — once wired, every forced-on codex session emits a spurious `POSTURE_MISMATCH`.

So a healthy codex session, whose real lever (the stable `prompt_cache_key`) is live, reports "ACTIVE but inert" / "behaved PASSIVE" — the exact false posture the banner fix eliminated, still live on the panes and audits operators actually watch. The `prompt_cache_key` path itself is unaffected; this is an observability/reporting defect.

## Why it matters

It trains codex operators to distrust an ACTIVE posture that is in fact working, and it drowns the *real* Anthropic-lever inert signal — the weekly ACTIVE-but-inert misconfiguration review (`debug.go:832-835`; the inert-lever gap detection of #2180) — in guaranteed false positives from every codex session.

## Suggested fix / acceptance

- Thread the resolved provider/wire through the managed-cache posture path: add a wire field to `guardvars.ManagedCacheVars` / `sessionaudit.ManagedCacheClaim`, populated from `guardManagedCachePosture.provider`.
- Make `managedCacheVars`, `guardInfoManagedCacheText`, and `ReconcileManagedCachePosture` wire-aware: on `openai-responses`, an ACTIVE session with zero 1h upgrades must NOT report `Inert` / "ACTIVE but inert" / `POSTURE_MISMATCH` — render the `prompt_cache_key` lever instead, mirroring `bannerLine`'s `provider == "openai-responses"` branch. Keep Anthropic-wire behavior unchanged (a genuinely all-refused 1h head still shows inert).
- Acceptance: a test that boots an `openai-responses` session with `--managed-cache on`, drives one turn, and asserts `/debug/vars`, the `fak info` line, and the reconcile verdict do NOT report inert/PASSIVE; the Anthropic ACTIVE-with-zero-upgrade case still does.

---
*Filed after an adversarial review of the wire-aware banner fix; this is the same wire-blindness on the three surfaces the banner fix did not touch. Chain re-verified against current source.*

records.title: fix(resume): #4140 relaunch cache-affinity is dead — RelaunchCacheAffinityKey never threaded onto `claude --resume` (closed issue's deliverable unimplemented)
records.body:
## Problem

The transcript-keyed relaunch cache-route subsystem in `internal/resume/relaunch_affinity.go` has **zero production callers**. A grep for its exported symbols across every `*.go` returns only the definition file and its own test:

```
$ grep -rln "RelaunchCacheAffinityKey\|FoldRelaunchAffinity" --include=*.go .
./internal/resume/relaunch_affinity.go
./internal/resume/relaunch_affinity_test.go
```

- `RelaunchCacheAffinityKey` — `internal/resume/relaunch_affinity.go:14` (`sha256("fak-resume-cache-affinity\x00"+uuid)[:32]`)
- `RelaunchCacheAffinity` alias — `relaunch_affinity.go:26`
- `RelaunchAffinityRow` — `relaunch_affinity.go:33`
- `FoldRelaunchAffinity` — `relaunch_affinity.go:40`

This subsystem exists to satisfy issue **#4140** — *"feat(resume): carry CacheAffinity across the `claude --resume` relaunch so the warm route survives"* — which is **CLOSED**. But its deliverable is unrealized. The only path that relaunches a dead session, `rwResumeArgv` (`cmd/fak/resume_watchdog_runtime.go:354-374`), builds the child argv as `claude --resume <session> -p <prompt> --dangerously-skip-permissions` (+ posture/budget-envelope args) and **never derives `RelaunchCacheAffinityKey(session)` and never carries it** — no flag, no env var. Nothing folds a `RelaunchAffinityRow` into a live route either. So the warm cache route #4140 promised does not survive the relaunch.

The contrast with the sibling leaf is decisive: `relaunch_reset.go`'s `RelaunchResetRow` / `FoldRelaunchResets` **are** wired into the watchdog (`cmd/fak/resume_watchdog_cli.go:365`, `resume_watchdog_runtime.go:527`). The reset half of the resume-keyspace work shipped; the cache-affinity half was left inert.

## Why it matters

- **False-positive closure.** #4140 is closed and green, but its user-visible effect (cache warmth surviving an OS relaunch) is not implemented. The passing `relaunch_affinity_test.go` gives false confidence.
- **Unrealized cache warmth.** Every watchdog relaunch of a long-lived session starts cold on the provider prompt cache — exactly the cost this leaf was meant to avoid.
- **Yet another un-chokepointed key derivation.** This is now a fourth hardcoded `sha256(...)[:32]` affinity-key producer alongside `agent.responsesPromptCacheKey` (`internal/agent/adapters.go:578`, cap at `:601`), `session.deriveCacheAffinityKey` (`internal/session/cache_affinity.go:56`), and `vcachegov.AffinityKey` (`internal/vcachegov/affinity.go:49`) — each re-hardcoding its own domain separator and the load-bearing 64-char-cap `[:32]` truncation, with no shared helper. (See the companion dead/duplicated-producers ticket.)

## Suggested fix / acceptance

Pick one and record the decision (wire-or-cut):

- **Wire it** (honors #4140): in `rwResumeArgv`/`rwSpawnResume`, derive `RelaunchCacheAffinityKey(session)` and thread it onto the relaunched child so the warm route is carried, and fold `RelaunchAffinityRow` through a durable ledger the way `RelaunchResetRow` is folded at `resume_watchdog_runtime.go:527`. Add a test asserting the relaunch argv/env carries the derived key. Then #4140's closure is truthful.
- **Cut it**: delete `internal/resume/relaunch_affinity.go` + its test and reopen/annotate #4140 as not-yet-implemented, so a closed issue no longer implies a shipped feature.

Acceptance: either a non-test caller threads `RelaunchCacheAffinityKey` onto the `claude --resume` request path (with a proving test), or the dead symbols are removed and #4140's state reflects reality.

---
*Filed after an adversarial review of the cache-affinity producers; #4140's CLOSED state and the zero-caller grep were re-verified against the current tree.*

records.title: chore(cache): dead/duplicated cache-affinity key producers never reach the wire + glossary claims a non-existent "Shipped mechanism"
records.body:
## Problem

Two cache-affinity key producers are computed but never threaded to any outbound provider hint, and one of them is advertised in the public glossary as a live, load-bearing mechanism.

### 1. `vcachegov` affinity router is dead but documented as "Shipped"

`vcachegov.AffinityKey`/`AffinityHeader`/`RehashDetector`/`BurstCap` have **zero non-test callers**. A tree-wide grep for `vcachegov.AffinityHeader`/`vcachegov.AffinityKey` outside the package and tests finds only two *comments* in `internal/agent/adapters.go` (`:467`, `:568`):

```
internal/agent/adapters.go:467:  // ... (its derivation mirrors vcachegov.AffinityHeader). It
internal/agent/adapters.go:568:  // The value mirrors vcachegov.AffinityHeader — a 32-hex-char (128-bit) sha256 truncation.
```

- **Hazard A — false "Shipped mechanism" doc.** `docs/managed-context-glossary.md:223-229`, under **"Shipped mechanism,"** claims `vcachegov.AffinityKey` "biases chained requests onto one shard ... watches for a correlated warmth collapse ... and throttles its own warming bursts." None of that router code executes on any live path, so the documented autoscale-rehash detection and burst cap provide zero live protection.
- **Hazard B — misleading "mirror" comment on the live wire key.** adapters.go:568-575 tells maintainers the live `responsesPromptCacheKey` (adapters.go:554/578, truncated at `:601`) "mirrors `vcachegov.AffinityHeader`" and is "recomputed here ... to keep the agent wire layer decoupled" — implying a live parallel implementation to keep in sync. But the two hash disjoint tuples: `responsesPromptCacheKey` hashes `(model, system messages, tools)` while `AffinityHeader` hashes `(tenant, chain, region)`. The only shared, load-bearing invariant is the 32-char cap (the Codex/ChatGPT backend 400s a `prompt_cache_key` > 64 chars). A maintainer "keeping the mirror in sync" — e.g. widening `[:32]` — would edit dead code believing it governs the live wire key.

### 2. Session-continuation `AffinityKey` is never consumed

On a hidden budget/coherence reset, `cacheAffinityForContinuation` mints `CacheAffinityDecision{Action: Preserve, AffinityKey: deriveCacheAffinityKey(parentTrace)}` (`internal/session/cache_affinity.go:32,56`). It is re-exported as `SessionCacheAffinity.AffinityKey` (`internal/gateway/gateway.go:867-869`) and serialized onto the reset directive (`session_admit.go:316-321`, `mcp.go:510-515`) — but from there it is only ever copied struct-to-struct and read in tests. No routing path converts it into an outbound `prompt_cache_key` or affinity header: `responsesPromptCacheKey` derives purely from `model + RoleSystem content + tools` and never consults it; `vcachegov.AffinityHeader` (the function that would bound it) is dead (see above). So the reset directive advertises `Action: preserve` and hands the host an `affinity_key` that nothing in fak's own wire path acts on.

### Cross-cutting: four un-chokepointed `sha256(...)[:32]` producers

`responsesPromptCacheKey` (adapters.go:578), `session.deriveCacheAffinityKey` (cache_affinity.go:56), `vcachegov.AffinityKey` (affinity.go:49), and `resume.RelaunchCacheAffinityKey` (see the #4140 companion ticket) each independently re-hardcode a domain separator and the load-bearing 64-char-cap `[:32]` truncation, with no shared helper — so a future change to the cap has four disconnected sites to find.

## Why it matters

Cache state is never load-bearing for correctness (a miss only costs latency), so blast radius is bounded to cost/latency and maintainer confusion — hence low severity. But (a) the glossary advertises warm-set-collapse protection that does not exist, (b) the "mirror" comments point maintainers at dead code when touching the single truncation invariant that keeps Codex requests from 400ing, and (c) a stated `preserve` guarantee is inert on every wire.

## Suggested fix / acceptance

Make one explicit wire-or-cut decision per producer (per the #2128 inert-code posture) and remove the false framing either way:

- **Cut:** delete the dead `vcachegov` router (`AffinityKey`/`AffinityHeader`/`RehashDetector`/`BurstCap`) and, if unused, `session.deriveCacheAffinityKey`/`AffinityKey`; demote the `docs/managed-context-glossary.md:223` "Shipped mechanism" claim to what actually ships; rewrite the adapters.go:467/568 comments to document the live key's own `[:32]`/NUL invariant without referencing a nonexistent live mirror; stop advertising `Action: preserve` on the reset directive.
- **Wire:** route real requests through `AffinityHeader` (warm + recall + the rehash/burst guards) and thread the preserved continuation `AffinityKey` into the outbound key, with an integration test proving the router executes.
- **Either way:** consolidate the four `sha256(...)[:32]` producers behind one helper so the 64-char Codex cap lives in one asserted place.

Acceptance: no comment or public doc claims a live "mirror" or "Shipped mechanism" that a grep for non-test callers cannot corroborate.

---
*Filed after an adversarial review of the cache-affinity producers; zero-caller greps and the glossary/comment claims were re-verified against the current tree.*

records.title: Complaint channel follow-on: land AGENTS discoverability + workflow/dev friction domain
records.body:
## Summary

Tracking issue for the `fak complain` appeal-channel improvement (goal:
"make sure friction files gh tickets, not just a private journal, automatically").

## Shipped

- `8e1d054cb` — `feat(complain): auto-file gh tickets via FAK_COMPLAIN_LIVE + disclose dry-run files nothing`.
  Adds `FAK_COMPLAIN_LIVE=1`, a fleet-wide default that makes every `fak complain`
  auto-file its deduped gh ticket without threading `--live` through each call, and a
  loud stderr disclosure on a dry-run so a printed plan is never mistaken for a filed
  appeal. Unit-tested (`complainLiveMode` flag/env resolution + dry-run disclosure),
  green on a clean HEAD checkout (`ok github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/cmd/fak`).
- `a1c91ded4` — `docs(complain): refresh friction note` — the friction-channel note
  (`docs/notes/CONCEPT-AGENT-FRICTION-COMPLAINT-CHANNELS-2026-06-29.md`) was still
  labelled `not yet` for the `fak complain` verb; it is now wired, so the note now
  documents the shipped surface and the `FAK_COMPLAIN_LIVE` auto-file default.

## Remaining (not yet)

1. **Surface `fak complain` in `AGENTS.md`.** A one-paragraph pointer under
   "If the kernel refuses you" telling an agent to *appeal a wrong refusal, not just
   journal it privately* was authored but lost the race to land: `AGENTS.md` is
   inlined into the generated `llms-full.txt`, and regenerating that 970 KB file on a
   hot trunk races concurrent peer doc commits. Land the `AGENTS.md` paragraph plus a
   fresh `llms-full.txt` regen (`python tools/gen_llms_full.py`) in one commit based on
   the current trunk HEAD so no peer-committed doc block is dropped.
2. **General agentic-dev friction domain.** The friction note's stated next step:
   add a `workflow`/`dev` complaint domain so the *same* deduping channel covers the
   non-guard friction classes (shared-tree clobber, tool-timeout, lane-collision)
   rather than only capability-floor appeals.

## Why this is filed as a ticket, not a journal note

This is the exact behaviour the goal asks for: friction and follow-on work registered
in a shared, trackable channel instead of an agent's private memory. Filed via
`fak issue create` (the sanctioned ungated filing path).

Parent epic: #4992. Follow-on to #2765.

The trajctl regime-gated nudge now enqueues a real `sessionctl.OpRedirect` control-bus packet, but it does not lower that applied/refused actuation through the shared `sessionctl.Move` / `NextRecord` seam shipped by #4993. The operator/autonomous families therefore still expose parallel witnesses.

sessionctl / cmd

records.title: feat(next): actuate witness-resolved operator answers through Stop-hook continuation
records.body:
## Parent context
Parent epic: #4992. Follows the native question-answer oracle work in #4887.

## Current state
The Stop-hook recognizes native Claude/Codex operator questions and can auto-resolve CLARIFY/CHOOSE_APPROACH from witness-backed oracles. But `OPERATOR_QUESTION_RESOLVED` currently exits 0 and therefore stops the harness; the resolved answer is printed to stderr only. No `sessionctl.Move` carries the answer back into the session, so "auto-resolved" is classification without actuation.

## In scope
- Preserve the resolved answer/action from `runGuardOperatorQuestionGate` through the Stop-hook disposition path.
- Lower an enforce-mode auto-resolution to the shared Next seam as an autonomous continuation carrying the answer payload (closed move/render mapping chosen explicitly and structurally tested).
- Refuse Stop so the harness reopens/continues with the witnessed answer instead of terminating.
- Emit applied/refused `NextRecord` evidence in the existing guard-stop ledger; preserve warn/shadow/off and HUMAN_RESIDUAL behavior.
- Add captured behavior tests for exit disposition, payload, render authority XOR, and fail-open witness errors.

## Out of scope
Changing oracle recognition or authority policy (#4887), answering genuine HUMAN_RESIDUAL questions, and harness-specific UI automation outside the Stop-hook transport.

A witness-resolved native question causes enforce-mode Stop refusal/continuation and emits exactly one applied shared `NextRecord` whose payload is the answer/action; the same trace does not carry an interactive splice; residual questions still escalate and stop fail-open; affected tests pass.

## Witness
A Stop-hook test supplies a native question transcript, captures emitted guidance and the guard-stop JSONL row, and asserts continuation plus the answer payload. Structural test pins the shared enqueue/drain authority. One diff-witnessed commit closes the issue.

## Lane
cmd / sessionctl

Contribution: 5/10 points.

An agent governed by `fak guard` judged a guard decision wrong and filed this appeal. This is the **subjective** channel: a false-positive refusal is byte-identical to a correct one in the decision journal, so `fak guard-verdict-rsi` cannot surface it — only the agent that made the call knows it was legitimate.

- kind: `over-broad` — a gate that refuses more than its stated danger class — collateral denials
- appealed reason: `SELF_MODIFY`
- refused tool: `shell_command`
- occurrences: `1`
- stable key: `guard-complaint/over-broad/self-modify/shell-command/read-only-remote-connectivity-checks-can-be-misclassified-as`

## Why the agent thinks the guard is wrong

A current guarded agent was unable to perform operator-authorized, read-only remote connectivity verification because ordinary shell inspection calls were repeatedly classified as SELF_MODIFY/ESCALATE. The workflow did not write to the guard, its policy, hooks, credentials, binaries, configuration, or source tree. This appears broader than one SSH command: command admission should derive actual local mutation targets and distinguish inspection, transport, and nested remote execution from writes to enforcement assets. Please add regression coverage for read-only network/socket/SSH probes, shell commands containing nested script text, and commands that mention guarded concepts without writing guarded paths. On denial, report the parsed mutation target and matched rule so an agent can safely narrow or appeal the call. No session ID, hostname, address, username, command payload, credential material, or private repository detail is included in this public report.

## Evidence

_No journal verdict attached — this appeal rests on the agent's rationale alone. Re-file with `--from-journal` after the refusal to attach the witnessed verdict._

records.title: fix(appversion): guard borrows latest checkout VERSION when stale PATH binary runs from repo
records.body:
## Problem

An installed or stale `fak` binary launched from a newer fak checkout can report that checkout's `VERSION` instead of its own build identity. `appversion.Current()` currently searches the process working directory before the executable directory.

Observed on 2026-07-17:

- PATH executable: `C:\Users\USER\bin\fak.exe`
- PATH executable build: `3af21b18e65b`
- current checkout HEAD: `ab9767f44282`
- running `fak version` from the checkout reported app version `0.41.0`, read from the checkout's `VERSION`

This is especially misleading in `fak guard`: its banner combines the old binary's build SHA with a friendly version borrowed from a different/newer checkout, so the operator can believe the wrong or latest guard loaded.

## Done when

- `appversion.Current()` never uses an unrelated process cwd as binary identity.
- Stamped release/dev/self-update binaries continue to report their embedded `BuildVersion`.
- An unstamped binary outside a source tree reports `dev` rather than borrowing cwd's `VERSION`.
- A regression test launches the resolver model from a cwd containing a sentinel `VERSION` and proves that sentinel is not returned.
- Guard/version identity paths continue to compile and the affected tests pass.

## Work estimate

2 points

records.title: feat(adjudicator): restore-toward-baseline self-widening (permissive, bounded by the shipped floor)
records.body:
## Parent context
Epic #5170 — Policy Amendment Classes. Track E (SELF-AMENDABLE frontier). Motivated by the deeper safety analysis in the E1 spike (#5185): more-permissive is often the SAFER choice.

## Problem
The convenience surface (which tools are allowed) is not where danger lives — danger lives in the FROZEN core (egress SSRF floor, structural danger arg-rules, self-modify-core globs, reversibility gate), which adjudicates effects downstream regardless of the allow-list. So a self-widening that stays WITHIN the shipped baseline (`DevAgentPolicy`) adds nothing the shipped policy didn't already deem safe. Yet today the agent cannot restore such a capability on its own — it must stall for an out-of-band operator even to return to the vetted default. That over-restriction causes the real hazards: false-refusal → evasion, run stalls, and self-wedge (a tightened agent that cannot un-tighten).

## In scope
- Add a **restore-toward-baseline** self-amendment: the agent may widen its own live floor WITHOUT operator ratification, admitted ONLY when the result is still bounded by the shipped baseline — checkable as `diffPolicyWidening(shippedDevAgentPolicy, proposed).Empty()` (proposed adds nothing beyond what `DevAgentPolicy` already allows). Anything beyond baseline ⇒ NOT restore; routes to the operator-gated grant path (E3).
- Every restore is journaled (a CapabilityGrant record, child #5178) and session-scoped by default (evaporates at teardown) so it is observed + reversible.
- The FROZEN core is untouched, so a restore provably cannot reach genuine danger.

## Out of scope
- widen-BEYOND-baseline grants (child E3) — those still need the out-of-band operator.
- self-tighten + anti-wedge (child E2).

## Done condition
An agent-issued restore of a tool that IS in the shipped `DevAgentPolicy` but was tightened away earlier is admitted without ratification and journaled; an attempt to restore a tool NOT in the baseline is refused and redirected to the grant/propose path.

## Witness
`go test ./internal/adjudicator -run RestoreToBaseline` covers both the admit (in-baseline) and refuse (beyond-baseline) cases; the admitted restore appears as a session-scoped CapabilityGrant.

## Lane
`adjudicator`. Path hints: `internal/adjudicator/decide.go` (`DevAgentPolicy`, `diffPolicyWidening` seam), `cmd/fak/policy_reload_widen.go`, `cmd/fak/guard_startup.go`.

## Closure binding
Resolving commit cites `#<this issue>` with a `(fak adjudicator)` trailer.

## Work estimate
Estimate: 3 points. Uncertainty: operator-supplied estimate; revise through the parent denominator when evidence changes.

## Overall completion contribution
Contribution: 3/40 points.

## Completion standard
development

records.title: epic(trajctl): intervention as a typed state operator — the physics-and-proof layer beneath next()
records.body:
**Concept note:** `docs/notes/CONCEPT-INTERVENTION-AS-STATE-OPERATOR-2026-07-17.md` (landing on `main`).

## One line

Every shipped intervention — the `trajctl` re-anchor nudge, every `sessionctl` Next move, the `doomloop` NUDGE — is a **token disturbance appended to an unchanged, poisoned context, escalated on elapsed time, topping out at hand-to-human.** Four independent lenses (control theory, Bayesian belief-state, the mechanistic actuator surface, causal verification) converge on the replacement: an intervention is a **typed operation on agent state / action-space / dynamics**, routed by which latent corrupted, stamped with the evidence-rung it may assert at, carrying its own witnessed acceptance predicate, escalating in **strength not time**, gated to do no harm, and evaluated on an **exact forked counterfactual**.

This is the *physics-and-proof layer* beneath the actuation family — it does not duplicate it:
- **`next()` #4992** — the witnessed move all drivers lower to; the typed `Intervention` record is the payload it should carry.
- **trajectory-control #2533 / re-anchor nudge #2540** — supplies the regime gate, witness rungs, curve; this supplies the diagnosis router, strength ladder, and fork-paired τ it lacks.
- **out-of-band control #2753** — supplies the control vocabulary; this ranks those ops by operand class + authority + acceptance predicate + reversibility.
- **policy-amendment classes #5170** — a `TOOL_POLICY` intervention is a guard-floor amendment and must obey those classes.

## Why prose fails (one mechanism, four derivations)
A bad trajectory is a **stable attractor basin** (control) = a **concentrated wrong posterior `P(z*|C)` the model is provenance-blind to** (Bayes) = **appended tokens competing in the softmax lottery while a guard/grammar edit vetoes at measure-zero** (actuator) = **unprovable on the instance** (causal). Adding instruction-shaped tokens is structurally the wrong operation; the failure lives in the accumulated prior/state, not a missing instruction.

## The unification
For an LLM agent the **belief state is copyable — the context prefix IS the state** — so rollback/handoff (actuator), fork-and-probe (Bayes), and the randomized twin arm (causal) are the **same primitive**: a checkpoint/fork. Build it once → strongest actuator + exact evaluator + causal identification, together.

## Fan-out (worst-first)
- [ ] **S — typed `Intervention` record** generalizing `SteerDecision`/`NextRecord`: `operand`, `diagnosis`, `authority`, `φ`, `reversibility`, witness `{pre-hash, op, post-hash, curve-delta@+k}`.
- [ ] **1 — G/W/P diagnosis router**: refine the `trajctl` signal into a latent-type so the controller *selects an actuator* instead of always nudging.
- [ ] **2 — authority stamping + fail-closed assert rule**: `authority = min witness rung`; refuse a `W3` assertion the supervisor cannot witness (reuse `dos_check_reason` vocabulary).
- [ ] **3 — excision-for-hygiene**: point compaction at the culprit span + descendant closure (epistemic hygiene, not budget), reusing `fak_context_spans`/tombstone-restore.
- [ ] **4 — tool-policy / grammar U-edit actuators** through the guard, regime-gated, obeying #5170 amendment classes.
- [ ] **5 — `φ` acceptance predicates + strength-escalation ladder**: replace the time-driven `doomloop` ESCALATE with witnessed-`φ`-driven strength escalation (append → obs-shape → sampler → tool-policy/grammar → surgery → rollback → handoff → halt).
- [ ] **6 — paired checkpoint/fork** (context + workspace SHA + lease, atomic) — unlocks strongest actuator + exact evaluator + causal twin at once.
- [ ] **7 — calibration child as an e-process**: emit `{e-value, confidence sequence}` per `(actuator × regime × outcome-version)`; CS lower bound gates enable-by-default. Lane-local / lease-epoch-clustered outcomes (SUTVA fence — shared tree breaks no-interference).

## Fences
Nothing shipped. Per-instance *benefit* is unprovable forever (report "took (φ witnessed)", never "worked"). W3 outcome is the only confirmatory endpoint (anti-Goodhart) + placebo arm + McCrary + permanent hold-out. Bayesian abstraction is a design calculus, not a theorem. Citation hygiene: `arXiv:2602.03338` / `arXiv:2505.02709` (the regime-gate + re-anchor anchors) did not resolve on search — needs a `dos_citation_resolve` pass.

records.title: fix(guard): denied Codex tool call becomes terminal assistant message and false task_complete
records.body:
## Summary

A guarded Codex TUI session was converted from an active implementation turn into a terminal assistant message containing only the guard's denial/recovery text. Codex then emitted `task_complete`, despite the user's requested code changes being neither implemented nor verified. Repeating `keep going` reproduced the stop.

This is distinct from whether the underlying `POLICY_BLOCK` / `SELF_MODIFY` classifications were correct. Those false-positive reports are tracked in #5197 and #5194. This issue is about **denial handling becoming a false terminal completion** instead of returning control to the model (or producing an explicit blocked state).

## Reproduction evidence

Local rollout:

`C:\Users\USER\.codex\sessions\2026\07\17\rollout-2026-07-17T14-11-36-019f71eb-a468-7e22-9966-52eb2ab55057.jsonl`

Repository at session start: `anthony-chaudhary/Benchmark`, branch `main`, commit `802002c06cce778843a3093421afff029cf9fefe`.

The requested work was to fix `install-openssh-linux.sh` and then copy the generic Tailscale/SSH setup concept to `host-maintenance`.

Observed sequence (UTC):

1. `21:16:08` — last ordinary model tool call (`shell_command`) returns at `21:16:16`.
2. `21:17:11` — without a corresponding refused `response_item/function_call` in the rollout, an `event_msg/agent_message` appears containing only:
   `Allowed next step ... Constraint: shell_command: DENY (POLICY_BLOCK/TERMINAL)`.
3. The same text is serialized as `response_item/message role=assistant` (line 54).
4. `21:17:13` — `event_msg/task_complete` is emitted (line 56).
5. User says `keeep going`; session resumes inspection, but the same denial-only assistant message appears at `21:19:44` and `task_complete` follows at `21:19:50` (lines 90-93).
6. User says `go`, then `keep going`; after one read-only `Get-Content AGENTS.md`, the session emits a denial-only `SELF_MODIFY/ESCALATE` assistant message at `21:30:57` and `task_complete` at `21:30:59` (lines 104-107).

Current-state witness that the goal was not complete:

- `C:\work\Benchmark\install-openssh-linux.sh` remains untracked.
- `C:\work\host-maintenance` has no corresponding generic Tailscale/SSH setup artifact.
- The session's `update_plan` never reached completion and no edit/test/commit followed the denial messages.

## Why this matters

A guard denial is not successful task completion. Treating generated remediation prose as the assistant's final answer strands interactive work and requires repeated operator nudges. It also makes downstream status consumers unable to distinguish `done` from `guard interrupted this turn`.

## Acceptance criteria

- A denied tool call is returned to the model as a structured tool error/result and the same turn can choose a safe alternative.
- Guard remediation text is not promoted to a final assistant message unless the model explicitly authors a terminal response.
- `task_complete` is not emitted solely because a guard denial occurred while requested work remains open.
- If recovery cannot continue, emit a typed `BLOCKED`/`NEEDS_OPERATOR` state containing the denied call ID, reason, and evidence—not a normal completion.
- Add an end-to-end regression test: deny one shell call during a multi-step Codex task, permit a safe alternative, and assert that the model gets another actuation opportunity and no premature `task_complete` occurs.
- Track metrics for denial->task_complete transitions and alert on sessions with repeated user `keep going` continuations after the same denial class.

## Related

- #5197 — over-broad `POLICY_BLOCK` classification
- #5194 — over-broad `SELF_MODIFY` classification
- #5018 — adjacent early-stop / anti-stall work for autonomous Opus sessions; this report covers guarded Codex interactive turns and denial-to-completion semantics

records.title: fix(guard): persist refused Codex call provenance and ground remediation in the matched rule
records.body:
## Summary

When `fak guard` denied work in a Codex TUI session, the persisted rollout did not contain the attempted/refused tool call. It only contained a later free-form remediation sentence and a reason class. The advice was not grounded in the user's task and was sometimes nonsensical for the visible action history.

This prevents reliable audit, appeal, and safe recovery: an operator cannot determine what command was refused, which path/rule matched, or whether the suggested alternative is relevant.

## Reproduction evidence

Local rollout:

`C:\Users\USER\.codex\sessions\2026\07\17\rollout-2026-07-17T14-11-36-019f71eb-a468-7e22-9966-52eb2ab55057.jsonl`

Session repository: `anthony-chaudhary/Benchmark` at `802002c06cce778843a3093421afff029cf9fefe`.

The user asked to repair an OpenSSH installer and copy the generic setup concept to `host-maintenance`.

Three interruption points are visible:

- Lines 53-56: `POLICY_BLOCK/TERMINAL`, advising deletion without `-r/-f` or moving a path aside.
- Lines 90-93: same `POLICY_BLOCK/TERMINAL` deletion advice.
- Lines 104-107: `SELF_MODIFY/ESCALATE`, advising `fak commit --core-lock-maintenance-witness` or `fak slack send`.

At each interruption:

- There is no preceding `response_item/function_call` for the refused call.
- There is no call ID, original arguments/digest, parsed mutation target, matched rule, policy source, or journal row reference.
- The last visible commands were benign reads (`Get-Content install-openssh-linux.sh` or `Get-Content AGENTS.md`).
- The suggested deletion, Slack, and core-lock alternatives do not explain how to continue editing/testing an installer or add the requested host-maintenance artifact.

Existing complaints #5197 and #5194 explicitly say their journal matching was ambiguous or unavailable. This rollout demonstrates the underlying observability/provenance gap that makes those appeals rationale-only.

## Why this matters

Without a durable refused-call record, a denial cannot be independently audited. Generic remediation can also send the agent down an unrelated or more privileged path. The Growth-Mindset status is: the denial is **not witnessed yet**; missing are the exact call and matched policy evidence. Next checkable step is to preserve and expose those fields end to end.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every denied tool attempt is persisted in the session rollout (or linked durable journal) with:
  - session/turn/call IDs,
  - tool name,
  - redacted argument summary + stable digest,
  - parsed operation and mutation targets,
  - matched policy rule/reason and policy source/version,
  - journal row/decision ID.
- The model receives the same structured denial payload, not only free-form prose.
- Remediation is derived from the matched operation/rule and validated as applicable to the denied call; otherwise say no sanctioned alternative is known.
- `fak complain --from-journal` can deterministically select the denial from session + call ID without scanning ambiguous rows.
- Add regression coverage for nested shell commands and multi-repo edits, asserting that unrelated deletion/Slack/core-lock advice is not emitted.
- Add a redaction test proving secrets/raw credentials do not leak while enough structure remains for audit.

## Related

- #5212 — denial text becoming a terminal assistant completion
- #5197 — over-broad `POLICY_BLOCK` complaint, currently rationale-only due ambiguous journal matching
- #5194 — over-broad `SELF_MODIFY` complaint, currently rationale-only due missing exact verdict

The live agent loop already turns a denied stop into a synthetic user message:

records.title: fix(next): make the shared queue the production actuation authority
records.body:
## Parent context

Parent: #4992. Related doctrine: #2768. This is a closure-truth correction discovered while auditing #5233.

## Problem

The closed children #4993/#4994 claim a production single-authority enqueue/drain topology, but current trunk does not implement that topology:

- `NextQueue.Enqueue` and `NextQueue.Drain` have no non-test callers.
- `internal/sessionctl/next_test.go::TestNextDrainHasSingleProductionAuthority` counts the method definition, not production call sites, so it passes when production has zero drains.
- Native producers still append USER/SYSTEM messages directly in `internal/agent/loop.go` and only afterward write producer-specific Next witness ledgers.
- Stop-hook/operator-answer and respawn use `WitnessMove` directly as foreign decisions; they do not share an actuation queue with the native sink.

Therefore #4992's done condition (native loop drains exactly one seam and two sinks never co-drive a trace) is not yet structurally proven. #5233 truthfully ratchets the direct append denominator, but it does not turn those appends into a shared actuation authority.

## Done

- Replace the definition-count test with an AST production-call-site test that requires exactly one native `NextQueue.Drain` call in the agent turn boundary and rejects a second native drain.
- Route all model-facing synthetic native moves through one `NextQueue.Enqueue` -> one turn-boundary `Drain` -> render switch; no producer directly appends its synthetic USER/SYSTEM payload.
- Preserve exact payload/timing semantics for tool-terminal wake, steer, redirect, context advisory, stop-unwitnessed continuation, and gateway guard recovery (or explicitly classify gateway as a separate boundary if it cannot share the native agent trace).
- Prove a trace is bound to one render class and cannot be actuated by both native splice and foreign reopen/stop sinks.
- Keep question-answer lowering exact: resolved answer remains `continue/reopen`, applied only after answer consumption; unresolved/denied states remain witnessed refusals.
- Reconcile #4992's implementation relationship in #2768 docs before epic closure.

## Witness

A clean-source test suite with an AST mutation that adds a second production drain and fails; captured behavior tests for each native producer and the resolved/unresolved operator-answer paths; `go vet` and clean `cmd/fak` build.

## Work estimate

Estimate: 8 points. Uncertainty: cross-boundary queue ownership and gateway trace integration require source proof.

## Overall completion contribution

Contribution: 8/30 points toward #4992's corrected production-authority denominator.

## Completion standard

development

## Target operating envelope

- production native drain sites: = 1 sites
- direct synthetic native append authorities: = 0 sites
- per-trace render classes: <= 1 classes

## Witnessed operating envelope

- production native drain sites: = 0 sites
- direct synthetic native append authorities: = 6 sites
- per-trace render classes: <= 1 classes
