records.title: feat(moe): deferred-expert cross-layer CPU/GPU pipeline — run lowest-router-weight experts one layer late (ktransformers-borrow, child #3900)
records.body:
Child of the ktransformers study epic **#3900**. That pass used a **caching-observability** lens and explicitly scoped out compute; this is the deeper **compute-overlap** mechanism it left unmined. Fresh re-study pinned at a newer SHA **`0c2912a`** (the repo has since restructured: the old framework moved to `archive/`, `kt-kernel` is now primary).

## The borrow (inspire — Apache-2.0 → Apache-2.0, clean-room, no bytes)
ktransformers hides CPU cold-expert latency behind GPU work by **deferring the lowest-router-weight experts by one layer** and reconciling them incrementally:

- Split each token's top-k into "immediate" (highest router weight, protected) vs "deferred": `select_deferred_experts` — `protected_k = num_experts_per_tok - max_deferred`, a `torch.topk` on routing scores keeps the protected set, the rest are masked to `-1`. `kt-kernel/python/experts_base.py:347-375@0c2912a`.
- Two-phase submit on the same stream: immediate work writes `output_cpu[layer%2]`; deferred work writes the next slot and sets `_layer_has_pending_deferred[layer]=True`, reconciled at layer L+1 via an `incremental` flag. `kt-kernel/python/experts_base.py:414-455@0c2912a`.
- The deferred partial is **summed onto** the already-emitted token vector, not recomputed: `merge_results(qlen, output, incremental)` reads back `output`, adds `local_output`, folds TP partials. `kt-kernel/operators/llamafile/moe.hpp:789-816@0c2912a`.
- A pipeline-depth valve: `sync(allow_n_pending)` waits until `pending <= allow_n_pending` (1 in-flight deferred task tolerated across the sync boundary). `kt-kernel/cpu_backend/task_queue.cpp:53-59@0c2912a`, driven from `experts_base.py:480-481`.

**Axis (narrow):** trade a bounded, router-weight-ranked slice of expert accuracy for latency by running the least-important experts one layer late, so the GPU never stalls on the CPU expert tail. Their README bands `1-4` deferred as "good latency/quality balance", `5-7` as "noticeable accuracy loss" — it is an explicit quality-for-latency knob for the consumer-GPU + big-MoE (VRAM-starved) world.

## fak seam (where this lands)
- `internal/model/moe_offload.go` — `splitKernel.mul` routes each expert weight to the host or device sub-kernel and runs it **synchronously**; there is no deferral/overlap across layers (`splitKernel.mul`, lines 40-45). This is fak's `--n-cpu-moe` hybrid.
- `internal/model/expert_readahead.go` — fak's only expert-side "overlap" today is `MADV_WILLNEED` prefetch of the next expert's bytes into page cache (disk-read/compute overlap on the mmap path), **not** compute deferral. `willneedExpertSlice`, lines 71-.

So fak overlaps *disk reads*, not *CPU/GPU compute*. The cross-layer deferred-compute pipeline is **ABSENT on-axis**.

## Dogfood witness
Confirmed via `fak_feature_query "deferred pipelined expert execution overlap"` + direct read of `moe_offload.go` (synchronous `mul`) and `expert_readahead.go` (mmap readahead only). No open fak issue covers cross-layer expert-compute deferral (`gh issue list --search "defer layer CPU GPU expert overlap"` → empty). Distinct from #3174/#2726/#3886 (residency/placement, not compute deferral).

## First checkable step
Add a pure, host-free scorer `internal/model/expert_defer_plan.go`: given per-token router weights, `num_experts_per_tok`, and a `maxDeferred` budget, return the immediate/deferred partition (protected = top `k-maxDeferred` by weight) — the deterministic partition function, off the serve path, witnessed against a fixture. This mirrors how #3902/#3901 landed the residency gauges as pure functions before any serve wiring. The `splitKernel` double-buffer + one-layer-behind reconcile is the fenced follow-on.

## Honest scope
- Witness is a 2026-07 snapshot (`0c2912a`) + lexical query + `gh` dedup; re-witness before wiring.
- Not a from-scratch borrow: it is a *delta* on the existing `splitKernel` offload seam.
- The GPU half (stream host-callback, `cpuinfer.h:87-95`) only matters once a device backend is present; the CPU-only degenerate config keeps today's bit-exact synchronous path.

records.title: feat(model): native FP8 CPU MoE compute — keep FP8 experts compressed in RAM instead of expanding to f32 at load (ktransformers-borrow, sota-gated, sibling #3900)
records.body:
Sibling of the ktransformers study epic **#3900** — a **kernel** borrow the prior pass explicitly scoped out ("the transferable surface is the management pattern, **not CUDA/AMX/tensor code**"). A deeper kernel-level read (fresh SHA **`0c2912a`**) surfaces a concrete RAM-footprint win for fak's own RAM-bound serving.

> **SOTA-matrix gate:** this is a compute-kernel borrow. Bind it to `internal/sotamatrix` (the production-reference ladder) and route through the sota-check flow before implementation — do not dispatch as a ready leaf until the reference kernel + numeric target are pinned.

## The borrow (inspire — Apache-2.0 → Apache-2.0, clean-room)
ktransformers keeps FP8 expert weights **compressed in RAM** and dequantizes per-tile *inside* the MoE matmul, instead of expanding to f32 at load:

- FP8(e4m3)→BF16 decode in-register via an AVX-512 VBMI byte-permute LUT (two `permutex2var_epi8`), no float ops: `kt-kernel/operators/amx/la/amx_raw_kernels.hpp:324@0c2912a` (`fp8x64_to_bf16x64`).
- **Per-channel** scale applied once, after full-K accumulation (one FP32 scale per output row): `amx_raw_kernels.hpp:816@0c2912a` (`float_mat_vec_perchannel`) + dispatch `kt-kernel/operators/amx/fp8-perchannel-moe.hpp:92-108@0c2912a`.
- The **block-wise 128×128** variant folds a scale per k-group into the accumulator: `amx_raw_kernels.hpp:504,528@0c2912a` (`apply_scale_kgroup` / `float_mat_vec_kgroup`), scale buffer `[ceil(n/128),ceil(k/128)]` at `amx_raw_buffers.hpp:178@0c2912a`.

**Axis (narrow):** keep FP8 weights at 1 byte/elem resident and dequant lazily per compute tile — 4× less RAM than an f32 expansion — for a CPU-offloaded MoE. This is precisely the RAM-bound regime fak targets (GLM-5.2 Q4_K ~424 GB in ~1007 GB host RAM, per `moe_offload.go`'s own header).

## fak seam / the gap
- `internal/model/fp8_blockscale.go` — fak's FP8 e4m3 128×128 block-scale path **dequantizes to f32 at load**: `decodeFP8BlockScale` allocates `out := make([]float32, elems)` and the loader appends f32 bytes into the resident buffer (lines 88-95, and `decodeFP8BlockScaleTensor` 107-128). An FP8 expert tensor therefore costs **4×** its on-disk size in RAM.
- Contrast: fak already keeps **Q4_K native** and decodes lazily in the CPU kernel (`internal/model/quant_q4k.go`, and `moe_offload.go`'s comment "run them on the CPU Q4_K/Q8 kernel"). So the "native-compressed compute" pattern exists in fak for Q4_K — it is only **missing for FP8**.

Net: **PARTIAL** — fak has native-compressed CPU MoE compute for Q4_K but expands FP8 to f32, forfeiting the RAM win exactly where it matters most (the largest FP8 checkpoints, DeepSeek-V4 / GLM-5.2-FP8).

## Dogfood witness
Direct read of `fp8_blockscale.go` (f32 expansion) vs `quant_q4k.go` (native). No open fak issue tracks a native FP8 CPU compute path (`gh issue list --search "FP8 native compute compressed"` → empty). fak's FP8 today is decode-at-load only (#4360 landed the decode math; #4209 tracked FP8 parity).

## First checkable step
A pure scalar Go kernel `fp8DotBlockScale(actF32, fp8Weight []byte, scaleInv []float32, ...)` that computes one output row directly from FP8 bytes + block scales (LUT decode per element, scale folded per 128-block) and is asserted **bit-exact** against `decodeFP8BlockScale` then dot — proving the compressed path is numerically identical to expand-then-dot before wiring it into `splitKernel`'s host side. Add per-channel scale as a second scale-application mode.

## Honest scope
- SIMD/AMX is out of scope for a first Go port; the win is the **RAM footprint** (native-compressed residency), reachable with a scalar kernel + LUT. Throughput parity is a separate, sota-matrix-gated rung.
- Snapshot `0c2912a`; re-witness. No bytes vendored — technique only.

records.title: feat(serve): inference-hardware serve-readiness doctor — CPU ISA tier / VRAM-for-model / NUMA capability report (ktransformers kt-doctor borrow, sibling #3900)
records.body:
Sibling of the ktransformers study epic **#3900** — an **operator-tooling** borrow outside that pass's KV/MoE lens. Fresh SHA **`0c2912a`**.

## The borrow (inspire — Apache-2.0 → Apache-2.0, clean-room)
`kt doctor` is a one-shot, operator-facing **"will this model serve here, and optimally?"** report — a table of green/yellow/red rows, each carrying an actionable remediation hint:

- CPU ISA → perf tier + upgrade hint (AMX / AVX512 / AVX2), and a cross-check that the *loaded* kernel variant matches CPU capability: `kt-kernel/python/cli/commands/doctor.py:163,224@0c2912a`.
- GPU count + VRAM, NUMA topology, RAM ≥ threshold, disk ≥ threshold per model path, required package versions: `doctor.py:95-507@0c2912a`.
- A dependency **behavior probe** (is the installed serving fork the required one) by grepping its `--help` for a fork-only flag: `doctor.py:366@0c2912a`, `cli/utils/sglang_checker.py:287@0c2912a`.
- Companion `kt run` auto-derives runtime knobs from detected hardware (threads = 0.8×cores, threadpool = NUMA nodes, TP = #GPUs): `cli/commands/run.py:416-460@0c2912a`.

**Axis (narrow):** a **model-serving hardware/environment preflight** that turns "it crashed / it's slow" into a capability report with fixes — before the model loads.

## fak seam / the gap
fak has a rich **doctor family**, but it is **fleet/agent-ops** focused, not inference-hardware:
- `cmd/fak/doctor.go`, `doctor_mcp.go` (MCP health), `doctor_terminalrisk.go`, `accounts_doctor.go`, `internal/appversion/binarydoctor.go`, `internal/treedoctor` (git tree) — none report CPU ISA tier / VRAM headroom for the target model / NUMA layout as a serve preflight.
- `cmd/fak/serve_backend_preflight.go` — validates the backend **forward-path** compatibility (reads the GGUF header, checks arch↔backend via `ValidateBackendForwardConfig`), but not *hardware capability / perf tier / memory headroom*.
- fak owns the ingredients elsewhere: `internal/compute/cpuref.go` (CPU feature detect), `internal/compute/numa_nodes.go` (NUMA topology), `internal/kvbudget` + `internal/compute/hostfit` (VRAM/host fit). They are **not composed into an operator-facing serve-doctor report**.

Net: **PARTIAL** — the detection primitives exist and a forward-path preflight exists; the **hardware-capability serve-readiness report** (ISA tier, VRAM-for-this-model, NUMA, with remediation) does not.

## Dogfood witness
`gh issue list --search "serve doctor hardware preflight capability"` → empty. Read of `serve_backend_preflight.go` (forward-path only) and the doctor family (fleet-ops). fak's world is a fleet with machine-parseable telemetry, so the framing should be a `--json`-able readiness report, not only a Rich table — but the *capability rows* are the borrow.

## First checkable step
`fak serve --preflight` (or extend the existing backend preflight) that emits, for a given model path + selected backend, a structured readiness report composing existing primitives: `compute/cpuref` ISA tier, `compute/numa_nodes` layout, `kvbudget`/`hostfit` KV+weights vs free memory, and the current forward-path check — each row `ok|warn|error` + a one-line reason. Pure over injected hardware facts so it is unit-witnessable without a GPU (same posture as `kvbudget`).

## Honest scope
- Snapshot `0c2912a`. The dependency-fork `--help` probe is ktransformers-specific (fak has no such external serving fork) — **dropped** as not-applicable.
- Divergent worldview note: ktransformers' whole CLI targets a novice on a single air-gapped box (`~/.ktransformers` state, Rich tables); fak targets fleets. Only the **inference-hardware capability report** slice transfers; the novice-single-box UX does not.

records.title: feat(kvbudget): generalize KV-cache sizing to read attention arch from the model header (MLA/MHA/NSA) instead of the GLM-5.2 hardcode (ktransformers-borrow, sibling #3900)
records.body:
Small sibling leaf of the ktransformers study epic **#3900**. Fresh SHA **`0c2912a`**.

## The borrow (inspire — Apache-2.0 → Apache-2.0, clean-room)
ktransformers' `kv_cache_calculator` computes KV-cache VRAM footprint for **any** model by reading its config and **branching on attention architecture**:
- MLA (DeepSeek-V2/V3): `(kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim) * num_layers * bytes` per token, plus an NSA indexer term when `is_deepseek_nsa`: `kt-kernel/python/cli/utils/kv_cache_calculator.py:86-97@0c2912a`.
- MHA: `num_kv_heads * (head_dim + v_head_dim) * num_layers * bytes`: `kv_cache_calculator.py:121@0c2912a`.
- × `max_total_tokens` → GB, from the loaded `ModelConfig` (`get_kv_size_gb`, `:34`).

**Axis (narrow):** **model-agnostic** KV-cache sizing driven by the model header's attention arch, not a per-model constant.

## fak seam / the gap
`internal/kvbudget/kvbudget.go` already computes MLA+DSA KV bytes/token and max concurrent streams — rigorously and doc-witnessed — **but hardcodes GLM-5.2 estimates**:
- `GLM52DSA = Shape{Layers:92, KVLoraRank:512, QKRopeHeadDim:64, IndexHeadDim:128}` are marked `ESTIMATE` "until Lane F pins the real GGUF header" (lines 81-87).
- The package deliberately does **not** import `internal/model` and does not read any header — it carries the constants inline (see package doc, lines 30-41).

Net: **PARTIAL** — fak's KV-sizing math is present and arguably more rigorous (MLA latent + decoupled rope + DSA indexer, `MLAElemsPerToken`/`KVElemsPerToken`), but it is **GLM-5.2-specific**; it cannot size an arbitrary served model, and its numbers are estimates rather than the loaded header. ktransformers' contribution is the **general branch over attention arch read from the config**.

## Dogfood witness
Read of `kvbudget.go` (GLM52DSA hardcode, `ESTIMATE` markers) vs `kv_cache_calculator.py` (reads `ModelConfig`, branches MLA/MHA/NSA). fak already has the header source: `internal/model/config.go` exposes `NumLayers`/`KVLoraRank`/`QKRopeHeadDim`/`IndexHeadDim` (kvbudget's own doc says its `Shape` "mirror[s] model.Config"). The wire is unbuilt.

## First checkable step
Add `kvbudget.ShapeFromConfig(cfg)` in a small adapter (kept out of the pure package, or via an interface so `kvbudget` stays import-light) that populates `Shape` from a real `model.Config` and selects an MLA-vs-MHA element formula by the config's attention kind — replacing the `GLM52DSA` estimate at the call site with the header's actual values. Witness: the GLM-5.2 GGUF header reproduces (or corrects) the doc's estimated cells.

## Honest scope
- Snapshot `0c2912a`. Low-risk, high-leverage: it turns a single-model calculator into a general one using values fak already parses.
- Keep the pure/laptop-composable property of `kvbudget` — the adapter, not the math, takes the `model` dependency.

records.title: epic(net-toks): multi-agent net tokens/sec on slow SSD-offloaded MoE via cross-agent expert coalescing
records.body:
## Epic — Net tokens/sec on a slow SSD-offloaded MoE via cross-agent expert coalescing

**Thesis.** On a frontier MoE (GLM-5.2, 753 B, 256 experts, K=8) whose routed experts stream
from SSD, the *single-agent* decode rate is bandwidth-bound and "slow" (sub-1 tok/s CPU-offload;
0.243 tok/s WITNESSED GPU server 2 CPU-only). That is the **wrong meter** for a fleet. With **B
concurrent agents**, their per-step top-K expert selections **coalesce**: the union `U(B)` of
experts a batch touches is far smaller than `B·K`, so each SSD-streamed expert serves many agents
at once. SSD bytes *per agent-token* fall as B grows, per-agent tok/s holds or rises, and
**aggregate net tok/s scales with B** — 4–10×+ over B independent un-coalesced streams — until the
working set becomes fully resident and the box rides its ordinary RAM/compute roofline.

Full model, roofline, and the measured-vs-projected labelling:
[`docs/notes/MOE-SSD-MULTI-AGENT-NET-TOKS-2026-07-18.md`](../blob/main/docs/notes/MOE-SSD-MULTI-AGENT-NET-TOKS-2026-07-18.md).

### The three compounding levers

- **L1 — weight-stream amortization** (dense): the RAM-resident non-routed band, one stream over B rows. **WITNESSED** (`internal/model/batch.go`, MODEL-BATCHING-RESULTS.md).
- **L2 — cross-agent expert coalescing** (the new lever): B agents' top-K unions to `U(B) ≪ B·K`. **NOT BUILT.** Intra-agent analogue is #4355; single-stream trace is `deepseekv4moe.SimulateExpertCache`.
- **L3 — cross-agent prefix KV reuse**: shared system prompt / tools / repo computed once. **WITNESSED** mechanism (`internal/radixkv`, #1535).

### Scope guard (load-bearing)

This is an **inference-throughput** claim (aggregate decode tok/s under batching), the same axis
as MODEL-BATCHING-RESULTS.md. It is **NOT** the agent-orchestration concurrency metric of
`docs/explainers/ultracode-multi-agent-dogfood.md` (a wall-clock concurrency factor N with an
Amdahl ceiling over *deliverables*). Per that doc's rule the two multiples **must never be
blended.** Every child ticket keeps net-tok/s in the inference family and cites its baseline
(vs B un-coalesced streams — the honest headline; never bare aggregate-over-latency).

### Children (decompose, don't dispatch the epic)

- **A** — `SimulateExpertCacheBatch`: cross-agent coalescing simulator (pure Go). **top**
- **B** — net-tok/s replay bench: B=1…128 curve + coalescing ratio `C(B)=(B·K)/U(B)`. **top**
- **C** — coalescing ratio + effective-bytes/token as an admission/telemetry metric; wire to `fak serve --plan-json` (#4361).
- **D** — fused grouped-GEMM over the coalesced resident expert union + serial-parity test.
- **E** — L2×L3 compounding proof (shared prefix computed once AND experts coalesced).
- **F** — routing-skew model: real GLM-5.2 top-K load is non-uniform → `U(B)` grows slower than uniform (the coalescing is *better* than the uniform bound).
- **G** — per-user ⊗ cross-user batching composition note + non-overlap statement (the hyperscaler stacking).
- **H** — witness the coalescing ratio on **real** GLM-5.2 routing traces (operator/hardware-gated).
- **I** — SSD-offload net-tok/s demo cell for the #4762 browser demo (aggregate climbs with B, per-agent flat).

A and B are the spine: they turn the projected coalescing curve into a **witnessed, deterministic,
zero-hardware** one. Everything downstream rests on the number they produce.

### Prior art (do not re-derive)

`internal/deepseekv4moe/cache_trace.go` (single-stream trace) · #4355 (intra-agent draft/verify
union) · `internal/stripeload` #4298/#2722 (SSD read path) · #4359 (readahead) · #4357 (residency
policy) · `internal/radixkv` #1535 (L3) · MODEL-BATCHING-RESULTS.md (L1) · colibri epic #4352 ·
demo epic #4762.

### Child issue tracker

- [ ] #5244 — **A** SimulateExpertCacheBatch (L2 spine, dispatchable) **top**
- [ ] #5245 — **B** coalescebench net-tok/s(B) curve (dispatchable) **top**
- [ ] #5246 — **C** coalescing metric + `--plan-json`
- [ ] #5247 — **D** fused grouped-GEMM over coalesced union (CPU path dispatchable; GPU gated)
- [ ] #5248 — **E** L2×L3 compounding proof
- [ ] #5249 — **F** routing-skew model
- [ ] #5250 — **G** per-user ⊗ cross-user composition note
- [ ] #5251 — **H** real GLM-5.2 trace witness (operator-gated)
- [ ] #5252 — **I** #4762 demo cell

records.title: feat(moe): SimulateExpertCacheBatch — cross-agent expert-cache coalescing simulator (L2 spine)
records.body:
Epic: #5243. Design: `docs/notes/MOE-SSD-MULTI-AGENT-NET-TOKS-2026-07-18.md`.

## What

Add a **cross-agent** expert-cache coalescing simulator to `internal/deepseekv4moe`, a sibling to
the existing single-stream `SimulateExpertCache` (`cache_trace.go`). Where `SimulateExpertCache`
replays one agent's sequential per-token top-K route against a resident set, the new
`SimulateExpertCacheBatch` replays **B agents advancing one decode step together** and streams
each *distinct* (layer, expert) group **once per step**, however many agents in the batch routed
to it.

## Why

This is lever **L2** of the epic — the reason a *MoE* box scales differently from a dense box.
A dense batch amortizes one fixed weight stream; an MoE batch additionally **shrinks its own SSD
working set** as it grows, because `U(B)` (distinct experts a B-agent step touches) grows
sublinearly in B (bounded by `N`, concentrated by routing skew). Today nothing in the repo
models that. #4355 is the *intra-agent* draft/verify union — this is the cross-**agent** sibling.

## API (proposed — refine in review)

```go
// BatchStep is the per-layer top-K selection of every agent in the batch for one decode step.
type BatchStep struct {
    Layer   int
    PerAgent [][]int // PerAgent[b] = the topK expert ids agent b selected at this layer/step
}

type BatchCoalesceTrace struct {
    Hits, Misses      int64   // resident-set hits/misses over DISTINCT (layer,expert) groups
    DistinctStreamed  int64   // Σ over steps of |U_step| actually paged in (the SSD stream)
    NaiveStreamed     int64   // Σ over steps of Σ_b K  (B independent un-coalesced streams)
    CoalesceRatio     float64 // NaiveStreamed / DistinctStreamed  == mean (B·K)/U(B)
    PeakResident      int
}

func SimulateExpertCacheBatch(steps []BatchStep, capacity, layers, expertsPerLayer, topK, agents int) (BatchCoalesceTrace, error)
```

Keep it **weight-free and deterministic** exactly like `SimulateExpertCache` — it proves neither
model I/O nor dequant/GPU exec nor latency; it counts distinct-group page-ins under a stated
capacity. Reuse the same `ExpertGroup`/`groupLess` ordering and the same LRU/resident-set
structure so the single-agent case (`agents==1`) is bit-identical to `SimulateExpertCache`.

## DoD

- [ ] `SimulateExpertCacheBatch` lands in `internal/deepseekv4moe`, deterministic, allocation-conscious.
- [ ] Table test: `agents==1` reproduces `SimulateExpertCache` Hits/Misses/PeakResident exactly.
- [ ] Table test: full-overlap batch (all B agents pick the same K each step) → `DistinctStreamed == single-agent`, `CoalesceRatio == B`.
- [ ] Table test: disjoint batch (no two agents share an expert, `B·K ≤ N`) → `CoalesceRatio == 1`, `DistinctStreamed == NaiveStreamed`.
- [ ] Table test: partial overlap with a fixed synthetic route → asserted exact `CoalesceRatio`.
- [ ] `AdmitExpertCacheTrace` sibling (or an option) that fails closed when the *batch* peak working set exceeds cache (one full B-agent step's union must fit), mirroring `ErrRouteWorkingSetExceedsCache`.
- [ ] `internal/deepseekv4moe` stays tier-declared (it already is); no new leaf.

## Files

`internal/deepseekv4moe/cache_trace.go` (+ new `cache_trace_batch.go`), `cache_admission.go`,
`*_test.go`. Pure Go, CPU-only, **no hardware gate** — this is the spine ticket.

records.title: feat(bench): coalescebench — net-tok/s(B) curve + coalescing ratio for SSD-offloaded MoE
records.body:
Epic: #5243. Design: `docs/notes/MOE-SSD-MULTI-AGENT-NET-TOKS-2026-07-18.md` §2. Depends on: A (`SimulateExpertCacheBatch`).

## What

A deterministic replay bench (new `cmd/coalescebench`, mirroring `cmd/batchbench`) that drives
the cross-agent coalescing simulator over synthetic (and later real, #H) GLM-5.2-shaped routing
traces at **B = 1, 4, 16, 64, 128** and emits the **net-tok/s(B) curve** plus the coalescing
ratio `C(B) = (B·K)/U(B)`, applying the §2 roofline:

```
t_agent(B) = max( SSD_term(B), RAM_term, FLOP_term )
net_toks(B) = B / t_agent(B)
SSD_term(B) = (DistinctStreamed_per_step · expert_bytes) / (B · BW_ssd)
```

Bench inputs (`BW_ssd`, `BW_ram`, `expert_bytes`, `NR`, K, N, L) are **flags with GLM-5.2
header-derived defaults** cited to `GLM52-DGX-THEORETICAL-CEILING`; every emitted row is labelled
**PROJECTED** (roofline, not a served measurement) except a future `--trace` mode fed by #H.

## Why

Turns the epic's projected coalescing curve into a **witnessed, deterministic, zero-hardware**
number — the table the demo (#I), the metric (#C), and the honest headline all rest on. Reports
the two baselines from §2.1 side by side so the 4–10×+ is never stated without its denominator:
`× vs B un-coalesced streams` (the defensible headline) and `× vs single-agent latency` (labelled
aggregate/latency-tolerant only).

## DoD

- [ ] `cmd/coalescebench` prints a markdown table: `B | U(B) | C(B) | SSD_term | net_toks | ×vs-uncoalesced | ×vs-1agent | binding-roofline`.
- [ ] A synthetic router with a tunable skew knob (uniform → Zipf) so `U(B)` growth is inspectable; default skew cites a source or is labelled a placeholder.
- [ ] The regime transition (B* where `SSD_term` drops below `RAM_term` → the box goes effectively resident) is detected and printed.
- [ ] Determinism test in `cmd/coalescebench` (or `internal/`): same seed/flags → identical table (no `Math.random`/time).
- [ ] A `docs/benchmarks/` results note with the projected curve, every cell labelled, and the explicit statement that it is a roofline pending #H's real-trace witness.
- [ ] New leaf `coalescebench` gets its architest tier row (`TestEveryPackageDeclaresTier`) and, if import-free at root, `pureRoot`.

## Files

`cmd/coalescebench/` (new), `docs/benchmarks/COALESCE-NET-TOKS-RESULTS.md` (new), architest tier
row. CPU-only, **no hardware gate**.

records.title: feat(serve): coalescing ratio + effective-bytes/token as admission/telemetry; wire to --plan-json
records.body:
Epic: #5243. Design: `docs/notes/MOE-SSD-MULTI-AGENT-NET-TOKS-2026-07-18.md` §2, §4. Depends on: A.

## What

Promote the coalescing ratio `C(B)` and the **effective-bytes-per-agent-token** `= (NR + U(B)·e)/B`
from bench-only quantities into first-class **admission + telemetry** on the serving path, so the
planner can choose a batch size B and an expert-cache capacity together, and `fak serve --plan-json`
(the #4361 memory-plan dry-run) reports the projected net-tok/s regime before commit.

## Why

L2 only pays off if the runtime *knows* the coalescing it is getting. Without a metric, the
planner sizes the expert cache for the single-stream working set and never batches into the
resident-transition regime (§2 — the B* where SSD drops out). This ticket is the seam that lets
`fak serve` pick B on the resident/roofline transition instead of guessing.

## DoD

- [ ] `BatchCoalesceTrace` (from A) exposes `EffectiveBytesPerAgentToken(NR, expertBytes)` and `CoalesceRatio`.
- [ ] `fak serve --plan-json` gains a `coalescing` block: `{ batch_B, distinct_experts_per_step, coalesce_ratio, effective_bytes_per_agent_token, ssd_bound, ram_bound, projected_regime }`, all header-derived, allocation-free (same discipline as #4361).
- [ ] The block is labelled PROJECTED and never blended with any orchestration metric (epic scope guard).
- [ ] A test asserting the plan JSON round-trips and the regime flips from `ssd_bound` to `ram_bound` as B crosses B*.

## Files

`internal/deepseekv4moe`, the `fak serve --plan-json` command path, `*_test.go`. No hardware gate.

records.title: perf(moe): fused grouped-GEMM over the coalesced resident expert union + serial-parity
records.body:
Epic: #5243. Design: `docs/notes/MOE-SSD-MULTI-AGENT-NET-TOKS-2026-07-18.md` L1×L2. Sibling: #4355.

## What

The **fusion** half of the epic. Once a B-agent decode step's coalesced expert union `U(B)` is
resident, execute those experts as **one fused grouped GEMM** over the `(expert × agent-rows)`
panel — each resident expert consumed by all agents in the batch that routed to it, in a single
kernel — instead of per-agent, per-expert GEMV calls. This is the MoE analogue of the dense
`matMulBatch` in `internal/model/batch.go` (L1), applied to the routed stream.

## Why

Coalescing (L2) makes the working set small; **fusion makes executing it cheap** — it amortizes
kernel launch, weight-tile movement, and dequant over the whole batch's routing to each expert.
Without it the coalesced union is still walked per-agent and the SSD win is partly given back at
the compute/launch layer.

## DoD

- [ ] A CPU grouped-GEMM path that, given the resident expert set and per-expert agent-row lists, produces per-agent expert outputs in one pass.
- [ ] **Serial-parity test**: fused grouped-GEMM output is bit-identical (f32) / cosine-gated (quant) to per-agent serial expert application, mirroring `TestBatchedDecodeMatchesSerial`.
- [ ] The GPU kernel is scoped as a **follow-on** and explicitly hardware-gated (8-GPU DGX, ties #4784/#4843); this ticket ships the CPU path + parity.

## Files

`internal/deepseekv4moe`, `internal/model` (grouped-GEMM helper), `*_test.go`. CPU path
dispatchable; GPU follow-on gated.

records.title: feat(bench): L2xL3 compounding proof — shared-prefix reuse times expert coalescing per turn
records.body:
Epic: #5243. Design: `docs/notes/MOE-SSD-MULTI-AGENT-NET-TOKS-2026-07-18.md` §1 (L2×L3). Depends on: A, B.

## What

Show the two witnessed-mechanism levers **compound**: the shared prefix (L3, `internal/radixkv`,
computed once for all B agents) AND the coalesced routed stream (L2). Extend the replay bench (B)
with a prefill term so the reported net effect over an agent *turn* (prefill + decode) folds both:
`saved = prefix_tokens·(B−1)` reads deleted (L3) **times** the decode coalescing gain (L2).

## Why

The fleet workload's real unit is a *turn*, not a decode step. L3 deletes duplicated prefill work
(`agents × turns × working-set × reread-rate`, SCALING-LAWS); L2 shrinks the decode SSD stream.
They act on different phases, so they multiply — this ticket quantifies the product and keeps it
honest (both cited to their witnessed mechanism, not asserted).

## DoD

- [ ] Bench (B) gains `--prefix-tokens` and reports prefill-reads-avoided (L3) alongside decode net-tok/s (L2), and the combined per-turn effect.
- [ ] A short results section tying the L3 number to an existing radixkv reuse witness (do not re-derive the prefix mechanism).
- [ ] The compound number states both baselines explicitly; no blending with orchestration concurrency.

## Files

`cmd/coalescebench`, `docs/benchmarks/COALESCE-NET-TOKS-RESULTS.md`, radixkv citation. No hardware gate.

records.title: research(moe): routing-skew model — U(B) grows slower than uniform, bounding the coalescing ratio
records.body:
Epic: #5243. Design: `docs/notes/MOE-SSD-MULTI-AGENT-NET-TOKS-2026-07-18.md` §2. Depends on: A, B.

## What

Model the **routing skew** that makes coalescing *better than the uniform bound*. A real MoE
router does not spread top-K uniformly over N experts — some experts are hot. Under skew, the
distinct-expert union `U(B)` grows **slower** than the uniform expectation, so the coalescing
ratio `C(B)` is **higher** than a uniform model predicts. Give the bench (B) a skew knob (uniform
→ Zipf(s)) and derive `E[U(B)]` for the skewed selection so the projected curve has a defensible
lower and upper bound.

## Why

The uniform assumption **understates** the L2 advantage — but an unlabelled optimistic skew would
overstate it. This ticket pins the honest interval: `C(B)` under uniform (conservative) vs a cited
router-load distribution (realistic), so the epic's 4–10×+ claim carries an explicit assumption
and is falsifiable by #H's real trace.

## DoD

- [ ] Closed-form or exact-simulated `E[U(B)]` for uniform and Zipf(s) selection at (N, K, B).
- [ ] Bench emits `C(B)` for both, side by side, each labelled with its distribution assumption.
- [ ] Test asserting the uniform `E[U(B)]` matches the classic coupon/occupancy expectation for small (N,K,B).
- [ ] Doc note: skew makes coalescing better; the honest headline uses the **conservative** (uniform or measured-whichever-lower) number.

## Files

`cmd/coalescebench`, `internal/deepseekv4moe` (or a small `internal/` stats helper), `*_test.go`,
`docs/benchmarks/COALESCE-NET-TOKS-RESULTS.md`. No hardware gate.

records.title: docs(serve): per-user coalesced batch times cross-user continuous batching — composition + non-overlap
records.body:
Epic: #5243. Design: `docs/notes/MOE-SSD-MULTI-AGENT-NET-TOKS-2026-07-18.md` §3.

## What

A short design/framing note stating precisely how the **per-user** coalesced batch composes with
**cross-user** continuous batching in a hyperscaler, and — the load-bearing part — the
**non-overlap**: the two do not compete, the per-user coalesced batch is itself one contributor to
the machine-wide batch. Machine net-tok/s `= (per-user coalesced) ⊗ (cross-user batch)` up to the
SSD/compute roofline.

## Why

The epic's "in theory this is per user, so in a hyperscaler the rest of batching applies too"
claim needs to be made honestly and without double-counting. fak owns the per-user, in-kernel,
trust-scoped half (per-user `Evict`/`Clone` KV survives batching, MODEL-BATCHING-RESULTS.md); the
cross-user half is the standard serving stack's job. The note draws that line so the multiples are
never multiplied twice or blended with orchestration concurrency.

## DoD

- [ ] `docs/notes/` (or `docs/`) note: the ⊗ composition, what fak owns vs the serving stack, and the explicit "do not double-count / do not blend" rule.
- [ ] Cites MODEL-BATCHING-RESULTS.md (per-user KV survives batching) and the epic roofline.
- [ ] Links from the epic doc's §3.

## Files

`docs/notes/`. Doc-only, no hardware gate.
