records.title: fix(commitlane): auto-reap a stale bare .git/index.lock left by a dead raw-git holder (recurring fleet-wide commit wedge)
records.body:
## Symptom

Recurring **fleet-wide commit outage**: for 10–15+ minutes at a stretch, `HEAD` goes static, `git log --since='3 minutes ago'` shows **0 commits across the whole fleet**, and every `fak commit` returns `LOCK_BUSY` (`another git process is active (index.lock held Ns); retry shortly`). Polite spaced retries starve — dozens of workers all block on the same held lock.

## Evidence (observed twice in one session)

- `.git/index.lock` held **512s**, then later **713s**, by a holder that was **already dead** — no live `git.exe` process was anywhere near that age (verified via process start-times; newest real git PIDs were 0–1s reads, the rest 15h-idle daemons).
- Throughout, `.git/fak-commit.lock` churned young (1–16s) — peers were *trying* and failing, not holding.
- Each wedge eventually cleared on its own (HEAD advanced again), but only after the multi-minute outage.

## Root cause: a bare `index.lock` is never auto-reaped

The fleet reaps the *other* lock classes but deliberately not this one:
- `internal/treedoctor` reaps a **dead-holder `fak-commit.lock`** and renamed-aside **`.lock.orphan`** residue only. Its own invariant (`treedoctor.go`): *an active git lock ends in exactly `.lock` (`index.lock`, …), so a name carrying `.lock.orphan` is provably NOT a lock git holds* — i.e. a **bare `index.lock` is conservatively skipped**.
- `internal/commitlane/status.go` `DefaultStaleIndexAge = 15m` only sets `StaleHint` on the **operator surface** — it triggers no auto-clear.
- The `leaseref` reaper keys on a **holder PID**, which git's `index.lock` does not carry.

So when a *raw* `git` subprocess (not `fak-commit`) dies holding `index.lock`, nothing recovers it until a human/operator intervenes or it happens to clear.

## Why this is safely fixable

git writes `index.lock` with `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` — a **plain leftover file**, no OS-level lock (unlike `fak-commit.lock`'s Windows `LockFileEx`). A stale one is just a stale file. treedoctor already owns the safe "rename-aside to `*.lock.orphan-recovered-<n>` then reap residue" pattern.

## Proposal

Extend `fak dev tree-doctor --apply` (and/or the commit-lane maintenance tick) to recover a bare `.git/index.lock` when **both**:
1. age ≥ a conservative threshold (reuse `DefaultStaleIndexAge = 15m`), **and**
2. a liveness gate shows no committer is actually mid-write (e.g. no live `fak-commit` lease holder + no advancing HEAD),

by renaming it aside to the existing `index.lock.orphan-recovered-<n>` residue form (which the current residue reaper then removes). Report-only by default; only `--apply` acts.

Impact: turns a 10–15min recurring fleet-wide commit stall into a self-healing event, and is the same delicate contention/wedge class the always-on loop keeps hitting.

records.title: perf(compaction): repeated shell tool-result spans are the dominant post-compaction regrowth class (66%, 296 windows)
records.body:
## Context

Child of #4768 (parent #4763). The 2026-07-18 regrowth attribution witness (`internal/session/testdata/compactaudit/regrowth-witness-2026-07-18.md`) decomposed 1.55 GB of transcript rows appended across 1,510 post-compaction windows in native Codex sessions:

- `tool_result/shell_command` alone is **1,032,156,451 bytes — 66.4% of all regrowth**, across 223,643 rows.
- **296 of 1,510 windows (19.6%) carry byte-identical repeated tool-result spans** (`REPEATED_TOOL_RESULT`), 12.5 MB duplicated under different call ids — the same output re-entering the window it was just compacted out of.
- The fast (<=30 min) rebound cohort runs the same median tool-call volume as the slow cohort (170 vs 172), so this is not excess tool use; it is retention of repeated result bytes.

## Problem

Two thirds of the 22-minute rebound from 25k back to 200k resident tokens is shell tool output, and a fifth of windows re-append spans that are byte-identical to output already seen. Deduplicating or referencing repeated result spans (rather than re-retaining them) is the highest-leverage regrowth cut that does not touch useful work.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Decide the mechanism (e.g. hash-referenced repeated tool-result bodies, bounded re-emission, or shedder-side dedup) with a design note.
- [ ] Implement behind the existing session/compaction seam; no tool-output bodies persisted in receipts.
- [ ] Witness: re-run `fak session compact-audit --since <date> --json --scrub --aggregate-only` and show `REPEATED_TOOL_RESULT` window share and `tool_result/*` dup_bytes materially reduced on new sessions.

Related: #4768 (attribution parent), #3071 (suffix recreation — the compaction_summary class stays there), #2785 (cache-creation pricing).

records.title: perf(compaction): instruction/setup payload re-injected after fires is 71% duplicated bytes (85 windows)
records.body:
## Context

Child of #4768 (parent #4763). The 2026-07-18 regrowth attribution witness (`internal/session/testdata/compactaudit/regrowth-witness-2026-07-18.md`) found the `instructions` class (reinjected `<user_instructions>` / `<environment_context>` / skill payloads) is small in absolute bytes but almost entirely duplication:

- 4,743,754 bytes across 325 rows in post-fire windows, of which **3,390,235 bytes (71%) in 134 rows are byte-identical to instruction payloads already present earlier in the same session** (`DUPLICATE_SETUP_REINJECTION` in 85 of 1,510 windows).
- `message/developer` and `message/user` reinjection show the same pattern at trace levels.

## Problem

Invariant setup re-enters the window after compaction as a byte-identical copy. Unlike tool output, this class is pure re-statement: every duplicated byte is context the model already had, re-paid on every request until the next fire.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Identify the injector(s) that re-emit identical instruction payloads post-compaction (Codex-side reinjection vs harness skill payloads), with row-hash evidence.
- [ ] Deduplicate or reference the payload instead of re-appending it, preserving the invariant the reinjection exists to guarantee.
- [ ] Witness: `DUPLICATE_SETUP_REINJECTION` window count and `instructions` dup_bytes drop on new sessions in the compact-audit aggregate.

Related: #4768 (attribution parent), #2638 (repeated past-compact nudges).

records.title: epic(tensorrt-llm-study): mine NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM for fak — witnessed borrows (adaptive spec gate, no-evict admission, per-request KV retention, block-hash cache events)
records.body:
## epic(tensorrt-llm-study): mine NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM for fak — witnessed borrows

A `/study --deep` pass over **NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM** (`https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM`, pinned `@f4c5c935aa891b0826f73936c4831236cb6ff836`, "Consolidate test coverage for helix (#16570)"). Child of the superset epic #2236 (fak > best of vLLM + SGLang + Dynamo + TRT-LLM), sibling of the other study epics (#3983 kvcache-factory, #3900 ktransformers, #3366 lmcache, #4352 colibri, #4207 inference-radar, #4040 claude-code).

**Worldview (reconstructed from defaults/non-goals/benchmarks).** TensorRT-LLM serves **NVIDIA-GPU production at maximum throughput/latency** via *compiled* engines plus hand-tuned CUDA kernels. Every scheduling/policy choice serves peak hardware utilization of a **token-serving** fleet: the default capacity policy is `kGUARANTEED_NO_EVICT` (a started request never stalls mid-decode), the dynamic batch tuner reshapes the batch to the live ISL/OSL mix, and speculation self-disables when it stops paying. fak's world is different — an **agent-orchestration substrate** that fronts (often third-party) engines and optimizes *cross-agent* cache economics and *fleet* liveness. So the borrows are the **CPU-witnessable POLICY/CONTROL ideas** (gating, admission math, retention vocabulary, event granularity), not the kernel/engine-compilation stack. Pure-kernel items (attention/GEMM `.cu`, CUTLASS, deep_gemm/flash_mla, the un-checked-out `cubins/`) are routed to the `sota-check` lane, not here.

**Fan-out coverage (6 sub-readers, all verified against the tree):** batch_manager scheduling (capacity/microBatch/pause/dynamicBatchTuner), kvCacheManager + evictionPolicy + blockKey + kvCacheEventManager, executor API surface, speculative (`_torch/speculative`), disaggregation (P/D transceiver/formatter), quantization + autotuner + auto_deploy + mapping + watchdogs. Full candidate table + all citations in `docs/notes/CONCEPT-STUDY-TENSORRT-LLM-2026-07-18.md`.

### Child leaves (ship-alone, CPU-witnessable)

1. **Adaptive acceptance-rate speculation gate on `SpecDecode`** — fak's spec loop measures `MeanAcceptanceLength` but never acts; borrow TRT-LLM's rolling-window accept-rate gate + load gate + batch-size draft-length schedule.
2. **Guaranteed-no-evict admission for concurrent decode streams** — fak's `kvbudget` sizes streams-that-fit but has no admission gate that reserves worst-case blocks-to-completion so an admitted stream never evicts mid-decode.
3. **Client-declared per-request KV retention (priority + TTL window) feeding `radixkv` eviction** — fak's victim rule is telemetry-only (hits/recency/cost); borrow the (priority 0-100, durationMs) per-token-range retention config + TTL demotion + context-vs-decode split.
4. **Per-block-hash KV cache event stream (tier-move + priority diffs) for prefix-aware routing** — fak's `cacheevents` are aggregate metrics and `residency_router` tracks resident/dropped only; borrow the created/stored/removed/**updated**(cacheLevel/priority diff) block-hash events so the router knows *which tier* and *how hot*.

### Note-only residue (see study note; not auto-decomposed — "we don't do everything")
- **DIVERGENT (stated tradeoff):** relaxed/approximate acceptance in the thinking span (`mtp.py:807`) — fak sells *lossless byte-identical* spec decode; cross-topology KV reshaping and the `auto_deploy` compiled-engine pipeline — fak fronts engines, it does not compile them.
- **sota-check route (kernel-adjacent):** the persistent, device-capability+version-stamped, shape-bucketed **autotune-decision cache** with atomic+locked writes and an `exclude_from_cache` JIT-warmup opt-out (`autotuner.py`).
- **Fold into existing epics:** prefix-reuse-aware admission *deferral* (`beneficialToSkip`) → coalescing epic #5243; the typed prefill→decode handoff token (`ContextPhaseParams` + `disaggRequestId`) → disagg epic #50 / session-migration #3352; dynamic batch tuner + TTFT reordering → dispatch load-signal epic #3365.
- **PRESENT-on-axis (witnessed, dropped):** SGLang-style pluggable victim registry / SLRU (`radixkv/eviction_strategy.go`), per-namespace reuse isolation = cacheSalt (`radixkv/namespace.go`), cache-event→prefix-aware fleet routing skeleton (`gateway/residency_router.go`), lossless greedy spec-decode loop (`polymodel/specdecode.go`).

License: TensorRT-LLM is Apache-2.0 (LICENSE read). All borrows are **INSPIRE** (clean-room, cited); no bytes vendored.

records.title: feat(polymodel): adaptive acceptance-rate gate for the SpecDecode loop — stop drafting when it stops paying (epic #5256)
records.body:
## feat(polymodel): adaptive acceptance-rate gate for the SpecDecode loop — stop drafting when it stops paying

**Study borrow from NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM `@f4c5c935` (Apache-2.0, INSPIRE / clean-room). Epic #5256 (tensorrt-llm-study).**

### The axis
Adaptive **acceptance-rate-gated speculation**: track a rolling-window average of the *real* per-iteration draft acceptance rate and turn speculation OFF when it falls below a threshold, so a draft model that mispredicts on this workload cannot make decoding net-negative (extra verify cost, few accepts). Two companion gates ride the same seam: a **load gate** (speculate only when the batch is small enough that the target isn't already compute-bound) and a **batch-size→draft-length schedule** (shrink K, down to 0, as concurrency grows).

### Source (code I read)
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/speculative/speculation_gate.py:33-82@f4c5c935` — `SpeculationGate`: an O(1) rolling-sum `deque`; once `window` samples exist, if `acceptance_rate_sum/len < threshold` it sets a **permanent one-way disable**. Metric fed at `tensorrt_llm/_torch/pyexecutor/py_executor.py:2206@f4c5c935` (`acceptance_rate = total_accepted_tokens / total_draft_tokens`).
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/speculative/drafter.py:41-65@f4c5c935` — `should_use_spec_decode`: disable when effective concurrent requests exceed `max_concurrency`.
- `tensorrt_llm/_torch/speculative/drafter.py:106-134@f4c5c935` — `get_draft_len_for_batch_size`: `bisect_right` over a `{batch_threshold: draft_len}` schedule (entry `0` disables).

### fak seam (where it lands)
`internal/polymodel/specdecode.go` — `SpecDecodeRun` already computes `MeanAcceptanceLength` and `AcceptedDrafts`/`DraftedTokens` (the exact metric the gate needs) but the loop **always drafts** whenever a `Drafter` is bound; there is no adaptive control action. Add a pure gate that consumes the per-round acceptance already tracked and returns a draft/no-draft (or a K) decision. Because `specdecode.go` is a tier-1 leaf that imports nothing internal, the gate stays pure control-structure and the host binds the thresholds.

### Witness (dogfood + raw grep)
- `mcp__fak__fak_feature_query "adaptive speculative decoding gate: disable speculation when acceptance rate falls below threshold"` → ranker returns the whole index (unusable inline; noted honest-limit).
- Raw `Grep` over `*.go` for `speculation.?gate|disable.{0,15}spec|accept.{0,10}rate` — the only accept-rate uses are **measurement** (`polymodel.EffectiveTokensPerVerify`, `cmd/polymodelbench`) and `SpecDecodeRun.MeanAcceptanceLength`; the only "spec disabled" is a shell-script env echo. No rolling-window gate, no load gate, no dynamic-K. Witnessed **ABSENT** (control action) twice, varied phrasing.
- Dedup: #4102/#4106 are **tool-call** speculation (the assumption ledger — a different axis, agent tool calls not token draft/verify); #23 is the original spec-decode ride. None gate the token loop on acceptance.

### Verdict
**PARTIAL → FILE (INSPIRE).** fak has the lossless loop and the measurement; it lacks the adaptive control that makes speculation safe-by-default.

### First checkable step
Add `AcceptanceGate` to `internal/polymodel` (pure: `Record(accepted, drafted int) (draft bool)` over a fixed window + threshold) with a table test proving: (a) below-threshold accept over a full window flips to no-draft; (b) it is byte-output-identical to today's loop while enabled (losslessness preserved — the gate only changes *whether* we draft, never *what we commit*). Then wire it as an optional field on `SpecDecodeConfig`.

records.title: feat(kvbudget): guaranteed-no-evict admission — reserve worst-case blocks-to-completion before admitting a decode stream (epic #5256)
records.body:
## feat(kvbudget): guaranteed-no-evict admission — reserve worst-case blocks-to-completion before admitting a decode stream

**Study borrow from NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM `@f4c5c935` (Apache-2.0, INSPIRE / clean-room). Epic #5256 (tensorrt-llm-study).**

### The axis
**Capacity-based admission with a no-evict guarantee**: admit a new decode stream only if the KV blocks needed to drive *every already-running* stream to completion **plus** this stream's own worst-case blocks all fit the free pool — so a stream, once started, never gets evicted/paused mid-decode. The budget is on the *maximum* length a request can reach (`prompt + maxNewTokens`), not its current length.

### Source (code I read)
- `cpp/tensorrt_llm/batch_manager/capacityScheduler.cpp:397-427@f4c5c935` — the `GuaranteedNoEvict` admission loop: check `reservedBlocks.enoughAvailableBlocks`, `commitBlocks`, and `break` on the first request that doesn't fit; running requests pre-reserved to completion at `:277-291`.
- `cpp/tensorrt_llm/batch_manager/kvCacheManager.cpp:3550-3589@f4c5c935` — the worst-case math: `numTotalBlocksPerBeam = ceilDiv(min(promptLen + maxNewTokens, ...))`, minus already-allocated, minus *ref-held* reusable blocks (free cached blocks deliberately **not** double-subtracted, `:3579-3585`).
- Policy enum `cpp/include/tensorrt_llm/executor/types.h:219-233@f4c5c935` (`kGUARANTEED_NO_EVICT` is the default, `executor.h:1023`); its foil `kMAX_UTILIZATION` pays for utilization with LIFO pause/resume (`capacityScheduler.cpp:561-587`).

### fak seam (where it lands)
`internal/kvbudget/kvbudget.go` — a pure, GPU-free calculator that already returns **KV GiB/stream and max concurrent streams that fit** a VRAM budget for GLM-5.2 MLA+DSA decode (issue #3080 / epic #3809's many-agent serving case). It computes the *static* ceiling but has **no per-request admission verdict**: nothing reserves each running stream's worst-case remaining blocks so a newly-admitted stream can't force a mid-decode eviction. Add an `Admit(running []Stream, candidate Stream, freeBudget) (ok bool, reason)` on top of the existing sizing.

### Witness (dogfood + raw grep)
- Raw `Grep` for `worst.?case|blocks?.to.?completion|reserve.{0,15}completion|guaranteed.?no.?evict|run.?to.?completion` over `*.go`: no per-request no-evict admission; `kvbudget` sizes, `dispatchtick/footprint_ceiling.go` admits on **OS process footprint** (handles/threads/ws), a different resource; `gateway/gateway_admit.go` is request-shape admission, not KV-block reservation.
- `internal/engine/capacity_*.go` price DRAM/disk/far capacity tiers, not a no-evict reservation over concurrent decode streams.
- Witnessed **PARTIAL** (fak has the block-sizing; lacks the admission policy that uses it to guarantee no mid-decode eviction).

### Verdict
**PARTIAL → FILE (INSPIRE).** Directly relevant to fak's native many-agent GLM-5.2 serving (epic #3809): a stream that thrashes mid-decode wastes the prefill and stalls a tenant.

### First checkable step
Add a pure `Admit` fold to `internal/kvbudget` (worst-case = `ceilDiv(prompt+maxNew)` blocks minus allocated minus ref-held reusable, summed over running + candidate vs free budget) with a table test: N streams that fit admit; the N+1th that would force an eviction refuses with a structured reason. No GPU in the loop (mirrors the package's existing GPU-free posture).

records.title: feat(radixkv): client-declared per-request KV retention — (priority, TTL-window) over token ranges feeding the victim rule (epic #5256)
records.body:
## feat(radixkv): client-declared per-request KV retention — (priority, TTL-window) over token ranges feeding the victim rule

**Study borrow from NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM `@f4c5c935` (Apache-2.0, INSPIRE / clean-room). Epic #5256 (tensorrt-llm-study).**

### The axis
**Client-declared, per-request KV retention as (priority, retention-window) over token ranges**, projected to a per-block weight the eviction rule honors — as opposed to a purely *telemetry-derived* victim score. Three concrete pieces:
1. a request attaches non-overlapping `TokenRangeRetentionConfig{tokenStart, tokenEnd, priority(0-100), durationMs}`, projected per-block by `getPerBlockRetentionPriorityDuration` (earlier ranges win);
2. a **context-vs-decode priority split** — decode-generated blocks get a distinct (usually lower) priority because freshly-decoded KV is rarely a reuse target;
3. **TTL demotion**: a block with a non-default priority + `durationMs` is pushed to an expiration min-heap and auto-demoted back to the default priority when its window passes ("keep this hot for 5 s, then age normally") — no explicit release.

### Source (code I read)
- `cpp/include/tensorrt_llm/executor/executor.h:589-617@f4c5c935` — `KvCacheRetentionConfig` / `TokenRangeRetentionConfig`; scale `kMinRetentionPriority=0..kMaxRetentionPriority=100`, `kDefaultRetentionPriority=35`; decode split at `executor.h:655-657`.
- `cpp/tensorrt_llm/executor/kvCacheRetentionConfig.cpp:125@f4c5c935` — the per-block projection loop.
- `cpp/tensorrt_llm/batch_manager/evictionPolicy.cpp:246-270@f4c5c935` — `refresh()` TTL demotion via `mExpiringBlockHeap`; priority-bucketed LRU free queues `mFreeQueues[level][priority]` at `evictionPolicy.cpp:144-159`; leaf-only detach preserving high-priority interior prefixes at `kvCacheManager.cpp:1322-1337`.

### fak seam (where it lands)
`internal/radixkv/eviction_strategy.go` — the victim rule is `victimKey{seg, cost, age}` where `seg` comes from an observed hit-count threshold (SLRU), `cost` from `compute.KVEvictionCost`, `age` from `lastUsed`. Every input is **telemetry the tree observes**; there is no channel for a *caller* to declare "pin this prefix at priority P for T ms." `internal/cacheprice/retention.go` prices remote-pool residency by signed net-compute but likewise takes no client priority/TTL. The borrow: add a client-declared retention band as a new highest-precedence `seg` tier + a TTL-demotion pass, leaving the telemetry keys as the within-band tie-break.

### Witness (dogfood + raw grep)
- Raw `Grep` for `retention|priorit|evict` × `block|kv|window`: fak's retention is `cacheprice/retention.go` (value-priced, not client-declared) and `radixkv` victim scoring (telemetry). `radixkv/namespace.go` already has the **cacheSalt/namespace isolation** equivalent (PRESENT — dropped). No per-request priority scale, no context-vs-decode split, no TTL demotion heap.
- Witnessed **PARTIAL** twice (fak has an eviction *seam* and value pricing; it lacks the *client-declared priority + TTL* vocabulary feeding it).

### Verdict
**PARTIAL → FILE (INSPIRE).** Lets a caller pin a shared system prompt / tool-world prefix hot for a bounded window while the tail stays freely evictable — the reuse-shaping knob telemetry alone can't express. Complements #3320 (cachemeta authorization) and #3661 (cachevalue) without duplicating them.

### First checkable step
Add a `RetentionBand{Priority uint8 /*0-100*/, TTL time.Duration}` input to `radixkv` that maps into a new top-precedence `victimKey.seg` tier, plus a pure `refresh(now)` demotion over an expiration heap. Table test: a high-priority band survives a scan of cold inserts; after its TTL elapses `refresh` demotes it and it evicts by normal LRU — byte-identical to today when no band is set (zero-value = current behavior).

records.title: feat(engine): per-block-hash KV cache event stream — tier + priority diffs for prefix-aware routing (epic #5256)
records.body:
## feat(engine): per-block-hash KV cache event stream — created/stored/removed/updated with tier + priority diffs for prefix-aware routing

**Study borrow from NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM `@f4c5c935` (Apache-2.0, INSPIRE / clean-room). Epic #5256 (tensorrt-llm-study).**

### The axis
A **per-block-hash event stream** an external KV-aware router consumes to know *which tier each block lives on* and *how hot it is* — not just aggregate counters. TRT-LLM emits four typed events: `KVCacheCreatedData`, `KVCacheStoredData{parentHash, blocks[]}` (each block carries blockHash, tokens, priority, cacheLevel), `KVCacheRemovedData{blockHashes[]}`, and crucially `KVCacheUpdatedData{blockHash, cacheLevel:Diff, priority:Diff}` — a *diff* payload emitted when a block moves GPU↔host or changes priority. The stream is parent-hash-chained (so a consumer can reconstruct prefix trees) and coalesces removals per window to bound volume.

### Source (code I read)
- `cpp/include/tensorrt_llm/executor/executor.h:1741-1848@f4c5c935` — the four event structs + `KVCacheEventDiff{oldValue,newValue}`; each event carries `eventId`, `windowSize`, `attentionDpRank`.
- `cpp/tensorrt_llm/batch_manager/kvCacheEventManager.cpp:83-144@f4c5c935` — emit sites; level-change UPDATE on offload (`kvCacheManager.cpp:1309`), priority-change UPDATE (`kvCacheManager.cpp:1690`); per-window removed-event coalescing (`kvCacheEventManager.cpp:115-139`); bounded drop-oldest ring (`:271-284`) so telemetry never stalls the forward pass.

### fak seam (where it lands)
`internal/engine/cacheevents.go` — fak already normalizes live-engine residency events into the shared `cachemeta.Entry` stream and renders **aggregate** Prometheus metrics keyed by (direction, outcome, to_tier). `internal/gateway/residency_router.go` already ingests `ResidentAdd`/`ResidentDrop` into a per-worker prefix-residency index for cache-aware fleet routing. The gap: the current `CacheEvent` is resident-or-dropped + tier at rest; it has **no `Updated` variant carrying a (from_tier→to_tier) or priority *diff* keyed by block hash**, so the router can't distinguish "block migrated GPU→host" from "block evicted" and can't rank replicas by block hotness. Add an `Updated` direction + block-hash/parent-hash fields to `CacheEvent` and fold the diff into the residency index.

### Witness (dogfood + raw grep)
- Raw `Grep` for `cache.?event|block.{0,10}(stored|evicted|reused|removed)|KVCacheEvent`: fak's `engine/cacheevents.go` (metrics) + `gateway/residency_router.go` (add/drop routing) are the neighbors. The block-hash **created/stored/removed** granularity is largely PRESENT via residency_router's op stream; the **UPDATED (tier-move / priority diff)** granularity is ABSENT.
- Witnessed **PARTIAL** (an enhancement to two existing seams, not a new capability).

### Verdict
**PARTIAL → FILE (INSPIRE).** Composes with the existing residency router (#41) and the cache-verify epic #3569; makes tier-move observable so a KV-aware balancer routes to the replica that holds the prefix *on the hot tier*, not merely one that once held it.

### First checkable step
Add `KVUpdated` to `cachemeta.KVTransferDirection` and a `{BlockHash, ParentHash, FromTier, ToTier, OldPriority, NewPriority}` shape on `engine.CacheEvent`; extend `residency_router` ingest to move a span's tier on an UPDATE rather than drop+re-add. Table test: an offload UPDATE keeps the span resident-but-cold in the index (routable, deprioritized), distinct from a DROP (unroutable).

records.title: feat(model/spec): model-free prompt-lookup (n-gram) drafter feeding the shipped verify-accept substrate — zero draft head
records.body:
## Borrow (study-repo, vllm @ b6ff8a2f)

A **model-free, head-free speculative drafter** that proposes draft tokens by
matching the recent context suffix against earlier context (KMP longest-prefix-suffix
scan) and emitting the tokens that followed the earliest prior occurrence — verbatim
n-gram / prompt-lookup copying with **no draft model and no draft head**. It is the
cheapest drafter possible and rides fak's already-shipped verify-accept substrate for
losslessness.

**Source (vllm, Apache-2.0, inspire — clean-room Go, no bytes vendored):**
- `vllm/v1/spec_decode/ngram_proposer.py:206@b6ff8a2f` — `_find_longest_matched_ngram_and_propose_tokens` (batch driver `batch_propose_numba` `:177`, entry `propose` `:135`); O(n) KMP LPS table over flipped tokens instead of naive O(n·max_n).
- Losslessness comes from the shared rejection verify, `vllm/v1/sample/rejection_sampler.py:746@b6ff8a2f` — any drafter (even a dumb n-gram) can never change the output distribution; drafters only affect speed.

## The one axis

Zero-draft-model token proposal from *repeated context* (RAG, code, agentic reprompting,
long shared prefixes) where the answer literally reappears in the prompt. Distinct from
every drafter fak has or has planned: MTP (`#5154`, needs a NextN head), EAGLE (`#3197`,
needs a trained draft head), and `FastForwardDrafter` (schema-driven, needs a tool schema).
This one needs **none of those** — it works on an arbitrary GLM/Qwen decode with nothing
extra to host.

## fak seam + why this is ABSENT

fak already ships the verify-accept substrate that `#3197`/`#5154` wire heads into, plus:
- `internal/model/selfspecgov.go` — the `SelfSpecGovernor` acceptance governor (charges
  page-ins, auto-offs when drafting stops paying) — a ready home for a new drafter.
- `internal/model/fastforward.go` — `FastForwardDrafter.Draft(history) []int` feeding the
  `VerifyForward` accept loop (`internal/model/verify.go`), default-off behind
  `FAK_NATIVE_GUIDED_DECODE`.

But fak has **no model-free drafter**. The technique is only *listed* as a SOTA rung —
`internal/sotamatrix/ladder.go:159` (Level 4 "Lookahead / n-gram drafts",
arXiv:2402.02057) — tracked, unbuilt. The one prior prompt-lookup issue (`#3078`) was
GLM-5.2 / DGX-2-specific and is **CLOSED**. Witnessed absent twice (grep for an n-gram
*proposer* finds only repetition *detection* in `internal/model/recurrent_canary.go`, plus
the ladder mention; the drafter roster is FastForward + MTP only).

## Why vllm's users made them build it

vllm built the n-gram drafter for repetition-heavy serving (RAG / code / agentic loops)
because a dumb copy-from-context drafter gives a large speedup with **no extra GPU model to
host**. That is exactly fak's slow-tier world: CPU/SSD-offloaded MoE decode is memory/
page-in-bound (~2 tok/s on GLM-5.2), and fak's own agentic-coding / tool-loop traffic is
maximally repetitive — the highest-leverage place a free drafter pays off.

## Scope (ship-alone leaf)

A pure-Go `NgramDrafter.Draft(history []int) []int` implementing suffix-match-and-copy
(KMP LPS over the context window), gated default-off exactly like `FastForwardDrafter`,
emitting draft token ids into the existing `VerifyForward` accept loop and governed by the
existing `SelfSpecGovernor`. No new wire, no head, no draft model.

**First checkable step:** a unit test — a context containing a repeated span yields the
continuation as draft tokens and `VerifyForward` accepts the correct prefix; a
non-repeating context drafts nothing (inert, byte-identical to today).

## Follow-on (NOT this leaf — split later)

- Suffix-decoding **trie** over *past outputs* for cross-request repetition —
  `vllm/v1/spec_decode/suffix_decoding.py:81@b6ff8a2f` (ArcticInference, variable-length).
- Per-position acceptance metrics (accepted-count vector by draft position → acceptance
  curve) to tune depth — `vllm/v1/spec_decode/metrics.py:41@b6ff8a2f`. fak's governor
  tracks only a scalar accept-rate today.

Parent: `#23` (speculative decoding); composes with the verify-accept substrate `#3197`/`#5154`.
Study note: docs/notes/CONCEPT-STUDY-VLLM-2026-07-18.md.

records.title: feat(guideddecode): gate the constrained-decode mask on reasoning-end — don't constrain the <think> block
records.body:
## Borrow (study-repo, vllm @ b6ff8a2f)

**Gate the constrained-decode mask on reasoning-end.** Defer applying the structured-output /
tool-envelope token mask until the model's `<think>…</think>` reasoning phase ends, and trim
the end-marker mid-window so the constrainer never chokes on it — so a reasoning model thinks
freely, *then* the schema kicks in.

**Source (vllm, Apache-2.0, inspire — clean-room Go, no bytes vendored):**
- `vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py:351@b6ff8a2f` — `should_fill_bitmask` (do not mask
  while reasoning), `:371` `should_advance` (mid-step reasoning-end detection), `:449`
  `trim_reasoning_for_advance` (strip tokens up to and including the end marker before the
  grammar advances). Config gate `enable_in_reasoning`. Fixes vllm #44006 / #42452.

## The one axis

Correctness of the reasoning→answer boundary under constrained decoding: the grammar/mask is
neither advanced nor applied until the reasoning block closes, so the schema does not corrupt
the model's chain-of-thought and the reasoning tokens do not dead-end the matcher.

## fak seam + why this is PARTIAL (both halves exist, UNWIRED)

fak has both pieces but they are not connected:
- `internal/guideddecode/guideddecode.go` — `AllowedNextBytes` constrains the tool-call
  envelope `{"name":"<enum>","arguments":…}` from **byte 0**, with no notion of a reasoning
  prefix.
- `internal/agent/reasoning_strip.go` (`splitReasoning`) — parses `<think>…</think>` from the
  decoded string; the in-code comment calls it "the in-kernel equivalent of vLLM's
  `--reasoning-parser qwen3`".

Nothing gates guideddecode on the reasoning boundary (grep of `internal/guideddecode` for
reasoning/think returns nothing). So if native guided decode were applied live to a reasoning
model, it would force the tool-envelope grammar *during* the think block — corrupting the
reasoning or dead-ending the mask. The two features are currently mutually exclusive.

## Why vllm's users made them build it

vllm serves reasoning models (DeepSeek-R1, Qwen3, gpt-oss) that must reason unconstrained and
only then emit schema-valid tool calls; without the gate the schema kills the think phase.
fak targets the same class — GLM-5.2 (`glm_moe_dsa`), Qwen3.5 / Ornith, DeepSeek V4 — so
`FAK_NATIVE_GUIDED_DECODE` + a reasoning model is a real combination fak will hit.

## Scope (ship-alone leaf)

A reasoning-boundary predicate wrapping guideddecode that: (1) returns UNCONSTRAINED while
inside an open, unclosed `<think>`; (2) begins constraining only after the close tag; (3) trims
tokens up to and including the close marker before the constrainer advances. Reuse the existing
`thinkOpen`/`thinkClose` constants; default-off / no-op for non-reasoning turns (byte-identical
to today).

**First checkable step:** a unit test — a stream `<think>…</think>{"name":"…` is unconstrained
through the close tag, then constrained to the declared tool-name enum after it; a non-reasoning
stream is byte-identical to today.

Relates to guideddecode `#26`. Milestone: Substrate, grammar & interop foundation.
Study note: docs/notes/CONCEPT-STUDY-VLLM-2026-07-18.md.

records.title: feat(deepseekv4kv): servable-prefix across heterogeneous attention windows (fold/unfold) — bound a prefix hit by the SWA window
records.body:
## Borrow (study-repo, LMCache @e38ee415): servable-prefix under heterogeneous per-layer attention windows (fold/unfold)

**Source (read):** `lmcache/v1/distributed/bitmap_ops/fold.py:67` (`fold`), `:127` (`unfold`), `:166` (`fold_unfold_ranked`); window descriptor `lmcache/v1/distributed/api.py:264` (`AttnWindowDesc`) — all @e38ee415 (`git.io` pin `e38ee4157a11`).

**The one axis:** compute a single "how much of this prefix is actually cache-*hittable*" answer for a model whose layers obey **different** token-dependency rules — full-attention vs sliding-window vs mamba. A model-wide prefix hit of length L is only valid if **every** attention group can serve length L under its own rule; `fold` **intersects** the per-group servable-prefix bitmaps (full-attn reduces to plain prefix intersection; sliding-window of `w` chunks only needs the last `w`), and `unfold` expands the agreed hit length back into the concrete chunks each group must retain. LMCache built this because hybrid architectures now ship and a naive prefix-length over-counts the hit whenever a windowed layer can't actually serve the early tokens.

**fak seam:** `internal/deepseekv4kv/deepseekv4kv.go:112` (`MandatoryDurableUnits`/`PrefixHitUnits` = CSA+HCA blocks per layer) and `:104` (`SubCacheUnits(KindSWA, seq) = min(seq, 128)`). `deepseekv4kv` already models a **heterogeneous KV plane** (CSA rate-4, HCA rate-128, SWA window-bounded to 128, dense tail) in normalized units — but it accounts per-kind **storage/amplification**, not the cross-kind **servable-prefix intersection**. Today a long prefix hit on a request is over-counted: the SWA layers can only serve their last 128-token window, so the true model-wide hittable prefix is bounded by the most restrictive group. That intersection is exactly `fold`.

**Witness (on-axis):** raw grep of `internal/deepseekv4kv/*.go` for `servable|fold|intersect|window|hittable|min.*prefix` — SWA window is modelled (`:105`) and prefix-hit *units* are summed (`:112`), but there is **no** fold-style intersection that answers "given a length-L request over CSA+HCA+SWA+dense layers, how many leading tokens are hittable in *all* groups." `gh issue list --search "servable prefix heterogeneous"` / `"fold unfold attention window"` → no match. ABSENT-on-axis (an enhancement to the existing `deepseekv4kv` accounting fixture, not a new capability).

**Route:** inspire (clean-room Go; both repos Apache-2.0; index math, no tensors — a perfect fit for the weight-free `deepseekv4kv` fixture). Source cited, no bytes vendored.

**First checkable step:** add `ServablePrefixUnits(seq int, kinds []Kind) int` to `internal/deepseekv4kv` that returns the min over per-kind hittable prefix lengths (dense/CSA/HCA = seq; SWA = `min(seq, SWAWindow)` measured from the tail), with a unit test proving a 512-token request with an SWA layer yields a servable prefix bounded by the window, not 512.

Study note: `docs/notes/CONCEPT-STUDY-LMCACHE-2026-07-18.md`. Parent epic #3366 (lmcache-study); relates to #3319 (regenerable KV) / #3320 (cachemeta plane).

records.title: feat(l3kv): layer-group write-sharding of a large KV object to fit a backend per-object byte cap
records.body:
## Borrow (study-repo, LMCache @e38ee415): layer-group sharding of a large KV object to fit a backend per-object byte cap

**Source (read):** `lmcache/v1/distributed/l2_adapters/bigtable_l2_adapter.py:692-739` (`_execute_store`: `sharding_enabled = layer_group_size > 0`, per-shard 90 MB / per-row 240 MB caps, parallel `write_sharded_key`), `:1014-1071` (reassembly on read), and `lmcache/v1/distributed/l2_adapters/bigtable_key_encoder.py:16-40` (the shard scheme is embedded in the key: `{model}@lg{N}`) — @e38ee415.

**The one axis:** when a single logical KV object is larger than a backend's hard per-object size cap (Bigtable's ~256 MB/row), **shard it by layer-group** — N layers per shard (default 10), each shard a separate keyed object whose key records the grouping (`@lg{N}`), written **in parallel** and reassembled on read. This turns one oversized, serial, all-or-nothing put into many capped, parallel, independently-retryable puts, and lets a reader fetch only the layer groups it needs.

**fak seam:** `internal/stripeload/stripeload.go:69` (`WithMinChunk` — splits a *read* across N byte-identical mirrors by bandwidth) and `internal/blob` / `internal/blobfs/store.go:202` (2-hex directory-fan sharding). fak's `stripeload` fans a single logical **read** across mirrors for aggregate bandwidth; it has **no** write-side path that shards a large object into backend-cap-sized pieces keyed with the shard scheme. `internal/l3kv` (the `abi.KVBackend` seam) puts/gets whole objects.

**Witness (on-axis):** raw grep of `internal/{blob,blobfs,l3kv,stripeload,xenginekv}/*.go` for `Shard|SplitInto|maxObjectBytes|maxRowBytes|sizeCap` → empty (only stripeload's read-side `MinChunk` and blobfs directory-fan). `gh issue list --search "layer group shard"` → only the disaggregation epic #3259, no leaf. PARTIAL: fak has the tiered-object plane and a read-side splitter, but not the write-side object-cap shard-by-layer-group.

**Route:** inspire (clean-room Go; both Apache-2.0). Source cited, no bytes vendored.

**First checkable step:** add an object-cap shard planner to the `abi.KVBackend`/`l3kv` write path: `PlanShards(objBytes, layerBoundaries []int, capBytes int) []Shard` that groups whole layers into ≤`capBytes` shards and emits shard keys carrying the group size; unit-test that a 512 MB object under a 240 MB cap yields ≥3 layer-aligned shards that reassemble byte-exact.

Study note: `docs/notes/CONCEPT-STUDY-LMCACHE-2026-07-18.md`. Parent epic #3366 (lmcache-study); relates to #4296 (KV mobility / remote memory) and #3259 (disaggregation).

records.title: feat(cachemeta): fail-open-until-synced eviction default so a not-yet-synced managed-cache controller can't mass-evict
records.body:
## Borrow (study-repo, LMCache @e38ee415): fail-open-until-synced eviction default for a per-tenant cache byte-quota registry

**Source (read):** `lmcache/v1/distributed/quota_manager.py:42-128` (the two-lens resolver) and `lmcache/v1/distributed/storage_controllers/eviction_controller.py:347-384` (`_check_and_evict_by_cache_salt`, allowlist rule) — @e38ee415 (pin `e38ee4157a11`).

**The one axis:** a multi-tenant cache byte-quota registry keyed by tenant id (`cache_salt`) whose **boot-time default is fail-OPEN (exempt from eviction), not fail-closed**. A freshly-booted coordinator whose quota table has not yet been re-synced by the external quota controller resolves unknown tenants to `None` = exempt, so it **cannot mass-evict every tenant's cache on restart**. Allowlist enforcement (unknown → 0 bytes → evict) is *armed explicitly* only after the controller syncs quotas (`set_default_limit_bytes(0)` via `PUT /quota/config`). The subtle safety property is in the module docstring: two resolver lenses (`get_limit_bytes` = legacy allowlist-immediate vs `effective_limit_bytes` = default-until-armed) exist precisely so a not-yet-synced control plane fails safe.

**fak seam:** `cmd/fak/guard_managed_cache.go:27-32` (managed-cache posture auto/on/off, epic #1844) and `internal/cachemeta` (the authorization + coherence plane; `prefix_coherence.go:71` already encodes "a nil predicate refutes nothing — fail-OPEN"). fak deeply holds the **fail-open philosophy** (guard landlock `DecideFailOpen`, cachemeta nil-predicate) but has **no** cache admission/eviction control-plane whose *default posture on a not-yet-synced restart is provably non-destructive*. When fak grows a managed-cache eviction/admission controller (or a fleet cache-budget authority), the same reboot-must-not-mass-evict hazard applies: a controller that comes up before its budget table syncs must not treat "unknown = evict."

**Witness (on-axis):** raw grep of `internal/{cachemeta,kvbudget,cacheprice,l3kv,guard}/*.go` for `quota|byte.?budget|per.?tenant|fail.?open|arm.*enforce` — fail-open exists as a *coherence/sandbox* predicate, not as a *cache-eviction default posture*; no per-tenant byte-quota registry. `gh issue list --search "cache byte quota tenant"` → no match. PARTIAL/ABSENT: the transferable nugget is the **default-safety invariant** (a control plane that hasn't re-synced fails open, and deny is armed post-sync), which is squarely on fak's guard/coherence safety axis even though fak's fleet is not multi-customer SaaS.

**Route:** inspire (clean-room Go; both Apache-2.0). Source cited, no bytes vendored.

**First checkable step:** when fak lands a managed-cache eviction authority, encode the invariant as a typed default: `EvictionPosture{ default: Exempt; ArmDeny() }` where an un-synced controller returns `Exempt` for unknown keys and a test proves a controller restart before budget-sync evicts **zero** entries (only an explicit `ArmDeny()` after sync makes unknown keys evictable). Until then, file as the documented safety requirement on the managed-cache seam.

Study note: `docs/notes/CONCEPT-STUDY-LMCACHE-2026-07-18.md`. Parent epic #3366 (lmcache-study); relates to #3320 (cachemeta plane) and #3569 (cache-verify loops).

records.title: feat(admission): set the admission TokenBudget from a measured warmup capacity probe, not a static default (TGI borrow)
records.body:
_Field-borrow from HuggingFace **text-generation-inference** (TGI) v3 @`b4adbf2`. Part of epic #2236 (fak superset of vLLM+SGLang+Dynamo). Companion to #2242 (SLO/goodput admission). Study note: `docs/notes/BORROW-TGI-SERVING-ADMISSION-STUDY-2026-07-18.md`._

## Borrow (technique) — measure the machine, then set the budget

TGI does **not** ask the operator to guess how many tokens the GPU can hold. At startup the router sends a synthetic max-size batch to the shard; the shard runs the largest possible prefill, measures **peak memory**, and computes the KV block budget from what is actually free — then the router sets its admission budget (`max_batch_total_tokens`) to that *measured* value, discounted by a safety margin.

- Router side: `backends/v3/src/lib.rs:124-138@b4adbf2` — warmup RPC returns `max_supported_batch_total_tokens`; the router adopts it (and errors `NotEnoughMemory` if `max_total_tokens` exceeds it, `lib.rs:98-107`).
- Shard probe: `server/text_generation_server/models/flash_causal_lm.py:1517-1565@b4adbf2` — `num_blocks = free_memory // total_cache_size + batch_num_blocks`.
- Safety margin: `TGI_WIGGLE_ROOM=0.90` at `server/text_generation_server/models/globals.py:30-33@b4adbf2` (provision against only 90% of free memory; comment: "Test a 70B model on 4xA100 under load").
- Fail-fast on OOM with an actionable message: `flash_causal_lm.py:1549-1553@b4adbf2` ("decrease `--max-batch-prefill-tokens`").

## fak seam — witness: PARTIAL

fak **already issues a boot warmup** but only records **latency**, not **capacity**:
- `internal/gateway/readiness_warmup.go:134` `RunWarmup` fires one synthetic 1-token completion and records boot to first-token (`timeToReady`), exposed as `time_to_ready_ms`. It measures *how long*, never *how much*.
- `internal/gateway/admission.go:94` — `DefaultAdmissionPolicy.TokenBudget` is a **hardcoded 8192**. Nothing derives it from the backend's real headroom.

So fak has the warmup turn and the admission budget, but the wire between them is missing: the budget is a static guess where TGI's is a measurement.

## Proposal (small, default-off, ship-alone)

1. Extend the warmup / serve-stage probe to optionally measure the backend's token/KV headroom (native in-kernel path can report resident KV capacity; a proxy path can carry a provider/config-supplied ceiling).
2. When a measured capacity is available, set `AdmissionPolicy.TokenBudget` from it (times a configurable wiggle-room, default ~0.90) at `SetAdmissionController` (`cmd/fak/serve.go:401`); otherwise keep the static default as fallback.
3. Surface the chosen budget plus its provenance (measured vs default) on `/metrics` next to `fak_sched_tokens_in_use` / `fak_sched_max_num_seqs`.

## Acceptance / witness

- A native serve with a measurable KV capacity sets `TokenBudget` from the measurement (not 8192), witnessed deterministically (inject a fake capacity, assert the policy budget and the `fak_sched_*` gauge).
- A serve with no measurable capacity is byte-for-byte unchanged (static default).
- Over-budget `max_total_tokens` fails fast at boot with an actionable message, mirroring TGI's `NotEnoughMemory`.

## Why it matters

Turns "how many concurrent tokens can this box hold" from an operator guess into a measured value — the structural signature that lets TGI auto-size to any GPU. For fak this is an operability win on the *already-shipped* admission seam, and it makes the 429 shed boundary honest (it sheds at real capacity, not an arbitrary 8192).

records.title: feat(cacheobs): declarative map-reduce MetricSpec registry that proves reporter parity across collection paths
records.body:
## Borrow (study-repo, LMCache @e38ee415): declarative map-reduce MetricSpec registry that proves reporter parity across two collection paths

**Source (read):** `lmcache/usage_telemetry/metric_specs.py:26-78` (`MetricSpec{event_type, field, extract, reduce}` + `default_metric_specs`) and `lmcache/usage_telemetry/mp_continuous.py:99-112` (the spec list is validated to cover every wire-schema field exactly once) — @e38ee415 (pin `e38ee4157a11`).

**The one axis:** define each cache metric as a **declarative map-reduce spec** — one `event_type` off an event bus, an `extract` (map: event → numeric sample), a `reduce` (fold: interval samples → one field), and the target message `field` — so a metric is a **data row, not new plumbing**. The payoff LMCache extracts from it: they run two reporters (single-process and multiprocess) and make them **provably at-parity** because both consume the *same* spec list, and a startup check asserts the specs cover the message schema exactly once. Drift between the two reporters becomes structurally impossible.

**fak seam:** `internal/cacheobs/cacheobs.go:73` (`type Observer struct` with hand-written `Observe(...)` methods and hardcoded counters) and the recent Go↔Python control-pane debt-key parity gate (commit `9d1d5034c`, `internal/scorecardpane`). fak already *cares* about cross-implementation parity (it gates Go vs Python panes against drift) and has a rich KV-observability surface (`cacheobs`, `cacheprice`, `cachevalue`), but its metrics are **imperative Go counters**, each wired by hand — there is no declarative spec that a second emitter (or a Python mirror) can be proven to reproduce field-for-field.

**Witness (on-axis):** raw grep of `internal/{cacheobs,cacheprice,cachevalue,rungobs}/*.go` for `MetricSpec|map.?reduce.*metric|extract.*reduce|event.*extract.*field` → empty. `gh issue list --search "metric spec parity reporter"` → no match. ABSENT-on-axis: fak has the observability capability but not the declarative-spec-drives-parity mechanism.

**Route:** inspire (clean-room Go; both Apache-2.0). Source cited, no bytes vendored.

**First checkable step:** introduce `cacheobs.MetricSpec{ Event EventKind; Field string; Extract func(Event) float64; Reduce func([]float64) float64 }` and a `DefaultSpecs()` registry, refactor one existing counter (e.g. token-level hit ratio) to be spec-driven, and add a test that asserts the spec set covers the exported snapshot schema exactly once — the same "covers the wire schema exactly once" check LMCache runs at `mp_continuous.py:99-112`.

Study note: `docs/notes/CONCEPT-STUDY-LMCACHE-2026-07-18.md`. Parent epic #3366 (lmcache-study); relates to #4254 (observability hot-path plane).

records.title: feat(admission): anti-hog preallocation cap — decouple charged generation budget from requested max_tokens (TGI borrow)
records.body:
_Field-borrow from HuggingFace **text-generation-inference** (TGI) v3 @`b4adbf2`. Part of epic #2236. Companion to #2242 (typed early-reject admission). Study note: `docs/notes/BORROW-TGI-SERVING-ADMISSION-STUDY-2026-07-18.md`._

## Borrow (technique) — decouple the *preallocated* generation budget from the *requested* max_tokens

TGI refuses to let one request reserve the whole pool with a giant `max_new_tokens`. It caps the **preallocated** generation chunk at `DEFAULT_GENERATION_LENGTH = 1024` while tracking the true requested max separately, and re-queues the request every time it consumes that chunk — so a "10-token prompt asking for 120k output" cannot preallocate 120k of budget up front.

- `router/src/validation.rs:152-179@b4adbf2` — `chunk_size = min(max_new_tokens, DEFAULT_GENERATION_LENGTH)`; comment: *"prevent a single user from taking up all the slots in a handful of queries that consume little... but request 120k."* The full request re-queues each time it completes `DEFAULT_GENERATION_LENGTH` tokens.

## fak seam — witness: ABSENT

`internal/gateway/admission.go:627-642` `estimateServedAdmissionTokens` charges the **full requested `maxTokens`** onto the single `SeqRequest.Tokens` axis (`tokens += maxTokens`), and `token_admission.go:207-218` does the same for the provider window (`output = maxTokens`). A request with a large `max_tokens` reserves proportionally large budget — and under a full budget it can be the one that sheds everyone else (429), or hogs the running set.

There is no preallocation-vs-request decoupling anywhere in the admission path (the only `max_new_tokens` symbol is a native request field at `debug.go:264`).

## Proposal (small, ship-alone)

1. Charge admission a **preallocation ceiling** `min(requestedMax, PreallocCeiling)` (default e.g. 1024) instead of the full `maxTokens`, at `estimateServedAdmissionTokens` (`admission.go:627`).
2. When a lease has consumed its preallocated chunk and the generation continues, **re-admit** the next chunk against the live budget (a running request tops up its footprint rather than reserving the whole thing at t=0). The lease already exists (`AdmissionLease`); add a `Grow` / re-charge step driven by the decode loop / `SettleUsage`.
3. Keep the *true* requested max for the stopping condition — only the *preallocated footprint charged to the budget* is capped.

## Acceptance / witness

- A request with `max_tokens = 120000` is admitted charging ~`PreallocCeiling`, not 120000 (deterministic unit witness on `estimateServedAdmissionTokens`).
- Under a saturated `TokenBudget`, a single huge-`max_tokens` request no longer sheds a queue of small requests that would have fit (extends the existing `TestAdmissionShed429` family).
- A long generation still completes correctly by re-charging per chunk (no premature stop).

## Why it matters

Fairness under load: one greedy `max_tokens` cannot reserve or shed the whole pool. This is the admission-side complement to #1912 (chunked-prefill execution) — that issue chunks the *prefill* pass; this one stops the *decode* budget from being over-reserved at admission time.

records.title: feat(gateway): model a peer instance's KV cache as a read-only fetch tier — the data-plane half of cache-aware routing
records.body:
## Borrow (study-repo, LMCache @e38ee415): model a peer instance's KV cache as a read-only L2 tier so cross-instance reuse rides the same fetch path (the data-plane half of cache-aware routing)

**Source (read):** `lmcache/v1/distributed/l2_adapters/p2p_l2_adapter.py:128` (`P2PL2Adapter`), read-only store no-op `:186-202`, lookup-RPC-then-transfer-read `:213-358`; the uniform async tier contract it implements at `lmcache/v1/distributed/l2_adapters/base.py:78` — @e38ee415 (pin `e38ee4157a11`).

**The one axis:** expose *another instance's* cache through the **same** interface as any storage tier (S3, disk), where store/evict/delete are no-ops ("a peer's cache is read-only"), `lookup` goes over a message queue to the peer's controller, and `load` **pulls the KV bytes** from the peer over a transfer channel. Because it is just another tier, cross-instance KV reuse rides the exact same prefetch/lock/trim machinery as disk or object-store reuse — no separate code path. This is the **data-plane** move (fetch the bytes), distinct from routing the request.

**fak seam:** `internal/gateway/residency_router.go:12-33` — fak's cache-aware fleet router tracks "which worker already holds the shared prefix" and routes the **request** there, but the code states explicitly (`:31`): *"control-plane signal only: no KV bytes move here (that is the native KV-transport seed's documented prerequisite)."* So fak has the **control-plane half** (route to the warm node) and deliberately defers the **data-plane half** (fetch the peer's KV as a tier). `internal/xenginekv` co-resides an *external engine's* KV in one arena (cross-engine, same node); it does not model a *remote peer instance* as a fetchable cache tier.

**Witness (on-axis):** raw grep of `internal/{xenginekv,l3kv}/*.go` + `residency_router.go` for `peer.*(tier|fetch|pull)|remote.*kv.*(fetch|pull)|read.?only.*tier` → empty; residency_router is control-plane-only by its own comment. PARTIAL/ABSENT on the data-plane axis: the request routes to the warm peer, but fak cannot yet treat that peer's KV as a tier to pull from when co-locating the request is not possible.

**Route:** inspire (clean-room Go; both Apache-2.0). Source cited, no bytes vendored.

**First checkable step:** define a `PeerKVTier` implementing the existing `abi.KVBackend` interface whose `Put/Evict` are no-ops and whose `Get` resolves holder + address via the residency index (`gateway/residency_router.go`) and pulls bytes over the native KV-transport seam; unit-test with a mock transport that a prefix present only on peer B is served to worker A through the standard `l3kv` fetch path.

Study note: `docs/notes/CONCEPT-STUDY-LMCACHE-2026-07-18.md`. Parent epic #4296 (distributed-compute: KV mobility / remote memory); relates to #3366 (lmcache-study) and #3259 (disaggregation).

records.title: feat(gateway): fail-closed front-door validation of the structured-output contract (422 before upstream) (TGI borrow)
records.body:
_Field-borrow from HuggingFace **text-generation-inference** (TGI) v3 @`b4adbf2`. Part of epic #2236. Study note: `docs/notes/BORROW-TGI-SERVING-ADMISSION-STUDY-2026-07-18.md`._

## Borrow (technique) — fail-closed validation of the structured-output contract at the front door

TGI validates a request's structured-output grammar **at the router, before it reaches the GPU**, and rejects a malformed one with 422 rather than burning a compute slot:

- `router/src/validation.rs:341-406@b4adbf2` — for `response_format` / `json_schema`: (a) if a string, re-parse to confirm valid JSON; (b) `jsonschema::draft202012::meta::validate` the schema; (c) **require a `properties` field** (a valid-but-propertyless schema is rejected with a clear message); (d) then compile `json_schema_to_regex`. Any failure is a typed `ValidationError` mapped to HTTP 422 (`router/src/server.rs:2409`).

(The *compile-and-cache* half — `server/text_generation_server/utils/logits_process.py:526-543`, FSM keyed by `(grammar_type, schema, tokenizer)` — is **DIVERGENT for fak** and explicitly out of scope: fak proxies decoding to vLLM/SGLang, which own the FSM. This borrow is the **validation half only**.)

## fak seam — witness: ABSENT (currently pass-through by choice)

fak forwards `response_format` / `json_schema` / `guided_grammar` / `logit_bias` **verbatim** to the ride engine, enforced there, never validated at fak's door:
- `internal/gateway/http.go:541-546` (`WithResponseFormat` / `WithLogitBias`), `stream_proxy.go:89-93`, carriers as raw `json.RawMessage` in `wire.go:330-367`. The pass-through is a deliberate, tested behavior (`structured_output_passthrough_test.go`).

Consequence: a malformed / propertyless / oversized JSON-schema costs a full upstream round-trip (and the tokens/latency of a provider 400) before anyone learns it was bad. For a **trust/governance door** whose whole identity is fail-closed early-reject, that is a gap.

## Proposal (small, ship-alone, on-brand)

Add a **cheap, fail-closed door check** on the structured-output contract in the request-admission path (alongside the existing body-cap / admission gate), NOT a decoder:
1. If `response_format` / `json_schema` is present, parse it; if it is a JSON-schema, run a lightweight draft-2020-12 well-formedness check plus a `properties` / size sanity guard.
2. On failure, refuse at the door with the existing typed-error to status vocabulary (`admissionErrorStatus` style) as a **422 `structured_output_invalid`**, before any upstream call.
3. On success, forward verbatim exactly as today (pass-through unchanged for valid schemas).

Seam: `internal/gateway/http.go:541` / `wire.go:330`; reuse the closed error to status machinery already in `admission.go:657-682` plus `http_upstream_error.go`.

## Acceptance / witness

- A malformed / propertyless / over-size JSON-schema is refused with 422 `structured_output_invalid` **without** an upstream call (witness: assert no proxy dispatch, mirrors `structured_output_passthrough_test.go` inverted).
- A valid schema forwards byte-for-byte as today (pass-through preserved).
- Default-on is safe (only rejects contracts the ride engine would 400 anyway); a config flag can force legacy pure pass-through.

## Why it matters

Fail-closed at the trust door is fak's worldview: reject a broken structured-output contract for the price of a schema parse instead of a wasted upstream round-trip. Cheap, on-brand, and it closes the one structured-output gap the seam-map flagged ABSENT.

records.title: feat(spec/grammar): compose speculative decoding with an active grammar — forked matchers advanced by accepted tokens only (fak polymodel)
records.body:
## Borrow (study-repo: lmdeploy @67c18b90)

Compose **grammar/structured decoding with speculative decoding** correctly: when the
target is under a grammar (JSON / tool-call schema), a naive spec-decode advances the
grammar matcher by the *draft*'s guessed tokens and corrupts constraint state on a
rejection. lmdeploy solves this by **forking the grammar matcher across the N+1
speculative positions** and only committing the forks that correspond to *accepted*
tokens.

Part of epic #4102 (tool-call speculation & the assumption ledger). This is the
grammar-composition correctness leaf, distinct from the (closed) schema-fast-forward
drafter #4103 — that drafter covers *fully forced* spans (100% acceptance, nothing to
speculate); this covers the *partially* constrained regions (enum choices, free strings
inside JSON) where spec-decode and the grammar must co-advance.

### The one axis
Speculative decoding under an active grammar, where grammar state may advance **only by
accepted tokens**, while the per-position token bitmask must be applied **speculatively**
across all N+1 draft positions — with rollback-free correctness on rejection.

### Source (read at 67c18b90)
- `lmdeploy/pytorch/spec_decode/guided_spec_helper.py:124-215` — `apply_serial_bitmask`
  forks xgrammar matchers, masks each of the N+1 positions, advances forks by *draft*
  tokens; `accept_rejection_sampled_tokens:173-215` replays exactly
  `num_spec_tokens - num_rejected` accepted (+bonus) tokens onto the *real* matchers.
  CPU matcher work offloaded via `asyncio.to_thread`.
- `lmdeploy/pytorch/spec_decode/proposers/eagle3.py:54-87` — `_translate_bitmask`
  converts a target-vocab grammar bitmask to a reduced *draft* vocab via precomputed
  word/bit indices + `scatter_add_` (bit positions never overlap so add ≡ OR); needed
  when the draft model has a smaller vocab than the target.

### fak today — witness (dogfooded `fak_feature_query` + raw Grep + code read)
- Speculative decoding is **PRESENT but greedy-only**: `internal/polymodel/specdecode.go:139`
  (`SpecDecode`) + `internal/model/verify.go:36` (`VerifyForward`), tree accept for
  Medusa/EAGLE-2, schema jump-forward / prompt-lookup drafter at
  `internal/polymodel/fastforward.go:54`.
- Grammar/constrained decoding is **PRESENT**: `internal/grammar/grammar.go`,
  `internal/grammar/compile.go`.
- The **composition** is ABSENT: nothing forks/rolls-back the grammar matcher across
  speculative positions, and there is no draft-vocab bitmask translation. Under a grammar
  at partial constraint, fak's spec path would either disable speculation or risk advancing
  grammar state by rejected draft tokens.

Seam to attach: `internal/polymodel/specdecode.go` accept loop + `internal/grammar` matcher
(add a fork/clone + advance-by-accepted API), and a draft↔target vocab bitmask map alongside
the EAGLE/heterogeneous-vocab drafter (#4208).

### Verdict
**INSPIRE** (clean-room Go; cite source). lmdeploy is Apache-2.0 (LICENSE read at
67c18b90) so vendoring would be license-legal, but this is an algorithm/discipline borrow
best reimplemented against fak's own grammar matcher.

### First checkable step
Add a `Fork()`/`AdvanceByAccepted(tokens)` capability to the grammar matcher and a unit
test proving: given a draft of K tokens under a JSON-enum grammar, after verify accepts J≤K,
the matcher's state equals the state reached by feeding exactly the J accepted tokens (and
never the rejected ones) — the invariant `guided_spec_helper.py` encodes.

### Provenance
study-repo pass over https://github.com/InternLM/lmdeploy @67c18b900cad, 2026-07-18.
Note: `docs/notes/CONCEPT-STUDY-LMDEPLOY-2026-07-18.md`.

records.title: feat(route): tier-weighted overlap credit in the fleet residency scorer (borrow dynamo selector.rs)
records.body:
## Borrow (from a deep /study of NVIDIA Dynamo @ea89e8bd)

fak's fleet cache-aware router scores a worker's cached-prefix match as a **plain prefix
length** — `overlap-length × 1/(1+load)` — treating every resident block as equally
valuable regardless of which memory tier holds it. Dynamo's KV router instead credits an
overlap hit by **how expensive it is to reach**: a GPU-device-resident block is full
credit, a host-pinned block ~0.75, a disk/SSD block ~0.25, an external shared-pool block
~0.5, all summed into one "blocks of work saved" term before it enters the routing cost.

The effect: fak will currently route to a worker whose overlapping prefix has been evicted
down to SSD over a worker holding a shorter prefix still resident on-device — even though
the on-device hit avoids a page-up the SSD hit does not. fak already *has* the tier data
(`internal/radixkv/crosstier.go` hot/cold spans; `internal/cacheprice/route.go` local vs
remote-fabric toll) — the fleet scorer just ignores it.

### Axis
Value-per-cache-hit as a function of the tier it must be reached from — not raw match length.

### Source (read at pinned SHA)
- `lib/kv-router/src/scheduling/selector.rs:199-202@ea89e8bd` — `overlap_credit_blocks = device + host_weight*host + disk_weight*disk + shared_multiplier*shared`
- `lib/kv-router/src/scheduling/overlap.rs:201-239@ea89e8bd` — tier aggregation
- default weights `lib/kv-router/src/scheduling/config.rs:37-42@ea89e8bd` (host 0.75, disk 0.25)

### fak seam
- `internal/gateway/residency_router.go:491` — `CacheAwarePolicy.score` (`overlap-length × inverse-load`)
- `internal/gateway/residency_router.go:209` — `workerResidency.overlap` returns a plain segment prefix length
- tier data available but unused by the scorer: `internal/radixkv/crosstier.go` (TierHot/TierCold), `internal/cacheprice/route.go`

### Shape
Extend `PrefixResidencyIndex` to record, per resident prefix, the tier it currently sits in
(fed by the existing `ResidentAdd`/`ResidentDrop` events + native `IngestResidentPrefixes`),
and change `score`/`overlap` to sum a **tier-weighted** credit (configurable weights,
defaulting to device 1.0 / host 0.75 / disk 0.25) instead of a raw length. Keep the
power-of-two-choices + skew-threshold structure unchanged; this only reshapes the credit term.

### First checkable step
A pure unit test on `CacheAwarePolicy`: two workers, worker A holds the longer prefix but
tagged cold/disk, worker B a shorter prefix on-device at equal load — assert the
tier-weighted scorer picks B while the current length-only scorer picks A.

### Provenance
INSPIRE (clean-room Go; Dynamo is Apache-2.0 — no vendored bytes). Second-witnessed against
fak's actual scorer code, not the pitch.

Epic: #50 (serving — RIDE+NATIVE routing spine). Refines the shipped baseline in #2238.

records.title: feat(radixkv): fence prefix-cache reuse by decode regime (modelID·dtype·quant_policy·RoPE), not token path alone (fak radixkv)
records.body:
## Borrow / worldview-finding (study-repo: lmdeploy @67c18b90)

lmdeploy's prefix cache (both engines) keys a reusable KV block on **tokens only**
(+ multimodal fingerprint / LoRA adapter) — never on the *numeric regime* the KV was
produced under. A block's KV bytes therefore carry an **implicit, unenforced invariant**:
the cache is only valid within one fixed `dtype` / `quant_policy` / RoPE configuration per
process. Safe for them in practice (config is process-fixed), but there is no cross-check
that would stop KV produced under one quant/dtype from being reused to serve a request
running under a different one.

fak should **enforce** what lmdeploy leaves implicit, because fak's differentiators make
the hazard live: fak sells bit-exact mid-run eviction from a lossless pre-RoPE `Kraw`
(`internal/model/kvcache.go`), regenerable KV across model rollout (epic #3319), and a
trust plane — all of which assume the resident KV was produced under the *same* regime the
current request decodes under. When KV quantization lands (#2240) and models hot-swap in
one process, token-only reuse identity becomes a correctness/isolation hole, not just a
perf detail.

Relates to epic #3319 (regenerable KV — whose body already lists an unfiled child
"re-check ModelID at the live radix reuse site on a same-process model switch") and epic
#2240 (KV-cache quantization ladder). This is the fence that makes both safe.

### The one axis
Prefix-cache **reuse identity must include the decode regime** — `(modelID, kv dtype,
quant_policy, RoPE/position scheme)` — so a cached prefix is structurally unreachable from
a request that would decode it under a different regime.

### Source (read at 67c18b90)
- `lmdeploy/pytorch/paging/block_trie.py:304-311` — node key is
  `hash(('random', tuple(tokens), extra_hashes))`; regime/dtype/quant absent.
- `src/turbomind/engine/prefix_trie.h:22-36` + `prefix_key.h:36-90` — identity = parent +
  tokens + image fingerprints; no dtype/quant field. (Study readers confirmed: no
  `quant`/`dtype` symbol in the trie or scheduler.)

### fak today — witness (raw Grep + code read)
- Radix reuse identity is `(tokens, nsKey)`: `internal/radixkv/namespace.go:3-11`, node
  identity at `internal/radixkv/radixkv.go:374`. `nsKey` is a **generic** "LoRA-adapter id /
  cache-salt / namespace" — it *can* carry a discriminator but does not **require** the
  decode regime; `namespace.go` itself flags "silent cross-namespace reuse … is an
  ISOLATION/CORRECTNESS hole."
- KV is f32-only today (`internal/model/kvcache.go:13-15`) so the regimes that can differ
  are currently `{modelID, RoPE-scheme}`; the surface widens the moment #2240 adds a
  quantized KV tier. So this is PARTIAL (a salt exists) trending to ABSENT-of-enforcement.

Seam to attach: make the regime a **required** component of the radix key (or a mandatory
namespace derivation) at `internal/radixkv/radixkv.go:374` / `namespace.go rootFor`, and
assert it at the reuse site (`internal/cachemeta` model-switch recheck).

### Verdict
**INSPIRE** — an inverted worldview finding: adopt the *enforcement* lmdeploy omits. Cite
source as the design that left the invariant implicit.

### First checkable step
A failing test that inserts KV under regime A (e.g. quant_policy=8 or modelID=X), then
attempts a longest-prefix reuse under regime B on the same token path, and asserts the
