records.title: feat(route): anticipatory decode-footprint load term (expected-output scaled) in the fleet scorer (borrow dynamo)
records.body:
## Borrow (from a deep /study of NVIDIA Dynamo @ea89e8bd)

fak's fleet router costs a worker's load as its **live in-flight request count**
(`effectiveLoad` = fill term + external in-flight count). A count treats a request that
will emit 20 tokens the same as one that will emit 20k — but a long-output request's
growing decode KV is exactly what will blow up that worker's footprint *after* it's placed.
Dynamo's router pre-books an **anticipatory decode-block footprint** into the load term:
`additional_active_blocks = query_len − overlap_depth` plus placeholder output blocks that
grow with generation and are scaled by a `decay_fraction` toward the request's *expected
output length* hint. A worker about to materialise a large decode footprint therefore looks
expensive at selection time, before its in-flight count reflects it.

This is directly on fak's axis: fak's agentic 1.0-style per-request hints already carry an
expected-output-length signal, and fak's long agent turns are the exact case a count
under-weights.

### Axis
Anticipatory load accounting — project a request's decode-KV footprint (expected-output
scaled) into the load term, so a worker isn't over-selected before its in-flight decodes
materialise their KV cost.

### Source (read at pinned SHA)
- `lib/llm/src/kv_router/sequences/prompt_registry.rs:334-336@ea89e8bd` — `additional_active_blocks = query_len − overlap_depth`
- `lib/kv-router/src/scheduling/config.rs:482-485@ea89e8bd` — `router_track_output_blocks`
- `lib/llm/src/kv_router/scheduler.rs:397-403@ea89e8bd` — `add_output_block` with `decay_fraction` toward `agent_hints.osl`

### fak seam
- `internal/gateway/residency_router.go:480` — `CacheAwarePolicy.effectiveLoad` (fill term + in-flight count only)
- `internal/gateway/replica_router.go` — `load func(name string) int` is a live in-flight *count*

### Shape
Let the `load` seam accept (or the policy derive) a projected footprint = in-flight count
plus a per-request expected-decode-block estimate that decays as the turn's output length
becomes known. Keep it a pure additive term in `effectiveLoad`; no change to the pick structure.

### First checkable step
Unit test: two workers at equal in-flight *count*, one already hosting a long-output turn;
assert the projected-footprint load steers a new request to the other worker.

### Provenance
INSPIRE (clean-room Go; Apache-2.0 source). Witnessed against `effectiveLoad`'s count-only body.

Epic: #50 (serving — RIDE+NATIVE routing spine). Distinct from #2238's overlap baseline (this is the load half).

records.title: feat(route): route by expected drain time — normalize live in-flight by per-worker throughput + observed-latency EWMA (fak gateway)
records.body:
## Borrow (study-repo: lmdeploy @67c18b90)

lmdeploy's request-distribution proxy routes across backends by **expected drain time**,
not raw least-loaded: it divides each node's live in-flight count by that node's throughput
weight so a fast GPU box is preferred over a slow one at equal queue depth, and it keeps a
bounded deque of recently-observed finished-request latencies as a second, empirical signal.

fak's residency router is load-aware but uses an **unweighted** `1/(1+load)` term, which
mis-routes on a heterogeneous fleet (fak runs a mix of A100 / B200 / consumer boxes whose
per-worker service time differs several-fold) — two workers at equal in-flight count are
treated as equal even when one drains twice as fast.

Enhancement to fak's existing load-aware routing under epic #2236 (superset). Distinct from
#2238 (KV-overlap routing) — this is the *service-time* axis, orthogonal to prefix overlap;
they compose (overlap × expected-drain-time).

### The one axis
Backend selection by **expected drain time = in-flight / worker-throughput** (plus an
optional observed-latency EWMA), so heterogeneous-speed workers are compared on time-to-
serve, not on queue depth alone.

### Source (read at 67c18b90)
- `lmdeploy/serve/proxy/proxy.py:288-303` — `MIN_EXPECTED_LATENCY` (default): picks the node
  minimizing `unfinished / speed`, shuffling ties to spread low-concurrency load.
- `lmdeploy/serve/proxy/proxy.py:304-316` — `MIN_OBSERVED_LATENCY`: picks the node with the
  lowest mean over a bounded (len-15) deque of recent finished-request latencies.
- `lmdeploy/serve/proxy/proxy.py:419-437` — `pre_call`/`post_call` maintain `unfinished` and
  append observed latency, the cheap live signals it already has by proxying.

### fak today — witness (code read)
- **PRESENT but unweighted**: `internal/gateway/residency_router.go:480-491` — `CacheAwarePolicy`
  computes `effectiveLoad = occupancy + external in-flight`, `score = overlap × 1/(1+load)`,
  power-of-two-choices; `internal/gateway/replica_router.go:248-274` supplies each worker's
  live in-flight count. There is **no per-worker throughput normalization** (no `load/speed`)
  and **no observed-latency signal**; least-loaded is also opt-in (default is round-robin,
  `replica_router.go:274`).

Seam to attach: add a per-worker `speed`/service-time weight and an observed-latency EWMA to
`replica_router.go` load reporting, and change `residency_router.go:491` from `1/(1+load)` to
an expected-drain-time term `1/(1 + load/speed)`.

### Verdict
**INSPIRE** (clean-room Go; cite source).

### First checkable step
A router unit test with two workers at equal in-flight count but 2× different throughput
weights, asserting the faster worker is chosen (and, with an observed-latency deque seeded,
that a worker whose recent latencies spiked is de-preferred) — the `MIN_EXPECTED_LATENCY` /
`MIN_OBSERVED_LATENCY` behaviors.

### Provenance
study-repo pass over https://github.com/InternLM/lmdeploy @67c18b900cad, 2026-07-18.
Note: `docs/notes/CONCEPT-STUDY-LMDEPLOY-2026-07-18.md`.

records.title: feat(serving): advisory (shadow) ScaleMode for the serving autoscaler — decide+journal, actuate nothing (borrow dynamo planner)
records.body:
## Borrow (from a deep /study of NVIDIA Dynamo @ea89e8bd)

fak's serving autoscaler (`internal/gateway/serving_autoscaler.go`) can only run in
`native` (it actuates) or `defer_to_dynamo`. There is no **advisory / shadow** mode that
runs the *full* decision pipeline against live traffic — computing the scale action,
journalling it, exporting the metric — but deliberately **actuates nothing**. Dynamo's
planner ships exactly this: an `advisory` flag runs the whole decision fold and publishes
`[ADVISORY]` decisions + gauges, then short-circuits before `_apply_scaling_targets`.

This is the standard "trust an autoscaler on production traffic before you let it move
capacity" pattern, and it is squarely fak-aligned (governed, auditable, witness-before-act).
The mechanism is nearly free here: fak *already* emits a structured, replayable
`ScaleDecision` into `ScaleDecisionJournal` on every tick — an advisory mode is a
`ScaleMode` that takes the decided `Action`/`DesiredReplicas` but skips the
`scaleUp`/`scaleDown`/`Drain` actuation and stamps `AppliedReplicas = CurrentReplicas`.

### Axis
Validate a scaling *policy* against live traffic before granting it actuation — decide +
journal + export, actuate nothing.

### Source (read at pinned SHA)
- `components/src/dynamo/planner/core/base.py:118-122,371-376@ea89e8bd` — `if self.config.advisory: return` after publishing the decision + gauges
- `components/src/dynamo/planner/config/defaults.py:103@ea89e8bd` — the `advisory` default

### fak seam
- `internal/gateway/serving_autoscaler.go:14` — `ScaleMode` (only `native` / `defer_to_dynamo`)
- `internal/gateway/serving_autoscaler.go:467` — `emit`; `:487` `scaleUp`; `:520` `scaleDown` (actuation to gate)
- `internal/gateway/serving_autoscaler.go:290` — `ScaleDecisionJournal` (the trace sink already exists)

### Shape
Add `ScaleModeAdvisory`. `reconcileRole` computes the decision unchanged; when the mode is
advisory, `Reconcile` emits the `ScaleDecision` (with `Action` populated, `AppliedReplicas
= CurrentReplicas`, reason `advisory`) and returns without calling the actuator or `Drain`.

### First checkable step
Unit test with a stub `ScaleActuator` that fails the test if `Start` is ever called: drive
a signal that would scale up in `native`, assert advisory mode journals `scale_up` with
`AppliedReplicas == CurrentReplicas` and never touches the actuator.

### Provenance
INSPIRE (clean-room Go; Apache-2.0 source).

Epic: #50 (serving — dual-track spine; the autoscaler is its scale-control half).

records.title: feat(serving): forecast-driven predictive MinReplicas floor beneath the reactive autoscaler (borrow dynamo dual-timescale planner)
records.body:
## Borrow (from a deep /study of NVIDIA Dynamo @ea89e8bd)

fak's serving autoscaler is **purely reactive**: `reconcileRole` acts on the current tick's
signals against a **static** `PoolObjective.MinReplicas`. It has strong anti-thrash already
(consolidation-aware `survivorWouldBreach` veto, hysteresis, cooldown, drain-before-remove)
— but nothing raises capacity *before* an SLA breach. Provisioning a new worker takes real
wall-clock time, so a reactive-only loop is always one control-lag behind a ramp.

Dynamo solves this with a **dual-timescale** controller: a slow (~180s) loop forecasts
near-future load and inverts the perf model to a **minimum replica count**, installing it
only as a *lower bound*; a fast (~5s) reactive loop then tunes above that floor and can
never drop below it. The two loops don't fight because the slow one only ever raises the
floor. fak already has the coalesced load-signal substrate for this
(`internal/loaddebounce`, itself a Dynamo `worker_metrics.rs` borrow — currently unwired).

### Axis
Reconcile proactive provisioning latency vs reactive control precision — a forecast-driven
`MinReplicas` floor beneath the existing reactive scaler, without the two loops oscillating.

### Source (read at pinned SHA)
- `components/src/dynamo/planner/core/throughput_scaling.py:52-59,96-101@ea89e8bd` — slow loop sets `_throughput_lower_bound_*`
- `components/src/dynamo/planner/core/load_scaling.py:196-199@ea89e8bd` — `max(reactive, floor)`
- cadence `components/src/dynamo/planner/config/defaults.py:29,84-86@ea89e8bd` (throughput 180s, load 5s)
- forecasters `components/src/dynamo/planner/core/load/predictors.py:56-96@ea89e8bd` (idle-skip base; ARIMA/Kalman variants)

### fak seam
- `internal/gateway/serving_autoscaler.go:162` — `PoolObjective.MinReplicas` (static config)
- `internal/gateway/serving_autoscaler.go:415` — `reconcileRole` (reactive only)
- `internal/loaddebounce/loaddebounce.go` — the coalesced per-worker load-signal primitive to feed a forecaster (currently unwired)

### Shape
A slow companion loop that folds a short-horizon forecast of per-pool demand (start with a
robust idle-skipping moving-estimate; keep the forecaster pluggable) into a *dynamic* floor,
and change `reconcileRole` to clamp `desired` up to `max(forecastFloor, MinReplicas)`. Keep
it a lower bound only — the reactive loop still owns everything above it.

### First checkable step
Unit test: a rising-demand signal series; assert the forecast floor raises `desired` a tick
*before* the reactive band would have, and that on a falling series the floor only ever
raises (never forces a scale-down below the reactive decision).

### Provenance
INSPIRE (clean-room Go; Apache-2.0 source). fak's reactive half + `survivorWouldBreach`
veto were witnessed present and are explicitly *not* re-filed — this is only the missing
predictive floor.

Epic: #50 (serving — dual-track spine; scale-control half). Pairs with the advisory-mode leaf.

records.title: feat(resume): refuse token-replay migration when structured-decode or n>1 makes state non-transferable (borrow dynamo migration.rs)
records.body:
## Borrow (from a deep /study of NVIDIA Dynamo @ea89e8bd)

Epic #3352 wants to warm-continue a live turn across worker death by replaying already-
delivered tokens to a fresh worker. Dynamo's request-migration path does exactly that — and
carries a **correctness guard fak's migration story does not yet name**: it **hard-disables**
token-replay migration whenever the decode state is *not transferable*, specifically:

- **guided / structured decoding** (a constrained-grammar FSM) — the FSM would restart from
  its schema root on the new worker, so replaying tokens mid-constraint produces invalid or
  double-constrained output; and
- **n>1 / multi-choice** requests — per-choice sampler state is not reconstructable from the
  delivered token stream alone.

In both cases a naive "reconnect + replay delivered tokens" silently corrupts the response
rather than failing honestly. Dynamo refuses the migration for these classes and lets the
request error cleanly instead. fak's migration surface today is session-state / objective-pin
migration (`internal/session/descriptor.go` migration log) — the mid-stream token-replay path
under #3352 should adopt the same non-transferable-state guard *before* it ships, so the
warm-continue can never re-emit structured output incorrectly.

### Axis
Availability without silent corruption — survive a mid-stream worker death by replaying
delivered tokens, but *refuse* the replay when structured-decode or n>1 makes the decode
state non-transferable.

### Source (read at pinned SHA)
- `lib/llm/src/migration.rs:214-241@ea89e8bd` — disable migration for guided-decoding and n>1
- `lib/llm/src/migration.rs:260-308@ea89e8bd` — rebuild stream on a fresh worker, replay delivered `token_ids` as context
- `lib/llm/src/migration.rs:59-68@ea89e8bd` — the migratable-error set

### fak seam
- `internal/session/descriptor.go:94` — the branch/migration log (session-state migration today)
- `cmd/fak/resume.go` — the warm-continue / resume path #3352 extends
- gateway structured-output / n-choice request metadata is where the guard reads its inputs

### Shape
When the #3352 token-replay migration path is built, gate it: if the in-flight request used
constrained/grammar decoding or n>1, mark it non-migratable and surface a typed refusal
(clean error) instead of replaying. Everything else migrates as planned.

### First checkable step
A pure predicate + unit test: `migratable(req)` returns false for a guided-decode request
and for n>1, true for a plain single-choice free-form turn — with the refusal carrying a
structured reason.

### Provenance
INSPIRE (clean-room Go; Apache-2.0 source).

Epic: #3352 (fault-tolerant in-flight session migration across worker death).

records.title: feat(moe): length-gated prefill compute-placement — switch expert GEMMs between host-hybrid and device-layerwise by prefill token count (ktransformers-borrow, child #3900)
records.body:
Child of the ktransformers study epic **#3900** (sibling of the #5239–#5242 compute cluster filed at `0c2912a`). Fresh re-study pinned at **`def0f931`** (`git rev-parse HEAD` = def0f9313d6e). The #524x cluster mined deferred-experts (#5239), native FP8 (#5240), the ISA/VRAM doctor (#5241) and KV-sizing (#5242); none of them covers ktransformers' **length-gated prefill strategy**, which is the gap this leaf fills.

## The borrow (inspire — Apache-2.0 → Apache-2.0, clean-room, no bytes)
ktransformers switches its whole-model **prefill compute placement** on a single token-count threshold, `--kt-gpu-prefill-token-threshold` (default 4096):

- **Below threshold → CPU-GPU Hybrid prefill.** Hot experts on GPU, cold experts on CPU concurrently; **no extra VRAM** beyond the resident hot experts. Cheap for short prompts where CPU MoE is not yet the bottleneck. `doc/en/kt-kernel/Native-Precision-Tutorial.md:261-283@def0f931`.
- **At/above threshold → Layerwise GPU prefill.** Cold-expert weights are streamed CPU→GPU **one MoE layer at a time** and the GEMM runs on GPU tensor cores; costs ~**one MoE layer of expert weights** of extra VRAM (scales with `chunked-prefill-size`), but prefill latency then scales with GPU FLOPs instead of CPU MoE bandwidth. Same doc.
- Plumbed as one knob: `--kt-gpu-prefill-token-threshold` at `kt-kernel/python/cli/commands/run.py:447@def0f931` (default 4096); FP8/RAWINT4-only per the README parameter table `kt-kernel/README.md:543-546@def0f931`. Layerwise prefill is also the trigger point for live expert redistribution (`doc/en/kt-kernel/experts-sched-Tutorial.md:206-212@def0f931`).

**Axis (narrow):** *peak VRAM vs prefill throughput, gated on sequence length.* A fixed choice either OOMs on long context (always-stage-to-GPU) or is slow on long prefill (always-CPU-hybrid); the length gate gives each regime its best case from one config. Their VRAM-starved consumer-GPU + big-MoE world is exactly where this pays.

## fak seam (where this lands)
- `internal/model/moe_offload.go` — `splitKernel` routes each expert GEMM host-vs-device by a **static, name-only** predicate `onHost(name)` (`splitKernel.mul`, lines 40-45; predicate built at line 139, `isExpertWeight`). Placement never varies by the current prefill's token count — this is fak's `--n-cpu-moe` equivalent, fixed for the whole run.
- `internal/cacheprice/breakeven.go` — `TransferBreakEvenLength(fixedOverheadTokens, recomputePerToken, transferPerToken)` (line 27) already computes the **exact length break-even** for a fixed-floor-plus-per-token transfer vs a per-token local cost. fak has the length-gate *arithmetic*; it just applies it to KV fetch-vs-recompute (`internal/cacheprice`), not to prefill compute placement.

So fak owns both ingredients — a per-weight host/device split (`splitKernel`) and a length break-even (`TransferBreakEvenLength`) — but has **never composed them into a length-gated prefill-placement decision.** ABSENT on-axis.

## Dogfood witness
Twice-witnessed: `fak_feature_query` + raw `Grep` for `prefill.?token.?threshold | layerwise | dual prefill | length.*prefill.*placement` → only the fixed module-split hybrid (`internal/model/metal_prefill_hybrid_core.go`: projection GEMMs → device / GDN scan → host — **not** length-gated) and prefill benchmarks (`internal/glm52prefillsweep`). `gh issue list --search "prefill placement length gate" / "layerwise vram prefill" / "dual prefill"` → empty. Distinct from #5239 (defers experts by *router weight*, not by *sequence length*) and from #3886 (which rank owns which expert, not per-prefill placement).

## First checkable step
Add a pure, host-free planner `internal/model/prefill_placement_plan.go`: given `prefillTokens`, a per-token CPU-MoE cost, a per-token device-stream cost, and the fixed layerwise-staging VRAM/overhead, return `{stageToDevice bool, breakEvenTokens int}` by calling `cacheprice.TransferBreakEvenLength` (or an inlined twin). Witness against a fixture: short prompt → host-hybrid, long prompt → device-layerwise, monotone in `prefillTokens`. This mirrors how #3902/#3901 landed as pure gauges before any serve wiring; the `splitKernel`-consults-the-plan step is the fenced follow-on (needs a device backend, so the CPU-only path stays bit-exact).

## Honest scope
- Witness is a 2026-07 snapshot (`def0f931`) + lexical query + `gh` dedup; re-witness before wiring.
- The *threshold-selection loop itself* (the runtime that reads `num_tokens` and picks the mode) lives in the kvcache-ai `sglang-kt` fork, not in this repo; the in-repo anchors are the design doc (`doc/en/kt-kernel/Native-Precision-Tutorial.md:261-283@def0f931`) + the CLI plumbing (`kt-kernel/python/cli/commands/run.py:447`, `kt-kernel/README.md:543-546`). The borrow is INSPIRE and composes fak's own existing mechanisms, so this is sufficient grounding.
- Not a from-scratch borrow: a *delta* composing `splitKernel` + `TransferBreakEvenLength`. The "one MoE layer of VRAM" cost is fak's `hot-experts-into-idle-VRAM` budget — this gate decides *when* the stage is worth it.

records.title: feat(model): user-supplied per-tensor placement override (name-regex, first-match-wins) for the CPU-offload split
records.body:
Borrow from a witnessed `/study` of **llama.cpp @571d0d54** (`https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp`). License MIT — verdict **inspire** (clean-room re-implementation in Go idiom, cite-only, **no bytes vendored**).

## Axis (the one property this targets)
Per-tensor CPU/GPU placement chosen by an **ordered list of user `{name-regex -> device}` overrides, first-match-wins** — independent of, and finer than, fak's built-in expert/dense predicate. An operator can place one arbitrary tensor (or a non-standard tensor class in a new arch) on host without patching Go.

## llama.cpp source (read @571d0d54)
- Override loop with `std::regex_search`, first-match `break`, fallback `select_weight_buft`: `src/llama-model-loader.cpp:1162-1219`.
- Sugar that synthesizes the expert regexes (`--cpu-moe`): `common/arg.cpp:2509-2530`, `common/common.h:1073-1081` (`LLM_FFN_EXPS_REGEX`).

## fak seam today

- `internal/model/moe_offload.go:108-117` — `onHost` is hard-wired to `isExpertWeight` (routed + shared experts) via `CPUOffloadExperts`. All-or-nothing, non-overridable.

fak's split can only ever move *the experts*. A user whose attention almost fits VRAM but wants one specific projection (or a non-standard MoE tensor name) on host has no dial short of a code change. llama.cpp users hit exactly this ("my MoE attention+router fit VRAM but the expert stacks don't; pin exactly these tensors to RAM"), and the regex override is the answer.

records.title: feat(model): graded expert-spill knob (--n-cpu-moe N) + auto-fit N to a measured device budget
records.body:
Borrow from a witnessed `/study` of **llama.cpp @571d0d54** (`https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp`). License MIT — verdict **inspire** (clean-room, cite-only, no bytes vendored).

## Axis (the one property this targets)
A **graded** offload dial — spill only the first *N* layers' experts to host RAM (not all-or-nothing) — plus an **auto-search that picks N** to maximize device utilization under a *measured* memory budget. fak today has only a binary "all experts on CPU or none," and a fit check that *refuses* when neither endpoint fits.

## llama.cpp source (read @571d0d54)
- Graded knob: `common/arg.cpp:2509-2530` — `--n-cpu-moe N` emits per-layer `blk\.<i>\.ffn_..._exps -> CPU` for the first N layers.
- Auto-fit search: `common/fit.cpp:527-728` — force all MoE experts to CPU, probe real per-device memory with `no_alloc=true` dry loads, method-of-false-position over layer counts, convert dense-only -> full layers, even fit a fractional layer, then emit `tensor_buft_overrides` + `tensor_split`.

## fak seam today
- `internal/model/moe_offload.go:132-142` — `glmDsaMatKernel`: `s.CPUOffloadExperts` is a **bool** (split or not).
- `internal/ggufload/estimate.go:473-499` — `FitOnDevice` / `FitCPUOffloadExpertsOnDevice`: binary estimate-and-**refuse**; exactly two plans (all-device, all-experts-host).
- Adjacent pieces already present: `internal/kvbudget`, and `#4361` (`fak serve --plan-json` dry-run plan).

## Gap
fak has two placement plans and a fit check that refuses when neither fits; there is no gradient between them and no search that fills the device to the largest split that fits. When experts *almost* fit VRAM, fak can only refuse or dump every expert to slow host RAM.

## First checkable step
Replace `CPUOffloadExperts bool` with a graded spill count consumed by an `isExpertWeight`-with-layer-index predicate; add a **pure** `FitExpertSpill(endpointPlans, budget) -> N` search interpolating between the two existing `Estimate*MemoryPlan` endpoints (no device alloc); unit-test the monotone fit.

Composes with the per-tensor regex override (sibling issue). **Distinct from #1045** (auto-fit KV *context*) — this fits the expert-SPLIT. Provenance: study-repo pass over llama.cpp @571d0d54 (2026-07-18). Related: #5243, #3900, #4361.

records.title: feat(model/spec): model-free n-gram (prompt-lookup) drafter feeding the shipped verify-accept substrate
records.body:
Borrow from a witnessed `/study` of **llama.cpp @571d0d54** (`https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp`). License MIT — verdict **inspire** (clean-room, cite-only, no bytes vendored).

## Axis (the one property this targets)
Draft tokens with **no draft model and no MTP/EAGLE head** — find the current suffix n-gram earlier in the token history and copy the m-gram that followed it; degrade gracefully (empty draft = normal decode). This is the *head-free* draft source, distinct from every existing fak spec-decode ticket (all of which require a second model or a trained head).

## llama.cpp source (read @571d0d54)
- Linear self-lookup: `common/ngram-map.cpp:49` (`common_ngram_simple_draft`).
- Hashed single-probe map: `common/ngram-mod.cpp:15-41`.
- 3-tier statistical cache (context/dynamic/static) with sample-size + percent gates: `common/ngram-cache.cpp:146`.
- Priority-chained dispatcher (first non-empty draft wins): `common/speculative.cpp:2357-2388, 2568-2614`.
- Accept loop it feeds: `common/sampling.cpp:624` (`common_sampler_sample_and_accept_n`).

## fak seam / gap
fak has the verify-accept **substrate** (`internal/model/config.go:791` `SelfSpeculationSubstrateReady`; #3197 EAGLE-3 draft head; #4202 stochastic accept) but every drafter is model/head-bound. There is **no** drafter that reads only the token history. Repo-scoped issue search confirms no prompt-lookup / n-gram ticket exists.

## Why their users needed it (and why fak's do)
Single-box local users often can't afford a second draft model's VRAM/latency, but their outputs heavily quote the input. fak's headline workload is the agentic coding loop (milestone #6): code edits, JSON reformat, tool-echo — all repetition-heavy. Prompt-lookup gives multi-token-per-step speedup there at **zero extra weight memory** and no second model to host.

## First checkable step
A pure `internal/ngramdraft` leaf: `Draft(history []int, suffixN, maxDraft int) []int` (linear back-search first), wired as one drafter behind fak's existing accept-n verify; a table test on a repetitive sequence proving >=1-token accept and **lossless** output vs plain decode.

Provenance: study-repo pass over llama.cpp @571d0d54 (2026-07-18). Sibling to #3197 / #5154 (head-based) — this is the head-free source.

records.title: feat(engine): Hadamard-rotation outlier smoothing for quantized K/V cache (KV-quant ladder enhancement)
records.body:
Borrow from a witnessed `/study` of **llama.cpp @571d0d54** (`https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp`). License MIT — verdict **inspire** (clean-room, cite-only, no bytes vendored). Enhancement to the KV-quant ladder (#2240, epic #2236).

## Axis (the one property this targets)
Multiply K/V by an **involutory Walsh-Hadamard** matrix before quantizing so outlier channels spread across the block — recovering the accuracy that aggressive (q4) KV quant otherwise loses — **without changing the stored bit-width**. Involution (R^2 = I) is the trick that lets RoPE K-shift still compose: dequant -> un-rotate -> RoPE -> re-rotate -> quant.

## llama.cpp source (read @571d0d54)
- Hadamard matrix generation: `src/llama-kv-cache.cpp:22`.
- Enable gate (only when `ggml_is_quantized` && head_dim % 64 == 0): `src/llama-kv-cache.cpp:319-336`.
- The dequant -> un-rotate -> rope -> re-rotate -> quant K-shift path: `src/llama-kv-cache.cpp:1857-1871`.

## fak seam / gap
fak has (or is building) an int8/fp8 KV-quant ladder (#2240, #3410, #4874) but **no outlier-smoothing rotation** — grep of `internal/**` for hadamard/walsh/rotate-quant/outlier is empty, and the repo-scoped issue search is empty. Low-bit KV without outlier handling loses quality on a few channels, which is what caps how far the ladder can push bits.

## Why their users needed it
Milestone #2 ("KV cache value owned & 2x") wants smaller KV. The rotation is the cheap fixed transform that makes q4 KV **usable** instead of quality-lossy, so the ladder can drop a tier at equal quality.

## First checkable step
A pure `HadamardRotate(vec, headDim)` / inverse pair (involutory; head_dim % 64 gate) + a test showing round-trip identity and reduced quant error on a synthetic outlier-heavy K row; then wire it behind the existing KV-quant store path so the rotation is applied before quant and inverted after dequant.

Provenance: study-repo pass over llama.cpp @571d0d54 (2026-07-18). Child of KV-quant ladder #2240 / epic #2236.

records.title: perf(model): NUMA-aware weight-mmap policy — MADV_RANDOM under NUMA, sequential hints otherwise
records.body:
Borrow from a witnessed `/study` of **llama.cpp @571d0d54** (`https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp`). License MIT — verdict **inspire** (clean-room, cite-only, no bytes vendored).

## Axis (the one property this targets)
Match the kernel's page-population policy to the access pattern **and topology**: on a NUMA box, DISABLE eager prefetch and mark the weight map `MADV_RANDOM` so pages fault **local to the thread that first touches them** (first-touch) instead of piling onto one node; on non-NUMA, use `FADV_SEQUENTIAL` + `MAP_POPULATE` + `MADV_WILLNEED` for a fast bulk load. Plus a one-line warning when Linux `numa_balancing` (autonuma) is on, because kernel page migration sabotages first-touch.

## llama.cpp source (read @571d0d54)
- posix policy branch (fadvise SEQUENTIAL, MAP_POPULATE, madvise WILLNEED; NUMA branch disables prefetch + MADV_RANDOM): `src/llama-mmap.cpp:445-476`.
- autonuma warning: `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c:709`.
- NUMA wired into the loader: `src/llama-model-loader.cpp:1349-1358`.

## fak seam / gap
- fak maps weights read-only with a plain `syscall.Mmap(..., PROT_READ, MAP_SHARED)` and **no madvise-at-map**: `internal/model/mmap_unix.go:34`.
- fak has per-expert `MADV_WILLNEED` readahead (`internal/model/expert_readahead.go:76`) but no **map-time NUMA policy**.
- fak DOES run NUMA: `internal/compute/numa_replica_store*.go`, `internal/compute/decode_numaschedule.go`, `numactl --interleave` references. So today the weight mmap can fault every page onto one node under NUMA, defeating the interleave story fak already invests in.

## First checkable step
In the unix mmap path, after mapping, issue `MADV_RANDOM` when the process is NUMA-multinode (reuse the existing NUMA detection) else `MADV_SEQUENTIAL` + best-effort populate; add a startup log if `/proc/sys/kernel/numa_balancing` reads `1`. Guard behind the existing `madviseWillneed` platform split (no-op on Windows). Unit-test the policy selector.

Provenance: study-repo pass over llama.cpp @571d0d54 (2026-07-18). Related: #4974 (in-process NUMA interleave decode placement).

records.title: perf(cpu): online weight repack into SIMD-interleaved blocks selected by runtime CPU-feature detection
records.body:
Borrow from a witnessed `/study` of **llama.cpp @571d0d54** (`https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp`). License MIT — verdict **inspire** (clean-room, cite-only, no bytes vendored).

## Axis (the one property this targets)
At load time, re-serialize a row-major quant weight (Q4_K / Q8_0 / ...) into an N-wide **column-interleaved** block layout so the CPU GEMM loads contiguous vector lanes with **no gather**; the interleave width (4x4 / 4x8 / 8x8) is chosen by **runtime** SIMD-feature detection. One-time load cost; every subsequent token's matmul becomes streaming-load-bound instead of gather-bound.

## llama.cpp source (read @571d0d54)
- Repack at set_tensor: `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/repack.cpp:4726-4733`.
- Layout picker: `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/repack.cpp:4528`.
- Feature branch (AVX2 -> 8x8, NEON+i8mm -> 4x8, dotprod -> 4x4, RVV): `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/repack.cpp:4573-4599`.
- Interleave primitive: `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/repack.cpp:143-205`.

## fak seam / gap
fak dequants quant weights via `internal/ggufload/gguf_dequant_simd_amd64.s` and repacks for the **GPU** at upload (`internal/compute/cuda.go:378`, ColMajor transpose), but there is **no CPU-side load-time repack into an interleaved block layout** for the host GEMM. Repo-scoped issue search is empty. fak's CPU decode (Qwen3.6 campaign #4623, mac offload #2722) is exactly where this throughput lever applies.

## Why their users needed it
A local user runs one fixed model for the whole session on whatever CPU they have; paying a one-time repack to make every token's expert/dense matmul SIMD-lane-contiguous is free amortized, and the layout MUST be auto-picked because the binary ships to unknown CPUs.

## First checkable step (kept small — do NOT boil the ocean)
Spike ONE quant type — Q4_K experts, the host-resident bulk under `internal/model/moe_offload.go`: a `repackQ4KInterleaved(width)` + an AVX2/NEON `runtime`-detected width selector (reuse `golang.org/x/sys/cpu`), behind a benchmark on the fak microbench harness proving the interleaved host GEMM beats the current path. One type, measured, then decide whether to generalize.

Provenance: study-repo pass over llama.cpp @571d0d54 (2026-07-18). Related: #4623, #2722.

records.title: feat(agent): witnessed think-token budget — count reasoning tokens and force </think> exit at a cap (sglang-study)
records.body:
## Borrow (study-repo, sglang @ b8ec5449)

Enforce a per-request **think-token budget**: count the tokens the model emits inside its
`<think>…</think>` reasoning span and, when the budget is hit, force the model out of thinking
(allow only the think-end token). sglang bounds a reasoning trace deterministically at the
logit-mask level instead of leaving its length to the provider's discretion.

## Source (sglang, Apache-2.0, INSPIRE — clean-room Go, no bytes vendored)

- `python/sglang/srt/constrained/reasoner_grammar_backend.py:44-46@b8ec5449` — "enforces
  max_think_tokens budget. When the budget is exhausted, only think_end_id is allowed, forcing
  the model to exit the thinking phase."
- `python/sglang/srt/constrained/reasoner_grammar_backend.py:137@b8ec5449` — `_can_think_more()`
  gate: `max_think_tokens < 0 or tokens_in_think < max_think_tokens`.
- `python/sglang/srt/constrained/grammar_manager.py:117-129@b8ec5449` — per-request
  `thinking_budget` custom param → `req.grammar.max_think_tokens`.
- `python/sglang/srt/sampling/custom_logit_processor.py:75-80@b8ec5449` — sampler-level
  enforcement of the same budget.

## The one axis

A fak-OWNED, WITNESSED cap on the number of reasoning tokens per turn, with a forced
`</think>` exit at the budget — distinct from a provider's opaque `reasoning_effort` string.

## fak seam + gap (witnessed ABSENT on-axis)

fak today only FORWARDS a provider's coarse `reasoning_effort` string
(`internal/agent/chat.go:1223`, `cmd/fak/guard_codex.go:121`, `internal/agent/kimi_k3.go:32`) —
it neither counts nor bounds the think tokens the provider actually spends, and there is no
forced exit. fak's reasoning code is response-side stripping only (`internal/agent/reasoning*.go`).
Two enforcement paths:

- **Native kernel** — force the think-end token at the budget in the logit mask at
  `internal/grammar/compile.go:180` (`MaskLogits`), reusing the reasoning-end boundary detection
  already scoped in #5262.
- **Hosted provider** — enforce by a stop-policy at the gateway/stream: cut (or stop-witness)
  the stream when the counted think-token span exceeds the budget, and PRICE the overspend
  rather than trusting the effort string.

## Why sglang's users needed it / fak fit

sglang bounds a reasoning model's think phase so a pathological chain-of-thought can't consume
the whole latency/compute budget. fak's angle is cost governance + witness: fak already prices
turns and governs cost, so a witnessed think-token budget turns reasoning spend into a bounded,
audited quantity instead of an opaque provider knob.

## Scope

Smallest independently-shippable leaf: a pure think-token counter + budget gate (native mask
forced-exit; hosted stop-policy is a follow-on if this lands native-first). No new decode loop.

Companion: **#5262** (reasoning-end boundary detection — the prerequisite this budget reuses).
Study note: `docs/notes/CONCEPT-STUDY-SGLANG-2026-07-18.md`. Superset epic **#2236**.

records.title: feat(resume): soft watchdog — capture a diagnostic state dump on an alive-but-stalled session before nudge/revive (sglang-study)
records.body:
## Borrow (study-repo, sglang @ b8ec5449)

A **soft watchdog** that, when a worker is alive-but-stalled, captures a diagnostic STATE DUMP
(stack of every worker) WITHOUT killing it — so the wedge is debuggable — kept distinct from the
hard kill/respawn path. sglang runs a soft watchdog daemon separate from the hard one and
dumps every scheduler's stack via py-spy for post-mortem before any hard action.

## Source (sglang, Apache-2.0, INSPIRE — clean-room Go, no bytes vendored)

- `python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:1080-1089@b8ec5449` — `init_soft_watchdog` (soft=True)
  starts a daemon thread SEPARATE from the hard `watchdog`.
- `python/sglang/srt/utils/cudacore_pyspy_dump_utils.py:70-71@b8ec5449` — `pyspy_dump_schedulers()`,
  a py-spy stack dump of all schedulers (diagnostic capture, no kill).
- `python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:4520@b8ec5449` (`faulthandler.enable()`) and
  `:4609@b8ec5449` (`send_signal(SIGQUIT)`) — the HARD path the soft dump precedes.

## The one axis

Capture a reversible DIAGNOSTIC dump of an alive-but-stalled session BEFORE the destructive
intervention — soft (observe) distinct from hard (revive/kill).

## fak seam + gap (witnessed ABSENT on-axis)

fak's watchdogs are pure relaunch/intervention decision cores that capture NO diagnostic state:

- `internal/resume/trajectory_watchdog.go:32-36` — the alive-but-stalled branch returns
  `NUDGE` then escalates to `REVIVE_WITH_FRESH_ANCHOR`; it records only an action + reason string.
- `internal/resume/watchdog.go:151` (`DecideWatchdogRow`) — launch/skip decision, no dump.

A grep for `dump|goroutine|pprof|SIGQUIT|stack` over the resume/supervision code finds nothing
on-point. The `NUDGE` branch (`trajectory_watchdog.go:34`) is the natural attach point: before it
nudges or revives, capture the stalled session's trajectory-state (and, for a local process, a
goroutine/pprof stack dump) into the durable record so the stall is diagnosable after the fact.

## Why sglang's users needed it / fak fit

A production serving fleet that only kills-and-restarts a wedged worker throws away the evidence
of WHY it wedged. fak's fleet has the same failure mode; and fak already sells witnessed,
auditable interventions — a soft state-dump makes the "alive but stalled" verdict carry evidence
instead of a bare reason string, and feeds the crashed-session recovery story (#3871).

## Scope

Smallest independently-shippable leaf: a diagnostic-capture step on the alive-but-stalled branch
that writes a state/stack snapshot to the durable session record, gated behind a soft timeout,
BEFORE the existing nudge/revive decision runs. No change to the revive path itself.

Related: supervision epic **#4748**, crashed-session-WIP epic **#3871**.
Study note: `docs/notes/CONCEPT-STUDY-SGLANG-2026-07-18.md`. Superset epic **#2236**.

records.title: feat(serving): prefix-delta KV handoff — destination advertises its held prefix, sender ships only the suffix (sglang-study)
records.body:
## Borrow (study-repo, sglang @ b8ec5449)

On a node-to-node KV handoff, transfer ONLY the suffix the destination does not already hold:
the **destination advertises its cached-prefix length**, and the **sender skips that prefix** and
ships only the delta. sglang's prefill→decode disaggregation does exactly this so a decode node
that already has a warm L1 prefix never re-receives it over the wire.

## Source (sglang, Apache-2.0, INSPIRE — clean-room Go, no bytes vendored)

- `python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/prefill.py:297-300@b8ec5449` — sender side:
  `decode_prefix_len = req.disagg_kv_sender.pop_decode_prefix_len()`;
  `req.start_send_idx = decode_prefix_len`;
  `num_kv_indices_to_send = num_kv_indices - decode_prefix_len` — start sending at the
  destination-held offset, send only the delta.
- `python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/decode.py:974-980@b8ec5449` — destination side computes
  `prefix_len` (tokens already on device, "L1 hit") vs `total_prefix_len` (full prefix), and the
  `[prefix_len, total)` range is what it requests; this is the protocol's `decode_prefix_len`.

## The one axis

A held-prefix negotiation on a KV handoff — the receiver reports how much of the prefix it
already caches, the sender computes the divergence offset and transfers only the uncached suffix.

## fak seam + gap (witnessed PARTIAL on-axis)

fak has both halves but not the handshake that joins them:

- The transfer can already move an arbitrary suffix span — `internal/model/paged_kv_transfer.go:60`
  (`MarshalPagedKVTransfer(seq, transfer, from, n)`) — but `from` is **caller-supplied**; there is
  no protocol where the destination advertises its held prefix and the sender derives `from`.
- The delta MATH already exists and is standalone — `internal/cachemeta/prefix_stability.go:224`
  (`AlmostHit(reusableHitLen, longestCachedPrefixLen)` → `UncachedCommonPrefixTokens`, the gap
  above the deepest cached extent).

Missing: the negotiation that wires the destination's `longestCachedPrefixLen` into
`MarshalPagedKVTransfer`'s `from`, so a KV teleport (#4301) / heterogeneous P/D split (#4302)
skips the prefix the destination already holds instead of re-teleporting the full KV.

## Why sglang's users needed it / fak fit

At disaggregation scale the prefix is often the largest, most-shared part of the KV; re-sending
it dominates handoff bandwidth. fak's fleet-KV-mobility story (#4296) has the same cost, and fak
already computes the divergence offset for pricing — this borrow spends that same number to cut
teleport bytes, and the skipped range is witnessed (destination proves it held the prefix).

## Scope

Smallest independently-shippable leaf: a handoff-request field carrying the destination's
held-prefix length + a sender-side `from = min(held, common)` derivation feeding the existing
`MarshalPagedKVTransfer`. Reuses `AlmostHit`; no new transport.

Parent: distributed-compute epic **#4296**; builds on KV-teleport **#4301**, P/D split **#4302**,
gossip prefix directory **#4303**. Study note: `docs/notes/CONCEPT-STUDY-SGLANG-2026-07-18.md`.
Superset epic **#2236**.

records.title: epic(mooncake-study): mine Mooncake (KVCache-centric disaggregated LLM serving) for fak — witnessed borrows
records.body:
## epic(mooncake-study): mine Mooncake (KVCache-centric disaggregated LLM serving) for fak — witnessed borrows

A `/study --deep` pass over **kvcache-ai/Mooncake** (`https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake`, pinned **`@5d87a43d2474`**, "[Store] Serialize ssd_total_capacity_bytes in local disk snapshot (#2927)"). Mooncake is the serving substrate for **Kimi / Moonshot AI** and won FAST'25 Best Paper.

Sibling of the other serving/cache study epics: #5256 (TensorRT-LLM), #3900 (ktransformers), #3983 (kvcache-factory), #3366 (LMCache), #4352 (colibri), #4207 (inference-radar). Feeds the disaggregation admission-kernel epic #3259, the MoE net-tok/s coalescing epic #5243, and the distributed-compute-substrate epic #4296.

### License gate
Mooncake is **Apache-2.0** (`LICENSE-APACHE`); fak is Apache-2.0. All candidates are C++/CUDA/Python → Go, so **every borrow is `inspire`** (clean-room, source-cited). **No bytes vendored.**

### Worldview (reconstructed from defaults / non-goals / benchmarks)
Mooncake pools otherwise-idle CPU/DRAM/SSD across a GPU cluster into a **shared, tiered, distributed KV-cache object store** so that a *separated* prefill cluster and decode cluster reuse KV globally, moved over a topology-aware multi-NIC RDMA fabric. Its whole design optimizes **cluster goodput under SLO** at hyperscale where **a rank/NIC/peer is broken at all times**: eviction is watermark-driven and on by default, everything expensive is opt-in, and *nothing* is allowed to block the put/get/transfer hot path or deadlock on a dead peer. The three pillars: **Transfer Engine** (topology-aware NIC ranking + retry-indexed failover + rail circuit-breakers; the `tent/` subtree is a QoS/deadline-aware rewrite), **Store** (master-driven placement, two-band near-LRU eviction, soft/hard pin classes, CMSketch-gated promotion, reserve/commit tenant quota, fork-COW snapshot + oplog HA), and **EP/PG** (fault-tolerant elastic expert parallelism via an `active_ranks` membership mask).

The recurring finding vs fak: **fak has the observability + identity halves strongly** (distinct CacheFill/Evict/Revoke events `internal/gateway` sink, self-instrumenting `internal/tracesink`, gap-detecting `pkg/fakclient/changes_consumer.go`, fencing tokens `internal/scmbridge/fence.go`, COW `PagedKV.Fork()`, capability matrix `internal/model/kv_transport_registry.go`, GDSF value-density eviction `internal/cacheprice/retention.go`) **but stops short of the closed-loop CONTROL halves** Mooncake pushes into. This epic files the four cleanest net-new control borrows; the rest are carried in the study note.

### Fan-out coverage (5 sub-readers, verified against the tree @5d87a43d)
store-core (allocator / master / eviction / replication / tenant-quota / hot-cache), store-HA + storage-tiers (leadership / oplog / snapshot / standby / io_uring / SPDK / 3FS), transfer-engine (topology / multi-transport / failover / `tent`), ep + pg + rl (fault-tolerant EP, ProcessGroup), integration + kv_event + engram + benchmarks/traces. **Completeness-critic residue:** `mooncake-p2p-store` (weight-transfer demo, superseded by the checkpoint-engine repo — off-axis), `mooncake-common` (shared etcd/k8s-lease utils, covered via HA), `monitoring`/`docker`/`mooncake-wheel` (packaging) — justified skips.

### Filed children (net-new control borrows)
- CMSketch frequency-gated **anti-thrash re-admission** for the disaggregated KV pool (source `mooncake-store/src/master_service.cpp:5236@5d87a43d` + `include/count_min_sketch.h:35@5d87a43d`; fak seam `internal/radixkv/thrash.go` is observe-only)
- **active-rank membership mask** for fault-tolerant expert dispatch/combine (source `mooncake-store`… `mooncake-ep/src/mooncake_ep_kernel.cu:708@5d87a43d`; fak seam `internal/model/v4_expert_collective.go:19` fails closed) — cross-links #5243
- **earliest-deadline admission ordering + predicted-miss load-shedding** (source `mooncake-transfer-engine/tent/src/runtime/admission_queue.cpp:227@5d87a43d`; fak seam `internal/dispatchtick/priority.go` + `footprint_ceiling.go`) — cross-links #3259
- **receiver-granted credit flow control** for cross-node KV transfer backpressure (source `mooncake-transfer-engine/tent/src/runtime/receiver_credit.cpp:122@5d87a43d`; fak seam `internal/loaddebounce/loaddebounce.go` coalesces/drops, no credits) — cross-links #3259 / #4296

### Candidates carried in the note (mapped to existing epics / cards)
- Two-band target/floor eviction + **soft-pin/hard-pin** per-object classes → overlaps #3900 (eviction/pinning/residency); fak PARTIAL (`internal/radixkv/eviction_strategy.go` SLRU protected segment + lease immunity, no operator pin classes).
- Reserve/commit **tenant quota** + largest-remainder **proportional fair-share** → maps to fairness-floors #2674; fak PARTIAL/ABSENT.
- Declarative capability-filtered **transport selection policy** + topology-aware NUMA/PCIe **path ranking** → fak PARTIAL (`kv_transport_registry.go` hardcoded first-match single backend; `numa_interleave.go` placement-only). RDMA/hardware-gated for the executor; the selection policy is CPU-witnessable.
- **fork-COW BGSAVE snapshot**, snapshot+oplog log-compaction bootstrap, view-version fencing → fak PARTIAL/PRESENT (`PagedKV.Fork()` COW, `scmbridge/fence.go` fencing PRESENT).
- Released **prefix-block-hash trace** + **wall-vs-storage-IO latency** benchmark decomposition → overlaps #5256 (block-hash events) / #4254 (wall-clock plane); fak PARTIAL.
- PRESENT-on-axis cards (witnessed, not filed): distinct cache-event kinds, countable-loss consumer, self-instrumenting emitter, fencing token.

Note: `docs/notes/CONCEPT-STUDY-MOONCAKE-2026-07-18.md` (full candidate table + witness verdicts).

records.title: feat(cacheprice): count-min-sketch frequency-gated anti-thrash re-admission for the disaggregated KV pool
records.body:
Parent epic: #5289 (mooncake-study). Sibling cache epics: #3900, #5256, #3661.

### Borrow (inspire, clean-room — Mooncake is Apache-2.0, no bytes vendored)
Mooncake gates a KV object's **re-promotion** from a slow tier (LOCAL_DISK) back to the fast DRAM tier behind a **CountMinSketch frequency threshold**, so a key that gets touched once after eviction is NOT copied back on the first hit — only a genuinely re-hot key earns a promotion, and only when DRAM has headroom and a global in-flight promotion budget isn't saturated.

- **Source** `mooncake-store/src/master_service.cpp:5236@5d87a43d` (`TryPushPromotionQueue`: freq gate `:5249` → DRAM-watermark gate `:5260` → dedup `:5277` → cluster-wide in-flight cap `:5291`) and the self-decaying sketch `mooncake-store/include/count_min_sketch.h:35@5d87a43d` (counters halve once `total_increments` crosses `width*depth`, so stale popularity ages out with no timer).
- **Axis**: frequency-**sketch**-gated re-admission to the fast cache tier to prevent promotion **thrash** under a bounded promotion budget.
- **Their-worldview reason**: after eviction a re-accessed key is common at Kimi scale; promoting on first touch thrashes DRAM, so only keys whose sketched frequency clears a threshold (with headroom + an in-flight cap) are copied back.

### fak witness (ABSENT on-axis, witnessed twice + raw grep)
- `internal/radixkv/thrash.go` is explicitly **OBSERVE-ONLY**: it records an evicted victim's identity and later notices a reuse gap, but the header states it *"never steers victim choice"* — it is a detector, not an admission gate.
- The SLRU protected segment (`internal/radixkv/eviction_strategy.go`) gives frequency-based *protection* (`hits>=2`) but there is **no sketch** and **no re-admission gate** on promotion back into a fast tier.
- No count-min / TinyLFU anywhere in the tree (grepped `count-min`, `sketch`, `TinyLFU`, `promote`, `readmit`).
- `internal/cacheprice/retention.go` already prices GDSF value-density eviction — this borrow is the **admission** dual it lacks: a cheap frequency estimator that gates *whether to re-admit at all*.

### Scope (ship-alone leaf)
1. Tier-1 foundation primitive `internal/cmsketch` (plain ints, imports nothing internal): fixed width×depth uint8 counters, `Add`/`Estimate`, and self-decay-on-saturation — mirrors `count_min_sketch.h`. Ships + unit-tests alone.
2. A gate `func ShouldReadmit(freq, threshold int, headroom bool, inflight, cap int) bool` that `internal/radixkv` (or the disaggregated pool) can call before re-promoting an evicted prefix.

**First checkable step**: land `internal/cmsketch` with a table test proving decay halves all counters at the saturation boundary and estimate is an upper bound; no radixkv wiring yet.

Labels: enhancement, agentic-serving, prompt-caching, class:dev.

records.title: feat(moe): active-rank membership mask for fault-tolerant expert dispatch/combine — partial-but-valid output around a dead expert-owner
records.body:
Parent epic: #5289 (mooncake-study). Cross-links: #5243 (net-tok/s MoE coalescing), #4296 (distributed compute substrate).

### Borrow (inspire, clean-room — Mooncake is Apache-2.0, no bytes vendored)
Mooncake's fault-tolerant expert parallelism threads a single mutable **`active_ranks` membership vector** through **both** MoE dispatch and combine. It is simultaneously the routing **mask** (skip a dead expert-owner rank) and the fault **ledger** (a receiver flips a peer inactive on timeout instead of spinning forever). The combine reduction then sums **only live** expert contributions, emitting a **partial-but-valid** output vector rather than crashing the batch.

- **Source**: combine skips a failed expert-rank `mooncake-store`… `mooncake-ep/src/mooncake_ep_kernel.cu:708@5d87a43d` (`expert_src_rank = topk_idx/num_local_experts; if(!active_ranks[expert_src_rank]) continue;`); dispatch spin-loop flips a non-responding peer inactive on a cycle-budget timeout `mooncake-ep/src/mooncake_ep_kernel.cu:417@5d87a43d`; the vector is caller-owned and reused across the round-trip `mooncake-ep/src/mooncake_ep_buffer.cpp:272@5d87a43d` / `:431` (API contract `mooncake-ep/include/mooncake_ep_api.cuh:9`).
- **Axis**: route-around-a-failed-expert-owner in MoE dispatch/combine → degraded partial output instead of a hung/failed collective.
- **Their-worldview reason**: in a 100-way EP group a single hung GPU would wedge every rank's forward pass; dropping one expert's share of a token is far cheaper than failing the whole batch.

### fak witness (ABSENT on-axis)
- `internal/model/v4_expert_collective.go` dispatch/combine reduces per-rank partials **in rank order but FAILS CLOSED** (`ErrV4ExpertPlacement`) on any rank/width mismatch (`:18-19`); there is **no membership vector** masking a failed rank and **no degraded partial-but-valid output** (confirmed by `v4_expert_collective_test.go`).
- The Go policy is fully CPU-witnessable even though Mooncake's is a CUDA kernel — the borrow is the **membership-mask + skip-in-reduction** contract, not the kernel math.

### Scope (ship-alone leaf)
Add an optional `activeRanks []bool` (default all-true = today's behavior) to the v4 collective dispatch/combine so that: (a) a rank marked inactive contributes zero to the weighted combine and is skipped in the reduction, and (b) the combine still produces a valid vector over the live subset. No timeout/detection wiring in this leaf — the caller supplies membership.

**First checkable step**: a Go test that feeds a 4-rank collective with rank 2 marked inactive and asserts the combined output equals the exact reduction over ranks {0,1,3} (partial-but-valid), instead of `ErrV4ExpertPlacement`.

Labels: enhancement, moe, agentic-serving, class:dev.

records.title: feat(dispatchtick): earliest-deadline admission ordering + predicted-miss load-shedding
records.body:
Parent epic: #5289 (mooncake-study). Cross-links: #3259 (disaggregation admission kernel).

### Borrow (inspire, clean-room — Mooncake is Apache-2.0, no bytes vendored)
Mooncake's `tent` admission queue orders pending transfers **earliest-deadline-first**, promotes near-deadline owners, and — the load-bearing half — **drops** degradation-eligible requests it **predicts will miss** their deadline (`predicted_time / window >= threshold`), shedding doomed work so the survivors keep their SLO instead of everyone missing.

- **Source** `mooncake-transfer-engine/tent/src/runtime/admission_queue.cpp:227@5d87a43d` (`pickForDispatch` EDF ordering + proximity promotion; predicted-miss `shouldDrop` `:279`; bounded owners/bytes admit `tryAdmit` `:79`). Pure policy, CPU-witnessable — no RDMA in the decision path.
- **Axis**: earliest-**deadline**-ordered admission + **predicted-miss** load-shedding under contention (vs priority-weight ordering + a measured-resource ceiling).
- **Their-worldview reason**: under KV-transfer overload a late prefetch should be shed (or recomputed locally) rather than blow every request's SLO; predicting the miss lets it shed *before* wasting the transfer.

### fak witness (PARTIAL — enhancement to an existing seam)
- `internal/dispatchtick/priority.go` orders by **priority weight** (+ optional aging with a "starvation deadline") — priority, not earliest-deadline.
- `internal/dispatchtick/footprint_ceiling.go` sheds admission via `RefuseHostFootprint` on a **measured resource ceiling** — reactive shedding, not **predicted-deadline-miss** shedding.
- So fak has load-shedding-under-pressure but **no EDF ordering and no predict-then-shed** gate. This files as an enhancement to the dispatchtick admission path (and is the concrete scheduling policy the disaggregation admission-kernel epic #3259 would host).

### Scope (ship-alone leaf)
A tier-1 policy `internal/deadlineadmit` (plain ints, no internal imports): given a slice of `{id, deadline, predictedCost, degradable}` and a `now`, return (a) the EDF dispatch order and (b) the set to shed because `predictedFinish` would exceed `deadline` by the drop threshold and the item is degradable. `dispatchtick` adopts it as an optional ordering/shedding mode.

**First checkable step**: table test — three items, the middle one degradable and predicted to miss; assert EDF order = [earliest, latest] and the middle is shed, while a non-degradable predicted-miss is retained (never silently dropped).

Labels: enhancement, dispatch, agentic-serving, class:dev.

records.title: feat(kvtransport): receiver-granted credit flow control for cross-node KV transfer backpressure
records.body:
Parent epic: #5289 (mooncake-study). Cross-links: #3259 (disaggregation admission kernel), #4296 (distributed compute substrate).

### Borrow (inspire, clean-room — Mooncake is Apache-2.0, no bytes vendored)
Mooncake's `tent` runtime meters a sender with **receiver-granted credits**: the receiver grants cumulative, monotonic-non-decreasing credits per `(receiver_session, sender_peer, qos_class)`, and a sender must hold credit (two-phase reserve/rollback per resource, epoch+sequence deduped) before it may transfer. A fast prefill node therefore cannot overrun a slow decode node's KV-ingest buffers.

- **Source** `mooncake-transfer-engine/tent/src/runtime/receiver_credit.cpp:122@5d87a43d` (`tryReserve` / `rollbackReservation`; cumulative grant apply `applyUpdate` `:76`). Pure in-memory ledger — CPU-witnessable, no RDMA in the credit logic.
- **Axis**: **receiver-granted credit** backpressure (the consumer meters the producer per class) — distinct from producer-side coalescing/drop.
- **Their-worldview reason**: prefill produces KV faster than decode ingests it; credits let the *receiver* set the pace per QoS class instead of dropping or blocking blindly at the source.

### fak witness (ABSENT on-axis)
- fak's backpressure primitives are **producer-side**: `internal/loaddebounce/loaddebounce.go` (dedup + reset-on-change coalescing) and the bounded drop-oldest change feeds. These coalesce or drop; none is a **receiver-granted credit** a sender must hold.
- The KV transfer plane `internal/model/kv_transport_registry.go` selects a backend but has no flow-control ledger between a producer and a consumer of KV blocks.
- Grepped `credit`, `flow control`, `backpressure`, `grant`, `window` — no receiver-credit mechanism.

### Scope (ship-alone leaf)
A tier-1 primitive `internal/flowcredit` (plain ints/maps, no internal imports): a per-`(receiver, sender, class)` ledger with `Grant(cumulative)` (monotonic, idempotent by seq), `TryReserve(n) bool`, and `Rollback(n)`. Ships + unit-tests standalone; the cross-node KV transport plane (or the #3259 admission kernel) adopts it later.

**First checkable step**: table test proving (a) a reserve past the granted cumulative credit is refused, (b) a stale/lower cumulative grant is ignored (monotonic), and (c) reserve+rollback restores available credit exactly.

Labels: enhancement, distributed, agentic-serving, class:dev.

records.title: fix(gitgate): stale/orphaned .git/index.lock wedges fak commit fleet-wide — no worker-reachable reclaim
records.body:
## Symptom

A stale/orphaned `.git/index.lock` in the hot shared clone (`C:\work\fak`) wedges
**all** index-writing git ops fleet-wide — every `fak commit` refuses with
`LOCK_BUSY: another git process is active (index.lock held Ns)` and no commit lands.

## Evidence (observed 2026-07-19 ~00:04–00:12 local)

- `.git/index.lock` present, size ~1.27 MB (a fully-written index snapshot), **mtime
  frozen at 00:04:43** while wall-clock advanced past 00:12 — held >7 min with zero
  mtime advance.
- No live git process is the holder: a scan of `Win32_Process` for `git.exe` shows only
  (a) fresh `git.exe` staging ops that spawn and die in 1–2 s (they bounce off the lock),
  (b) `git fsmonitor--daemon` processes ~1.5–2.3 days old, and (c) NO process aged
  ~120–400 s and none whose command line contains `commit`/`write-tree`/`update-index`.
  A live index writer would advance the lock mtime; nothing is.
- Interpretation: the holder wrote the new index to `index.lock` and died before the
  atomic rename to `index`, leaving the real `index` intact and the lock orphaned.

## Why a worker cannot self-recover

- `fak commit` reclaims its **own** `fak-commit.lock` when the holder pid is dead
  (`LOCK_BROKEN holder_dead ... allowed`) but does **not** reclaim git's `.git/index.lock`
  — it only reports `LOCK_BUSY` and refuses.
- The capability floor refuses **every** Bash write/delete to `.git/index.lock` as a
  guarded core-lock path (`SELF_MODIFY/ESCALATE`) — plain remove, remove-without-flags,
  and move-aside were all refused. So a worker has no admissible path to clear it.
- No fak verb reaps a stale git index.lock: `fak dev git-maint` is lock-aware object-DB
  consolidation (would itself abort on a held lock), `fak treedoctor` has no lock option,
  and #4605 reaped `refs/fak/locks/session-*.lock` refs — not `.git/index.lock`.

## Impact

Fleet-wide: while the orphaned lock stands, no session can land a commit through the
sanctioned path. This is a distinct sibling of the orphaned-lock cluster #4602/#4603/#4605
(loose objects / dead fsmonitor / session ref-locks), none of which covers `.git/index.lock`.

## Proposed fix

- Teach `fak commit` (or a `fak dev git-maint` sub-mode) to detect a stale `.git/index.lock`
  — holder pid dead **and** mtime frozen past a grace window (e.g. > N s with no live
  index-writing git process) — and reap it under the same holder-dead evidence it already
  uses for `fak-commit.lock`, so recovery routes through the trusted binary rather than a
  guarded Bash op.
- Alternatively expose a narrow, witnessed `fak dev git-maint --reap-stale-index-lock`
  that applies the frozen-mtime + no-live-writer test before removing.

## Provenance

Discovered while landing the witness test for #2890 (feat(dispatch): collision-safe shared
board). That change is complete and green (test passes ×5, vet/gofmt clean, `fak commit
--preview` 100/100 stamped `(fak leaseref)` binding #2890); it is blocked from landing
solely by this orphaned lock and will auto-land when the lock clears.

records.title: guard managed-cache: forced-on OAuth downgrade misses the passthrough path (oauthSource empty)
records.body:
## Gap

Commit `43cbdb14a4da` (`fix(guard): degrade forced --managed-cache on to passive on subscription OAuth`) stops a forced `--managed-cache on` from crash-looping a subscription-OAuth seat on the provider's 1h-TTL 400. It keys the downgrade on `in.oauthSource != ""` in `resolveGuardManagedCache` (`cmd/fak/guard_managed_cache.go`).

`oauthSource` is only populated on the **fak-resolved-OAuth** path (fak injects the subscription token). On the **passthrough** path — where the client (Claude Code) forwards its *own* OAuth bearer — `oauthSource` is empty, so the new downgrade branch does not fire: forced `on` still resolves `active:true` → the gateway authors a `ttl:"1h"` body → the provider 400s every turn → the seat crash-loops in ~30s.

## Evidence

5 rows in the local gateway-usage ledger (2026-07-18/19, contexts `claude` / `...\claude.exe`, OAuth) authored 3–6 upgrades with **zero traffic in any direction** (in=read=write=out=0), 20–42s uptime, `errored=0`, while 1000+ sibling sessions the same days served normally with `upgraded=0`. See `docs/notes/MANAGED-CACHE-FAMILY-OWN-SESSIONS-AUDIT-2026-07-18.md` §7 and the 2026-07-18 cache-frontier witness.

## Options

1. Detect the client-forwarded OAuth bearer (the `sk-ant-oat…` token shape on the passthrough `Authorization` header) and set a passthrough-OAuth signal the downgrade can read.
2. Degrade forced-`on` to passive whenever billing is **unknown** on the Anthropic wire (`apiKey == "" && oauthSource == ""`). Conservative — narrows honored `on` to proven-API-key billing, i.e. `on` ≈ `auto` on a passthrough Anthropic seat.
3. Fail-closed per-seat after the first observed 1h-tier 400 (needs the acceptance/rejection signal the audit names as the cheapest missing witness).

Also audit the `auto` branch (`oauthSource != ""` at the AUTO case) for the same passthrough blind spot — it appears safe via the `apiKey == ""` → passive path, but confirm.

## Interim mitigation (already applied)

`HKCU\Environment\FAK_MANAGED_CACHE` reverted `on` → `auto` on the dogfood box; `auto` stays passive on passthrough-OAuth, so the crash-loop is neutralized until a code fix lands.

records.title: fix(hooks): a pre-commit gate that errors is skipped silently — no stderr, no counter
records.body:
## Parent context
Follow-on finding from #2865 (fail-closed guard audit), itself part of #2834 (Track H). Recorded in `docs/proofs/failclosed-audit.md` as FINDING 1; fixing it was explicitly out of scope for #2865.

## Current state
`cmd/fak/hooks.go:139-143` continues past any gate whose Check returns an error:

    findings, gerr := g.Check(d)
    if gerr != nil {
        // a single gate that could-not-run is skipped (fail-open), the others still run.
        continue
    }

The fail-open itself is deliberate and contractual (`internal/hooks/hooks.go:36-39`, ErrCouldNotRun: "fail-open, never a block"), and the rationale is sound — a broken checker must not wedge every commit on a shared trunk.

## The defect
Not the fail-open: the SILENCE. There is no stderr line, no counter, and no distinction in the exit code between "all 17 gates ran clean" and "PUBLIC_LEAK errored and the other 16 ran clean". An operator cannot tell a green commit from a degraded one, so a persistently-broken security gate can go unnoticed indefinitely.

## In scope
Emit the skipped gate name on stderr; count skipped gates; surface the count in the `--json` output.

## Out of scope
Changing the fail-open to fail-closed. The never-wedge-the-fleet rationale still holds.

## Done condition
A commit erroring in one gate prints that gate name and a non-zero skipped count, while still exiting 0.

## Witness
A test that injects a gate whose Check returns ErrCouldNotRun and asserts the gate name appears on stderr and the skipped count is non-zero, while the exit code stays 0.

## Lane
cmd

records.title: fix(repoguard): separate a malformed PreToolUse payload from a guard bug in the fail-open path
records.body:
## Parent context
Follow-on finding from #2865 (fail-closed guard audit), itself part of #2834 (Track H). Recorded in `docs/proofs/failclosed-audit.md` as FINDING 2; fixing it was explicitly out of scope for #2865.

## Current state
`cmd/repoguard/main.go` fails open on any internal error and always exits 0, signalling a deny only through the JSON decision payload. The package doc states this plainly: "Fail-OPEN on any internal error (a guard bug must never wedge a live fleet)." On error it prints `repo_guard: internal error, allowing (%v)` and returns 0.

## The defect
That single fail-open branch collapses two different failure classes:

- a **guard bug** (a panic, a logic error in the classifier) — fail-open is clearly right here; a broken guard must not wedge a fleet;
- a **malformed payload** (an unmarshal failure on hook input) — this is attacker-influenceable input, and treating it identically means malformed input is a reliable way to obtain "allow".

The hook is a heuristic floor and not a sandbox by its own documentation, so this is a hardening item rather than a breach. But the two classes deserve different handling.

## In scope
Distinguish an unmarshal/parse failure from an internal guard error; decide the policy for the parse-failure class (at minimum a distinct journal reason and stderr line so it is countable via `repoguard --summary`).

## Out of scope
Changing the guard-bug fail-open default, and turning the hook into a sandbox.

## Done condition
A malformed payload produces a distinct, countable journal reason rather than being indistinguishable from a guard bug.

## Witness
A test feeding a malformed payload and asserting the distinct reason/label, alongside an existing internal-error case asserting the unchanged guard-bug behavior.

## Lane
cmd

records.title: feat(hooks): extend the fail-closed ledger gate to bind repoguard severities and the dos.toml reason vocabulary
records.body:
## Parent context

records.title: fix(tools): dispatch_worker_test opencode guard_wrap case is host-state dependent and reds the tools lane gate
records.body:
## Problem
`tools/dispatch_worker_test.py::test_guard_wrap_opencode_skips_without_base_url_but_wraps_with_one` fails on this host at the committed tip, independent of any working-tree change. It is one of the two acceptance gates named by dispatch-lane issue contracts, so it reds the lane gate for every `tools` worker.

The test asserts that `guard_wrap(..., backend="opencode", env={})` returns the argv UNCHANGED — i.e. with no base URL in the passed env, guard must not wrap. Observed instead:

```
AssertionError: Lists differ:
['/usr/bin/fak', 'guard', '--provider', 'openai', '--api-key-env',
 'FAK_OPENCODE_GUARD_UPSTREAM_API_KEY', '--addr', '127.0.0.1:63646', ...]
!= ['opencode', 'run', '--print-logs', ...]
```

Note the resolved `127.0.0.1:<port>`: despite `env={}` the code path reaches live host state and finds a base URL, so the "fail open when we don't know the upstream" branch never runs. The port differs run to run.

## Reproduced against the committed tip
Confirmed NOT caused by working-tree changes — extracting `HEAD:tools/dispatch_worker.py` to a temp path and calling `guard_wrap` with the test's exact arguments wraps identically:

```
COMMITTED-TIP wraps? True
first 8: ['/usr/bin/fak','guard','--provider','openai','--api-key-env',
          'FAK_OPENCODE_GUARD_UPSTREAM_API_KEY','--addr','127.0.0.1:65490']
```

## Likely cause
`opencode_guard_base_url` (or a helper it calls) consults process/host state — `os.environ`, a config file, or a running local serve — rather than only the injected `env` mapping. That makes the test host-dependent: it passes on a host with no local serve and fails on one with. Either the function should read only the injected `env`, or the test should inject the isolation it needs.

## Done condition
`python3 tools/dispatch_worker_test.py` is green on a host that has a local serve running, and the hermetic guarantee in the module docstring ("NOTHING live is ever invoked") holds for this path.

records.title: feat(mcpfootprint): compute the frequency axis of the footprint bill, not just marginal prefix tokens
records.body:
Follow-on from #2866 (the Footprint Ladder doctrine, shipped in `fda0828cf`).

## Current state

`docs/footprint-ladder.md` defines the ladder's decision variable as a two-axis bill:

```
footprint_bill(tool) = marginal_prefix_tokens(tool) x call_frequency(tool)
```

and documents `call_frequency` as "drawn from usage telemetry (the gateway usage logs / nightrun feed)".

**Only the first axis is computed.** A grep for `call_frequency` / `frequency` across
`internal/mcpfootprint/`, `cmd/fak/footprint.go`, and `cmd/fak/footprint_audit.go` returns
zero hits. `mcpfootprint.Price` prices marginal prefix tokens; `CheckFloor` ratchets that
total against `FloorBudgetTokens` (currently 5888) with frequency pinned at the
conservative `1.0` always-resident fallback.

## Why this is not a defect in #2866

The `1.0` fallback is deliberate and documented ("Frequency fallback for a brand-new tool"):
a new tool is scored at its maximum possible bill first. #2866's done condition is met.
This issue is the enhancement that makes the *second* axis real.

## Why now

With frequency fixed at 1.0, the gate cannot distinguish a cheap-and-hot tool from an
expensive-and-cold one — precisely the comparison the doctrine's rung-3 (deferral) advice
turns on. A reviewer justifying a rung-6 addition today raises a ceiling against an
assumed frequency, not a measured one.

## In scope

- Read per-tool selection counts from the existing gateway usage logs / nightrun feed.
- Surface a frequency-weighted bill in `fak footprint` (e.g. a `--bill` column), keeping the
  `1.0` fallback for tools with no telemetry.
- Keep provenance explicit (Law A2): estimated tokens x observed frequency, never a
  provider-billed count.

## Out of scope

- Changing `CheckFloor`'s always-resident ratchet. The floor gate should keep pricing the
  registry at worst case; the weighted bill is a reviewer-facing read, not a relaxation of
  the ceiling.
- New instrumentation, if the usage logs already carry per-tool selection counts.

## Done condition

`fak footprint` can print a frequency-weighted footprint bill for each always-sent tool,
sourced from real usage telemetry with a documented `1.0` fallback, and the doctrine doc's
bill formula cites the command that computes it.

## Witness

A `fak footprint` run showing a per-tool weighted bill with a non-1.0 observed frequency for
at least one tool, plus a test over the frequency-join in `internal/mcpfootprint`.

## Assumptions

- The gateway usage logs / nightrun feed already record per-tool selection counts. If they
  do not, this issue's first step is naming that missing instrumentation, not adding it here.

## Lane

docs / gateway (metric lives in `internal/mcpfootprint`, telemetry in the gateway feed)

## Stale claims to re-check

- Scope note: "**Scope:** design only. No NCCL/RCCL binding ... lands here." A real multi-process NCCL process group has since landed: `internal/compute/cuda_nccl_pg.cu` (`ncclGetUniqueId` -> `ncclCommInitRank` -> `ncclAllReduce`) with the Go bridge `internal/compute/cuda_collective_pg.go`.
- Ground-truth row: "CUDA is single-device by construction today. **[GAP]** `internal/compute/cuda_kernels.cu:52-57` (`cudaSetDevice(0)`)." Per-rank device binding now exists: `fcuda_set_device(int device)` at `cuda_kernels.cu:233`, `fcuda_malloc_on` at `:242`. The `cudaSetDevice(0)` at `:63` is now only a probe.

## Drifted anchors in its own ground-truth table

- `compute.Backend` cited at `internal/compute/compute.go:318-344`; actual `type Backend interface` is at `:337`.
- `compute.CollectiveBackend` cited at `internal/compute/compute.go:346-408`; actual is at `:431`.

Not `[SHIPPED]`. Both new files compile only under `-tags cuda,nccl` with `FAK_CUDA_NCCL=1`, are excluded from the default `go build ./cmd/fak` and from a plain `-tags cuda` build, and self-declare `STATUS: unverified on a GPU-free host`.
