records.title: feat(policy): wire the T1 MountView refusal into the call-side adjudicator (it parses but never runs)
records.body:
Parent: #2576 · Spine: [agent-virtual-filesystem.md](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/explainers/agent-virtual-filesystem.md)

## What
`policy.MountViewRefusal` (the T1 mount-view reference monitor landed by #2577) is **not wired into the call-side adjudicator**. The manifest field parses, the pure kernel is correct and tested, but nothing on the request path ever calls it — so a declared `mount_view` is inert.

## Witness (empirical, reproducible)
A manifest declaring a view over `src` only:

```json
{ "version": "fak-policy/v1", "allow": ["Read","Write"],
  "mount_view": [ { "path": "src", "mode": "rw" } ] }
```

```
$ fak preflight --policy mv.json --tool Read --args '{"file_path":"src/main.go"}'
verdict=ALLOW reason=NONE by=monitor          # in view — correct

$ fak preflight --policy mv.json --tool Read --args '{"file_path":"secrets/id_rsa"}'
verdict=ALLOW reason=NONE by=monitor          # OUT OF VIEW — should be DENY DEFAULT_DENY
```

Corroborating: `fak policy --check examples/mountview-policy.json` prints all 17 floor dimensions and the mount view appears in **none** of them; `grep -rn MountViewRefusal --include=*.go .` finds no non-test caller.

## Why it matters
This is the one gate blocking acceptance item (a) of #2581 (the VM-vs-boundary witness): "an out-of-view `Read` refused by the mount view (T1)". `examples/vm-fs-guard/run.sh` can witness the write-side `SELF_MODIFY` refusal, the T2 quarantine, and the exit ledger — but it cannot witness a read-side out-of-view DENY, because no CLI path reaches the view. #2577 closed on the kernel half only.

## Done condition
`fak preflight --policy <manifest-with-mount_view> --tool Read --args '{"file_path":"<out-of-view>"}'` returns `verdict=DENY reason=DEFAULT_DENY`, and a read under a `ro` subtree with a write shape returns `POLICY_BLOCK` — the refusals `MountViewRefusal` already computes.

## Out of scope
- Changing `MountViewRefusal`'s semantics; it is already correct and unit-tested.
- Providing the filesystem; fak stays the boundary, not the FS provider.

## Notes / risk
The view is deny-by-default for any path matching no rule, so wiring it changes refusal behavior for every existing manifest that carries a `mount_view`. An empty/omitted view must stay a no-op (the kernel already fails open on that, deliberately) so the change is backward-compatible.

## Lane
policy

## Likely files
- `internal/adjudicator/decide.go`
- `internal/policy/mountview.go`

records.title: feat(conceptbench): wire the #2731 model-arm registry into cmd/conceptbench so a live arm can emit a headline row
records.body:
**Parent epic:** #2721 · unblocks #2741

## Wire the model-arm registry into the runnable conceptbench CLI

`internal/conceptbench` is imported by **nothing outside itself**:

```
$ grep -rln "internal/conceptbench" --include=*.go . | grep -v "^./internal/conceptbench"
(empty)
```

Nine closed leaves of #2721 (#2729–#2739) landed a green, fully-tested library —
the model-arm registry (`modelarm.go`, `Bind`/`Transport`), the dos-refereed
grader adapter, the six scenarios, and the `report.v1` honesty gate. All of it is
orphaned. `cmd/conceptbench` carries its own separate replay-only implementation
and never touches the package.

Consequence: **no headline (non-replay) row can be produced by any code path**,
regardless of API keys or host capability. This is a wiring gap, not a key gap.

### Current state (witnessed at `internal/conceptbench` + `cmd/conceptbench` green, `go test -count=1`)

- `cmd/conceptbench/spine.go:134-139` hard-refuses any arm whose `Source != "replay"`
  with `return 2`, and its message still reads *"until the model-driver registry
  (#2731) lands"* — but #2731 is **CLOSED**; the registry landed as a library.
- `cmd/conceptbench/spine.go:160` hard-codes `Mode: "replay"`.
- `cmd/conceptbench/spine.go:166` hard-codes `ResultClaimAllowed: false`.
- The one on-disk artifact, `experiments/agent-live/conceptbench/spine-replay.json`,
  is `mode:"replay"`, every row `source:"replay"`, `result_claim_allowed:false`.

So `report.go`'s honesty gate is correct and working — it has simply never been
handed a row it could pass.

## In scope

Make the registry reachable from the binary so a live arm can produce a headline row:

1. Import `internal/conceptbench` from `cmd/conceptbench`; bind a live `Transport`
   for the `gateway` arm (and `serve` where a local GGUF is present).
2. Replace the `Source != "replay"` hard refusal with a dispatch on arm kind: a
   `live` source resolves through the registry, `replay` keeps today's path.
3. Derive `Mode` and `ResultClaimAllowed` from the resolved arms instead of
   hard-coding them, so a genuinely live run can pass `report.go`'s existing gate.
4. Refresh the stale `#2731`-has-not-landed comment.

## Out of scope

- Running the official frontier-vs-small comparison (that is #2741's job once unblocked).
- Any change to `report.go`'s honesty gate — it is correct as written.

## Done condition

`cmd/conceptbench --spine` with a live-source arm emits a `fak.conceptbench.v1`
whose gate reports `headline_rows >= 1` and `result_claim_allowed: true`, and the
`arm_gated` refusal still fires (typed, not a crash) when no Transport is bound.

## Witness

A test in `cmd/conceptbench` that binds a stub live Transport and asserts the
emitted report carries `headline_rows >= 1`, plus the existing gated-arm refusal
test still passing.

## Acceptance gate

`go test ./cmd/conceptbench/ ./internal/conceptbench/ -count=1`

## Closure binding

Closing commit references this issue in the subject.

## Lane

cmd

## Likely files

- `cmd/conceptbench/spine.go`
- `cmd/conceptbench/main.go`
- `internal/conceptbench/modelarm.go`

## Assumptions (invalidating)

- **Invalidating assumption:** that a live gateway arm is reachable from a fleet
  host at all. If every arm is walled by entitlement, the registry classifies it
  `arm_gated`/walled and #2741 stays blocked on capability rather than wiring —
  that outcome should be recorded, not scored as a concept failure.

## Promotion / demotion evidence

- **Promotes** when a headline row appears and #2741's gap analysis can cite it.
- **Retire** if the epic decides the replay corpus is the intended terminal
  deliverable — in which case #2741's DoD should be rewritten to drop "real rows".

records.title: fix(boundarylint): TestTestSuitePolicy is red on the committed tip — two ungrandfathered change-detectors
records.body:
## What

`TestTestSuitePolicy` (`internal/boundarylint/changedetector_test.go:147`) **fails on the
committed tip**, with zero working-tree edits. Reproduced against `6306acd74` by
`git archive HEAD` into a clean temp dir, so this is trunk state, not a peer's dirty tree:

```
--- FAIL: TestTestSuitePolicy (0.95s)
    NEW change-detector test (not grandfathered in changeDetectorBaseline):
      cmd/coalescebench/coalescebench_test.go:161      len() frozen to the magic count 5
      internal/codexlifecycle/analytics_test.go:418    len() frozen to the magic count 8
```

Both files are committed and clean (`git status` reports nothing for either), so the
change-detector ratchet is red for **every** clone: any agent running the touched
package's suite inherits a red that is not theirs. Found while shipping #4070 in the same
package — that work is unrelated to this red and its own tests pass.

## Why it matters

The ratchet is shrink-only by design: a NEW change-detector must be converted to an
invariant, not grandfathered. Two landed without either, so the gate no longer
distinguishes "someone added change-detector debt" from "the trunk is already red" — the
signal that makes the ratchet worth having is currently off.

## Scope

- Convert the two flagged assertions to invariant assertions (assert the relation the
  count stands for), **or** `//boundarylint:ignore CHANGE_DETECTOR_TEST` each with a
  tracking issue if the fixed width is genuinely deliberate.
- Re-run `TestTestSuitePolicy` against a clean `git archive HEAD` checkout, not the
  working tree, so the fix is proven against trunk rather than local state.

## Non-goals

- Widening `changeDetectorBaseline` to grandfather these two in — the ratchet only ever
  tightens, and grandfathering would retire the signal instead of paying the debt.
- Any change to the SOFT families (`SKIP_DEBT`, `UNPARSEABLE_SOURCE`), which do not gate.

## Witness

`go test ./internal/boundarylint/ -count=1 -run TestTestSuitePolicy` exits 0 from a clean
`git archive HEAD` extraction. Independent progress evidence: the flagged file:line pairs

records.title: epic: Org Policy Plane — centrally-administered fak fleets (company/IT admin)
records.body:
## Epic: Org Policy Plane — centrally-administered fak fleets (company/IT admin)

**Parent:** #5170 (Policy Amendment Classes) · **Track label:** `org-policy` · **Class:** class:dev (kernel/guard) + class:infra · **Kind:** epic (decompose, don't dispatch)

### Why

Today a `fak` floor is authored and owned **per checkout**: a local operator edits a `fak-policy/v1` manifest or `.fak/guard/{allow,deny}.json` overlays, and that is the whole authority story. There is no way for a **company-level administrator** to set policy once and have a fleet of local `fak` instances read it, obey it, and report against it. IT cannot say "every enrolled dev box denies `deploy_prod` but MAY use the 1h cache tier and a 200-call/min budget," and cannot *raise* a team's ceiling centrally without touching each machine.

The user ask: *imagine `fak` administered by a company-level admin — local instances read AND set policy from a central source; IT enables/allows more usage, but inside a managed, company-controlled context.*

### The model — a new amendment channel, not a new floor

This extends #5170's amendment-channel model rather than inventing a parallel one. #5170 defines four amendment **classes** (FROZEN / RATCHET / GATED_WIDEN / SELF_AMENDABLE) and five **channels** (compiled-in, operator-overlay, live-reload, operator-escalation, agent-self). This epic adds a **sixth channel**:

- **`central` (org policy).** An out-of-band channel the wrapped agent cannot reach, whose authority sits **above** the on-disk operator overlay and **below** the compiled-in FROZEN floor. It is delivered as a **signed** manifest pulled from a company endpoint. It may:
  - **RATCHET** the floor fleet-wide (tighten: deny a tool, add egress blocks, union secret patterns) — honored by the existing most-restrictive fold.
  - **GATED_WIDEN** *per enrolled device/user/group* to **enable more usage** (raise `rate_limit` ceilings, unlock a model/cache tier, grant an account seat) — the IT-enable-more path, done by an authority the agent can't reach.
  - Never move a **FROZEN** knob (the compiled-in floor still caps every central grant).
  - A device operator may only **tighten further** than the org grant, never widen past it.

Precedence lattice (most to least authority): **compiled-in FROZEN floor → central org overlay → operator overlay → agent-self (closed)**.

### Managed-context requirements

1. **Trust anchor via enrollment.** Un-enrolled `fak` behaves exactly as today (no central authority). `fak enroll --org <url>` pins the org root public key + a device identity so the central plane can target grants.
2. **Signed, fresh, anti-rollback distribution.** A `fak-org-policy/v1` envelope wraps a `fak-policy/v1` body with issuer, signature, `not_before`/`expires`, `min_version`, and a device/user/group target selector. Local `fak` verifies against the pinned root key, caches last-good, tolerates offline up to a max-staleness bound, and past that bound **falls back to the compiled-in floor (refuse-to-widen), never fail-open**.
3. **Pull + optional push.** `--org-policy-url` / `FAK_ORG_POLICY_URL` fetch on startup + periodic refresh; long-lived `fak serve` reuses the existing `POST /v1/fak/policy/reload` seam for push.
4. **IT visibility.** Local `fak` emits redacted adjudication + usage receipts to an org sink so IT sees fleet activity.
5. **Explainability.** `fak org status` / `fak policy explain` shows the resolved posture — which channel set which knob, and the staleness of the central manifest.

### Children

- **Research:** R1 prior-art + threat model; R2 signing/freshness/key model spike; R3 precedence + entitlement semantics spike.
- **Work:** W1 `central` amendment channel in the registry; W2 signed `fak-org-policy/v1` envelope + verifier; W3 remote pull + cache + offline fallback; W4 precedence fold + `fak org status`; W5 `fak enroll` trust anchor + device identity; W6 central usage-entitlement grants (enable-more); W7 audit-telemetry sink (IT visibility).

### Invariants this epic must preserve

- The `central` channel can never weaken a FROZEN knob (red-team amendment matrix).
- A stale/expired/bad-signature central manifest **refuses to widen** and falls back to the compiled-in floor — never fail-open.
- Every central widening is journaled with issuer + envelope provenance.
- Un-enrolled `fak` is byte-for-byte today's behavior (the org plane is opt-in).

Anchor files: `internal/policy/amendment.go` (channel/class registry), `internal/policy/policy.go` (manifest schema), `internal/adjudicator/decide.go` (Policy fold), `cmd/fak/guard_startup.go` (floor assembly + precedence), `cmd/fak/policy_reload_widen.go` (widening gate), `cmd/fak/serve.go` (`/v1/fak/policy/reload`), `cmd/fak/accounts.go` (seats/usage), `POLICY.md`.

records.title: research(org-policy): prior art + threat model for a centrally-administered fak policy plane
records.body:
**Parent:** #5315 · **Lane:** research (docs note) · **Class:** research

### Why
Before we design a central policy plane for `fak`, capture the prior art and a threat model so we borrow proven mechanisms and name the attacks up front. Centrally-administered policy for endpoints is a solved-ish problem in adjacent domains; we should not reinvent it.

### Spine (survey targets)
- Endpoint fleet management: MDM/Intune/Jamf config-profile distribution (enrollment, targeting, revocation).
- Signed policy/config bundles: TUF / Sigstore, OPA/Rego bundle API + signing, Kubernetes-style signed admission.
- Device identity: SPIFFE/SPIRE SVIDs, mTLS device certs, hardware attestation.
- The fak-native seam: how #5170's amendment channels + `internal/policy/amendment.go` already frame "who may amend what."

### Threat model to enumerate
Rollback/replay of an old (more-permissive) manifest; org root-key compromise; offline/air-gap; insider using the central channel to *widen* past the compiled-in floor; the wrapped agent reaching the central channel; a malicious/MitM policy endpoint; a device spoofing another device's usage tier.

### Definition of Done
- Committed `docs/notes/RESEARCH-org-policy-plane-prior-art-*.md` with (a) a borrow/avoid table across the survey targets and (b) the threat model with, per threat, the fak mitigation that W1–W7 must carry.
- The note names which prior-art mechanism each of R2/R3/W2/W5 should adopt (a concrete recommendation, not a menu).
- Cross-links #5315 and #5170; no code changes.

records.title: research(org-policy): signing, freshness, and key-distribution model for the signed org manifest
records.body:
**Parent:** #5315 · **Lane:** research (decision spike) · **Class:** research

### Why
The central plane's whole safety rests on a local `fak` being able to prove a pulled manifest is (a) authentic (issued by the org), (b) fresh (not a rolled-back older, more-permissive manifest), and (c) usable offline without failing open. Pick the scheme before W2 implements it.

### Spine (decide)
- Signature: Ed25519 detached signature over the canonicalized envelope vs x509 chain vs COSE/JWS. Zero-dependency constraint (fak ships one static binary, stdlib-only) strongly favors `crypto/ed25519`.
- Freshness / anti-rollback: monotonic `version` counter + `not_before`/`expires`; local persists highest-seen version and refuses any lower.
- Key distribution: org **root** public key pinned at `fak enroll` time (TOFU-at-enroll), with a signed key-rotation path.
- Offline posture: last-good cache + a max-staleness bound; past the bound → refuse-to-widen, fall back to compiled-in floor (never fail-open).

### Definition of Done
- Committed `docs/notes/RESEARCH-org-policy-signing-model-*.md` recommending ONE scheme end-to-end (signature alg, canonicalization, freshness counter, key-pin + rotation, offline bound) with a rejected-alternatives table and the exact stdlib primitives.
- A written envelope field list that W2 can implement verbatim (`issuer`, `sig`, `alg`, `version`, `not_before`, `expires`, `min_version`, `target`, body).
- States the anti-rollback and offline-max-staleness semantics precisely enough to become W2/W3 test assertions.

records.title: research(org-policy): precedence + entitlement semantics reconciling central-widen with the most-restrictive fold
records.body:
**Parent:** #5315 · **Lane:** research (decision spike) · **Class:** research

### Why
IT wants to BOTH tighten a fleet (deny a tool everywhere) AND *enable more usage* on enrolled boxes (raise a rate cap, unlock a tier). But the adjudicator fold is "most-restrictive-wins," and #5170 forbids any channel weakening a FROZEN knob. We need the exact precedence lattice reconciling "central authority widens" with "the fold tightens" before W4 codes it.

### Spine (formalize)
- Authority order: compiled-in FROZEN floor > `central` org overlay > operator overlay > agent-self (closed).
- Per amendment class, what `central` may do: RATCHET (always honored via the fold), GATED_WIDEN (raise a ceiling but never above the FROZEN cap), FROZEN (untouchable), SELF_AMENDABLE (n/a).
- The device-operator rule: a local operator may only tighten BELOW the central grant, never widen past it — so a central widen is a *ceiling*, a local overlay is a *further floor*.
- Reconcile with #5170 Track D precedence so there is one precedence model, not two.

### Definition of Done
- Committed `docs/notes/RESEARCH-org-policy-precedence-*.md` with a per-knob-class truth table: (compiled-in, central, operator) inputs → resolved verdict, for RATCHET / GATED_WIDEN / FROZEN.
- A failing-first Go matrix-test stub (skipped or `t.Skip` with the intended cases enumerated) that W4 turns green — so the semantics ship as an executable spec.
- Explicitly answers: "can central raise a cap the operator lowered?" and "can the operator widen past a central grant?" (expected: no).

Add `central` so no knob can be moved by the org plane without declaring it, and so the red-team matrix can prove the org channel cannot weaken a FROZEN knob.

### Spine

- For each `PolicyKnob`, decide whether `central` is an authorized channel (RATCHET knobs: yes; GATED_WIDEN knobs: yes but capped; FROZEN: never).

records.title: feat(policy): fak-org-policy/v1 signed envelope + verifier (auth, freshness, anti-rollback)
records.body:
**Parent:** #5315 · **Depends on:** #5317 (signing spike) · **Lane:** policy · **Class:** class:dev + security

### Why
Local `fak` must prove a pulled org manifest is authentic, fresh, and anti-rollback before it may change the floor. Implement the `fak-org-policy/v1` signed envelope + verifier the R2 spike specifies.

### Spine
- New `fak-org-policy/v1` envelope in `internal/policy`: `{issuer, alg, sig, version, not_before, expires, min_version, target, body}` where `body` is a `fak-policy/v1` manifest.
- Verifier: Ed25519 (stdlib `crypto/ed25519`) signature over the canonicalized envelope against a caller-supplied org root public key; check `version` monotonicity (anti-rollback), `not_before`/`expires` window, and `min_version` against the running binary.
- Extend `fak policy --check` to accept and validate an org envelope (report issuer, expiry, target, and the inner floor).

### Definition of Done
- Parse + verify + round-trip tests pass; a good envelope verifies, and each of {bad signature, expired, `not_before` in future, rolled-back `version`, wrong issuer, `min_version` too high} FAILS CLOSED with a distinct closed-vocabulary reason.
- `fak policy --check org-envelope.json` prints the resolved inner floor + envelope metadata and refuses a malformed/oversized envelope (fail-loud, matching the existing loader discipline).
- Stdlib-only; `go test ./internal/policy/` green.

records.title: feat(policy): remote org-policy pull + last-good cache + offline refuse-to-widen fallback
records.body:
**Parent:** #5315 · **Depends on:** #5316, #5317, W2 · **Lane:** policy · **Class:** class:infra + security

### Why
The central floor has to reach the local instance and survive being offline without ever failing open. Implement the pull + cache + offline-fallback path.

### Spine
- `--org-policy-url` flag / `FAK_ORG_POLICY_URL` env: fetch the org envelope on startup and on a periodic refresh timer.
- Last-good cache on disk (verified envelopes only); a `max_staleness` bound.
- Offline/stale posture: within bound -> use last-good; past bound OR never-fetched-and-required -> **refuse to widen**: drop every `central` GATED_WIDEN grant and fall back to the compiled-in floor. NEVER fail-open.
- Wire the long-lived `fak serve` path to accept a pushed refresh through the existing `POST /v1/fak/policy/reload` (behind the same bearer-token gate).

### Definition of Done
- Fetch loop is unit-tested with an in-process transport double (no live network): fresh fetch applies, offline-within-bound serves last-good, offline-past-bound falls back to the compiled-in floor.
- A stale/expired/unreachable source can only ever make the floor STRICTER than the last-good widen, proven by a test asserting no grant survives past the staleness bound.
- `go build ./cmd/fak` + `go test ./internal/policy/` green.

records.title: feat(policy): fak enroll — pin org root key + device identity (opt-in trust anchor)
records.body:
**Parent:** #5315 · **Depends on:** #5317 (key model) · **Lane:** policy · **Class:** class:infra + security

### Why
The central plane needs a trust anchor and a device identity, established opt-in. Un-enrolled `fak` must stay byte-for-byte today's behavior.

### Spine
- `fak enroll --org <url>`: fetch + pin the org root public key (TOFU-at-enroll), record a device/user identity, and persist the enrollment (org URL + pinned key + device id) to a local config.

records.title: feat(policy): central usage-entitlement grants (raise rate/tier ceilings per device)
records.body:
**Parent:** #5315 · **Depends on:** W2, W4 · **Lane:** policy · **Class:** class:dev

### Why
This is the IT-**enable-more** half of the ask: an admin raises a team's ceiling centrally - a bigger `rate_limit`, an unlocked model/cache tier, an account seat - per enrolled device/user/group, without touching each box. It is GATED_WIDEN performed by an authority the agent cannot reach.

### Spine
- A usage-entitlement block in the org envelope `target`: per device/user/group, the granted `rate_limit` ceiling, model/cache-tier unlocks, and seat/account grants.
- The governor (`rate_limit`) and account resolution (`cmd/fak/accounts.go`) honor the granted ceiling - bounded by the compiled-in max (a grant can raise the local cap up to, never above, the FROZEN ceiling).
- The managed-cache posture (`guard_managed_cache.go`) can be centrally enabled where billing permits.

### Definition of Done
- An org grant raising `max_calls`/`max_cost` takes effect on the resolved governor; a local operator can only lower it further, not raise past the grant (test both directions).
- A grant is capped by the compiled-in FROZEN ceiling: a grant exceeding it clamps, with a journaled note.
- Model/cache-tier unlock path is covered by a test; `go test ./internal/policy/ ./cmd/fak/` (scoped) green.

records.title: feat(policy): redacted org audit-telemetry sink with offline buffering
records.body:
**Parent:** #5315 · **Depends on:** W5 · **Lane:** policy · **Class:** class:infra + observability

### Why
The "managed, company-controlled context" is not just push-down policy - IT needs to SEE what the fleet did. Emit redacted adjudication + usage receipts to a company sink.

### Spine
- A receipt emitter: on each adjudication (or batched), emit `{device_id, tool, verdict, reason, ts, usage_delta}` to the org's audit endpoint.
- Privacy floor: apply the manifest's `redact_fields` before emit; never ship secret values or full argument bytes - verdict + reason + counters only.
- Best-effort + offline buffering: buffer to disk when the sink is unreachable, flush on reconnect; the sink being down never blocks a tool call.

### Definition of Done
- Receipts are emitted for allow + deny verdicts, carry the device identity from enrollment (W5), and are redacted (a test asserts no `redact_fields` value and no raw secret leaves the process).
- Sink-unreachable buffers to disk and flushes later; a down sink never blocks adjudication (test).
- Emitter is opt-in via the enrollment/org config; `go test ./internal/policy/` green.

records.title: feat(hooks): enforce the committed-blob GOFMT gate at the write boundary — the format sibling of FC-1 (epic #4142)
records.body:
## Parent

Child of #4142 (first-class trunk-green — kill "dirty tree build fails" at the two write
boundaries). The epic's FC-1/FC-2/FC-3 (#4152/#4151/#4153) all attack the **compile** red.
This is the sibling **format** boundary: the committed trunk can be gofmt-red (fails
`make ci` / `fak ci-preflight` gofmt-check) for every lane, and nothing on the automatic
commit or push path refuses it.

## Problem

#5302 just demonstrated the cost: 6 gofmt-unformatted files sat on the committed trunk,
reding `fak ci-preflight` gofmt-check for every lane regardless of their own change. Root
cause (mapped):

- **Commit gate `GOFMT`** (`internal/hooks/gate_gofmt.go:41-69`, registered
  `internal/hooks/hooks.go:120`) is already **committed-blob-correct** — it reads the staged
  INDEX blob via `git show :<path>` (`internal/hooks/hooks.go:306-325`, Treeish `":"`), which
  is LF-normalized under `core.autocrlf=input`, so it is immune to the Windows-CRLF false
  positive. But it is registered `DefaultMode: "warn"` — it *names* the unformatted files and
  lets the commit proceed.
- **Push gate** (`cmd/fak/prepush_build.go`) has **no gofmt rung** at all (compile-only:
  `TRUNK_WOULD_NOT_COMPILE` / `IMPORT_OF_UNCOMMITTED_PACKAGE`).
- **`fak ci-preflight`** (`cmd/fak/ci_preflight.go`) is the committed-blob-correct check
  (archives the tip, runs real `gofmt -l`) but is a **manual verb** wired into no hook,
  Makefile target, or CI script.
- **`make ci` gofmt-check** (`Makefile:335`) is **working-tree-based and Linux/WSL-only**
  (a Windows checkout's CRLF would false-positive, so `scripts/ci.ps1` omits it).

Net: the only automatic gate that sees committed-blob gofmt drift at commit time is advisory;
the push gate omits gofmt; the correct verb is manual; and real GitHub CI is billing-blocked
on the private repo. A worker who commits + pushes lands gofmt drift with nothing refusing it.

## Why now (readiness)

You cannot flip an advisory gate to blocking while the trunk is already dirty — it would red
every in-flight commit for pre-existing drift. **As of `3ef23f8555` (the #5302 fix) the
committed trunk is verifiably gofmt-clean**: `git archive origin/main | tar -x` then
`gofmt -l` over the whole committed LF tree returns empty. So the ratchet can be flipped now
with zero pre-existing-drift blast radius — it only refuses NEW drift.

## In scope — pick one enforcement shape (design fork for the owner)

- **Option A — hard block:** `internal/hooks/hooks.go:120` `DefaultMode: "warn"` → `"block"` on
  the GOFMT gate (or set `FLEET_GOFMT_GUARD=block` in the shared/committed env). Detection
  logic is already committed-blob-correct; escape hatch `ALLOW_GOFMT_DRIFT=1` stays for a
  one-off bypass.
- **Option B — drift ceiling (ratchet):** keep advisory as the floor but red only when
  committed-blob gofmt drift *increases* vs a checked-in baseline count — closes the
  "no drift ceiling beside it" gap. Gentler; lets residual drift bleed down without a hard
  stop. (Given the trunk is at 0 now, the baseline is 0, so this is effectively A with a
  friendlier message.)
- **Defense-in-depth (either option):** add a committed-blob gofmt rung to the push gate
  (`cmd/fak/prepush_build.go`), so drift is refused at the actual trunk-poisoning boundary
  even if it slipped a commit.

## Companion edits (keep the tree green)

- Update the fail-closed ledger row `docs/proofs/failclosed-audit.md:139`
  (`GOFMT | warn | fail-open | advisory`) to match the new mode, else
  `internal/hooks/failclosed_ledger_test.go:126-142` reds.
- `internal/hooks/gate_gofmt_test.go` already binds `gateGofmt`; add a mode-is-block
  assertion for Option A.

## Done condition

A committed-blob gofmt violation is **refused** at a write boundary (commit or push) by
default, not merely named; the ledger + binding tests are green; `fak ci-preflight` stays
green on trunk.

## Witness

A test that stages a gofmt-dirty `.go` and asserts the commit/push is **refused** (not just
warned), plus the failclosed-ledger test green with the updated row, plus
`fak ci-preflight` green on the tip.

## Notes

Committed-blob is the correct signal (what a Linux/LF CI checkout sees). Do NOT switch any
gate to working-tree `gofmt -l`, which false-positives on Windows CRLF checkouts
(`core.autocrlf=input`) and can both mask genuine breaks and red clean ones — see #5302 for the
CRLF-artifact analysis and #4061 (checkout-line-ending sensitivity). The commit gate already
does this right; this issue is only about its enforcement *mode*, not its detection.

## Lane

hooks

## Likely files

- `internal/hooks/hooks.go` (mode registration, line ~120)
- `docs/proofs/failclosed-audit.md` (ledger row ~139)
- `internal/hooks/gate_gofmt_test.go` / `internal/hooks/failclosed_ledger_test.go` (binding)
- `cmd/fak/prepush_build.go` (optional push-gate rung)

records.title: epic(enterprise): API-based corporate fak usage — API-key accounts, org access spine, SSO
records.body:
## Epic: API-based corporate fak usage

Make fak usable by an organization that authenticates and bills via **API keys** (not consumer subscription seats), and lay the groundwork for a corporate identity/access spine. Three facets, each a child issue:

1. **API-key accounts** — "log in with an API key and use that as a fak account" as a first-class thing, not just a guard billing posture.
2. **Org-scoped API access to the spine** — multi-key, per-principal access to `fak serve` so audit + residency attribute per tenant.
3. **SSO / OIDC federation** — corporate identity, deliberately a *control-plane* concern per the open-core boundary.

### Where fak is today (grounded in the binary)

- **A fak account** = a `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` seat in `registry.json` (`internal/accounts`, `cmd/fak/accounts.go`). Identity is derived by probing the **OAuth profile** the credential authenticates as — subscription-OAuth-shaped (`claude setup-token` → `sk-ant-oat…`).
- **API-key billing already exists, but only as a guard posture**: `fak guard --api-key-env VAR` / `$FAK_GUARD_API_KEY_ENV` (`cmd/fak/guard_cache_posture.go`). On the Anthropic wire it opts into API billing and flips managed cache **ACTIVE**. It is *not* a registry credential kind.
- **Gateway auth** to `fak serve` is a **single bearer** (`--require-key-env`, `x-api-key`), enforced on every route except `/healthz` (`internal/gateway`).
- **Residency/routing spine** already models per-provider credential rosters as env-var *references* (`internal/modelroute`, `RouteAccounts`); `KindAnthropic` already accepts "an API key OR a subscription OAuth token."
- **SSO / OIDC / org RBAC** appear only in docs/RFC, never in code: `docs/fak/hosted-control-plane.md` (epic #576, closed) puts multi-tenant auth + org RBAC + SSO in the **paid hosted control plane**, a read-side aggregator over the audit stream the binary emits — never in the request path, never weakening the capability floor.

### Open-core boundary (design constraint for all children)

The Apache-2.0 binary stays runnable with **key-based auth only** (single or org-scoped API keys). Real corporate **SSO/OIDC/SAML + org RBAC federate in the hosted control plane**, not the binary. No child may re-introduce a catch-based gate or move SSO into the request path.

### Children
- [ ] #5331 — API-key account credential kind (the initial, shippable spine)
- [ ] #5332 — Org-scoped multi-key API access to `fak serve`
- [ ] #5333 — SSO/OIDC federation design (control-plane)

### References
- `docs/fak/hosted-control-plane.md`, `docs/enterprise-positioning.md`
- `internal/accounts`, `cmd/fak/accounts.go`, `cmd/fak/guard_cache_posture.go`
- `internal/modelroute` (Roster / RouteAccounts), `internal/gateway` (`--require-key-env`)

records.title: feat(accounts): first-class API-key account credential kind (login with an API key as a fak seat)
records.body:
Parent epic: #5330

## Goal — "log in with an API key and use that as a fak account"

Make an **Anthropic API key** a first-class account credential *kind* in the `fak accounts` registry, alongside today's subscription-OAuth seats. This is the **initial spine** for corporate/API-based fak usage.

## Today

- `internal/accounts` models a seat's identity by probing the **OAuth profile** the credential authenticates as (`accounts.ProbeToken`, `.credentials.json`/`.oauth-token`). Enroll is `claude setup-token` or `--adopt`.
- API-key *billing* already exists as a **guard posture** — `fak guard --api-key-env VAR` / `$FAK_GUARD_API_KEY_ENV` (`cmd/fak/guard_cache_posture.go`) — but the seat is still OAuth-identity-shaped. There is no way to enroll a seat *whose credential is an API key*.

## Scope

1. **Registry credential kind** — teach `accounts.Identity` / the registry an `api_key` credential kind: identity is derived from the **key's org/workspace** (a Console/profile probe of the key), not an OAuth profile. Preserve the existing rotation/drift/reconcile invariants (this is the load-bearing part — do not regress `NameLie()`, `identity_metadata_stale`, `AccountKey()`).
2. **Enroll verb** — `fak accounts add --name X --api-key-env ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (and adopt-from-env), landing the credential *reference* (env var name, never the secret) in the registry, consistent with `internal/modelroute`'s `CredEnv` posture.
3. **Launch wiring** — `fak accounts launch` on an api-key seat auto-splices `--api-key-env` + managed-cache ACTIVE (the plumbing in `guardCachePostureArgs` already exists).
4. **Status/rotation** — an api-key seat reports and rotates like any other; login-status reflects "key present/valid" rather than OAuth readiness.

## Non-goals

- No SSO/OIDC (that is #5330's SSO child, control-plane).
- Never store the secret — only the env-var reference (`CredEnv` posture).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `fak accounts add --name corp --api-key-env ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` enrolls a seat with kind=api_key and an org-derived identity.
- [ ] `fak accounts list/status --json` shows the seat with a truthful identity + can_serve.
- [ ] `fak accounts launch --name corp` fronts guard with `--api-key-env` and ACTIVE managed cache.
- [ ] Rotation/drift/reconcile tests stay green; new unit tests cover the api_key identity path.
- [ ] `make ci` green; shipped on trunk per repo convention.

## Files
`internal/accounts/*` (identity + registry + login report), `cmd/fak/accounts.go`, `cmd/fak/accounts_launch.go`, `cmd/fak/guard_cache_posture.go`.

records.title: feat(gateway): org-scoped multi-key API access to fak serve (per-principal auth + audit attribution)
records.body:
Parent epic: #5330

## Goal — org-scoped, multi-key API access to the `fak serve` spine

Corporate API access needs more than the single bearer `fak serve` accepts today. Map **multiple API keys → org/project principals** so audit and residency attribute per tenant, while staying key-based (open-core boundary; real SSO stays control-plane, see #5330).

## Today

- Gateway auth is a **single** `--require-key-env` bearer (`internal/gateway`, `x-api-key`), enforced on every route except `/healthz`. `--read-bearer` adds a read-only observability key.
- The audit join key `X-Trace-Id` and `/v1/fak/events` already carry per-turn verdicts; the residency PDP already binds per-account routes (`internal/modelroute` `RouteAccounts`, `Target.EngineRoute()`). There is no principal attached to an inbound API key.

## Scope

1. **Keyset config** — accept a key→principal map (env-referenced, hashed-at-rest; never the raw key in a file) so N corporate keys authenticate against one `fak serve`.
2. **Principal propagation** — stamp the authenticated org/project principal onto the trace so `/v1/fak/events`, JSON access logs, and the session/route surfaces attribute per tenant.
3. **Residency tie-in** — let the principal scope which `RouteAccounts` targets a request may reach (a tenant/sensitive call denied at the boundary, never fail-open — reuse the existing PDP).
4. **Backwards compatible** — a single `--require-key-env` still works byte-for-byte; the keyset is additive.

## Non-goals

- No SSO/OIDC/session cookies (control-plane, #5330 SSO child).
- No user database; keys map to principals, nothing more.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `fak serve` accepts a keyset and authenticates multiple keys, each bound to a principal.
- [ ] The authenticated principal appears on `/v1/fak/events` + access logs, joinable by `X-Trace-Id`.
- [ ] Residency PDP can scope route targets by principal; denial is fail-closed.
- [ ] Single-key path unchanged; new tests cover multi-key auth + attribution; `make ci` green.

## Files
`internal/gateway/*` (auth, http, messages, metrics), tie-in to `internal/modelroute`.

records.title: design(enterprise): SSO/OIDC federation for the hosted control plane (open-core boundary)
records.body:
Parent epic: #5330

## Goal — SSO/OIDC federation design (control-plane, open-core boundary)

Design how corporate **SSO/OIDC/SAML + org RBAC** federate into fak, respecting the open-core boundary: the Apache-2.0 binary stays key-based; identity federation lives in the **hosted control plane** (`docs/fak/hosted-control-plane.md`, epic #576), a read-side aggregator over the audit stream the binary emits.

## Why this is a design ticket, not a dispatch leaf

SSO in the request path would re-introduce a session/identity dependency the capability floor deliberately avoids. The hosted-plane RFC already sequences "multi-tenant auth + org model (RBAC over policies)" as child track #1, adoption-gated behind the MCP wedge + context-debugger. This ticket produces the **design note**, not binary code.

## Scope (deliverable = a design note under `docs/fak/`)

1. **Boundary restatement** — what stays in the binary (API-key auth, #5330 children 1–2) vs. what federates in the plane (SSO login, org/project/role model, SCIM provisioning).
2. **Federation flow** — how an SSO'd operator in the plane maps down to the key-based principals the binary authenticates (children 1–2 are the substrate).
3. **Audit tie-in** — SSO identity ↔ `X-Trace-Id` / `/v1/fak/events` join so per-user governance is answerable in the plane without the binary trusting a session.
4. **Provider survey** — OIDC/SAML/SCIM options and where prior art in `docs/notes/RESEARCH-org-policy-plane-prior-art-2026-07-20.md` applies.

## Non-goals

- No binary-side SSO code (that would breach the open-core boundary).
- No hosted-plane implementation (adoption-gated).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A design note lands under `docs/fak/` (e.g. `enterprise-identity-federation.md`) covering the four scope items.
- [ ] It cross-links `hosted-control-plane.md`, `enterprise-positioning.md`, #5330, and children 1–2.
- [ ] It states the open-core boundary explicitly and names the request-path invariant it must not break.

records.title: feat(metrics): wire metrics.FleetView into a live fak status --watch verb and capture the operator dogfood screenshot (parent #4366, epic #3236)
records.body:
## Parent context

Parent: #4366 (interactive fleet TUI renderer - landed 3e3ea4ea6737). Epic: #3236.

## Why

#4366 landed the fleet TUI as a pure LIBRARY renderer over the device-spine
snapshot (FleetView: overview grid, per-device drill-down, responsive
column-wrap layout, bounded sparkline rings, plus OneShot delegating to
RenderText). Its renderer-contract gate is green. The second half of that
issue's gate - an operator dogfood screenshot - is unreachable today because NO
cmd/fak verb consumes metrics.FleetView, so the renderer has no live surface to
screenshot. This issue closes that gap.

## Spine

Landed spine: internal/metrics/device_spine_tui.go and
internal/metrics/device_spine_tui_oneshot.go, witnessed at 3e3ea4ea6737.
FleetView.Observe(Buffer.Poll(...)) feeds the rings; RenderOverview /
RenderDrilldown / OneShot render them.

## Scope

A thin cmd/fak shell that polls Buffer.Poll on a ticker and renders FleetView.

## Non-goals

No new metric collection path (read Buffer.Snapshot()/Federate only, exactly as
the renderer does). No second aligned-table renderer - OneShot already delegates
to RenderText. No change to metricTable.

## Acceptance

- A `fak status` (or `fak metrics --watch`) verb renders RenderOverview on a
  ticker, and OneShot for the non-interactive one-shot pretty-print.
- Per-device drill-down reachable from the overview.
- An operator dogfood screenshot captured on a real multi-device host and
  attached to this issue.

## Closure

A witnessed commit citing this issue with a `(fak cmd)` or `(fak metrics)`
trailer, plus the attached dogfood screenshot.

## Lane

cmd (the verb shell) reading metrics (the landed renderer).

## Steps

1. Add the cmd/fak shell wiring Buffer.Poll -> FleetView.Observe -> RenderOverview.
2. Add the --watch ticker plus a one-shot path calling FleetView.OneShot.
3. Dogfood on a multi-device host per docs/fleet-compute-nodes.md; attach the screenshot.

## Work estimate

3 points. Two of the three steps are a thin cmd/fak shell over an already-landed
renderer (no new logic, no new collection path); the third (the dogfood capture)
is operator/host time, not code.

## Overall completion contribution

Contribution: 3/15 points.

~20% of the #4366 renderer arm. The renderer, its layout, the bounded rings and
the one-shot seam are already landed and gated green at 3e3ea4ea6737; what
remains is the live verb surface plus the captured screenshot that promotes the
arm from gen/next to gen/now.

## Completion standard

demo

The acceptance here is an operator dogfood capture of a read-only renderer on a
host, not a served production path with a concurrency/latency envelope. The
renderer adds no collection path and no request-path work, so a production
operating envelope would be a fabricated number rather than a real bar.

## Generation

gen/next - this IS the promotion evidence that would move #4366's renderer to
gen/now. Demotion / retirement evidence: if operators only ever consume the
one-shot RenderText or the Prom/JSON scrape, the interactive surface is dead
weight - retire FleetView and keep the one-shot. Invalidating assumption: a
multi-device host is assumed reachable for the dogfood; if the fleet is
single-device in practice, the grid's column-wrap value is unproven and the
screenshot would prove less than it appears to.

records.title: fix(commitlane): pre-commit hook hangs on an 18k-ref lease/fold and a peer git-add-A swarm regenerates stale .git/index.lock, wedging the shared commit lane
records.body:
## Summary

The shared-trunk commit lane in `C:\work\fak` is intermittently wedged fleet-wide.
Every commit path — `fak commit`, raw `git commit -- <paths>`, and a private-index
`git commit` — hangs for 30s to 2min+, and stale `.git/index.lock` files regenerate
faster than the sanctioned reclaim can clear them. Peers still land commits in the
brief clear windows, so the lane is *thrashing*, not dead — but any committer with a
sub-3-minute timeout is repeatedly killed mid-flight, and each kill can leave a fresh
stale lock, which is a self-reinforcing feedback loop.

This is a P0: agents cannot reliably ship, and the failure mode manufactures more of
its own cause.

## Evidence (measured live 2026-07-22 in C:\work\fak, fak 0.41.0)

1. **The pre-commit hook hangs independent of `index.lock`.** `fak hooks pre-commit`
   (the Go fast-path behind `tools/githooks/pre-commit`) hangs >=30s at *near-zero CPU*
   (`user 0m0.03s, sys 0m0.22s`, `real 0m30s`) **even when `.git/index.lock` is clear
   at start** — so it is blocked on a lock / lease / fold, not computing. Ref counts at
   the time: `refs/fak/wip/*` = 4051, `refs/fak/locks/*` = 14194 (18245 side-refs). It
   prints the `BARE_COMMIT_SWEEP` advisory, then blocks.

2. **The hook's fail-open has a hole.** `tools/githooks/pre-commit` documents "FAILS
   OPEN if its checker cannot run -- a non-1 exit is treated as could-not-run, skipped."
   That only covers a non-1 *exit code*. A checker/lease that *hangs* never returns an
   exit code, so it wedges every commit. The fail-open invariant does not cover hangs.

3. **A peer `git add -A` retry-swarm regenerates stale locks.** A peer session
   (`fak.exe guard -- claude`, e.g. PID 7304, plus 75256 / 55404) spawns `git add -A`
   on the shared tree every ~8-20s in a retry loop — a direct violation of the
   shared-tree "never `git add -A`" rule. Each spawn that hits its own ~2-min tool
   timeout is SIGTERM'd mid index-write, leaving a fresh `.git/index.lock` (observed:
   a 1.29 MB lock frozen at one mtime for 12+ minutes with no live holder).

4. **The reclaim false-positives against the swarm.** `fak commit status
   --reclaim-stale-index-lock --apply` refused 14 times in a row with
   `keep_live_writer` — each transient `git add -A` spawn reads as a "live writer." It
   only succeeded on the 15th rapid retry, when it happened to sample a swarm gap. A
   12-minute-frozen lock with a dead creator should reclaim on the first try.

5. **Tool-timeout / commit-runtime mismatch feeds the loop.** `fak commit` needs
   ~100-180s under this contention; a 120s foreground cap (or a peer's 2-min tool cap)
   kills it mid-commit, and the killed committer can itself leave a stale lock.

## Impact

Fleet-wide: agents cannot reliably `fak commit` / push. The lane recovers only in
short windows between swarm-induced stale locks. This blocks the very WIP-shipping the
fleet is trying to do, and the reclaim ceremony (15 retries to catch a gap) is not a
sustainable workaround.

## Definition of Done

1. **Bound the pre-commit hook.** `fak hooks pre-commit` gets a per-gate deadline; on
   expiry it fails OPEN (treat a hang exactly like could-not-run -> exit 2 -> skip the
   Python fallthrough or the whole gate), so a slow lease/fold can never wedge every
   commit in the clone. A test asserts a deliberately-stalled gate does not block a
   commit past the deadline.

2. **De-O(refs) the hook's wait.** Identify the lease/fold `fak hooks pre-commit`
   blocks on and make it O(1) in ref count, or drop the acquisition. Coordinate with
   the `wipListRecords` single-`for-each-ref` fix and the `leaseref` fold — 18k+
   side-refs must not be walked on the commit hot path.

3. **Fix the reclaim liveness test.** `--reclaim-stale-index-lock` must distinguish a
   genuine holder (a process with the lock fd open) from a fail-fast `git add -A`
   spawn. Add an age + no-open-fd witness so a lock frozen past a grace age with a dead
   creator reclaims on the first attempt, not the 15th. A test: N transient git spawns
   racing a stale lock still reclaims the stale lock; a genuinely-held lock is kept.

4. **Stop the stale-lock generator.** Find the peer `fak guard`/session loop issuing
   `git add -A` on the shared tree and stop it (route it through `fak commit`'s vetted
   pathspec staging instead). That loop is the upstream source of the regenerating
   stale locks.

## Relevant paths

- `tools/githooks/pre-commit`
- `cmd/fak/hooks*.go` (the `fak hooks pre-commit` Go gates)
- `internal/commitlane/reclaim.go`, `internal/commitlane/status.go`
- `cmd/fak/commit_status.go` (the `--reclaim-stale-index-lock` flag)
- the `fak guard -- claude` session loop that emits `git add -A`

Part of the shared-trunk WIP-hygiene follow-on to epic #3871.

records.title: fix(wip): fold wipListRecords to a single batched for-each-ref so status/reconcile/reap scale past 4k refs
records.body:
## Summary

`fak wip status | reconcile | attribute | reap` spawn one `git log -1 --format=%B`
per checkpoint ref (and reap adds 2 more `git diff` per ref via `wipOwnerState`). At
4051 local `refs/fak/wip/*` refs (7 days' accumulation, still growing) these fan out
to 4k-12k child processes and time out >120s, so orphaned WIP is never reconciled —
the reconciliation spine is effectively unrunnable.

## Evidence

- `git for-each-ref refs/fak/wip | wc -l` = 4051 (local-only refs).
- `wipListRecords` in `cmd/fak/wip.go` loops `gitWipOut(... "log","-1","--format=%B",
  obj)` once per ref.
- `wipReap` / `wipOwnerState` add per-ref `git diff --name-only` + `git diff --quiet`.
- `wipReap` keeps `OwnerUnknown` (the fail-safe for any crashed/unlanded owner)
  forever — only `OwnerLanded` is deleted — so the ref set grows without bound; there
  is no GC cadence for crashed-owner *unlanded* checkpoints. This is the source of the
  ref bloat that also wedges the commit hook (see the P0 commit-lane wedge issue).

## Definition of Done

1. `wipListRecords` reads the object + stamp in a single
   `git for-each-ref --format=...%(contents)...` (NUL-delimited) — zero per-ref
   subprocess. `status`/`reconcile` over 5000 refs complete in <5s. **A fix is already
   staged for landing** (folds the per-ref `git log` into one `for-each-ref`, with a
   table test `TestWipListRecordsSingleCall`); this issue tracks that fix + the reap
   half below.
2. A bounded reap/GC cadence deletes crashed-owner *unlanded* checkpoints under a
   witnessed disposition (not "keep forever"), so the ref count is self-bounding.
3. A table test at N=5000 refs asserts the listing subprocess count is O(1) in N.

## Relevant paths

- `cmd/fak/wip.go` (`wipListRecords`, `runWipReap`, `wipOwnerState`)
- `internal/wipref/`, `internal/wiprecon/`

Coordinate with the retention/GC thread #3873 (OPEN) under epic #3871.

records.title: feat(wip): attach a linked GH ticket to each QUARANTINE/orphan WIP checkpoint via fak wip reconcile --file-ticket
records.body:
## Summary

`fak wip reconcile` is advisory only — it classifies a crashed session's checkpoint as
`DISCARD_WITNESSED | RECLAIM | QUARANTINE` and prints the verdict, but nothing links a
QUARANTINE/orphan delta to a process. A truly-WIP delta with no live owner has no
"next step is Z" record, so no human or agent ever picks it up and it accrues silently.
This is the systemic gap behind "clear remaining files are truly WIP — and if so they
must have some process (a linked GH ticket) associated with them."

## Evidence

- `wipReconcile` (`cmd/fak/wip.go`) returns `wiprecon.Reconcile(cands)` verdicts and
  `runWipReconcile` only `Fprintf`s them; no side effect, no ticket.
- #3875 (CLOSED) *classifies* a crashed owner's delta; #3880 (OPEN) *enumerates* peer
  crashed WIP. Neither attaches a durable follow-up ticket.

## Definition of Done

On a QUARANTINE (or a RECLAIM that will not auto-apply) verdict, `fak wip reconcile
--file-ticket` files/updates ONE idempotent GH ticket per orphan checkpoint, keyed by
`session + start-SHA` (marker `<!-- fak-wip-ticket-key: wip-orphan-<session>-<sha12>
-->`), carrying: the attributed file set, the disposition, and the concrete next step.
The ticket id is recorded back on the WIP ref/ledger. Re-running reconcile does not
duplicate the ticket (dedup against `gh issue list --state all` by the marker key).
Offline-safe: with no network, it prints the ticket it *would* file and exits 0.
Scope v1 to the QUARANTINE disposition; wire it into the `FleetStaleWorkGarden`
watchdog (a `-Live` variant) as a follow-on.

## Relevant paths

- `cmd/fak/wip.go` (`runWipReconcile`, `wipReconcile`) + a new `cmd/fak/wip_ticket.go`
- `internal/wiprecon/`
- `tools/register_stale_work_watchdog.ps1`, `tools/stale_work_watchdog.py`

Extends closed #3875, complements open #3880, under epic #3871.

records.title: fix(commitlane): reap orphaned .git/next-index-*.lock residue and surface --reclaim-stale-index-lock on 'fak commit'
records.body:
## Summary

Two discoverability/residue gaps around the recurring commit-lane wedge:

(a) The shipped stale-index.lock reclaim (from #5294 / #5253) lives only under
    `fak commit status --reclaim-stale-index-lock [--apply]`, so a committer hitting a
    lock wedge on `fak commit` cannot find it from `fak commit --help`.

(b) git's `.git/next-index-<pid>` temp files, left behind by dead index writers, are
    never reaped — 61 have accumulated (oldest ~8.7 days) alongside the recurring
    `index.lock` residue.

## Evidence

- `ls .git/next-index-*.lock | wc -l` = 61.
- `grep -r next-index` over the source tree = 0 handlers; `internal/commitlane/
  reclaim.go` reclaims only `index.lock`.
- Deployed fak 0.41.0 exposes `--reclaim-stale-index-lock` under `fak commit status`,
  absent from `fak commit --help`.

(Note: the reclaim itself is shipped + deployed — this issue is residue + discoverability,
NOT re-filing the reclaim. See #5294 / #5253.)

## Definition of Done

1. The stale-lock reap (same dead-owner / no-live-writer evidence as `index.lock`)
   also removes orphaned `next-index-*.lock` residue past a grace age.
2. `fak commit`'s refusal text on a lock-busy condition names the reclaim path, and/or
   the `--reclaim-stale-index-lock` flag is aliased onto `fak commit`.
3. Test: N stale `next-index-*.lock` with no live writer are reaped; a young/live one
   is kept.

## Relevant paths

- `internal/commitlane/reclaim.go`, `internal/commitlane/status.go`
- `cmd/fak/commit_status.go`, `cmd/fak/commit.go`

Post-#5294 / #5253; part of the WIP-hygiene follow-on to epic #3871.

records.title: fix(commitlane): detect and clear no-op staged deletions (rm --cached residue byte-identical to HEAD) from the shared index
records.body:
## Summary

51 files are staged for deletion in the shared index yet present on disk and
byte-identical to HEAD — pure `git rm --cached` no-op churn. It has no commit effect
but pollutes `git status`, confuses committers about what will land, and complicates
sweep-guard / BARE_COMMIT_SWEEP reasoning on the shared trunk.

## Evidence

- `git diff --cached --diff-filter=D --name-only | wc -l` = 51.
- For every one, `git hash-object <disk>` == `git rev-parse HEAD:<file>` (0 differ, 0
  absent) — a staged-delete of an on-disk file identical to HEAD.

No existing issue detects or clears this (related but different: sweep-guard #3879,
"committed tip + only my change" #4995, file-level sweep #4607).

## Definition of Done

A doctor/hygiene check (e.g. under `fak commit status` or `treedoctor`) flags staged
deletions whose working-tree file is byte-identical to HEAD as no-op index churn and
offers a scoped `git restore --staged` clear for exactly those paths — never touching
real staged content. A test with mixed real + no-op staged deletions clears only the
no-ops.

## Relevant paths

- `cmd/fak/commit_status.go` (or a `treedoctor` gate)
- `internal/commitlane/`

Part of the shared-trunk WIP-hygiene follow-on to epic #3871.

records.title: fix(wipref): wire the closed-session cut into wip reap so dead-session checkpoints are collected, not kept forever
records.body:
## Parent context

Child of the wipref retention/GC mandate in #3873. Scaling of the read path landed in #5336 (single `for-each-ref`); this ticket fixes the *collection* path so the ref set stops growing unbounded in the first place.

## Problem

`fak wip reap` currently collects **0** of the **4051** live `refs/fak/wip/*` checkpoints on the shared tree (dry-run over the full set returns an empty delete list). The refs span 8 days and only grow: `autocheckpoint` creates them automatically at every risky boundary (session stop, compaction, doomloop), but nothing collects them.

Root cause is in the reap *owner resolver*, not the fold. `cmd/fak/wip.go:wipOwnerState` can only ever return two of the five owner states from git alone:

- `OwnerLanded` — but only when HEAD carries the checkpoint delta **verbatim**: it runs `git diff --quiet HEAD <obj> -- <files>` and requires exit 0. Real work lands with edits / rebases / squashes, so the committed file contents diverge from the raw checkpoint blob and the match fails.
- `OwnerUnknown` — the fail-safe default for everything else, which the fold **keeps**.

The resolver never emits `OwnerLive` or `OwnerClosedClean`. Its own comment defers those to "later cuts with a session registry" — that cut is not wired into the reap path. So every long-dead session whose delta did not land byte-identical collapses to `UNKNOWN` and is kept forever. The `OwnerClosedClean`/`OwnerClosedDirty` vocabulary and the delete/keep fold already exist in `internal/wipref/reap.go`; only the resolver fails to populate the closed states.

Consequence: monotonic ref growth. This already caused one incident — the 4051-ref count is exactly what forced the #5336 fan-out fix. Each ref also pins its checkpoint objects, so `.git` grows with it.

## Fix direction (must preserve the fail-safe invariant)

Wire a closed-session cut into `wipReap` so a checkpoint whose owning session is provably **not live** AND whose delta is provably **non-recoverable** resolves to `OwnerClosedClean` and is reaped. Two safe signals compose:

1. Session liveness: cross-reference the session registry / live-session set (the same source `wip status` / `reconcile` use for `OwnerLive`). A session absent from the live set is a candidate.
2. Delta recoverability: reap only when the delta is subsumed by HEAD (the changed files' HEAD contents already contain the checkpoint's added lines, even if not byte-identical) OR the delta is empty. A non-empty, unlanded, still-recoverable delta from a dead session is `OwnerClosedDirty` → KEEP (that is exactly what `wip restore` / `reconcile --file-ticket` exist to recover).

Do NOT add a blanket age-based delete — a 10-day-old recoverable `CLOSED_DIRTY` snapshot must survive. Age may gate *candidacy* but recoverability, never age, decides deletion.

## Likely files

- cmd/fak/wip.go (`wipOwnerState`, `wipReap`)
- internal/wipref/reap.go (fold already handles the closed states)

## Expected steps

1. Add a closed-session resolver that returns `OwnerClosedClean` only when session-not-live AND delta-subsumed-or-empty; keep `OwnerUnknown` on any uncertainty.
2. Wire it into `wipReap`'s owner map alongside the existing `wipOwnerState` landed check.
3. Unit-test the resolver over the full vocabulary; assert a recoverable dead-session delta stays KEPT and only a subsumed/empty one reaps.
4. Re-run `fak wip reap --dry-run --json` against the live tree; confirm it now proposes the dead-session garbage and still keeps every recoverable snapshot.

## Batch policy

One focused change to the reap resolver. Not a spam batch; do not fan this out into per-ref tickets.

## Work estimate

3 points. A single closed-session resolver added to `cmd/fak/wip.go` plus its wiring into `wipReap`; the delete/keep fold and closed-state vocabulary in `internal/wipref/reap.go` already exist.

## Overall completion contribution

3/20 points of the #3873 retention/GC epic (about 15%): it closes the *collection* half of retention, complementary to the #5336 read-path scaling that already landed.

## Target operating envelope

- tests: >= 3 cases
- dead-session refs reaped in a live dry-run: >= 1 ref
- recoverable snapshots kept: >= 1 snapshot

## Witnessed operating envelope

- tests: >= 3 cases
