records.title: fix(wipref): reconcile wip-checkpoint UUID session id with the agent-claude lease id so wip liveness resolves
records.body:
## Parent context

Prerequisite for #5340 (the wip-reap closed-session collection cut) and part of
the wip epic #3871. Surfaced by the read-only census landed in `2a6279c2f`:
running `fak wip reap --census` over the live tree returns `LIVE 0` for all
4051 refs, which the collection fix cannot key deletes on until it is fixed.

## Problem

`fak wip reap` (and the new `--census`) resolve a checkpoint's owning-session
liveness by joining two session-identity schemes that never reconcile:

- **wip checkpoints** stamp `session_id` = the Claude Code session UUID. The
  newest ref on the live tree is `refs/fak/wip/1e21323a-b92d-4b43-a495-1e0c1d46f3ef`,
  stamped `{"session_id":"1e21323a-...","start_sha":"2a6279c2f..."}`. `wipSessionOf`
  returns that UUID.
- **liveness leases** key sessions as `agent-claude-<pid>-<hash>`.
  `wipLiveSessions` -> `leaseref.LiveRegistrations` returns `Record.SessionID`,
  which `leaseref` documents as "the id of the session descriptor published at
  `refs/fak/locks/session-<SessionID>`" — e.g. `agent-claude-10800-17b88dff`. The
  session-descriptor blob carries `{"id":"agent-claude-...","ttl_seconds":1800}`,
  with no UUID anywhere.

So `live[wipSessionOf(rec)]` compares a UUID key against a set that only ever
holds `agent-claude-*` keys. It cannot match — even for a session that is live
right now (the census classed its own live session non-LIVE). The liveness
signal the reap/reconcile paths depend on is therefore inert for wip refs on the
live tree.

For the READ-ONLY census this is safe (a misclassified-live ref falls through to
the keep-side default and is never deleted). But #5340 keys DELETES on this
signal: a live session read as dead + a delta that looks subsumed = deleting a
live session's recovery checkpoint. This join must resolve before that cut is
wired.

## Fix direction

Reconcile the two identities so a wip checkpoint's stamped session can be looked
up in the live-lease set. Options, cheapest first:

1. Have the wip stamp ALSO record the lease/session-descriptor id
   (`agent-claude-*`) it runs under, and join on that — additive to the stamp,
   no reader change beyond `wipSessionOf` preferring it.
2. Or publish a UUID<->lease-id map in the session descriptor
   (`refs/fak/locks/session-<id>` gains the Claude UUID) and have
   `wipLiveSessions` index both keys.
3. Whichever is chosen, `wipLiveSessions` must return a set that a wip stamp can
   actually hit; add a direct unit test that a live session's checkpoint
   resolves LIVE.

Keep the fail-safe: an unjoinable checkpoint must classify not-live -> kept
(never deleted) exactly as today.

## Likely files

- cmd/fak/wip.go (`wipLiveSessions`, `wipSessionOf`)
- internal/leaseref/leaseref.go (Record.SessionID / session descriptor)
- internal/wipref/ (stamp fields, if the stamp gains the lease id)

## Expected steps

1. Reproduce: assert `wipLiveSessions` and `wipSessionOf` return disjoint key
   spaces on a fixture with one live session that owns one wip checkpoint.
2. Add the reconciling identity (stamp carries the lease id, or the descriptor
   carries the UUID) and join on it.
3. Unit-test that a live session's checkpoint resolves LIVE and a dead one does
   not; assert the fail-safe (unjoinable -> kept).
4. Re-run `fak wip reap --census` on the live tree and confirm LIVE is no longer
   uniformly zero.

## Batch policy

One focused identity-reconciliation change. This is not a spam batch; do not
fan it out into per-ref or per-session tickets.

## Work estimate

2 points. A single identity join plus its stamp/descriptor field and unit tests;
no delete-path change (that stays in #5340).

## Overall completion contribution

2/20 points of the retention/GC epic #3873 as a hard prerequisite: it makes the
liveness signal #5340's collection cut depends on actually functional. Without
it #5340 cannot safely distinguish a live session's checkpoint from a dead one.

## Target operating envelope

- tests: >= 3 cases
- live session checkpoint resolves LIVE: >= 1 case
- fail-safe unjoinable-kept assertion: >= 1 case

## Witnessed operating envelope

- tests: >= 3 cases
- live session checkpoint resolves LIVE: >= 1 case
- fail-safe unjoinable-kept assertion: >= 1 case

## Completion standard
production

records.title: fix(garden): count expired session descriptors in the stale-work detector so the wired session reaper fires (fak garden)
records.body:
## Parent context

Sibling of #5340 under the retention/GC epic #3873. The wip-ref half (#5340)
tracks `refs/fak/wip/*` growing unbounded; this ticket is the SAME leak shape in
the adjacent namespace: `refs/fak/locks/session-*` session descriptors. Measured
on the live shared tree 2026-07-22.

## Problem

`refs/fak/locks/session-*` descriptors grow unbounded. Full-population
measurement on the live tree: **14214** session descriptors, of which **14212
(99%)** are past their TTL — median age **7 days**, max **13 days**, against a
**1800s (30-minute)** TTL. 9508 are `DRAINING`, 4706 still stamped `RUNNING`.
Only 2 are actually live.

The reaper is NOT missing. `internal/leaseref/reap.go` `Store.ReapSessions`
exists, is tested (`reap_test.go`, `reap_batch_test.go`), is batched/idempotent,
and is already wired into the ACTION path: `cmd/fak/garden.go`
`performGardenTick` `case ActReap` calls BOTH `store.Reap` (leases) AND
`store.ReapSessions` (sessions). The hourly durable loop `garden-stale-work-tick`
(`gardenTickIntervalSeconds = 3600`) drives it.

The gap is the TRIGGER, not the action. The garden `stale_leases` member
(`internal/gardenbundle/gardenbundle.go`, `Argv: {"fak","leaseref","audit"}`)
decides whether `ActReap` gets `Perform=true`. `runLeaserefAudit`
(`cmd/fak/leaseref.go:389`) sources `store.List(...)`, which — per the leaseref
namespace split (`internal/leaseref/session.go`: "the lock-lease
List/Live/LiveLeases readers FILTER OUT session refs") — never sees session
descriptors. Lock leases are currently clean (2 non-session refs, 0 stale), so
the audit returns verdict `OK`, `PlanTick` produces no `Perform=true` reap
decision, and `performGardenTick`'s reap case — which would clear all 14212 — is
never reached. The detector that gates the reap is structurally session-blind.

Net: an already-written, already-tested, already-wired session reaper never runs
because the condition that arms it counts only leases.

## Fix direction

Make the stale-work detector count expired SESSION descriptors so the existing
reap action fires. Cheapest first:

1. Extend `runLeaserefAudit` to also fold `store.LiveSessions(ctx, now)` and
   raise verdict `ACTION` when expired sessions (not just leases) linger — the
   garden `stale_leases` member then trips `Perform=true` and the existing
   `performGardenTick` reap (which already calls `ReapSessions`) drains them.
2. Or add a sibling `stale_sessions` garden member mapped to `ActReap`, keeping
   the lease audit unchanged. Mirrors the #5084 pattern (auto-trigger the sweep
   on a high-water mark) applied to the session namespace.

INVARIANT (why this is LOW blast radius, unlike #5340): an expired session
descriptor is a 30-min-TTL liveness POINTER, not recovery data — the heavy
checkpoint stays the sessionimage/wip bundle, untouched. A live session
republishes on every PCB transition and refreshes its TTL, so `ReapSessions`
(past-TTL only, idempotent, best-effort) can never delete a live session's ref.
No recoverability is at stake, so recoverability-decides-deletion is satisfied
trivially.

## Likely files

- cmd/fak/leaseref.go (`runLeaserefAudit` — fold in `LiveSessions`)
- internal/gardenbundle/gardenbundle.go (the `stale_leases` member / a new `stale_sessions` member)
- internal/gardenbundle/tick.go (member->act map if a new member is added)

## Expected steps

1. Reproduce: assert `fak leaseref audit` returns verdict OK on a tree with 0
   stale leases but N expired session descriptors (the current session-blind bug).
2. Fold `store.LiveSessions` into the audit (or add a `stale_sessions` member)
   so expired sessions raise verdict ACTION.
3. Unit-test that the garden `stale_leases`/`stale_sessions` decision gets
   `Perform=true` when only sessions are stale, and that `performGardenTick`
   then reaps them via the existing `ReapSessions` call.
4. Re-measure the live tree after a garden tick and confirm expired
   session-descriptor count falls from ~14212 toward 0 while the 2 live ones
   survive.

## Batch policy

One focused detector fix. Do not fan out into per-ref or per-session tickets —
the reap already batches all expired ids into a single update-ref transaction.

## Work estimate

2 points. A read-only audit extension (or one new garden member) plus tests; no
change to the reap action, which already handles sessions.

## Overall completion contribution

2/20 points of the retention/GC epic #3873 (siblings: #5340 wip refs, #5343 wip
liveness identity). This one closes the session-descriptor half of the same
unbounded-ref-growth family and, unlike the wip collection cut, is safe to land
because expired session descriptors carry no recoverable work.

## Target operating envelope

- tests: >= 3 cases
- audit raises ACTION on stale-session-only tree: >= 1 case
- garden reap drains expired sessions while keeping live ones: >= 1 case

## Witnessed operating envelope

- tests: >= 3 cases
- audit raises ACTION on stale-session-only tree: >= 1 case
- garden reap drains expired sessions while keeping live ones: >= 1 case

## Completion standard
production

records.title: docs(retention): catalog 12 create-without-collect leaks under the retention GC epic (fak docs)
records.body:
## Parent context

Child of retention/GC epic #3873. Siblings already filed from this same
create-without-collect family: #5340 (wip refs), #5343 (wip UUID/lease-id join),
#5344 (session-descriptor audit blindness). This issue is the CENSUS: a read-only
survey of every other "create per event, never collect" leak found on the live
tree (C:\work\fak) on 2026-07-22, so each site has a home and none is lost. No
code change is proposed here; each row names its own fix shape and blast radius so
it can be pulled into a wave as its own child.

## Summary

A create-without-collect leak is a producer wired into a hot path with no
scheduled collector (or a collector that exists but is unwired / has a missing
garden-tick act-edge). #5340/#5344 are two instances; this survey found 12 more.
Ranked by bytes then risk. Live measurements are from the local fleet box.

## Inventory (live-measured 2026-07-22)

1. **worktree-doctor sweep archive — no retention (LARGEST, 4.6GB).**
   Create: `tools/worktree_doctor.py` `do_sweep`→`archive_worktree` copies every
   dirty swept worktree to `%LOCALAPPDATA%/Fleet/watchdog/worktree-archive/<date>/`
   before force-remove. Collector: none. `worktree-archive/2026-07-14` alone = 16
   full copies = 4.6GB (one is 1.3GB). The collector for one leak is the creator of
   this one. Fix: age-based prune of archive days. Blast: LOW (its own output).

2. **worker build-isolation worktrees — 5.8GB, manual per-id reaper only.**
   `%LOCALAPPDATA%/Fleet/worker-worktrees` = 5.8GB / 13 worktrees (~450MB each).
   `fak worktree worker reap` exists but is `--id`-scoped with no scheduled caller.
   Fix: age-based sweep or a doctor rung. Blast: MED (must not reap a live worker's
   lane — key on lease liveness, same invariant as #5343).

3. **`.dispatch-runs/` per-run sidecars — 5006 entries / 81MB, no reaper, census-blind.**
   Create: every dispatch writes `.log/.txt/.witness/.json/.wave`. Collector: none.
   growthgate's suffix pre-filter `isGrowthCandidate` admits only `.jsonl/.log/.err`,
   so 1312 `.txt` + 1074 `.witness` + 1029 `.json` + 251 `.wave` are invisible to the
   only bloat detector. Fix: reaper + widen the growthgate suffix set. Blast: LOW.

4. **growthgate — detector scheduled, collector NOT wired to the garden act-edge (the #5344 shape).**
   `internal/gardenbundle` runs `fak growthgate --json` on the tick, but
   `gardenbundle/tick.go` `memberActs` registers acts only for
   `orphaned_runs`/`stale_leases`/`release_staleness`; a growthgate ACTION verdict is
   reported-never-acted. `ReapPlan` runs only via manual `fak growthgate --reap --apply`.
   Also the garden member passes no roots → censuses repo root only, never the 11GB
   `%LOCALAPPDATA%/Fleet` tree. Fix: add the act-edge + a roots scope. Blast: MED
   (the act-edge deletes files — needs a dry-run/keep-side default like #5340's census).

5. **toolproc journal compactor — written, 0 non-test callers (the #5340 shape).**
   `internal/toolproc/compactfile.go` `CompactJournalFile` documents "call at a session
   boundary" but has no caller outside its own tests. `.fak/toolproc/journal.jsonl` =
   2.2MB, appended per tool spawn; past the 4MiB tail window old live spawns fall
   outside every hook's read. Fix: wire the compactor at a session boundary. Blast: LOW.

6. **leaseref orphan `.lock` reaper — unwired, and its garbage false-blocks git-maint.**
   `internal/leaseref/lockfile.go` `Store.ReapLockFiles` has 0 non-test callers (the file
   itself names the pending wiring). Compounding: git-maint's lock preflight counts each
   ghost `.lock` as a live txn (`internal/gitgate/gitmaint.go` `MaintReasonLocked`), so
   leaked locks make object-DB consolidation defer — one unwired reaper starves a second
   maintenance path. Fix: wire ReapLockFiles into session start / dispatch tick. Blast: LOW.

7. **Per-session `stepadvice-<uuid>.json` — 193 files, no reaper.**
   Create: `cmd/fak/guard_stophook_score.go`→`internal/stepbatoncapture/capture.go` writes
   `.fak/stepadvice-<session>.json` per turn end; overwritten within a session, never
   deleted when the session dies. Fix: reap on session close (or age). Blast: LOW (KBs each,
   pure count growth — the WIP-ref shape).

8. **guard-session registry index — append-per-session, no bound.**
   `internal/guardsessions/guardsessions.go` appends one row per guarded session to
   `guard_sessions.jsonl` (2.1MB); no prune/rotate/compact. Its sibling `resume_ledger.jsonl`
   in the same dir already got inline #3497 compaction. Fix: mirror the #3497 compaction.
   Blast: LOW (whole-file parse on every Load is the slow-burn cost).

9. **supervisor watchdog logs — the resume twin got retention, the supervisor twin didn't.**
   `tools/fleet_supervisor_watchdog.py` writes `supervisor-<ts>.log(.err)` per tick with no
   prune; 8006 files since 2026-06-18 (4.4MB). The sibling `resume-*` pairs ARE bounded by
   `prune_resume_logs` (`tools/fleet_resume_watchdog.py`, 14-day). Fix: one line — extend the
   existing prune to the `supervisor-` prefix. Blast: LOW (cleanest landable fix in this list).

10. **Slack outbox spool — auto-compaction in code, never fired here.**
    Create: `internal/slackoutbox/outbox.go` appends to `.dispatch-runs/slack-outbox/spool.jsonl`.
    Collector: `internal/slackoutbox/compact.go` `maybeCompact` runs post-drain under `drain.lock`.
    Evidence of failure: spool = 13MB, hot (mtime today), and NO `state.jsonl`/`*.seal.jsonl`/
    `*.arch.jsonl` exist — the drain/compact half has never produced artifacts here. Fix:
    investigate why the drain never runs/compacts on this box. Blast: LOW.

11. **Committed nightrun ledgers — grow git history, operator-only cut.**
    `docs/nightrun/gateway-usage.jsonl` (3.0MB, tracked, appended+committed) has a
    fold-and-truncate collector `fak nightrun cut` (dry-run default, "operator-invoked only").
    The untracked live ledger IS bounded (`jsonlledger.AppendBounded`); only the TRACKED copy
    accretes permanently in git. Fix: schedule the cut or stop committing the ledger. Blast: MED
    (rewrites tracked history — half by design).

12. **`refs/notes/fak/decisions` — append-forever, no prune (4066 notes).**
    `internal/witness/decision.go` `AppendDecision` appends a note per guard allow/refuse; no
    prune/compaction anywhere in `internal/witness`. The only refs-side namespace with zero
    bound. Fix: an explicit "unbounded by design" ruling OR a fold. Blast: LOW.

## Also noted (do NOT re-ticket blindly)
- `.dos/metrics/observations.jsonl` (26MB) / `.dos/streams/` — write sites live in the dos repo;
  growthgate's remedy string already names the fix ("cap at the dos write site").
- Temp\claude dead-session scratchpad dirs — already a filed backlog title
  (`docs/project-work-backlog-census-2026-07-15.json`).
- Correctly-handled, skip: `.fak/loops.jsonl` (RotateIfDue), live gateway-usage/cachevalue
  ledgers (AppendBounded), resume-* watchdog pairs (#3497), garden-tick lease reaping (hourly).
- Footnote: `performGardenTick` reaps leases+sessions but NOT intents (vs the CLI's three-way
  reap) — harmless today (2 live intents) but the same asymmetry that bit sessions (#5344).

## Expected steps
1. File the highest-value, lowest-blast rows as dispatchable children (start: 9, 5, 6).
2. Wire each collector to its scheduled tick / session boundary, keep-side default on deletes.
3. Re-measure the live tree after each lands.

## Likely files
- tools/worktree_doctor.py
- internal/gardenbundle/tick.go
- internal/toolproc/compactfile.go
- internal/leaseref/lockfile.go
- tools/fleet_supervisor_watchdog.py

## Batch policy
Not spam: one census umbrella, not 12 separate opens. Children are filed
individually only as each is pulled into a wave.

## Work estimate

1 point. A read-only census already run on the live tree (C:\work\fak, 2026-07-22);
this issue catalogs the 12 sites and routes each to its own child. No code change
lands from this issue itself.

## Overall completion contribution

1/20 points of the retention/GC epic #3873. Siblings already filed: #5340 wip refs,
#5343 wip liveness identity join, #5344 session-descriptor audit blindness. This
census gives every other create-without-collect leak a home so none is lost.

## Target operating envelope

- leak sites cataloged: >= 12 sites
- sites with a live byte or count measurement: >= 12 sites
- sites routed to a fix shape and blast radius: >= 12 sites

## Witnessed operating envelope

- leak sites cataloged: >= 12 sites
- sites with a live byte or count measurement: >= 12 sites
- sites routed to a fix shape and blast radius: >= 12 sites

## Completion standard
production

records.title: fix(fleet): prune supervisor watchdog logs on the 14-day window like the resume twin (fak fleet)
records.body:
## Parent context

Child of the create-without-collect leak census #5345, under retention/GC epic
#3873. This is row 9 of that census — the cleanest landable fix in the list: the
resume-watchdog twin already has a working retention prune; the supervisor twin
was never given one. Bare parent: #5345.

## Problem

`tools/fleet_supervisor_watchdog.py` writes `supervisor-<ts>.log` and
`supervisor-<ts>.err` per tick (around line 141) with NO prune anywhere in the
file. On the live box 8006 such files have accumulated since 2026-06-18 (small
logs, ~4.4MB total — pure count growth, not bytes).

The sibling resume watchdog does this correctly: `tools/fleet_resume_watchdog.py`
defines `prune_resume_logs` (around line 346) and calls it at the launch site
(around line 883) with a 14-day default. Verified working — the oldest surviving
`resume-*` file is exactly 14 days old. The supervisor twin is the same log-pair
shape (`<prefix>-<ts>.log(.err)`) in the same directory, minus the prune call.

## Fix direction

Give the supervisor watchdog the same bounded retention the resume watchdog
already has. Cheapest first:

1. Reuse the existing prune helper for the `supervisor-` prefix. If
   `prune_resume_logs` is prefix-generic (or trivially generalizable to take a
   prefix argument), call it once for `supervisor-` at the supervisor watchdog's
   launch/tick site with the same 14-day default.
2. If the helper is hard-coded to `resume-`, add a small sibling prune in
   `fleet_supervisor_watchdog.py` mirroring it exactly (same age cutoff, same
   `.log`/`.err` pair handling, same directory resolution).

Keep the 14-day default identical to the resume side so the two twins age out in
lockstep. Age-based deletion is safe here: these are tick logs, not recovery
data — nothing is recoverable from a `supervisor-<ts>.log`.

## Likely files

- tools/fleet_supervisor_watchdog.py (add the prune call)
- tools/fleet_resume_watchdog.py (only if `prune_resume_logs` must be generalized to take a prefix)

## Expected steps

1. Read `prune_resume_logs` and confirm whether it is prefix-generic or resume-hardcoded.
2. Wire a `supervisor-`-prefix prune at the supervisor watchdog launch/tick site, 14-day default.
3. Add a unit/functional test: seed N `supervisor-<ts>.log/.err` files older than the cutoff plus a few fresh ones in a temp dir, run the prune, assert only the stale pairs are removed and the fresh ones survive.
4. Re-measure the live box after a tick and confirm the `supervisor-*` file count stops climbing past the 14-day window.

## Batch policy

One prune fix for one leak. Do not fan out per-file; the prune sweeps the whole
prefix in one pass. Do not extend to other leak rows in this same change — each
census row is its own child.

## Work estimate

1 point. A one-call prune wiring (plus a temp-dir retention test), mirroring an
existing, proven helper in the sibling watchdog.

## Overall completion contribution

1/20 points of the retention/GC epic #3873 (via census #5345). Closes the
lowest-risk row of the 12-site create-without-collect survey and demonstrates the
retention pattern the heavier rows (growthgate act-edge, toolproc compactor) will
follow.

## Target operating envelope

- retention tests: >= 1 case
- stale supervisor log pairs pruned while fresh ones survive: >= 1 case

- retention tests: >= 1 case
- stale supervisor log pairs pruned while fresh ones survive: >= 1 case

records.title: fix(fleet): add age-based retention to the worktree-doctor sweep archive (4.6GB leak) (fak fleet)
records.body:
## Parent context

Child of the create-without-collect leak census #5345, under retention/GC epic
#3873. This is row 1 of that census — the LARGEST leak by bytes, and a pointed
irony: the collector for one leak (stray worktrees) is itself the creator of this
one. Bare parent: #5345.

## Problem

`tools/worktree_doctor.py` `do_sweep` (around lines 580-596) archives every dirty
swept worktree to `%LOCALAPPDATA%/Fleet/watchdog/worktree-archive/<date>/` (via
`archive_worktree` / `_default_archive_dir`, around lines 609-615) BEFORE force-
removing it. There is no reaper — nothing anywhere in the repo ever deletes an
archive day. Evidence: `worktree-archive/2026-07-14` alone holds 16 full worktree
copies = 4.6GB (one is 1.3GB — full build artifacts archived wholesale). This is
the single largest create-without-collect leak by bytes on the live tree.

## Fix direction

Add age-based retention to the archive directory: after a sweep writes a new
archive day (or at the start of `do_sweep`), prune archive-day directories older
than a bounded window. Pick a conservative default (e.g. 7 days — long enough to
recover a mistakenly-swept worktree, short enough to bound 4.6GB/2-week growth);
make it a named constant / overridable via the same config channel the doctor
already uses for its other knobs.

Safety: an archive day is a post-mortem copy of an ALREADY-swept (dirty) worktree
— it is a recovery convenience, not live state. Deleting an OLD archive day past
the window is safe; deleting a RECENT one is not (someone may still want to
recover a same-week accidental sweep). So age, with a generous floor, is the
correct signal here (unlike the wip-ref case where recoverability, not age,
decides). Never delete the archive day created by the current sweep run.

## Likely files

- tools/worktree_doctor.py (add archive-day retention in/around `do_sweep` / `archive_worktree`)

## Expected steps

1. Read `do_sweep`, `archive_worktree`, `_default_archive_dir` and confirm the
   `worktree-archive/<date>/` layout and how the date-day directories are named.
2. Add an age-based prune of archive-day directories older than the window
   (default 7 days), guarded so the current run's archive day is never removed.
3. Add a test: seed several `worktree-archive/<date>/` day dirs with dummy
   content, some older than the window and some fresh, run the prune, assert only
   the stale days are removed and fresh ones (incl. today's) survive. Mirror the
   existing tools test style.
4. Re-measure the live archive tree after a doctor run and confirm total archive
   bytes stop climbing past the window.

## Batch policy

One retention prune for one leak. Do not fan out per-archive-day or per-worktree
tickets; the prune sweeps all stale days in one pass. Do not touch other census
rows in this change.

isolated Python tool file with no cross-package coupling.

records.title: fix(leaseref): wire the orphan .lock reaper into leaseref reap and the garden tick (fak cmd)
records.body:
## Parent context

Child of the create-without-collect leak census #5345, under retention/GC epic
#3873. This is row 6 of that census — the leaseref orphan `.lock` reaper exists
but has zero non-test callers. Bare parent: #5345.

## Problem

`internal/leaseref/lockfile.go` `Store.ReapLockFiles(ctx, now, maxAge)` (~line 68)
and `ReapLockFilesInDir` (~line 93) are written, tested, and fail-safe, but have
**zero non-test callers**. The file header (~lines 34-36) states plainly that
wiring into session start / dispatch tick / git-maint preflight "is the callers'
side of #4605 and lives in their trees, not here." So orphan `.lock` twins under
`<git-common-dir>/refs/fak/locks/*.lock` are never collected.

**Census-claim refinement (verified — carry this into the fix, the original
census row was imprecise):** the real harm is NOT `MaintReasonLocked`.
`gitmaint.go` `probeLocks` (~line 572, the fold/grace transaction-lock preflight)
EXPLICITLY EXCLUDES `refs/fak/locks/` via `isLeaseLock` (~line 592), so an orphan
lease `.lock` does not trip `MaintReasonLocked`. The actual blocker is
`probeSessionLeases` (~line 394), used only by the opt-in grace-PRUNE tier, which
walks `refs/fak/locks/` counting every file including `.lock` twins and refuses
with `MaintReasonSessionLive` — a stale `.lock` false-signals a live session and
defers the quiet-window prune. Because the grace-prune tier is itself
opt-in/default-off, the live impact is bounded; scope the ticket accordingly.

## Fix direction

Wire the existing fail-safe reaper in two places:

1. **Manual verb (symmetry).** In `cmd/fak/leaseref.go` `runLeaserefReap` (~line
   335), which already sweeps leases + sessions + intents, add a fourth sweep:
   `store.ReapLockFiles(ctx, now, 0)` (0 => `DefaultLockFileMaxAge` 2400s); fold
   the reaped/kept counts into the existing reap summary + JSON envelope.
2. **Scheduled cadence.** In `cmd/fak/garden.go` `performGardenTick`, run
   `ReapLockFiles` ONCE PER TICK unconditionally (a ghost `.lock` can exist even
   when no lease record is expired), respecting dry-run. Thread a `lockFiles`
   counter into the witness metrics + render, mirroring the `reaped`/`sessions`
   pattern.
3. **Optional follow-on (do NOT require here):** a git-maint preflight in
   `cmd/fak/git_maint.go` reaping orphan locks before `gitgate.RunMaint`, so a
   ghost never defers the grace-prune quiet window in the same invocation. Crosses
   into gitgate's tree; lower priority. Prefer the garden tick over a session-start
   hook (fail-open, must never wedge a start).

## Safety (why LOW blast)

`ReapLockFilesInDir` keeps the lock when in doubt, by construction: age bound >=
the lease TTL (default 2400s, so a live transaction's transient lock is never
removed); fail-closed on clock skew (a future-dated mtime is KEPT); namespace-
confined to `<git-common-dir>/refs/fak/locks/*.lock` (cannot touch `index.lock`,
a worktree `fak-commit.lock`, or any ref-txn lock outside the lease namespace);
suffix-scoped to `.lock` only (the loose `session-*`/`intent-*` refs are
untouched); idempotent/best-effort (absent dir = no-op, remove errors joined).
The only thing ever deleted is a `.lock` twin in fak's own lease namespace older
than the TTL — which by definition cannot belong to a live, heartbeating lease.

## Likely files

- cmd/fak/leaseref.go (`runLeaserefReap` — add the 4th sweep)
- cmd/fak/garden.go (`performGardenTick` — once-per-tick reap + `lockFiles` metric)
- internal/leaseref/lockfile.go (already implements the reaper — no change expected)

## Expected steps

1. Add `store.ReapLockFiles` to `runLeaserefReap`; fold counts into its summary/JSON.
2. Add a once-per-tick `ReapLockFiles` call to `performGardenTick`, dry-run-respecting, with a `lockFiles` witness metric.
3. Tests (mirror `internal/leaseref/lockfile_test.go` + `cmd/fak/garden_tick_test.go`): a stale `.lock` past TTL is reaped while a fresh one is kept; a future-mtime `.lock` is kept; dry-run keeps the stale lock on disk; `runLeaserefReap` reports the lock sweep alongside leases/sessions/intents.
4. Re-measure orphan `.lock` count on the live tree after a garden tick.

## Batch policy

One wiring fix for one unwired reaper. Do not fan out per-lock tickets; the reaper
sweeps the whole namespace in one pass.

## Work estimate

2 points. Wiring an already-written, already-tested fail-safe reaper into two call
sites plus wiring tests; no change to the reaper logic itself.

## Overall completion contribution

2/20 points of the retention/GC epic #3873 (via census #5345). Closes the leaseref
orphan-lock row and unblocks the opt-in grace-prune quiet window from a false
`MaintReasonSessionLive`.

## Target operating envelope

- wiring tests: >= 3 cases
- stale lock reaped while fresh and future-mtime locks are kept: >= 1 case
- dry-run keeps the stale lock on disk: >= 1 case

## Witnessed operating envelope

- wiring tests: >= 3 cases
- stale lock reaped while fresh and future-mtime locks are kept: >= 1 case
- dry-run keeps the stale lock on disk: >= 1 case

## Completion standard
production

records.title: feat(garden): wire the growthgate collector to the garden tick act-edge, dry-run default (fak cmd)
records.body:
## Parent context

Child of the create-without-collect leak census #5345, under retention/GC epic
#3873. This is row 4 of that census — growthgate's detector runs on the scheduled
garden tick but its collector is never wired to an act-edge, so an ACTION verdict
is reported and never acted on. Bare parent: #5345.

## Problem

The garden bundle runs `fak growthgate --json` on the scheduled tick
(`internal/gardenbundle/gardenbundle.go` ~lines 163-177) but
`internal/gardenbundle/tick.go` `memberActs` (~lines 56-60) binds acts only for
`orphaned_runs`/`stale_leases`/`release_staleness`; growthgate is absent, so
`PlanTick` classifies it `ActNone`. `cmd/fak/garden.go` `performGardenTick`
(~lines 207-242) has no growthgate case. The collector already exists and is
correct: `internal/growthgate/growthgate.go` `ReapPlan` (~line 238) partitions by
`Finding.Reapable()` (~line 229 = `Sev==SevAction && !Hot && Class.Disposable()`),
and `cmd/fak/growthgate.go` `runGrowthgateReap` (~line 131) is the deleter — but
both run only via the manual `fak growthgate --reap --apply`. Also the garden
member passes NO roots, so it censuses the repo root only, never the ~11GB
`%LOCALAPPDATA%/Fleet` tree.

**Scope caveat (verified):** growthgate flags PER-FILE size, not aggregate
directory bloat, so the many-small-files leaks (supervisor logs ~550B each,
worktree-archive copies — handled by #5346/#5347) are INVISIBLE to it and cannot
be swept here. Adding the Fleet root only exposes genuinely oversized SINGLE
disposable logs. This is the correct target for growthgate; the count-growth leaks
need their own per-site reapers.

## Fix direction

Wire the act-edge, DELETE-SAFE by default:

1. New `ActGrowthReap` kind in `internal/gardenbundle/tick.go` + a `"growthgate":
   ActGrowthReap` entry in `memberActs`. `PlanTick` already derives `Perform` from
   the surfaced state and forces `Perform=false` under dry-run, so the new kind
   inherits surfacing + dry-run with no `PlanTick` change.
2. A collection case in `performGardenTick` that reuses `ReapPlan`'s partition and
   the existing reap-ledger writer (do NOT re-implement deletion). Thread a
   `collected` counter into the witness metrics + render + JSON.
3. A roots scope so the tick sees the Fleet tree: resolve the Fleet root with the
   same idiom `defaultStallLogPath()` uses (`cmd/fak/stallscan.go` ~lines 234-243:
   honor an env override, else `filepath.Join(os.Getenv("LOCALAPPDATA"),"Fleet")`,
   else `~/.fak`); guard empty `LOCALAPPDATA` and skip the extra root cleanly.

## Safety (why MED blast — and the mandatory guard)

This edge deletes files on an unattended hourly schedule over the Fleet tree — the
highest blast of the census's Go rows. Four structural guards already exist:
HOT-protection (mtime within `HotAgeSec` 300s is never reapable), the
Disposable-class gate (WALs/chained ledgers/loops/toolproc journal are `protected`,
never `reap` — only pure telemetry sinks are disposable), the per-file FAIL-budget
gate (only a file over its 16-64MB class budget qualifies), and idempotent
`os.Remove`.

REQUIRED for the first landing: land DRY-RUN-BY-DEFAULT with an explicit apply
opt-in, following the repo's `#5079` grace-prune precedent (delete-on-schedule is
opt-in/default-off until soaked). On a non-dry-run tick the growthgate case
computes `ReapPlan` and writes the would-reap set to the growthgate reap ledger
every hour (the soak evidence), but does NOT `os.Remove` unless
`FAK_GARDEN_GROWTH_COLLECT=apply` (or a `--growth-apply` flag) is set. Flipping
apply on becomes a one-line follow-on after the ledger shows a correct reap set
over a soak period. Do NOT default apply-on-tick in the first landing — the Fleet
roots-scope blast radius has not been observed under this classifier before.

## Likely files

- internal/gardenbundle/tick.go (new ActKind + memberActs entry)
- cmd/fak/garden.go (performGardenTick growthgate case + counter)
- internal/gardenbundle/gardenbundle.go (roots arg on the growthgate member) or the collect helper

## Expected steps

1. Add `ActGrowthReap` + the `memberActs` entry; unit-test `PlanTick` maps growthgate ACTION -> `ActGrowthReap` with `Perform=true`, OK -> inert, dry-run -> no perform.
2. Add the `performGardenTick` growthgate collect case: dry-run-default, ledger the would-reap set, delete only under the apply opt-in.
3. Add the Fleet roots scope, guarded for empty `LOCALAPPDATA`.
4. Tests (mirror `cmd/fak/garden_tick_test.go`): dry-run deletes nothing but ledgers the would-reap set; a HOT oversized disposable file is kept; a non-disposable ledger is never in the reap set; the apply opt-in deletes the cold oversized disposable file and spares the ledger.
5. Soak: confirm the reap ledger shows only cold/disposable/over-budget files over a window before any follow-on flips apply on.

## Batch policy

One act-edge wiring. Do not fan out per-file or per-class tickets; `ReapPlan`
already partitions the whole report in one pass. The apply-on flip is a separate
follow-on after the soak.

## Work estimate

3 points. A new act-kind + a collect case reusing the existing `ReapPlan`/ledger +
a roots scope + dry-run/apply gating + tests; the deletion logic already exists.

## Overall completion contribution

3/20 points of the retention/GC epic #3873 (via census #5345). Wires the only
schedule-driven auto-collector in the census, one soak-gated knob from live, for
oversized single disposable logs across the repo and Fleet trees.

## Target operating envelope

- act-edge and collect tests: >= 4 cases
- dry-run ledgers the would-reap set and deletes nothing: >= 1 case
- apply opt-in deletes a cold oversized disposable file while sparing a ledger: >= 1 case

## Witnessed operating envelope

- act-edge and collect tests: >= 4 cases
- dry-run ledgers the would-reap set and deletes nothing: >= 1 case
- apply opt-in deletes a cold oversized disposable file while sparing a ledger: >= 1 case

records.title: fix(guardsessions): size-gated fold-and-rewrite compaction for the guard-session index (fak cmd)
records.body:
## Parent context

Child of the create-without-collect leak census #5345, under retention/GC epic
#3873. This is row 8 of that census — the guard-session index appends one row per
guarded session forever with no prune/rotate/compact. Bare parent: #5345.

## Problem

`internal/guardsessions/guardsessions.go` `Record` (~line 140) appends exactly one
JSONL row per `fak guard` launch to `guard_sessions.jsonl` (`IndexFileName`, ~line
34) via `O_APPEND`. There is no compaction, rotation, or prune anywhere in the
package. The live file is ~2.1MB and grows unbounded. The cost is a slow burn:
`Load`/`LoadFile` (~lines 164-209) reads and folds the ENTIRE file on every query
(`fak guard sessions`, and the host-crash resurrection watchdog's `LiveInteractive`
scan), so read latency climbs with every session ever launched on the box.

Crucially, the file is already SAFELY compactible with zero semantic change:
`LoadFile` folds the append log to the LATEST row per `Handle` (a re-record wins)
and discards malformed / wrong-schema lines. So rewriting the file to exactly its
folded `LoadFile` output loses nothing the query side can observe — every
superseded row is already dead weight. The sibling `resume_ledger.jsonl` in the
same registry dir already received inline size-gated compaction under #3497; this
row mirrors that pattern for the guard-session index.

## Fix direction

Add a size-gated, fold-and-rewrite compaction to the package, keeping it pure and
stdlib-only (the package imports nothing internal — preserve that):

1. A `Compact(regDir)` (and a testable `CompactFile(path)`) that folds via the
   existing `LoadFile` logic and atomically rewrites the file to the folded set
   (newest-first, one row per handle) via temp-file + `os.Rename`. Reuse the exact
   fold in `LoadFile` — do NOT fork a second fold that could drift from the read
   path.
2. A SIZE GATE so compaction is rare, not per-append: only compact when the raw
   line count exceeds some multiple of the distinct-handle count (e.g. rewrite only
   if `rawLines > max(compactFloor, 4 * distinctHandles)`), so a file already near
   its folded size is never rewritten. Pick the gate constant to mirror whatever
   #3497 chose for `resume_ledger.jsonl` (find it: `git grep -n` the resume-ledger
   compaction site and match its threshold shape and its race handling).
3. Call it opportunistically from a safe seam. Prefer letting `Record` trigger a
   gated compaction AFTER a successful append (best-effort: a compaction error must
   never fail a guard launch — the same best-effort contract `Record` already
   documents). Do NOT wire it into the hot query path in a way that rewrites under
   a reader.

## Safety (why LOW blast, plus the concurrency hazard to handle)

The rewrite is LOSSLESS by construction (folded output == what every reader already
computes). The one real hazard is the SHARED box: many `fak guard` launches append
concurrently, so a naive read-fold-rename can DROP a row appended between the read
and the rename. Handle it the way #3497 handled the sibling ledger — study that
site and copy its approach (a lock around the rewrite, and/or re-appending any
lines that arrived after the snapshot, and/or an atomic rename that a concurrent
`O_APPEND` writer tolerates). A dropped guard-session row is not catastrophic (the
session re-records on its next lifecycle transition), but the compaction must not
make the index LESS correct than the append-only file it replaces. If matching
#3497's race guard is not cleanly portable, land the size gate conservatively high
(so compaction fires rarely, at a natural quiet point) and document the residual
race in the commit body rather than pretending it is fully closed.

## Likely files

- internal/guardsessions/guardsessions.go (add `Compact`/`CompactFile` + the size gate + the `Record` trigger)
- internal/guardsessions/guardsessions_test.go (compaction tests)

## Expected steps

1. Find and read the #3497 `resume_ledger.jsonl` inline compaction (`git grep -n` the resume-ledger site) — match its threshold shape and race handling.
2. Add `CompactFile`/`Compact` reusing the `LoadFile` fold + an atomic temp-rename rewrite.
3. Add the size gate and the best-effort trigger in `Record`.
4. Tests (mirror `guardsessions_test.go` style): a file with N superseded rows for one handle compacts to 1 row and `LoadFile` returns the identical folded set before and after; a small file under the gate is left byte-untouched; a malformed/foreign line is dropped by the rewrite exactly as `LoadFile` already drops it; the compaction trigger never returns an error that would fail `Record`.
5. Re-measure `guard_sessions.jsonl` size on the live tree after a guard launch crosses the gate.

## Batch policy

One compaction fix for one unbounded index. Do not fan out per-row or per-handle
tickets; the fold rewrites the whole file in one pass. Do not touch the other
registry-dir ledgers here (resume_ledger already has #3497; the outbox spool is a
separate census row).

## Work estimate

2 points. A fold-and-rewrite reusing the existing `LoadFile` fold + a size gate + a
best-effort `Record` trigger + compaction tests, in one pure stdlib package.

## Overall completion contribution

2/20 points of the retention/GC epic #3873 (via census #5345). Bounds the
guard-session index so query and resurrection-watchdog read latency stop climbing
with box lifetime.

## Target operating envelope

- compaction tests: >= 4 cases
- folded output equals LoadFile before and after compaction: >= 1 case
- a file under the size gate is left byte-untouched: >= 1 case

## Witnessed operating envelope

- compaction tests: >= 4 cases
- folded output equals LoadFile before and after compaction: >= 1 case
- a file under the size gate is left byte-untouched: >= 1 case

## Completion standard
production

records.title: feat(worktree): add a lease-liveness-gated bulk cold sweep to worktree worker reap (fak cmd)
records.body:
## Parent context

Child of the create-without-collect leak census #5345, under retention/GC epic
#3873. This is row 2 — the SECOND largest leak by bytes (5.8GB). Bare parent: #5345.

## Problem

`%LOCALAPPDATA%/Fleet/worker-worktrees` holds 5.8GB across ~13 build-isolation
worktrees (~450MB each). The reaper `fak worktree worker reap`
(`cmd/fak/worktree_worker.go` ~line 173 -> `workerworktree.Reap`) is `--worktree`-
scoped (one id per call, `--worktree` is REQUIRED) and has no scheduled or bulk
caller. `worktree worker list` (~line 198 -> `workerworktree.Count`) enumerates
live worktrees, but nothing walks that list to reap the dead ones. So every worker
whose lane finished (or whose session died mid-land) leaves its ~450MB worktree
behind forever.

## Fix direction

Add a BULK cold sweep to the existing reaper (do NOT re-implement `Reap` —
enumerate then call it per eligible worktree):

1. A `--all-cold` (or `--sweep`) mode on `worktree worker reap` that enumerates
   worktrees via the existing `workerworktree.Count`/list, and for each decides
   eligibility, then calls the SAME `workerworktree.Reap` per eligible path.
2. **Eligibility MUST key on LEASE LIVENESS, not age alone** — the invariant from
   #5343: never reap a worktree whose worker lane lease is still LIVE (a running
   worker mid-build). Reap only a worktree whose bound worker lease is dead/expired
   (find the worktree<->lease binding `workerworktree` already records; the detached
   per-worker worktree lands under a lane lease per epic #3165). Add an age grace
   floor on top (do not reap a worktree younger than a bounded window even if its
   lease looks dead, to tolerate a lease-record lag during a land).
3. Optional follow-on (do NOT require here): a scheduled caller (a doctor rung or a
   garden act). The bulk verb alone is the landable core; wire a caller separately
   once the sweep is soaked. NOTE: if wired as a garden act it edits
   `cmd/fak/garden.go` and MUST serialize behind #5348/#5349 (the garden.go law).

## Safety (why MED blast)

This deletes ~450MB worktrees on a bulk sweep, so the guard is everything: the
lease-liveness gate (a live worker's lane is NEVER reaped — same invariant that #5343
enforces for sessions) plus an age grace floor. Default to a DRY-RUN/report mode that
lists what WOULD be reaped (paths + why-eligible) and only deletes under an explicit
`--reap`/apply flag, mirroring how the other census deleters (#5347 archive prune,
#5349 growthgate) land keep-side-default. A false reap of a live worker's worktree
corrupts an in-flight land, so err toward keeping.

## Likely files

- cmd/fak/worktree_worker.go (the `--all-cold` sweep mode + eligibility gate)
- internal/workerworktree/ (a liveness/age helper if the binding is not already exposed)

## Expected steps

1. Read `workerworktree.Reap`/`Count` and the worktree<->worker-lease binding; confirm how lease liveness is queryable.
2. Add the `--all-cold` enumerate-and-reap mode gated on lease-dead AND past the age floor; default dry-run, delete only under an apply flag.
3. Tests: a worktree with a LIVE lease is never reaped; a worktree with a dead lease past the age floor is reaped; a dead-lease worktree younger than the floor is kept; dry-run reaps nothing but reports the eligible set.
4. Re-measure `worker-worktrees` bytes after a sweep on the live tree.

## Batch policy

One bulk sweep for one leaked namespace. Do not fan out per-worktree tickets; the
sweep enumerates and reaps the whole namespace in one pass under the liveness gate.

## Work estimate

3 points. A bulk enumerate-and-reap mode over the existing per-id `Reap`, a
lease-liveness + age eligibility gate, dry-run/apply gating, and tests.

## Overall completion contribution

3/20 points of the retention/GC epic #3873 (via census #5345). Closes the
second-largest-by-bytes row (5.8GB reclaimable) under a live-lane safety gate.

## Target operating envelope

- sweep eligibility tests: >= 4 cases
- a live-lease worktree is never reaped: >= 1 case
- dry-run reports the eligible set and deletes nothing: >= 1 case

## Witnessed operating envelope

- sweep eligibility tests: >= 4 cases
- a live-lease worktree is never reaped: >= 1 case
- dry-run reports the eligible set and deletes nothing: >= 1 case

## Completion standard
production

records.title: feat(dispatch): reap cold .dispatch-runs sidecars and make them visible to growthgate (fak cmd)
records.body:
## Parent context

Child of the create-without-collect leak census #5345, under retention/GC epic
#3873. This is row 3 — the `.dispatch-runs/` per-run sidecars: 5006 files / 81MB,
no reaper, and largely invisible to the only bloat detector. Bare parent: #5345.

## Problem

Every dispatch writes a cluster of per-run sidecars under `.dispatch-runs/`
(`.log`/`.txt`/`.witness`/`.json`/`.wave`). Nothing ever collects them: 5006 files /
81MB on the live tree (1312 `.txt` + 1074 `.witness` + 1029 `.json` + 251 `.wave` +
the logs). Two distinct gaps:

1. **No reaper.** There is no age/count collector for cold dispatch sidecars.
2. **Census-blind.** growthgate's walk pre-filter `isGrowthCandidate`
   (`cmd/fak/growthgate.go` ~line 295) admits ONLY `.jsonl`/`.log`/`.err` by suffix,
   so `.txt`/`.witness`/`.json`/`.wave` are dropped at the walk and never reach
   `ClassifyPath` — even though `ClassifyPath` already maps anything under
   `.dispatch-runs/` to `ClassDispatchLog` (which `Class.Disposable()` returns true
   for). So the census under-counts this tree.

**Scope reality (verified):** growthgate budgets PER-FILE size, not aggregate
directory count, so even after fixing visibility it will NOT collect 5006 SMALL
files — count growth needs an age/count reaper, not a per-file size gate. The reaper
(gap 1) is the substantive fix; the visibility fix (gap 2) is observability only.

## Fix direction

1. **Reaper (substantive).** Add an AGE-based reaper for COLD `.dispatch-runs/`
   sidecars: keep the newest run's sidecars and everything inside a bounded grace
   window; reap older cold ones. A dispatch RUN is a set of sidecars sharing a run
   id/stem — reap by mtime age with a generous floor (do not delete a run whose
   `.witness` is still being read by a live progress scan; key on COLD mtime). Land
   dry-run/report default + an apply flag, keep-side default (mirror #5347/#5349).
2. **Visibility (cheap).** Widen `isGrowthCandidate` to PATH-admit files under
   `.dispatch-runs/` regardless of suffix (so the census byte-total sees them and
   `ClassifyPath` labels them `ClassDispatchLog`). Do NOT blindly add `.json`/`.txt`
   as global suffixes — that would admit repo source configs as `ClassOther` noise.
   Path-scope the widen to the dispatch dir (and update `TestIsGrowthCandidate` /
   `TestGatherGrowthArtifacts` in `cmd/fak/growthgate_test.go`).

## Safety (why LOW blast)

`.dispatch-runs/` sidecars are disposable dispatch traces (`ClassDispatchLog` is
already `Disposable()==true`). The one hazard is reaping a run whose `.witness` a
live progress scan still reads — so gate on COLD mtime with a generous floor and
keep the newest run. Report-default + apply-flag so the first landing observes the
would-reap set before deleting.

## Likely files

- cmd/fak/growthgate.go (path-admit `.dispatch-runs/` in `isGrowthCandidate`)
- cmd/fak/growthgate_test.go (update the pinned pre-filter tests)
- a reaper site (a `fak dispatch reap`-style verb or a doctor rung; if a garden act, it edits cmd/fak/garden.go and MUST serialize behind #5348/#5349)

## Expected steps

1. Widen `isGrowthCandidate` to path-admit `.dispatch-runs/` sidecars; update the two pinned growthgate tests to include a `.witness`/`.wave` under the dispatch dir.
2. Add the age-based cold-sidecar reaper, report-default + apply-flag, keeping the newest run and a grace window.
3. Tests: a cold sidecar past the floor is reaped; the newest run's sidecars are kept; a sidecar inside the grace window is kept; report mode reaps nothing but lists the eligible set; the widened pre-filter admits a `.witness` under `.dispatch-runs/` but not a repo `.json` config.
4. Re-measure `.dispatch-runs/` file count and bytes after a reap on the live tree.

## Batch policy

One reaper + one visibility widen for one leaked tree. Do not fan out per-suffix or
per-run tickets; the reaper sweeps all cold runs in one pass.

## Work estimate

3 points. An age/count reaper with a report/apply gate + a path-scoped pre-filter
widen + updating the two pinned growthgate tests + reaper tests.

## Overall completion contribution

3/20 points of the retention/GC epic #3873 (via census #5345). Collects the
5006-file dispatch-sidecar tree and makes it visible to the growth census.

## Target operating envelope

records.title: fix(guard): reap per-session stepadvice sidecars on session close and by age (fak cmd)
records.body:
## Parent context

Child of the create-without-collect leak census #5345, under retention/GC epic
#3873. This is row 7 — per-session `stepadvice-<uuid>.json` files accrete with no
reaper. Bare parent: #5345.

## Problem

`cmd/fak/guard_stophook_score.go` -> `internal/stepbatoncapture/capture.go` writes
`.fak/stepadvice-<session>.json` per turn-end. Within one session the file is
OVERWRITTEN (so it stays one-per-session), but when the session dies it is NEVER
deleted. 193 orphaned files on the live tree. KBs each — pure COUNT growth, the same
shape as the WIP-ref leak (#5340): recoverability/liveness, not bytes, is the signal.

## Fix direction

1. **Reap on session close (primary).** A guard session already has a clean-exit
   boundary (the SessionEnd -> "stop" hook path — the same boundary
   `cmd/fak/toolproc.go:171` uses to fire `CompactJournalFile`). On that boundary,
   delete the CURRENT session's `stepadvice-<session>.json` (best-effort: a delete
   failure must never fail the hook, mirroring the toolproc compactor's contract).
2. **Age sweep for orphans (secondary).** A host crash cannot execute the clean-exit
   delete, so add a bounded age sweep of `.fak/stepadvice-*.json` older than a grace
   floor (so a live session's current-turn file is never removed). Prefer keying on
   session liveness where cheaply available (a stepadvice file whose session is no
   longer live), with an age floor as the fallback signal.

## Safety (why LOW blast)

Each file is a KB advisory-score sidecar, disposable once its session is gone. The
only hazard is deleting a LIVE session's current file — avoided by the clean-exit
boundary (deletes only the closing session's own file) and, for the orphan sweep, an
age floor / session-liveness check. Best-effort throughout: never fail a hook on a
reap error.

## Likely files

- cmd/fak/guard_stophook_score.go (fire the session-close delete on the stop boundary)
- internal/stepbatoncapture/capture.go (a delete/reap helper beside the writer)

## Expected steps

1. Read the writer in `internal/stepbatoncapture/capture.go` and the stop-hook path in `cmd/fak/guard_stophook_score.go`; confirm the session-id -> filename mapping.
2. Add a best-effort delete of the closing session's `stepadvice-<session>.json` on the clean-exit boundary.
3. Add a bounded age sweep of orphaned `stepadvice-*.json` past a grace floor (session-liveness-aware where cheap).
4. Tests: the closing session's file is deleted on stop; a fresh live-session file is kept by the age sweep; an orphan past the floor is reaped; a reap error never surfaces as a hook failure.
5. Re-measure `.fak/stepadvice-*.json` count on the live tree after a session close.

## Batch policy

One reaper for one per-session sidecar family. Do not fan out per-session tickets;
the age sweep collects all orphans in one pass.

## Work estimate

2 points. A best-effort session-close delete + a bounded age sweep beside the
existing writer + tests, no change to the scoring/write logic.

## Overall completion contribution

2/20 points of the retention/GC epic #3873 (via census #5345). Bounds the
per-session stepadvice sidecar family so orphaned files stop accreting.

- the closing session file is deleted on stop while a live-session file is kept: >= 1 case
- a reap error never fails the hook: >= 1 case

records.title: investigate the slackoutbox drain that never fires on the headless fleet (census #5345 row 10)
records.body:
## Parent context

Child of the create-without-collect leak census #5345, under retention/GC epic
#3873. This is row 10 — the slack outbox spool (13MB on the live tree) never drains
or compacts on the headless fleet. Bare parent: #5345.

## Problem

`internal/slackoutbox` maintains an on-disk outbox spool meant to drain (send) and
compact (fold sealed entries) as messages flush. On the headless fleet box the spool
has grown to ~13MB and neither drain nor compact appears to fire: there is no
`state.jsonl` and no `*.seal.jsonl` present, the artifacts a normal drain/compact
cycle leaves. So the producer writes but no collector runs — the create-without-collect
shape — but unlike every other census row the COLLECTOR ALREADY EXISTS; something
upstream keeps it from ever firing. That must be explained before any reaper is safe:
a blind spool delete could drop un-delivered outbound messages.

## Fix direction

This is an INVESTIGATION, not a blind reaper. Determine WHY the existing
drain/compact never fires on a headless box:
1. Trace the drain/compact trigger — is it gated on an interactive Slack session, a
   token the headless box lacks, or a scheduler edge the fleet cron never wires?
2. Dump the actual on-disk spool state and compare it to what a healthy
   drain/compact leaves (the absent `state.jsonl` / `*.seal.jsonl`).
3. Classify: missing wiring (remedy = wire the drain trigger into the fleet path) vs
   intentional (headless never sends Slack, so the spool should be reaped as
   undeliverable, not drained). File the correct follow-on handle.

## Safety (why investigation-first)

The spool may hold UN-DELIVERED messages. A reaper that deletes it before the
non-firing is explained could silently drop outbound Slack. The safe first step is to
explain the non-firing and classify the remedy; only then wire a drain or a bounded
reap. Nothing in this ticket deletes spool data.

## Likely files

- internal/slackoutbox/ (the drain/compact trigger and the spool state machine)
- the fleet scheduler wiring that would fire a periodic drain on the headless box

## Expected steps

1. Read `internal/slackoutbox` and locate the drain/compact trigger and its preconditions.
2. Dump the live spool state on the headless box and confirm the absent `state.jsonl` / `*.seal.jsonl`.
3. Classify the non-firing: missing wiring vs intentional no-send-on-headless.
4. File the correct follow-on: a wiring fix ticket, a bounded undeliverable-reap ticket, or a design ruling that the spool is intentional.
5. Post the root-cause finding as a comment on this issue and on census #5345.

## Batch policy

One investigation for one spool family. Do not fan out per-message tickets; the
finding produces exactly one follow-on remedy handle.

## Work estimate

2 points. A read-and-trace of the slackoutbox trigger, a live-state dump, a
classification, and one follow-on handle. No production code change in this ticket.

## Overall completion contribution

2/20 points of the retention/GC epic #3873 (via census #5345). Explains the one
census row whose collector exists but never fires, unblocking its correct remedy.

## Target operating envelope

- live spool-state dump proving the non-firing: >= 1 artifact
- root-cause classification of the non-firing: >= 1 finding
- follow-on remedy handle filed: >= 1 ticket

## Witnessed operating envelope

- live spool-state dump proving the non-firing: >= 1 artifact
- root-cause classification of the non-firing: >= 1 finding

records.title: fix(garden): FleetStaleWorkGarden runs the file-ephemera watchdog, not `fak garden tick` — the wired session/lock/growth reapers never fire
records.body:
## Parent context

Child of the loop-fleet-operator epic #4954 ("keep every loop + super loop doing
REAL work, not just running"). Also the shared root cause behind the still-open
retention/GC census tickets #5344, #5348, #5349 (epic #3873): their reap-drain
witnesses cannot close because the loop that runs their collector never fires.

## Summary

The Go `fak garden tick` durable loop (`garden-stale-work-tick`, hourly) is the
ACTING collector for four stale-work classes, all wired into
`cmd/fak/garden.go performGardenTick`:

- expired session descriptors `refs/fak/locks/session-*` via `store.ReapSessions` (#5344)
- orphan `refs/fak/locks/*.lock` files via `store.ReapLockFiles` (#5348)
- over-budget growth logs via `collectGrowthLogs` (#5349)
- expired leases via `store.Reap` (base)

**Every one of these collectors is INERT in production: `fak garden tick` is
never invoked on this fleet.** The three landed census fixes wired their reaper
into a tick that does not fire, so the git-ref leaks keep growing.

## Evidence (all directly verified 2026-07-22)

1. `refs/fak/locks/session-*` = **14238 refs**, ~99% TTL-expired (1800s TTL, median
   age ~7d), and **growing** (14223 -> 14238 across one observation window).
   `refs/fak/wip/*` = 4053. Consistent with a collector that never runs.
2. The loop ledger `.fak/loops.jsonl` (live: 1.5MB, updated today, 1276
   issue-dispatch rows) contains **0 `garden-stale-work-tick` events over 8 days**.
   The five loop ids that DO fire are `issue-resolve-dispatch/claude`,
   `issue-resolve-progress`, `logvault-capture`, `logvault-verify`,
   `scout-loop/task-scheduler`. `witnessGardenTick` appends a row on EVERY run
   (act OR dry-run), so 0 rows == never invoked.
3. The only OS scheduled task carrying the "StaleWorkGarden" name,
   **`FleetStaleWorkGarden`** (State: Ready, LastTaskResult: 0, hourly, 0 missed
   runs, last ran 09:46 today), does **not** run `fak garden tick`. Its action is:
   `python3 C:\work\fak\tools\stale_work_watchdog.py --repo C:\work\fak --max-age-days 7 --live --json`
4. `tools/stale_work_watchdog.py` is a **different leak class**: it GCs over-age
   *gitignored disk ephemera* (files), not git refs. It never invokes
   `fak garden tick`, never calls `ReapSessions`/`ReapLockFiles`, never touches
   `refs/fak/locks/session-*`. Its own docstring notes "nothing is reaping these."
5. The task-name collision (`FleetStaleWorkGarden` OS task vs the
   `garden-stale-work-tick` Go loop) **masks** the gap: an operator reasonably
   assumes the task covers the garden tick, but it covers an unrelated file sweep.

Net: the census strategy ("wire the collector into `performGardenTick`") has a
missing final link — nothing on this box triggers `performGardenTick`. This is a
false-shipped hazard: the collector code is on trunk (correctly non-resolving),
but it has never executed in production.

## Likely files

- tools/stale_work_watchdog.py (add a `fak garden tick` invocation to the existing
  hourly path — the pragmatic code-only fix; it already runs hourly at the right cwd)
- cmd/fak/garden.go (the acting tick + its `--timeout`; may need a larger first-drain budget)
- internal/gardenbundle/gardenbundle.go (the `stale_leases` member shells `fak leaseref audit`)
- docs/fak/ (operator runbook note for the scheduled-task alternative)

## Expected steps

1. Close the trigger gap so the wired Go reapers fire hourly. Recommended (code-only,
   lowest blast): have `tools/stale_work_watchdog.py` also shell out to
   `fak garden tick` (non-dry-run, generous `--timeout`) as an added step, so the
   Go collectors run on the existing hourly `FleetStaleWorkGarden` cadence.
2. Alternative (operator): add a second Action to the `FleetStaleWorkGarden`
   scheduled task that runs `fak garden tick`, or register a dedicated hourly task.
3. Mitigate the audit cost: `fak leaseref audit` currently takes >120s over the
   14k-ref backlog and the `stale_leases` member timeout is 240s, so the FIRST
   drain over a large backlog risks timing out before ActReap trips. Bound or batch
   the first pass, or raise the member timeout for the initial catch-up.
4. Witness: after one hourly fire, confirm `.fak/loops.jsonl` gains a
   `garden-stale-work-tick` acted row and `refs/fak/locks/session-*` count drops
   toward ~2 live; this also unblocks the #5344/#5348/#5349 re-measure witnesses.

## Batch policy

Single leaf — this is one trigger-wiring fix (do not batch/spam multiple loop
schedulers into one change). It is the shared prerequisite that lets #5344, #5348,
and #5349 close their witnesses; land it once and re-measure all three.

## Work estimate

2 points. A one-call wiring change (invoke `fak garden tick` on the existing
hourly watchdog path) plus a first-drain timeout guard and tests; no change to
the reap actions, which already handle sessions/locks/growth.

## Overall completion contribution

2/20 points of the loop-fleet-operator epic #4954. This closes the shared trigger
gap that keeps three landed retention collectors (#5344 sessions, #5348 locks,
#5349 growth) inert, so it unblocks their re-measure witnesses in one change.

## Target operating envelope

- tests: >= 2 cases
- watchdog invokes the acting garden tick on the hourly path: >= 1 case
- garden-tick acted row appears in the loop ledger after a fire: >= 1 case

## Witnessed operating envelope

- tests: >= 2 cases
- watchdog invokes the acting garden tick on the hourly path: >= 1 case
- garden-tick acted row appears in the loop ledger after a fire: >= 1 case

records.title: filter resolved classes out of the trunk-red ledger fold so stale breaks stop reading as live (census #5345 row 13)
records.body:
## Parent context

Child of the create-without-collect leak census #5345, under retention/GC epic
#3873. This is row 13 — the trunk-red witness ledger's fold never ages out or
resolves stale break rows, so `fak trunk-red` reports breaks that are already fixed
at HEAD. Bare parent: #5345.

## Problem

`.fak/trunk-red.jsonl` is an unbounded, prune-less append log (currently 319 rows /
70KB, appended by the commit + pre-push gates via `emitTrunkRedWitness` in
`cmd/fak/trunk_red_ledger.go`). The READER, `summarizeTrunkRed`, folds EVERY row
into distinct classes with NO filter for whether the break is still live — so
`fak trunk-red` reports **104 "shared break(s)" across 319 witness row(s)**, and the
top classes are provably STALE: `undefined: cmdAuditExport` and `undefined: rawCostUSD`
at base `0b0724753877`, whose symbols are DEFINED at HEAD (`cmd/fak/audit.go`,
`internal/sessionaudit/sessionaudit.go`). This is the create-without-collect shape on
the READ/fold side: a producer appends, nothing ever ages out or resolves a row. The
real cost is SIGNAL, not disk — a stale fold reads as a wall of live fleet blockers
and misleads triage (it nearly misled a reviewer into treating resolved breaks as a
current outage).

## Fix direction

Fail-safe, keep-side default — never drop a row whose break is still live at HEAD:
1. Teach the fold to RESOLVE a class whose base SHA is now an ancestor of origin/main
   AND whose first-break symbol is defined at HEAD (drop it from the live view as
   resolved), OR
2. add `fak trunk-red --prune` that rewrites the ledger dropping resolved classes, OR
3. an age-bound fold that drops rows older than a generous floor.
On any uncertainty (cannot resolve ancestry, cannot check the symbol) KEEP the row —
a hidden live break is far worse than a surfaced stale one.

## Safety (why keep-side)

A stale row misread as live wastes triage, but dropping a STILL-LIVE break row would
hide a real trunk outage from every stuck clone. The filter must fail toward keeping:
only age out a class that is provably resolved (ancestor base and its first-break
symbol now defined) or past a generous age floor; otherwise surface it. The append
path stays untouched — this changes only the read/fold and an optional prune.

## Likely files

- cmd/fak/trunk_red_ledger.go (the `summarizeTrunkRed` fold and a new resolve/prune path)

## Expected steps

1. Read `cmd/fak/trunk_red_ledger.go` and locate `summarizeTrunkRed` and `runTrunkRed`.
2. Add a keep-side resolve check: a class is resolved when its base SHA is an ancestor of origin/main and its first-break symbol is defined at HEAD.
3. Fold resolved classes out of the live view (and/or add `fak trunk-red --prune` to rewrite the ledger dropping them), keeping every unresolved or uncertain row.
4. Add a table-driven test over a synthetic ledger mixing a live class and a resolved class, asserting only the live one surfaces.
5. Post the re-measured `fak trunk-red` count as a comment on this issue and on census #5345.

## Batch policy

One reader-fold fix for one ledger family. Do not fan out per-class tickets; the fix
is a single resolve/prune path over the whole fold.

## Work estimate

2 points. A read-and-trace of the trunk-red fold, one keep-side resolve/prune path,
and one table-driven test. The append path is untouched; no gate behavior changes.

## Overall completion contribution
Contribution: 2/8 points.

## Completion standard
production

## Target operating envelope
- resolve paths: >= 1 path

## Witnessed operating envelope
- resolve paths: 1 path

records.title: fix(leaseref): bound ttl_secs=0 session descriptors — publisher clamp + reaper heartbeat-staleness floor
records.body:
## Summary

Session descriptors under `refs/fak/locks/session-*` are being published with `ttl_secs=0`, and a `ttl_secs=0` descriptor is **structurally unreapable**: `internal/leaseref/refhelpers.go:expired()` returns `false` whenever `ttlSeconds <= 0` (pinned by `leaseref_test.go` — *"a zero TTL must never expire"*), so `LiveSessions` classifies every zero-TTL descriptor as permanently LIVE and `ReapSessions` can never collect it.

A pruned census over origin ground-truth (2026-07-22) found the entire remaining population is this cohort:

```
total session descriptors : 5884
  ttl_secs = 0 (immortal)  : 5884  (100%)
  ttl_secs > 0 (expirable) :    0
pcb_state                  : DRAINING 4551 | RUNNING 1333
updated_at age (days)      : min 0.0  median 10.2  max 13.7
age < 1800s (plausibly live):    2 of 5884
```

The earlier ~14.2k population's `ttl>0` cohort has already TTL-drained; the count now **stalls at 5884** because none of the survivors can ever expire. 4551 are `DRAINING` (never reached `STOPPED` → `RemoveSession` never called) and 1333 `RUNNING` (process died without cleanup) — all immortal. Dominant publishers by id-prefix: `win-*` (~4200), `dispatch-DESKTOP-*` (584), `tools-claude-*` / `contract-repair-*` / `ci-claude-*`.

This is a distinct root cause from #5344 (whose landed detector fix folds `LiveSessions` into the audit — correct, but it can only trip ACTION on *expired* descriptors, and this cohort is never expired). A TTL-only reaper cannot bound a no-expiry population.

## Parent context

Blocks the ~0 target of #5344 and is a create-without-collect child of retention/GC epic #3873. Sibling of #5340 (wip checkpoints) and #5343 (wip-liveness UUID join). A session descriptor is a liveness pointer, not recovery data, so — unlike the #5340 wip-checkpoint invariant — a heartbeat-staleness signal is the correct, recoverability-preserving collector here.

## Likely files

- `internal/leaseref/refhelpers.go` — the `expired()` predicate that short-circuits on `ttlSeconds <= 0`
- `internal/leaseref/reap.go` — `ReapSessions` / `LiveSessions` reap seam
- `cmd/fak/session_durable.go` — `publishBestEffort` sets `TTLSecs: int64(d.ttl / time.Second)`; the source of a zero TTL
- `cmd/fak/leaseref.go` — `session-publish` CLI defaults `--ttl 0`

## Expected steps

1 Publisher clamp: never publish a session descriptor with `ttl_secs=0` — clamp to a finite session heartbeat TTL (e.g. 1800s) at the publish site(s), so no new immortal descriptor is ever created and the existing garden/audit reaper drains future ones naturally.
2 Reaper heartbeat-staleness floor: add an absolute `now - updated_at > floor` collection path for `ttl_secs=0` descriptors (generous floor, e.g. ≥ 24h), orthogonal to TTL, so the legacy 5884-ref backlog drains. A live process refreshes `updated_at`, so only genuinely-dead descriptors are collected (only 2 of 5884 are younger than 30 min).
3 Read-only census first: land a classification that counts zero-TTL-stale descriptors without deleting, mirroring the #5340 census-first slice, before wiring any delete.
4 Re-measure witness: after a garden tick, the `refs/fak/locks/session-*` count should fall from 5884 toward ~0 while live descriptors (fresh `updated_at`) are preserved.

## Batch policy

One tracking issue for the whole zero-TTL cohort — do NOT file per-descriptor tickets (5884 individual issues would be spam). The collector is a single sweep keyed on the heartbeat-staleness floor; dedupe by treating the immortal cohort as one population.

## Work estimate

3 points — a publisher clamp (one-line TTL floor at the publish site) plus a reaper heartbeat-staleness path in `internal/leaseref`, both small and unit-testable, preceded by a read-only census slice.

## Overall completion contribution

3/100 points. A prerequisite for the ~0 target of #5344 under retention/GC epic #3873: without bounding the zero-TTL cohort the session-descriptor namespace cannot converge, so this closes the remaining ~5884-ref residual the TTL reaper cannot reach.

## Target operating envelope

- tests: >= 3 cases
- zero-TTL descriptors reaped in a live dry-run: >= 1 ref
- fresh live descriptors kept: >= 1 descriptor

## Witnessed operating envelope

- tests: >= 3 cases
- zero-TTL descriptors reaped in a live dry-run: >= 1 ref
- fresh live descriptors kept: >= 1 descriptor

records.title: worktree-land freshness invariant over-refuses on peer-stale HEAD — gate on non-regression (child of #3165)
records.body:
## Parent context

Child of the per-worker worktree isolation epic #3165. The isolated worktree land (`fak worktree worker land`) is the sanctioned off-main-index ship path — it is what lets a worker land while the shared `.git/index.lock` is wedged. This issue is a land-gate over-refusal that makes that path unusable across the fleet whenever an unrelated peer leaves a generated concept artifact stale at HEAD.

## Problem

`internal/workerworktree/disambiguation.go` `verifyAppliedDisambiguation` refuses an isolated worktree land whenever the post-apply tree is not concept-`Fresh`, using an ABSOLUTE bar:

```go
ok := post.Fresh && post.SemanticValid && post.CriticalClean &&
      post.Coverage+0.0001 >= before.Coverage &&
      post.CoverageDebt <= before.CoverageDebt &&
      !coverageFamilyRegressed(before.FamilyCoverage, post.FamilyCoverage)
```

The three coverage terms are correctly written as NON-REGRESSION (`post >= before`, `post <= before`). But `post.Fresh` is an ABSOLUTE requirement: it demands the landed tree be fresh regardless of whether HEAD was already stale.

Consequence: when a peer positions concept rows without regenerating `docs/concept-disambiguation-scorecard/README.md` (a routine doc-regen lag), HEAD carries `before.Fresh=false`. A worker's diff that touches ZERO concept surface still produces `post.Fresh=false` (it did not regen the README either), so `post.Fresh` is false and the land is refused with `post-apply disambiguation invariant failed` — even though the diff regressed nothing. This wedges EVERY isolated worktree land of a concept-relevant path (`disambiguationRelevant`: any `internal/`, `cmd/`, `docs/`, `tools/` `.go`/`.md`/`.json`) fleet-wide until someone unrelated regenerates the README.

## Live witness

Hit this landing the #5358 report-first slice (a pure read-only `internal/leaseref/drain.go`). I had to route the slice through the main-index `fak commit` path instead (landed `923657fc029b`).

Make freshness a NON-REGRESSION check, mirroring the coverage terms already beside it: only require freshness when HEAD was fresh, i.e. `(post.Fresh || !before.Fresh)`. A land may never REGRESS freshness (fresh HEAD -> stale post is still refused), but it is not required to FIX a peer's pre-existing staleness. Consider the same non-regression treatment for `SemanticValid`/`CriticalClean` if they can legitimately vary at HEAD; `Fresh` is the demonstrated over-refusal. Keep the compact witness detail so a genuine freshness regression still reports clearly.

- internal/workerworktree/disambiguation.go
