records.title: close the git push --prune mass-delete loophole in gitgate — an unattributed prune wiped ~8400 lock/wip refs (child of #3873)
records.body:
## Parent context

Child of the retention/GC epic #3873. The census under umbrella #5345 measures the
origin `refs/fak/locks/session-*` backlog that the #5358 drainer is meant to converge.
On 2026-07-22 that backlog dropped 14278 -> 5882 in a ~100-minute window (16:23-18:06
PDT) -- NOT by any shipped collector. Investigating that drop surfaced this loophole.
#3873

## Problem

`internal/gitgate` -- the in-kernel git prefilter -- refuses `git push --mirror`
(gitgate.go:161, "overwrites EVERY remote ref and deletes remote refs absent
locally") but has NO `git push --prune` rule. `git push --prune <refspec>` deletes
every remote ref absent from the pushing clone under that refspec WITHOUT --mirror --
the same mass-delete, unguarded. On a shared fleet remote where each clone holds only
a subset of refs, a `--prune` push from a stale clone deletes every ref that clone
has not fetched: peers' branches, lock leases, and WIP checkpoint refs.

## Live witness

The 2026-07-22 origin drop matches a `--prune` converge, not a targeted drain:

- The residual cohort is OLD refs only (session descriptors aged 8.2-13.7 days
  survived; everything published in the last ~8 days was deleted) -- the OPPOSITE of
  a targeted expired-drain (which deletes old/expired and keeps recent). That is the
  signature of a prune from a clone last fetched ~8 days ago.
- `refs/fak/wip/*` on origin went 4061 -> 0 in the same window. A session-descriptor
  drain never touches the wip namespace; a namespace-wide prune does.
- No origin-side deleter exists in code or ledgers: ReapSessions is local-only
  (reap.go), the lock sync is deliberately no-prune (sync.go: "DELETIONS DO NOT RIDE A
  REFSPEC"), and the #5358 drainer is read-only and landed 75 min AFTER the drop.

The prune deleted then-LIVE descriptors and all WIP refs as collateral.

## Fix direction

1 gitgate: add a `{sub:"push", long:"--prune"}` hazard mirroring the --mirror entry,
  scoped to push so `git fetch --prune` / `git remote prune` (safe local-tracking
  cleanup) stay deferred. This ticket ships this half.
2 Pre-push hook (tools/githooks/pre-push): refuse a bulk remote-ref DELETION (a ref
  update to the all-zeros SHA) beyond a small bound, so a NON-kernel actor -- a peer
  VM, a human, a stale-clone converge -- is also stopped. gitgate only binds agents
  routing tool calls through the kernel; the actual 2026-07-22 prune was almost
  certainly non-kernel, so the hook is the load-bearing half for prevention.
3 Forensic: attribute the 2026-07-22 prune (which host/clone) if a ref-transaction
  reflog or push log can be recovered.

## Likely-files

- internal/gitgate/gitgate.go
- internal/gitgate/gitgate_destructive_test.go
- tools/githooks/pre-push

## Expected steps

1 Add the push --prune hazard plus table-test rows (deny `push --prune`; defer `fetch
  --prune` and `remote prune`) in internal/gitgate.
2 Add a pre-push hook refusal for an unbounded remote-ref deletion batch.
3 Attempt forensic attribution of the observed prune.

## Batch policy

Single safety-hardening fix motivated by one observed catastrophe; not a batchable
duplicate/spam sweep. One issue, scoped commits.

## Done-when

- gitgate refuses `git push --prune` and still defers `git fetch --prune` /
  `git remote prune`; `go test ./internal/gitgate/` green.
- the pre-push hook refuses a bulk remote-ref deletion from any actor.
- best-effort: the 2026-07-22 prune actor is attributed or recorded as unrecoverable.

## Work estimate
Estimate: 3 points. Uncertainty: operator-supplied estimate; revise through the parent denominator when evidence changes.

## Overall completion contribution
Contribution: 3/100 points.

## Completion standard
production

## Target operating envelope
prune-guard: >= 1 push --prune refused in-kernel with fetch/remote prune still admitted

## Witnessed operating envelope
prune-guard: >= 1 push --prune refused in-kernel with fetch/remote prune still admitted

## Progress (updated 2026-07-22)

Both PREVENTION halves shipped on origin/main, non-resolving (this issue stays open
for the block-promotion + forensic tail):

- **Item 1 — gitgate `--prune` refusal: SHIPPED `348440546077`.**
  `internal/gitgate/gitgate.go` now carries a `{sub:"push", long:"--prune"}` hazard
  beside `--mirror`, with table-test rows in `gitgate_destructive_test.go` proving
  `git push --prune` is refused while `git fetch --prune` / `git remote prune`
  (safe local-tracking cleanup) still defer. Binds KERNEL-routed agents only.
- **Item 2 — pre-push hook complement: SHIPPED `21ef92e3c3ac` (WARN mode).**
  `tools/githooks/pre-push` counts deletion rows on the pre-push stdin (local-oid
  all-zeros SHA) and prints REF_PRUNE above `FLEET_REFPRUNE_MAX` (default 25).
  ADVISORY by default (`FLEET_REFPRUNE_GUARD=warn`) because (a) a wrongly-blocking
  push seam is a fleet ship outage, and (b) whether `--prune`'s IMPLICIT deletions
  reach pre-push stdin is UNVERIFIED — the verification experiment is guard-blocked
  from the agent path (writing `.git/hooks/*` trips SELF_MODIFY, and `git push
  --prune` is now gitgate-refused, so it can't be run to observe). Explicit `:ref`
  bulk deletions DO reach stdin, so the gate has teeth today. Escape for the
  sanctioned drainer: `FLEET_ALLOW_REF_PRUNE=1`.

Scope correction learned while shipping item 2: a pre-push hook binds ONLY clones
that install it, and the 2026-07-22 actor was almost certainly a foreign/stale
clone with no such hook — so the load-bearing defenses are the gitgate rung (our
agents) + a **sanctioned-only-deleter** policy, not the hook. The hook is
defense-in-depth for our own clones.

Design constraint this now imposes on the #5358 drainer: the targeted per-id
`git push origin :refs/fak/locks/session-<id>` delete-push is refused if routed as
a shell ToolCall (`pushDeleteRefspecLaw` for `:refspec` + the new `--prune` guard),
so the drainer MUST be a compiled Go verb calling git via internal `exec.Command`
(like `fak sync push`), scoped to proven-expired `session-*` refs, setting
`FLEET_ALLOW_REF_PRUNE=1` for the pre-push hook.

### Still open (item 3 + promotion)
- Promote the pre-push gate `FLEET_REFPRUNE_GUARD` to `block` once `--prune`'s
  pre-push stdin behavior is confirmed OUT OF BAND (operator/CI, not the agent path).
- Best-effort forensic attribution of the 2026-07-22 prune actor (which host/clone),
  if a ref-transaction reflog or push log can be recovered.

records.title: Bound the unbounded empty-tree sentinel note on refs/notes/fak/decisions
records.body:
## Parent context

Row 12 of the create-without-collect leak census #5345 (child of the retention/GC
epic #3873). The census surveys durable artifacts a producer writes on a hot path
with no scheduled collector to bound them. This row was documented-deferred pending a
retention RULING (unbounded-by-design vs a fold); that ruling is now made below, so it
becomes an actionable child.
#5345

## Problem

`internal/witness/decision.go` records every kernel adjudication/refusal as a git note
on the dedicated side ref `refs/notes/fak/decisions` (`AppendDecision`, decision.go:130).
A COMMIT-anchored decision is one note per commit SHA — bounded, per-object forensic
evidence. But a PRE-COMMIT refusal (`commitSHA==""`) has no commit to anchor to, so it
anchors to git's well-known empty-tree SENTINEL object (`EmptyTreeSHA`, decision.go:52,
`anchorFor` decision.go:117). `git notes append` concatenates each JSON line onto that
SINGLE sentinel note forever — the only UNBOUNDED producer on the ref. Every OFF_TRUNK
/ PATHSPEC_RACE / LEASE_HELD pre-commit refusal, fleet-lifetime, piles line-by-line
onto one object.

No collector bounds it: `performGardenTick` (cmd/fak/garden.go) reaps leases, sessions,
orphan .lock files, lapsed intents and over-budget growth logs, but never touches git
notes; the growth census walks the filesystem and prunes `.git` wholesale so the notes
objects in the git store are never seen. Repo-wide there is no notes prune / fold /
rotate anywhere. Local-only (git does not push refs/notes/* by default), tiny JSON
payloads — so this is slow, durable, per-clone bloat, not a fast disk filler; the real
cost is an ever-growing forensic object that read-back must scan.

## Ruling

Bound ONLY the empty-tree sentinel note (a keep-last-N fold on the most-recent
decisions — recency = forensic value). Commit-anchored notes are bounded forensic
evidence and are NEVER touched, so pruning them (a retention-policy debate on the
witness/forensics "durable journal" principle) is explicitly out of scope. This keeps
the fix self-contained and preserves the forensic contract.

## Likely-files

- internal/witness/decision.go
- internal/witness/decision_test.go
- cmd/fak/garden.go

## Expected steps

1 Add a `CompactSentinelDecisions(ctx, maxLines)` fold to internal/witness that
  rewrites ONLY the empty-tree sentinel note (side-ref only, never HEAD / refs/heads /
  push), keeping the most-recent maxLines lines; fail-safe no-op on maxLines<=0 or a
  missing note; witnessed by a real-git temp-repo test.
2 Wire the fold as one more once-per-tick sweep in performGardenTick with a bounded
  keep-N policy, threaded through the tick's witnessed metrics.

## Batch policy

Single self-contained retention fix for one specific unbounded producer; not a
batchable duplicate/spam sweep. One issue, scoped commits.

## Done-when

- internal/witness bounds the empty-tree sentinel note to a keep-last-N tail, touching
  no commit-anchored note and never HEAD / refs/heads / push; `go test ./internal/witness/`
  green.
- performGardenTick invokes the fold once per tick with a witnessed dropped-lines count.

## Work estimate
Estimate: 2 points. Uncertainty: operator-supplied estimate; revise through the parent denominator when evidence changes.

## Overall completion contribution
Contribution: 2/100 points.

## Completion standard
production

## Target operating envelope
sentinel-fold: >= 1 sentinel note bounded to a keep-last-N tail with commit-anchored notes untouched

## Witnessed operating envelope
sentinel-fold: >= 1 sentinel note bounded to a keep-last-N tail with commit-anchored notes untouched

records.title: feat(gateway): surface the #3425 session-saturation readout on /healthz (blocked on a clean http.go window)
records.body:
Follow-on to **#3425** (epic #3256, Workstream E). #3425 shipped in `02197604e`:
the sizing model + guide, the `/metrics` saturation gauges, and the
`SESSION_CEILING_SATURATED` admission backpressure. All three of its **Acceptance**
bullets are met.

Its *"What to build"* prose additionally asked for the saturation readout as **a field
on the readiness/status surface**, not only a `/metrics` gauge. That half is written and
green locally but could **not** be committed with #3425.

## Why it was held back

The only readiness surface is `Server.handleHealth` in `internal/gateway/http.go`, and
that file is currently carrying three other in-flight features whose helper files are
still untracked. Committing `http.go` would red the trunk — witnessed by applying the
worktree `http.go` onto a clean `HEAD` archive:

```
internal/gateway/http.go:125: s.handleFakSharedTask undefined      (#3885)
internal/gateway/http.go:132: s.handleFakAgentSessions undefined   (#3258)
internal/gateway/http.go:345: s.keyset undefined                   (#5332)
internal/gateway/http.go:359: s.keyset undefined                   (#5332)
```

`session_ceiling.go` already exports everything needed (`sessionSaturationNow` returns
the `SessionSaturation` readout); this is purely a scheduling problem, not a design one.

## The change (small, already drafted)

In `handleHealth`, after the existing `served_failures` block:

```go
// #3425: an operator or autoscaler probing /healthz sees live sessions against the
// configured ceiling and can scale out BEFORE the box starts shedding. Saturation does
// NOT flip ok:false — the deployment is healthy at the ceiling, it just backpressures
// NEW sessions while the loops in flight run untouched. Absent when no ceiling is set.
if sat := s.sessionSaturationNow(r.Context()); sat.Bounded {
    health["session_saturation"] = sat
}
```

Plus `TestSessionCeilingReadinessField` in `internal/gateway/session_ceiling_test.go`
and a `/healthz` bullet in `docs/fak/deployment-guide.md` (both drafted).

## Acceptance

- `/healthz` carries `session_saturation` (`ceiling`, `live`, `ratio`, `headroom`,
  `bounded`) when a ceiling is configured, and omits it entirely when unbounded.
- Being at the ceiling does **not** flip `ok` to `false`.
- Gate: `go test ./internal/gateway -run TestSessionCeiling -count=1`.

## Doing it

Wait for a window where `git status internal/gateway/http.go` is clean (or where the
three features above have landed), then apply the hunk and commit `http.go` +
`session_ceiling_test.go` + `deployment-guide.md` by explicit path. Do **not** commit
`http.go` while its peer symbols are untracked.

Lane: `gateway` (stamp `(fak gateway)`), per `fak index lane internal/gateway`.

records.title: feat(accounts): fak guard finds no Claude login on macOS — read Claude Code's Keychain credentials
records.body:
On a Mac where the operator is logged into Claude Code (2.x), `fak guard` refuses to launch:

    fak guard: no Claude subscription token found and no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set, and stdin is not a terminal — refusing to spawn a headless agent ... login=needs_login can_serve=false

Root cause: every fak credential probe is disk-only — `hasClaudeCredentials` / `resolveAnthropicOAuthToken` / `readLiveAccessToken` / `credExpiresAt` / `credExpiry` read `<config>/.credentials.json` and `<config>/.oauth-token`. Claude Code on macOS stores the live subscription OAuth credential in the login Keychain instead (generic password, service `Claude Code-credentials`, account `$USER`; a non-default `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` login appends `-<first 8 hex of sha256(NFC(dir))>` to the service). The plaintext file is only Claude Code's fallback store, so on a healthy Mac none of the probed files exist and every seat reads as `needs_login`.

Fix: one Keychain reader in `internal/accounts` (exec `/usr/bin/security find-generic-password -a <user> -w -s <service>`, darwin-only seam, short TTL cache, credential-safe), consulted as a fallback by:
- `hasClaudeCredentials` (login posture / `guardSubscriptionLoginPresent`)
- the guard OAuth token loader (between `.credentials.json` and `.oauth-token`)
- `credExpiresAt` / `credExpiry` (headless StaleCred rung, park-for-relogin, TriggerRefresh)
- `readLiveAccessToken` (account failover picker)

Non-darwin behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged (the seam is nil). Verified end to end on a Mac with a live Keychain login: `fak guard status` reports ready/can_serve and a guarded session boots.

records.title: feat(guard): --split has no macOS host — an attended Mac launch shows no fak surface at all
records.body:
On macOS, `fak guard -- claude` in Terminal.app or iTerm2 displays no fak items for the entire session: the animate banner is painted over by the agent TUI within a second, and `--split` auto-mode only recognizes tmux (`$TMUX`) and Windows Terminal (`$WT_SESSION`). A stock Mac ships neither, so the split silently no-ops — the one attended platform with NO fak surface. #5363 made guard *run* on macOS (Keychain credentials); this closes the visibility half.

Fix: add macOS rungs to the split plan, scripted via osascript (always present on macOS):
- **iTerm2** (`$ITERM_SESSION_ID` / `TERM_PROGRAM=iTerm.app`): true inline split of the current window (`split horizontally|vertically with same profile command …`). The AppleScript API has no pane-size parameter, so labels say "even split", not 20%.
- **Apple Terminal** (`TERM_PROGRAM=Apple_Terminal`): no split panes exist, so the overlay opens as a companion window (`do script`), the script re-fronts the agent window, and a trailing `; exit` lets the window close itself when the overlay ends. The agent still launches inline — nothing orphans the in-process gateway.
- Auto-enable extends to these hosts through the `guardSplitGOOS` seam; unknown `TERM_PROGRAM` values (vscode, …) keep today's silent no-op; tmux-inside-Terminal.app still resolves to the tmux rung; nesting via `FAK_GUARD_SPLIT` unchanged.

Witnessed on a Mac in Apple_Terminal: `fak guard --split-dry-run -- claude` resolves `host: terminal-app`, and the exact spawn argv opened a live companion window rendering the fak-info line against a running guard gateway.

records.title: fix(info): interactive overlay staircases in POSIX terminals — MakeRaw kills ONLCR for output too
records.body:
The interactive `fak info` overlay (the pane `fak guard --split` opens) renders as a torn staircase mosaic in Apple Terminal (witnessed 2026-07-23, 120×29 companion window from #5366): rows start at the column where the previous row ended, frames smear over each other, and fragments of old frames survive ("why  why …").

Root cause: `runGuardInfoOverlay`'s interactive path calls `term.MakeRaw(stdin)` to read focus/mouse/key bytes. On POSIX, termios is a property of the tty DEVICE, not one fd's direction — MakeRaw's `OPOST` clear also drops `ONLCR` for everything the process WRITES to that terminal. `writeGuardInfoFrame` joins rows with bare `"\n"`, which then moves down WITHOUT returning to column 0; one tick later the cursor-up redraw math desyncs and every frame lands shifted. Windows consoles keep LF→CRLF regardless of input mode, which is why Windows Terminal panes never showed it.

Fix: a stateful `crlfWriterTUI` that re-adds the LF→CRLF mapping at the write site (idempotent for already-CRLF bytes, correct across chunk boundaries), wrapped around BOTH stdout and stderr immediately after MakeRaw succeeds — frames, notes, and the exit line all flow through the locals.

Witness: 5s pty capture (120×29) against a live guard gateway — 0 bare LFs, no row over 120 cells; live companion window renders the panel stack cleanly.

records.title: docs(cache-value): add the session-SHAPE view to the cache-value rollup spine doc

`docs/cache-value-rollup.md` is the operating spine doc for the **cache-optimization** program (named as such in `AGENTS.md` § "Planning: two kinds of work"). It does not mention the session-SHAPE view at all — `Select-String -Path docs/cache-value-rollup.md -Pattern 'shape'` returns only one unrelated hit ("benchmark packet shape", line 243).

Meanwhile `fak cachevalue shapes` shipped (keystone #3115, children #3116 `health` column and #3117 `--trend`, all closed) and is documented in exactly one place: the one-line synopsis at `docs/cli-reference.md:184`. A reader who starts from the program's own spine doc — the documented entry point — never learns the shape view exists.

## Parent context
Follow-on to the closed cache-value shape line: keystone #3115, children #3116 (failure-shape `health` flag) and #3117 (week-over-week `--trend` drift). Origin epic #1301 (cachevalue P&L, closed).

## Current state
`internal/cachevaluereport.FoldShapes` + `FoldShapeTrend` ship; `fak cachevalue shapes [--since] [--json] [--trend] [--ledger]` is wired into the `cachevalue` dispatcher; both acceptance gates are green. Discovery surface is one `docs/cli-reference.md` line. `docs/cache-value-rollup.md` — the spine doc `AGENTS.md` routes cache-optimization readers to — has zero shape coverage.

## Why now
The shape line is fully shipped and closed, so the doc gap is now pure discovery debt with no moving target underneath it. A reader following `AGENTS.md` → `docs/cache-value-rollup.md` currently cannot find a shipped analytic surface, which is how shipped work gets re-implemented.

Any change to `internal/cachevaluereport/**` or `cmd/fak/cachevalue_shapes.go` — the code is shipped and closed. No new verb, flag, or report field. Not the unfiled Slack-card child (posting the shape table beside `fak cachevalue feed`).

records.title: fix(serve): refuse an auth-less bind on a routable interface (#3279 bind-safety default)
records.body:
Found while shipping the [air-gapped deployment kit](../docs/air-gapped-deployment-kit.md)
for [#3279](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/3279) (epic #3256).

## Problem

`fak serve` has a **safe default but no guard**. Verified at `ed0bd394b`:

- `--addr` defaults to `127.0.0.1:8080` (loopback) — good.
- `--require-key-env` defaults to `""`, i.e. **no auth** (`cmd/fak/serve.go`).
- A search of `cmd/fak/serve.go` for a loopback/routable check finds **nothing**.

So this starts silently and is reachable by anyone who can route to the host:

```sh
./fak serve --addr 0.0.0.0:8080        # routable AND auth-less — not refused today
```

That is precisely the failure mode #3279 cites as the market opening: the January 2026 scan
that found 175,108 publicly-reachable, auth-less local-model servers. fak's whole claim is
"local-first **and governed**"; today an operator who overrides the default gets neither a
refusal nor a warning. The kit page documents compensating host controls, but a convention
in a runbook is weaker than a kernel refusal, and #3279's Direction explicitly asks for
"a bind-safety default (never expose auth-less on a routable interface)".

## Scope

In `fak serve` startup, when the resolved listen address is **not** loopback and no token
door is configured (`--require-key-env` empty / env var unset), refuse to bind with a
structured reason rather than starting. Provide an explicit operator override for the
deliberate "routable and genuinely public" case so the refusal is escapable but conscious.

## Non-goals

- Changing the `--addr` default (loopback is already right).
- Any change to the gateway's bearer comparison path (already constant-time digest compare).
- Retrofitting the same check onto `fak guard`'s own `--require-key-env` seam.

## Acceptance

- `fak serve --addr 0.0.0.0:8080` with no token door **refuses** and names the reason.
- `fak serve --addr 0.0.0.0:8080 --require-key-env FAK_API_KEY` (env set) still binds.
- `fak serve` with default loopback and no token door still binds — unchanged.
- A test covers all three cases.

## Witness

The new test in the owning package, failing before the guard and passing after, plus the
refusal token reachable via `dos check-reason`.

## Parent context

Parent: #3279 (air-gapped single-binary deployment kit + SBOM), itself a child of epic #3256
workstream C. Parent production-scope baseline: 10 points.

## Work estimate

3 points — one startup check plus a three-case test.

## Overall completion contribution

3/10 points of parent #3279 — turns the documented bind-safety convention into a kernel
refusal, which is one of the two promotion-evidence items named in the kit page.

## Target operating envelope

- refused auth-less routable binds: >= 1 case

## Witnessed operating envelope

- refused auth-less routable binds: >= 1 case

## Completion standard
production

records.title: test(sbom): add a drift gate failing CI when go.mod diverges from the committed SBOM (#3279)
records.body:
Found while shipping the [air-gapped deployment kit](../docs/air-gapped-deployment-kit.md)
for [#3279](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/3279) (epic #3256).

## Problem

`docs/sbom/fak.spdx.json` landed in `ed0bd394b` as a generated SPDX 2.3 SBOM listing the
real dependency set (`golang.org/x/term v0.44.0` direct, `golang.org/x/sys v0.46.0`
indirect). **Nothing reds the trunk when `go.mod` grows and the SBOM does not.**

This is not hypothetical — it is the exact failure this repo already made once. The
dependency set went from zero modules to two, and the stale "zero external dependencies,
no `go.sum`" claim survived in `go.mod`'s own header comment, in #3279's issue body, and in
several docs pages until a build-verified triage caught it. A hand-refreshed SBOM in a
regulated deployment kit is a supply-chain artifact that silently rots — which is worse than
no SBOM, because a reviewer trusts it.

## Scope

A contract test (or CI check) that parses `docs/sbom/fak.spdx.json`, compares its package
set and versions against the live `go list -m all` / `go.mod` / `go.sum`, and **fails** on
divergence, naming the drifted module. This is the automated half of the manual
"Regenerate and verify this SBOM" recipe already documented in the kit page.

Per AGENTS.md ("New tooling is Go, not Python"), this lands as Go — a test in the owning
leaf, not a new `tools/*.py`.

## Non-goals

- Generating the SBOM automatically at build time (a checked-in artifact a reviewer can
  read is the deliverable; auto-generation can follow).
- CycloneDX output alongside SPDX.
- Vulnerability scanning / VEX — separate concern from set-drift.

## Acceptance

- Adding or bumping a module in `go.mod` without re-cutting the SBOM fails the check.
- The check passes at the current commit with the SBOM as landed.
- The failure message names the specific drifted module and the expected version.

## Witness

The test failing against a deliberately mutated `go.mod` fixture and passing against the
committed tree.

## Parent context

Parent: #3279 (air-gapped single-binary deployment kit + SBOM), itself a child of epic #3256
workstream C. Parent production-scope baseline: 10 points.

## Work estimate

2 points — one comparison test over an existing artifact.

## Overall completion contribution

2/10 points of parent #3279 — closes the "invalidating assumption" the kit page records
against its own SBOM (that the two-module set stays put with nothing enforcing it).

## Target operating envelope

- detected SBOM/go.mod drift cases: >= 1 case

## Witnessed operating envelope

- detected SBOM/go.mod drift cases: >= 1 case

## Completion standard
production

records.title: feat(serve): add general-PII redaction on the served request/response path (gateway parity gap from #3280)
records.body:
Split out from #3280 (gateway governance parity, epic #3256, workstream C — corporate
adoption). The #3280 audit confirmed **secret/credential** redaction is present and
test-covered, but found no **general-PII** detector on the served path.

## Gap

`fak serve`'s redaction machinery matches **credential shapes** and prompt-injection only:

- `internal/normgate` masks-in-place (`SECRET_REDACTED`, warn-first default) or seals
  (`SECRET_EXFIL`, opt-in fail-closed) plaintext/obfuscated **secrets**.
- `internal/gateway/forbidden_detail.go` (`tokenShapedRe`) scrubs credential shapes from
  403 bodies; the proxy/anthropic exfil floors gate credential exfil; egress delivery
  redacts before send.

None of these detect general **PII**: email addresses, phone numbers, national IDs
(e.g. SSN), payment card / IBAN numbers, postal addresses. A tool result or a model
response carrying a customer's email or card number passes through unmasked.

## Scope

- Add a deterministic **PII needle set** that composes with the existing `normgate`
  redaction seam — same warn-first mask-in-place default, same opt-in fail-closed seal —
  so PII is redacted on **both** inbound (client→provider) and outbound (provider→client)
  served traffic. Reuse the quarantine needle machinery (the #3280 direction).
- Policy-as-git and fail-closed on residency, consistent with the secret path.

## Non-goals

- Not a new gateway or a rebuild; extends the existing redaction seam only.
- Not ML/NER-based detection — a deterministic pattern set (email/phone/national-id/PAN/IBAN)
  ships first; a pluggable detector can follow.
- Does not change the secret/credential path (already shipped + test-covered).

## Witness / DoD

- A test proving a PII-bearing tool result is masked-in-place by default and sealed under
  the fail-closed posture, covering inbound and outbound.
- `go test ./internal/normgate ./internal/gateway -count=1` green.

Lane: `gateway` (+ `normgate`).

records.title: feat(serve): add per-key/per-tenant rate limits composing the keyset principal with the token-rate gate (gateway parity gap from #3280)
records.body:
Split out from #3280 (gateway governance parity, epic #3256, workstream C — corporate
adoption). The #3280 audit confirmed **provider-token** rate limiting is present and
test-covered, and that tenant **identity** already exists — but the two are not composed
into a **per-key/per-tenant** budget.

## Gap

- `internal/gateway/token_admission.go` (`TokenRateGate`) enforces a rolling-window
  TPM + concurrency budget, but **per provider budget (one account/seat)**. Its own honest
  fence: *"One gate = ONE provider budget … the per-seat pool (M20) composes ABOVE this."*
- `internal/gateway/keyset.go` (#5332) authenticates many api keys, each bound to an
  org/project **principal** that rides the request (`X-Fak-Principal`, joinable in audit).

So the identity axis and the token gate both exist, but nothing keys the gate **by the
authenticated principal**: a single noisy key/tenant can consume the whole provider budget,
and there is no per-key/per-tenant ceiling.

## Scope

- Key a `TokenRateGate` pool by the authenticated keyset principal (per-key/per-tenant
  token + request-rate budget), selected before the shared provider gate.
- Compose with budgets (#C1) and tenancy (#B5); fail-closed; policy-as-git.
- A refusal is the typed shed → HTTP 429 naming the **principal** and the cap that fired.

## Non-goals

- Not the global provider cap (already shipped as the host-level `TokenRateGate`).
- Not billing/metering — this is admission, not accounting.

## Witness / DoD

- A test proving two principals get independent windows and one principal's exhaustion
  429s **only** that principal, leaving others admitted.
- `go test ./internal/gateway -count=1` green.

Lane: `gateway`.

records.title: bench(conceptbench): echo the (fak <leaf>) stamp + witness rule as a tier-gated affordance hint for weaker models
records.body:
## Parent context
Filed as the concrete fak adaptation named by #2741 (conceptbench analysis), under
conceptbench epic #2721. The replay-graded `commit_stamp` contrast in
`docs/benchmarks/conceptbench-findings-2026-07-24.md` shows the small-model arm
(`claude-3-5-haiku`) failing the concept two ways at once: it emitted a subject-only
"all tests pass" claim over an EMPTY diff (`CLAIM_UNWITNESSED` / subject-only) AND
omitted the `(fak <leaf>)` ship-stamp trailer (`stamp=none`). The frontier arm
(`claude-opus-4-8`) passed (`OK` / diff-witnessed, `stamp=trailer/gateway`).
Parent: #2741

## Current state
The conceptbench task frame conveys the whole commit-stamp contract as one terse prose
clause ("commit it the fak way: verb-led Conventional-Commits subject, path-scoped
diff, `(fak gateway)` ship trailer, on main"). A weaker model does not reliably
discover the exact trailer grammar or the "witness, don't claim" rule from that clause.

## Why now
This is the adaptation-loop payoff of #2741: the replay contrast localizes the small
model's fall-off to a fak-affordance discoverability gap (terse injection), not (only)
a raw capability gap — so the fix is a fak change we can make and re-measure, not a
model swap.

## In scope
Add a model-tier-aware, in-band affordance hint to the conceptbench commit-stamp task
frame (and the shared injection seam it reuses) that, for a weaker arm, ECHOES the
exact `(fak <leaf>)` trailer template for the concept's lane and the "report `not yet`
with evidence; never claim a witness you did not produce" rule. Gate it behind a
tier/model flag (gen/next: dogfood before default). Re-run the spine/live arm and
record whether the small-model arm's `stamp_kind` and `verdict` move.

## Out of scope
The `lane_models` frontier-pin alternative (`cmd/fak/dispatch_model_policy.go`) and a
new `ModelSwitchableReason` class — those are separate candidate adaptations; this
issue owns only the echoed-affordance-hint arm.

## Done condition
A gated affordance-hint injection lands with a contract test asserting that (a) the
hint carries the concept's exact `(fak <leaf>)` trailer template and the witness rule,
and (b) it fires only for the weaker tier. Promotion evidence: a re-run row where the
small-model arm's `stamp_kind` flips off `none` and/or its `verdict` moves off
`CLAIM_UNWITNESSED`, with the frontier arm unchanged (no regression).

## Witness
A conceptbench re-run report (`fak.conceptbench.v1`) whose small-model row shows the
moved `stamp_kind`/`verdict`, plus the contract test above green.

## Lane
conceptbench

- `internal/conceptbench/` (the affordance-hint injection + tier gate)
- `cmd/conceptbench/spine.go` (task-frame wiring)
- `cmd/conceptbench/spine_live_test.go` (contract test)

records.title: fix(procguard): every POSIX process census is empty on macOS — ps rejects Linux-only keywords and runTool discards stdout on nonzero exit
records.body:
**What**

On macOS, every POSIX process census in `internal/procguard` comes back **empty**. `ps` rejects the
Linux/procps-only output keywords the collectors ask for (`etimes`, `nlwp`, `cputimes`) and exits **1** —
while still printing a complete, valid process table to stdout. `runTool` uses `exec.Command(...).Output()`
and, on any non-zero exit, throws the captured stdout away and returns only the error string. So the row
parser never runs at all.

Several safety rails are built on top of that census. On macOS they are silently inert or fail open.

**Why it matters**

Verified consequences, all on `darwin`:

- **`fak process-guard` is entirely inert.** `scanned: 0`, nothing is ever flagged, so nothing would be
  killed even with `--enact`. (This one at least fails *loudly* — it reports `collect_error`.)
- **The `claude --resume` concurrency ceiling fails open, silently.** `countLiveResumes()` discards the
  error with `procs, _ := procguard.CollectRelations()`, so `fak resume admit --explain` prints
  `census: 0 live claude --resume process(es)` no matter how many are actually running. Observed: it
  reported `0` while 4 real `claude --resume` processes were live — i.e. exactly at the default
  `max_live_resumes=4` ceiling, which therefore never fires. No error is surfaced to the operator.
- **`fak resume sweep` lists live sessions as resumable.** `liveResumeSIDs()` gets an empty set, so
  sessions with a running driver are printed under `N resumable NOW … launch sequential`. Observed: 6
  sessions listed as resumable, 4 of which had a live `claude --resume` process at that moment. Acting on
  that list double-drives healthy sessions. `--probe` does not change the output.
- **The fleet janitor's stale-child reap never fires** (fails safe, but with no signal that it stopped working).

Note the asymmetry: `process-guard` surfaces `collect_error`, but the two resume paths swallow it, so on
macOS they are indistinguishable from a genuinely quiet host.

**Repro**

Any Mac, no fak needed for the first part:

```console
$ ps -eo pid=,ppid=,etimes=,comm=,args= >/dev/null; echo "exit=$?"
ps: etimes: keyword not found
exit=1

$ ps -eo pid=,nlwp=,rss=,cputimes=,comm= >/dev/null; echo "exit=$?"
ps: nlwp: keyword not found
ps: cputimes: keyword not found
exit=1

$ ps -eo pid=,ppid=,comm=,args= >/dev/null; echo "exit=$?"   # control: all keywords valid
exit=0
```

Each failing invocation still writes a full ~880-line table to stdout; only the exit code is non-zero.
(Careful when checking this by hand: piping `ps` into `head` makes `$?` report *head's* status, which hides
the bug.)

Then, from a fak checkout on macOS:

```console
$ fak process-guard scan --json
{
  "platform": "darwin",
  "scanned": 0,
  "flagged_count": 0,
  "flagged": [],
  "collect_error": "exit status 1",
  "next_action": "process scan failed; rerun the guard and inspect collect_error"
}
```

`scanned: 0` on a host with hundreds of live processes.

**Root cause**

1. `internal/procguard/collect.go:207` — `collectPOSIXRelations()` runs `ps -eo pid=,ppid=,etimes=,comm=,args=`.
   `internal/procguard/collect.go:168` — `collectPOSIXCPU()` runs `ps -eo pid=,nlwp=,rss=,cputimes=,comm=`.
   `etimes`, `nlwp` and `cputimes` are procps-ng extensions; BSD/macOS `ps` has none of them.
2. `internal/procguard/collect.go:284-292` — `runTool()`:
   ```go
   out, err := exec.CommandContext(ctx, name, args...).Output()
   if err != nil {
       return "", err.Error()   // <- valid stdout discarded on any non-zero exit
   }
   ```
3. Both collectors return `(nil, err)` on the resulting `*exec.ExitError`, so `[]Proc` is empty.
4. `cmd/fak/resume.go:441` — `procs, _ := procguard.CollectRelations()` drops the error, making
   "collection failed" indistinguishable from "zero live resumes".

There is no `GOOS == "darwin"` branch anywhere in `internal/procguard`; the POSIX path assumes GNU `ps`.

Same keyword problem at three more sites:
- `cmd/fak/slack_fleet_process_unix.go:16` — `ps -eo pid=,ppid=,etimes=,args=` (read-only consumer).
- `cmd/fak/dispatch_tick_preflight_host.go:118` — `ps -eo pid=,nlwp=,rss=,comm=`.
- `cmd/fak/dispatch_tick_preflight_host.go:213` — `ps -eo nlwp=` (degrades gracefully: the `if err == nil`
  guard skips the block).

**Suggested fix**

- Use a keyword set BSD and GNU `ps` both accept, or add a darwin branch. macOS has `etime=` (a formatted
  duration, not `etimes=`' seconds) and no `nlwp`/`cputimes` equivalent, so darwin needs its own column set
  and parser rather than a keyword rename.
- Harden `runTool()`: a non-zero exit with usable stdout should not be treated as "no data". Return the
  captured stdout alongside the error and let each caller decide.
- Stop discarding the error at `cmd/fak/resume.go:441`. A census that failed to collect must not read as
  `0` to a concurrency ceiling — that turns a safety rail into a no-op. Surfacing it the way `fleet.go`
  already does with `collectErr` would be enough.
- Add a test that runs the real collector and asserts a non-empty census on the host it runs on. Every
  current `procguard` test injects synthetic `[]Proc` fixtures, so none of them exercise the `ps`
  invocation — which is why `macos-latest` in `.github/workflows/cross-platform.yml` (build + vet only)
  never caught this.

**Environment**

macOS (darwin arm64), fak built from main.

records.title: fix(resume): STOPPED_MIDTOOL can't tell a crashed session from one merely blocked in a slow tool call
records.body:
**What**

`STOPPED_MIDTOOL` (Go) / `DEAD_MIDTOOL` (Python) is classified from exactly two facts: the transcript file's mtime is older than a fixed 4-minute `LiveMinutes`/`LIVE_MIN` threshold, and the tail of the transcript has an assistant `tool_use` block with no matching `tool_result`. That signature is produced identically by two very different situations:

1. the agent process actually crashed while a tool call was in flight, or
2. the agent process is alive and healthy, and the *single tool call it's running* just hasn't returned yet after 4+ minutes (a slow build, a big test suite, a large file operation, a slow network/MCP round trip, ...).

Nothing in the record set the classifier reads (no PID, no heartbeat, no liveness probe) can tell these apart, and the decision layer treats `MIDTOOL` as the *safest* case to auto-resume — so case (2) gets a second `claude --resume` process launched onto a transcript whose original process is still actively writing to it.

**Why it matters**

`stopped.Decide` puts `STOPPED_MIDTOOL` straight into the `Resume` bucket (safe to relaunch headlessly), and the Python `decide()` stamps any autonomous `DEAD_MIDTOOL` row `AUTO_RESUME` unconditionally. If the watchdog fires on a session whose original process is only slow (not dead), you now have two `claude` processes racing the same transcript file and the same working directory — the exact "two drivers on one transcript" hazard the resume subsystem's own self-guard and `#3459` liveness guard were built to prevent. But that liveness guard turns out to be blind to precisely this case (see Root cause) — it only protects against a *different* copy of the session being alive elsewhere, not against the session's own still-running, never-`--resume`d process.

**Repro**

```bash
git clone https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak
cd fak
go build -o /tmp/fak ./cmd/fak

RD=/tmp/fak-midtool-repro
rm -rf "$RD"
mkdir -p "$RD/.claude/projects/demo-project"
SID=00000000-1111-2222-3333-444444444444
F="$RD/.claude/projects/demo-project/$SID.jsonl"
cat > "$F" <<EOF
{"type":"user","sessionId":"$SID","cwd":"/tmp/demo","gitBranch":"main","version":"1.0.0","message":{"role":"user","content":"please run the build"}}
{"type":"assistant","sessionId":"$SID","message":{"role":"assistant","model":"claude","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Running the build now."},{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_1","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"make build"}}]}}
EOF

# Simulate 30 minutes with no new transcript line (macOS; Linux: touch -d "30 minutes ago" "$F")
touch -t "$(date -v-30M +%Y%m%d%H%M.%S)" "$F"

/tmp/fak resume stopped --home "$RD" --window-h 999
```

Output:

```
resume stopped ...  window=999h  resume=1 defer=0 skip=0
  RESUME (safe to resume headlessly now):
     STOPPED_MIDTOOL    00000000 .claude  proj=demo-project  age=30m  pending=Bash
```

This is exactly what the same 2-line transcript + backdated mtime would look like whether `make build` crashed the agent process at minute 1, or the agent is still alive at minute 30 with `make build` simply still running. `fak resume stopped` (and the plan `fleet_sessions.py` writes for the watchdog) cannot distinguish the two, and reports the row as safe to auto-resume either way.

**Root cause**

The mtime-only heuristic:
- `internal/resume/stopped/stopped.go:41` — `const LiveMinutes = 4.0`, documented as "a live agent appends to its transcript at least this often" (an assumption a single slow tool call violates).
- `internal/resume/stopped/stopped.go:256,260-261` — `Classify` reaches `DispStoppedMidtool` only once `ageMin > LiveMinutes` *and* an unmatched trailing `tool_use` exists; no process/PID signal is consulted.
- `internal/resume/stopped/stopped.go:419` (`Decide`) routes `DispStoppedMidtool` straight into the `Resume` bucket; the package doc at `stopped.go:13` literally calls it "the safest resume candidate."
- The same heuristic is duplicated in `tools/fleet_sessions.py:44` (`LIVE_MIN = 4.0`) and `tools/fleet_sessions.py:327,332` (`age <= LIVE_MIN` / `"DEAD_MIDTOOL"`), and `tools/fleet_sessions.py:1197` + `tools/fleet_sessions.py:1033` (`_resume_inplace_or_escalate`) stamp `action = "AUTO_RESUME"` unconditionally for any autonomous `DEAD_MIDTOOL` row.

The one existing defense against launching a second driver onto a live session is itself blind to this shape:
- `internal/resume/watchdog.go:179` (`WatchdogSkipLive`, added for #3459) only skips a row when `g.LiveSIDs[row.Session]` is true.
- `LiveSIDs` is populated by `liveResumeSIDs()` in `cmd/fak/resume_sweep_cli.go:208-221`, which finds a live driver by regex-extracting a session-UUID literal out of each process's **command line** (`ps`/`procguard.CollectRelations`, no other signal — confirmed in `internal/procguard/collect.go`).
- But a normal autonomous worker launch never puts the session UUID in argv at all: `cmd/dispatchworker/worker.go:106` builds the process as `["claude", "-p", "--permission-mode", "bypassPermissions", <prompt>]` (same shape in `internal/dispatchtick/dispatchtick.go:238`). The transcript UUID is minted internally by `claude` once the session starts and only ever appears inside the transcript file — never on the command line of the *original* (non-`--resume`) process.

So `WatchdogSkipLive` can only ever catch a live driver that was itself launched via `claude --resume <uuid>` (or something else that happens to put the UUID in argv). A session that is still on its very first, original process — which is the overwhelmingly common case for an autonomous dispatch worker that's simply stuck mid-tool — is structurally invisible to the only liveness check in the pipeline. #3459 fixed the "an older copy under a different account dir is classified as dead while a newer copy is live" variant of this bug; this is a different, still-open variant where there is only ONE copy, and it just hasn't finished its current tool call yet.

**Suggested fix**

- Give the classifier (or the plan builder / watchdog) a real liveness signal instead of inferring death purely from transcript mtime — e.g. have the launcher (`cmd/dispatchworker`, `internal/dispatchtick`) record the child PID (or touch a per-session heartbeat/lock file) that a liveness check can consult directly, independent of whether the session's UUID ever appears in `ps` output.
- Failing that, make the `MIDTOOL`/`DEAD_MIDTOOL` signal advisory rather than immediately resume-eligible: require the same row to still read `MIDTOOL` across two consecutive watchdog ticks (or after a second, later re-stat) before it is eligible for `AUTO_RESUME`, so a session that appends again a few minutes later (because the slow tool call finally returned) is never raced.
- At minimum, extend `liveResumeSIDs()`/`WatchdogSkipLive` to match on something more general than a UUID literal in argv — for example the transcript's own `(account, cwd)` pair plus process start time — so the guard also covers a session's original, never-`--resume`d driver.

**Environment**

macOS (darwin arm64), fak built from main.

records.title: fix(agent): a failed messages[] decode is labeled too_few_msgs — the only structural bail without its own CompactReason
records.body:
### What happened

`anchorCompactablePrefixMode` collapses two unrelated outcomes into the single
`too_few_msgs` bail reason — `internal/agent/anthropic_compact.go:293-296`:

```go
elems, spans, decoded := decodeArrayElements(raw, msgsRaw)
if !decoded || len(elems) < minElems {
    return nil, nil, 0, CompactOutcome{Reason: CompactReasonTooFewMsgs}, false // nothing safe to compact
}
```

Two different classes of event land on the same label:

1. `len(elems) < minElems` — the request genuinely has fewer than 3 messages
   (`minElems` is the literal `3` at `:352`). Nothing to compact, entirely benign,
   and expected to be high-volume since every short auxiliary request on the
   passthrough takes this branch.
2. `!decoded` — `decodeArrayElements` (`:755-765`) could not decode `messages[]`,
   either because `bytes.Index` did not locate the value or because its delegate
   `decodeArrayElementsAt` (`:787-813`) found the value was not a JSON array
   (`:793-795`) or hit an element decode error (`:805-807`). This is a structural
   failure, not an idle.

The branch comment — `// nothing safe to compact` — and the vocabulary comment at
`:118` — `// < 3 messages — nothing safe to drop` — both describe only case 1,
while the code reports case 2 under the same name.

**To be clear about severity: I am not reporting an incident.** On well-formed
traffic the `!decoded` half is close to unreachable, and deliberately so. `msgsRaw`
comes from `json.Unmarshal(raw, &obj)` on the same `raw` one line earlier (`:286`),
and `json.RawMessage` keeps the literal input bytes, so `bytes.Index` cannot miss —
as the comment at `:756-759` already argues. Because that same `Unmarshal` proves
the document is valid JSON, an element decode error cannot fire either. The one
genuinely reachable path is a client sending `messages` as a non-array (`null`, an
object), which a spec-compliant client will not do. So this is an attribution and
vocabulary-hygiene report about defensive code, not a live fault.

What makes it worth fixing anyway is that the vocabulary is explicitly a *closed
set*, and this is the one structural failure in it without its own reason. The
sibling failures in the very same function each got one a few lines earlier:
`CompactReasonNonJSON` (`:287`) for a non-object body and `CompactReasonNoMsgsKey`
(`:291`) for an absent key. A `messages` value that is present but undecodable is
the same class of event and the only one folded into a benign bucket — the bucket
where a rising count is expected and therefore raises no suspicion.

It also is not confined to one call site. The identical branch shape appears in two
sibling subsystems:

```go
// internal/agent/anthropic_elide.go:114-117
elems, spans, ok := decodeArrayElements(raw, msgsRaw)
if !ok || len(elems) < 2 {
    return raw, ElideOutcome{Reason: ElideReasonTooFewMsgs}
}
```

```go
// internal/agent/anthropic_elide_stale.go:108-111
elems, spans, ok := decodeArrayElements(raw, msgsRaw)
if !ok || len(elems) < 2 {
    return raw, StaleElideOutcome{Reason: StaleReasonTooFewMsgs}
}
```

And in both of those the vocabulary comment states the merge outright —
`anthropic_elide.go:62` and `anthropic_elide_stale.go:54` are identical:

```go
ElideReasonTooFewMsgs     = "too_few_msgs"    // messages[] could not be decoded / nothing to scan
```

So the conflation is already documented as intentional in two of the three
subsystems; only the compaction one describes itself as purely the message-count
case while behaving like the other two. Whichever way you'd rather resolve it —
split the reason, or correct `:118` to match the siblings' honest wording — the
three should agree.

Downstream, nothing can separate the two halves. `observeCompaction`
(`internal/gateway/metrics_observe.go:179`) increments
`compactBailReasons[out.Reason]`, so the ledger, the
`fak_gateway_compaction_bail_reason_total` counter, the
`fak_cachevalue_compaction_bail_reason` gauge and `fak cachevalue compaction` all
inherit the merged label. Given a nonzero `too_few_msgs` count there is no query
that recovers whether any of it was a decode failure.

### What you expected

A structural decode failure should be distinguishable from a short request. Add a
`CompactReasonDecodeFailed = "decode_failed"` to the closed vocabulary
(`anthropic_compact.go:114-131`) and split the branch:

```go
elems, spans, decoded := decodeArrayElements(raw, msgsRaw)
if !decoded {
    return nil, nil, 0, CompactOutcome{Reason: CompactReasonDecodeFailed}, false
}
if len(elems) < minElems {
    return nil, nil, 0, CompactOutcome{Reason: CompactReasonTooFewMsgs}, false
}
```

This is behaviour-preserving. `CompactReasonTooFewMsgs` has exactly two references
in the repo — the constant at `:118` and the single return at `:295` — so no
control flow anywhere switches on it; both paths still return the fail-safe
identity, so nothing changes on the wire. The gain is that `decode_failed > 0`
becomes assertable as fak-fault the way `prefix_mismatch > 0` already is.

`anchorCompactablePrefixMode` is reached from two paths —
`CompactAnthropicHistoryWithOptions` (`:352`, `minElems` 3) and
`CompactAnthropicHistoryToView` via `anchorCompactablePrefix` (`:263-265`,
`anthropic_compact_view.go:45`, `minElems` 1) — so the split covers the `ctxview`
twin without further change.

### One thing the fix would touch

Adding a reason means updating the enumerated closed set in the counter's help
string, `internal/gateway/metrics_render.go:1179`:

> `...why a compaction attempt bailed to identity (closed set: under_budget|non_json|no_messages_key|too_few_msgs|no_breakpoint|window_no_drop|splice_failed|redecode_failed|prefix_mismatch). prefix_mismatch>0 is the ONLY fak-fault cache signal and must stay 0...`

That list has nine reasons; `anthropic_compact.go:114-131` currently defines
twelve. `cached_span`, `malformed_body` and `burst_unprofitable` are already
missing from a string that calls itself a closed set — worth a separate small fix
regardless of what happens to this issue, and I'm happy to fold it in.

### Version / environment

Source read at commit `f1f6eb6f`; go1.26.5, darwin/arm64.

records.title: fix(cachevalue): too_few_msgs is a non-candidate, not a declined candidate — it pins bail_rate near 1.0 and is documented as "tuning-sensitive"
records.body:
### What happened

Compaction health is reported with non-candidates in the denominator, so
`bail_rate` is structurally pinned near `1.0` and cannot indicate health.

`compactAnthropicRawWithReason` (`internal/gateway/messages.go:706`) attempts
compaction on every Anthropic passthrough request once
`--compact-history-budget` is set — it calls `CompactAnthropicHistoryWithOptions`
at `:771` — and `observeCompaction` counts every non-fired outcome as a bail
(`internal/gateway/metrics_observe.go:186-192`):

```go
default:
    m.compactAttempts["bailed"]++
    m.compactBailReasons[out.Reason]++
```

`too_few_msgs` is one of those outcomes — but it is not a *declined* compaction,
it is a request that was never a compaction **candidate**: fewer than 3 messages,
nothing to drop. Any session that spawns subagents or issues short auxiliary
requests puts a stream of sub-3-message bodies through the same passthrough, so
the non-candidate share is not a corner case and can dominate the count.

Those non-candidates then flow straight into the headline rate —
`internal/gatewayusageledger/compaction_segments.go:97` and `:218`:

```go
BailRate float64 `json:"bail_rate"` // Bails / (Fires+Bails); 0 when neither
...
seg.BailRate = float64(seg.Bails) / float64(tot)
```

So `fak_cachevalue_compaction_bail_rate` (`cmd/fak/cachevalue_metrics.go:336`)
and the `bailrate` column of `fak cachevalue compaction` read ~1.0 whether
compaction is perfectly healthy or completely broken. The one number an operator
looks at first cannot distinguish those cases.

Two knock-on effects:

**1. The headline `top_bail` points at a non-actionable cause.** Because
non-candidates are counted, `too_few_msgs` can win `TopBailReason` and become
the single reason surfaced in the table and in
`fak_cachevalue_compaction_top_bail_share`. The operator is directed at the one
bucket where there is nothing to do.

**2. The metric help text misclassifies it.** `cachevalue_metrics.go:357`
documents the reason mix as:

> `under_budget is correct-by-design; burst_unprofitable/too_few_msgs are the tuning-sensitive slices`

`too_few_msgs` is not tuning-sensitive. No budget, anchor mode, or burst-economics
setting makes a 2-message request compactible — unlike `burst_unprofitable`, which
genuinely moves with `--compact-history-budget` / `--assume-session-turns`. Grouping
them invites an operator to tune in response to a signal that tuning cannot move.

This is a gap in an otherwise deliberate design rather than a missing idea. The
codebase already draws exactly this benign/pathological distinction one level
down, for `under_budget`, via `AnchorStarved` (#1409) —
`metrics_observe.go:195-199`:

```go
if out.AnchorStarved {
    // A subset of under_budget: the anchor protected a prefix larger than the budget, so
    // the lever could not fire. Counted apart so "idle" can be proven NOT a short session.
    m.compactAnchorStarved++
}
```

That is the same move this asks for, applied one level up: separate "declined a
real candidate" from "was never a candidate". The comment at
`cachevalue_metrics.go:346-350` already notes that the reason mix exists to carry
"the WHY the single `bail_rate` gauge cannot carry" — the reason breakdown was
added, but the headline rate it was meant to compensate for was left
uninformative.

### What you expected

`bail_rate` should measure decisions about real candidates.

- Partition the closed vocabulary into **non-candidate** (`too_few_msgs`,
  `non_json`, `no_messages_key`, and `decode_failed` if #5387 lands) and
  **declined-candidate** (`under_budget`, `burst_unprofitable`, `cached_span`,
  `no_breakpoint`, `window_no_drop`, …).
- Either exclude non-candidates from `Bails` and expose them as
  `attempts_not_candidate`, or keep `Bails` as-is for continuity and add
  `candidate_bail_rate = (Bails − NonCandidate) / (Fires + Bails − NonCandidate)`,
  making that the column `fak cachevalue compaction` prints. Restricting
  `TopBailReason` to candidate reasons follows from either choice.
- Correct the `cachevalue_metrics.go:357` help text: move `too_few_msgs` out of
  "tuning-sensitive" and describe it as not-a-candidate.

The distinction matters beyond the display: with non-candidates removed, a
`bail_rate` that stays high is genuinely actionable, and a health alert can be
written against it — which it currently cannot be, since the metric is high by
construction.

### Related (not duplicates)

- **#2790** (bail opportunity cost) consumes this partition directly: the tokens a
  non-candidate bail "would have shed" are definitionally zero, so folding them in
  would dilute the opportunity-cost signal the same way they dilute `bail_rate`.
- **#2811** (bail-policy ablation, "is the compactor too conservative?") can only be
  answered over declined *candidates*; non-candidates are not a policy choice.
- **#3152** (durable per-session compaction-health witness) is orthogonal — it
  concerns whether the health row survives at all, this concerns how the counted
  outcomes are classified.

### Version / environment

Source read at commit `f1f6eb6f`; go1.26.5, darwin/arm64.

records.title: feat(adjudicator): add the egress allow/block-list rung so egress.block_lists reaches the decide path
records.body:
## Context

`internal/egresslist` compiles adblock/hosts-style rules into an allow/block matcher and
now ships a real community feed: `stevenblack-curated` (2843 block rules, MIT, pinned
sha256) landed for #4977 under `internal/egresslist/lists`, selectable by name through
`egresslist.BundledList` / `BundledListNames`.

That artifact is INERT at runtime today. The #4977 Context paragraph asserts the
adjudicator "consults it above the hardwired `egressfloor` and below the research
allowlist (see `internal/adjudicator/decide.go` `compileEgressList` + the egress rung)"
and that `egress.{allow_hosts,block_hosts,block_lists}` are `internal/policy` manifest
fields. Neither is true on the trunk:

- `internal/adjudicator/decide.go` declares `type Policy struct` (line 40) carrying
  `ResearchEgressAllowHosts` only. There is no `EgressAllowHosts`, `EgressBlockHosts`,
  `EgressBlockLists`, or `EgressRestrict` field, and no `compileEgressList`.
- `git grep block_lists HEAD -- internal/policy` is empty: `egress.block_lists` is not a
  parsed manifest field at HEAD.
- `internal/adjudicator` does not import `internal/egresslist` at all.

Because the rung is missing, #4977 acceptance bullet 2 (a test proving a known host on the
ingested list is refused EGRESS_BLOCK end-to-end through the adjudicator) is unsatisfiable,
and bullet 1's "selectable via `egress.block_lists`" holds only at the registry seam, not
through an operator manifest.

## Ask

Add the egress allow/block-list rung to the adjudicator plus its policy plumbing:

- Add `EgressAllowHosts`, `EgressBlockHosts`, `EgressBlockLists`, `EgressRestrict` to
  `adjudicator.Policy`.
- Add `compileEgressList` and the egress rung in the decide path, ordered above the
  hardwired `egressfloor` and below the research allowlist, refusing with
  `egressfloor.ReasonEgressBlock`.
- Parse `egress.{allow_hosts,block_hosts,block_lists}` in `internal/policy`, failing LOUD
  on an unknown bundled list name.

## Likely files

- internal/adjudicator/decide.go
- internal/policy/policy.go
- internal/adjudicator/decide_egresslist_test.go

## Expected steps

1 add the four Policy fields, `compileEgressList`, and the egress rung
2 wire the three manifest fields in `internal/policy` with a loud unknown-name refusal
3 prove EGRESS_BLOCK end-to-end for a host carried by the bundled `stevenblack-curated` list

`go test ./internal/adjudicator ./internal/policy -count=1` green, including a test that a
host carried by the bundled `stevenblack-curated` list is refused `EGRESS_BLOCK` through
`Adjudicate` when a policy names that list in `egress.block_lists`. That is exactly #4977
acceptance bullet 2, which cannot be met until this rung lands.

## Agent context

An UNCOMMITTED working-tree attempt at the policy half exists on this shared clone and
currently RED-lights `go build ./...`: `internal/policy/policy.go` (modified) and
`internal/policy/amendment_delta.go` (untracked) already assign the four
`adjudicator.Policy` fields that do not exist, so `internal/policy` does not compile. An
untracked `internal/adjudicator/decide_egresslist_test.go` (mtime 2026-07-15) is the
matching test for the missing rung. HEAD itself is green — the breakage is entirely
uncommitted. Triage and adopt that work before re-implementing it.

Contribution: 3/100 points.

records.title: accountprobe: RegDir() cwd-relative default silently forks a second, block-blind fleet registry
records.body:
## Symptom

`internal/accountprobe.RegDir()` falls back to a **cwd-relative** `tools/_registry`
when `FLEET_REG_DIR` is unset. A `fak` process running from the clone root therefore
maintains a *second* fleet registry alongside the per-user one, and the two disagree in
a way that silently disables block detection.

Observed on one host, both files regenerated within ~60s of each other:

| registry | `generated_utc` | blocks carried |
|---|---|---|
| `<clone>/tools/_registry/sessions.json` | `…T12:54:04Z` | **none** — every seat `block_kind=None` |
| `%LOCALAPPDATA%/Fleet/registry/sessions.json` | `…T12:55:03Z` | correct — 2 seats `block_kind=auth` |

Same 9 accounts, same `app_version` (0.41.0). The difference is that the clone-root
registry directory contains `sessions.json` but **no `probe_ledger.jsonl`** — the prober
writes its ledger only under the per-user dir. No ledger means no probe verdict, which
means no block can ever be derived, so that registry reports a fleet with zero blocked
seats.

## Why it matters

Absence is not neutral here. A seat missing from a registry reads as "no probe", and
"no probe" reads as "available". A block-blind registry does not make a consumer
cautious, it makes it blind — and because an entitlement failure (403) burns no quota,
a dead seat reports *full headroom* and a headroom-weighted allocator ranks it among the
**emptiest** seats and sends it the **most** workers.

This is the same class of bug just fixed on the consumer side (see the sibling job-repo
fix `fix(account-switcher): read the live fleet registry and treat access blocks as
blocking`) and partially on the read side by 9b982fb7b, which stopped entitlement
verdicts from aging out of a 20-minute window sized for quota walls. Those two fix the
*reading*. This issue is the *writing*: the fork itself.

Related: `shouldConsultProbeLedger()` (`internal/fleetaccounts/status.go`) gates the
ledger rung on `FLEET_REG_DIR` being set. With it unset the rung never runs at all, so
the two defects mask each other — even a correct `RegDir()` would not be consulted.

## Why this was not just fixed

`RegDir()` governs where fak **writes** registry state, not only where it reads. Flipping
the default would redirect live registry writes to a directory another writer is already
updating every minute, so the fix needs a decision about which writer owns that file
rather than a one-line default change. Filing instead of flipping.

## Suggested shape

- Resolve the default to the per-user Fleet dir when it exists, keeping the clone-root
  path as a last resort (mirrors what the job-repo consumer now does).
- Order by **authority, not mtime** — "freshest wins" lets the choice flap between ticks
  as two writers run on their own schedules.
- Decide explicitly whether a clone-root registry should exist at all, or whether a
  process finding no ledger beside its `sessions.json` should refuse to write blocks
  rather than write "no blocks".
- Whatever the resolution: make the *fork* observable. A second registry appearing
  silently is the actual failure.

## Acceptance

- Two `fak` processes on one host converge on one registry, or the divergence is
  reported rather than silent.
- A registry with no adjacent probe ledger never reports "zero seats blocked" as if it
  were a positive finding.

records.title: accountprobe: claude-class seats go days without a probe row, so seat-health folds read them as available
records.body:
## Symptom

The account-probe ledger is written for some account classes on a tight cadence and for
others barely at all. On one host, `probe_ledger.jsonl` (4579 lines) showed:

- `opencode-*` accounts: rows current to within minutes.
- Claude seats: last rows **8–9 days old** for several seats; the freshest claude row was
  from the previous day.

## Why it matters

Every consumer of seat health is a *read* of this ledger, and no read-side fix can invent
a verdict that was never recorded. Two fixes just landed downstream of it —

- `9b982fb7b` (fak): entitlement verdicts (auth/access/credit) no longer age out of the
  20-minute freshness window sized for quota walls, because a 403 does not heal by
  waiting.
- job-repo `fix(account-switcher): read the live fleet registry and treat access blocks
  as blocking`: read the registry that is actually written, and classify `access` as
  blocking.

— and both are bounded by cadence. A seat with no probe row for 8 days has no verdict to
carry forward, fresh or stale, so it reads as available no matter how correct the
downstream folds are.

The concrete cost: workers were being dispatched to a seat whose org had disabled Claude
subscription access, dying in roughly half a second with `oauth_org_not_allowed` / 403.
Because a 403 burns no quota, the seat reported full headroom and the headroom-weighted
allocator *preferred* it. Concurrency oscillated between 1 and 2 lanes instead of
climbing.

## Note on the failure direction

Deliberately filing this as a **cadence/coverage** gap, not as a request to treat
unprobed seats as blocked. Treating "no data" as "blocked" would strand seats and repeats
a mistake already made here once: a transient org-disabled blip led to a seat removal,
and the removal froze the very probe that would have cleared it. The fix is to *have*
data, not to guess in its absence.

## Suggested shape

- Establish why claude-class seats are probed on a different (or no) schedule from
  `opencode-*` — same prober with a class filter, or a separate path that is not running?
- Surface staleness as a first-class signal: a seat whose freshest probe is older than
  some threshold should be *reported* as unknown-health, distinct from both "OK" and
  "blocked".
- Make the gap visible in whatever operator view already shows seat health, so the next
  occurrence is noticed without a manual ledger read.

## Acceptance

- Every enrolled seat has a probe row within a stated freshness budget, or its staleness
  is explicitly surfaced.
- "Never probed" and "probed OK" are distinguishable at every consumer, rather than both
  collapsing to "available".

records.title: CORE_SELF_MODIFY core lock does not run on the sanctioned detached worker-worktree commit path
records.body:
## Summary

The `CORE_SELF_MODIFY` core lock does not run on the sanctioned detached per-worker
worktree ship path. A commit touching `internal/adjudicator/**` lands there with no
core-lock check at all, and no `--core-lock-maintenance-witness` is ever demanded.

This is the path CLAUDE.md explicitly blesses for build isolation (#1334 / epic #3165),
so the gap is not on an exotic route — it is on the one workers are told to use.

## Evidence

The pre-commit gate chain (`internal/hooks/hooks.go`) registers 16 gates:

    PUBLIC_LEAK SECRET_SHAPE DOC_PLACEMENT BROKEN_LINK FILE_ADMISSION INDEX_SYNC
    CONCEPT_ADMISSION CONCEPT_FRESHNESS PROVENANCE_LABEL HARDWARE_TELL
    BARE_COMMIT_SWEEP TRUST_WIDENING PRIOR_ART UNTIERED_LEAF GOFMT DUPLICATION

`CORE_SELF_MODIFY` is not among them. The classifier is only reached from
`internal/safecommit/corelock.go` (plus `cmd/fak/corelockwarn.go` and
`internal/corelockaudit/`), i.e. from the `fak commit` path.

And `fak commit` refuses on a detached worktree:

    $ fak commit --path internal/adjudicator/egresslist.go ... --core-lock-maintenance-witness "..."
    OFF_TRUNK: on detached HEAD, expected development branch main
      score: 62/100 (D)

So the two facts compose into a hole: the only path that enforces the core lock is the
one path the sanctioned worktree cannot use, and the path it must use has no core-lock
gate registered.

Witnessed live while landing #5389: a raw `git commit` of five paths including
`internal/adjudicator/decide.go` and `internal/adjudicator/egresslist.go` drew
CONCEPT_ADMISSION, BARE_COMMIT_SWEEP and E2E_OVER_MOCKS — and no core-lock finding.

## Why it matters

The core lock exists because the decision kernel deciding about itself is the one
change class where an independent witness should be mandatory. Today an agent can
satisfy every gate it *does* see, land a kernel change, and never learn the core lock
applied. It fails silent and permissive, which is the worst posture for this
particular control: the absence of a refusal reads as clearance.

## Suggested fix

Register a `CORE_SELF_MODIFY` gate in the `internal/hooks` chain so it runs on every
commit path, not only `fak commit`. It has the staged file list, which is all
`corelocks.Classify` needs. Keep the witness escape, but source it from an env var or
a commit-message trailer (the pre-commit hook never sees flags), the same way
E2E_OVER_MOCKS accepts an `E2E-verified:` trailer — that pattern already solves exactly
this "hook cannot see the flag" problem.

Second, smaller: `fak commit`'s OFF_TRUNK refusal on a detached worktree is arguably
wrong on its own, given CLAUDE.md sanctions that worktree. If `fak commit` learned the
worker-worktree shape, the witness flag would work there and this hole would close from
the other side too.

## Acceptance

- A raw `git commit` touching `internal/adjudicator/**` from a detached worker worktree
  is refused with `CORE_SELF_MODIFY` unless a witness is supplied.
- The witness is expressible without a CLI flag (env or message trailer).
- A test pins that the gate is registered in the hooks chain, so it cannot be dropped
  silently again.

## Likely files

- `internal/hooks/hooks.go`
- `internal/hooks/gate_corelock.go` (new)
- `internal/safecommit/corelock.go`
- `internal/corelocks/corelocks.go`
- `cmd/fak/commit.go`

records.title: Community feed for #4977 is held: bundled StevenBlack artifact trips PUBLIC_LEAK, needs an operator disclosure decision
records.body:
## Summary

#4977's community-feed ingest is complete, green, and held: the bundled artifact trips
`PUBLIC_LEAK` on 16 lines, and clearing it is a disclosure decision for the operator,
not a call this lane should make.

The consumer half shipped separately as #5389 (the adjudicator egress band), which is
independent of which feed is bundled — its bundled-list test drives `sample-malware`,
already on trunk. So only the feed itself is blocked.

## The finding

The candidate feed is StevenBlack/hosts' own curated source (`data/StevenBlack/hosts`,
MIT, 2843 rules, sha256 pinned). Sixteen of its rules are `[redacted:public-corpus]*` ad/telemetry
domains:

    ||ad.[redacted:public-corpus]adhub.com^      ||ads.[redacted:public-corpus]ads.com^     ||config.[redacted:public-corpus]ads.com^
    ||events.[redacted:public-corpus]ads.com^    ||gld.[redacted:public-corpus]osp.com^     ||log-1.[redacted:public-corpus]acr.com^
    ... (16 total, lines 310-2294)

`PUBLIC_LEAK` matches these because `"sam"+"sung"` is a redact needle in
`internal/hooks/gate_publicleak.go`'s `auditNeedles`. That list is not a generic brand
detector — it sits alongside the operator's home directory path, private GPU host
aliases (`dgxN`), `[redacted:public-corpus]`, and a private IP. It reads as a deliberate policy
that this string does not appear in the public repo.

## Why this needs a human

The content itself is benign by every other measure. I scanned the artifact
independently: **0 dotted-quad IP literals, 0 credential-shaped tokens**, pure adblock
domain syntax (2843 `||host^` rules, 9 comment lines, nothing else). It is byte-identical
to a public MIT-licensed upstream at a pinned public URL. Nothing private is disclosed.

But the needle list encodes a repo policy about a *name*, not about secrets, and
overriding a policy about what may be published is the operator's call. `FLEET_ALLOW_LEAK=1`
would clear it in one keystroke and leave no durable record of the decision, which is
the wrong shape for this.

## Options

1. **Approve the exemption.** Add a durable, reviewed exemption for this path rather
   than a one-shot env override, so the decision is recorded where the next reader
   finds it. Best if the needle is about business relationships and a third-party
   public blocklist is agreed not to implicate one.
2. **Choose a different upstream feed** that carries no needle match — e.g. URLhaus or
   EasyPrivacy. Preserves the whole point of #4977 (ingest a real feed nobody here
   authored) with no disclosure question. Costs a re-pin and a fresh review.
3. **Filter the 16 lines** and re-pin. Cheapest now, but it breaks the refresh
   contract: `fak egresslist refresh` re-fetches upstream and the checksum would
   diverge every time, so it trades a one-time decision for permanent drift. Not
   recommended.

My recommendation is **2** if the needle policy is firm, **1** if it is not — option 2
costs the least trust and needs no exemption at all.

## What is held (all green, nothing else blocking)

- `internal/egresslist/lists/stevenblack-curated.txt` (new, the flagged artifact)
- `internal/egresslist/community_ingest_test.go` (new, the acceptance witness)
- `internal/egresslist/lists/manifest.json` (the `stevenblack-curated` entry)
- `internal/egresslist/manifest.go` (`Source.License` + `! Upstream-License:` header)
- `internal/egresslist/manifest_test.go` (`TestAtLeastOneCommunityListIsIngested`)

Note `manifest.go` and `manifest_test.go` are held *with* the feed rather than shipped
ahead of it: the ratchet asserts at least one bundled list records a real upstream, so
landing it without a feed reds the trunk, and landing the `License` field alone would
ship an untested struct field ahead of its only consumer.

`go test ./internal/egresslist/` passes with the full set applied.
