records.title: Wire the sanctioned compiled sidestep: auto-substitute a bare `git push` with `fak sync push` when the operator opts in
records.body:
## Context

`docs/notes/IN-FLIGHT-REPAIR-SANCTIONED-SIDESTEP-2026-07-15.md` designs an opt-in
auto-substitution: when the reversibility gate holds a call whose family already
NAMES a sanctioned equivalent (`git push` → `fak sync push`), repair the call in
flight as a TRANSFORM instead of making the agent re-issue it by hand.

The note is explicit that this is **not** #4428 ("error affordance rewrites") and
must not reintroduce the confirm-token loop (#3306).

Today the gate names the sidestep as advisory text only. The producer half is
written — `internal/adjudicator/reversibility.go` computes `RewriteCommand` /
`RewriteTool` behind its own safe-subset gate — but nothing consumes it, because
there is no `Policy.AutoRepairSidestep` knob and no actuation in the rung.

## The gap

Three pieces are missing between the design note and a working capability:

1. `adjudicator.Policy` has no `AutoRepairSidestep` field, so the producer's
   `RewriteCommand` is computed and discarded.
2. The reversibility rung has no actuation branch — it goes straight to
   `reversibilityGateVerdict(env)`.
3. There is no operator-facing way to turn it on.

## Why the safe subset is the whole design

For a bare `git push` the preview-confirm pause is theater: the operator confirms,
the agent re-issues, the same effect happens one round-trip later. For a
`--force` / `--delete` / refspec push the pause is load-bearing.

The safe-subset test therefore belongs at the PRODUCER (`reversibility.go`), which
attaches a `RewriteCommand` only when the call is in the safe subset. The actuation
site then needs no danger analysis of its own — a dangerous push simply arrives
with no `RewriteCommand` and still holds. That placement is what makes it
impossible for the knob to launder a dangerous push into a weaker one.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `Policy.AutoRepairSidestep`, default false — an unset deployment decides
      byte-identically.
- [ ] Reversibility rung emits `abi.VerdictTransform` with the substituted command
      when the knob is on AND `env.RewriteCommand != ""`; preserves every
      non-confirmation arg (notably `workdir` — dropping it would push a different
      repo).
- [ ] A `--force` / `--delete` / refspec push still HOLDS with the knob on.
- [ ] An operator-facing setter.
- [ ] Tests pinning the opt-in gate, the safe-subset boundary, and correspondence
      between the substituted verb and the family remedy table.

## Constraint

`internal/adjudicator/**` is core-locked (`CORE_SELF_MODIFY`) — see #5392 for the
gate's absence on the sanctioned worktree commit path. The change must be purely
additive and remove no existing check.

records.title: Guard floor: pin the Playwright browser family so a dropped grant cannot masquerade as scout_zero_sections
records.body:
The embedded guard floor (`cmd/fak/guard-default-policy.json`) enumerates the
`mcp__dos__*` and `mcp__fak__*` tool families. For a period it listed no
`mcp__playwright__browser_*` identity at all, so every browser call the apply
pipeline made fell through to DEFAULT_DENY.

The grant is on trunk now. What is missing is anything that keeps it there.

## Why this specific grant needs a ratchet

The failure is silent and it points at the wrong subsystem.

The apply pipeline's scout phase reads a page through
`mcp__playwright__browser_snapshot`. A scout that cannot snapshot enumerates ZERO
form fields — and zero fields is not distinguishable, downstream, from "this page
genuinely has no form". The apply classifier bucketed that as
`scout_zero_sections` structural-doom and applied a 6h cooldown plus retirement.

So a guard false-positive walked HEALTHY jobs toward permanent skip. Nothing in
the pipeline reported a refusal; there was only an empty result that read as a
legitimate finding. Anyone debugging the resulting retirements starts at the
classifier, three layers from the missing line in a policy JSON file.

## Partial grants are the real hazard

A floor that admits `browser_snapshot` but not `browser_fill_form` fails at a
different stage with a different misleading symptom. A single representative
assertion would not catch that, so the test should enumerate the family the
pipeline actually drives across scout/fill/submit:

- read-only: `browser_snapshot`, `browser_navigate`, `browser_take_screenshot`,
  `browser_tabs`
- write/interactive: `browser_click`, `browser_type`, `browser_fill_form`,
  `browser_select_option`, `browser_file_upload`, `browser_press_key`

## Proposed

A test in `internal/policy` that drives `ParseRuntime` over the REAL embedded
floor — so it fails if the grant is dropped from
`cmd/fak/guard-default-policy.json`, not merely if a fixture is edited.

Test-only. No production behaviour changes.

records.title: fix(gateway): the #4855 EP streaming stall is still live on the in-kernel buffered path
records.body:
## The finding

`#4855` is CLOSED, but the streaming-stall half is still reproducible on trunk for the
**pure-fak in-kernel serve** — the exact topology the original [redacted:public-corpus] 8-rank GLM-5.2 EP
report came from. A `stream:true` request served by `agent.InKernelPlanner` emits **no
HTTP status line, no headers, and no SSE byte** until the entire decode completes.

The mechanism, read off trunk:

- `agent.InKernelPlanner` implements **only** `Complete` (`internal/agent/inkernel_planner.go:644`).
  It is not an `agent.StreamingPlanner` — no `StreamingSupported`, no `CompleteStream`
  (`internal/agent/stream.go:39`).
- `internal/gateway/http.go:581` therefore falls through: `streamChatLive` declines and
  writes nothing, which is correct and documented.
- The buffered path then blocks in `completeServed` (`internal/gateway/http.go:593`) and
  only reaches `writeChatCompletionStream` (`internal/gateway/http.go:662`) once the whole
  turn exists. That function writes the headers and the `200` at its own line 995-998.

So for the full duration of a multi-rank decode the client cannot distinguish an accepted
streaming request from a dead socket. On the original report that was 1120+ seconds.

## Witness

A CPU-modeled, GPU-free repro is written and currently RED against `origin/main`. It
models the persistent-rank topology in-process: a fake follower rank receives the fanout
mirror, and a planner implementing only `Complete` blocks on a modeled per-step
collective, standing in for the sharded decode. Every wait is bounded, so it can fail but
never hang.

```
--- FAIL: TestEPStreamingEmitsFirstSSEChunkBeforeCollectiveJoin (3.01s)
    ep_stream_stall_test.go:135: no HTTP headers/first SSE byte before the EP collective
      join — the #4855 streaming stall
FAIL	github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/internal/gateway	16.547s
```

The gateway's own turn log from that run confirms the shape rather than a test artifact:
`{"event":"gateway_http_request","status":200,"bytes":1045,"duration_ms":3003.494}` —
1045 bytes, all of them after 3003ms, i.e. after the modeled collective was released.

The test is held out of trunk deliberately: landing a red test would red the trunk. It is
parked and ships **with** the fix, in the same commit, so the fix arrives witnessed.

## Why this is not a one-line flush

Emitting the SSE preamble before `completeServed` is easy; doing it without lying is the
work. Three constraints have to be resolved together, and each one is a real decision:

1. **Error semantics after the preamble.** Today the buffered path can still answer with
   a real HTTP status: `writeUpstreamErr` (502 + `Retry-After`), the tool-call
   conformance fail-closed 502 at `http.go:632`, and `writeSessionRefusal`. Once a `200`
   and headers are on the wire none of those can be sent. The preamble must therefore be
   placed strictly after every pre-decode refusal, and the post-preamble upstream failure
   has to become an SSE error event plus `[DONE]` — which is what OpenAI does for a
   mid-stream failure, but it IS a behavior change for existing clients and existing
   tests assert the current shape.

2. **The opening chunk currently carries adjudicated tool calls.** `http.go:1016` builds
   the role announcement together with `streamToolCalls(choice.Message.ToolCalls)`, which
   is not known before the decode. Splitting it means tool calls move into a later delta.
   Standard OpenAI clients accumulate `tool_calls` by index across deltas, so this is
   wire-compatible in principle — but it must be asserted, not assumed.

3. **The `model` field vs. #82.** `respModel` prefers `comp.Model` — the model the
   **upstream reported it served** — precisely so the gateway never silently substitutes
   `s.model`. That value does not exist before the decode, so an early opening chunk can
   only carry `reqModel`. Either the chunks disagree on `model` mid-stream (ugly, and
   OpenAI keeps it constant) or #82's echo weakens on the streaming path. This needs a
   decision, not a default.

## Acceptance

- `TestEPStreamingEmitsFirstSSEChunkBeforeCollectiveJoin` passes: status line, SSE
  headers, and the opening role chunk reach the client **while** the collective is still
  pending, and the stream still terminates with the turn content, a finish chunk, and
  `[DONE]` once it completes.
- The follower rank still receives the mirrored `stream:true` body: the early flush
  augments the fanout, it must never replace it.
- A post-preamble upstream error is asserted to arrive as an SSE error event + `[DONE]`,
  with a named test, rather than silently truncating the stream.
- The existing `internal/gateway` suite stays green, including whatever asserts the
  current opening-chunk shape.

## Likely files

- `internal/gateway/http.go` (the `req.Stream` fall-through at 581, `completeServed` at
  593, the `writeChatCompletionStream` call at 662, and the writer itself at 994-1044)
- `internal/gateway/ep_stream_stall_test.go` (the parked repro, lands with the fix)
- `internal/gateway/stream_proxy.go` (`streamChatLive`, for the decline path's contract)

## Work estimate

Estimate: 3 points. The flush itself is small; the three constraints above and the
existing-test reconciliation are the cost.

## Parent context

Parent: #4855 — this is the remaining half of that issue's scope. #4855 was closed with
the rank-0 residency work and the `streamChatLive` path for planners that CAN stream; the
in-kernel buffered fall-through documented above was not covered by that closure and is
still reproducible on trunk.

## Overall completion contribution
Contribution: 3/1000 points.

## Completion standard
development

records.title: fix(guard/session): nothing ever publishes gateway_url/bearer into guard_sessions.jsonl — #3461's producer half is missing (0 of 6769 rows)
records.body:
## The finding

`#3461` is CLOSED and its title names the deliverable exactly — *"publish gateway addr in
guard_sessions.jsonl"* — but **nothing in production ever publishes it**. The consumer half
shipped and is 100% inert.

Read off trunk:

- `guardsessions.Row.WithGateway` (`internal/guardsessions/guardsessions.go:75`) is the ONLY
  writer of `gateway_url` / `bearer`. It has **zero production call sites** — every reference
  outside its own definition is in a `_test.go`.
- Both record sites build the row and never stamp it:
  `cmd/fak/guard.go:744` (`NewInteractiveRow`) and `cmd/fak/guard_sessions.go:50`
  (`NewRow` + `Record`, the `maybeRecordGuardSessionIndex` path called at `guard.go:738`).
- `gateway.Config.ReadBearer` (`internal/gateway/gateway.go:411`) — the read-scoped token the
  published bearer is supposed to BE — likewise has **zero assignment sites** in production.
  The gateway honors it (`internal/gateway/http.go:373`, read-scoped paths only), so the
  accepting side is built; nothing ever mints one.

So the discovery contract has a reader, an authenticator, and no producer.

## Witness

On this box's real Fleet registry (`$LOCALAPPDATA\Fleet\registry\guard_sessions.jsonl`),
single-pass read of the whole index:

```
index rows 6769   with gateway_url 0   with ended_at 270
oldest 2026-07-06T23:09:09Z   newest 2026-07-26T20:30:41Z
of newest 50: gateway_url set = 0
keys on newest row: ['agent','audit','cwd','handle','nonce','pid','schema','started_utc','trace_id']
```

Zero of 6769 rows across three weeks, including a row written today. The field is not merely
rare — it has never been written by any fak version.

The downstream effect is visible from the new census verb (`aa55fd4475`):

```
$ fak cachevalue census
fleet managed-cache posture census — INSUFFICIENT
  72 worker(s), none reachable — no posture observed
  workers 72 (reached 0, unreachable 72)
```

72 live guard sessions, none reachable, because none published anything to reach.

## Why this is worse than a missing feature

The consumer's refusal message actively MISDIAGNOSES it. `cmd/fak/session_query.go:161`:

> `fak session status: guard session %s published no gateway_url (recorded by an older fak?)`

There is no older fak. That parenthetical sends an operator looking for a version-skew
problem that does not exist, on every session, forever. Whatever else this ticket does, that
string has to stop guessing.

Two surfaces are inert today and a third is about to be:

- `fak session status <handle>` — cannot read ANY live session cross-process (exit 1).
- `fak cachevalue census` (#3650) — every worker folds to UNKNOWN.
- Anything else built on "the index tells you how to reach a live worker" inherits the same
  hole.

## Acceptance

- A `fak guard` launch that binds a gateway records a row carrying BOTH `gateway_url` and a
  read-scoped `bearer`, and a test asserts the recorded row over the real record path — not
  over `WithGateway` in isolation, which is what is already covered.
- The bearer is genuinely read-scoped: a test drives the recorded token against a mutating
  route on the same gateway and asserts it is refused there while admitting `/debug/vars`.
  Publishing a control-grade token into a world-readable JSONL index would be a strictly
  worse outcome than publishing nothing.
- `fak session status <live-handle>` returns that session's `/debug/vars` on a box where a
  guard is running, with no `--addr` and no prior port knowledge.
- The "recorded by an older fak?" guess is replaced by a message that names the real cause,
  and is reached only when a row genuinely predates the publish.
- A guard that binds NO gateway still records its row and still omits both fields — the
  fields stay `omitempty` and their absence must remain a legal, non-erroring shape.

## Likely files

- `cmd/fak/guard.go` (the interactive record at 744, and `maybeRecordGuardSessionIndex` at 738)
- `cmd/fak/guard_sessions.go` (the `NewRow` + `Record` path at 50-51)
- `internal/gateway/gateway.go` (`Config.ReadBearer` at 411 — minting and plumbing it)
- `internal/guardsessions/guardsessions.go` (`WithGateway` at 75 — the writer that gains its
  first caller)
- `cmd/fak/session_query.go` (the misdiagnosing refusal at 161)

## Work estimate

Estimate: 3 points. The stamp itself is small; minting a genuinely read-scoped bearer at
guard-launch time, plumbing it into the gateway config, and proving the scope boundary is
the cost.

## Parent context

Parent: #3461 — this is the producer half of that issue's own stated scope. #3461 closed with
the index, the `fak session ls`/`status` readers, and the gateway's read-scoped auth; the
publish step named in its title was never wired, which is why every consumer it enabled reads
empty.

## Overall completion contribution
Contribution: 3/1000 points.

## Completion standard
development

records.title: feat(gateway): wire AnchorRefusalMonitor into observePlacement — the live half of #3622 (the fold ships unwired)
records.body:
## The finding

`1830aa325` shipped the fold half of #3622 — `internal/metrics.AnchorRefusalMonitor`, the
edge-triggered `ANCHOR_REFUSED_RISING` alarm over cache-breakpoint placement outcomes — and
declared itself `gen/next foundation` **because it has no live caller**. This is that caller.

Today the two halves do not touch:

- The producer exists and is always-on. `observePlacement`
  (`internal/gateway/metrics_observe.go:248`) is called on every Anthropic passthrough turn
  while compaction is configured on, and buckets the closed `agent.BreakpointReason*`
  vocabulary into `placementAttempts` (`internal/gateway/metrics.go:131`).
- The consumer exists and is unreachable. `AnchorRefusalMonitor.Observe` has **zero
  production call sites** — every reference outside its own definition is in a `_test.go`.
- What ships to an operator today is a monotone counter and nothing else:
  `fak_gateway_cache_breakpoint_placement_total{outcome=…}`
  (`internal/gateway/metrics_render.go:1224-1235`).

## Why the counter alone does not answer the question #3622 asked

A cumulative counter cannot express a RISING fraction. The failure #3622 is named for —
a session whose head turns volatile partway through, so the star-anchor quietly stops
EARNING caching — reads on the counter as `placed` simply *not incrementing*. Nothing
crosses a threshold, nothing fires, and the absence of an increment is invisible on a
dashboard that only shows lines going up.

Worse, these counters are **process-cumulative, not per-session** (the same trap already
witnessed on `compaction_shed_tokens`, epic #3095). A long-lived `fak serve` that spliced
cleanly for a thousand turns and then went volatile still shows a healthy lifetime ratio.
The monitor's rolling window over DECISIVE turns is precisely the thing the counter cannot
be post-processed into after the fact.

## The seam

`observePlacement` already receives the exact `agent.BreakpointOutcome` the monitor
classifies. The wiring is one call and a lifecycle decision:

1. Hold an `*metrics.AnchorRefusalMonitor` on `gatewayMetrics`, constructed with
   `NewAnchorRefusalMonitor` (default thresholds unless a knob is warranted).
2. Feed it from `observePlacement` — `outcome` is already normalized to `"placed"` there,
   which is the metric's own spelling of `BreakpointReasonNone` and the exact string
   `ClassifyAnchorOutcome` expects.
3. Surface the verdict where an operator sees it: a `BannerRow()` line and/or a
   `/debug/vars` block, alongside the existing placement counters.

The monitor is already concurrency-naive by design; `observePlacement` holds `compactMu`
around its own mutation, so the call belongs inside that critical section or behind the
monitor's own lock — whichever the reviewer prefers, but it must be decided rather than
inherited.

## Acceptance

- A live `fak serve` turn that refuses placement for `volatile_head` moves the monitor,
  asserted through the REAL gateway path (an outbound Anthropic passthrough), not by
  calling `Observe` directly — that is what the shipped unit tests already cover.
- A session that crosses the refusal threshold surfaces `ANCHOR_REFUSED_RISING` on an
  operator-visible surface, and a test asserts it appears there rather than only in the
  report struct.
- The false-positive guard survives the wiring: a Claude-Code-shaped session (~100%
  `already_set`) drives many turns through the real seam and raises NOTHING. This is the
  one that decides whether the alarm is mutable-by-operators or trusted — `already_set` is
  DEFERRED, and the wired path must keep it out of the denominator.
- The finding stays edge-triggered end to end: a long volatile stretch raises it once, not
  once per turn, when driven through the gateway rather than through `Observe` in isolation.
- The exposed number is honest about its window. If the surfaced fraction is
  process-cumulative like its neighbours, it must be LABELLED as such; the whole point of
  the monitor is that the lifetime ratio is the wrong denominator.

## Non-goals

Tuning the default thresholds against real fleet traffic. Ship the wiring with the shipped
defaults; a threshold change earns its own ticket once there is live data to tune against.

## Likely files

- `internal/gateway/metrics_observe.go` (`observePlacement` at 248 — the seam)
- `internal/gateway/metrics.go` (`gatewayMetrics`, the monitor field; `placementAttempts` at 131)
- `internal/gateway/metrics_snapshot.go` (the snapshot copy at 181-189, if the verdict rides along)
- `internal/gateway/metrics_render.go` (the placement block at 1224-1235 — where a banner row lands)
- `internal/metrics/anchor_refusal.go` (the fold being promoted; its header states this exact
  promotion evidence)

## Work estimate

Estimate: 3 points. The call itself is one line. The cost is the lifecycle decision (per
process vs per session), the operator surface, and driving the acceptance through the real
gateway path instead of through `Observe`.

## Parent context

Parent: #3622 — this is the second half of that issue's own stated scope. #3622 asked for a
"live breakpoint-placement outcome monitor + volatile-head refusal alarm"; `1830aa325`
delivered the alarm as a pure fold and explicitly deferred the *live* half, which is this
ticket. #3622 stays open until both land.

## Overall completion contribution
Contribution: 3/3 points.

## Completion standard
development

records.title: chore(tools): widen capture_fleet_task_xml scrub refusal beyond host identity before the capture set grows (#3323)
records.body:
## The finding

`921677ecc` shipped `tools/capture_fleet_task_xml.ps1` — the scrubber that exports live Windows
Scheduled Tasks into `tools/scheduled-tasks/*.xml` for this **public** repo. It fails closed,
which is the right shape: it re-scans its own output and throws `SCRUB_INCOMPLETE` rather than
writing a file that still carries an identity needle.

The problem is what the re-scan looks for. Today it checks **three needles and nothing else**:

- the machine SID (`$sid`)
- `$env:COMPUTERNAME`
- `$env:USERPROFILE`

and it carries exactly **one** value-redaction rule — a GCP project id
(`(?<=PROJECT=)[a-z0-9][-a-z0-9]{4,}` → `%GCP_PROJECT%`).

So the guarantee the script actually provides is "this export contains no *host path or machine
name*". The guarantee a reader will assume it provides — because it fails closed and because
its output is committed to a public repo — is "this export contains no *sensitive value*".
Those are not the same claim, and the gap is only invisible because the 13 captured tasks
happen not to exercise it.

## Why this is worth a ticket rather than a comment

An independent public-repo safety audit cleared all 14 files at `921677ecc`: zero findings, no
SID, no IPv4, no FQDN, no email, no credential. That verdict is real, but it is a verdict about
**those 13 files as they stand today**, established by a human-equivalent review — not by the
script. The script would have passed the same 13 files whether or not they contained an API key.

That matters the moment the captured set grows. `internal/taskvc` now has a live gate
(`MISSING_TASK_CAPTURE`) that makes adding a capture the *normal* way to close an orphan, so the
next fleet loop someone versions goes through this script. A task whose command line carries
`--token sk-…`, a bearer in an argument, an internal FQDN, or a bare IP literal would be
scrubbed of its paths, pass the fail-closed re-scan, and land in a public repo looking reviewed.

Fail-closed on a narrow needle set is more dangerous than no check, precisely because the
`SCRUB_INCOMPLETE` throw teaches the operator to trust the green.

## What to add

Widen the re-scan (and, where a safe replacement exists, the redaction map):

- **Generic secret shapes** — `sk-`, `ghp_`/`gho_`/`ghs_`, `xox[baprs]-`, `AIza`, `eyJ`
  (a JWT's base64 header), `-----BEGIN * PRIVATE KEY-----`, and long high-entropy hex/base64
  runs. These should REFUSE, not redact: a credential in a task command line is a finding about
  the task, not a formatting problem in the export.
- **IPv4 literals** and **FQDNs**, excluding loopback/`RFC 5737 TEST-NET` and any host already in
  the placeholder vocabulary. This repo's standing rule is that real IPs and hosts are never
  tracked.
- **The bare username** — `$env:USERNAME` on its own, not only as the `COMPUTERNAME\USERNAME`
  pair the current scrub map handles. A username appearing alone (in an argument, a share path,
  a log target) survives today.
- **Email addresses**, for the same reason.

Two design fences worth deciding explicitly in the ticket rather than inheriting:

1. **Refuse vs redact.** Host identity is redactable — there is a faithful placeholder
   (`%LOCALAPPDATA%`). A credential is not: replacing it with `%TOKEN%` produces an export that
   silently cannot be restored and hides that a secret was ever in the command line. Recommend
   REFUSE with a reason naming the needle class and the offending task, never the matched value.
2. **The refusal must not print the secret.** `SCRUB_INCOMPLETE` today can echo context. A
   widened scanner that prints what it matched would write the credential to a terminal and,
   plausibly, into a fleet log — turning the safety check into a leak.

## Acceptance

- A synthetic task XML carrying each needle class (one per class) is REFUSED by the script, and
  a test asserts the refusal names the class. Prove the negative first: the same fixture without
  the needle passes, so the test is not vacuously red.
- The refusal message does NOT contain the matched value. Assert this directly — it is the one
  regression that would make the hardening actively harmful.
- `-Check` over the 13 captures already on trunk still reports 13/13 ok with no DRIFT, i.e. the
  widened scanner does not false-positive on the audited real-world set. If it does, that is a
  finding about a capture and should be recorded, not suppressed.
- Loopback, RFC 5737 TEST-NET addresses, and the existing placeholder vocabulary are explicitly
  ALLOWED, so the repo's own documented example addresses do not trip the gate.

## Non-goals

Rewriting the scrub map's replacement strategy. The longest-prefix-first ordering
(`LOCALAPPDATA` before `USERPROFILE`) is correct and load-bearing — a shorter prefix would eat
the longer path — and should be left alone.

Auditing the 13 existing captures again. That was done independently at `921677ecc` and came back
SAFE; this ticket is about the NEXT capture.

## Likely files

- `tools/capture_fleet_task_xml.ps1` (the scrub map at 57-64, the value redaction at 73, the
  fail-closed re-scan at 96-106 — the three sites that change)
- `internal/taskvc/inventory.go` (the header states the two coverage tiers; the XML tier's
  honest-weakness paragraph should record what the scrubber does and does not refuse)
- `tools/scheduled-tasks/` (the fixture corpus the widened `-Check` must still pass)

## Work estimate

Estimate: 2 points. The needle set is small and well known. The cost is the refuse-vs-redact
decision, keeping the refusal from echoing what it matched, and building a synthetic fixture per
class so the gate is proven red before it is trusted green.

## Parent context

Parent: #3323 — this is the residual explicitly recorded in `921677ecc`'s commit message rather
than fixed there. That commit captured the 13 orphan tasks and said in as many words that the
fail-closed re-scan is "adequate for these 13 audited files and NOT adequate as a general
capture tool, so widening it is a follow-on". This is that follow-on. #3323's own done condition
(zero orphans) is met and does not depend on this.

## Overall completion contribution
Contribution: 2/2 points.

## Completion standard
development

records.title: test(dispatch): make the three opencode guard-lane tests hermetic instead of host-dependent (#4771)
records.body:
Three tests in `tools/dispatch_worker_glm_guard_test.py` read the **real host's**
`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` and therefore pass or fail depending on which box runs
them. They are red on this machine, red on pristine `origin/main`, and would be green on a
host with no opencode seat configured. That is a non-hermetic test, not a broken product
path — the code under test is behaving as designed.

## The red, baselined

Run in a **clean detached worktree at `origin/main` HEAD** (no local WIP), and again with
the ambient `FLEET_DOGFOOD_GUARD_BASEURL` unset to rule out environment:

```
tools/dispatch_worker_glm_guard_test.py .. 3 failed / 2 passed
  FAILED test_opencode_guarded_when_base_url_set
  FAILED test_opencode_guarded_with_loopback_lab_proxy_base
  FAILED test_opencode_unguarded_without_base_url
```

## Root cause: the test's knob is outranked by a file it doesn't control

`tools/dispatch_worker.py:795-815` documents `opencode_guard_base_url`'s precedence:

```
1. provider-scoped FLEET_DOGFOOD_GUARD_BASEURL_<PROVIDER>   (e.g. ..._ZAI_CODING_PLAN)
2. the selected provider's opencode account config `options.baseURL`
3. legacy FLEET_DOGFOOD_GUARD_BASEURL, and only for the default GLM provider
```

The tests' `_env()` helper sets exactly two variables — `FAK_BIN` and
`FLEET_DOGFOOD_GUARD_BASEURL`. That is **tier 3**. Tier 2 reads the seat config off disk
and wins first. Measured on this box just now, against the real modules:

```
provider      -> zai-coding-plan
configured    -> https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4        <- tier 2, read from disk
with env knob -> https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4        <- tier 3 never consulted
```

So each failure is the same single cause wearing three faces:

* `test_opencode_unguarded_without_base_url` expects `guarded is False` when no base URL is
  set — but a base URL *is* found (from the seat config), so the lane guards.
* the two `--base-url` equality assertions compare against `GLM_BASE` / `LAB_PROXY_BASE`
  and get the provider endpoint instead.

Note the ordering itself is **correct and should not change**: #4771 depends on tier 1
out-ranking tier 2, and tier 2 out-ranking tier 3 is what lets a per-seat config front its
own upstream. The bug is that the test asserts against tier 3 while a tier-2 source is live.

## Why this is worth a lane rather than a shrug

A host-dependent test is worse than a missing one. It is red for everybody who has an
opencode seat — i.e. exactly the people working on this lane — so it trains readers to
treat this file's failures as background noise. The two tests added under #4771 and the two
under #2400 live in the same file and are hermetic; their signal is being buried by
neighbours that are not.

## Acceptance

* The three tests inject the account-config read (as `test_glm_gateway_*` already do via
  `target_resolver`) instead of reaching for the real `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`.
* They pass on a host **with** a configured opencode seat and on one **without** — prove
  both, don't assume; the second case is the one that currently masks the defect.
* `python -m pytest tools/dispatch_worker_glm_guard_test.py` is 0 failed on this box.
* The precedence chain in `dispatch_worker.py` is **unchanged** — this is a test fix. A
  patch that reorders the tiers to make the tests green is the wrong fix and would regress
  #4771's provider-scoped pin.
* Negative witness: show each repaired test still reds when the behaviour it names is
  broken, so the repair isn't a stub that asserts nothing.

## Parent context

Parent: #4771 (the glm docs worker's local :18080 guard-gateway route). Both `4fba2fde516b`
and `69a856f37d83` record this red in their commit messages as pre-existing, untouched, and
"filed separately" — this is that filing. The precedence inversion #4771 fixed on the
product path is the same mechanism that makes these tests host-dependent.

## Work estimate
Estimate: 2 points. Uncertainty: operator-supplied estimate; revise through the parent denominator when evidence changes.

## Overall completion contribution
Contribution: 2/40 points.

## Completion standard
development

records.title: feat(egresslist): carry the upstream copyright NOTICE, not just the SPDX identifier (#4977)
records.body:
`internal/egresslist` records a redistributed list's license as an SPDX **identifier**
(`"license": "MIT"`), and renders it into the bundled artifact as `! Upstream-License: MIT`.
That names the terms but does not satisfy them. MIT says the copyright notice and permission
notice "shall be included in all copies or substantial portions of the Software"; CC BY-SA
requires attribution to the named licensor. A 2843-rule verbatim-derived copy of someone
else's curation, embedded in every fak binary, is a substantial portion by any reading.

So the current state is: we know what the terms are, we say what they are, and we do not
carry them. That is better than the prior state (no license recorded at all) and still short
of correct.

## Why it wasn't fixed in the lane that introduced the field

The artifact is **generated** by `fak egresslist refresh` and **checksum-pinned** — see
`Checksum` / `Verify` in `internal/egresslist/manifest.go`, gated by
`TestBundledListsMatchPinnedChecksum`. Hand-adding a notice line to the rendered `.txt`
would break the pin and red the trunk. Carrying the notice therefore needs a manifest field
plus renderer support, which is a separate change from ingesting a list.

## Scope

* Add a notice-carrying field to `Source` — e.g. `license_notice` (the verbatim upstream
  copyright + permission text, or a path to a vendored `LICENSE` copy under
  `internal/egresslist/lists/`). Prefer vendoring the upstream LICENSE file: a full MIT text
  inlined into every artifact header is noise repeated per list, and a vendored file is what
  a downstream packager's license scanner actually looks for.
* Emit a reference to it in `RenderArtifact` so the copy points at the notice that travels
  with it.
* Populate it for `stevenblack-curated` from the upstream repo's own LICENSE, fetched — not
  retyped from memory. **Do not guess the copyright holder or year**; read it from the
  source. Getting an attribution wrong is worse than the current omission.
* Re-pin the affected artifacts via `fak egresslist refresh` (the checksum will change) and
  confirm `TestBundledListsMatchPinnedChecksum` is green.

## Acceptance

* Any list with a non-empty `license` and a real upstream also carries its notice, enforced
  the same way the license field is — extend `TestAtLeastOneCommunityListIsIngested` rather
  than adding a parallel gate, so there is one place that says what provenance means.
* Negative witness: blanking the notice on an ingested list reds that test. Prove the red
  before trusting the green — and prefer `go test -overlay` over mutating the shared tree,
  as the parent lane did for its three negatives.
* The vendored notice file is tracked, and `check_committed_files.py` is content with it.
* `fak egresslist refresh` regenerates byte-identically against an unchanged upstream, so
  the notice does not reintroduce diff churn.

## Not in scope

Changing which lists are bundled, or the deliberate decision to ship StevenBlack's curated
source rather than the ~220k-entry unified merge.

## Parent context

Parent: #4977 (ingest a real community filter feed). The commit that added `Source.License`
records this gap explicitly as a residual — "the manifest records the SPDX IDENTIFIER, not
the upstream's copyright NOTICE ... filed separately". This is that filing.

## Work estimate
Estimate: 3 points. Uncertainty: operator-supplied estimate; revise through the parent denominator when evidence changes.

## Overall completion contribution
Contribution: 3/40 points.

## Completion standard
development

records.title: fix(scrub): let PUBLIC_LEAK exempt checksum-pinned third-party artifacts from the affiliation needles (#4977)
records.body:
The `PUBLIC_LEAK` gate refuses any commit whose **added lines** contain an
`AUDIT_NEEDLES` substring. That is right for hand-written content. It is wrong for a
**generated third-party data artifact**, where the needle is upstream data rather than
anything this repo is asserting — and today there is no way to express that difference, so
a whole class of legitimate artifact cannot be committed at all.

## The concrete block

`internal/egresslist` ingests community filter feeds through `fak egresslist refresh`, which
renders a checksum-pinned artifact under `internal/egresslist/lists/`. Ingesting the
StevenBlack/hosts curated source (2843 rules, MIT) is refused:

```
PUBLIC_LEAK: 16 finding(s):
  internal/egresslist/lists/stevenblack-curated.txt:310:  [[redacted:public-corpus]]  ||ad.[redacted:public-corpus]adhub.com^
  internal/egresslist/lists/stevenblack-curated.txt:367:  [[redacted:public-corpus]]  ||ads.[redacted:public-corpus]ads.com^
  ... 14 more, all *.[redacted:public-corpus]ads / [redacted:public-corpus]acr / [redacted:public-corpus]adhub / [redacted:public-corpus]cloudsolution
```

Every hit is an ad-or-telemetry domain published verbatim on a widely-mirrored public block
list. The `[redacted:public-corpus]` needle exists to stop **employer-affiliation** leakage
(`tools/scrub_public_copy.py:340-348`). A domain appearing on a public ad-block list is not
an affiliation claim — it is the opposite, a record of something being blocked.

## Why the documented escape is the wrong tool here

The needle's own comment offers `FLEET_ALLOW_LEAK=1` for "a genuine public mention". Do not
use it for this, for a reason stronger than the one the comment anticipates:

`[redacted:public-corpus]` is in `AUDIT_NEEDLES` and therefore in `EXPORT_AUDIT_NEEDLES`, and it has **no
entry in `REPLACEMENTS`** (verified: zero `[redacted:public-corpus]` lines in the `REPLACEMENTS` block).
`EXPORT_AUDIT_NEEDLES` are needles that must be ABSENT from the public copy *after* scrubbing
— so nothing would rewrite these on export. Overriding the commit gate once would leave 16
permanent needles that fail the post-scrub audit on **every future publish**, not just this
commit. The friction is not one-commit friction; it is a broken publish pipeline.

## Why the obvious workarounds are worse

* **Drop the 16 domains and re-pin.** The next `fak egresslist refresh` pulls them straight
  back in. A filter list that cannot survive its own refresh command is broken, and
  determinism-across-refresh is the property the registry is built on.
* **Add a `REPLACEMENTS` rewrite for the domains.** The published fak would then block
  *different hosts* than the private one. Silently divergent behaviour in a security artifact
  is unacceptable.
* **Pick a feed without [redacted:public-corpus] domains.** [redacted:public-corpus] is a large ad network; any real
  ads/tracking feed carries them. This just relocates the problem.

## What to build

An exemption class for **generated, provenance-pinned, third-party artifacts**, honoured by
BOTH the commit-time scan and the post-scrub export audit — the second half is the one that
is easy to forget and is what makes `FLEET_ALLOW_LEAK=1` insufficient.

Design notes, not prescriptions:

* Scope it by path AND by shape, not path alone: a file under
  `internal/egresslist/lists/*.txt` that carries the generated header and whose bytes match
  its pinned `sha256` in `lists/manifest.json`. A checksum-verified generated file cannot be
  a hand-smuggled leak, which is the property that makes the exemption safe.
* Exempt only the **affiliation** needle class. Credential shapes, real operator home paths,
  real IPs, and private host aliases must stay strict even inside these artifacts — an
  upstream feed could legitimately contain an IPv4 literal, and that is still not something
  to normalise.
* Existing mechanisms deliberately do not cover this and should not be widened into it:
  `SELF_REFERENTIAL` (`scrub_public_copy.py:501`) is audit-only and is about files that
  *define* the scrub; `_is_intentional_fixture` (`:510`) is whole-tree-only and explicitly
  keeps "staged/range scans strict".

## Acceptance

* The egresslist ingest unit commits without `FLEET_ALLOW_LEAK`, and `python
  tools/scrub_public_copy.py`'s post-scrub export audit passes with the artifact present.
* Negative witness, three ways — prove each red before trusting green, and prefer `go test
  -overlay` / a scratch copy over mutating the shared tree:
  1. the same needle in a **hand-written** file under the same directory is still REFUSED;
  2. a **credential-shaped** or real-IP string inside an exempted artifact is still REFUSED;
  3. an artifact whose bytes **do not match** its pinned checksum loses the exemption.
* The export audit's behaviour is pinned by a test, not just the commit gate — the export
  half is the one that fails silently and late.

## Parent context

Parent: #4977 (ingest a real community filter feed). That unit is complete and green locally
— 2843 rules, license provenance, three negative witnesses — and is **held unshipped** solely
by this gate. It ships the moment this lands.

## Work estimate
Estimate: 5 points. Uncertainty: operator-supplied estimate; revise through the parent denominator when evidence changes.

## Overall completion contribution
Contribution: 5/40 points.

## Completion standard
development

records.title: fix(gateway): the corpus-drift guard reads an untracked per-box ledger and its two constants now track the wrong population (#3803)
records.body:
`internal/gateway/calibration_corpus_drift_test.go` currently reds on any box that runs the
headless fleet, and skips everywhere else. Both of its tests fail here:

```
calibration_corpus_drift_test.go:119: DefaultAssumedSessionTurns=50 has drifted outside the
  calibrated [p75=6, p95=13] session-length band (corpus p90=10 over n=2401 real sessions).
calibration_corpus_drift_test.go:155: headHorizonHeavyResidentFloor=60000 has drifted outside
  the calibrated [p10=60385, p50=69462] per-turn cached-prompt band (n=2398 sessions).
```

Both messages say "recompute the distribution and either recalibrate the const or update the
calibration comment". **Do neither yet.** The measurements below say the guard is reading a
different population than the one its constants serve, and recalibrating on this input would
drag two production economic constants toward whatever workload happens to dominate a
developer's local box.

## What the guard actually reads

`findCorpus` resolves `gatewayusageledger.DefaultLedgerRel`, which is
`.fak/nightrun/gateway-usage.jsonl` (`internal/gatewayusageledger/ledger.go:21`) — the
**live, gitignored, machine-local runtime ledger**. Not the tracked
`docs/nightrun/gateway-usage.jsonl` mirror.

That is the first defect on its own: the guard's input is untracked, so it can never red in
CI (it skips — "thin corpus: only 0 nonzero-length sessions") and reds only on the boxes
running the fleet. A drift guard whose verdict is per-box and irreproducible is a guard
nobody can act on: the person who sees the red cannot show it to anyone else, and the tree
that CI blesses was never actually checked.

## The two corpora disagree, and the tracked one passes

Measured with the same interpolation the test uses (single pass over each file, exit rows
only):

| corpus | branch | n | p50 | p75 | p90 | p95 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `docs/nightrun/` (tracked) | CachedTurns fallback | 508 | 7 | 33 | 52 | 70 |
| `docs/nightrun/` (tracked) | ObservedTurns | 307 | 35 | 44.5 | 58.4 | 77.7 |
| `docs/nightrun/` (tracked) | **blended = what the test would use** | **815** | 25 | **40** | 54 | **74** |
| `.fak/nightrun/` (live, read) | ObservedTurns | 2399 | 6 | 6 | 10 | 13 |
| `.fak/nightrun/` (live, read) | CachedTurns fallback | 2 | 345.5 | 477.8 | 557.1 | 583.5 |
| `.fak/nightrun/` (live, read) | **blended = what the test uses** | **2401** | 6 | **6** | 10 | **13** |

The tracked corpus's CachedTurns row — n=508, p50 7, p75 33, p90 52, p95 70 — reproduces the
calibration comment (`calibration_corpus_drift_test.go:105-106`: "median 7, p75 33, p90 52,
p95 70 — 50 sits just under p90") to the digit. That is the population the constant was
sized on, and against it `DefaultAssumedSessionTurns=50` sits inside `[p75=40, p95=74]` and
**passes**.

Same for the second const. Per-turn cached-prompt volume: tracked corpus p10=51986,
p50=64963, so `headHorizonHeavyResidentFloor=60000` is comfortably **inside**. Live corpus
p10=60385, p50=69462 — and 60000 is **385 tokens, 0.6%, below the band edge**.

## The crux

The live ledger is ~2400 sessions with a **median of 6 turns**. That is the night-dispatch
fleet: each headless resolver is a short, mostly-automated session. The tracked corpus is
~800 sessions with a median of 7-35 depending on branch and a long tail out to p95≈74 — the
interactive shape.

`DefaultAssumedSessionTurns` is a prior about how many turns an early burst will be repaid
over. Recalibrating it 50 → ~10 because 2400 short headless sessions arrived would be sizing
the interactive burst gate's economics on fleet automation traffic, and the two populations
want opposite answers. The guard is not detecting that the world moved; it is detecting that
the *sample* changed composition. So the question this ticket has to answer first is **which
population these constants are for**, and only then what the number should be.

Worth flagging honestly as unresolved: the tracked corpus's own `ObservedTurns` rows have
p50=35 while the live ledger's have p50=6 — same field, very different. That is consistent
with a pure population shift, but a change in what `ObservedTurns` counts is not ruled out
by anything measured here and should be checked before any number is trusted.

## The second failure is a different bug and should not be lumped in

60000 vs a p10 of 60385 is a 0.6% miss on a band edge. The file's own header says the bands
are "deliberately WIDE (a drift GUARD, not an exact-match assertion): they catch a gross
shift ..., not the normal wobble of an appended corpus". A 0.6% crossing IS the normal wobble
of an appended corpus. The guard is failing its own stated contract — a band edge with no
hysteresis and no minimum-margin flips red and green as rows are appended, and that is the
fastest way to teach people to ignore a security-adjacent gate.

## Scope

1. **Decide and document the population.** Either the guard reads the tracked mirror (making
   it reproducible and CI-meaningful), or it segments the live ledger and asserts against the
   interactive segment only. Whichever is chosen, the constant's comment should name the
   population, since "the corpus" is now ambiguous and that ambiguity is the whole bug.
2. **Do not blend two length signals silently.** `sessionLengths` prefers `ObservedTurns` and
   falls back to `CachedTurns`; on the live ledger 2396 of 2399 rows carry BOTH. Mixing bases
   within one distribution should be either justified in the comment or stopped.
3. **Give the band a margin.** Require the const to be outside by some real fraction before
   failing, so a 0.6% edge crossing does not red the trunk.
4. **Only then** revisit the two numbers, on the population settled in (1).

## Acceptance

* Both tests give the SAME verdict on a clean checkout and on a fleet box — i.e. the verdict
  no longer depends on untracked local state. If they must stay corpus-dependent, the skip
  path must be loud enough that a permanently-skipping guard is not mistaken for a passing
  one.
* Negative witness, and prove each red before trusting the green — prefer `go test -overlay`
  or a scratch copy over mutating the shared tree:
  1. a genuinely gross shift (set the const to 5, or to 500) still REDS;
  2. a 0.6%-scale band-edge crossing does NOT red;
  3. an absent/thin corpus still skips rather than passing vacuously.
* The recalibration, if any, cites which population it was computed over and n.

## Parent context

Parent: #3803, which introduced this guard together with the resume/heal watchdog debug
surface. The guard is doing its job in the sense that it noticed something real; what it
noticed is that its input changed composition, which is not what its failure message claims.

Found while shipping the #3622 anchor-refusal gateway wiring: these two reds appeared in
`go test ./internal/gateway/` and were proven NOT attributable to that change by re-running
them with the changed files reverted to origin/main under an overlay, in the tree that has
the corpus. Noting the method because the obvious one fails silently — these tests SKIP in a
clean worktree, so a worktree baseline reads "ok" while proving nothing.

## Work estimate
Estimate: 5 points. Uncertainty: operator-supplied estimate; revise through the parent denominator when evidence changes.

## Overall completion contribution
Contribution: 5/40 points.

## Completion standard
development

records.title: feat(toolproc): arm the reuse verdict vocabulary — register the pairs and cite the code on a served repeat (#5119)
records.body:
`internal/toolproc/repeatreason.go` allocates the reuse verdict vocabulary — six codes at
1090–1095, their stable `REUSE_*` names, `ReuseReasonPairs()` for registration and
`ReuseReasonCode()` for receipt→code lookup. It is complete, total over `ReuseReason`,
collision-checked against the process-table family, and **has no consumer**. Nothing in the
tree calls either exported function, so no live seam renders a reuse verdict today.

That is a deliberate ship-as-foundation, declared in the file rather than implied. This
ticket is the arming rung it defers to.

## What "armed" means here

`abi.ReasonName(code)` must round-trip to a stable token for a verdict a seam actually
emitted. Three things have to become true together:

1. **Some consumer registers the pairs exactly once at startup** — `for _, p := range
   toolproc.ReuseReasonPairs() { abi.RegisterReason(p.Code, p.Name) }`. Not this leaf's
   `init`: `internal/toolproc` is an init-free fold with no defconfig entry, and the offline
   `fak toolproc repeats` path folds rollout logs in a process where nothing is registered.
   Registration belongs to the consumer that serves repeats, which is why `ReasonPairs()` is
   registered by its consumers too.
2. **A seam that serves a repeat cites the code**, mapping `Receipt.Reason` through
   `ReuseReasonCode`. The contract's fail-closed half matters at this call site: `ok=false`
   (an empty `Receipt.Reason` — a zero-valued receipt that never ran the fold — or an
   invented token) means "no registered verdict" and the consumer **must not fabricate one**.
   Pinning that the consumer honours it is the point of the lane, not a detail.
3. **The verdict is visible** wherever other kernel refusals are, so a served repeat is
   distinguishable from a fresh fetch on the surface an operator reads.

## Why this was not done in the lane that allocated the block

Allocating a vocabulary and wiring a live seam are different risks. The vocabulary is pure
data and can be reviewed for collisions and totality on its own; arming touches a serving
path where a wrong verdict is worse than no verdict. Splitting them also means the block is
claimed, so a second consumer cannot independently invent an overlapping range in the
meantime — which is the concrete value the unwired file already delivers.

## Acceptance

* One registration site, run once; registering twice with different names for a code must be
  impossible by construction (there is no unregister in `abi`).
* A seam-level test that a served repeat renders its `REUSE_*` token — not `REASON_1090`.
  The forward-compat fallback rendering is precisely the symptom of forgetting step 1, and it
  is silent: the wire still looks well-formed.
* A test that an unmapped/empty `Receipt.Reason` yields NO verdict at the consumer rather
  than a fabricated one.
* Negative witness, and prove each red before trusting the green — prefer `go test -overlay`
  or a scratch copy over mutating the shared tree:
  1. drop the registration call → the seam test reds with `REASON_<n>`;
  2. make the consumer fabricate a verdict for `ok=false` → the fail-closed test reds.
* Update the "AND TODAY THERE IS NO CONSUMER" paragraph in `repeatreason.go` when it stops
  being true. A foundation file that still declares itself unwired after it is wired is a
  fresh unwitnessed claim in the other direction.

## Not in scope

Changing `ReuseReason`, the decision fold in `repeatreuse.go`, or the 1090–1095 allocation.

## Parent context

Parent: #5119 (the last DoD rung of #4764), which is what `repeatreason.go` cites as its
origin. Filed while shipping that file with its totality witness
(`repeatreason_test.go`); the file's doc comment had named
`internal/toolprocgate/reusearm.go` as registering the pairs "today", and that file does not
exist and no caller does either — the comment was corrected to declare the unwired posture,
and this is the lane it defers to.

## Work estimate
Estimate: 3 points. Uncertainty: operator-supplied estimate; revise through the parent denominator when evidence changes.

## Overall completion contribution
Contribution: 3/40 points.

## Completion standard
development

records.title: fix(commit): refuse a stale untracked path that already exists on origin/main — the routine #1088 misfire in a behind-HEAD shared checkout (#1088)
records.body:
In a shared multi-session checkout whose `HEAD` has fallen behind `origin/main`, a file that is **already on trunk** shows up in `git status` as `??` — untracked — and is therefore indistinguishable from genuinely new work. `fak commit --path

` then writes the **working-tree** copy, which is the #1088 revert: whatever peers pushed to that path is silently replaced by a local copy that predates it. This is not hypothetical. Measured in this checkout today (`HEAD` 90 commits behind `origin/main`, 69 untracked paths): | class | count | what committing it does | |---|---|---| | on `origin/main`, byte-identical | 40 | no-op — pure wasted work | | on `origin/main`, content DIFFERS | 4 | **silently reverts trunk** | | genuinely new | 25 | the actual work | So 44 of 69 untracked paths — 64% — were already shipped, and 4 of them are live landmines. An agent draining this list top-to-bottom has a two-thirds chance per path of doing nothing and a real chance of reverting a peer. ## The diagnostic an agent naturally reaches for is actively misleading `git diff --stat origin/main -- ` is the obvious way to ask "how does my copy compare to trunk?". For an **untracked** path it does not answer that question at all: the path is absent from the index, so git renders trunk's version as wholly **deleted**. Run against the four differing files here it printed: ``` cmd/fak/superloop_fleet_test.go | 188 -------------------- internal/policy/amendment_matrix_test.go | 193 --------------------- .../rows-compute-4362.json | 79 --------- .../rows-session-quarantine.json | 80 --------- 4 files changed, 540 deletions(-) ``` Every one of those numbers is just the trunk file's own line count. It reads as "my copy deletes 540 lines of trunk" — a conclusion that is wrong in both directions: one of those files (`superloop_fleet_test.go`, 215 lines local vs 188 on trunk) is actually **longer** than trunk's. The correct comparison is content-to-content (`git show origin/main:` against the file), which is exactly the step the misleading output discourages. ## What to build **1. A refusal in `fak commit`.** For each `--path`, if the path is untracked in `HEAD`, present on `origin/main`, and its content differs from the `origin/main` blob, refuse with a structured reason (`STALE_UNTRACKED` or similar) naming the trunk sha and the byte delta. The identical case should not refuse — it should report the path as a no-op and drop it from the commit rather than manufacturing an empty change. This is the same posture the existing build check already takes, and it should carry the same escape: an operator who genuinely intends to supersede trunk's version passes an explicit flag, having seen the diff. **2. A triage verb.** Something like `fak status --classify` that buckets untracked paths into the three classes above. The 40-identical case is the common one and is pure waste; an agent should be able to see it in one call instead of hand-rolling the comparison, which is what happened here. ## Why the existing guards do not cover it `fak commit`'s build check compares the *prospective committed tree* assembled on the local `HEAD`. When `HEAD` is 90 behind, that tree is not the tree that lands, so the check reasons about a fiction — it both misses this class entirely and produces false `COMMITTED_RED`s for unrelated reasons (a commit today was refused for `undefined: metrics.AnchorRefusal*` against symbols that are already on `origin/main`). Fetching `origin/main` and classifying against it is the missing input, and it fixes both symptoms. ## Acceptance * Committing an untracked path whose content differs from `origin/main` is REFUSED with a reason naming the trunk sha, not silently accepted. * Committing an untracked path byte-identical to `origin/main` does not produce a commit. * A genuinely new path is unaffected — no new friction on the 25 real ones. * Negative witness, and prove each red before trusting the green — prefer `go test -overlay` or a scratch copy over mutating the shared tree: 1. stage a stale copy of a trunk file → refused; 2. stage a byte-identical copy → reported as a no-op, no commit; 3. stage a genuinely new file → commits normally, no regression in the common path. * The refusal message must not rely on `git diff` against an untracked path, for the reason documented above. ## Parent context Parent: #1088, the original "`git commit -- path` commits working-tree state and can silently delete a peer's pushed block" finding. That issue named the hazard; this one is the mechanism that makes it fire routinely rather than occasionally, plus the guard that would catch it. Found while draining parked units in this shared checkout — the four landmine paths above were caught by hand-classifying every untracked path against `origin/main` before committing anything, which is precisely the step this ticket proposes to mechanize. ## Work estimate Estimate: 5 points. Uncertainty: operator-supplied estimate; revise through the parent denominator when evidence changes. ## Overall completion contribution Contribution: 5/40 points. ## Completion standard development

records.title: fix(tools): reconcile FleetWorktreeDoctor installer name drift so a reinstall updates the live task in place
records.body:
## Current state

`tools/register_worktree_doctor.ps1` defaults `-TaskName` to an **interpolated** value:

```powershell
$repoSlug = ([IO.Path]::GetFileName($Repo) -replace '[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]', '-')
$TaskName = "FleetWorktreeDoctor-$repoSlug"
```

The live task is the **bare** `FleetWorktreeDoctor` (root task path, State=Ready). So a
re-run of the installer registers `FleetWorktreeDoctor-fleet` (or `-fak`) *alongside* the
existing task instead of updating it in place — a second worktree-doctor loop.

This is the identical failure class #3323 reconciled for `FleetStaleWorkGarden`, and it is
the last `StatusDrift` row in the fleet task inventory:

- `internal/taskvc/inventory.go` — `{Task: "FleetWorktreeDoctor", Status: StatusDrift, ...}`
- The row's own `Reason` says the reconcile "needs an operator decision on whether the live
  task or the per-clone naming scheme is canonical."

Filed as a real tracked item because #3323 is closing and that residual would otherwise
survive only as a code comment.

## Why now

Name drift is worse than a plain orphan: the repair action (re-running the installer) is
what *causes* the duplicate, and it looks like it worked. The task is currently covered by
a versioned XML capture (`tools/scheduled-tasks/FleetWorktreeDoctor.xml`), so reboot
survival is not at risk — only reinstall-in-place is.

## The operator decision this needs

Either is a valid resolution; both are behavior-preserving for the live task:

1. **Bare name is canonical** — drop the interpolation, default `-TaskName` to the literal
   `'FleetWorktreeDoctor'`. Loses per-clone multi-instance registration.
2. **Per-clone naming is canonical** — keep the interpolation and *rename the live task* to
   `FleetWorktreeDoctor-fleet`, then re-point the capture and the inventory row.

Option 1 matches what #3323 did for the stale-work installer. Option 2 preserves the
ability to run a doctor per checkout. Pick one — the point is that the tree and the host
must agree.

## Done condition

`tools/register_worktree_doctor.ps1` statically declares a task name that binds the live
task, so a reinstall updates it in place; the `FleetWorktreeDoctor` inventory row moves off
`StatusDrift`.

## Witness

`go test ./internal/taskvc/ -run TestFleetTaskInventoryBindsToVersionedInstallers -count=1`
green with the row promoted to `StatusInstaller`, plus a single live `FleetWorktreeDoctor*`
task at the root task path after a dry re-run of the installer.

## Acceptance gate

`go test ./internal/taskvc/ -count=1` green (the tree gate), and `make ci` (Windows:
`./test.ps1`).

## Lane

`tools`

## Out of scope

The principal/SWA migration (#3322) and the capture tier itself — this is one installer's
`-TaskName`.

records.title: chore(toolproc): retire or bound zz_replaywitness_test.go — a tracked test that calls itself throwaway, cannot fail, and runs unbounded off a per-box corpus (#4764)
records.body:
`internal/toolproc/zz_replaywitness_test.go` opens with, verbatim:

```go
// zz_replaywitness_test.go — THROWAWAY (not committed): replays the real captured
// Codex rollout corpus through the shipped IngestRollout+ClassifyRepeats to produce
// the #4764 Witness part (A) — the distribution + avoidable-saving over real data.
```

It is committed. `git ls-files` on `origin/main` matches it. So the repo carries a tracked
test that documents itself as untracked, and every reader who checks the comment before the
index draws the wrong conclusion about whether it is safe to change.

That is the cosmetic half. The mechanical half is worse.

## Its runtime is a function of how long the operator has owned the machine

The test walks `$HOME/.codex/sessions` (or `FAK_ROLLOUT_DIR`) — a per-box path **outside the
repo** — and caps the corpus at the **top-100 files by size**. It caps files. It does not cap
**records**. On a box with a long rollout history those 100 files carried **207,337
`CallRecord`s** into `ClassifyRepeats`, which tokenizes each observation body.

Measured on this checkout today: `go test ./internal/toolproc/ -count=1` ran past a **600s**
timeout and panicked, taking the whole package's result to `FAIL` with it. The stack was live
in `tokenize` (`repeatnormalize.go:317`) — not deadlocked, just still working. Skipping this
one test, the same package on the same tree is **`ok, 0.698s`**.

So the package's wall-clock is ~1000x'd by a test whose input is the developer's own
accumulated history. It gets slower every day the machine is used, and nothing in the repo
bounds it.

## CI never sees any of this

```go
if len(files) == 0 {
    t.Skip("no rollout corpus on this host")
}
```

A CI runner has no `~/.codex/sessions`, so the test skips and the package is green. The
failure is reserved exclusively for developer machines that actually have the data — the
boxes where a red is most expensive and least expected. This is the same defect shape as
**#5406** (a gate reading an untracked per-box path and therefore measuring a different
population than the one CI measures); worth fixing together as a class, not one at a time.

## And it cannot fail

Every result is `fmt.Printf`. There is no `t.Error`, no `t.Fatal`, no assertion of any kind.
The test has exactly three reachable outcomes: skip, print, or hang. It is a **script wearing
a test's costume** — it consumes a `go test` slot and a CI timeout budget while being
incapable of reporting a regression in the code it exercises.

## What to do

Pick one, deliberately:

**(a) Delete it.** It produced the #4764 witness; that witness is recorded in the issue. A
one-shot measurement script that has already been run does not need to live in the test
binary. This is the default and the file's own comment agrees with it.

**(b) Keep it as a real witness, and make it honest.** Then all four of these, not a subset:
cap records (not just files) so runtime is bounded on any host; assert something so it can
actually fail; move it behind an explicit opt-in (a build tag or a required `FAK_ROLLOUT_DIR`
— not a silent skip that hides it from CI); and fix the comment that calls it uncommitted.

A half-measure — capping records but leaving it assertion-free, or fixing the comment but
leaving it unbounded — leaves the package's runtime hostage to a machine-local directory,
which is the thing to eliminate.

## Acceptance

* `go test ./internal/toolproc/` completes in seconds on a box **with** a large local rollout
  corpus present. Verify on such a box; a green run on a machine with no corpus proves
  nothing here, which is the whole point of the ticket.
* No tracked file in the package describes itself as not committed.
* If (b): a negative witness — corrupt the corpus, or feed input that should classify
  differently, and show the test **reds**. Prove the red before trusting the green. If no
  such negative can be constructed, that is the argument for (a).

## Parent context

Parent: **#4764**, the epic this file was written to produce witness part (A) for. The
witness has been produced; what remains is the scratch artifact left behind in the tree.
Found while running the full `internal/toolproc` package on the landing tree to verify an
unrelated unit (#5119) — the package failed at 600s, and the failure was neither mine nor
the package's.

Estimate: 3 points. Uncertainty: operator-supplied estimate; revise through the parent denominator when evidence changes.
