records.title: feat(guard): arm the self-tighten gate — route the propose-only channel through admitSelfTightenOverlay and journal the verdict (#5181)
records.body:
`cmd/fak/guard_self_tighten.go` decides whether a self-authored policy overlay may be applied
on the agent's own authority: it routes the delta through `policy.DiffAmendment` and admits
only `AmendmentNone` or `AmendmentTighten`. It is correct, tested, negative-witnessed — and
**nothing calls it**. `grep -rn admitSelfTightenOverlay` returns the definition and its four
test call sites, nothing else.

So the envelope described in #5185 is currently a decision function with no seam. Any overlay
that reaches the propose-only channel (#5182) today does so without passing this gate. This
ticket is the arming rung the file's header defers to.

## What "armed" means here

1. **The propose-only channel calls it before applying anything.** The overlay's `current` must
   be the *effective* floor as actually installed, not a re-derived or default policy — a gate
   fed the wrong baseline classifies a widening as a no-op, which is the one outcome that is
   silently unsafe.
2. **The refusal is journaled with its class and reason**, both of which the function already
   returns and no caller currently records. A refusal an operator cannot see is
   indistinguishable from a gate that never ran.
3. **Admission is not the same as application.** A `tighten` verdict says the delta may be
   applied without operator gating; it does not say the overlay is well-formed. Whatever
   validation the gated path does must still happen on the self-authored path.

## The mixed-delta case is the one to pin

`AmendmentDelta.Class()` folds by severity — most severe wins — so an overlay that adds a Deny
*and* adds an Allow classifies as `widen` and is refused whole. That is the correct behaviour
and it is also the tempting thing for a caller to "improve" by applying the tightening half
and dropping the widening half. It must not: a partial application of a delta the agent
authored as a unit produces a floor the proposer never proposed. Worth an explicit test that
a mixed delta is refused **entirely**, with nothing applied.

## Known-unreachable branch — do not paper over it

`AmendmentFrozenViolation` cannot be produced by `DiffAmendment` as it stands: `DiffAmendment`
emits changes under eight `Field` names, all eight are registered in the knob registry, and
none is `AmendFrozen` (the FROZEN knobs carry `Field: ""` and are compiled-in only). This was
measured, not assumed — flipping both fail-closed branches to *admit* leaves the whole suite
green.

Keep the branch. `route()` sends an **unregistered** field to `Frozen`, so it arms itself the
moment a new `adjudicator.Policy` field is added to `DiffAmendment` without a registry row —
exactly the fail-closed case it exists for. Arming this gate must not "simplify" it away
because coverage tooling reports it unhit.

## Acceptance

* A self-authored overlay that only tightens is applied with no operator confirm, and the
  applied floor matches the proposal exactly.
* A self-authored overlay that widens in any field is refused, with class and reason on the
  journal row.
* A mixed tighten+widen overlay is refused whole, with **no** partial application.
* The `current` argument is the installed effective floor; a test pins that feeding a stale or
  default baseline is not possible from the call site.
* Negative witness, and prove each red before trusting the green — prefer `go test -overlay`
  or a scratch copy over mutating the shared tree:
  1. drop the gate call from the propose path → the widen-refusal seam test reds;
  2. feed the gate a default `Policy` as `current` instead of the installed one → the baseline
     test reds.
* Update the "AND TODAY THERE IS NO CALLER" paragraph in `guard_self_tighten.go` when it stops
  being true. A file that still declares itself unwired after it is wired is a fresh
  unwitnessed claim in the other direction.

## Not in scope

Changing `policy.DiffAmendment`, the knob registry, or the amendment classes.

## Parent context

Parent: **#5181** (epic #5170, Track F), which `guard_self_tighten.go` cites as its origin.
Filed while shipping that file with its four tests and three negatives — the header had framed
it as "the enforcement companion to the propose-only channel (#5182)", which is true as a
design relationship and false if read as a call site. The header now declares the unwired
posture outright, and this is the lane it defers to.

## Work estimate
Estimate: 3 points. Uncertainty: operator-supplied estimate; revise through the parent denominator when evidence changes.

## Overall completion contribution
Contribution: 3/40 points.

## Completion standard
development

records.title: fix(cmd/fak): the package cannot be run to completion — ~4000 tests blow a 15m go test timeout on a clean origin/main checkout (#1325)
records.body:
`go test ./cmd/fak/` does not finish. Measured on a clean detached worktree checked out at
`origin/main` — no local WIP, no dirty peer state:

```
panic: test timed out after 15m0s
	running tests:
		TestLoopDriveHoldsAndReleasesRegionLease (7s)
FAIL	github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/cmd/fak	900.624s
```

The test binary carries **~4002 tests** (`runTests` was handed a 0xfa2-element slice). The
named test is not the culprit — it had been running 7 seconds when the *package-wide* deadline
expired. Nothing is deadlocked; the package is simply larger than any reasonable timeout.

## Why this matters more than "tests are slow"

**It makes the package unverifiable as a unit, which quietly changes how work gets shipped.**
An agent or contributor who wants to know "did I break anything in `cmd/fak`?" has no answer
available. The two workable responses are both bad:

* run `-run 'TestMyThing'` and ship on a targeted witness, which cannot see cross-test
  interference (shared package vars, `init()` ordering, global registries with no unregister —
  `cmd/fak` has all three); or
* raise `-timeout` and wait past 15 minutes per iteration, which nobody does twice.

The first is what actually happens, so the package's integration risk is currently uncovered
in practice regardless of what CI nominally runs. Worth checking what CI does here: if it
passes a longer timeout, the gap is dev-loop only; if it shards or skips, the shards are the
real unit and the monolithic package is a fiction.

## What to do

Diagnose before reshaping — the fix depends on which of these it is:

1. **A few pathological tests dominate.** Then `-timeout 900s` with `-v` and a sort by
   duration names them, and they get bounded, marked `testing.Short`, or moved. Note the
   related finding in **#5410**: `internal/toolproc` had a single tracked test that blew a 600s
   budget while the rest of the package ran in 0.7s. The same shape is likely here — start by
   assuming one or two offenders, not 4000 uniformly-slow tests.
2. **The tail is genuinely 4000 tests.** Then the package is doing too much and the answer is
   structural: `cmd/fak` is a `package main` that has accumulated the logic of a dozen
   subsystems, and the leaf-per-concern split the repo already favours would move most of
   those tests into `internal/` packages that each run in under a second.

Either way, produce the duration profile FIRST and put it in the ticket. A reshape argued from
a guess about which tests are slow is how the wrong half gets moved.

## Acceptance

* `go test ./cmd/fak/` completes within the default 10m timeout on a clean checkout, without
  raising `-timeout`.
* The duration profile is recorded in the ticket — the top ~20 tests by wall-clock, before and
  after.
* No test is made to pass by being skipped by default. A test moved behind `testing.Short()`
  must still run somewhere that is actually run, and the ticket must say where.
* Negative witness, and prove the red before trusting the green: with the fix in place,
  deliberately reintroduce the dominant cost (or a stand-in for it) and show the package
  returns to blowing the budget. If the runtime cannot be attributed to anything specific
  enough to reintroduce, that is evidence for reading (2) and should be stated.

## Parent context

Parent: **#1325**, the pre-push witness line of work — the tree's ability to tell a
contributor "your change is safe to push" before they push it. A package that cannot be run to
completion is a hole in exactly that witness, and it is the hole an agent silently routes
around.

Found while shipping `cmd/fak/guard_self_tighten.go` (#5181): the whole-package run was
attempted on the landing tree precisely to catch cross-test interference, it timed out, and
the commit shipped on a targeted witness plus an argument that the unit is a pure function
with no global state. That argument happens to hold for that unit. It will not hold for the
next one.

## Work estimate
Estimate: 5 points. Uncertainty: operator-supplied estimate; revise through the parent denominator when evidence changes.

## Overall completion contribution
Contribution: 5/40 points.

## Completion standard
development

records.title: feat(ablate): wire a live TierScorer so the model-strength axis produces measured verdicts
records.body:
Follow-on to #4412, which has now shipped: the model-strength axis (`TierScorer` seam, the weak/mid/strong ladder replay, the LOAD_BEARING / REDUNDANT / HOBBLING / UNMEASURED classifier, and the flat `verdicts[]` payload consumed by `fak harness-debt-dispatch`) is on trunk and green.

**What is NOT done:** production measures nothing. `emitAblation` binds `StubTierScorer`, which returns `Measured:false` with a detail string, so every live verdict is UNMEASURED. That is an honest refusal rather than a fabricated grade -- `hddSelectDebt` drops UNMEASURED, so a stub can never auto-file a deletion issue -- but it means the axis earns nothing today.

**Remaining work**
- A real `TierScorer` that makes per-rung model calls, with a budget and deterministic replay.
- Recalibrate the two cut points and expose them as flags. `DefaultStrengthEpsilon = 0.01` and `DefaultStrengthThreshold = 0.05` are un-calibrated policy constants, inert only because nothing measures. Once a live scorer lands, every REDUNDANT verdict -- hence every auto-filed deletion issue -- hangs off that 0.01, and nothing currently forces a recalibration at that moment.
- `emitAblation` hardcodes `StrengthParams{}`, so the exported tuning surface is unreachable from the CLI.
- `cmd/fak`'s `ablateTierScorer` is documented as "a test swaps in a fake", but no `cmd/fak` test actually does.

**Gate:** do not promote any verdict to auto-filing until the cut points are calibrated against measured data.

records.title: feat(policy): give each swept RATCHET knob a directional amendment rule instead of blanket-gating it as WIDEN
records.body:
Follow-on to the policy-amendment spine (epic #5170).

**Context.** `DiffAmendment` originally computed a direction for only 8 of `adjudicator.Policy`'s 19 exported fields. A reload delta touching only the other 11 returned an empty delta and therefore `AmendmentNone`, which both admission gates (`guard_core_lock.go`, `guard_self_tighten.go`) admit unconditionally with a reason string asserting a falsehood. Under `--core-lock-all` -- the strongest posture -- that admitted changes to `Complain`, `AdvisoryReasons`, `SecretPosture`, `Profile`, `EgressAllowHosts`, and drops of `RedactFields` / `EgressExtraDenyHosts` / `ResearchEgressAllowHosts` / `EgressBlockLists` / `LintWrites` as no-ops. That fail-open has been closed by a reflection `residualAmendmentChanges` sweep that routes any otherwise-unanalyzed changed field to WIDEN (gated), with unregistered fields still landing in Frozen, plus `TestDiffAmendmentCoversEveryPolicyField` so a field added tomorrow cannot silently re-open the hole.

**What remains.** The sweep is correct but blunt: it is deliberately conservative, so a legitimate *tightening* of one of the 11 swept RATCHET knobs is now gated as if it widened. Give each of the 11 its own directional diff rule, keeping the reflection sweep as the backstop for anything still unclassified.

**Acceptance**
- Each of the 11 knobs has a directional rule with a test proving a genuine tighten is admitted and a genuine widen is gated.
- `TestDiffAmendmentCoversEveryPolicyField` still passes; the residual sweep remains as the fail-closed backstop.
- No knob regains an `AmendmentNone` path.

**Note for the `cmd/fak` owner:** `guard_self_tighten.go`'s "exactly eight Field names" comment is now stale, though its conclusion still holds.

records.title: fix(gateway): flush the SSE preamble before the buffered decode on stream:true (#4855 residue)
records.body:
`internal/gateway/ep_stream_stall_test.go` is an untracked, genuinely behavioural witness that currently **FAILS**, and its failure is the proof that a DoD rung of the now-CLOSED #4855 was never actually met.

**Repro**
```
go test ./internal/gateway/ -run '^TestEPStreamingEmitsFirstSSEChunkBeforeCollectiveJoin$' -count=1 -v
```
**Result:** `FAIL 3.01s` — `ep_stream_stall_test.go:135: no HTTP headers/first SSE byte before the EP collective join`. Server log shows `status 200 bytes 1045 duration_ms 3005`: nothing reaches the wire until `Complete` returns.

**Cause.** `agent.InKernelPlanner` implements only `Complete`, so `streamChatLive` (`internal/gateway/stream_proxy.go:36`, called from `http.go:582`) declines the streaming path and falls back to the buffered one, which writes the first byte only after the full decode. On `stream:true` the SSE preamble should be flushed before the buffered decode begins.

**Why this matters.** #4855 is closed, but its rung "endpoint emits a first valid SSE chunk" is demonstrably unmet. The fanout half *did* land (`ep_fanout_test.go:63`); the streaming-preamble half did not. A client on `stream:true` sees a 3-second silence and cannot distinguish it from a stall.

**Fix shape.** Flush headers + the first SSE chunk before entering the buffered decode when `stream:true`, so time-to-first-byte is bounded by admission rather than by decode.

**Note.** The test is not tautological: it drives the real handler over `httptest`, models the EP collective, and every wait is bounded, so it can fail but never hang. The `internal/gateway` package is separately already red from two unrelated tracked failures in `calibration_corpus_drift_test.go`.

records.title: epic(modelroute): three-zone model placement — device, company fleet, vendor — with automatic escalation
records.body:
## The concept

Take a company with 100–500 engineers. Every engineer has a powerful laptop or desktop.
The company also operates its own machines. fak should make those three tiers feel like
**one integrated model**, and place each request on the cheapest rung that can actually
do the work:

1. **Device** — a small model on the engineer's own machine for small local tasks (the
   "haiku/sonnet-class" role): Qwen3.6-class and below.
2. **Fleet** — open-weights models the *company* hosts on its own servers: GLM-5.2-class,
   Kimi-K3-class, Inkling-class.
3. **Vendor** — a third-party frontier lab, used only when the work genuinely needs it.

**The thesis, stated as a falsifiable number:** the bulk of token volume is served by
rungs 1 and 2, and only specifically-identified requests escalate to rung 3. This must
hold *especially* for sub-agents and background work, which are high-volume, low-stakes,
and today go wherever the parent session goes.

This epic is about the **placement and escalation economy**. It is a different axis from
epic #595 (*which* model/ensemble serves an aspect); #595 picks the model, this picks
**where the model runs, and who pays**. The two compose: #595 emits a model id, this
decides its rung.

## What already exists (verified, not aspirational)

- `internal/modelroute` — the routing spine: `Subject → Route() → Decision{Plan}`,
  ensemble `Combine`, version-tagged `Manifest`/`Roster`, and `WorkTier` (work class sets
  a risk *floor*, model capability sets a *ceiling*).
- The account switcher — `Roster{Accounts, Bindings, Default}` resolves a routed model id
  to a `Target`, which stamps `abi.ToolCall.Engine` via `Target.EngineRoute()`.
- The residency floor — `internal/engine` `residencyGate` (adjudicator rank 12) denies a
  tenant-scoped or sensitivity-tagged call whose engine route is remote. Route-*before*-
  adjudicate is already wired: the host writes the chosen model to `abi.ToolCall.Engine`
  before `Kernel.Submit`, so a dispatch-time route cannot fail open.
- The live per-tool-call routing seam — `internal/agent/loop_session.go`
  (`routeToolEngine` / `resolveToolEngine`), mirroring the gateway's `routeEngine`/`resolveRoute`.
- **`PlacementZone` (landed in `c36eabceff08`)** — `device` / `fleet` / `vendor` as a
  closed, ranked ladder, plus `kind: "fleet"` accounts. This is the vocabulary the rest of
  the epic is written in. Before it, the middle rung was *inexpressible*: a company-operated
  GLM server declared `local` was refused (a local account must be loopback-pinned), and
  declared `openai` it became indistinguishable from `api.openai.com` in every downstream
  record — the org got zero attribution for hardware it owns.

Critically, `ZoneFleet.SelfHosted() == true` but `ZoneFleet.OnBox() == false`: naming the
zone changed what fak can **attribute**, deliberately not what it **permits**.

## The gaps this epic closes

Each is verified against the tree at `c36eabceff08`.

**1. Nothing chooses a zone.** The ladder exists and is ranked (`device` 0 → `fleet` 1 →
`vendor` 2) but no policy walks it. Placement today is whatever a human wrote in a binding.

**2. The headline number is unmeasurable on the serving path.**
`(*DualPlanner).RoutesLocal` (`internal/gateway/dual_planner.go:95`) computes the
local-vs-proxy decision per request — and it is discarded before the metric is recorded.
`internal/gateway/gateway.go:2740` calls
`s.metrics.observeInference(comp.Usage.PromptTokens, comp.Usage.CompletionTokens, …)`
with no model and no locality argument; the same conflation is at
`session_admit.go:304` and `messages_stream_passthrough.go:454`. Downstream,
`internal/gatewayusageledger.Counters` — the only durable served-turn token ledger —
carries `InputTokens`/`OutputTokens`/`CachedPromptTokens`/… as flat per-session totals
with **no** model, provider, or zone field. So fak cannot today answer *"what fraction of
our tokens were self-hosted?"* about its own serving path. The information is computed and
destroyed one line apart.

**3. The one shipped stratum classifier is wrong in both directions.**
`internal/sessionaudit.ProviderBucket` (`sessionaudit.go:731`) buckets by **model-id
substring**, but a model *family* does not determine *where it ran*:
- `deepseek*` → `"local / self-hosted"` (`:743`) while the same file prices it from the
  **published DeepSeek API** rate card (`:34`). One turn is reported as costing
  third-party dollars *and* as having been self-hosted.
- `qwen*` → `"local / self-hosted"`, but fak's own shipped roster
  (`examples/model-accounts.example.json`) binds `qwen/qwen3.6-27b` to the **Groq** vendor
  account.
- `glm-5.2` and `kimi-k3` are priced (`:35-36`) yet match no bucket substring, so they land
  in `"UNKNOWN (unpriced bucket)"` — a label that says *unpriced* about two models the same
  file prices. These are exactly the middle-rung models this epic is about.

**4. Savings are unfalsifiable.** `internal/modelroute/cost.go` prices
`local`/`in-kernel`/`on-device`/`kernel` at `{0, 0}`, so `EstimateSavings` can only ever
report a saving. The honest headline is a **token fraction**, not a dollar fraction.

**5. Escalation has no trigger.** `internal/modelroute/outcome.go` keys `Outcome{Cost,
Latency, Quality, Verify}` by `AspectRuleKey{Aspect, Rule}` — **not** by model or zone —
and its journal is in-memory only. `verify.go:67 Verification.Trusted()`
(`None < Judge < Witness`) is a ready-made "was this good enough?" predicate, but nothing
feeds it a placement, and nothing survives the process.

**6. Capability grading measures nothing.** `internal/ablate/model_strength.go:124-139`
`StubTierScorer` is a stub, so every production run grades `UNMEASURED`. "Can the device
rung actually do this class of work?" currently has no evidence behind it.

**7. Sub-agents and background work have no placement policy** — the case the concept
calls out specifically. They inherit the parent's model.

**8. The residency floor does not yet trust a fleet host.** Deliberate: widening it needs
an operator-declared trust boundary (authenticated transport, a named host allowlist), not
a side effect of declaring a zone.

## Child tracks

- **A. Zone-aware placement policy — LANDED** (#5419). `Roster.Place` (`e710bc675`) walks
  the ladder and returns the lowest-ranked zone whose capability ceiling meets the work's
  `WorkTier` floor, with a per-rung `Ladder []ZoneVerdict` recording why each cheaper rung
  lost. Two rules are executable, not aspirational: the floor is fixed by the WORK
  (`TierPolicy.Admit`), and **an UNMEASURED capability may not descend the ladder** — an
  asserted number cannot win a cheap rung, though it may still serve as the vendor
  fallback. `Roster.PlaceSubject` + `ClassOf` (`2183d4edc`) then close the
  `Subject → WorkClass` joint that `Place` needed and `Route` never supplied.
  Comparisons go through `WorkTier.MeetsRequirement` throughout;
  `TestInvertedTierComparisonWouldBeCaught` fails if anyone substitutes a raw `>=`
  (mutation-verified: the substitution puts a 4B laptop model on both the ultra-hard and
  the security/release work).
  **The oracle — `fak route --place` (`a8ba9fa29`).** Walks the ladder for one subject
  against a real roster and prints the rung, the per-rung verdicts, and *why* a cheaper
  rung lost. Run against fak's own shipped roster it reproduces the epic's thesis in one
  screen: with nothing measured, routine work escalates to `zone=vendor` with
  `escalated-past-cheaper-zone`; supply a measurement and the identical subject places on
  `zone=device upstream=qwen/qwen3.6-4b`. It also forced a source-level honesty fix —
  `Placement.Measured` (`e1fdbaff6`), without which the surface renders the *unmeasured*
  zero-value tier as `T0 (OVER-TIER)`, asserting both a capability and a waste finding
  about a model nobody graded.
  **Superseded — the dispatch path now calls `Place`.** This bullet used to read "nothing
  on the live dispatch path calls `Place` yet ... the identified seam has no zone notion at
  all", and both halves are now out of date: `cmd/fak/dispatch_tick.go:559` calls
  `applyRungPlacement`, which resolves a rung through `roster.Place` and pins it via
  `dispatch_rung_pin.go`'s `modelSourceRung` — written as a step AFTER
  `resolveWorkerModelPolicy` rather than another branch inside it, so the precedence chain
  (explicit > lane > bench-gate > tier profile > work-class > seat-default) is unchanged and
  only a seat-default worker — one nothing else pinned — is placed.
  **What remains true is narrower, and is a deliberate posture rather than missing work:**
  it moves no traffic BY DEFAULT, because it is gated twice and both gates fail closed.
  `FLEET_DISPATCH_RUNG_PLACEMENT` is off unless set, and `FLEET_DISPATCH_RUNG_ACCOUNTS` has
  **no default at all** — turning the ladder on while declaring nothing places nothing.
  That second gate is the honest one: `Roster.Place` answers which rung is *cheapest*, not
  whether the worker about to launch can open a socket to it, and `WorkerLaunch` carries no
  base URL and no credential, so an unreachable pin is a slot that walls on `model_unknown`
  rather than a saving. An allowlist defaulting to "everything" would read as protection
  while enforcing nothing. So the remaining gap on this track is not code — it is that
  reachability is an operator ASSERTION rather than a verified fact, which is exactly what
  track G (#5421) would make verifiable, and that is the honest precondition for this
  being on by default.
- **B. Self-hosted token fraction (the headline metric)** — #5418. Two halves:
  - **The arithmetic — LANDED** (`5bc4e5288`). `sessionaudit.FoldSelfHostedShare` computes the fraction
    over a real corpus and reports the **coverage** that qualifies it. Unattributable
    volume is scored on NEITHER side (folding it into the denominator would punish us for
    our own missing wiring; into the numerator would claim an unprovable saving), and a
    corpus with no placement signal reports `UNKNOWN`, never `0%`.
  - **The serving path — LANDED end to end** (`6526117f3` → `9ac57b662` → `8c9224d6a`
    → `62a61fe9a` → `ec1790d60`). The decision computed at `dual_planner.go:95` now
    survives to disk and back out through a command. `servingLocality` carries it from
    `selectChatPlanner`'s four exhaustive modes — dual resolves per request through the
    planner's own `RoutesLocal`, so there is one definition of "this id decodes in-kernel"
    and the metric cannot drift from the routing — into `observeInferenceServed`, into six
    `omitempty` `Counters` fields, across the `gatewayUsageCounters` bridge, up through
    `auditusage.GatewayRollup.SelfHosted`, to one line of `fak audit usage`.

    Three properties are executable rather than intended:
    (1) **classification consumes the REQUESTED model** — the identical input `pick()`
    routed on, not the model the response reported, because an in-kernel decode need not
    echo an id back and an empty one would then read as vendor;
    (2) **the two groups are disjoint SUBSETS of the unsplit totals**, accumulated in the
    same observation and never derived by subtracting one from the other — that shortcut
    books every unclassified turn as self-hosted, which is the single direction of error
    that flatters us — so the shortfall measures coverage honestly, and no surface prints
    the share without it;
    (3) **absent ≠ zero**, all the way to the wire. `observeInference` kept its arity so
    untaught call sites report an honest unknown instead of being defaulted into a side by
    a zero argument, and an unclassified corpus serializes no share key at all rather than
    a `0.0` a reader would chart as "self-hosts nothing" — the opposite finding from the
    earned `0.0` an all-vendor corpus produces, which does serialize.

    **The number, now measured rather than asserted.** On this box today `fak audit usage`
    reports: `self-hosted: NOT INSTRUMENTED — no row among 3248 recorded which side served
    it (17662384 output tokens unattributed; this is not a measured zero)`. That is this
    track's opening gap, restated by a command instead of by an epic, and it becomes a real
    fraction as soon as one session runs on the new build. The bridge is pinned by a
    reflective witness — add a seventh split field to `Counters` and forget the literal in
    `gatewayUsageCounters` and the test fails, because `omitempty` would otherwise hide the
    omission from every consumer forever.
- **C. Honest stratum classification — LANDED.** `ProviderBucket` no longer asserts
  placement from a model name: an open-weights family reports
  `open-weights (placement unknown)`, `BucketForPlacement(model, zone)` takes a real
  `PlacementZone`, and `BucketIsSelfHosted` returns `(selfHosted, known)` so
  unattributable volume stays out of both sides of the fraction.
  `TestPricedModelsAreNeverBucketedSelfHosted` makes the rule executable and total over
  the rate card. *(Gap 3.)*
- **D. Escalation ladder + outcome feedback — LANDED end to end: the record, the rule, the
  classifier, the actuator that spends against them, and the surface that reads the spend
  back.** The feedback half needs somewhere for outcomes to live, and
  `modelroute.TurnOutcome` / `AppendTurnOutcome` / `ReadTurnOutcomes` / `FoldTurnOutcomes`
  (`51869cf3f`) is that place: an append-only journal, one JSON object per turn, folded
  into the same `ClassEvidence` the track-F grader already consumes and keyed by
  `(model, class, verification)`. It is written to **lose** evidence rather than invent it,
  because each alternative inflates a claim:
  (1) a repeated `id` is counted once — replaying a file is the cheapest possible way to
  manufacture a grade, and the same 20 successes appended three times must not read as 60;
  (2) an undated row cannot be shown to be inside a freshness window — capability is a
  property of a model AS DEPLOYED, and the exclusion is counted *apart* from a stale row
  because one needs a wider window and the other needs a producer that stamps its rows;

    four separate numbers because they are four different missing wires with four different
    fixes.
  - **What names the class — `dispatchtick.WorkClassForIssue` (`e4590079d`).** The producer
    takes `Class` with no default, and this is the one place that answers it: from the issue's
    own tier labels, read through the **same parser that chose the slot's launch profile**, so
    a model cannot be launched as one class and graded as another. Two answers are
    deliberately empty and stay distinguishable — an untagged issue grades nothing (the fix is
    triage; calling untagged work "routine" is how a small model earns a rung off a backlog
    nobody triaged), and a coordination/PM slot grades nothing (the fix is a vocabulary with a
    coordination class; mapping it to the cheapest existing one would let a model earn the
    routine *implementation* rung by labelling issues). Nothing in the path can mint
    `ClassSecurityRelease`. Mutation-verified: 12/12.
  - **The live caller — `cmd/fak/dispatch_placement_evidence.go` (`1368adc77`), closing
    #5428.** The gap
    this track kept naming: every pure piece was correct and **nothing ran them**, so a live
    fleet's journal was empty. Now `fak dispatch tick` resolves both facts at prepare time,
    writes them beside each worker log as `.workclass` / `.zone` sidecars at spawn — both are
    *point-in-time* (labels get re-tagged, rosters get re-bound), so a later sweep reads what
    was true at launch instead of re-deriving a present-tense answer about a finished slot —
    and the witness sweep folds them into `turn-outcomes.jsonl`, the journal
    `fak route --place --outcomes` already grades from. Both sidecars are read back through
    **allowlist** parsers derived from the launch-bucket table (`1bad910d1`), so a truncated
    or hand-edited file grades nothing rather than picking its own rung, and a file naming
    `security-release-destructive` is refused by construction. Double counting is structural
    rather than hopeful: the sweep skips any slot already carrying a `.witness` sidecar, so a
    finished worker is journalled exactly once however many ticks run. The seam is opt-in
    (`FLEET_DISPATCH_PLACEMENT_EVIDENCE`); off, a fleet's payload keys, runs directory and
    journal are byte-identical to before. Mutation-verified: 8/8 (wiring) + 6/6 (sidecar
    grammar).
  - **Still open:** `internal/ablate/model_strength.go:124` `StubTierScorer` still grades
    nothing — the ablation path keeps its own scorer and does not yet read this journal. And
    a fleet only produces rows for slots it can both *pin* and *classify*, so the corpus grows
    at the rate the backlog is triaged and models are pinned; the four refusal counters are
    what tell an operator which of the two is the bottleneck. *(Gap 6.)*
- **G. Fleet trust boundary** — #5421. Operator-declared allowlist + authenticated
  transport that lets the residency floor treat a named org host as inside the boundary.
  Enforcement change; must stay fail-closed. Filed partly so nobody assumes declaring
  `kind: fleet` already granted this — it does not. *(Gap 8.)*
- **H. Fleet health, capacity, and failover — the GATE has landed; the prober has not.**
  The ladder decided on two static facts about a candidate: the tier its capability was
  graded at, and whether that grade was measured. Neither says whether anything is
  currently answering. So a company GPU host that reboots, OOMs, or loses power keeps
  being handed work — from the ladder's point of view nothing changed, and the artifact
  that exists to answer "why did this land here?" reports the placement as fine while
  every dispatch fails.
  - **The liveness gate — `Roster.PlaceWithServing` (`8e9e0943c`).** A
    `ServingReport` is an injected, credential-free snapshot of what is answering; the
    walk passes over candidates the operator's own probes say are not. It is injected
    and carries its own `AsOfUnix` rather than reading a clock, so placement stays pure
    — same roster, same candidates, same report, same placement, on any machine at any
    time. `Place` now delegates with an EMPTY report, which is the point: a fleet with
    no prober takes the identical code path to the identical placement, so "liveness
    changes nothing until someone measures liveness" is a property of the definition
    rather than a default someone could flip. Keyed by BOUND MODEL, not by zone: a
    fleet rung is several hosts, and a zone-keyed signal would take the whole rung out
    because one box rebooted, sending every token to a vendor to route around a machine
    whose neighbor was idle. Per model, the ladder tries the next candidate ON THE SAME
    RUNG first — failing over within the rung before failing over up it is the
    difference between a resilient fleet and an expensive one. Three rules bound what a
    snapshot may do. **Silence is only meaningful where the snapshot claims coverage**:
    inside a declared rung, a candidate nobody reported on is UNKNOWN and passed over,
    because reading a crashed prober's silence as health is a fail-open; outside it,
    absence gates nothing. **An observation that exists is always honored, coverage or
    not** — coverage answers "is silence meaningful?" and nothing else, so a report
    naming a host DOWN still keeps work off it even if its rung was never declared,
    which is what stops a config typo from reaching the exact failure the gate exists
    to prevent. **Freshness is fail-closed, and so is every way of not having it**:
    under a declared bound, too old, no timestamp, no as-of stamp to measure against,
    and stamped AFTER the report containing it all read the same, the last because a
    producer whose clock runs ahead would otherwise pin a rung open forever and nobody
    files a bug for "the gate silently stopped working". That third rule has a real
    cost — a dead prober escalates covered rungs to a vendor that charges money — and
    it is still the right side, because it is the side the ladder can EXPLAIN: a bill
    that rises with a `zone-serving-stale` token in the artifact is a diagnosis, while
    requests failing against a rung the artifact calls healthy is not. DEGRADED is
    recorded and NOT acted on: a loaded host is still serving, and shedding work at the
    first sign of queueing would abandon the fleet in the busy hour that carries the
    bulk of the tokens — whether saturation should cost money is an operator's policy
    call, not the placer's. Two smaller calls: the liveness check runs LAST, after the
    measured and tier gates, so a candidate that fails both reports the PERMANENT
    reason — a transient one would make the same misconfiguration diagnose differently
    depending on when you looked, and rebooting the host would not move the placement;
    and `FailedOver` is carried separately from `Escalated`, because "a cheaper rung
    could not do this work" and "a rung that could have was routed around" want
    different fixes, and without the distinction an operator reads vendor spend as work
    that needed a vendor and hunts a capability problem that does not exist while the
    dead host stays dead. An invalid snapshot is an ERROR, never an ignored one — every
    refusal in `Validate` is a case where ignoring the malformed field would leave the
    operator believing a rung was gated when it was not, which is worse than no gate
    because it is believed. 19 tests, mutation-verified 27/27.
  - **Reachable since `e9b2c5538788`:** `fak route --place --serving FILE` is the first
    input to this gate, at the rung `--evidence`/`--outcomes` took for capability. It also
    closes a fail-open neither half could see alone: `Validate` cannot see the roster and
    the ladder never asks about a non-candidate, so an observation filed under an id the
    roster does not bind was honored *nowhere*, silently. Both halves are now named —
    `UNBOUND` (an observation nothing binds) and `SILENT` (a covered candidate nothing
    observed) — and each unbound id resolves to the candidate whose upstream name it is.
  - **Still open:** nothing *produces* a snapshot automatically, so nothing moves by
    itself; the producer reads the network and a clock, and stays its own unit. What
    changed is that it is now a wiring job rather than a code change. Also open: a
    cooldown, so a host that just failed is not retried on the next tick; and capacity as
    a *load* signal distinct from `RerouteCapacity`'s static model-size and context-window
    fit.

## Related work (reference, do not duplicate)

#595 (routing spine — picks the model, this picks the rung) · #5315 (Org Policy Plane —
the admin surface a fleet policy would be published through) · #5330 (enterprise API
accounts) · #2528 (live multi-account dispatch) · #4867 (Qwen3.6) · #4352 (GLM-5.2) ·
#600 · #3006 · #2902 · #2861 · #3521 · #3575 · #4588 · #4632

## The measured baseline (2026-07-26)

`fak session-audit audit --all --since-days 30` over this fleet's own transcripts, using
the fold landed under track B:

| Placement | Turns | Output tok | Cache-read tok |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| self-hosted (device + fleet) | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| vendor API | 14,535 | 20,430,331 | 1,469,408,694 |
| unattributable (no placement signal) | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| non-billed (harness, not inference) | 843 | 0 | 0 |

**Self-hosted share of attributed output = 0.0%, over 100.0% coverage.** 20.4M output
tokens, 1.47B cache-read tokens, $11,622.24 estimated, 30 days.

Read it honestly: this corpus is Claude Code session transcripts, so it is Anthropic by
construction and 0% is the *expected* answer, not a surprise finding. What it establishes
is (a) the number is now computed rather than asserted, (b) coverage is 100%, so the
number will be believable when it stops being zero, and (c) every later track has a
concrete floor to move rather than a claim to make.

## Done means

A company can declare its three rungs in one roster; routine work and sub-agents land on
device or fleet without anyone choosing per-request; escalation to a vendor is triggered by
a recorded signal rather than a default; and `fak` can print the self-hosted token fraction
for a real fleet from a durable record — a number that can come out *low*, and be believed
when it comes out high.

records.title: Arm the guard allow SESSION-scope drop at boot/teardown so `--session` is actually ephemeral (#5180 follow-on)
records.body:
`fak guard allow --session <tool>` lands a widening in the narrowest allow layer and the read
path honors it (witnessed: `fak guard allow --list` shows the session layer at precedence 2, and
`TestGuardAllowWritePathForScopeRoutesSessionAwayFromDurableLayers`). **The ephemeral half does
not happen.** Two independent gaps:

### 1. No boot caller for the drop

`armGuardAllowSessionScopeTeardown()` and `dropGuardAllowSessionScope()`
(`cmd/fak/guard_allow_scope.go`) have no production call site. Their contract is already
witnessed by `cmd/fak/guard_allow_session_scope_teardown_test.go` (the drop removes ONLY the
armed session file and leaves repo/user intact; an unarmed drop is a no-op; the drop
self-disarms so a double teardown cannot delete the next launch's file).

Intended wiring, both in `cmd/fak/guard.go`:

- after `guardTraceID = resolveGuardSessionID(...)` (`guard.go:744`):
  ```go
  setGuardAllowSessionScopeID(guardTraceID)
  armGuardAllowSessionScopeTeardown()
  ```
- beside the interactive-session-registry defer (`guard.go:757`):
  ```go
  defer func() { _ = dropGuardAllowSessionScope() }()
  ```

Open design question for the owner: whether the drop should also run on the crash /
WT-RDP-teardown paths that cannot execute a `defer` (the interactive-session registry already
treats that as a distinct case).

### 2. No session id reaches the layer

Nothing calls `setGuardAllowSessionScopeID` in production and nothing exports
`$FAK_GUARD_SESSION_ID`, so `guardAllowSessionID()` always returns `""` and every launch shares
`<repo>/.fak/guard/sessions/current.allow.json`. Even with (1) fixed, two concurrent guarded
sessions on one checkout would share — and drop — each other's session layer. Fixing (1) as
written above also fixes this, since it feeds `guardTraceID` in; the guard should additionally
export `$FAK_GUARD_SESSION_ID` to the child so an out-of-process `fak guard allow --session`
beside a live session hits the same file.

### Regression to watch for

Until both land, the code, the `--session` flag help, `guardAllowUsage()` and the `--list`
legend all state plainly that the drop is **NOT ARMED** and that the widening persists — that
honesty landed in `fix(cmd): stop the guard allow session scope from claiming an ephemerality it
does not perform (fak cmd)`. Reverting those notes without doing the wiring is the regression to
watch for.

Follow-on to #5180 (epic #5170).

records.title: feat(gateway): record the self-hosted token fraction on the serving path
records.body:
Track **B** of epic #5416.

## The problem

fak's own serving path cannot answer the question epic #5416 is scored on — *what
fraction of our tokens were served on hardware we operate?* The information is computed
and then thrown away one line later.

`(*DualPlanner).RoutesLocal` (`internal/gateway/dual_planner.go:95`) already decides,
per request, whether the turn is served by the in-kernel/local planner or proxied to a
third party. Nothing carries that decision into the usage record:

```go
// internal/gateway/gateway.go:2740
s.metrics.observeInference(comp.Usage.PromptTokens, comp.Usage.CompletionTokens,
    comp.Usage.CachedPromptTokens(), comp.Usage.CacheCreationInputTokens,
    comp.FinishReason, dur)
```

No model argument, no locality argument. The same conflation is at
`internal/gateway/session_admit.go:304` and
`internal/gateway/messages_stream_passthrough.go:454`.

Downstream, `internal/gatewayusageledger.Counters` — the only *durable* served-turn token
ledger — carries `InputTokens`, `OutputTokens`, `CachedPromptTokens`,
`CacheCreationTokens`, … as flat per-session totals. There is no model, provider, or zone
field anywhere in the struct. A session that ran 90% on a company GPU and 10% on a vendor
API is indistinguishable from its exact inverse.

## Why the obvious workarounds don't work

- **Don't tag `Provenance`.** It is session-level, and a session legitimately mixes
  strata — that is the entire design. The split belongs on `Counters`.
- **Don't derive it from the model id.** That was `internal/sessionaudit.ProviderBucket`'s
  approach and it was wrong in both directions (fixed under track C): open-weights
  families are servable from company hardware *or* a vendor API, so the id cannot settle
  it.
- **Don't report dollars.** `internal/modelroute/cost.go` prices
  `local`/`in-kernel`/`on-device`/`kernel` at `{0, 0}`, so a dollar-denominated saving is
  unfalsifiable — it can only ever come out positive. The honest headline is a **token
  fraction**.

## Proposed slice

1. Add a self-hosted split beside the existing totals in
   `internal/gatewayusageledger.Counters` (`ledger.go:69-75`), e.g.
   `LocalInputTokens` / `LocalOutputTokens uint64` with `json:",omitempty"`. `omitempty`
   matters: existing rows stay byte-compatible, and an **absent** field must read as *not
   instrumented*, not as *zero local* — otherwise every historical session silently
   becomes evidence that nothing was self-hosted.
2. Thread the locality already available from `RoutesLocal` into a new metrics entry point
   beside `observeInference` (`internal/gateway/metrics.go:620-669`), called from
   `gateway.go:2740` and the two sibling sites above.
3. Classify through `sessionaudit.BucketIsSelfHosted`, honoring its two-valued
   `(selfHosted, known)` contract: unattributed tokens must stay out of **both** sides of
   the fraction rather than being scored as vendor.

## Done means

`fak` can print a self-hosted token fraction for a real fleet from a durable record, the
number can come out **low**, and an uninstrumented session is visibly uninstrumented
rather than silently counted as 0%.

records.title: feat(modelroute): choose the cheapest placement zone that meets the work tier
records.body:
Track **A** of epic #5416.

## The problem

The placement ladder exists and is ranked, but nothing walks it. `PlacementZone`
(`internal/modelroute/zone.go`, landed in `c36eabceff08`) gives `device` (rank 0) →
`fleet` (1) → `vendor` (2), and `Zones()` returns them in ladder order. Placement today is
still whatever a human hand-wrote into a `Binding`. There is no policy that says *put this
work on the cheapest rung that can actually do it*.

## What the policy has to respect

**The floor/ceiling asymmetry is already in the codebase and must be routed through, not
re-derived.** In `internal/modelroute/tierpolicy.go`, `WorkTier` numbers run T0 = most
demanding = **lowest** number, and the two constraints point in opposite directions:

- the **work class** sets a risk **floor** (this work may not be done below tier X)
- the **model capability** sets a **ceiling** (this model cannot serve above tier Y)

So the comparison must go through `WorkTier.MeetsRequirement`. A raw `<` on the tier int
reads backwards and will silently place demanding work on the cheapest rung — the exact
failure that makes an automatic placer worse than a hand-written binding.

## Proposed slice

1. A pure function over the existing vocabulary: given a `Subject`/`Decision` and a
   `Roster`, choose the lowest-`Rank()` zone whose bound account can meet the work's tier
   floor; fall back up the ladder when no account in that zone qualifies.
2. Keep it **separate from `Route()`**. `Route()` answers *which model*; this answers
   *which rung*. Epic #595 owns the first axis. Composing them beats entangling them.
3. Fail toward the higher rung when capability evidence is missing, and say so — an
   unmeasured device model must not be assumed capable. (Track F replaces the
   `StubTierScorer` at `internal/ablate/model_strength.go:124-139` that makes every
   production run grade `UNMEASURED`; until then the fallback is the only honest default.)
4. Pure and stdlib-only: `internal/modelroute` is architest tier 1 and imports nothing
   internal.

## Explicit non-goals

- No health, load, or failover signal — the account switcher is a static binding resolver
  by design (track H).
- No change to what the residency floor permits (track G).

## Done means

Routine work lands on `device` or `fleet` without anyone choosing per-request, the choice
is a comparison on declared values rather than a string switch, and a demanding task still
reaches the rung it needs.

records.title: feat(agent): give sub-agents and background turns their own placement decision
records.body:
Track **E** of epic #5416.

## The problem

Sub-agents and background turns inherit the parent session's model. The concept behind
epic #5416 calls these out specifically, and for good reason: in a 100–500 engineer shop
they are the **high-volume, low-stakes** majority of traffic — file searches, greps,
classification probes, summarizations, scouted lookups — and they are exactly the work a
device- or fleet-class model can serve. Sending them to a frontier vendor because the
parent happened to be there is where the token budget silently goes.

This is the single largest lever on the epic's thesis ("the bulk of token usage gets
covered by these self-hosted items"), because it moves volume rather than individual
requests.

## Where the seam already is

The per-tool-call routing seam is live and does not need to be invented:

- `internal/agent/loop_session.go` — `WithRouteManifest(*modelroute.Manifest)`,
  `WithRouteAccounts(*modelroute.Roster)`, `routeToolEngine(tool)`,
  `resolveToolEngine(tool)`, which roster-resolves to `Target.EngineRoute()` and fails
  loud on an unresolvable id.
- The gateway mirrors it with `routeEngine` / `resolveRoute`.

**Route-before-adjudicate is already the contract**: the host writes the chosen model to
`abi.ToolCall.Engine` *before* `Kernel.Submit`, so the residency floor sees the real
destination. A placement decision made at dispatch time instead would fail open. Any work
here must keep that ordering.

## Proposed slice

1. Give a sub-agent / background turn its **own** placement decision rather than
   inheriting the parent's, defaulting to the lowest rung that clears its work tier
   (track A supplies the chooser).
2. Treat the parent's zone as an input, never a floor — a sub-agent spawned from a vendor
   turn should still be able to land on `device`.
3. Preserve the existing fail-loud behavior on unresolvable ids; a placement policy must
   not turn a misconfiguration into a silent fallback.

## Open question worth settling early

Whether "background" is a property of the turn, the session, or the tool call. `routeAspect`
already distinguishes aspects, so the cheapest correct answer is probably an aspect rather
than a new orthogonal flag — but that should be decided deliberately, not by whichever call
site is edited first.

## Done means

A sub-agent sweep that today burns frontier tokens runs on a company GPU or the engineer's
own machine, the escalation to a vendor is a recorded decision rather than an inherited
default, and track B's fraction can show the change.

records.title: feat(engine): operator-declared trust boundary for org-operated fleet hosts
records.body:
Track **G** of epic #5416. **Enforcement change — must stay fail-closed.**

## The state today, stated precisely

Declaring a company-operated server (`kind: "fleet"`) changed what fak can **attribute**,
deliberately **not** what it **permits**:

- `ZoneFleet.SelfHosted()` is `true` — its tokens count as served on hardware the org owns.
- `ZoneFleet.OnBox()` is `false` — so `Target.Remote()` stays `true`, and the residency
  gate (`internal/engine`, adjudicator rank 12) still **denies** a tenant-scoped or
  sensitivity-tagged payload routed there.

`"fleet"` is deliberately absent from `localRoute`'s on-box family list in
`internal/engine/engine.go`, and two tests pin that this stays true:
`TestFleetZoneStaysRemoteAtTheFloor` and `TestFleetTargetIsRemoteToTheFloor`.

**This issue exists so nobody assumes otherwise.** A reasonable person reading "self-hosted"
would expect a sensitive payload to be allowed onto company hardware. It is not, and it
should not be until the trust boundary is actually declared and verified.

## Why "the org owns it" is not sufficient

`ZoneFleet` today means only *an operator wrote `kind: fleet` in a roster*. That is an
assertion, not a boundary. Nothing verifies the endpoint is reachable only inside the org
network, that the transport is authenticated, or that the host is one the org actually
operates. `kind: fleet` currently requires just an explicit, parseable, non-loopback
`http(s)` `base_url` — and notably does **not** require a `cred_env`, because org-operated
servers on private networks commonly have no API key. A plain `http://` endpoint named in
a config file is not a trust boundary.

## What a real widening needs

1. An **operator-declared** allowlist of fleet hosts — the trust must come from the
   operator's policy, not from the account kind.
2. **Authenticated transport** to a host on that list.
3. A floor change that keeps the failure mode closed: a route the floor cannot place must
   read *remote*, never *on-box*. The current classifier is fail-closed by construction
   and must stay that way.
4. The tier-1 mirror stays in sync — `modelroute.IsRemoteRoute` duplicates the on-box
   family list because `internal/modelroute` sits below `internal/engine` and cannot
   import it. `TestTierOneRouteMirrorAgreesWithTheFloor` runs both classifiers over one
   corpus; a family added on one side only is a test failure rather than a fail-open.

## Relationship to #5315

The Org Policy Plane is the natural place for a fleet-host allowlist to be **administered
and distributed**. This issue is the **enforcement** half at the floor; #5315 is the
administration half. They should land in that order — an allowlist nothing enforces is
worse than none, because it reads as protection.

## Done means

An operator can declare specific authenticated org hosts as inside the trust boundary, the
floor admits a sensitive payload to exactly those and nothing else, and an undeclared or
unverifiable fleet host is still denied.

records.title: Move the lease-write publish out of the leaseWriteMu critical section, and cover the endpoint wiring with a cmd/fak test
records.body:
`cmd/fak/leasewrite_endpoint.go` landed in `f02811ab5` — it supplies the missing `init()` that
calls `gateway.SetLeaseWriteFunc`, so `POST /v1/leases/{acquire,renew,release}` stops refusing as
unconfigured. Before that commit the handler, the `leaseWriteMu` single-arbiter serialization, the
route at `internal/gateway/http.go:159`, a package test and the `docs/fak/openapi.yaml` contract had
all shipped in `fec8da6f7`, but a whole-tree grep found **zero callers of `SetLeaseWriteFunc`**
outside the gateway package and its own test — `leaseWriteFn` was nil in every real binary, so the
documented write plane 404'd everywhere.

Two follow-ons were identified during triage and deliberately **not** bundled into that commit:

### 1. `publishAcceptedLease` does a `git push` while the gateway holds `leaseWriteMu`

`publishAcceptedLease` (`cmd/fak/leasewrite_endpoint.go:126`) pushes the local
`refs/fak/locks/*` namespace to origin (plane 0) so offline nodes converge via a plain
`git fetch`. It runs on the accepted-write path, **inside** the `leaseWriteMu` critical section
that serializes the arbiter. A network round trip under the single-arbiter mutex serializes every
concurrent lease write behind the slowest push.

This is a throughput property, not a correctness bug — the push is explicitly best-effort and a
push failure is swallowed, so the arbitrated verdict still stands. Worth deciding whether the
publish should move outside the mutex (or onto a queue / goroutine) before the endpoint carries
real fleet traffic.

### 2. No `cmd/fak`-side test

The wiring has no test in `cmd/fak`. Its already-shipped read-plane twin
(`cmd/fak/leaseplane_endpoint.go`, same injection shape over the same `leasePlaneDir()` store) has
none either, so this matches the established bar rather than falling below it — but a regression
test that asserts the `init()` actually installs the hook would catch a silent un-wiring, which is
exactly the failure mode that left the write plane dead until now.

Follow-on to `fec8da6f7` / `f02811ab5`.

records.title: Wire the --core-lock-all launch posture onto the landed self-tighten gate (drop the duplicate verdict)
records.body:
The pure half of the session-wide ratchet posture (#5175, epic #5170 Track C) exists as untracked
WIP in `cmd/fak/guard_core_lock.go` plus a 4-test sibling: `stripCoreLockAllFlag` peels the flag
out of argv, and `coreLockAllReloadVerdict` classifies a proposed floor through the shipped
`policy.DiffAmendment` engine, admitting only None/Tighten and failing closed on anything
unclassified. Every symbol it references resolves against `origin/main`, so it would compile today.

What is missing is **both ends of the wiring**: nothing registers the flag or sets the
`guardCoreLockAll` package var at guard launch, and no reload/overlay path calls
`coreLockAllReloadVerdict` — so the posture is currently inert, and the file's own comment about
being peeled off "at the guard entrypoint" describes a call site that does not exist.

**Next checkable step:** find the live overlay/reload admission seam (neighbours worth reading are
`cmd/fak/guard_allow_watcher.go` and `cmd/fak/guard_allow_proposals.go`), add one call plus one flag
registration in `guard.go`, then extend the test to drive the verdict *through that seam* rather
than calling it directly.

Triaged 2026-07-26; the WIP file is untracked in the shared checkout and was deliberately not
landed, since landing an inert flag would ship a posture the binary does not perform.

records.title: Expose the guard capability floor's widen-drift report as a reachable `fak guard policy` subcommand
records.body:
`cmd/fak/guard_policy_diff.go` (untracked WIP, #5173 / epic #5170 Track A3) implements the
widen-drift answer to "how does the floor I am RUNNING differ from the floor the binary SHIPPED,
and did any of that drift loosen the guard?" — `policyDiffReport` classifies the
shipped-vs-effective delta through the shipped `policy.DiffAmendment` registry into
FROZEN/WIDENED/TIGHTENED buckets and returns a gateable bool, and `runGuardPolicyDiff` wraps it with
exit 0/1/2 so CI can gate on widening drift. Three unit tests cover the pure renderer and all
referenced symbols resolve against `origin/main`, including the 4-value `loadGuardCapabilityFloor`
destructure (its in-file NOTE worrying about a 5th return is stale — `guard_startup.go:201` still
returns 4).

**The blocker is not this file:** there is no `fak guard policy <verb>` subcommand router anywhere
in `origin/main`, and the already-landed sibling `runGuardPolicyExplain` (#5172) is likewise called
only from its own test. Two orphaned functions, one missing router.

**Next checkable step:** add the `guard policy` verb table in `guard.go` and route both `explain`
and `diff` through it, converting two orphaned functions into one reachable operator surface. The
checkable witness is an end-to-end test that invokes the verb through `cmdGuard`-level argv and

records.title: Carry a witnessed look-ahead lesson across the compaction boundary instead of losing or re-poisoning the reset
records.body:
Untracked WIP in `cmd/fak/guard_lookahead.go` (#5207, epic #5202) builds the consumer half of the
look-ahead reset: a base-SHA-keyed lesson channel that goes stale the moment trunk moves, a renderer
that leads with the lesson's witnessed rung (W3 fact vs W2 risk), and a SessionStart pickup that
injects a fresh lesson only when the hook payload's source is `compact`. Five unit tests cover it and
every symbol the implementation references resolves against `origin/main`.

**Three gaps block landing.**

1. The only production call site (`guard_sessionstart.go:112`, plus the `runGuardSessionStart` →
   `runGuardSessionStartHook` stdin-carrying split it needs) is an **uncommitted** working-tree edit
   that also bundles an unrelated unlanded negframe change, and the sibling test depends on that
   unshipped `runGuardSessionStartHook` symbol — so the test does not compile against committed
   trunk.
2. The file's header claims the PreCompact admission gate is "REAL and wired", but
   `maybeSpawnLookaheadRolloutFailOpen` has zero callers and `guard_precompact.go` is untouched. That
   claim should be corrected or the call added.
3. The producer — the transcript-fork transport plus the rollout runner that would witness an outcome
   and distill a lesson — is explicitly unbuilt, so the channel can never be non-empty in production.

**Next checkable step:** split the SessionStart signature change out as its own small landed commit
and re-run `go test ./cmd/fak -run 'Lookahead|SessionStart'` against committed trunk. Only then is the
pickup half independently shippable behind an empty channel.

Triaged 2026-07-26. Note for anyone landing `cmd/fak/guard_sessionstart.go`: it calls
`lookaheadLessonForCompact`, which is defined **only** in this untracked file. Landing
`guard_sessionstart.go` alone makes the trunk compile-red and hard-refuses every lane's push — the two
must land together, or neither.

records.title: feat(modelroute): produce capability evidence from real turns so the grader has something to grade
records.body:
Track **F** of epic #5416 — the open half.

## What already landed

The **fold** and the **surface** are shipped and mutation-verified:

- `modelroute.GradeCapability` / `GradeCandidates` (`b6d8e661a`) turn observed
  `ClassEvidence{Class, Attempts, Successes, Verify}` into a `Grade` a `Candidate` can
  carry down the placement ladder — or honestly decline to. Self-reported outcomes are
  refused (and *reported* as refused); an unrecognised class label cannot mint a grade
  through `PolicyFor`'s conservative T0 default; a grade is the **floor** of the work
  observed, never its optimal tier; failing every bar is `UNMEASURED` with a reason, not a
  grade of the worst tier. `GradeFloor` defaults to 20 independently verified attempts at
  80%.
- `fak route --place --evidence FILE` grades a whole roster from a file of outcomes and
  reports what the evidence bought *and what it did not*
  (`no-trusted-evidence` / `insufficient-samples` / `below-success-floor`).

## The gap

**Nothing produces `ClassEvidence`.** `internal/ablate/model_strength.go:124`
`StubTierScorer` still grades nothing, so on the live tree every candidate is `UNMEASURED`,
and rule 2 of `Roster.Place` (an unmeasured capability may not descend the ladder) means
**every** placement resolves to the vendor rung. That is the correct fail-closed behaviour
and it is also why no other track in the epic can move real traffic yet: wiring dispatch,
sub-agents, or the gateway to `Place` today would change nothing at all.

## What has to be true of a producer

1. **Provenance is not optional.** Every emitted row carries a `Verification`. The two
   sources already in the tree are a DOS git witness (`VerifyWitness` — the work
   demonstrably shipped) and a judge score (`VerifyJudge`). A turn that ended with the
   model saying it succeeded carries `VerifyNone` and must still be emitted — it is
   counted as *refused*, which is a different and more useful report than silence.
2. **Class is attributed, not inferred from the model.** The class must come from the work
   (a declared `work_class` label, `ClassOf`'s subject classification), never from which
   model served it — inferring the class from the model is how a cheap model gets graded on
   the easy work it was *given because it was cheap*.
3. **Per (model, class), not per model.** The grade is "the most demanding class this model
   cleared"; a producer that flattens classes cannot express that.
4. **Durable.** `internal/modelroute/outcome.go`'s journal is in-memory only (gap 5), so a
   producer needs a record that survives the process — this overlaps track D and should be
   designed with it rather than twice.

## Candidate seams (unverified — pick one and say why)

- `internal/sessionaudit` already folds real transcripts and keys `PerModel` by raw model
  id; it has volume but no class attribution and no independent success signal.
- DOS `dos_verify` is the strongest available success witness (it confirms a landing from
  git rather than from a worker's self-report) and is already wired into this fleet.
- `internal/modelroute/outcome.go` `Outcome{Cost, Latency, Quality, Verify}` has the right
  provenance field and the wrong key (`AspectRuleKey`, which carries no model and no zone).

## Done means

`fak route --place` against this fleet's own roster reports a non-zero number of MEASURED
models from a durable record that nobody hand-wrote, and the placement that follows can be
audited back to the turns that earned it.

records.title: [feature] compaction calibration knobs are corpus-fit, flag-only, and one contradicts --help
records.body:
## The problem

Whether history compaction ever fires is decided by three constants:

| constant | value | where |
|---|---|---|
| `DefaultCompactHistoryBudget` | 48000 | `internal/gateway/gateway.go:68` |
| `HeadlessCompactHistoryBudget` | 96000 | `internal/gateway/gateway.go:85` |
| `DefaultAssumedSessionTurns` | 50 | `internal/gateway/gateway.go:123` |

They are fit to one committed corpus. `internal/gateway/calibration_corpus_drift_test.go`
pins `DefaultAssumedSessionTurns` inside `[p75, p95]` of the session lengths in
`docs/nightrun/gateway-usage.jsonl`, and the calibration comments record that corpus's
shape: **median 7 turns, p75 33, p90 52, p95 70**.

Pinning the constant to a corpus is good discipline. The gap is what happens to someone
whose traffic doesn't look like that corpus — say a session an order of magnitude longer
than its median. Today that user gets a lever that silently never engages, and three
separate things stop them from noticing or fixing it.

### 1. The knobs don't say what they do, and one of them contradicts `--help`

`fak guard -h -all` prints `--compact-history-budget … (default 48000)`. That default is
never what a guard launch uses. `resolveGuardCompactBudget`
(`cmd/fak/guard_resolve.go:62`) replaces it with `HeadlessCompactHistoryBudget` (96000) on
**every** guard launch where the flag was not passed explicitly — so the help text states a
number that is off by 2× from the running value. It is observable on any guard gateway:

```sh
curl -s localhost:$PORT/debug/vars | jq .adjudication.compaction_budget   # -> 96000
```

Separately, the budget's units are easy to misread. It is applied to the `messages[]`
array alone — `CompactAnthropicHistoryWithOptions` sums `estimateElementTokens` over
message elements only (`internal/agent/anthropic_compact.go:368-372`) — while the
system+tools block is not counted. A user reasoning from "my context is N tokens" will set
this wrong in the safe-looking direction, and the only symptom is an `under_budget` bail.
The doc comment on `resolveGuardCompactBudget` itself reasons about the system+tools
"floor" when sizing a budget that is applied to `messages[]`, which is the same conflation.

### 2. The budget is both the trigger and the target, so a fire sheds only the overflow

`suffixTokens <= budget` bails `under_budget` (`anthropic_compact.go:372`), and
`chooseKeptWindow` (`:389`) then keeps the recent window back down to that same `budget`.
Trigger and target are one number, so a body just over the line sheds almost nothing, and
re-fires next turn to shed almost nothing again.

That coupling is what forces the 48000-vs-96000 tension: the lower value fires constantly
for a tiny shed, the higher value stops firing at all. There is no setting that gives
"cut rarely, but cut deeply". A high-water trigger with a separate low-water target would
dissolve the tradeoff instead of trading one failure mode for the other.

### 3. There is no supported way to set, override, or adapt them

- **No env override.** Both are flag-only, so they can only be chosen at launch and cannot
  be set once for a machine or a fleet. The pattern already exists for a neighbouring guard
  knob — `FAK_GUARD_EXPOSE_PROFILE` overrides `--expose-profile` at
  `cmd/fak/guard_resolve.go:75-81` — it just wasn't applied here.
- **No adaptation, though the tuner is already written.** `rsiloop.TuneFirePolicy`
  (`internal/rsiloop/firenettune.go:216`) learns a `MinHorizonMargin` from scored per-fire
  receipts, and the live gate already accepts one (`CompactOptions.MinHorizonMargin`,
  consumed at `anthropic_compact.go:521`). Nothing in `internal/gateway` or `cmd/fak` ever
  sets it — `cmd/fak/cachevalue_firebacktest.go:28` describes wiring it into the live gate
  as future work. So the feedback loop is built and disconnected.
- **The overlay reports the outcome, not the reason.** `fak info` renders a
  "fak compaction shed" bar (`cmd/fak/info_cache_ablation.go:56`). When the lever is
  permanently disengaged that bar reads zero — indistinguishable from a session that simply
  had nothing to shed. The dominant bail reason and the effective budget are both already
  in `/debug/vars` under `adjudication.compaction_*`; they just aren't in the plain-words
  view where someone would notice.

The three compound: a mis-sized budget produces a bail, the bail is invisible, and the
knob that would fix it isn't discoverable, isn't settable outside a launch flag, and never
adapts. The failure is silent and stable — a user can run for hours accumulating
`under_budget` bails and zero fires while the overlay shows a calm zero.

## Proposed solution (optional)

Roughly in order of value per unit of work:

1. **Make the effective value honest.** Either have `resolveGuardCompactBudget` be
   reflected in the flag's printed default, or state in the flag help that a guard launch
   resolves to `HeadlessCompactHistoryBudget` unless the flag is explicit. A one-line help
   fix; happy to send it separately if you'd rather keep it out of this issue.
2. **Say what the budget is measured against** in the flag help — `messages[]` resident
   tokens, excluding the system+tools block — since that is the thing users will get wrong.
3. **Env overrides** `FAK_COMPACT_HISTORY_BUDGET` / `FAK_ASSUME_SESSION_TURNS`, following
   the existing `FAK_GUARD_EXPOSE_PROFILE` precedent, so the values can be set once rather
   than per-launch.
4. **Surface the bail reason in `fak info`** — one field, the dominant
   `adjudication.compaction_bail_reasons` key, next to the shed bar. This is what turns a
   silent misconfiguration into a visible one, and it is probably the highest
   value-to-effort item here.
5. **Split trigger from target** (high-water / low-water) so shed depth stops being tied to
   how far over the line the body happened to land.
6. **Derive `DefaultAssumedSessionTurns` from the live trace** rather than a constant, or
   wire the already-written `TuneFirePolicy` margin into the gate. `volumeAwareHorizon`
   (`internal/gateway/messages.go:679`) already does exactly this kind of
   observed-signal adaptation for the resident-volume axis; the turn axis is still a flat
   constant.

Items 1-4 are small and independent. 5 and 6 are the real fix and clearly larger — happy
to be told they're out of scope, or to split this into separate issues if a single thread
is too broad.

records.title: fix(commitlane): a code-effect subject on a doc-only diff wedges the push gate with no non-rewrite cure (2 residuals overridden)
records.body:
## What happened

The `pre-push` claim-honesty gate (`tools/githooks/pre-push`, DOS reason `CLAIM_UNWITNESSED`)
blocked the whole `origin/main..HEAD` range of 34 commits on **two** residuals. Both are real
findings, not false positives:

| commit | subject | diff |
|---|---|---|
| `3e2404d4d` | `fix(dgxbridge): separate host-noise prune failure from a real readback regression (#5103)` | `docs/private-comms-channel.md` only (+15/-6) |
| `bf05047c7` | `fix(dgxbridge): correct the offline-check note to match the witnessed package run (#5103)` | `docs/private-comms-channel.md` only (+9) |

The kernel's verdict was exact:

```
RESIDUAL — your 100% (2)  [a CLAIM the kernel could not witness]
  3e2404d4d  subject-only   fix(dgxbridge): separate host-noise prune failure ...
             |- code-effect claim but the diff touches no SOURCE file
                (only: docs/private-comms-channel.md) — the claim rests on the subject text
```

A `fix(...)` subject is a code-effect claim. A diff that touches only a doc cannot witness one.
The correct type for both was `docs(dgxbridge): ...`.

## Why it was overridden rather than cured

The hook's own guidance is *"prefer fixing the subject"*, and its `FLEET_ALLOW_RESIDUAL=1`
hatch is documented for **known false positives**. Neither cure was available here:

- **Amending is forbidden.** Both commits are ~30 deep in a shared multi-session trunk. Fixing
  the subjects means an interactive rebase that rewrites peer history and moves `HEAD` under
  every other live session on the box.
- **Waiting does not help.** The gate reviews the whole `origin/main..HEAD` range, so every
  later commit — including correctly-typed ones — stayed unpushable, and the range only grew.

So the override was spent on a **true** positive, with operator approval, to unwedge 33 commits.
This issue is the honest record of that: two mistyped claims are now on `origin/main` and were
not cured.

## Why this is worth a ticket rather than a shrug

The residual is cosmetic *in these two cases* — the doc edits were real, only the type prefix
was wrong. The process hole is not cosmetic:

**A mistyped subject on a shared trunk is uncurable by design.** The gate assumes the author can
amend, but this repo forbids amending the trunk. So any commit that reaches `main` with a
subject its diff cannot witness permanently wedges the push lane for everyone until someone
spends the override. The escape hatch becomes the only exit, which erodes exactly the signal the
gate exists to protect.

## Proposed fix

- [ ] **Catch it at commit time, not push time.** The commit-lane subject gate already classifies
      type-vs-diff (`internal/commitsubject`, `cmd/fak/guard_commit_gate.go`). Make a code-effect
      type (`fix`/`feat`/`perf`) on a **doc-only or data-only** diff a refusal *before* the commit
      lands, where amending is still legal. That closes the hole at the only seam where the cure
      is cheap.
- [ ] **Give the push gate a non-rewrite cure.** A forward-only annotation — a follow-up commit or
      note that reclassifies an earlier commit's claim — so a landed residual can be *witnessed*
      without rewriting shared history. Today `FLEET_ALLOW_RESIDUAL=1` is the only exit, and it
      is indistinguishable in the log from a genuine false positive.
- [ ] **Make a spent override leave a trace.** When the hatch is used, record which commits it
      cleared, so it is auditable rather than silent.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `fix()`/`feat()` commit whose diff touches zero source files is refused at **commit** time
      with the suggested `docs()`/`chore()` type in the message.
- [ ] An already-landed residual can be cleared by a forward-only annotation, with a test proving
      the push gate then passes without `FLEET_ALLOW_RESIDUAL`.
- [ ] A spent `FLEET_ALLOW_RESIDUAL=1` push records the commits it waved through.
- [ ] Regression test: the exact pair above (code-effect subject, doc-only diff) is refused at
      commit time.

Found while unwedging the ship path before a fleet dispatch on 2026-07-28.

records.title: fix(dispatch): resolve backlog closure by acceptance-symbol presence and caller-count, not by commit-subject grep
records.body:
## Problem

A fleet wave dispatched against the P0/P1 view spent **2 of 7 worker slots (29%) on issues that had already shipped** (#4591, #5244 — the latter open for 9 days after landing). Both workers found nothing to build and reported back empty. A follow-up audit of all 31 open P0/P1 leaves, every verdict witnessed against `origin/main`, found the waste is systemic rather than incidental: **4 SHIPPED, 11 PARTIAL, 11 OPEN, 5 GATED.**

Two distinct defects produce it.

### 1. The only binding between a landing and an issue is the issue number in the commit subject — and the highest-value stale-opens do not have it

All four SHIPPED issues are **invisible to `git log --all --grep "#<N>"`**:

| issue | landing commit | why the grep misses it |
|---|---|---|
| #5319 | `cfa7c19fcf1e692eeeabb67a7afe0cd2dfa50f42` | subject names `(#5171, epic #5170)` — never #5319 |
| #4871 | `a4a2c6c82bc435f06ef08538b622dc88e6925ef5` | subject names no issue |
| #3269 | (see audit) | subject names no issue |
| #4750 | `e668fbd08997456e14b2c79c7540d8827a257c62` | subject names no issue |

#5032 is worse still: its second DoD item — the `[reasons.OVERLAY_WOULD_GATE]` declaration — landed inside a **peer's unrelated `dos.toml` commit** (`2cf82f9f27b1d5bca750eaabe2cac4fe0309da27`), two days *after* a comment on the issue said it was intentionally not swept. No subject-grep can ever see that.

These were only found by searching for the acceptance criteria's **named symbols** on trunk (`ChannelCentral`, `TensorQ1_0`, `internal/computeadmit`, `systemd_project.go`). That is what an auditor has to do, and what the dispatch view does not do.

Aggravating factor: **"Landed: `<sha>`" comments are written and never re-read.** #3376, #3599, #5032, #5245 all carry one.

### 2. The "ship the pure primitive first" convention manufactures PARTIALs that read as SHIPPED

Eleven issues landed a fully table-tested `internal/` primitive with **zero production callers outside its own tests**:

- `internal/loaddebounce` (#3376) — `cmd/fak/dispatch_tick_preflight.go:67` still calls `dispatchProbeWorkerCount` directly
- `ResolveHostSpill` (#3599) — appears only in its own file and test; `hostplacement` appears nowhere in `cmd/fak`
- `ShellRack` (#3405) — no caller; the ConPTY spawn path is unchanged
- `SubmitAdmitter` / `computeadmit.Decide` (#3269) — nothing installs it into `Kernel.Submit`
- `DecideFallbackProduct` (#3575) — computed into `out["fallback"]`, never consumed

The acceptance sentence is literally satisfied while production behavior is unchanged. A dispatched worker reads "acceptance met", finds nothing to build, and reports back empty — the identical #5244/#4591 failure mode. But **closing them would silently drop the wiring**, which is the half that carries the user-visible value. The discriminator is a caller-grep, which no gate performs.

## Proposal

1. **Resolve closure by acceptance-symbol presence on `origin/main`, not by subject grep.** Where an issue's acceptance names a symbol, file, or refusal token, check for it on trunk. This is the check that actually found all four SHIPPED issues.
2. **Add a caller-count check.** A new `internal/` primitive whose only referents are its own package, its tests, and `architest` reports **PARTIAL**, not clean — and the remaining work is named as "wire it into `<seam>`". This is what turns eleven dead-end dispatches into eleven crisp, well-scoped units.
3. **Exclude hardware-gated issues from the dispatch view.** *(Done — `gated/hardware` created and applied to #4754, #4769, #4784, #4835, #5112. They cannot be witnessed from a dev box and were consuming worker slots.)*

## Why this is worth a durable guard rather than another sweep

The manual sweep that produced these numbers cost a full auditor pass over 31 issues. It will be stale again within days, because both defects are structural: subjects will keep omitting issue numbers, and the spine-first convention will keep landing caller-less primitives — correctly, by design. The recurring class deserves a guard, not a repeated instance patch.

## Witnessed this session

Closed with re-run witnesses: #5319, #5032, #5245. Closed obsolete with evidence: #4782. Left open with the remaining step narrowed to a single check: #4871.

Related: #5434 (the push-gate claim-honesty residual, same family — a subject that cannot be bound to what the diff proves).
