Worth noting the failure would be invisible in single-rank use, which is presumably why it has survived — with no followers configured, `epFanoutURLsFromEnv` returns an empty list and the chat route no-ops too.

## Suggested shape

Give `epFanoutURLsFromEnv` the route suffix as a parameter instead of hardcoding it, and call `startEPFanoutFollowers` from `handleCompletions` at the point corresponding to `http.go:485` — after method validation, before the decode. The follower-header recursion guard (`epFollowerHeader`) already generalises, since it is checked on entry regardless of route.

The existing `ep_fanout_test.go` structure should extend to cover the legacy route directly; `TestCompletionsStreamingEmitsPreambleBeforeCollectiveJoin` (added in `b32ab0586`) already models a collective join on this route and is a reasonable place to start.

records.title: fix(guard): the replay audit journal defaults to a clock-only temp path, so two concurrent replays interleave into one file and surface as a bogus sequence gap
records.body:
## What

`cmd/fak/guard_replay.go:295` derives the default replay audit-journal path from the wall clock
alone, with no PID and no randomness:

```go
return filepath.Join(os.TempDir(), fmt.Sprintf("fak-guard-replay-%d.jsonl", time.Now().UnixNano())), false, false
```

Two `fak guard replay` runs that start inside the same clock tick resolve to the **same file** in a
shared temp dir and append into it. This is in HEAD — `cmd/fak/guard_replay.go` is clean in the
working tree and `git show HEAD:` carries the identical line, so it is not peer WIP.

## Why `UnixNano` is not enough here, specifically on Windows

The name looks collision-proof because nanoseconds are fine-grained. They are not fine-grained *on
this fleet*: Go's `time.Now()` on Windows is backed by a system timer whose practical granularity is
far coarser than 1 ns, so `UnixNano()` returns the same value for calls that are milliseconds apart.
Two suites starting a replay concurrently are well inside that window.

Nothing else disambiguates the path — no `os.Getpid()`, no `os.MkdirTemp`, no `O_EXCL`. Since the
journal is opened for **append**, the second writer does not fail; it interleaves.

## Observed symptom, and why it misleads

The corruption does not surface as a file error. It surfaces as a chain-verification failure that
points at the journal's contents rather than at the collision:

```
journal: sequence gap: seq=1 want 3
```

while the per-call table still shows every individual call ✓. So the run looks like a *replay
integrity* problem — a dropped or reordered call — when the real cause is a second process's records
interleaved into the same file.

This reddened `TestGuardReplayRunsCleanOnBothWires` under a multi-suite run. Isolated, the same test
is green (`ok … 2.228s`, exit 0). That pass-alone/fail-together signature is the tell, and it is
exactly the signature that gets misfiled as flake.

## Suggested shape

Make the default path unique per process, not per instant — `os.MkdirTemp` (which uses `O_EXCL` and
retries), or at minimum fold in `os.Getpid()` alongside the timestamp. `os.MkdirTemp` is the stronger
choice: it is the only option here that is actually atomic rather than merely less likely to collide.

An explicit `--audit PATH` is unaffected (`guard_replay.go:292` returns it verbatim), and so is the
`off` case — this is only about the generated default.

## Confidence

**Verified by reading:** the line, that it is in HEAD, that the explicit-path and `off` branches
bypass it, and that the journal is opened for append.

**Not independently reproduced by me:** I did not force two replays into one tick to watch them
interleave. The `seq=1 want 3` output above was observed during other work, and the causal link from
it to this line is inferred from the code path rather than demonstrated. Worth confirming with a
deliberate two-process repro before designing the fix — if the interleaving turns out to come from
somewhere else, this line is still worth fixing but the priority changes.

Found while working #5487; unrelated to that ticket's change.

records.title: fix(gateway): a result-floor 502 on the streaming passthrough is never counted or printed, so the upstream-error metric silently under-reports
records.body:
## What

`internal/gateway/messages_stream_passthrough.go:449-450` is the one arm of the streaming
passthrough's terminal switch that returns **without counting or printing anything**:

```go
case p.wroteError:
    return true // a clean terminal HTTP error was already written
```

Its two siblings both observe and render. The mid-stream arm:

```go
s.renderTurnDebugError(reqTrace, "anthropic_messages", err, time.Since(began))
```

and the `default:` arm at :455-456:

```go
s.metrics.observeUpstreamError(err)
s.renderTurnDebugError(reqTrace, "anthropic_messages", err, time.Since(began))
```

So a turn that reaches the `p.wroteError` arm is invisible on `/metrics` and prints no `FAILED`
line on the default debug output. The comment is accurate about what happened — a clean terminal
HTTP error *was* written to the client — but "the client was told" and "the operator was told" are
different questions, and only the first is satisfied.

## Why it matters now

The reachable producer of `wroteError = true` is the **result-floor** branch at :241-248:

```go
adms, aerr := p.s.admitInboundResults(p.r.Context(), p.req.Messages, p.req.Tools, p.reqTrace)
if aerr != nil {
    p.s.logf("gateway: result-floor error (messages stream): %v", aerr)
    writeErr(p.w, http.StatusBadGateway, "upstream model error")
    p.wroteError = true
    return errPassthroughResponded
}
```

A result-floor rejection therefore returns a 502 to the caller and leaves **no operator-visible
trace except an `s.logf`**, which only reaches the `--log` stream — OFF by default. The
`default:` arm's own comment says exactly why that is not enough: "the `s.logf` calls below only
reach the --log stream, OFF by default". The same reasoning applies here and was not carried over.

The failure mode is the bad one: a class of 502s that never appears in the error metric, so the
`/metrics` upstream-error count under-reports and the gap is silent. Nobody notices a number that
is too small.

## Scope note

This was found while working #5491. That fix removes the *in-band refusal* caller from this arm —
before it, the pre-start in-band error path also set `wroteError` — so #5491 narrows what reaches
:449 but does **not** close this. The result-floor branch at :247 still takes it, which is why this
is filed separately rather than folded in.

## Suggested shape

Make the arm consistent with its siblings: `observeUpstreamError` + `renderTurnDebugError` before
returning, without re-writing to the client (the HTTP error is already sent — that part is
correct). Care is needed not to double-count if any future caller observes before setting the flag;
today's single producer at :247 does not, so a straight addition is currently exact.

A witness would assert that a result-floor rejection increments the upstream-error metric exactly
once and emits a debug line, while still writing exactly one 502 body.

## Confidence

**Verified by reading**, at the current tip: the three switch arms and their differing calls, that
:247 is the surviving producer of the flag, and that `writeErr` sends the body. Line numbers are
from the working tree with #5491's change applied — the arm itself is untouched by that change.

**Not reproduced:** I did not drive a live result-floor rejection and diff `/metrics` before and
after. That is the checkable next step and would confirm the under-count directly.

records.title: guard: SessionStart installer is handed toolproc's input settings path, not the path toolproc created
records.body:
Found while fixing #5510, in the same file family but outside that ticket's fence.

## The bug

In `cmd/fak/guard.go`, the SessionStart installer is handed:

```go
sessionStartSettings := toolprocSettings
```

That is the toolproc installer's **input** path — not the path toolproc actually created. The
four guard settings installers (PreCompact, Stop, toolproc, SessionStart) are meant to converge
on one settings file: the first to run creates it, and the rest read-modify-write that same
path. Handing SessionStart the input path breaks that convergence whenever the first two
installers are disabled.

## Failure scenario

With **PreCompact and Stop both disabled**, toolproc creates the settings file at a path that
`sessionStartSettings` does not name. SessionStart then appends a *second* guard `--settings`
to the child argv. Claude's `--settings` is last-wins, so the two guard payloads now race each
other — the same class of silent disarming that #5510 fixed for the *caller's* payload, except
here both sides are guard's own.

## Why it is newly visible

Before #5510 this failed silently. After #5510 it surfaces loudly as `SETTINGS_HOOKS_DROPPED`
on stderr, because the fold refuses a second payload carrying a `hooks` key. That is strictly
better than silence, but it is a diagnostic, not a fix — the second installer's settings are
still dropped, just audibly.

## Fix

One line in `cmd/fak/guard.go`: hand SessionStart the path toolproc *created*, not the path it
was offered. The `#5510` fold in `cmd/fak/guard_precompact.go` is unaffected and needs no change.

## Checkable step

A test that disables PreCompact and Stop, runs the toolproc and SessionStart installers in
order, and asserts the resulting argv carries **exactly one** `--settings` occurrence. That
assertion fails today and passes after the one-line change. `cmd/fak/guard_settings_conflict_test.go`
(added by #5510) already has the argv-counting helper and the round-trip fixture to build on.

Not fixed in #5510 because `guard.go` was outside that lane's fence and was peer-dirty at the time.

records.title: guard: two temp-dir families are unreapable — 'lifecycle' missing from the hook set, 'handoff' created without a PID segment
records.body:
Found while fixing #5524. Two guard temp dirs are created in a shape the reaper cannot claim,
so they accumulate forever. The two failures drift in **opposite directions**, which is why
neither shows up as a simple typo.

The reaper (`cmd/fak/guard_tempreap.go`) claims a dir only if *both* hold:
1. its hook name is in the closed `guardTempDirHooks` set, and
2. its name carries a `<pid>` segment, so `guardTempDirOwner` can test the owner for liveness.

`guard_tempreap.go:46-48` documents exactly this hazard in its own comment.

## Leak 1 — hook name missing from the set

`cmd/fak/guard_lifecycle_ipc.go:46` calls `guardSessionTempDir("lifecycle")`, which produces a
correctly-shaped `fak-guard-lifecycle-<pid>-*` dir. But `"lifecycle"` is **absent** from
`guardTempDirHooks`, so rung 1 fails. Every lifecycle IPC dir ever created is still on disk.

## Leak 2 — in the set, but created off-convention

The converse. `"handoff"` **is** in `guardTempDirHooks`, but `cmd/fak/guard.go:1173` creates its
dir with a raw `os.MkdirTemp("", "fak-guard-handoff-*")` — bypassing `guardSessionTempDir` and
therefore emitting **no PID segment**. Rung 2 fails, `guardTempDirOwner` rejects it, and those
dirs are likewise never reaped.

## Fix

- Leak 1: add `"lifecycle"` to `guardTempDirHooks`.
- Leak 2: route `guard.go:1173` through `guardSessionTempDir("handoff")` rather than calling
  `os.MkdirTemp` directly — the same seam #5524 routed the replay path through.

## Checkable step

A table test over every `guardSessionTempDir` call site and every raw `os.MkdirTemp` with a
`fak-guard-` prefix, asserting each produced name is claimable by `guardTempDirOwner`. That is
the invariant both leaks violate, and it is the one that keeps drifting — a third call site
added tomorrow breaks the same way in whichever of the two directions the author picks.

Deliberately not fixed in #5524: leak 2 lives in `guard.go`, which was outside that lane's fence.
Leak 1 is a one-word change but belongs with its converse, since a fix for either alone leaves
the invariant unguarded.

records.title: gateway: EP follower fanout still missing on the messages, responses, denial-recovery and Gemini routes
records.body:
#5523 wired the EP follower fanout into the legacy text-completion route. The same gap remains
on every other inbound wire.

## Evidence

Exhaustive grep of the production call sites of the bridge (`_test.go` excluded):

```
completions.go:42   waitEPFanout, ok := s.startEPFanoutFollowers(w, r, epRouteCompletions)
http.go:485         waitEPFanout, ok := s.startEPFanoutFollowers(w, r, epRouteChatCompletions)
http_epfanout.go:55 func (s *Server) startEPFanoutFollowers(...)   <- the definition
```

Two call sites, both added by or predating #5523. Every other served route therefore reaches the
front rank and **never releases follower ranks into the collective** — the request is served by
one rank while the rest idle. The uncovered routes are the Anthropic messages wire, the responses
wire and its denial-recovery arm, and the Gemini wire.

## Why this is not just "add four more calls"

`#5523` established the shape, and one constraint from it must carry over: the route identity
must **not** be derived from `r.URL.Path`. That field is client-steerable, so deriving a follower
URL from it lets an inbound request choose where the fanout points. Each route needs its own
`epRoute*` constant, exactly as `epRouteCompletions` and `epRouteChatCompletions` do.

Each route also differs in body shape and streaming semantics, so each needs its own mirror test —
the streaming and non-streaming arms failed differently during #5523.

## The gate that should have caught this

`ValidateEPFanoutCoverage` in `internal/gateway/ep_fanout_topology.go` exists and is exercised
only from within its own file and `ep_fanout_topology_test.go`. Nothing asserts at startup, or in
a package test, that *every registered route* is either covered by the fanout or explicitly
exempt. That absence is why the gap could sit on four routes without a red test.

## Checkable step

A table test enumerating every route the server registers and asserting each is either in the
fanout set or in a named exemption list — failing today with four entries, passing once they are
wired. That test is the durable fix; the four call sites are the mechanical part.

Suggested order: land the coverage assertion **first** (red, listing exactly the four), then wire
routes until it goes green. That way the ticket cannot be closed on a partial.

records.title: concept-admission: token extractor glues Go string escapes onto the next word, inventing blocking tokens like tSESSION
records.body:
The concept-admission token extractor treats a Go string escape as part of the identifier that
follows it, so it invents tokens that do not exist and then blocks the commit until someone
classifies them.

## Reproducer

`cmd/fak/wip.go:1028` contains an ordinary tab-separated header literal:

```go
fmt.Fprintln(stdout, "DRIFT\tAGE_H\tSESSION\tLEAVES")
```

`fak commit` refused with:

```
HOOK_REFUSED: CONCEPT_ADMISSION: 2 finding(s):
  cmd/fak/wip.go:1028: family=session-runtime token=tSESSION introduced at cmd/fak/wip.go:1028
  is neither positioned nor classified
```

There is no `tSESSION` symbol anywhere in the repo. The extractor split the literal at `\t` and
glued the escape's `t` onto the column name `SESSION`.

## Why it matters

The false token is not merely noise — `CONCEPT_ADMISSION` is a **blocking** pre-commit gate. The
only ways past it are to position a concept that does not exist, or to classify the non-symbol as
`incidental`. Both write a permanent row into
`tools/concept_disambiguation_scorecard.data/_meta.json`, so the corpus accumulates entries for
tokens that were never in the source. It also inflates discovered-token counts, which are the
denominator of the coverage figure the scorecard reports.

I took the `incidental` route to unblock #5480, with the reason string recording that it is a
tokenizer artifact rather than a real symbol. That row should be removed once this is fixed.

## Likely fix

Decode Go string escapes (or skip string literals entirely) before tokenizing. `\t`, `\n` and `\r`
followed immediately by an uppercase word are the cases that produce plausible-looking camelCase
tokens; a TSV or format-string header is the common shape.

## Checkable step

A unit test over the extractor asserting that `"DRIFT\tAGE_H\tSESSION\tLEAVES"` yields no token
beginning with the escape letter — currently yields `tSESSION`. Worth also asserting `\n`-joined
literals, which will have the same shape with an `n` prefix.

records.title: flake: TestTUIGuardHumanOutputColorAlways inherits ambient NO_COLOR and contradicts its own sibling test
records.body:
`TestTUIGuardHumanOutputColorAlways` (`cmd/fak/tui_test.go:453`) inherits `NO_COLOR` from the
ambient environment, so it passes or fails depending on who is running it. It is green on a
developer box that has never set the variable and red in any shell that exports it.

## The tension is with its own sibling

The two tests are adjacent and make opposite demands of the same flag:

- `tui_test.go:453` `TestTUIGuardHumanOutputColorAlways` — runs `--color always` and fails at
  `:469` (`--color always did not emit ANSI`) if the output carries no `\x1b[`. It never touches
  `NO_COLOR`.
- `tui_test.go:480` — the next test **does** `t.Setenv("NO_COLOR", "1")` and asserts at `:495`
  that `NO_COLOR should suppress ANSI even with --color always`.

So when `NO_COLOR` is set in the environment, the first test is asking for exactly the behavior
the second one pins as correct. Only one of them controls the variable.

## This is a test-hermeticity defect, not a product defect

The product behavior is deliberate and documented — `cmd/fak/info.go:306` describes `--color
always` as "force on unless `NO_COLOR`", and `cmd/fak/info_color.go:26` is the single predicate
(`isTTY && os.Getenv("NO_COLOR") == ""`). `NO_COLOR` winning over `--color always` is the
community-standard opt-out the rest of the guard honors. Nothing in the shipped code should
change.

## Reproducer

With `NO_COLOR=1` exported:

```
--- FAIL: TestTUIGuardHumanOutputColorAlways
    tui_test.go:469: --color always did not emit ANSI
```

Unset it and the same commit is green. The files are clean at HEAD in both cases.

## Fix

One line in `TestTUIGuardHumanOutputColorAlways`: `t.Setenv("NO_COLOR", "")`, mirroring how the
sibling test at `:480` already takes control of the variable. `t.Setenv` restores the prior value
at test end, so it is safe under `-count` and does not leak into neighbours.

## Checkable step

Run the single test twice in one shell — once with `NO_COLOR` exported and once without — and
assert the same verdict both times. That is the invariant being violated today, and it is worth
a sweep: any other test asserting on ANSI presence without pinning `NO_COLOR` has the same latent
split.

## Provenance

Surfaced while auditing a worker's claim that this was a HEAD-level failure. It is not — the
worker reported `NO_COLOR` as unset, which was wrong. The failure is real but environmental, and
the honest scope is the missing `t.Setenv`, not a product bug.

records.title: cmd/fak/sessions_codex_loop.go is 1513 lines at HEAD, so TestGodfileGate_LiveTreeClean is red on a clean trunk
records.body:
`TestGodfileGate_LiveTreeClean` (`internal/hooks`) is red on a clean checkout of `main`, with no
uncommitted work involved. It is not a flake and not a lane's fault — the trunk itself carries the
offense.

## Evidence

```
cmd/fak/sessions_codex_loop.go: NEW god-file: cmd/fak/sessions_codex_loop.go is 1513 lines (> 1500)
```

- `git show HEAD:cmd/fak/sessions_codex_loop.go` → **1513 lines**. Worktree is also 1513, and
  `git status --porcelain` reports the file **clean**, so this is HEAD's own content.
- The ceiling is `internal/hooks/gate_godfile.go:68` —
  `godFileMaxLines = gateEnvInt("FAK_GODFILE_MAX_LINES", 1500)`.
- `internal/hooks/godfile_baseline.go:41` grandfathers only the **function**:
  `"cmd/fak/sessions_codex_loop.go:diagnoseCodexLoop": 223`. There is **no file-level entry** for
  `sessions_codex_loop.go`, so the file gets no slack at all.

So the gate is doing exactly what it was built to do, and the answer it is giving is correct.

## Why it matters more than one red test

This is a self-auditing inventory gate: it grades the tree it runs in, so it stays red for
everyone until the file is split, and it masks any *subsequent* god-file regression behind the
same failure. A second file crossing 1500 tomorrow would not change the output in any way an
operator would notice — `t.Fatalf` on the first offense means the next one is invisible.

It also produces a bad incentive at exactly the wrong moment. The cheap way to clear it is to add
a file-level row to `godfile_baseline.go`, which grandfathers the file *at its current size* and
converts a "split this" signal into a permanent exemption.

## Fix

Split `cmd/fak/sessions_codex_loop.go` along a real seam, as was just done for `cmd/fak/wip.go`
(1608 → 1352, with the `reconcile` subcommand surface moved to its own file as a pure,
byte-identical move). `diagnoseCodexLoop` at 223 lines is the obvious candidate to carry out with
its helpers, and it already has its own baseline row, so moving it does not change the function
accounting.

**Do not add a file-level baseline entry.** That is the wrong cure and it is worth saying so in
the ticket rather than leaving it as the path of least resistance.

## Checkable step

`go test ./internal/hooks/ -run TestGodfileGate -v` — currently reports exactly one offense, and
it is this file. When the split lands, that run goes green with zero offenses, and the next file
to cross 1500 becomes visible again.

## Note on the gate itself

Because the check fails on the *first* offense, the offender list is not exhaustive. Worth
considering whether it should report every file over the ceiling before failing, so one split does
not simply reveal another red.

## Provenance

Surfaced while splitting `cmd/fak/wip.go` for #5480: that split cleared `wip.go` off the offender
list and left this one behind, which is how it became visible as a HEAD-level condition rather
than a consequence of in-flight work.

records.title: gateway: the agent-sessions route cannot use the EP fanout mechanism — a governed loop needs an in-loop rank barrier, not a request mirror (#5528 follow-on)
records.body:
## The one served route the EP fanout still cannot cover

`#5528` wired the follower fanout into the messages, responses and Gemini wires (`65e48886d`).
`TestEPFanoutCoverageClassifiesEveryServedRoute` now forces every served route to be either
covered or exempt-with-a-stated-reason, so what is left is explicit rather than silent.

One route is exempt for a reason that is a real gap rather than a property of the route:

```go
"/v1/fak/agent/sessions": epExemptOwnedLoop,
```

with the reason recorded as: *runs fak's own multi-turn governed loop: N forward passes and
real tool side effects from one inbound body, which a request mirror cannot reproduce without
diverging the ranks (needs an in-loop rank barrier; #5528 follow-on).*

## Why the existing mechanism does not extend to it

Every covered route fans out by mirroring the inbound request to the followers, which works
because one inbound body maps to one forward pass. The agent-sessions route breaks that
assumption in two ways:

- **N forward passes from one body.** The loop decides how many turns to run from model output
  the follower does not have. Mirroring the original body makes each rank run its own loop and
  choose its own turn count, so the ranks diverge instead of joining a collective.
- **Real tool side effects.** The loop executes tools. A mirrored request would execute them
  once per rank, which is not a read-amplification problem but a correctness one.

So the fix is not another `startEPFanoutFollowers` call site. It needs a barrier *inside* the
loop: the leader drives the loop, and at each forward pass the followers are released into that
one decode and rejoin before the leader proceeds to tool execution.

## Checkable step

A test in the shape of `TestEPFanoutCoveredRoutesDoNotFanOutAgain` but for the loop: drive a
two-turn agent session against a stub planner with a follower configured, and assert the
follower entered the collective exactly twice — once per forward pass — and executed zero
tool calls. That assertion fails today for the trivial reason that the follower is never
released at all, which makes it a usable red-first witness.

## Not urgent

Nothing regresses while this stays open: the route is on the exempt list, the coverage test
passes, and a single-rank deployment is unaffected. This matters when someone runs the agent
loop under a real EP world size, where today the follower ranks sit idle for the whole session.

records.title: concept-admission: a filename or test name quoted in a prose comment is extracted as an introduced symbol, blocking the commit (#5529 sibling)
records.body:
## A snake_case filename in a prose comment becomes a blocking concept token

Sibling of #5529 (`32c71d74c`, escape-aware tokenizer), same gate, different cause. That one
glued a Go string escape onto the next word; this one reads a **filename** as an identifier.

## Reproducer

`cmd/fak/guard_split.go:230` is an ordinary prose note in a header comment:

```go
// NOT VERIFIED END TO END: this was written without a Mac. guard_split_close_test.go witnesses
// the generated command line — that Terminal then closes that window, silently, is unwitnessed
// and wants a Mac operator (#5482).
```

`fak hooks pre-commit -json` reports:

```
family=guard-gate token=guard_split_close_test introduced at cmd/fak/guard_split.go:230
is neither positioned nor classified
```

The extractor took `guard_split_close_test.go`, dropped the extension, and offered the remainder
as a symbol. There is no `guard_split_close_test` identifier anywhere in the repo — the thing
that exists is a *file*.

## Why it matters

`CONCEPT_ADMISSION` is a **blocking** pre-commit gate, so the only ways past are to position a
concept that does not exist or classify a non-symbol as `incidental`. Both write a permanent row
into `tools/concept_disambiguation_scorecard.data/_meta.json`. The corpus then accumulates rows
for things that were never symbols, and those rows inflate the discovered-token count that is the
denominator of the coverage figure the scorecard reports.

This shape is common and will recur: a comment that names the test file witnessing the code it
sits above is good practice, and it is exactly what trips the gate.

Note the same class showed up independently in the #5411 set, where a *test function name* quoted
in a non-test header comment (`TestGuardSelfTightenOverlayPathIsAgentWritable`) also had to be
classified away. So the general defect is: **identifiers named in prose are treated as
identifiers introduced by the file.**

## Likely fix

Two candidate rules, either of which handles this case:

1. Do not extract tokens from a run that is immediately followed by a file extension
   (`.go`, `.md`, `.json`), since that run is a path, not a symbol.
2. More generally, require an extracted token to resolve to a declaration in the file that
   introduced it. A token that appears only inside a comment is a *reference*, not an
   introduction — and the gate's own message says "introduced at", which is the claim that is
   false here.

Rule 2 also covers the `TestGuard...` case and is closer to what the gate means.

## Checkable step

A unit test over the extractor asserting that a comment line containing `foo_bar_test.go` yields
no `foo_bar_test` token, and that a comment naming an existing test function does not register
that function as introduced by the non-test file quoting it. Both currently fail.

## Workaround in the meantime

Classified `incidental` to unblock #5482, with the reason string recording that it is a filename
rather than a symbol. That row should be retired when this is fixed, along with #5529's
`tSESSION` row.

records.title: concept-admission: the remedy it prints cannot clear it — the gate reads the index, but  ak concept position/classify writes the worktree
records.body:
## The gate's own prescribed cure cannot clear the gate

`CONCEPT_ADMISSION` refuses with a remedy line naming an exact command:

```
family=guard-gate token=guardSharedHookSettingsPath introduced at cmd/fak/guard.go:1379
is neither positioned nor classified; run `fak concept position --id ... --row-file rows-fak.json ...`
(or `fak concept classify --family guard-gate --token ... --category incidental --reason TEXT`)
```

Run exactly that command. It exits 0. `fak concept validate` prints `concept catalog valid`.
Re-run the gate — **the same finding is still reported.** Commit again, and it refuses again.

## Why

`fak concept position` / `classify` write into the **worktree** corpus. The gate reads the
**index**.

`internal/hooks/gate_conceptadmission.go:150`

```go
metaBytes, ok := d.FileBytes("tools/concept_disambiguation_scorecard.data/_meta.json")
```

`FileBytes` is the index-aware accessor, so `_meta.json` resolves to the staged blob — or, for a
path you did not stage, to HEAD. A worktree-only edit is invisible to it. The `Ignore`/`Exclude`
lists that `classify` writes live in that file, so **every classification is invisible until the
file is staged.**

The row files have the same shape at `:161`, and here there is a fallback that looks like it
covers the case but does not:

```go
paths := append([]string{}, d.IndexPaths...)
if len(paths) == 0 {
    matches, _ := filepath.Glob(filepath.Join(d.Root, "tools", "concept_disambiguation_scorecard.data", "rows-*.json"))
    ...
}
```

`IndexPaths` is documented at `internal/hooks/hooks.go:168` as *"all candidate-index paths (for
cross-file semantic gates)"* — the whole index listing, not the staged-modified subset. In any
real repo it is never empty, so **the worktree glob at `:163` is unreachable**. The comment above
it at `:159-160` says the accessor is used so the gate can see *"a newly staged row file that does
not exist in HEAD or a peer-dirty workspace"*, which is true and is the right call — the dead
fallback just makes it look like an unstaged row file is also covered.

## The interaction that makes this bite

This repo mandates `fak commit --path <yours>`, which stages **only the named paths**. So the
natural sequence — refuse, classify, re-commit the same code paths — stages the code and never
the corpus, and refuses identically forever. Nothing in the refusal says the corpus files have to
be in the commit.

## Reproducer

1. Add a new symbol under `cmd/` or `internal/` matching a family root.
2. `fak commit --path <that file>` → CONCEPT_ADMISSION.
3. Run the exact `fak concept classify` line from the refusal. Exit 0.
4. `fak hooks pre-commit -json` with only that file staged → **the identical finding**.
5. `git add tools/concept_disambiguation_scorecard.data/_meta.json` → finding gone.

Step 4 vs 5 is the whole bug.

## Cost observed

Three refused commits and a wrong root-cause hypothesis on my side (I concluded the gate read
HEAD, because the one run that came back clean happened to have the corpus sitting in prestaged
limbo from an earlier refused commit — indistinguishable from "committed" unless you check the
index). Four finished fixes sat unlandable meanwhile.

## Suggested fix — one line of prose, or a few of code

Cheapest honest fix: **name the corpus files in the remedy.** Append to the detail string at
`gate_conceptadmission.go:244` something like *"...then include
`tools/concept_disambiguation_scorecard.data/_meta.json` (and any new `rows-*.json`) in the same
`fak commit --path` set — this gate reads the index, not the worktree."*

Better fix: have `fak concept position` / `classify` `git add` the corpus files they wrote, so the
prescribed cure is self-completing. That is a behaviour change worth a second opinion, since it
stages a shared file on a shared trunk.

Either way this deserves a test: stage a new-symbol file, write a classification into the worktree
only, and assert the gate **still** fires — pinning the mechanism so nobody "fixes" it by
accidentally reading the worktree and reintroducing the peer-dirty bug `:159` was written to
avoid.

## Checkable step

`internal/hooks/gate_conceptadmission_test.go` currently has no case that separates worktree state
from index state for the corpus. Adding the pair above (worktree-only → still fires; staged →
clears) is the check.

records.title: guard: the stophook temp dir is created raw, so a third scratch family is unreapable (#5527 sibling)
records.body:
`installGuardStopHook` (`cmd/fak/guard_stophook.go:976`) creates its scratch directory with a raw

```go
os.MkdirTemp("", "fak-guard-stophook-*")
```

while `"stophook"` is already a member of `guardTempDirHooks` in `cmd/fak/guard_tempreap.go`.

That is the exact defect #5527 fixed for the `handoff` family: the reaper is told to own the token, but the creator emits no `<pid>` segment, so `guardTempDirOwner` cannot parse the name and the directory is never claimed. It leaks on kill-residue forever.

**Why it did not show up on disk.** The count of `fak-guard-stophook-*` directories is currently **0**, because the raw call only fires when no earlier installer has written a settings file to merge into. It is rare, not absent — which is why a disk census alone would wrongly clear it.

**Cure**, identical to the one #5527 applied to `handoff`: call `guardSessionTempDir("stophook")` instead of the raw `os.MkdirTemp`.

**There is already a ratchet waiting for this.** #5527 added `TestGuardTempDirCreationConvention` with a single self-policing waiver entry, keyed by file *and* token:

```go
guardTempDirRawWaiver["guard_stophook.go"] = "stophook"
```

When this is fixed, that waiver goes stale and the test fails with `stale waiver: ... no longer matches`. So the fix is two edits — the call site and the waiver removal — and the test will tell you if you forget the second.

**Checkable step:** change the call, drop the waiver row, run `go test ./cmd/fak/ -run TestGuardTempDirCreationConvention -v` and confirm it stays green with the waiver map empty.

Found by the #5527 worker, deliberately left out of scope by its file fence.

records.title: gateway: the planner-live result floor writes a 502 without observing it, so the upstream-error metric still under-reports (#5525 sibling)
records.body:
#5525 fixed the streaming passthrough's result-floor arm so a `502 upstream model error` is counted by `observeUpstreamError` and rendered on the `--debug-stats` FAILED line. The planner-live path has the identical blind spot and was left untouched.

`internal/gateway/messages_stream_planner.go:36-41` writes the same `502 upstream model error` and returns `true` with **no** `observeUpstreamError` and **no** `renderTurnDebugError`. Same under-count, different path: a turn refused by the result floor on the planner-live route is invisible to `/metrics`.

**The subtlety #5525 established, which this fix must repeat.** Observing the wrong value is worse than not observing. At the terminal switch the in-flight `err` is the control-flow sentinel `errPassthroughResponded`, which `upstreamErrorKind` (`internal/gateway/metrics.go:504-555`) classifies into the coarse `"other"` bucket. #5525's cure was to stash the *real* cause on a dedicated field beside the flag at the producer and observe that. A "straight addition" that observes `err` produces a green-looking metric filed under the wrong kind — #5525's test asserts exactly this distinction (`kinds = map[other:1], want transport=1`) and that mutant is worth reproducing here.

**Also unobserved, same shape, listed for scope**: the buffered / other-wire result-floor sites at `internal/gateway/http.go:565-569`, `responses.go:281`, `gemini.go:173`, `messages.go:1326` all return without observing.

**Checkable step:** extend the #5525 test pattern to the planner route — poisoned tool result quarantined by the result screen, engine control plane dropped with a non-dial `*net.OpError`, then assert the upstream-error counter is exactly 1 *and* lands in the `transport` kind, not `other`.

Found by the #5525 worker.

records.title: procguard: three ps call sites outside internal/procguard still carry the pre-#5385 keyword and stdout-discard defects
records.body:
`5230cc1c5` fixed the POSIX `ps` census in `internal/procguard` — it pinned the argv per `GOOS` (`psCensusSpec` / `psRelationSpec` / `psBSD` in `internal/procguard/collect.go`) and stopped `runTool` from discarding stdout on a non-zero exit. Three call sites outside that package still carry the original defects and were not covered.

**Both defects, intact:**
- `cmd/fak/slack_fleet_process_unix.go:16` — `ps -eo pid=,ppid=,etimes=,args=`. `etimes` is a procps-only keyword; BSD `ps` rejects it, so the whole census returns nothing on macOS. It also uses `.Output()` with `return nil, err`, discarding a partial table.

**Stdout-discard only:**
- `cmd/fak/dispatch_tick_preflight_host.go:451` — `ps -eo pid=,nlwp=,rss=,comm=` with `.Output()` → `return nil, err`. `nlwp` is likewise procps-only.

**Degrades correctly, listed for completeness:**
- `cmd/fak/dispatch_tick_preflight_host.go:545` — `ps -eo nlwp=`, but guarded by `if err == nil`, so it falls back to "threads unknown" rather than vanishing.

**Checked and clear** (no procps-only keyword): `internal/memgate/memgate.go:221` (`ps -axo pid,rss,comm`), `dispatch_tick_preflight_host.go:847` / `:892`, `internal/commitlane/status.go:673` — all use common vocabulary.

The prior art is in the same repo: `psSpec` carries the column→field map so argv and parser cannot drift, and `psNoColumn = -1` (`collect.go:175`) types "BSD has no thread keyword" as **nil** rather than a fabricated `0`. Reuse that seam rather than re-deriving one; the point of the #5385 fix was one enumeration implementation, not a fork per call site.

**Residual hazard flagged by the #5385 worker and not settled** — on darwin, `psRelationSpec` puts `comm` at column 3 of 5 with `args` last, so `splitN` gives `comm` exactly one whitespace-delimited token, while the repo's own test asserts BSD `comm` is an absolute path (`collect_posix_test.go:214`). A macOS executable path containing a space would split, putting a path fragment in `Name` and bleeding the rest into `Cmdline`. Blast radius looks limited (PID/PPID/age stay correct and `resumeProcRe` still matches, so the resume ceiling is not re-broken — only name-keyed classification in the guard is wrong). Nothing in this repo documents the BSD short-name keyword's semantics, so the argv was deliberately left alone. **Needs a witness from someone on a Mac.**

**Checkable step:** none of this is verifiable from Windows. `go test ./internal/procguard/ -run TestCollectPOSIXCensusIsNonEmpty -v` currently SKIPs for lack of `ps`; on a BSD-dialect host it should stop skipping.

records.title: guard: fak guard sets the three prompt-shrink levers with no wire admission, so they go silently inert exactly as serve did (#5493 sibling)
records.body:
#5493 established that the three prompt-shrink levers — `--compact-history-budget`, `--elide-stale-reads`, `--defer-cold-tools` — are gated on the Anthropic-passthrough predicate and go silently inert on any other wire. It shipped a startup admission for `fak serve` (`cmd/fak/shrink_lever_wire.go`): a lever the operator **typed** is a stated intent the wire cannot honor, so serve refuses to start (exit 2); a lever that is merely the shipped default gets a loud named NOTICE and serve continues.

`fak guard` has the identical defect and no admission. `cmd/fak/guard.go` sets the same three Config fields at `:901`, `:909`, `:934`, and it supports `--provider openai --base-url` plus `--local` (which forces `provider=openai`) — so the guard path reaches a non-passthrough wire at least as easily as serve does.

**This is a genuinely small fix.** `admitServeShrinkLevers` is already in package `main`, so the guard side is one call in guard's boot path plus a guard-side case in `cmd/fak/shrink_lever_wire_test.go`. It was left out of #5493 only because `guard.go` was outside that worker's file fence.

**Why it matters more than it looks.** All three levers ship default-on — `DefaultCompactHistoryBudget = 48000` (`internal/gateway/gateway.go:68`), `DefaultElideStaleReads = true` (`:249`), `DefaultDeferColdTools = true` (`:270`) — so silently-inert is the *default* experience for a self-hosted operator, not an edge case.

**Related finding from the same investigation, worth folding in:** a 2-or-more-upstream replica fleet is also not a passthrough *even on `--provider anthropic`*. `gateway.newProxyPlanner` (`internal/gateway/gateway.go:2337`) returns a `*ReplicaRouter` for 2+ URLs, which `unwrapHTTPPlanner` (`internal/gateway/messages.go:1476-1503`) cannot unwrap, so the predicate is false and all three levers go inert. Easy to configure by accident, impossible to notice.

**Also noticed, comment-only rot:** `cmd/fak/servewiring.go:86` cites the gate as `internal/gateway/messages.go:365`; the real gate is now `:730`.

**Checkable step:** add the `admitServeShrinkLevers` call to guard's boot path, then assert a guard-side case in `shrink_lever_wire_test.go` that a non-passthrough guard wire with an explicitly typed lever refuses, and that a default-only lever produces a named notice rather than silence.

records.title: wip checkpoints snapshot the whole shared tree, so a per-session ref is not that session's work
records.body:
## What

`wipCheckpoint` stages the **entire shared working tree** into every session's checkpoint, so a per-session WIP ref does not contain that session's work — it contains every concurrent peer's uncommitted edits at that instant.

`cmd/fak/wip.go:420-425`:

```go
idxEnv := []string{"GIT_INDEX_FILE=" + filepath.Join(tmp, "index")}
if _, err := gitWipOut(ctx, repo, idxEnv, "read-tree", "HEAD"); err != nil { ... }
if _, err := gitWipOut(ctx, repo, idxEnv, "add", "-A"); err != nil { ... }
```

The temp index is seeded from HEAD and then `add -A` sweeps the whole worktree. The commit is then minted against the capture-time HEAD (`wip.go:472`, `commit-tree <tree> -p <head>`), so the stored delta is a full snapshot of the shared tree, not an increment.

## Why it matters

This is the root cause of three separately-reported symptoms:

1. **Unbounded ref growth with no collectable class** (#5340). Because each checkpoint carries ~50 peers' edits, `Subsumed` can never become true — subsumption would require ~23k added lines to already be in HEAD. Measured on two live refs: `203 files changed, 23654 insertions(+), 529 deletions(-)` and `144 files changed, 20253 insertions(+), 504 deletions(-)`.
2. **71% tree duplication.** Sessions that checkpoint in the same window write byte-identical trees. Live tally: 1339 refs, 385 distinct trees, 954 refs (71%) sharing a tree with another ref; the largest group is 224 refs pinning one tree object.
3. **The per-session recovery model does not hold.** `fak wip land <session>` is session-keyed, but the object behind that key is not session-scoped. Landing one session's checkpoint would apply peers' in-flight edits along with it.

## Evidence

All read-only (`git for-each-ref`, `git diff --stat`, `git rev-parse`). Two refs in the 224-group verified identical on both axes — same tree **and** same parent, differing only in the stamp:

```
8d7a0310... -> tree=f4c1d814... parent=476240c9...
15511d3b... -> tree=f4c1d814... parent=476240c9...
```

## What is NOT being claimed

That the fix is obvious. Narrowing the capture to a session's own paths needs a source of truth for "this session's paths" that survives a crash — which is exactly what a checkpoint is for. A blunt narrowing would trade a too-wide snapshot for a lossy one, and losing a crashed session's edits is worse than storing too many. This ticket names the root cause and the measurements; the design is open.

## Checkable next step

Decide whether a checkpoint should be (a) whole-tree as today, with dedup happening at reap time on a duplicate-of-retained oracle, or (b) genuinely session-scoped at capture. Those lead to different fixes and (a) is strictly cheaper. #5340 is blocked on the same decision.

Found while investigating #5340; the reap-side consequences are recorded there.

records.title: trunk-red ledger: 28 rows are the build-check gate's own fixture and can never clear
records.body:
## What

28 rows in the production trunk-red ledger (`.fak/trunk-red.jsonl`) name the package `buildcheck.test/p` — the build-check gate's own test fixture. They are not real trunk breaks and they can never clear, because `buildcheck.test/p` is not a Go package anywhere in this module.

Verified directly:

```
$ rg -c 'buildcheck\.test/p' .fak/trunk-red.jsonl
28
```

## Why it matters

Until `71e166412` (#5356) these 28 rows were printed as live fleet blockers — `"Each break below is ALREADY red on the trunk — every clone that touches it inherits it"` — at the same moment `go build ./...` was exit 0. They were the single largest contributor to that false wall: 28 of the 37 surfaced classes.

`71e166412` fixed the *reporting* half. Each now carries a named reason:

```
- [unprovable: the failing package(s) are not inside this module] buildcheck.test/p
```

So they no longer lie. But they are still permanent residue in an append-only log that several gates hold open, and they still dominate the view — the honest reading of `fak trunk-red` today is "37 unprovable, 28 of which are a test fixture."

## Root cause

A gate's own fixture was able to write into the production ledger. Whatever scoping now prevents that came later than these rows; the investigation that surfaced this attributed the scoping fix to `c1fbc87ed`, but **I could not confirm that sha** — the repo was under heavy concurrent load and every `git log` probe timed out. Treat the sha as a lead to check, not as established. The 28-row count above is directly verified.

## Two things this ticket is NOT asking for

1. **Not a change to the fold.** `71e166412` deliberately drops nothing new, and the keep-side bias there is correct. Making the fold special-case these rows would put fixture knowledge into a general predicate.
2. **Not a blanket prune.** `bf458248ba` rejected prune generally, because it rewrites a live append-log that several gates hold open. That reasoning still stands and this ticket does not overturn it.

## Suggested next step

A one-off, narrowly-scoped removal of rows whose named package provably is not a Go package anywhere in the module — nothing broader. Because it mutates a ledger other gates read, it wants a maintainer's call rather than an automated pass, which is why it is filed rather than done.

Worth confirming first: that the write path which produced these rows really is closed, so a prune does not just refill.

Found while landing #5356; the reporting-side fix is there.

records.title: Three Python ps calls still use procps-only keywords, so an unmeasurable dimension reads as a measured zero
records.body:
## What

Three Python `ps` invocations still use procps-ng-only keywords. On a host whose `ps` is not procps-ng, the call errors and the result reads as a **silent zero** rather than a named absent measurement.

- `tools/dispatch_preflight.py:1442` — `nlwp`
- `tools/proc_resource_guard.py:689` — `cputimes`
- `tools/proc_resource_guard.py:784` — `etimes`

## Why this is filed separately

The Go half of exactly this defect was just fixed: `cmd/fak` used to run `ps -eo pid=,nlwp=,rss=,comm=`, and on a non-procps host the whole host-preflight process scan read as zero processes. That path now routes through `procguard.CollectProcesses`, and `internal/architest/ps_dialect_test.go` refuses any **Go** call naming `ps` with a procps-only keyword.

That gate is an AST gate over Go source. It structurally cannot see Python, so these three sites are out of its reach and there is nothing stopping the defect being reintroduced on the Python side.

## The failure mode is the point

The bug is not "the keyword is unportable" — it is that an *unmeasurable* dimension comes back indistinguishable from a *measured zero*. A host with no thread-count keyword should report "threads: not measured", never "threads: 0". Callers that cannot represent an absent measurement are part of the finding, not an obstacle to it.

## Constraint on the regression gate

A **new** `tools/*_test.py` cannot land — the pythongate ratchet refuses it. The gate must EXTEND a test file already listed in `internal/pythongate/baseline.go`. Also note CI runs `tools/*_test.py` **without** pytest, so any `__main__` block must stay last in the file and pytest-only features (fixtures, `parametrize`, assert rewriting) are unavailable.

## Suggested next step

Make the three invocations portable or platform-guarded, keep unmeasured distinct from zero, and add the regression assertion to an existing baselined Python test. A non-vacuity witness is expected: mutate the fixed call back to the procps-only keyword and show the gate failing, with a control that stays green.

Line numbers are from the state at filing and drift in a shared tree — re-verify each site before changing it. If one turns out to be already guarded, that is a legitimate partial refutation and worth recording rather than patching around.

Found while landing #5537.

records.title: resume stopped: first-generation dispatch workers record no driver pid, so the common case defers forever
records.body:
## What

`fak resume stopped` now classifies driver liveness from the process table (#5440, landed `c71025c06`), and the fail-safe is correct: a row only moves to RESUME when the census is readable, self-seen, a driver pid was recorded, and that pid is absent. Every other arm returns `LivenessUnknown` and defers.

The problem is that **the common case never supplies the witness**, so it defers forever.

A pid keyed by transcript UUID is written only by the resume watchdog — i.e. only for sessions that were already `--resume`d. A **first-generation** dispatch worker spawned as `claude -p …` has no UUID on argv, so no pid is ever recorded for it, so its liveness is `Unknown`, so it defers. In a real run on this host that was 12 `MIDTOOL_UNKNOWN` rows:

```
resume stopped  window=2h  resume=0 defer=4 skip=27
  driver liveness: 329 processes scanned, 319 recorded driver pids; 199 command lines not examined (unreadable)
liveness values seen: {'(unknown)': 63, 'live': 1, 'gone': 24}
```

This is honest behaviour, not a regression — the deferral is the fail-safe working. But it means the population #5386 was aimed at is still unresolved.

## The seam

`resume.IdentityRow` (`internal/resume/identitymap.go:43-57`) is the durable append-only uuid↔trace join. Its fields are `TS`, `UUID`, `Trace`, `Handle`, `Account`, `Via`. **There is no pid field.**

`recordGuardSessionStartIdentity` (`cmd/fak/guard_sessionstart.go:141`) writes those rows, and it already has the real transcript UUID in hand — it reads `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` out of the environment, which is populated for a first-generation worker too, not just a resumed one. So the one moment where the UUID is known *and* the process is alive is already instrumented; it simply records no process identity.

The row format is explicitly forward-compatible: the doc comment states unknown fields are dropped rather than trusted, so a forward-extended row still decodes on an older reader.

## Suggested next step

Record a process identity on the identity row at session start, and teach the liveness resolver to read it as a second source of recorded driver pids. Checkable step: after the change, a freshly dispatched first-generation `claude -p …` worker should produce an identity row carrying a pid, and killing that worker should move its row from `Unknown`/defer to `gone`/RESUME — with a control worker left alive staying `live`/skip.

## Constraints that are part of the ticket, not obstacles to it

- **Do not invert the fail-safe.** Five arms deliberately return `Unknown`: unreadable *or empty* census, no recorded pid, census that cannot see its own reader, pid running but command line unreadable, and pid reused by a different program. A change that resolves more rows by *assuming* liveness it did not witness is a regression dressed as a fix. The only new resolution allowed here is one backed by a pid that was actually recorded from a live process.
- **Which pid is the right pid is an open design question, not a settled one.** The hook runs as a child of the driver, so the obvious candidate is the parent — but parent-pid on a hook invocation is not self-evidently the driver on every platform, and a wrong pid is worse than no pid (it manufactures a false `gone` when that pid exits, or a false `live` on reuse). Establish which process is actually being identified before recording it, and if the answer is not stable, say so and stop rather than recording a guess.
- Pid reuse must stay defended: the existing resolver already cross-checks the command line and returns `Unknown` when it reads a different program. Any new pid source has to pass through the same check.
- `IdentityRow` is append-only and durable; older rows will have no pid. Absence must read as "not recorded", never as "gone".

Found while verifying #5440 (closed as already-fixed). Line numbers are from the state at filing and drift in a shared tree — re-verify each before changing it.

records.title: idea-scout re-files already-closed sources: the seen-cache is unreplicated local state and the 800-issue scan window has been outgrown
records.body:
## Summary

`docs/idea-scout.md:46` states the feeder's durability guarantee:

> "A source filed once is **never filed again, even years later**. This is the durable rung."

That guarantee is **false at HEAD**, and both dedup backstops have failed independently. The result is that `tools/idea_scout.py` re-files sources that were already triaged, closed, and written up — and the re-files land as fresh `needs-triage` tickets, so a triage worker re-does work that a previous worker already finished.

## Evidence — three sources re-filed after being closed AND written up

| Re-filed as | Original (CLOSED/COMPLETED) | Landed triage note |
|---|---|---|
| #5298 `fu351/Doberman-Core` | #528, closed 2026-06-23 | `docs/notes/RESEARCH-doberman-prior-art-triage-2026-06-23.md` |
| #5308 `tonbistudio/turboquant-pytorch` | #1266, closed 2026-06-29 | `docs/notes/RESEARCH-turboquant-kv-quant-triage-1266.md` |
| #5309 `luckyPipewrench/pipelock` | #1267, closed 2026-06-29 | `docs/notes/RESEARCH-pipelock-agent-egress-receipts-triage-2026-06-29.md` |

Separately, #5489 and #4393 carry the **identical** stamp `<!-- idea-scout-source: github:synvoya/codeinspectus -->`. It is the only duplicated `source_id` among the 67 currently-open `idea-scout:` tickets.

## Root cause — both backstops are out

**1. The seen-cache is unreplicated local state and was lost.**
`.idea-scout/seen.json` holds 52 entries, earliest `2026-07-16`. Cross-checking every open idea-scout ticket's stamp against it: 53 of 67 present, **14 absent** — precisely #4312–#4972 (filed 2026-07-11..07-15), plus all 29 closed ones. The file is gitignored (`.gitignore:422`), so nothing replicates it and nothing rebuilds it.

**2. The issue-body backstop is capped and the repo has outgrown the cap.**
`tools/idea_scout.py:162` sets `"issue_scan_limit": 800`, and `tools/idea_scout.py:527` fetches `gh issue list --state all --limit 800`. Running that exact query today returns issues **#4736–#5542 only**. Every idea-scout issue below #4736 — all 29 closed ones and 14 still-open ones — is invisible to dedup rungs 2 and 3. With ~1310 open issues and 1000+ created in the 2026-07-12..07-29 window alone, the 800-issue window now covers well under three weeks and keeps shrinking.

So a source filed more than ~3 weeks ago, on a host whose local cache has been cleared, is guaranteed to be re-filed.

## Why this is worth fixing before triaging the backlog

There are currently 67 open `idea-scout:` tickets. Triaging them while the feeder re-files already-closed sources means the backlog refills behind the worker.

## Success condition (exactly checkable)

Re-run the feeder's `--json` dry-run and confirm the `github:fu351/Doberman-Core`, `github:tonbistudio/turboquant-pytorch` and `github:luckyPipewrench/pipelock` source_ids are **dropped at the dedup rung**, naming which rung dropped each. The `docs/idea-scout.md:46` invariant should then be either restored in fact or amended to state the real guarantee.

## Not in scope

Closing the existing duplicates is separate bookkeeping; this ticket is the write path only.

## Related but distinct

#3947 and #4072–#4076 cover the decision-ledger and supersession edges. None of them address cache durability or the scan-limit window.

records.title: fix(ideascout): the Go port still rests dedup on an 800-issue recency window (the path SKILL.md points agents at)
records.body:
## The same windowed-dedup defect, in the path agents are told to use

#5543 fixed `tools/idea_scout.py`: the never-file-twice guarantee no longer rests on a
gitignored cache plus a recency window, but on a label-targeted enumeration
(`gh issue list --state all --label idea-scout`) whose size tracks the scout's own capped
output rather than the tracker's growth rate.

`internal/ideascout` + `cmd/fak/ideascout.go` (`fak idea-scout`) is a full, live-capable Go
port that still has the original defect:

- `internal/ideascout/ideascout.go:193` — `IssueScanLimit: 800`, the same window.
- `internal/ideascout/ideascout.go:803` — `fetcher.FetchExistingIssues(cfg.IssueScanLimit)`,
  the same windowed fetch (`LiveFetcher.FetchExistingIssues` at `:1085`).
- `internal/ideascout/ideascout.go:345` — the same three dedup rungs, with the durable
  guarantee resting on the same gitignored `seen.json` fast path.

## Why this is not covered by the Python fix

The daily scheduled task runs the **Python** (`docs/loops-inventory.md:38` →
`tools/idea_scout.py`, installed by `tools/register_idea_scout.ps1`), so the automated
filing path is fixed. But `.claude/skills/question-loop/SKILL.md:120` tells agents:

> To mine **external** sources for ideas → `fak idea-scout`.

So an agent or human following the skill invokes the **Go** binary. With `--live` that path
can still re-file a source whose original issue has aged out of the 800-window — exactly the
failure that produced #5298, #5308 and #5309 as duplicates of #528, #1266 and #1267.

## The defect is currently self-masking

Re-running either implementation today looks green, because the duplicates it already created
(#5298/#5308/#5309) sit *inside* the 800-window and are themselves matched. The bug unmasks as
those duplicates age out. Any verification must therefore simulate a narrower window (shrink
`issue_scan_limit`) rather than re-run at the current tip and observe a pass.

## Done when

- [ ] The Go port's durable rung is a query scoped to the deduped population (the `idea-scout`
      label), not a recency window — matching the Python's `filed-stamp` rung.
- [ ] A saturated scan **refuses** (ambiguous between complete and truncated) rather than
      silently proceeding on a truncated index.
- [ ] `seen.json` is a fast path only; losing it does not weaken the guarantee.
- [ ] A regression test pins that a source filed below the window is still deduped, proven
      with a shrunk window rather than at today's tip.
- [ ] The existing refusal when the scan fails outright is not relaxed.

## Prior art to clone

`tools/idea_scout.py` after #5543: `fetch_scout_issues()` / `stamp_index()`, the `filed-stamp`
rung reported separately from `issue-body`, and `scout_scan_limit` as a tripwire rather than a
window. Note the verified finding from that work: the `idea-scout` **label listing** is a
complete cover for genuinely-filed issues, whereas `gh search issues` full-text is not — it
missed 4 labelled issues (#861–864) and added 21 prose-only mentions carrying no real stamp.

records.title: feat(serve): the stream content-progress window has a config field and no operator route, so its escape hatch is unreachable
records.body:
## The window has a config field and no operator route

#5486 shipped a streaming CONTENT-progress deadline: how long a stream may stay warm
(keepalives arriving, so the inter-byte deadline never fires) without one frame that advances
the turn. It arrived reading `os.Getenv("FAK_STREAM_PROGRESS_TIMEOUT_S")`, which
`internal/envconfiglint`'s CONFIG_NOT_ENV ratchet correctly refused — a behavioral deadline is
configuration, not a credential.

The read has been relocated to the config surface: exported `agent.DefaultStreamProgressTimeout`
plus an `HTTPPlanner.StreamProgressTimeout` field, resolved by
`(*HTTPPlanner).streamProgressWindow`. That closes the ratchet, but **nothing in `cmd/fak` or
`internal/gateway` sets the field**, so the window is code-configurable only. Net effect today:
a hard 300s content-progress deadline with no operator-reachable escape hatch — the literal
`"0"`/`"off"` env spelling used to be that hatch, and its replacement (a negative field value)
is unreachable from a command line.

This is a small gap in practice — no tag contains `b66a2dba5`, so the env var was never in a
release, and the default is well above the worst prefill-to-first-token gap — but a provider
whose prefill legitimately outlasts the window currently has no way to say so.

## Done when

- [ ] `gateway.Config` carries the window, threaded onto the planner in
      `newConfiguredHTTPPlanner` (`internal/gateway/gateway.go`), the one place every
      `gateway.Config`-derived planner knob is set.
- [ ] `cmd/fak/serve.go` grows the matching flag, defaulting to
      `agent.DefaultStreamProgressTimeout` rather than a bare literal, so the constant stays the
      single source of truth (the `DefaultCtxViewBudget` idiom).
- [ ] The matching `servewiringData` row lands in `cmd/fak/servewiring.go` — a `Config` field
      `serve.go` sets with no row reds `fak serve-wiring --check` as UNAUDITED.
- [ ] `docs/serve-config.md` is regenerated.
- [ ] A test pins that the flag reaches `streamProgressWindow`, and that the disable spelling
      survives the trip end to end.

## Related: the ratchet has a scanner hole this class of bug walks through

`envConfigLint`'s scanner is a `git grep` for `os.Getenv("LITERAL")`, so a read that reaches
`os.Getenv` through a helper taking the key as a **parameter** is invisible to it.
`internal/agent/stream_stall.go:322 envClampedTimeout(key string, …)` is exactly that shape, and
two live reads hide behind it today — `FAK_STREAM_STALL_TIMEOUT_S`
(`internal/agent/stream_stall.go:241`) and `FAK_PLANNER_TIMEOUT_S`
(`internal/agent/chat.go:801`) — in neither `baseline.go` nor `admittedPostFreeze`, because the
gate cannot see them at all. `admitted.go` already documents the same SCANNER VISIBILITY hole
for `resolveChatopsEnv` / `resolveBudgetMS`.

Worth recording because it is also the cheapest **laundering** path available: deleting only a
literal `os.Getenv("X")` while keeping `envClampedTimeout("X", …)` turns the gate green with the
read fully intact and leaves no trace in the ledger. That path was identified and refused while
relocating the #5486 knob (the read was deleted outright), but the next author to hit the
ratchet will find it just as easily.

records.title: fix(cmd): `fak idea-scout` is unreachable — two skill lines point agents at a verb nothing dispatches
records.body:
## `fak idea-scout` is not a verb

Two skill lines tell agents to run it:

- `.claude/skills/question-loop/SKILL.md:22` — "| idea-scout (`fak idea-scout`) | mines **external** feeds (arXiv/GitHub/HN) for related **ideas** |"
- `.claude/skills/question-loop/SKILL.md:120` — "To mine **external** sources for ideas → `fak idea-scout`."

What an agent that follows them gets:

```
$ fak idea-scout --help
fak: unknown verb "idea-scout"
  'fak help' shows the overview; 'fak help --all' lists every verb.
```

This is not binary staleness. The command function exists and has **no caller anywhere in
the repo except its own test**:

```
$ grep -rn "runIdeaScout" --include=*.go .
cmd/fak/ideascout.go:13:func runIdeaScout(stdout, stderr io.Writer, argv []string) int {
cmd/fak/ideascout_test.go:34:  code := runIdeaScout(&stdout, &stderr, []string{
cmd/fak/ideascout_test.go:43:  t.Fatalf("runIdeaScout code=%d ...")
```

Compare a verb that *is* reachable — `ablate` — which has both a dispatch arm
(`cmd/fak/dojo.go:90 case "ablate":`) and a help row (`cmd/fak/help.go:78`). `idea-scout` has
neither. `cmd/fak/ideascout.go:14` builds a `flag.NewFlagSet("idea-scout", …)`, so the file
reads like a wired verb at a glance; nothing dispatches into it.

## Why this matters more than a missing help row

`internal/ideascout` is a full, live-capable Go port of `tools/idea_scout.py` — it can file
issues with `--live`. It has just had #5544's dedup fix landed (`00f270957d2a`). All of that
sits behind an entry point no operator or agent can reach, while the docs assert they can.
Effects, in order of cost:

1. An agent following the skill burns a turn on `unknown verb` and has no documented fallback.
2. The Go port's behavior is unexercised outside unit tests, so its divergence from the Python
   is invisible in practice.
3. `runIdeaScout` is an unexported symbol with exactly one module-wide use (its test), which is
   the shape the DEAD_CODE push gate flags.

## Also missing from the CLI reference

`docs/cli-reference.md` front-matter claims it documents "**every verb**". `idea-scout`
appears in it **zero** times. Eight *reachable* top-level verbs are absent too — `audit`,
`egress`, `info`, `ps`, `recover`, `resume`, `self-update`, `signal` — against 22 registered.
The file is hand-maintained; no generator writes it and no freshness check compares it against
the registered verb set, which is why the drift is silent. The repo already has the pattern to
copy: `db7843262` added a showcase-sync check to the README freshness audit.

## Done when

- [ ] Either `fak idea-scout` dispatches to `runIdeaScout` and carries a help row, **or** the
      two SKILL.md lines stop naming a verb that does not exist and name the real entry point
      (`tools/idea_scout.py`) instead. Decide which is intended — do not do both halves
      half-way.
- [ ] If it is wired: `docs/cli-reference.md` gains its row, and the `--live` path's blast
      radius is stated at the point of the flag (it files real issues).
- [ ] A check fails when a registered verb has no `docs/cli-reference.md` row, so the file's
      "every verb" claim is mechanical rather than aspirational. The eight absent verbs above
      are the current backlog for it.

records.title: test(ideascout): the two scout implementations share a contract with no mechanical guard, so the same defect had to be fixed twice
records.body:
## Two idea-scout implementations, one contract, no guard

`tools/idea_scout.py` and `internal/ideascout` implement the same never-file-twice contract.
Both were just fixed for the same defect, separately: `cfe66c656` (Python, #5543) and
`00f270957d2a` (Go, #5544). The second fix was needed *only because* the first one did not
propagate — which is the whole failure mode in one sentence.

Today the two are tied together by prose alone: `docs/idea-scout.md` carries a "Two
implementations, one contract" table. Nothing fails if a future edit changes one
implementation's dedup rungs and not the other's. The next divergence will be found the same
way this one was — after it re-files an already-triaged source.

## What would make the claim mechanical

A shared fixture corpus, asserted by both `tools/idea_scout_test.py` and
`internal/ideascout/ideascout_test.go`: the same candidate set, the same existing-issue set,
the same expected per-rung dedup verdict. A rung that changes in one implementation and not the
other then reds a test instead of aging into a duplicate issue.

The interesting cases are already written down on both sides — a source filed below the scan
window, a saturated index, a fetch failure with and without a seen-cache, and case-folded
`Acme/Repo` vs `acme/repo` — so the corpus is mostly a matter of lifting them into one JSON
file both suites read.

Note the constraint from `internal/pythongate/baseline.go`: a **new** `tools/*_test.py` cannot
land, so the Python half must extend `tools/idea_scout_test.py`, which is already in the
baseline. CI also runs `tools/*_test.py` **without** pytest, so the `__main__` block must stay
last.

## Related: a dead knob that can only weaken a refusal

`RunOptions.AllowIssueGap` (`internal/ideascout/ideascout.go:218`) is set by **no caller in the
repo** — it is only read, at `:915`, where it waives the refusal that fires when the window
fetch fails and no seen-cache exists. So its entire reachable effect is to turn a safety
refusal off, and nothing can currently turn it on. Either give it a caller with a stated reason
or drop it; a knob whose only possible use is to disable a guarantee should not sit there
unowned.

## Done when

- [ ] One fixture corpus is read by both test suites and pins the same per-rung verdicts.
- [ ] A rung changed in one implementation and not the other fails a test.
- [ ] `AllowIssueGap` is either wired to a real caller with a documented reason, or removed.

records.title: fix(agent): gemma4 partial prefix reuse prefills only the suffix — the "reuse is inert" invariant at gemma4_session.go:33 does not hold
records.body:
## A documented invariant that does not hold

`internal/model/gemma4_session.go:30-34` states, as the reason the recompute bridge is safe:

> Because it holds no K/V rows it leaves s.Cache untouched: `Cache.Len()` stays 0, and
> **eviction / prefix reuse are INERT rather than silently wrong.**

Eviction is indeed inert. **Prefix reuse is not.** A gemma4 session served through
`InKernelPlanner` with a *partial* prefix hit prefills only the suffix, against a session that
carries none of the prefix's history — wrong logits, no error, no panic.

## The path, link by link

Each line below was read at HEAD (local trunk, 51 commits ahead of `origin/main`).

1. `internal/agent/inkernel_planner.go:210-215` — reuse is enabled unconditionally on the host
   path:
   ```go
   func inKernelPlannerPrefixReuseSupported(m *model.Model, backend compute.Backend) bool {
       if backend == nil {
           return true
       }
       return m != nil && m.Cfg.InKernelBackendPrefixReuseSupported()
   }
   ```
   `backend == nil` is *exactly* the mode the gemma4 bridge is wired for —
   `gemma4_session.go:47-49` requires `s.Backend == nil && !s.Metal && !s.MetalQ4K &&
   s.PrecisionPolicy == nil`. So the one configuration gemma4 runs in is the one that skips the
   capability check entirely.

2. `internal/agent/inkernel_decode.go:196` — after a turn, `snap := s.Cache.Clone()` is admitted
   into the radix tree keyed by the full `ids`. For gemma4 that snapshot is **empty**.

3. `internal/radixkv/radixkv.go:793-806` — splitting that node does not reject it:
   ```go
   func truncatePrefix(c *model.KVCache, L int) *model.KVCache {
       cp := c.Clone()
       if L < cp.Len() { ... }   // Len()==0 ⇒ L < 0 ⇒ false
       return cp                 // non-nil, zero-length
   }
   ```

4. `internal/agent/inkernel_decode.go:68` — the nil-guard is the only gate, and an empty cache is
   not nil: `if k := b.KV(); k != nil { matchedKV = k.Clone() }`. Tree matching is on **token
   ids**, not on KV depth, so a later prompt sharing a prefix returns `m > 0`.

5. `internal/agent/inkernel_decode.go:418-427` — the rebuilt session drops the history:
   ```go
   s := p.m.NewSession()
   s.Cache = prefix
   ```
   `gemma4Hist` is never copied. `model.SessionFromPrefix` (`internal/model/kv.go:14-16`) has the
   same hole.

6. `internal/agent/inkernel_decode.go:157,173` — `prefillAt := matched`, then
   `logits = s.Prefill(ids[prefillAt:])`. The gemma4 recompute forward runs over **the suffix
   alone**, having been told the prefix is already in cache.

**The exact-hit case accidentally fails safe** and is why this has not been noticed:
`inKernelRefeedLastTokenForExactHit` (`inkernel_decode.go:429-430`) sees
`s.Cache.Len() (0) < promptLen` and discards the session. Only the **partial** hit is wrong —
i.e. the second turn of any multi-turn session, which is the common case in serve.

## Red-first witness — the harness already exists

`internal/ggufload/gemma4_test.go:157 tinyGemma4GGUF` builds a faithful 4-layer gemma4 GGUF
(3 sliding + 1 global, `head_dim` 16/32, `kv_heads` 2/1, `sliding_window: 2`), and
`internal/ggufload/gemma4_session_test.go:33` already asserts Session logits are bit-exact with
`Model.Forward`. So the new test is a small delta on an existing pattern:

- prefill prompt A through the reuse path and admit it;
- serve prompt A+B sharing a ~60% prefix through the same planner;
- compare against `Model.Forward(A+B)`.

That is red today. Note a plain unit test on `Session` alone will NOT catch this — the defect
lives in the planner's reuse wiring, so the test has to go through the reuse path.

## Two candidate fixes

1. **Fail closed** — a `Config.isGemma4()` arm in `inKernelPlannerPrefixReuseSupported`. Smallest
   diff; makes the `gemma4_session.go:33` comment true.
2. **Carry the history** — teach `SessionFromPrefix` / the planner's prefix clone to copy
   `gemma4Hist`. Strictly better: reuse becomes *correct but not yet cheap* (the recompute still
   re-runs the whole prefix), which turns the eventual cached path (#5496) into a pure
   performance change rather than a semantics change.

Either way the false sentence at `gemma4_session.go:33` must be corrected, since it is the thing
that made the hazard invisible.

## Scope note

This is **not** #5496. #5496 asks for a cached KV path (a performance feature, and per-layer
window bounding there is genuinely epic-sized because `KVCache.pos` is one array shared across
layers — `internal/model/kvcache.go:17`). This ticket is a correctness bug that exists *because*
#5496 has not landed, and it should be fixed first and independently.

## Open question an implementer should settle first (~10 min)

Whether a gemma4 GGUF can currently boot end-to-end through `fak serve` on the `InKernelPlanner`
route. Every link above was verified by reading, but that last step was not. If serve cannot yet
reach it, this is a **latent** bug rather than a live one — still worth landing fail-closed, but
the urgency changes. Say which it is in the fix.

## Done when

- [ ] A test drives a partial prefix hit for gemma4 through the planner's reuse path and compares
      against `Model.Forward`, and it is red before the fix.
- [ ] Partial prefix reuse for gemma4 either fails closed or carries `gemma4Hist`.
- [ ] `internal/model/gemma4_session.go:33`'s "INERT rather than silently wrong" claim is true, or
      corrected.

records.title: fix(ideascout): the HackerNews and Reddit lanes exist only in the Go scout, so a topic naming them silently gathers nothing on the scheduled Python path
records.body:
## Two source lanes exist in Go and not in Python — and Python is the one that runs

Surfaced while landing #5547 (the shared dedup corpus). That work tied the two scouts' **dedup**
contract together mechanically. This is a second, larger divergence one stage earlier, in
**gather**, and the corpus does not cover it.

`internal/ideascout`'s `GatherCandidates` has four source lanes:

```
internal/ideascout/ideascout.go:1057   appendPointsLane(..., "hn",     ..., ParseHackerNewsJSON)
internal/ideascout/ideascout.go:1062   appendPointsLane(..., "reddit", ..., ParseRedditJSON)
internal/ideascout/ideascout.go:638    func ParseHackerNewsJSON(...)
internal/ideascout/ideascout.go:697    func ParseRedditJSON(...)
internal/ideascout/ideascout.go:1166   func (f LiveFetcher) FetchHackerNews(...)
internal/ideascout/ideascout.go:1195   func (f LiveFetcher) FetchReddit(...)
```

`tools/idea_scout.py`'s `gather_candidates` (:738) has two — arXiv and GitHub:

```
tools/idea_scout.py:745   if topic.get("arxiv"):
tools/idea_scout.py:751   if topic.get("github"):
```

A case-insensitive search of `tools/idea_scout.py` for `hackernews|reddit|hn` returns **zero**
matches, and its `Topic` carries no such keys.

**Which one actually runs matters, and it is the Python one.** `.claude/skills/scout-loop/SKILL.md:12`
and `:28` both name `tools/idea_scout.py` as the automated feed ("files deduped `idea-scout` triage
issues from arXiv + GitHub"), and `tools/register_scout_loop.ps1` registers `FleetScoutLoop` around
it.

So a topic config naming `hn` or `reddit` sources **silently gathers nothing** on the scheduled
path. Not an error, not a warning — those keys are simply never read, so the lane contributes zero
candidates and the run reports a normal success.

## The docs claim the coverage that does not exist

`.claude/skills/question-loop/SKILL.md:22` describes the tool as one that

> mines **external** feeds (arXiv/GitHub/**HN**) for related **ideas**

HN is advertised. On the path that actually runs on a cadence, HN is not implemented.

`docs/idea-scout.md` describes only arXiv + GitHub, so it is honest about Python and **lags the Go**,
which has had four lanes for some time. Between the two docs, a reader can conclude either that HN
works or that it does not exist at all; neither is the true state.

## Note this is the same failure mode as #5543/#5544, one stage earlier

#5543 fixed a dedup defect in Python; #5544 had to fix the identical defect in Go because it did not
propagate. #5547 answered that for **dedup** with a shared fixture corpus both suites read. Gather is
the same shape of hazard with no such guard: two implementations of one contract, drifting silently,
where the drift is only visible when someone reads both files side by side.

## Done when

- [ ] Either the Python scout grows the `hn` and `reddit` lanes, **or** the Go lanes are documented as
      Go-only and `.claude/skills/question-loop/SKILL.md:22` stops advertising HN. Decide which —
      do not do both halves half-way.
- [ ] A config naming a source lane the running implementation cannot serve **fails loudly** instead
      of gathering zero and reporting success. Silence is the actual defect here; a topic key that no
      code reads should refuse, not no-op.
- [ ] `docs/idea-scout.md`'s source-lane list matches whatever the answer is, on both sides.

## Smaller thing found in the same pass, recorded so it is not lost

The two implementations order two refusals differently: Go checks "every source failed" **before** the
scout-index fetch (`internal/ideascout/ideascout.go:875-877`), Python checks it **after**
(`tools/idea_scout.py:873-876`). When both conditions hold, Go says `every source failed` and Python
says `cannot build the filed-issue index`. Both still refuse with exit 2, so there is no safety
difference — only the refusal text differs. Left alone deliberately; noted in case it confuses someone
debugging a refusal.

records.title: fix(leaseref): sync fails on a clone with zero lease refs — a zero-match push refspec exits 1, not 0
records.body:
`fak leaseref sync` fails on a clone that holds zero lease refs, because a zero-match push refspec exits 1.

## The wrong claim

`internal/leaseref/sync.go:53-55` states:

> a wildcard refspec matching ZERO refs is a successful no-op in git, so syncing an empty namespace is clean on both sides.

That is **true for fetch and false for push.** Git answers a zero-match push refspec with:

