records.title: Epic: centralized fleet control — one control point, N instances, command out / ack back
records.body:
## Epic: centralized fleet control — one control point, N instances, command out / ack back

Sibling of the out-of-band operator control epic #2753, one layer up. #2753 answers *"how do
I change what **this session** is doing?"* — a closed, typed, witnessed control vocabulary
over ONE live session's drive state. This epic answers the question #2753 explicitly fences
out: **"how do I change what the whole fleet is doing, from one place, and know it took?"**

### The concrete motivating case

An operator runs `fak accounts add`. Every live worker that was parked on seat exhaustion
should now go. Today that means finding every box, finding every session on every box, and
hand-fanning a signal to each — or killing and relaunching the wave. There is no
"tell the fleet `go`, and show me who heard."

Verified at HEAD: **nothing fires after `fak accounts add`** (`runAccountsAdd` ends at
`saveAccountsRegistry` + `syncViews` + `verifyServableAfterSync`), and **no loop-over-instances
caller exists anywhere** — `fak signal <id> steer` targets exactly one trace id against one
`--addr`.

### Current state — four halves, no whole

fak has every *half* of a fleet control plane and no plane:

| Half | Where | What it does | Why it is not the plane |
|---|---|---|---|
| The op grammar | `internal/sessionctl` (#2754) | Closed control-op vocabulary: per-op capability / boundary / witness / refusal | Per-**session**. Says nothing about who to send to, or how many heard. |
| The fan-out | `internal/sessionctl/broadcast.go` (#2764) | Fans ONE lifecycle op across a lane/wave/label selector | Explicitly per-**gateway** — one process's `session.Table`. Payload ops (`steer`/`redirect`) refused `BROADCAST_MALFORMED`. No ack. **And it has zero callers** — no CLI, no route. |
| The reach | `internal/fleetspine` | Live LAN peer discovery, UDP multicast heartbeat | Deliberately **display-only and one-way**: "carries ONLY display metadata — never a token or a request payload". Peers push; nothing is ever sent *to* a peer. |
| The registry | `internal/leaseref` | Cross-host live **session** descriptors (`refs/fak/locks/session-<id>`, TTL heartbeat, `ClassifyLiveness`) | Registers sessions, opt-in (`guardDurabilityWanted`), git-mediated. GET-only: the only write plane is lease acquire/renew/release, not a command fan-out. |

The gap is the join: **no cross-process addressing of a command, no payload, no return path.**

### Why the return path is the load-bearing half

fak already learned this lesson once, at the gateway steer route
(`internal/gateway/http.go`, `STEER_NO_OWNED_LOOP`): a serve process with no owned agent loop
refuses an enqueued steer with a closed reason rather than returning a false `202`, because
*"an enqueued steer there would sit in a mailbox nothing drains — an accepted-but-never-applied
phantom."*

That refusal is not rare. `Server.ownsSessionLoop()` returns `s.native`, so **every non-native
serve refuses a steer**. A fleet broadcast without acks would report success into that.

"I sent `go` to the fleet" is worth nothing without *"…and 11 of 14 instances applied it, 2
refused `STEER_NO_OWNED_LOOP`, 1 never answered."* **The ack is not a nicety; it is the
anti-phantom device** — and it is why this is an epic rather than a flag on
`sessionctl.Broadcast`.

### The core move

A **fleet control bus**: a transport-neutral data contract with three records and one
invariant.

- **Directive** — one op, plus a payload, a selector, an issuer, a TTL, and a
  content-addressed id. The id is the idempotency key: at-least-once delivery, **exactly-once
  application**.
- **Instance** — a self-announced presence record for a process that *can apply* a directive.
  This is what makes an ack report meaningful: without a declared roster there is no
  **denominator**, and "everyone acked" is unfalsifiable.
- **Ack** — one instance's outcome for one directive: a closed status (`applied` / `refused`
  / `expired`) and, on refusal, the **local** closed token the underlying op already refuses
  with. A fanned op refuses exactly as it would alone.

The invariant: **a directive is never its own witness.** The publish is not the proof; the ack
from the instance that consumed it at its own boundary is. This is `sessionctl`'s
witness-of-applied contract lifted from one loop to N processes.

Multiple control points are first-class, not an afterthought: the issuer is stamped on every
envelope, ordering is per-directive rather than global, and idempotency is per
`(directive, instance)` — so two operators issuing concurrently never double-apply and never
clobber each other. (Today there is no issuer identity anywhere: `SteerRequest.Principal` and
`sessionctl.Move.Source` are documented as attribution that confers no trust.)

### Children (worst-first)

- [x] **Spine** — directive / instance / ack envelopes, closed refusal vocabulary, the
      directory-backed transport, the roster+ack fold, `fak fleet control`, and ONE real
      production consumer that drains and acks (the e2e spine) — **landed** `bb2401e7a5`, #5600
- [ ] Cross-host transports behind the same interface: the git-mediated `leaseref` path, then
      the private comms bridge
- [ ] Roster join with `leaseref.LiveSessions` / `ClassifyLiveness` — bus membership corroborated
      by the existing cross-host registry instead of self-report alone
- [ ] Capability floor on publish — `sessionctl.CapOperatorControl` actually gated, not merely
      named (the fence #2753 carries today)
- [ ] Payload ops beyond `steer`: fleet-scoped `redirect` (structured objective change)
- [ ] Ack-driven follow-through: retry the outstanding set, escalate the refused set
- [ ] `fak accounts add --then-go` — the motivating case wired to the bus
- [ ] Doctrine page + front-door binding + a completeness gate over the bus vocabulary (the
      twin of `cmd/fak/control_plane_doc_test.go`)

### Spine repairs

Filed 2026-08-06 from a HEAD verification pass over the landed spine (after #5637-#5640). Each was
re-confirmed against the tree at filing time; two were witnessed live rather than read.

- [ ] #5822 — `Outcome.Affected` counts sessions the selector *matched*, not sessions whose run
      state changed, so an all-no-op fan acks `11/11 session(s) took it` at exit 0 (live-witnessed)
- [ ] #5823 — a retained directive still applies to instances that boot *after* the operator's
      exit 0, so a `terminate`/`pause` keeps acting on a report already closed
- [ ] #5824 — the default serve bus identity is neither restart-stable nor collision-proof, so the
      exactly-once apply claim breaks in both directions
- [ ] #5825 — `--fleet-bus-dir` scopes only the bus; the applier still mutates every session in the
      host's shared registry (live-witnessed: 12 sessions belonging to other agents were paused)
- [ ] #5826 — `foldFleetControl` discards the roster read error, reporting an unreadable roster as
      an empty fleet and completing on a denominator it failed to read
- [ ] #5827 — `send` and `status` hard-code the 90s roster TTL that only `instances --ttl` can change
- [ ] #5828 — `awaitFleetControl` sleeps on the wall clock inside a seam-measured budget, so the
      wait-expiry path (exit 1 after a real wait) has no test

### Honest fences

- The bus **carries** control ops; it does not invent them. The op set is `sessionctl`'s
  closed vocabulary, and each op keeps its declared boundary — a fanned `pause` still lands at
  the target's next turn boundary, never mid-decode.
- "Cross-host" in v1 means *a shared directory* (`FLEET_STATE_DIR` already exists as exactly
  that seam). That is a real cross-**process** control plane, and an honest cross-**host** one
  only where the directory is shared. The transport is an interface so this is a swap, not a
  rewrite — and the limitation is stated, not hidden.
- Bus membership is **"who can apply a directive"**, which is *not* the same set as
  `leaseref`'s "who has a live session". Joining the two is a named child above, not an
  assumption.
- An instance that cannot apply an op **must** ack refused with a closed token. Silent success
  is the one outcome the design forbids.

### Related

#2753 (per-session control vocabulary — the op grammar this bus carries) · #2764 (the
per-gateway fan-out this generalizes) · #2259 (inbound Slack chatops — a future control point)
· `internal/fleetspine` (peer discovery — the read-only twin) · `internal/leaseref` (the
cross-host session registry).

<!-- fak-fleet-control-key: epic -->

records.title: fleetbus: fleet control bus spine — directive out, ack back, one real drainer
records.body:
First child of the centralized-fleet-control epic #5599. This is the **e2e spine**:
the smallest thing that makes "one control point → N live instances → acks back" *true*,
end to end, with a real production consumer draining it.

## Parent context

#5599 (centralized fleet control). Op grammar comes from #2753 / `internal/sessionctl`;
the per-gateway fan-out this generalizes is #2764.

## Current state

Three halves, no whole:

- `internal/sessionctl/broadcast.go` (#2764) fans ONE lifecycle op across a selector, but
  is scoped **per-gateway** — "the fan-out is over ONE process's `session.Table`; cross-host
  fleet broadcast is out of scope" — and refuses every payload-carrying op
  (`BROADCAST_MALFORMED`). No ack.
- `internal/fleetspine` discovers LAN peers by multicast heartbeat but is **display-only and
  one-way** by construction: "carries ONLY display metadata — never a token or a request
  payload".
- `internal/sessionctl/vocab.go` (#2754) declares the closed op set with per-op capability /
  boundary / witness / refusal — for one session.

So an operator who adds an account today cannot say "fleet, go" and learn who heard.

## Why this is next

Every other child of the epic (cross-host transports, capability floor, retry/escalate,
`accounts add --then-go`) needs the same three envelopes and the same ack fold. Building any
of them first means building this one badly, inline. And the ack half must exist from the
first commit: fak already refuses to return a false `202` for an undeliverable steer
(`STEER_NO_OWNED_LOOP`, `internal/gateway/http.go`) precisely because *"an enqueued steer
would sit in a mailbox nothing drains — an accepted-but-never-applied phantom."* A fleet
broadcast without acks is that phantom times N.

## Working spine

```
fak fleet control send --all --op steer --text "go" --ttl 10m --wait 30s
  ->  directive  { id, issuer, selector, op, payload, ttl }  appended to the bus
  ->  N live instances (each a running `fak serve`) drain it at their tick,
      apply it locally through the SAME per-session write the single-session verbs ride,
      and append one ack each { directive, instance, status, reason, witness }
  ->  the control point folds roster + acks and prints:
      targeted 14 · applied 11 · refused 2 (CONTROL_SESSION_TERMINAL) · outstanding 1
```

## In scope

1. **`internal/fleetbus`** — the pure core + the v1 transport:
   - `Directive` / `Instance` / `Ack` envelopes with schema tags
     (`fak.fleetbus.{directive,instance,ack}/v1`). The bus **declares no op values**: it is a
     carrier, and the *applier* owns op meaning. So the closed `sessionctl` vocabulary is
     neither re-declared nor imported here — `cmd/fak`'s applier is what consults
     `sessionctl.Spec`, and an op it does not know is acked `FLEETBUS_UNKNOWN_OP`, never
     silently dropped. That keeps `internal/fleetbus` at architest tier 1 (stdlib + `flock`),
     the same posture as `internal/fleetspine`, and keeps it reusable for control ops that are
     not session ops.
   - `Selector` over instance axes (instance / machine / role) **and** session axes
     (lane / wave / label), plus an explicit affirmative `All` token. An **empty** selector is
     refused `FLEETBUS_MALFORMED` — match-all must be *stated*, never defaulted (the same
     fail-closed fence `sessionctl.Broadcast` sets).
   - Closed refusal vocabulary: `FLEETBUS_MALFORMED`, `FLEETBUS_EXPIRED`,
     `FLEETBUS_NO_TARGET`, `FLEETBUS_UNKNOWN_OP`, `FLEETBUS_APPLY_REFUSED` (the last carries
     the underlying local token verbatim — a fanned op refuses exactly as it would alone).
     Each gets a `[reasons.*]` block in `dos.toml`.
   - `Bus` interface (Announce / Instances / Publish / Directives / Ack / Acks) with ONE
     shipped implementation: a **directory-backed** bus — presence files per instance,
     `internal/flock`-guarded JSONL appends for directives and acks, and a per-`(instance,
     directive)` applied-marker for **exactly-once application under at-least-once delivery**.
   - `Drain(bus, self, applier, now)` — the instance side. Non-matching directives are
     skipped silently (the control point computes the expected set from the roster, so
     silence is not ambiguity); matching ones are applied once and acked; a directive past
     its TTL is acked `expired`, never applied.
   - `Fold(directive, roster, acks, now) Report` — the control side: targeted / applied /
     refused / expired / **outstanding** / complete. Outstanding is computable **only**
     because the roster supplies the denominator; that is why `Instance` exists.
2. **`fak fleet control`** — `send` / `status` / `instances` / `drain`, as a subcommand group
   under the existing `fak fleet` door (`cmd/fak/fleet.go`), `--json` on every read.
3. **One real production consumer** — `fak serve` announces itself to the bus and drains on a
   ticker (the `startGatewayUsageSnapshotLoop` pattern in `cmd/fak/serve_stages.go`), with an
   applier that routes lifecycle ops through `session.Table.Transition` and `steer` through
   the existing `steerSession` (`cmd/fak/main_session_control.go`) — the same writes the
   single-session verbs ride, so every op keeps its declared boundary. Off by default; armed
   by one flag.

## Out of scope

- Any transport other than the directory bus. The `Bus` interface exists so the git-mediated
  and private-bridge transports are a swap; they are separate children.
- The capability floor on publish (`CapOperatorControl` stays *named, not gated* — the same
  fence #2753 carries today).
- Retry / escalation of the outstanding set; `fak accounts add --then-go`; a TUI surface;
  fleet-scoped `redirect`.
- Editing `internal/sessionctl` or `internal/session`. This leaf **composes** them.

## Done condition

An operator on one box runs `fak fleet control send --all --op steer --text "go"` and a
second, independently-launched process applies it and acks; `fak fleet control status <id>`
prints a fold whose `outstanding` reaches 0. A directive is applied **at most once** per
instance across repeated drains, an expired directive is acked `expired` and never applied,
and an instance that cannot apply acks `refused` with the underlying closed token — never
silently.

## Witness

- `go test ./internal/fleetbus/...` — envelope/selector tables, the closed refusal set, the
  exactly-once marker under repeated drains, TTL expiry, and the fold's outstanding math.
- A **cross-process** e2e test: a temp bus dir, one publisher and N drainers in separate
  goroutines/processes, asserting N acks, `Complete == true`, and no double-apply.
- `go test ./cmd/fak -run FleetControl` — the CLI e2e over a temp `--bus` dir: send →
  drain → status, asserting the printed fold.

## Acceptance gate

`fak buildcheck --vet ./internal/fleetbus ./cmd/fak` then
`go test ./internal/fleetbus/... ./cmd/fak -run 'FleetBus|FleetControl'` (under WSL on the
Windows dev box, per AGENTS.md).

## Closure binding

Closing commit subject ends with `(fak fleetbus)` and references this issue.

## Work unit

leaf

## Expected steps

6

## Assumptions

- Op *meaning* belongs to the applier, not the carrier — so the bus can stay tier 1 and the
  closed `sessionctl` vocabulary is consulted exactly once, in `cmd/fak`, without editing
  `internal/sessionctl`.
- `internal/flock` + a per-record applied-marker file are sufficient coordination for
  multi-writer append on one filesystem; no daemon or lock server is needed.
- `defaultFleetRegistryDir()` (`cmd/fak/resume_sweep_cli.go` — `FLEET_STATE_DIR` →
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%/Fleet` → repo `tools/_registry`) is the right home and the existing
  "point it at a share for cross-host" seam.

## Confusion risks

- **This is not `sessionctl.Broadcast`.** That is per-gateway, lifecycle-only, ack-less.
  This carries payloads across processes and returns a witness.
- **This is not `fleetspine`.** That is one-way display discovery and must stay
  payload-free; the bus is the deliberate second, payload-carrying channel — do not merge
  them.
- **The publish is not the witness.** The ack from the consuming instance is. A `send` that
  reports "published" and nothing else has not proven anything.
- **`fak fleet control` vs `fak steering` / `fak steer` / `fak signal … steer`** — the
  existing three-way `steer` name collision documented in `docs/operator-control-plane.md`.
  This adds a *fleet-scoped carrier*, not a fourth meaning of "steer".
- Roster liveness here is **self-report freshness**, not a process-table join — the honest
  UNKNOWN rung, same as `fleetmon.Census`.

## Coordination notes

- New lane `fleetbus` (`internal/fleetbus/**`) — must be added to `dos.toml` (`lanes.trees`
  + the leaf list) and to the `tier` map in `internal/architest/architest_test.go`.
- Touches `cmd/fak/fleet.go` (one `subcommand` row), `cmd/fak/serve_stages.go` (one loop
  arm), `internal/devindex/verbs.go` (the `fleet` synopsis), `docs/cli-reference.md`.
  This tree is shared and dirty — commit by explicit path only.
- No edits to `internal/sessionctl` or `internal/session`; import-only.

## Trigger

Decomposition of the centralized-fleet-control epic #5599.

## Batch policy

One issue per bus concern; this leaf is the spine, the transports/floor/follow-through are
separate children of the epic.

## Lane

fleetbus

## Path hints

- `internal/fleetbus/**`
- `cmd/fak/fleet_control.go`
- `cmd/fak/fleet.go`
- `cmd/fak/serve_stages.go`
- `internal/devindex/verbs.go`
- `dos.toml`
- `internal/architest/architest_test.go`

records.title: epic(hooks): ground every gate verdict in the domain it quantified over (fak hooks)
records.body:
## The class

`∀x ∈ ∅ P(x)` is **true**. A check whose domain is empty is green and blind at the same
time, and its output is byte-identical to a check that really did judge everything. The
failure mode of such a lint is a *green tick*, which is worse than no lint — nobody
investigates a pass.

fak has already paid this class in several places and already fixed it in four others. That
is what makes it worth naming as a class rather than patching case by case.

## Where fak already gets this right — copy these, do not re-invent

- **`cmd/fak/hooks.go:390-393`** — `pre-commit: %d of %d gate(s) skipped (fail-open) — this
  commit ran a DEGRADED gate set: %s`. #5299 / #5335 made the *gate-set* denominator visible,
  so "every gate ran clean" became distinguishable from "PUBLIC_LEAK never ran and the rest
  were clean" — two states the hook used to report identically.
- **`internal/hooks/hooks.go:37-40`** — `ErrCouldNotRun` maps to exit 2, fail-open. A gate
  that could-not-run never impersonates a gate that passed. Soundness before completeness.
- **`internal/hooks/failclosed_ledger_test.go:110-125`** — bidirectional set membership: a
  gate registered with no ledger row fails, and a ledger row naming no registered gate fails.
  Neither direction can drift silently as gates are added.
- **`internal/architest/architest_test.go:22`** — the same binding at tree scale: every
  internal package must declare a tier row, enforced by a test rather than asserted in prose.
- **`cmd/fak/test.go:253`** — `unknown check %q`. A typo'd selector *refuses* instead of
  selecting nothing, running nothing, and exiting 0.

## The invariant this epic buys

**A verdict names the size of the domain it quantified over, or it is not a verdict.**

`0 findings` and `0 findings over 47 candidates` are different instruments. Only the second
can be trusted, because only the second can be *refuted* — it carries, on the same line, the
number that would expose it as vacuous.

The same reasoning already justifies exit 2 in `internal/hooks`: could-not-run must never
render as passed. This epic extends that discipline one step, from *the gate ran* to *the
gate had something to judge*.

## Leaves

Each is independently landable. **None changes any gate's verdict, mode default, or
fail-open behaviour** — this epic is about what a verdict *reports*, never what it *decides*.

**Core grounding — the modular example and its siblings**

- [ ] #5602 — **per-gate candidate denominator.** The exemplar for the whole class:
      `--json` reports `count: 0` identically whether 40 files were judged or none, and the
      human clean path prints nothing at all.
- [ ] #5603 — **name the scope the run judged.** "Clean" from a staged-only run and "clean"
      from a whole-tree run are different claims sharing one word.
- [ ] #5604 — **a selector that matches nothing must refuse.** `fak hygiene --gates TYPO`
      today runs zero gates and exits 0 clean. Live bug.
- [ ] #5605 — **bind an exhaustiveness claim to its registry.** `internal/hooks`'s own header
      says "all 8 gates"; `PreCommitGates()` registers 17.

**Applications of the same pattern to other surfaces**

- [ ] #5607 — **an agent-lifecycle hook that could not run must say so.** Every hook in
      `.claude/settings.json` ends `subprocess.call(...); sys.exit(0)`, discarding the child's
      exit code — a guard that fails to start reports the same success as one that admitted.
- [ ] #5608 — **bind the refusal-reason vocabulary to its emitters.** 74 of 75 declared
      reasons are wired; one is unemittable, and nothing would have caught it.
- [ ] #5609 — **a generator must refuse an empty provenance value.** The disambiguation
      scorecard renders `| As of |  (fak ) |` while five sibling scorecards carry a real date
      and version. Also: entries have no stable id to cite.
- [ ] #5610 — **a checked shape contract for the explainer description** (`gen/next`; no
      correctness defect behind it, unlike the leaves above).

## Out of scope

Changing what any gate *decides* — verdicts, mode defaults, escape hatches, or the fail-open
contract. A gate that today blocks must still block; a gate that today warns must still warn.

## Why an epic rather than eight unrelated issues

They share one acceptance test in spirit: take a fixture whose domain is empty, run the
check, and confirm the output is *not* byte-identical to a genuine full pass. Filed
separately they read as small polish items; filed together they are one trust floor.

## Honest scope note

Three of these (#5604, #5608, #5609) are live defects verified against the tree. The rest are
missing *reporting*, not broken behaviour — fak's gate layer is in good shape, and two
candidate findings were dropped during this audit precisely because the mechanism already
existed. This epic should be read as hardening a strong surface, not repairing a weak one.

## Boundary notes

Public issue. Every path, line number, count and quoted string above was read from the public
tree.

records.title: feat(hooks): report each gate's candidate denominator, not only its verdict (fak hooks)
records.body:
**Parent context:** #5601 (grounding epic) · `cmd/fak/hooks.go:390-393`, the gate-set
denominator landed by #5299 / #5335

**Generation:** now · **Work unit:** leaf · **Expected steps:** 4

## Current state

`fak hooks pre-commit --json` emits exactly four keys (`cmd/fak/hooks.go`,
`emitFindingsJSON`):

```json
{"findings": [], "count": 0, "skipped_gates": [], "skipped_count": 0}
```

That payload is **byte-identical** across two different worlds:

1. A large staged set where every enabled gate ran and each one genuinely found nothing.
2. A staged set where every gate ran but each one's own filter admitted **zero** items — no
   `.go` file for `GOFMT`, no doc for `INDEX_SYNC`, no new `internal/<leaf>/` for
   `UNTIERED_LEAF`.

The human path is worse. On a fully clean run `runHooksPreCommit`
(`cmd/fak/hooks.go:286-407`) prints **nothing at all** and returns 0. Silence reads as
"checked, nothing owed"; it equally means "nothing was checked."

fak already counts the **gate** denominator — `%d of %d gate(s) skipped` — so a degraded run
is visible. The missing half is the **candidate** denominator: how many staged items each
gate actually quantified over. 54 files match `internal/hooks/gate_*.go`; none reports one.

## Why this is next

This is the smallest change that turns the pre-commit report from an assertion into a
measurement, and it is the exemplar the other three leaves of #5601 copy. It is also the
cheapest place in the tree to prove the pattern: the gates already parse the staged diff
once, so the count is a length, not a new traversal — no extra `git` spawn, which matters
because the whole hook runs inside one wall clock (#5335).

Without it, the security-relevant gates (`PUBLIC_LEAK`, `SECRET_SHAPE`) report the same
clean payload whether they scanned forty files or none, and no consumer downstream can tell.

## Working spine

`fak hooks pre-commit --json` reports, per gate, how many staged candidates that gate
judged — so a gate that judged zero is visibly distinct from a gate that judged forty and
found nothing.

## Priority context

- **Working path:** staged diff → gate set → verdict a human or the dispatch loop trusts.
- **Current blocker:** the verdict carries no domain size, so "clean" is unfalsifiable.
- **Unblocks:** #5601 leaves B, C and D all reuse the reporting shape this lands.
- **Not polish:** this is the trust floor under every other gate; it is upstream of tuning
  any individual gate's precision.

## In scope

- Widen the gate result so a `Check` can return its candidate count alongside its findings —
  e.g. a `GateResult{Findings []Finding; Candidates int}`, or a second return value. Keep the
  `Finding` struct byte-unchanged so every existing JSON consumer still parses.
- Populate the count in each `internal/hooks/gate_*.go` as the number of staged items that
  gate's own filter admitted. The unit is per gate — files for file-scoped gates, added lines
  for line-scoped ones — and naming the unit matters more than forcing one unit on all of them.
- Add a `gates` array to the `--json` payload:
  `[{"gate": "GOFMT", "candidates": 12, "findings": 0}, ...]`, leaving `findings`, `count`,
  `skipped_gates` and `skipped_count` exactly as they are.
- Print one human summary line on the clean path, so silence stops carrying two meanings:
  `pre-commit: clean — N gate(s) over M staged file(s)`.

## Out of scope

- Any change to what a gate *decides*: verdicts, mode defaults, escape envs, fail-open.
- The whole-tree gates behind `fak hygiene` — same class, different surface (that is leaf B).
- Removing or renaming any existing `--json` key.

## Done condition

A test stages a fixture whose files match zero gate filters and asserts the report is
distinguishable from a fixture where the gates ran over real candidates. Today both produce
`count: 0` and, on the human path, no output whatsoever.

**Witness:** `go test ./internal/hooks ./cmd/fak -run 'Hooks|Gate'`

**Acceptance gate:** `go test ./internal/hooks ./cmd/fak -run Hooks`

## Assumptions

- Every gate can derive its candidate count from the already-parsed `StagedDiff` without a
  further `git` spawn — required, since the hook is wall-clock bounded (#5335).
- Downstream consumers read `findings` and `count`; adding keys is safe, changing them is not.

## Confusion risks

- **Candidate denominator ≠ gate denominator.** `skipped_count` (#5299) counts *gates that
  produced no verdict*. This issue counts *the items each gate judged*. A run can report
  `skipped_count: 0` — every gate ran — and still have judged nothing at all.
- **Candidates ≠ findings.** 40 candidates and 0 findings is the healthy case. The point is
  being able to see the 40.
- Not `Severity` (#4328), which grades a finding that already exists.
- Not a coverage metric. This is the domain of one run, not of the test suite.

## Coordination notes

- `cmd/fak/hooks.go` is shared with the hook-budget work (#5335) — rebase onto it rather than
  holding the file.
- Avoid concurrent edits to `internal/hooks/hooks.go` while a peer is registering a new gate;
  `PreCommitGates()` is the collision point.

## Trigger

Filed from an audit of the pre-commit report surface for the class in #5601.

## Batch policy

One issue for the whole gate set. Do **not** open one issue per `gate_*.go` file — the change
is a single result-type widening plus 54 one-line populations.

## Lane

`hooks`

## Path hints

- `internal/hooks/hooks.go` (the `Gate` and `Finding` types, lines 50-80)
- `internal/hooks/gate_*.go` (54 files)
- `cmd/fak/hooks.go` (`runHooksPreCommit`, `emitFindingsJSON`)
- `internal/hooks/failclosed_ledger_test.go` (the existing set-membership pattern to mirror)

## Hot-tree landing plan

**Owning lane(s)**
- `hooks` — `internal/hooks/**` (`dos.toml:804`) — the result type plus the 54 gate bodies
- `cmd` — `cmd/fak/hooks.go` — the `gates` array and the clean-path summary — frequently HOT

**Contention check**
`dos arbitrate --workspace . --lane hooks && git status -sb -- internal/hooks cmd/fak/hooks.go`

**Partition plan (clean-now vs hot-later)**
- **CLEAN NOW:** `internal/hooks/**` — the widened result type and the per-gate counts. Pure
  and unit-testable; lands alone, with the new count simply unread until part 2.
- **HOT LATER:** `cmd/fak/hooks.go` — the `gates` array and the summary line. `cmd` is among
  the hottest lanes in the tree; defer this half until it quiesces rather than blocking part 1.

**Commit recipe**
`fak commit --path internal/hooks -m "feat(hooks): count each gate's staged candidates (fak hooks)"`

## Boundary notes

Public issue. Every path, line number and quoted string is from the public tree; no operator,
credential, or private-lab evidence is involved.

## Closure binding

Resolving commit must cite this issue number (`#N`) and carry a matching `(fak hooks)` trailer
so the close arm can witness the diff.

records.title: feat(hooks): name the scope a gate run judged, so staged-clean stops reading as tree-clean (fak hooks)
records.body:
**Parent context:** #5601 (grounding epic) · sibling of the candidate-denominator leaf

**Generation:** now · **Work unit:** leaf · **Expected steps:** 3

## Current state

Several fak checks exist as a **pair**: a staged, commit-boundary gate and a whole-tree
twin. `internal/hooks/hooks.go` documents two of them in its own registration comments:

- `UNTIERED_LEAF` is "the STAGED, commit-boundary twin of the whole-tree `TIER_DECLARED`
  hygiene gate" (`internal/hooks/hooks.go:116-123`).
- `GOFMT` is "the commit-boundary sibling of `make ci`'s gofmt-check"
  (`internal/hooks/hooks.go:124-129`).

Both halves report the same word — clean — but they are **different claims**. "Clean over
the files this commit staged" does not imply "clean over the tree," and on a shared trunk
the gap between them is exactly where a peer's un-staged drift lives. Nothing in the output
of either half says which claim was made.

The same ambiguity exists wherever a run is narrowed: a gate that was softened to `warn` via
its `FLEET_*_GUARD` env, or skipped once via its escape env, is `continue`d at
`cmd/fak/hooks.go:340-342` and — by design — is *not* counted as skipped, because that is
operator intent rather than a degraded run. That reasoning is right, but it means the run's
**effective scope** is narrower than the gate list implies and the report never says so.

## Why this is next

A reader who cannot tell a narrow pass from a broad one will act on the narrow one as though
it were broad. This is the cheapest possible fix — a scope word appended to a line that is
already printed — and it removes a whole category of misread verdicts without touching a
single gate's logic.

It pairs with the candidate-denominator leaf: that one says *how many* items were judged,
this one says *which population* they were drawn from. Neither alone is sufficient.

## Working spine

Every gate verdict states the scope it was drawn over — staged-only vs whole-tree, and full
gate set vs operator-narrowed — so two different claims stop sharing one word.

## Priority context

- **Working path:** run a gate → read its verdict → decide whether to ship.
- **Current blocker:** "clean" is overloaded across at least two populations.
- **Unblocks:** any consumer that wants to promote a commit-boundary pass into a trunk-level
  claim can finally tell whether it is entitled to.
- **Not polish:** this is a correctness property of the report, not formatting.

## In scope

- Append an explicit scope note to the pre-commit human summary, e.g.
  `pre-commit: clean — STAGED-ONLY, untracked and unstaged paths NOT judged`.
- Add a `scope` field to the `--json` payload (`"scope": "staged"`), so a machine consumer
  can branch on it rather than inferring it from the command name.
- When one or more gates were softened to `warn` or skipped by an escape env, say so on the
  summary line — distinct wording from the `%d of %d gate(s) skipped` degraded-run line at
  `cmd/fak/hooks.go:390-393`, because operator intent and a broken checker are different
  states and must not collapse into one sentence.
- Do the same for the whole-tree twin so the two halves are readably different.

## Out of scope

- Making the staged gate scan the whole tree, or vice versa. The split is deliberate and
  load-bearing for hook latency (#5335).
- Changing which gates are enabled by default, or any `DefaultMode`.
- Reclassifying operator-softened gates as skipped — that would defeat the distinction
  `cmd/fak/hooks.go:340-342` deliberately draws.

## Done condition

A test asserts that a clean staged-only run and a clean whole-tree run emit **different**
scope strings, and that a run with a gate softened to `warn` is distinguishable from one
where every gate ran in `block` mode.

**Witness:** `go test ./cmd/fak -run 'HooksPreCommit|Hygiene'`

**Acceptance gate:** `go test ./internal/hooks ./cmd/fak -run Hooks`

## Assumptions

- The staged/whole-tree pairing is intended to persist; this issue makes it legible rather
  than removing it.
- Adding a `scope` key to the JSON payload is backwards-compatible for current consumers.

## Confusion risks

- **Scope ≠ denominator.** The sibling leaf reports *how many* items were judged; this one
  reports *which population* they came from. A run can name a large denominator over the
  wrong population.
- **Operator-narrowed ≠ degraded.** A gate set to `warn` is intent; a gate that could-not-run
  is degradation (#5299). The line must keep them apart.
- Not a new gate. No new class of violation is being detected here.

## Coordination notes

- Touches the same summary-line region of `cmd/fak/hooks.go` as the candidate-denominator
  leaf. Land that one first if both are in flight, then extend its line rather than adding a
  second one — two summary lines would re-create the ambiguity this closes.

## Trigger

Filed from an audit of the pre-commit report surface for the class in #5601.

## Batch policy

One issue covering both halves of the staged/whole-tree pair. Do not split per gate.

## Lane

`hooks`

## Path hints

- `cmd/fak/hooks.go` (`runHooksPreCommit`, `emitFindingsJSON`, lines 286-407)
- `internal/hooks/hooks.go` (the twin-gate registration comments, lines 116-137)
- `internal/hooks/gate_untieredleaf.go`, `internal/hooks/gate_tierdeclared.go`

## Hot-tree landing plan

**Owning lane(s)**
- `cmd` — `cmd/fak/hooks.go` — the summary line and the `scope` JSON key — frequently HOT
- `hooks` — `internal/hooks/**` — only if the scope word is derived inside the package

**Contention check**
`dos arbitrate --workspace . --lane cmd && git status -sb -- cmd/fak/hooks.go internal/hooks`

**Partition plan (clean-now vs hot-later)**
- **CLEAN NOW:** the `scope` constant and its test in `internal/hooks/**` — pure, lands alone.
- **HOT LATER:** the `cmd/fak/hooks.go` rendering. Single hot lane for the visible half; pair
  with the peer holding `cmd` rather than racing it.

**Commit recipe**
`fak commit --path internal/hooks -m "feat(hooks): name the scope a gate run judged (fak hooks)"`

## Boundary notes

Public issue. All cited evidence is in the public tree.

## Closure binding

Resolving commit must cite this issue number (`#N`) and carry a matching `(fak hooks)` trailer
so the close arm can witness the diff.

records.title: fix(cmd): refuse an unknown --gates name instead of exiting 0 having run nothing (fak cmd)
records.body:
**Parent context:** #5601 (grounding epic) · `cmd/fak/test.go:253`, the selector refusal that
already exists in one place

**Generation:** now · **Work unit:** leaf · **Expected steps:** 3

## Current state

`fak hygiene --gates <names>` selects gates by name and **silently selects nothing when the
name is wrong.**

`gateFilter` (`cmd/fak/hygiene.go:123-136`) upper-cases and splits the CSV into a `want` set
with no membership check against the real gate list. The run loop
(`cmd/fak/hygiene.go:53-57`) then does:

```go
for _, g := range hooks.HygieneGates() {
    if want != nil && !want[g.Name] {
        continue
    }
```

So `fak hygiene --gates NOSUCHGATE` — or, more likely, a real gate name with a typo, a
lower-cased hyphenation, or the singular of a plural — builds a non-empty `want`, matches no
registered gate, runs **zero** checks, leaves `blocked` false and `allFindings` empty, and
**exits 0**. With `--json` it emits an empty findings payload. That output is byte-identical
to a genuine full pass over the whole tree.

fak already refuses this exact mistake elsewhere: `cmd/fak/test.go:253` returns
`fmt.Errorf("unknown check %q", name)` rather than planning an empty run. The discipline
exists; it just is not applied here.

**Second silent-green in the same loop.** At `cmd/fak/hygiene.go:63-66` a gate whose `Check`
returns an error is `continue`d with no record:

```go
findings, gerr := g.Check(d)
if gerr != nil {
    // a single gate that could-not-run is skipped (fail-open); the others still run.
    continue
}
```

Fail-open is correct and must stay. But the pre-commit path already learned (#5299) that the
skip must be *visible* — it tracks `skipped` and prints `%d of %d gate(s) skipped (fail-open)
— this commit ran a DEGRADED gate set` (`cmd/fak/hooks.go:390-393`). `fak hygiene` never got
that treatment, so a persistently-broken hygiene gate is an invisible bypass.

## Why this is next

A lint whose failure mode is a green tick is worse than no lint, because a pass is the one
outcome nobody investigates. Both defects above are in the same ~45-line function, both
manufacture confidence, and `fak hygiene` is on the `make ci` path — the gate a shipper
trusts before pushing to a shared trunk.

The fix is small and the pattern is already written twice in this repo (`test.go:253` for the
refusal, `hooks.go:390-393` for the visible skip). This leaf is a port, not a design.

## Working spine

A gate selector either names gates that exist, or the command refuses — and a hygiene run
that skipped gates says so, rather than reporting a clean tree.

## Priority context

- **Working path:** `make ci` → `fak hygiene` → push to trunk.
- **Current blocker:** a typo'd `--gates` value and a broken gate both render as a clean pass.
- **Unblocks:** any automation that shells out to `fak hygiene --gates ...` can trust exit 0.
- **Not polish:** this is a false-negative in a pre-push gate, not ergonomics.

## In scope

1. **Refuse an unknown gate name.** Validate every entry of `--gates` against
   `hooks.HygieneGates()` and return a non-zero exit naming the unknown name and the valid
   set — mirroring `cmd/fak/test.go:253`. An empty selection must never be a silent pass.
2. **Make hygiene's skips visible.** Track `skipped` in the `gerr != nil` branch exactly as
   `runHooksPreCommit` does, and print the same shape of degraded-run line; add
   `skipped_gates` / `skipped_count` to the `--json` payload so the two commands' reports are
   readable by one consumer.
3. Audit the other name-based selectors in `cmd/fak/` for the same shape and fix or file
   them — `--suite` (`ablate.go:47`, `dojo.go:416`, `main.go:895`, `main.go:936`), `--tier`
   (`newleaf.go:17`), `--lane` where it is matched against a known set.

## Out of scope

- Changing fail-open. A gate that cannot run must still not wedge the command; this issue
  makes the skip *visible*, never blocking.
- Changing which gates are `DefaultOff`, or the rule at `cmd/fak/hygiene.go:59-61` that a
  `DefaultOff` gate runs only when named explicitly — that rule is correct and depends on the
  selector, so it must keep working after validation lands.
- The staged pre-commit path, which already has the skip tracking (#5299).

## Done condition

`fak hygiene --gates NOSUCHGATE` exits non-zero with a message naming the unknown gate and
the valid names; a test asserts it, and a second test asserts a run where a gate could-not-run
is distinguishable from a run where every gate passed.

**Witness:** `go test ./cmd/fak -run 'Hygiene'`

**Acceptance gate:** `go test ./cmd/fak ./internal/hooks -run 'Hygiene|Hooks'`

## Assumptions

- `hooks.HygieneGates()` is the complete registry of valid names — the same source the loop
  iterates, so validation cannot drift from execution.
- No current caller depends on a typo'd `--gates` value exiting 0. Scripts passing a correct
  name are unaffected.

## Confusion risks

- **Unknown-name refusal ≠ fail-open.** Refusing a bad *selector* is an argument error before
  any checking starts. Fail-open governs a gate that started and could not finish. This issue
  keeps the second and adds the first.
- **`DefaultOff` skip ≠ could-not-run skip.** The `DefaultOff` `continue`
  (`cmd/fak/hygiene.go:59-61`) is intent and must not be counted as degradation.
- Not the same as the candidate-denominator leaf under #5601: this is about a check that
  never *ran*, not one that ran over an empty domain.

## Coordination notes

- Single file for items 1 and 2 — `cmd/fak/hygiene.go` — so land them in one commit rather
  than leaving a known silent-green beside a freshly-fixed one.
- Item 3 is an audit; file what it finds as separate leaves under #5601 rather than widening
  this diff.

## Trigger

Found while auditing selector surfaces for the class in #5601.

## Batch policy

One issue for `hygiene`. Other selectors found by item 3 get their own leaves, capped at one
per command, cross-linked to #5601.

## Lane

`cmd`

## Path hints

- `cmd/fak/hygiene.go` (`gateFilter` at 123-136; the run loop at 50-95)
- `cmd/fak/test.go` (line 253 — the refusal to mirror)
- `cmd/fak/hooks.go` (lines 329-336 and 390-393 — the visible-skip pattern to mirror)
- `internal/hooks/hooks.go` (`HygieneGates`)

## Hot-tree landing plan

**Owning lane(s)**
- `cmd` — `cmd/fak/hygiene.go` — both fixes — frequently HOT

**Contention check**
`dos arbitrate --workspace . --lane cmd && git status -sb -- cmd/fak/hygiene.go cmd/fak/hooks.go`

**Partition plan (clean-now vs hot-later)**
Single hot lane — must wait for `cmd` to quiesce, or pair with the peer holding it. The diff
is narrow (one function plus one helper) and touches no file another lane owns, so a short
window is enough; do not split it, since fixing the selector while leaving the invisible skip
in the same loop would ship half a trust floor.

**Commit recipe**
`fak commit --path cmd/fak/hygiene.go -m "fix(cmd): refuse an unknown --gates name and count skipped hygiene gates (fak cmd)"`

so the close arm can witness the diff.

records.title: fix(hooks): bind the package's exhaustiveness claim to the registry it quantifies over (fak hooks)
records.body:
**Parent context:** #5601 (grounding epic) · `internal/architest/architest_test.go` and
`internal/hooks/failclosed_ledger_test.go`, the two places fak already binds a claim to a
registry

**Generation:** now · **Work unit:** leaf · **Expected steps:** 3

## Current state

A count a human types into prose is correct on the day it is written and unowned every day
after. fak has a live instance of this **in the package the rest of #5601 is about**.

`internal/hooks/hooks.go:6-10` says:

> This package collapses all **8** gates into one Go process that reads the staged diff ONCE
> and runs every gate over it

`PreCommitGates()` (`internal/hooks/hooks.go:85-139`) registers **17**.

The number was right when written — it described the Python-era set, 7 pre-commit gates plus
1 commit-msg gate, and the surrounding sentences are explicitly historical. It drifted because
nothing binds the prose to the registry. Ten gates were added since (`BARE_COMMIT_SWEEP`,
`E2E_OVER_MOCKS`, `TRUST_WIDENING`, `PRIOR_ART`, `UNTIERED_LEAF`, `GOFMT`, `DUPLICATION`,
`CONCEPT_FRESHNESS`, `PROVENANCE_LABEL`, `HARDWARE_TELL`), each correctly, and not one of them
was wrong to leave the header alone — there was no mechanism telling the author it had a debt.

This is the same class as the rest of #5601 read from the other side. A gate with an empty
domain reports a verdict with no denominator; a comment claiming exhaustiveness (*"all 8"*,
*"the only caller"*, *"every package"*) reports a denominator with nothing checking it.

**fak already solves this twice, mechanically:**

- `internal/architest/architest_test.go:22` — a tier row per internal package, with
  `TestEveryPackageDeclaresTier` failing when a package has no row. The claim "every internal
  package has a layer" is *enforced*, not asserted.
- `internal/hooks/failclosed_ledger_test.go:110-125` — bidirectional membership between the
  gate registry and its ledger; drift fails in either direction.

Both bind a claim to the registry it quantifies over. Prose counts do not.

## Why this is next

The cheap half of this is a one-line fix to a stale comment. The valuable half is the
mechanism that stops the next one, and it is small: the two enforcement patterns already
exist and only need pointing at a different kind of claim.

Doing it now, inside the epic that audits this package, means the fix lands next to its own
motivating example rather than as an abstract lint nobody can justify.

## Working spine

An exhaustiveness claim about a registry either derives its number from that registry, or a
test fails when the two disagree.

## Priority context

- **Working path:** read a package header → trust its description → act on it.
- **Current blocker:** hand-typed counts silently decay; a reader cannot tell a current count
  from a historical one.
- **Unblocks:** the same check covers future gate additions at no marginal cost.
- **Not polish:** a wrong count in a security-adjacent package's header misleads about how
  much checking happens.

## In scope

1. **Fix the live drift.** Correct `internal/hooks/hooks.go:6-10` so the present-tense claim
   matches the registry, and keep the historical 7+1 figure clearly marked as history — the
   spawn-cost rationale is still the reason this package exists and should not be deleted.
2. **Bind the claim.** Add a test in `internal/hooks` asserting that any gate count stated in
   the package doc comment equals `len(PreCommitGates())`, failing with both numbers named —
   the `failclosed_ledger_test.go` shape, applied to prose. Deriving the sentence from the
   registry at doc-build time is an acceptable alternative; a test is the smaller change.
3. **Name the pattern once** so it is reusable: a short note in the package doc that an
   exhaustiveness claim in this tree carries, on the same line, the witness that would refute
   it — a count bound to a registry, or a test naming the registry.

## Out of scope

- A tree-wide lint for every *"the only"* / *"every"* phrase in every comment. That is a much
  larger design with a real false-positive cost, and it should be justified by more than one
  observed drift. If item 2 proves cheap, file the generalization as a separate leaf under
  #5601 with the evidence this one produces.
- `INDEX.md` and the study notes, whose numeric claims are pinned to dated snapshots and are
  correctly historical.
- Changing any gate, verdict, or registration.

## Done condition

`internal/hooks/hooks.go`'s stated gate count matches `len(PreCommitGates())`, and a test in
`internal/hooks` fails if a future gate registration makes them disagree — naming both the
claimed and the actual number in the failure message.

**Witness:** `go test ./internal/hooks -run 'DocCount|Ledger'`

**Acceptance gate:** `go test ./internal/hooks`

## Assumptions

- The package doc comment is the right home for the count; if reviewers prefer it deleted
  rather than bound, the test becomes an assertion that no bare count appears there — either
  outcome satisfies the spine.
- `PreCommitGates()` remains the single registry for the pre-commit set.

## Confusion risks

- **Stale ≠ wrong-when-written.** The "8" was accurate for the Python-era set. The defect is
  the missing binding, not the original author's arithmetic; the fix must not read as blaming
  a past commit.
- **Historical figures are legitimate.** The 7+1 spawn-cost measurement should survive, marked
  as history. Only the present-tense claim needs binding.
- Not the candidate-denominator leaf: that one is about a *run's* domain, this one is about a
  *document's* claim over a registry.
- Not a docs-style issue. The deliverable is a failing test, not a rewritten paragraph.

## Coordination notes

- `internal/hooks/hooks.go` is the collision point with any peer registering a new gate — and
  such a peer is exactly who this test is for. Land it when the lane is quiet; the test itself
  makes future contention cheaper, since a gate addition that forgets the header fails locally
  instead of at review.

## Trigger

Found while auditing `internal/hooks` for the class in #5601.

## Batch policy

One issue. Generalizations to other files get their own leaves, cross-linked to #5601, only
after this one shows the check is cheap.

## Lane

`hooks`

## Path hints

- `internal/hooks/hooks.go` (the doc comment at 1-17; `PreCommitGates()` at 85-139)
- `internal/hooks/failclosed_ledger_test.go` (lines 110-125 — the binding pattern to mirror)
- `internal/architest/architest_test.go` (line 22 — the same pattern at tree scale)

## Hot-tree landing plan

**Owning lane(s)**
- `hooks` — `internal/hooks/**` (`dos.toml:804`) — comment fix plus one new test — usually clean

**Contention check**
`dos arbitrate --workspace . --lane hooks && git status -sb -- internal/hooks/hooks.go`

**Partition plan (clean-now vs hot-later)**
Single clean lane — land directly. The whole diff is one comment and one `_test.go`, entirely
inside `internal/hooks`, touching no `cmd/**` file and therefore not blocked by the hot `cmd`
lane the sibling leaves must wait on.

**Commit recipe**
`fak commit --path internal/hooks -m "fix(hooks): bind the package's gate count to the registry (fak hooks)"`

## Boundary notes

Public issue. Every path, line number and quoted string is from the public tree; the counts
above were read from the tree, not recalled.

## Closure binding

Resolving commit must cite this issue number (`#N`) and carry a matching `(fak hooks)` trailer
so the close arm can witness the diff.

records.title: epic(moe): first-class activated-expert offloading — promote the nine off-path expert-residency parts onto the serve path
records.body:
## Epic — make the MoE **activated working set** a first-class object

Full plan: [`docs/MOE-ACTIVATED-OFFLOAD-PLAN.md`](../blob/main/docs/MOE-ACTIVATED-OFFLOAD-PLAN.md).

**Thesis.** A frontier MoE checkpoint activates a small fraction of its experts per token
(GLM-5.2 routes top-8 of 256 per layer, ~3%; DeepSeek-V4 / Qwen3-MoE / gpt-oss / MiniMax are
shaped the same). The parameter bulk is the experts; the per-token demand is a thin
router-selected slice of it. Exploiting that gap is a **residency** problem — "is this token
fast?" reduces to "were its activated experts resident?" — and making it first-class means fak
must be able to **name, bound, observe and schedule the activated working set** as an object.

Today it cannot.

### The serve path offers two placements, both wrong for this

1. **All-host, forever.** `--cpu-offload-experts` selects `splitKernel`
   (`internal/model/moe_offload.go:132-142`) — a *static predicate over weight names*. Every
   expert GEMM runs on host RAM for the session's life; no activated expert ever becomes
   device-resident. The file calls itself "the floor, not a cache". The knob is one `bool`
   (`cmd/fak/serve.go:221`); there is no graded form.
2. **All-device, forever-growing.** Routed experts stage through `Session.expertSwiGLUHAL`
   (`internal/model/hal.go:248-284`) into `Session.weightHALStaged`
   (`internal/model/hal.go:170-181`), which memoizes each uploaded handle in `s.halW` and
   **never evicts** — the map is torn down only at session close
   (`internal/model/hal.go:83-103`). Device residency is therefore the *union of every expert
   activated since session start*, converging monotonically on the full expert bulk. That is a
   memoizer, not a cache: no budget, no victim, no accounting.

Neither has a bounded activated working set, and neither exposes a seam where a residency
policy, a prefetch, a pin-set or a byte budget could attach on the live path.

### The uncomfortable part: the parts are all built, and none are wired

| Capability | Where | Live-path status |
|---|---|---|
| Bounded per-weight device ring (byte budget, LRU victim, pinned-exempt, page-in/hit/evict counters) | `internal/model/paging_ring.go` | **Off-path** — sole constructor is `internal/model/v4_expert_runtime.go:67` (DeepSeek-V4 only); header `:38-44` names the session-HAL wiring as the follow-on rung |
| Graded spill sizing + auto-fit (`--n-cpu-moe N` semantics) | `internal/model/expert_spill_fit.go` (#5281 closed) | **No caller** — `ResolveExpertSpill`/`AutoFitExpertSpill` exported and unused outside tests; no CLI flag exposes N |
| Value-aware evictor (routing-heat hysteresis + LFU-decay) vs Belady | `internal/model/expert_residency_lfu.go` (#4357 closed) | **Simulation only** — ring is still plain LRU |
| Cross-session usage histogram, warm-start pins, `RepinPass` | `internal/model/expert_warmpins.go` (#4358 closed) | **Off-path** — `pagedRing.pins` never consulted; `matMulStaged` still takes a static `pinned` bool (`paging_ring.go:56-61`) |
| Per-expert range read + `MADV_WILLNEED` readahead | `internal/model/expert_readahead.go` (#4359 closed) | **Off-path** — no load/decode caller |
| Lazy per-expert GGUF slab source (reads `stride`, not `E*stride`) | `internal/model/gguf_expert_source.go` | **Off-path** — loader still materializes the whole fused block |
| Routed-expert observer + access-trace replay corpus | `internal/model/expert_replay.go` | **Off-path** — `SetExpertRouteObserver` has no non-test caller |
| Planned-vs-observed placement coverage/drift gauge | `internal/model/expert_placement_drift.go` (#3902) | **Off-path** — no caller |
| Expert-residency eviction regret vs the Belady oracle | #4233 (closed) on `compute/kvreplay_oracle.go` | **Off-path** — replay harness only |

**The invention is done; the promotion is not.** Each piece landed under a generation frame
that explicitly deferred wiring, and no issue owned the wiring itself. #2726 — which did own
it — was closed COMPLETED on the *primitive* while its own follow-on rung stayed open in the
code comments. This epic owns that rung.

### The ladder (children)

Ordered by leverage-over-cost. **R0 is the keystone** — R2/R3/R4/R5/R7 all attach to the seam
it creates and none can land without it.

- **R0 (P0)** — #5611 — bound the activated set: wire the ring under the expert weight HAL
- **R1 (P0)** — #5612 — ship the graded knob (`--n-cpu-moe N` / `auto`) and admit on the working set
- **R2 (P1)** — #5613 — consult the pin-set + persist the histogram on the live ring
- **R3 (P1)** — #5614 — router-lookahead prefetch (the deterministic floor beneath #4300)
- **R4 (P1)** — #5615 — promote the evictor on measured regret, not on faith
- **R5 (P2)** — #5616 — put a checkpoint tier under a ring miss
- **R6 (P2)** — #5617 — make it an operator-visible object (`fak` verb + serve telemetry)
- **R7 (P2)** — #5618 — cross-agent coalescing on a live ring (unblocks #5243 L2)
- **R8 (P3)** — already #5247 — grouped GEMM over the coalesced union (listed for position)

**Dependency shape.** R0 is the only rung with no prerequisite inside this epic; R1's knob half
is also independent (its admission half wants R0's budget). R2/R3/R4/R5/R7 all require R0. R6
measures R0 and should not slip far past R3.

### Composition with existing work (not a fork)

- **#3174** ranks the concept (M11) — this epic ships the mechanism it describes.
- **#4300 / #4318** own *predictive* prefetch; R3 is the deterministic same-step floor they
  attach to.
- **#5243** (+#5246/#5247/#5249/#5251) own cross-agent coalescing; R0 supplies the live shared
  ring they need to coalesce onto.
- **#5239** (deferred-expert pipeline) is compute scheduling, composes with R3, not duplicated.
- **#3886** (EPLB placement) balances experts *across ranks* — a different axis from bounding
  residency *within* a device.

### Epic-level witness

A checkpoint whose expert bulk exceeds the device budget serves with (a) bit-identical output
vs the resident path, (b) peak device weight bytes under a declared budget, and (c) an
operator-visible activated-set/hit/page-in report — none of which is possible today.

### Non-goals

No new evictor is invented here (R4 promotes a measured winner). No cross-engine performance
claim: every witness is a delta against fak's own current path on the same host.

records.title: feat(hooks): make an agent-lifecycle hook that could not run say so, instead of exiting 0 (fak hooks)
records.body:
**Parent context:** #5601 (grounding epic) · `internal/hooks`, the same collapse already done
once for the git hooks

**Generation:** now · **Work unit:** leaf · **Expected steps:** 4

## Current state

fak's agent-lifecycle hooks are four Python one-liners embedded as JSON string arguments in
`.claude/settings.json` — `PreToolUse` (repoguard, then `dos_hook.py pretool`), `PostToolUse`
(`dos_hook.py posttool`), and `Stop` (`dos_hook.py stop`).

Every one of them ends the same way:

```python
subprocess.call(args); sys.exit(0)
```

The child's return code is **discarded** and the hook exits 0 unconditionally. Because the
hook shells out via `sys.executable` — which always exists — a child that fails to start is
indistinguishable from a child that ran and approved. If `tools/dos_hook.py` or
`tools/repo_guard.py` is renamed, moved, or raises on import, the interpreter starts, prints
to stderr, exits non-zero, and the wrapper reports success. The tool call proceeds ungoverned
and nothing in the run says the guard was absent.

Two further properties make this hard to notice:

- The hook bodies are 200-900 character Python expressions inside JSON. Nothing compiles,
  vets, lints, or unit-tests them; the first evidence of a syntax error is a live session.
- `tools/.bin/repoguard.exe` is **not present** in the tree, so the `PreToolUse` guard is
  currently running its Python source fallback. That fallback is deliberate and correct —
  the one-liner even detects a stale binary and says so on stderr — but it means the fast
  path is unexercised and the failure surface is the untested one.

This is the same class as the rest of #5601: a check whose absence renders identically to a
check that passed.

## Why this is next

fak already did exactly this collapse once, for the git hooks, and documented why:
`internal/hooks/hooks.go:1-17` describes replacing per-gate Python spawns with one Go process,
and the package now carries a real test suite (`parity_test.go`, `failclosed_ledger_test.go`).
The agent-lifecycle hooks are the same shape of problem one layer up, and the pattern to copy
is in-tree.

The `PreToolUse` guard is the repo's capability boundary. A boundary that cannot report its
own absence is the highest-value instance of this class in the tree.

## Working spine

An agent-lifecycle hook that could not run says so, and its body is ordinary tested code
rather than a string inside a settings file.

## Priority context

- **Working path:** agent tool call → PreToolUse guard → admitted or refused.
- **Current blocker:** a guard that fails to start reports the same exit 0 as a guard that
  admitted the call.
- **Unblocks:** any later hardening of the guard can be tested instead of eyeballed.
- **Not polish:** this is the failure visibility of the capability boundary itself.

## In scope

1. **Stop discarding the child's exit code.** Propagate a distinguishable outcome when the
   child could not run — mirroring `internal/hooks`'s existing three-state contract of
   clean / violation / could-not-run (`internal/hooks/hooks.go:15-16`,
   `ErrCouldNotRun` at 37-40). Keep the fail-open posture: a broken hook must not wedge the
   session, exactly as a broken gate must not wedge every commit. Make the skip **visible**,
   the way #5299 made a skipped commit gate visible, rather than converting it to a block.
2. **Move the hook bodies out of JSON.** Replace the embedded one-liners with a single
   entrypoint — `fak hooks agent <pretool|posttool|stop>` alongside the existing
   `fak hooks pre-commit` / `commit-msg` verbs in `cmd/fak/hooks.go` — so `.claude/settings.json`
   holds a command name, not a program.
3. **Add a self-test with a floor.** A table-driven test over captured real hook I/O, plus an
   assertion that the table is non-empty and covers every registered lifecycle event. A suite
   that ran zero cases must fail, not pass: `0 passed, 0 failed` exiting 0 is the same vacuous
   green #5601 is about.

## Out of scope

- Changing what the guard decides, its rule set, or its default posture. Refusal behaviour is
  unchanged; only the reporting of could-not-run and the testability of the wrapper change.
- Removing the Python fallback. It is a deliberate resilience path and should keep working —
  but it should be reached deliberately, not by silent failure.
- Building the missing `tools/.bin/repoguard.exe`; that is a build concern, noted here only as
  evidence for which path is live.

## Done condition

A test asserts that a lifecycle hook whose child cannot start is reported distinguishably from
one whose child ran and approved, and `.claude/settings.json` no longer embeds executable
Python source.

**Witness:** `go test ./cmd/fak ./internal/hooks -run 'AgentHook|Hooks'`

**Acceptance gate:** `go test ./cmd/fak ./internal/hooks -run Hooks`

## Assumptions

- The hook contract permits a non-zero or structured could-not-run signal without blocking the
  session; if it does not, item 1 becomes a stderr line plus a counter, which still satisfies
  the spine.
- `tools/dos_hook.py` and `tools/repo_guard.py` keep their current stdout dialect, so moving
  the wrapper does not change what the host reads.

## Confusion risks

- **Visible skip ≠ block.** This issue does not make hook failure fatal. It makes it *legible*.
  Converting a broken hook into a hard stop would trap a headless worker in a loop it cannot
  argue its way out of.
- **Lifecycle hooks ≠ git hooks.** `internal/hooks` is the commit-boundary package; this is the
  agent tool-call boundary. Same pattern, different surface — do not merge the gate registries.
- The absent `repoguard.exe` is evidence about which code path runs, not the defect itself.

## Coordination notes

- `.claude/settings.json` is shared across every session in this checkout; changing it affects
  peers immediately. Land the Go entrypoint (item 2's first half) first and switch the settings
  file in a separate, clearly-messaged commit so a peer mid-session can attribute any change.
- Coordinate with whoever owns `tools/dos_hook.py`; this issue does not change its interface.

## Trigger

Found while auditing hook surfaces for the class in #5601.

## Batch policy

One issue for all four lifecycle hooks — they share one wrapper shape and one fix.

## Lane

`cmd`

## Path hints

- `.claude/settings.json` (the four embedded hook bodies)
- `cmd/fak/hooks.go` (`runHooks` at 34; the existing verb dispatch)
- `internal/hooks/hooks.go` (lines 1-17 and 37-40 — the three-state contract to reuse)
- `tools/dos_hook.py`, `tools/repo_guard.py` (the children; interfaces unchanged)

## Hot-tree landing plan

**Owning lane(s)**
- `cmd` — `cmd/fak/hooks.go` — the new agent-hook verb — frequently HOT
- `claude` — `.claude/settings.json` — the cutover — shared by every live session

**Contention check**
`dos arbitrate --workspace . --lane cmd && git status -sb -- cmd/fak/hooks.go .claude/settings.json`

**Partition plan (clean-now vs hot-later)**
- **CLEAN NOW:** the could-not-run reporting shape and its test, expressed inside
  `internal/hooks/**` — pure, no session impact, lands independently.
- **HOT LATER:** the `cmd/fak/hooks.go` verb and then the `.claude/settings.json` cutover.
  These are ordered, not parallel: the verb must exist and be green before the settings file
  points at it, or every peer session loses its guard at once.

**Commit recipe**
`fak commit --path internal/hooks -m "feat(hooks): report a lifecycle hook that could not run (fak hooks)"`

## Boundary notes

Public issue. `.claude/settings.json` is tracked in the public tree and contains no
credentials; the hook bodies quoted above are public. No operator or private-lab evidence is
involved.

## Closure binding

Resolving commit must cite this issue number (`#N`) and carry a matching `(fak hooks)` trailer
so the close arm can witness the diff.

records.title: fix(issuefanout): bind the refusal-reason vocabulary to its emitters (74 of 75 wired) (fak issuefanout)
records.body:
**Parent context:** #5601 (grounding epic) · `internal/hooks/failclosed_ledger_test.go`, the
bidirectional registry binding to mirror

**Generation:** now · **Work unit:** leaf · **Expected steps:** 2

## Current state

`dos.toml` declares **75** refusal reasons (`[reasons.*]`), and `AGENTS.md` documents each with
its meaning, its remedy, and the floor package that owns it. This closed vocabulary is one of
the strongest things in the repo — a refusal names a reason from a fixed set instead of free
text, so a consumer can act on it.

Measured across `cmd/`, `internal/` and `tools/` (`.go` and `.py`), **74 of the 75 are
referenced in code. One is not:**

- `ISSUEFANOUT_CONTRACT_REFUSED` — declared at `dos.toml:1721`, documented at `AGENTS.md:504`
  (and mirrored into `llms-full.txt:578`), naming `internal/issuefanout` as its floor. No file
  in the tree emits the string.

`internal/issuefanout` does refuse, and refuses well: it has typed outcomes
(`ClassifyOutcome`, `OutcomeRefused`) and a `failure_paths_test.go` that already forbids an
unrostered error construction from landing in the package. What is missing is the join — a
refusal from this floor never carries the reason code the vocabulary promises for it, so a
consumer reading reason codes cannot attribute it.

**74/75 is the point.** This is not a sick vocabulary; it is a healthy one with a single
unbound row and, more importantly, **nothing that would have caught it**. The next reason
declared without a caller drifts exactly the same way, silently, because the table and the
code have no test between them.

## Why this is next

The fix is small and the mechanism is already written twice in this repo
(`internal/hooks/failclosed_ledger_test.go:110-125` binds gates to their ledger in both
directions; `internal/architest/architest_test.go` binds packages to tier rows). Applying it
to the reason vocabulary converts a documented promise into a checked one at roughly the cost
of reading the file.

Doing it while the gap is one row is much cheaper than doing it at ten, and the resulting test
makes every future reason free to trust.

## Working spine

Every refusal reason declared in `dos.toml` is emittable by code, and a declared-but-unemitted
reason fails a test naming both sides.

## Priority context

- **Working path:** a floor refuses → names a reason → a consumer routes on it.
- **Current blocker:** one declared reason cannot be emitted, and nothing detects the class.
- **Unblocks:** consumers can treat the reason table as total rather than aspirational.
- **Not polish:** an unemittable reason is a documented capability the tree does not have.

## In scope

1. Emit `ISSUEFANOUT_CONTRACT_REFUSED` from `internal/issuefanout`'s contract-refusal path, so
   the refusal carries its declared code — or, if review concludes the reason is genuinely
   obsolete, remove the row from `dos.toml` and its documentation rows together. Either
   direction closes the gap; the test in item 2 is what must not be skipped.
2. Add a test binding the two registries in **both** directions, mirroring
   `failclosed_ledger_test.go`: a `[reasons.*]` row with no emitter fails, and an emitted
   reason string with no `dos.toml` row fails. The failure message must name the specific
   reason and both locations.
3. Keep the documentation mirrors consistent — `AGENTS.md` and `llms-full.txt` both carry the
   row, so whichever direction item 1 goes, both must move with it.

## Out of scope

- Redesigning the reason vocabulary, renaming reasons, or changing any refusal's semantics.
- Auditing whether each reason's *documented remedy* is still accurate — a real and larger
  question; file separately under #5601 if wanted.
- The `internal/issuefanout` refusal logic itself, which is already well-tested.

## Done condition

A test fails when a `dos.toml` reason has no emitter in the tree, or an emitted reason has no
`dos.toml` row — and the tree passes it, with `ISSUEFANOUT_CONTRACT_REFUSED` either wired or
retired along with its documentation rows.

**Witness:** `go test ./internal/issuefanout ./internal/architest -run 'Reason'`

**Acceptance gate:** `go test ./internal/issuefanout ./internal/architest`

## Assumptions

- A textual scan for the reason identifier across non-test sources is an acceptable emitter
  check — it is what produced the 74/75 measurement above, and it matches how
  `failclosed_ledger_test.go` reasons about registry membership.
- The reason vocabulary is intended to be total: every declared reason should be reachable.

## Confusion risks

- **Unemitted ≠ unused.** The reason is documented and may be referenced by operators and
  prompts. The defect is that no *code path* can produce it, so no consumer will ever observe
  it on a real refusal.
- **`internal/issuefanout` is not broken.** It refuses correctly through typed outcomes. The
  missing piece is the reason code on the wire, not the refusal.
- This is not the exhaustiveness-claim leaf (#5601's leaf D): that binds a *count in prose* to
  a registry, this binds *two registries* to each other. Same pattern, different pair.

## Coordination notes

- Touches `dos.toml` only if item 1 goes the retire-the-row direction; `dos.toml` is
  high-traffic and shared, so prefer the wire-it direction unless review says otherwise.
- `internal/issuefanout` is self-contained and usually quiet.

## Trigger

Found while measuring declared-vs-emitted refusal reasons for the class in #5601.

## Batch policy

One issue. If a future run of the same measurement finds several orphans at once, extend this
test rather than opening one issue per reason.

## Lane

`issuefanout`

## Path hints

- `internal/issuefanout/issuefanout.go`, `internal/issuefanout/failure_paths_test.go`
- `dos.toml` (line 1721 — the declared row)
- `AGENTS.md` (line 504), `llms-full.txt` (line 578) — the documentation mirrors
- `internal/hooks/failclosed_ledger_test.go` (lines 110-125 — the pattern to mirror)

## Hot-tree landing plan

**Owning lane(s)**
- `issuefanout` — `internal/issuefanout/**` — the emitter plus the binding test — usually clean
- `docs` — `AGENTS.md`, `llms-full.txt` — documentation mirrors, only if the row is retired

**Contention check**
`dos arbitrate --workspace . --lane issuefanout && git status -sb -- internal/issuefanout dos.toml`

**Partition plan (clean-now vs hot-later)**
Single clean lane — land directly. The whole change sits inside `internal/issuefanout` unless
review chooses to retire the row, which is the only branch that reaches the shared `dos.toml`
and the documentation mirrors; if that branch is taken, land the test first and the row removal
second so the test is what proves the removal was complete.

**Commit recipe**
`fak commit --path internal/issuefanout -m "fix(issuefanout): emit the declared contract-refusal reason (fak issuefanout)"`

## Boundary notes

Public issue. Every path, line number and count above was read from the public tree.

## Closure binding

Resolving commit must cite this issue number (`#N`) and carry a matching `(fak issuefanout)`
trailer so the close arm can witness the diff.

records.title: fix(tools): the disambiguation scorecard renders a blank provenance row, and its entries have no citable id (fak tools)
records.body:
**Parent context:** #5601 (grounding epic) · `tools/concept_disambiguation_scorecard.py`

**Generation:** now · **Work unit:** leaf · **Expected steps:** 3

## Current state

The concept-disambiguation scorecard is one of the better-grounded surfaces in the repo. Its
README states the discipline plainly:

> Every number below is re-derived by `tools/concept_disambiguation_scorecard.py` and
> cross-checked against the real tree (the grounding token must appear in the production
> corpus; the glossary anchor must exist; a `distinct_from` reference must resolve). No verdict
> is hand-typed.

Two things stop a reader from *citing* one of its decisions.

**1. Its own provenance line renders blank.** `docs/concept-disambiguation-scorecard/README.md:23`:

```
| As of |  (fak ) |
```

Every sibling scorecard renders a real date and version:

```
docs/industry-scorecard/README.md:31       | As of | 2026-06-27 (fak 0.31.0) |
docs/persona-fit-scorecard/README.md:22    | As of | 2026-06-26 (fak v0.34.0) |
docs/popularization-scorecard/README.md:21 | As of | 2026-07-18 (fak v0.41.0) |
```

The generator writes that row at `tools/concept_disambiguation_scorecard.py:2112`:

```python
out.append(f"| As of | {c.get('as_of', '?')} (fak {c.get('fak_version', '?')}) |")
```

The `'?'` fallback never fires, because the keys are *present and empty* — `.get` returns `''`,
not the default. So the one field that dates the whole scorecard silently rendered nothing,
and the table still looks well-formed. A document that says "no verdict is hand-typed" cannot
say when its verdicts were derived.

This is the epic's class in a generator: an absent value rendered as a valid-looking empty
string instead of refusing.

**2. Entries have no stable identifier.** `docs/fak/concept-glossary.md` states a clear entry
rule — one canonical name, one sentence on what it IS, one on what it is NOT — and the
scorecard checks that the anchor exists. But an entry is addressable only by its heading text.
There is no stable, append-only id, so a commit message, an issue, or a refusal message cannot
cite a *specific* disambiguation decision and have that citation survive a rename. The repo
already has the opposite pattern working well: 75 refusal reasons in `dos.toml` are cited by
stable code from both docs and source.

## Why this is next

Item 1 is a small, unambiguous bug in a claim about provenance — the highest-irony place in
the tree for a blank field, and cheap to fix properly (refuse rather than render empty).

Item 2 is what turns the glossary from a page people read into a thing people cite. Both live
in the same generator/doc pair, so they land together.

## Working spine

A disambiguation decision can be cited by a stable id and carries the date it was derived, and
a generator that lacks a provenance value refuses rather than rendering an empty one.

## Priority context

- **Working path:** two names collide → read the glossary → cite the decision in review.
- **Current blocker:** the page cannot be dated and its entries cannot be addressed.
- **Unblocks:** refusal messages and commit trailers can point at a specific entry.
- **Not polish:** an undated derived claim is not a derived claim.

## In scope

1. **Fix the blank provenance.** Treat empty-string `as_of` / `fak_version` as missing, not as
   a value: either populate them the way the sibling scorecards do, or fail the generation with
   a named error. Rendering an empty provenance field must not be a success path. Add a test
   asserting a generated scorecard's `As of` row is non-empty.
2. **Give entries a stable, append-only id.** Assign each glossary entry a short immutable id
   allocated once and never reused, independent of the heading text, so a rename does not break
   a citation. Follow the `dos.toml` reason vocabulary's precedent rather than inventing a
   second convention.
3. **Check the citation both ways.** Extend the existing scorecard checks so an id cited
   anywhere in the tree must resolve to an entry, and — the direction that usually rots — an
   entry's id must be unique and never silently renumbered.

## Out of scope

- Rewriting glossary content or re-adjudicating any disambiguation verdict.
- Changing the scorecard's metrics, the disambiguation-debt driver, or the legacy bounded score.
- Retrofitting ids into historical commit messages.

## Done condition

`docs/concept-disambiguation-scorecard/README.md` carries a non-empty `As of` row produced by a
generator that refuses to emit an empty one, and each glossary entry carries a stable id that a
test resolves in both directions.

**Witness:** `python tools/concept_disambiguation_scorecard.py --markdown-dir docs/concept-disambiguation-scorecard`
then confirm the `As of` row is populated.

**Acceptance gate:** `go test ./internal/devindex` plus the generator run above.

## Assumptions

- `as_of` and `fak_version` are meant to be populated here exactly as in the five sibling
  scorecards; the blank is a defect, not a deliberate omission for this scorecard.
- Ids can be added without renumbering existing entries, since none exist yet.

## Confusion risks

- **Blank ≠ unknown.** The generator's `'?'` fallback was written for a missing key and does
  not fire for an empty value. Fixing the symptom by defaulting harder would still render a
  placeholder; the fix is to refuse.
- **This surface is not broken.** Coverage is 97.4% of the discovered confusable space and no
  verdict is hand-typed. The gap is citability and provenance, not correctness — do not read
  this issue as a critique of the scorecard's method.
- Entry ids are not the same as the `dos.toml` reason codes; they name definitions, not refusals.

## Coordination notes

- `tools/concept_disambiguation_scorecard.py` regenerates the whole markdown directory, so run
  it and commit the regenerated output together — a hand-edited generated file will be
  overwritten on the next run.
- `docs/fak/concept-glossary.md` is referenced by the scorecard's anchor check; land the ids and
  the check in one commit so the tree is never in a state where ids exist but nothing verifies them.

## Trigger

Found while auditing generated-claim provenance for the class in #5601.

## Batch policy

One issue for the generator plus the glossary. If the blank-provenance defect turns out to
