records.title: perf(host): stop allocating a console per spawned child — 27.5 % of all process births are conhost
records.body:
## Why In the churn ablation, **conhost was the single largest image: 718 births of 2,610 (27.5 %)**. It is not an independent workload â€” Windows creates one console host per console-mode child that cannot inherit an existing console. Every one of those is pure overhead: a whole extra process creation, at a measured floor of ~8,166 page faults each, for a console nothing reads. At 25.8 births/sec sustained, this is the cheapest large win available: it is a spawn flag, not a refactor. ## Scope - Determine why children are allocating NEW consoles rather than inheriting. The likely cause is console-less parents (services / detached dispatchers), where each console-mode child must allocate its own. - For LEAF children only -- stdio bound to explicit handles, spawning nothing console-mode themselves, needing no console control event -- spawn with `DETACHED_PROCESS` (no console allocated at all). `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` is NOT sufficient on its own: it creates a console without a window, and conhost still starts. - Apply in the Go spawn path (`SysProcAttr`) ONLY. The Python spawn path stays on `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` -- detaching it is a reverted regression pinned by two passing tests. See the correction section. ## Work unit leaf -- one commit changing spawn creation flags in the two spawn paths. ## Done condition LEAF children -- explicit-handle stdio, no console-mode grandchildren, no CTRL_BREAK need -- are spawned with `DETACHED_PROCESS` in the Go spawn path, and the conhost birth count FOR THE SPAWN SUBTREE over a stated window drops as a result. Dispatcher/worker spawns and anything behind a `.cmd` shim keep their hidden console; the python path stays on `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`. ## Acceptance gate - The mechanism is **witnessed**, not assumed: show the conhost births tracking a specific spawn path before the change, and gone after. - conhost births per unit of work drop measurably, reported with the counting window. - Nothing that needed a console lost one: no regression in interactive/guarded sessions, and no output lost from a detached child. - The flag choice is documented at the spawn site, including why `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` alone was not used. ## Correction before you start `internal/windowgate` **already** sets `HideWindow` + `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` on background spawns (`ConfigureBackgroundCommand`, `internal/windowgate/exec_windows.go:135`), and 124 call sites route through it. Do not re-add that flag and do not close this rung on finding it present. The gap is one flag further on: `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` suppresses the console *window* but the child still gets a console **allocated** -- Windows still creates the conhost.exe host object, which is the per-spawn cost this rung is about. Only `DETACHED_PROCESS` (`0x00000008`) allocates no console at all. So the measurement to make is: same spawn, `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` vs `DETACHED_PROCESS`, counting conhost births and page faults, not wall time alone. **CORRECTED 2026-08-06.** This section previously said `git grep DETACHED_PROCESS` returns nothing in this tree. That was wrong, and it was the single most misleading line in the issue. `DETACHED_PROCESS` is a **documented rejected alternative** on the python side, with two regression tests pinning the rejection (`tools/issue_resolve_dispatch.py:2207-2222`, `tools/issue_resolve_dispatch_test.py:2498, 2507, 2514`; same conclusion at `tools/issue_dispatch.py:781`, `tools/fleet_dos_dispatch_watchdog.py:153`, `tools/claude_agent_chat.py:761`). Two failure modes, both **observed and reverted**, not theorized: 1. A `.cmd`/`.bat` launcher (`opencode.CMD`, the npm shim) runs under cmd.exe, which REQUIRES a console. Detached, the batch wrapper dies at the `Terminate batch job (Y/N)?` prompt with zero output -- every dispatched glm/opencode worker was DOA with a 0-byte log until it got a hidden console back. 2. A native worker (`claude.exe`) given `DETACHED_PROCESS` has no console, **so every console tool IT spawns -- git, gh, fak, the shell -- pops its OWN VISIBLE window.** That was the "random popup windows" during dispatched runs. Reason 2 is not an ergonomics footnote: it inverts this rung's arithmetic. A hidden console is INHERITED by the whole tool subtree, which is how one `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` console currently covers a worker and all of its git/gh/fak/shell children. Detach the parent and that shared console is gone, so every console-mode descendant allocates its own -- the Why-section mechanism, one level down, multiplied by the fan-out. For the dispatcher -> worker -> git/gh/fak chain that produces most of the 718 births, converting the parent is expected to **increase** conhost births. **Therefore: count conhost births for the spawn SUBTREE, not for the direct child.** A per-child count reports a clean win on exactly the change that made the tree worse. **Scope is LEAF spawns only.** Convert a call site only if it (a) has stdio bound to explicit handles, (b) spawns nothing console-mode itself, and (c) never needs a console control event -- a detached child cannot be reached by CTRL_BREAK. `internal/gitbroker.SpawnRunner`'s `git cat-file --batch` is that shape. A dispatched agent worker is exactly not, and neither is anything launched through a `.cmd` shim. ## Current state conhost is the single largest image in the churn ablation: 718 births of 2,610 (27.5 %) -- a whole extra process creation, at ~8,166 page faults each, for a console nothing reads. The Go helper now EXISTS: `internal/windowgate.ConfigureDetachedCommand` (`exec_windows.go:161`, no-op at `exec_other.go:17`) is on trunk, with `TestConfigureDetachedCommandClearsNoWindowAndDetaches` pinning that it CLEARS `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` rather than OR-ing it -- Windows treats the two as mutually exclusive and silently ignores the window flag when `DETACHED_PROCESS` is set. Its doc comment already states the leaf-only constraint. What remains is choosing which call sites qualify, and proving the subtree count moves. The python side deliberately does NOT get this flag; see the correction above. ## Witness A before/after conhost birth count over a stated window, with the mechanism WITNESSED rather than assumed: show conhost births tracking one specific spawn path before the change and gone after. `go test ./cmd/fak` passes and no guarded/interactive session loses output. ## Likely files - `internal/windowgate/exec_windows.go` - `cmd/fak/dispatch_helper_windows.go` - `tools/issue_resolve_dispatch.py` ## Why now conhost is the single largest image in the churn ablation -- 718 of 2,610 births, 27.5 % -- and it is pure overhead: a whole process creation, ~8,166 page faults, for a console nothing reads. At 25.8 births/sec it is the cheapest large win on the box because it is a spawn flag, not a refactor. ## Working spine Find which spawn path allocates new consoles, then pass `DETACHED_PROCESS` for children whose stdio is already redirected, in both the Go (`SysProcAttr`) and python (`creationflags`) spawn paths. ## In scope The spawn-flag change in both languages; a witnessed before/after conhost birth count; a note at the spawn site recording the flag choice. ## Out of scope Any change to what those children do, or to spawn frequency. This rung makes each spawn cheaper, not rarer. ## Expected steps 4 ## Assumptions - The affected children have their stdio redirected already and none of them opens an interactive console. - The parents are console-less (services / detached dispatchers), which is why each child allocates its own. ## Confusion risks - `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` is NOT sufficient. It creates a console without a window; conhost still starts. Only `DETACHED_PROCESS` allocates none. - ...but `DETACHED_PROCESS` on a NON-leaf parent moves the console allocation to the grandchildren and gives each one a VISIBLE window. Already shipped and reverted once; see the correction section. - A per-child conhost count can show an improvement while the subtree got worse. Count the subtree. - Witness the mechanism, do not assume it. conhost is a shadow of other spawns, so a drop could be caused by something else entirely -- tie it to a specific spawn path. - A guarded or interactive session that silently loses output is a worse regression than the churn. ## Coordination - Work directly on trunk (`main`); the trunk guard refuses off-trunk commits (`OFF_TRUNK`). - Commit by explicit path (`fak commit --path

-F `), never `git add -A` -- this is a shared multi-session checkout and a peer's uncommitted work sits in the same tree. - End the subject with a `(fak )` trailer or the ship stays NOT_SHIPPED. ## Trigger Ablation finding under #3153: conhost is the top image by births and is entirely overhead. ## Batch policy One issue covering both spawn paths through the single windowgate chokepoint; splitting per language would make the before/after count uninterpretable, and there is no ticket per spawn site -- the chokepoint is why this is one edit. Sites whose stdio wiring makes them unsafe to detach stay on CREATE_NO_WINDOW and are listed in the closing comment rather than filed separately. ## Closure binding Closes when conhost births tracking a specific spawn path are shown before the change and gone after, with the window stated, and nothing that needed a console lost one. ## Parent context Parent: #3153. ## Work estimate 3 points. ## Overall completion contribution 3/30 points of #3153: an independent spawn-reduction arm, not part of #5619. ## Completion standard development

records.title: perf(fak): fak.exe costs 172 ms and 65.5 MB to start, and hooks pay it every turn
records.body:
## Why Measured on the reference host, 10 calls each, warm: ``` /usr/bin/true (32 KB) 26 ms <- the Windows CreateProcess floor git --version 35 ms git status --porcelain 78 ms fak.exe version (65.5 MB) 172 ms fak.exe --help 235 ms ``` **fak is the most expensive image on the box** â€” 6.6x the spawn floor and ~5x git. `--help` costing more than `version` shows this is startup, not dispatch. Every hook that shells `fak` pays it, once per turn, per session, across 8 resident sessions. This is the same disease as #5619 but pointed at our own binary: the cost is in *starting the process*, and we start it constantly. ## Scope Two independent directions, either of which is worth landing alone: 1. **Make startup cheap.** Find what 65.5 MB of Go binary does before `main` dispatches. Likely suspects: package-level `init()` work, large embedded assets, eager config/registry loads that most verbs never use. Make it lazy. 2. **Stop starting it.** Hot hook queries should go to a resident process over the existing lifecycle socket (`cmd/fak/guard_lifecycle_ipc.go`) instead of a fresh 65 MB image. Same shape as #5619, different server. Defender real-time protection is ON on this host and image scanning is charged per spawn (see closed #2342, which measured the per-spawn scan tax at ~21 % of a core), so binary size is not merely a page-mapping cost. ## Work unit leaf -- one commit: profile first, then the single highest-cost laziness fix it names. ## Done condition `fak`'s startup cost is attributed by a committed profile and then measurably reduced, either by making pre-dispatch work lazy or by serving hot hook queries from a resident process instead of a new one. ## Acceptance gate - The startup cost is **attributed** before anything is optimized: a profile showing where the 172 ms goes. No blind trimming. - A measured reduction in `fak ` wall-clock, reported the same way as above (n calls, warm, same session). - If the resident route is taken instead: hot hook paths no longer spawn `fak`, and the fail-open contract holds (socket down => spawn as today), proven by test. - Binary size reported before/after, since Defender scans the image per spawn. ## Current state `fak.exe version` costs 172 ms against a 26 ms Windows CreateProcess floor, and `--help` costs 235 ms -- more than `version` -- which locates the cost in startup, not dispatch. The binary is 65.5 MB and Defender scans it per spawn. Every hook that shells `fak` pays this, once per turn, per session, across 8 resident sessions. Nothing is lazy today. ## Witness A committed profile attributing the 172 ms BEFORE anything is trimmed, then a measured wall-clock reduction for a cheap verb reported the same way (n calls, warm, same session), with binary size before/after. `go test ./cmd/fak` passes. If the resident route is taken instead, a test kills the socket and asserts the hook still works by spawning. ## Likely files - `cmd/fak/version.go` - `cmd/fak/guard_lifecycle_ipc.go` - `cmd/fak/guard_stophook.go` ## Why now `fak.exe version` costs 172ms against a 26ms Windows CreateProcess floor, and `--help` costs 235ms -- more than `version` -- which places the cost in startup rather than dispatch. Every hook that shells `fak` pays it once per turn, per session, across 8 resident sessions. It is the same disease as #5619 pointed at our own binary. ## Working spine Profile what runs before `main` dispatches, then either make the largest pre-dispatch cost lazy or serve the hot hook queries from the existing resident lifecycle socket instead of a fresh 65.5 MB image. ## In scope A committed startup profile; the single highest-cost fix that profile names; before/after wall-clock for a cheap verb and before/after binary size. ## Out of scope Blind size trimming, dependency removal for its own sake, or a broad refactor. The profile decides what gets touched. ## Expected steps 5 ## Assumptions - A meaningful share of the 172ms is package-level `init()` work or eager loading that most verbs never use. - Defender real-time protection stays on; closed #2342 measured the per-spawn image scan at ~21 % of a core, so binary size is not merely a page-mapping cost. ## Confusion risks - Attribute before optimizing. `--help` costing more than `version` is the clue that this is startup, not dispatch -- do not go hunting in the verb table. - Measure the same way as the baseline (n calls, warm, same session) or the before/after is not comparable. - If the resident route is chosen, the fail-open contract still applies: socket down must mean spawn as today, proven by test. ## Coordination - Work directly on trunk (`main`); the trunk guard refuses off-trunk commits (`OFF_TRUNK`). - Commit by explicit path (`fak commit --path

-F `), never `git add -A` -- this is a shared multi-session checkout and a peer's uncommitted work sits in the same tree. - End the subject with a `(fak )` trailer or the ship stays NOT_SHIPPED. ## Trigger Cost-ladder finding under #3153: fak is the most expensive image on the box, 6.6x the spawn floor. ## Batch policy One issue: profile plus the one fix it names. Do not fan out per suspected cost. ## Closure binding Closes when the profile is committed, one named cost is removed or deferred, and a measured wall-clock reduction is reported with n, warmth, and session held constant. ## Parent context Parent: #3153. ## Work estimate 3 points. ## Overall completion contribution 3/30 points of #3153: an independent spawn-reduction arm, not part of #5619. ## Completion standard development

records.title: feat(compute): add an optional async-upload fence so the activated-expert prefetch can be measured as overlap (epic #5606, follows #5614)
records.body:
## Problem

R3/#5614 landed the same-step activated-set prefetch: a layer's routed top-k is staged into the ring *before* its first expert GEMM, in route order, at zero extra page-ins (`internal/model/expert_ring_prefetch.go`, `aa78492e5fea`).

It could not deliver the witness that issue asked for — "fraction of activated-expert page-in latency overlapped with compute" — because **there is nothing to overlap against**. `compute.Backend` (`internal/compute/compute.go:352-378`) exposes

```go
Upload(t Tensor, as Dtype) Tensor // host -> resident, optionally narrowing dtype
Read(t Tensor) []float32          // resident -> host f32 (the only host fence on an async backend)
```

and no stream, event, or completion handle. So a caller can issue an upload early, but cannot:

- know when it landed,
- fence *only* that upload rather than the whole queue via `Read`,
- or attribute any measured time to transfer-vs-compute.

On a backend whose `Upload` is internally async the prefetch genuinely does overlap today — expert 0's GEMM runs while experts 1..k-1 are still landing — but that is unobservable and therefore untunable. On cpu-ref it is a pure reordering.

This is the prerequisite the R3 issue did not price, and it gates the actual latency win of the whole offload ladder: R0-R4 made expert residency **bounded, pinned, policy-chosen and prefetched**, but a ring miss is still a *synchronous* upload on the critical path.

## Scope

An optional async-staging extension on the backend interface, in the shape `compute` already uses for optional capabilities (`RankUploader`, `CollectiveInitializer` — type-asserted, absent on cpu-ref, never widening the core interface):

```go
// AsyncUploader is an OPTIONAL extension for backends that can issue a host->device
// transfer without fencing the caller.
type AsyncUploader interface {
    UploadAsync(t Tensor, as Dtype) (Tensor, Fence)
}
type Fence interface {
    Wait()          // block until this transfer is visible to subsequent ops
    Done() bool     // non-blocking poll, for overlap accounting
}
```

Then `pagedRing.stage` takes the async path when the backend offers one, and `prefetchActivatedExperts` returns without fencing — the demand staging in `weightHALStagedBounded` fences the specific weight it is about to multiply.

## Likely files

- `internal/compute/compute.go` — the optional interface, next to `RankUploader`.
- `internal/model/paging_ring.go` — `stage` issues async when available; `hold` already covers the lifetime question.
- `internal/model/expert_ring_prefetch.go` — drop the implicit fence; record issue/landing for the overlap meter.
- `internal/model/expert_ring_hal.go` — `ExpertRingStats` gains the overlap fraction.

## Acceptance gate

```
go test ./internal/model/ -run 'ExpertRingPrefetch' -count=1
```

- A backend advertising `AsyncUploader` records a non-zero overlapped fraction on a k>1 layer; cpu-ref (no async) reports 0 and is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- The bit-equality witness R0 established still holds on the async path: a ring-served GEMM equals a resident one.
- No fence is skipped — a weight is never multiplied before its transfer is visible. A deliberately-delayed test fence must make the *test* fail, not produce wrong numbers.

## Not in scope

Cross-layer / predictive prefetch (#4300), and the checkpoint tier under a miss (R5/#5616). This is only the primitive that makes issue-early observable.

Parent epic: #5606. Follows #5614.

records.title: feat(serve): expose the activated-expert ring as a --n-cpu-moe flag and admit on the activated set, not the stored one (epic #5606, completes #5612)
records.body:
## Problem

R1/#5612 is closed, and its *sizing math* did land: `Model.ResolveExpertSpillPlacement` builds a budget from measured resident bytes and real MoE layer ordinals, `Session.ApplyExpertSpillPlacement` installs it, and `InKernelPlanner.SetExpertSpill` resolves it once per serve against `compute.DeviceMemoryInfo`.

What did **not** land is the operator-facing half. Today the only way to reach any of it is the environment variable `FAK_N_CPU_MOE`. There is no `fak serve` flag, so the entire R0-R4 ladder — bounded ring (#5611), durable pin-set (#5613), same-step prefetch (#5614), measured victim policy (#5615) — is reachable only by a Go caller or an env var. That is the gap between "landed" and "first-class".

Two concrete edits, both small, both currently blocked on peer-held files in a shared checkout:

**1. Flag registration** — `newServeFlagSet` in `cmd/fak/serve.go`:

```
--n-cpu-moe N|auto
```

matching the semantics `expert_spill_fit.go` already implements (`auto` = fit to measured device headroom). It needs a `gateway.Config` field and to reach the `agent.NewInKernelPlanner` call at `internal/gateway/gateway.go:2354`, then the existing `SetExpertSpill`.

**2. The fit-predicate swap** — `refuseEPPlanIfUnfit` (`cmd/fak/serve.go:935-958`) still calls `FitCPUOffloadExpertsOnDevice`, which charges the checkpoint for **every** expert. The whole premise of this epic is that only top-k are activated (GLM-5.2: 8 of 256, ~3%), so the admission should use `FitActivatedExpertsOnDevice`. As it stands a serve refuses plans that would in fact fit, on a stored-bytes calculation the ring makes obsolete. One line.

## Blocker (why this is filed rather than done)

`cmd/fak/serve.go` and `cmd/fak/serve_stages.go` are index-staged by concurrent sessions, and `internal/gateway/gateway.go` carries unstaged peer hunks with untracked companions. `git commit -- <path>` takes the **worktree**, not the index, so committing these paths would sweep a peer's in-flight work into an unrelated commit. This needs a window when those three files are quiescent — or their owners to land first.

## Likely files

- `cmd/fak/serve.go` — `newServeFlagSet` registration; the `refuseEPPlanIfUnfit` predicate swap.
- `internal/gateway/gateway.go` — config field + plumb to `NewInKernelPlanner` (~line 2354).

## Acceptance gate

```
go test ./cmd/fak/ ./internal/gateway/ -count=1
```

- `fak serve --help` lists `--n-cpu-moe`; `--n-cpu-moe auto` on a device with a known memory probe produces a non-zero ring budget in serve telemetry, and `--n-cpu-moe 0` is byte-for-byte the current default path.
- A plan that fits the *activated* set but not the *stored* set is admitted rather than refused, with a witness naming both numbers.

## Not in scope

The residency *reporting* verb — that is R6/#5617, which also wants `ExpertRingStats` (now carrying pin count, prefetch count, and the activated-coverage meter) on a `fak` verb and in serve telemetry.

Parent epic: #5606. Completes the operator half of #5612.

records.title: feat(observability): W3C trace-context + OTLP span export — make fak the end-to-end trace backbone from agent endpoint to provider
records.body:
## What

`fak` correlates with a proprietary flat `X-Trace-Id`: the gateway honors a client-supplied one or
mints it (`internal/gateway/metrics_http.go:316`, `internal/gateway/http.go:526`), stamps it on the
access log, `/v1/fak/events`, and the journal `Row.TraceID`, and returns it in the response header.
There is **no W3C `traceparent`/`tracestate` and no OTLP export anywhere** in `internal/`, `cmd/`, or
`pkg/` — grep returns zero hits.

Add two things: (1) accept and propagate W3C trace-context, and (2) an optional OTLP span exporter so
one served turn becomes a real span tree.

## Why

fak is the only component that sits on the *whole* path — the agent endpoint, the kernel's
adjudication and optimization decisions, and the upstream provider call. That is a structural
observability advantage no per-layer tool has, and today it is discarded at both boundaries:

- **Inbound:** an endpoint already inside an OTel-instrumented app arrives with a `traceparent`. fak
  ignores it and mints an unrelated id, so the operator's trace *ends* at the gateway. Every fak
  decision is off-trace.
- **Outbound:** the provider call is not a child span, so time spent *inside* fak (adjudication,
  compaction, cache-breakpoint placement, routing, retries) is indistinguishable from provider
  latency in any external view. "Is fak slow, or is Anthropic slow?" is currently unanswerable from
  the operator's own tooling.
- **Flat, not a tree:** `X-Trace-Id` carries no parent/child, no duration, no sampling.
  `fak_gateway_operation_duration_seconds` gives aggregate per-operation latency but cannot show
  *one* slow turn's waterfall across the stages that produced it.

fak already owns the span vocabulary — `internal/metrics/microtrace.go` (MicroSpan, multiplexed by
trace id, JSONL round-trip) — but it is scoped to the `fak micro` microagent host and explicitly not
on the serve/guard path. That file names its own retirement condition: *"if OpenTelemetry-style
external tracing supersedes an in-process span store."* This is that.

This is also the **only** genuinely-missing half of the `observability-metrics-tracing` row in
`docs/industry-scorecard/operability.md`. The Prometheus metric set that row calls absent (TTFT,
TPOT, queue depth, KV-cache usage, prefix-cache hit) has shipped since `1d4855f200` (2026-06-29); see
the companion scorecard-correction ticket. OTel is the real gap.

Related but distinct: #4262 (Perfetto exporter for `fak micro trace` — a different sink for the
microagent span store, not the served-turn path), #4254 (guard/dispatch lifecycle wall-clock plane,
not the served-turn span tree).

## Working spine

- **Header layer:** honor inbound `traceparent`/`tracestate` and continue the trace. Keep
  `X-Trace-Id` as the fak-native id (derive it from the OTel trace-id) so every existing
  journal / `/v1/fak/events` / access-log join survives unchanged. Mint a fresh root when absent,
  exactly as today.
- **Span layer:** one server span per served turn, with child spans for the stages the gateway
  already times — adjudication, compaction/shed, cache-breakpoint placement, the upstream call, and
  retries. Attributes come from fields already recorded at those seams (verdict, reason, reuse
  regime, cache_read/cache_write tokens, model, tenant principal). **No payloads and no tool args** —
  the same rule `log_privacy` scores 100/100 on today, and the same egress discipline
  `internal/tracesink` already applies.
- **Export:** `--otlp-traces-endpoint` (named after the vLLM flag this dimension is judged against),
  off by default; a stdout/file exporter for dogfood.
- **Open design question, must be decided explicitly:** `go.mod` has **zero external dependencies**
  and that property is load-bearing for this project. Hand-rolling an OTLP/HTTP+protobuf writer vs.
  taking the OTel SDK as the first external dep is a real trade. Record the decision and its
  reasoning before implementing.

## DoD

- [ ] Inbound `traceparent` is parsed and validated per the W3C spec and the trace is continued; a
      malformed header falls back to minting (never a 4xx) and is counted in a metric.
- [ ] The outbound upstream request carries a `traceparent` naming the fak span as parent.
- [ ] Existing `X-Trace-Id` behavior is byte-identical when no `traceparent` is present — no
      regression to the journal / `/v1/fak/events` / access-log joins (assert in test).
- [ ] For one served turn: a span tree with a server span plus at least the upstream-call child,
      carrying the stage attributes above, and **no** payload or tool-arg attribute (asserted).
- [ ] `--otlp-traces-endpoint` exports to an `httptest` collector in a contract test; unset means
      zero spans constructed and no added allocation on the hot path.
- [ ] Dogfood readout: one real turn's waterfall showing fak-internal time separated from provider
      time.
- [ ] The zero-dep vs. OTel-SDK decision is recorded with its justification.

## Files

`internal/gateway/` (HTTP middleware, upstream client, the already-timed seams), a new
`internal/otelspan` or an extension of `internal/metrics/microtrace.go`, `cmd/fak/serve.go` (flag).
No hardware gate.

## Acceptance gate

A single agent turn issued with an inbound `traceparent` produces, in an OTLP collector, **one
connected trace** whose root is the caller's span and which contains a fak server span and an
upstream-provider child span, with fak-internal time separable from provider time — and the same
turn's `X-Trace-Id` still joins the access log, `/v1/fak/events`, and the journal row exactly as it
does today.

records.title: feat(gateway): cut the serving-latency histograms by cache regime — prove the reuse optimization in latency, not just token counters
records.body:
## What

`fak_gateway_inference_ttft_seconds`, `_tpot_seconds`, and `_e2e_seconds` are emitted with an **empty
label set** — literally `writeHistogram(b, "...", "", snap.ttftHist)` at
`internal/gateway/metrics_render.go:985,987,989`.

The gateway knows each turn's cache warmth at the exact moment it records that turn's latency:
`observeInferenceTimed` has `cachedTok` and `cacheCreateTok` in scope and already uses them to bump
`inferCachedHits`, three lines above the `inferTTFTHist.observe(...)` call
(`internal/gateway/metrics_observe.go:821-878`). That correlation is then thrown away.

Cut the three histograms by the reuse regime the same turn was in, reusing the shipped
`frozen | partial | cold` vocabulary (`cacheobs.FrozenFloor = 0.90` / `ColdCeil = 0.10`,
`internal/cacheobs/cacheobs.go:49-55`) that `fak_gateway_kv_prefix_turns_by_regime_total{regime}`
already publishes.

## Why

This is the one cut only fak can emit, and it is the cut that proves fak's own thesis.

fak's claim is *"warm prefix ⇒ faster and cheaper."* Today the two halves of that sentence live in
two unjoinable surfaces: `..._kv_prefix_turns_by_regime_total{regime}` counts **how many** turns were
frozen/partial/cold, and `..._inference_ttft_seconds` distributes latency over **all** turns blended
together. So an operator cannot ask the obvious question from the live surface:

> what does the cache actually buy me, in p95 TTFT, on my traffic?

Today that number exists only in offline benchmarks. With the label it is one expression:

```promql
histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(fak_gateway_inference_ttft_seconds_bucket{regime="frozen"}[5m]))
histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(fak_gateway_inference_ttft_seconds_bucket{regime="cold"}[5m]))
```

That is a per-deployment, continuously-measured, self-serving proof of the optimization — and it is
the regression detector for a cache that silently stops paying: the regime *counters* can look
perfectly healthy while the frozen-regime *tail* degrades, and nothing on the current surface would
show it.

vLLM structurally cannot emit this for the agent path, because it does not own the compaction /
breakpoint / vdso decisions that *set* the regime. fak owns both the decision and the measurement.
This is the end-to-end-position advantage, cashed in.

**Precedent for the label discipline already exists in-tree.** `internal/cacheobs/labeled.go` (#3391)
books per-(model, tenant) rows from the *same* clamped per-turn values inside the *same* critical
section, so summing label rows reconciles exactly with the global counters, and it normalizes an
absent component to `"unknown"` so a legacy tap and a labeled tap can never mint two spellings of one
series. Follow that contract exactly — a labeled histogram that does not sum back to the global one
is worse than no label at all.

Scope note: `fak_serving_*` already carries `worker`/`engine`/`model` labels
(`internal/gateway/serving_metrics.go:205-210`). **Regime** is the missing cut here, not model.

## DoD

- [ ] `observeInferenceTimed` classifies the turn's regime from the reuse ratio it already has,
      via `cacheobs.FrozenFloor`/`ColdCeil` — one vocabulary, never a second spelling of the buckets.
- [ ] The three histograms emit `{regime="frozen"|"partial"|"cold"|"unknown"}`. A turn whose reuse is
      unobservable books `unknown` rather than being defaulted into a real regime — the same honesty
      rule `localityUnknown` already applies in `attributeServedTurn`.
- [ ] **Reconciliation test:** summing every regime row's `_count` and `_sum` equals the values the
      previously-unlabeled global histogram would have produced for the same turns.
- [ ] Cardinality is bounded and stated in the help text: 4 regimes × 3 families. If a tenant cut is
      added later it rides the existing `cacheobs.Labels` normalization and states its own bound.
- [ ] Help text names the join to `fak_gateway_kv_prefix_turns_by_regime_total` so an operator finds
      the counterpart surface.
- [ ] A dashboard panel or doc line showing frozen-vs-cold p95 TTFT — keeps `metric_doc_coverage`
      moving and holds `dashboard_integrity` at 0 debt in `docs/OBSERVABILITY-SCORECARD.md`.

## Files

`internal/gateway/metrics_observe.go`, `internal/gateway/metrics_render.go`,
`internal/gateway/metrics_snapshot.go`, `internal/cacheobs/` (if the classifier is lifted to be
shared), plus `*_test.go`. No hardware gate.

## Acceptance gate

On a live `fak serve`, `histogram_quantile(0.95, ...{regime="cold"})` is measurably worse than
`{regime="frozen"}` over the same window on real traffic, **and** the regime rows' `_count`/`_sum`
sum exactly to the unlabeled totals the same scrape would have produced before the change.

records.title: docs(scorecard): the operability observability row is stale — fak ships the vLLM TTFT/TPOT/queue/KV-usage/prefix-hit set; only OTel remains a real gap
records.body:
## What

The `observability-metrics-tracing` row in `tools/industry_scorecard.data/rows-operability.json` is
stamped `"measured_on": "2026-06-23"` and grades `trails` on the stated grounds that fak has

> no committed TTFT/TPOT/queue-depth/cache-hit Prometheus series

**Six days later**, commit `1d4855f200` (2026-06-29, *"feat(gateway): add inference TTFT/TPOT/e2e
latency histograms to /metrics"*) landed exactly those series. The row has not been re-measured
since, so `docs/industry-scorecard/operability.md` currently **understates the shipped binary** to
every reader.

## Why

The scorecard's whole contract is that fak's column is re-derived from the tree, and
`docs/OBSERVABILITY-SCORECARD.md` makes the **Go binary the metric source of truth** — a doc that
references a metric the binary does not emit is scored as a defect. This row is that same defect
class pointed the other way: it asserts the *absence* of series the binary *does* emit. It
manufactures debt that does not exist, and it buries the one gap that does.

Every series the row calls missing, as emitted today:

| Row's claim | Emitted family | vLLM analogue |
|---|---|---|
| no per-request TTFT | `fak_gateway_inference_ttft_seconds` (histogram); `fak_serving_*` TTFT | `time_to_first_token_seconds` |
| no TPOT / inter-token | `fak_gateway_inference_tpot_seconds` (histogram); `fak_serving_*` ITL | `inter_token_latency_seconds` |
| no queue depth | `fak_gateway_inflight_requests{,_by_route}`, `fak_gateway_inflight_max_age_seconds`, `fak_serving_num_requests_waiting` / `_running` | `num_requests_waiting` / `_running` |
| no KV-cache usage | `fak_gateway_kv_memory_resident_bytes` / `_capacity_bytes` / `_headroom_ratio`, `fak_serving_kv_cache_usage_perc` | `kv_cache_usage_perc` |
| no prefix-cache hit rate | `fak_gateway_kv_prefix_reuse_ratio`, `fak_gateway_inference_cached_prompt_hit_ratio`, `fak_serving_prefix_cache_hit_rate` | `prefix_cache_hits` / `_queries` |

The parity intent is named in the source itself, not inferred:
`internal/gateway/metrics_render.go:982-989` ("*bringing the de facto serving-latency Prometheus SET
to parity*", with each family documented as "*fak analogue of vLLM …*"), and again per family at
`internal/gateway/serving_metrics.go:195-201` ("*Name aligns with vLLM …*"). `fak_gateway_inference_e2e_seconds`
additionally covers `e2e_request_latency_seconds`, which the row does not even claim credit for.

**The half of the row that is still true: OpenTelemetry.** `traceparent` / `tracestate` / OTLP appear
nowhere in `internal/`, `cmd/`, or `pkg/`; fak's correlation is a proprietary `X-Trace-Id`. That is
the gap this row should isolate rather than bundle — tracked in **#5629**.

## DoD

- [ ] Re-measure the row against the binary and update `verdict`, `comparison_note`, `fak_doc`, and
      `measured_on` in `tools/industry_scorecard.data/rows-operability.json`.
- [ ] `comparison_note` cites the emitted families above as the metric-set evidence and scopes the
      residual gap to **OpenTelemetry distributed tracing only**, pointing at #5629.
- [ ] The verdict moves off the "no series exist" grounds. Keep it honest: `trails` on the tracing
      half stays defensible; a metric-set claim must be worded as **metric-set** parity, not tracing
      parity. Do **not** collapse the two into one unqualified `parity`.
- [ ] The separate `[SIMULATED] metrics-service scrape adapter` grounds are either re-verified or
      dropped from this row — it is a distinct claim from the native surface and should not carry the
      whole verdict.
- [ ] Regenerate `docs/industry-scorecard/operability.md` and the scorecard index from the data file;
      the committed markdown matches regeneration byte-for-byte.
- [ ] Sweep the sibling operability rows for the same staleness class — several were measured on the
      same 2026-06-23 pass and predate later landings.

## Files

`tools/industry_scorecard.data/rows-operability.json`, `docs/industry-scorecard/operability.md`,
`docs/industry-scorecard/README.md` (regenerated). Docs + data only; no hardware gate.

## Acceptance gate

Regenerating the scorecard from `tools/industry_scorecard.data/` reproduces the committed markdown,
and the observability row's stated grounds contain **no claim contradicted by a `fak_*` family the
binary emits** — the same binary-is-source-of-truth rule `tools/observability_scorecard.py` already
applies to dashboards, alerts, and docs.

records.title: epic(gateway): the gateway is the fleet's front door — bind the model catalog, the worker roster, and the control spine to the live wire
records.body:
## Current state

fak's own glossary (`docs/fak/concept-glossary.md`, "The gateway / engine family") fixes the
word: the **gateway is the WIRE** — the HTTP/MCP surface fronting the kernel for non-Go clients —
while the kernel is the coordinator, the engine is the dispatch seam, and the vDSO is the local
fast path. That definition is honored inside `internal/gateway`: `Server.routeTable()`
(`internal/gateway/http.go:51-167`) enumerates exactly 44 patterns, and a drift gate
(`internal/gateway/openapi_spec_test.go` `TestOpenAPISpecDocumentsEveryServedRoute`) pins them
against `docs/fak/openapi.yaml`.

What the wire does **not** do is act as the fleet's front door. Measured at HEAD, the gateway is
disjoint from every fleet roster and from the model-placement ladder:

| Half that shipped | Where | Why it is not joined |
|---|---|---|
| Account roster binding model → provider/account/upstream | `modelroute.Roster`, stored at `internal/gateway/gateway.go:1732` and validated at `:1841` | `resolveRoute` has exactly **two** non-test callers, `internal/gateway/tool_routing.go:194,369` — both on the **tool-call** path. Every chat handler copies `req.Model` into `agent.WithModel(...)` (7 sites incl. `http.go:616`, `messages.go:1388`), which overrides only the request BODY, never the one fixed `BaseURL`/credential. |
| Live worker registry with health, hysteresis, drain, fail-closed pick | `internal/gateway/fleet_membership.go` | `NewFleetMembership` has zero non-test callers (**already tracked by #4013** — not re-filed here). |
| Placement ladder device → fleet → vendor with a closed reason vocabulary | `internal/modelroute/placement.go`, `zone.go` | `Place`/`PlaceWithServing` has **no caller in `internal/gateway`** — only `cmd/fak/dispatch_rung_escalate.go:392`, `dispatch_rung_resolve.go:310`, `route_place.go:172`. |
| Serving-liveness report schema | `internal/modelroute/serving.go:76` `ServingReportSchema = "fak.modelroute.serving.v1"` | **Zero producers** in the tree. Every occurrence is a `_test.go` fixture or `docs/model-accounts.md:516`; the only ingestion is an operator file via `--serving <path>`. |
| Fleet control bus: presence, directives, acks, honest `outstanding` fold | `internal/fleetbus` (epic #5599) | **No file imports both `internal/fleetbus` and `internal/gateway`.** The one applier (`cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus.go`) holds a `session.Table` and refuses every non-session op. |
| Host-many-models-decode-one | `internal/polymodel` | **No file under `internal/gateway` imports `internal/polymodel`.** |

Three separate presence records describe "the fleet" — `fleetbus.Instance`
(`internal/fleetbus/fleetbus.go:292`), `fleetspine.Heartbeat`
(`internal/fleetspine/spine.go:31`), `gateway.WorkerSpec`
(`internal/gateway/fleet_membership.go:67`) — and **not one of them carries a served model or a
placement zone**. So no fleet surface in fak can answer the first question an operator of a
multi-model fleet asks: *which model is served where?*

## Why this is next

Every recent structural landing pushes on this seam and then stops at it: the EP follower fanout
across four wires (#5523/#5528), the engine trust boundary (#5421), the fleet control spine
(#5599/#5600), and the July study wave (Dynamo, vLLM, SGLang, Mooncake, LMDeploy) whose borrows
— `TierWeightedOverlap`, `AnticipatedDecodeBlocks`, `ExpectedDrainTime` — landed as pure,
unit-tested folds **with no live caller**. The pattern is consistent and it is the thing to fix:
fak ships both halves of each join and not the join.

## Working spine

One `fak serve` process becomes a *fleet-aware, multi-model* front door in three independent
directions, each of which is a separate child so they can land in any order:

1. **Model catalog** — the chat wire resolves `req.Model` through the roster it already loads,
   and `GET /v1/models` advertises what that roster binds.
2. **Worker roster** — the registry records *which model* a worker holds, so a replica set can be
   heterogeneous, and its observed liveness feeds the placement ladder instead of a hand-written
   JSON file.
3. **Control spine** — the fleet bus reaches gateway-scoped posture (not just session lifecycle),
   its session selectors actually match, its applies reach durable state, and a running gateway is
   discoverable rather than announced out of band.

## In scope

- Filing and sequencing the children below; each child owns its own contract, witness and lane.
- Keeping the three axes disjoint so children in `gateway`, `modelroute`, `fleetbus`, `sessionctl`
  and `cmd` lanes can be worked concurrently by the arbiter.

## Out of scope

- Any implementation in this issue. Epics do not carry code.
- Re-filing #4013 (construct + attach `FleetMembership`) or #3967 (live replica add/drain/remove).
  Both are open and are dependencies, not children.
- MoE *expert* residency (#5606 and its rungs) — that is residency **within** one model; this epic
  is about **whole models** and **whole workers**.

## Done condition

Every child below is filed with a contract-shaped body, labeled, and either closed or explicitly
deferred with a stated reason. The epic closes when a single `fak serve` process can (a) front more
than one model on more than one upstream from its own roster, (b) name the model each worker in its
fleet holds, and (c) be steered and discovered from a control point that never learned its address
out of band.

## Witness

`gh issue view <this epic> --json body` shows every checkbox either checked with a closing SHA or
struck with a stated deferral. Per-child witnesses are named in each child.

## Acceptance gate

The three integration witnesses named by the children pass on one process:
`go test ./internal/gateway ./internal/modelroute ./internal/fleetbus ./internal/sessionctl` green,
plus the drift gate `TestOpenAPISpecDocumentsEveryServedRoute` still green after any route added by
a child.

## Children

- [ ] #5633 — chat wire resolves `req.Model` through `--route-accounts` (lane `gateway`)
- [ ] #5634 — `GET /v1/models` advertises the roster-bound catalog (lane `gateway`)
- [ ] #5635 — `WorkerSpec` carries the served model: heterogeneous replica sets (lane `gateway`)
- [ ] #5636 — produce `fak.modelroute.serving.v1` from a live gateway (lane `modelroute`)
- [ ] #5637 — `fleetbus.Instance` carries served-model capability (lane `fleetbus`)
- [ ] #5638 — gateway-scoped fleetbus applier (lane `cmd`)
- [ ] #5639 — fleetbus lifecycle apply reaches the durable session mirror (lane `cmd`)
- [ ] #5640 — something calls `sessionctl.TagSession` so selectors can match (lane `sessionctl`)
- [ ] #5641 — `fak serve` publishes its gateway URL into the discovery index (lane `cmd`)
- [ ] #5642 — A2A agent card serves this process's real endpoint (lane `gateway`)
- [ ] #5643 — the poly-model lane reaches the live serve path (lane `polymodel`)
- [ ] #5644 — a `--native` turn's in-loop tool calls skip the account roster (lane `gateway`)

**By lens.** Multi-model hosting: #5633, #5634, #5635, #5643, #5644. Fleet: #5635, #5636, #5637, #5641.
Spine: #5637, #5638, #5639, #5640. Front door: #5641, #5642.

## Confusion risks

- **"Fleet" is four different things in this tree** and they are code-level disjoint (verified: no
  tracked Go file imports both `fleetbus` and `gateway`, both `fleetbus` and `fleetspine`, or both
  `fleetspine` and `leaseref`). A child that says "the fleet" must say *which* roster.
- **`gateway.Router` (`internal/gateway/routing.go`) looks like the answer and is not on the path**
  — its only non-test caller is `cmd/fak/computeauto.go:216`, a launch-time compute-target picker.
- **A directive is never its own witness** (`internal/fleetbus` package doc). Any control child
  lands the ack, not the publish.

## Likely files

`internal/gateway/`, `internal/modelroute/`, `internal/fleetbus/`, `internal/sessionctl/`,
`internal/polymodel/`, `cmd/fak/serve*.go`, `docs/fak/openapi.yaml`

```routing
lane: gateway
paths: internal/gateway/**, internal/modelroute/**, internal/fleetbus/**
expected_steps: file children, sequence them, close on the three integration witnesses
```

## Parent context

This epic has no parent issue. Its upstream context is the fleet-control epic **#5599** (command out / ack back) and the serving superset epic **#2236**; it is the *gateway-side* join those two both assume and neither owns.

## Work unit

epic

## Work scale

S3

## Expected steps

12

## Trigger

Concept research on `gateway` across the last few weeks of commits, `docs/notes/CONCEPT-STUDY-*`, and the concept glossary (2026-08-05), which found every half of the gateway/fleet/multi-model join shipped and no join.

## Batch policy

One epic plus eleven leaves, filed once from a single research pass; each leaf is independently dispatchable and lives in a distinct lane, so no follow-on batch is expected from this trigger.

## Closure binding

Closes when all eleven children are closed or explicitly deferred with a stated reason, and `fak epicprogress` reports 100% for this epic. No commit closes this issue directly.

- **Required model tier:** T2
- **Optimal model tier:** T2

### Related

#5599 (fleet control epic), #4013, #3967, #4231, #595, #5416, #2236, #5606, #4302

records.title: feat(gateway): resolve the chat wire's model id through the same --route-accounts roster that already binds tool calls
records.body:
_Parent epic: #5632 — the gateway as the fleet's front door._

## Current state

`fak serve` already loads, validates and consults a model-**account** roster: `Config.RouteAccounts`
(`internal/gateway/gateway.go:781-791`) is a `*modelroute.Roster` whose `Target` carries
Model / Account / Kind / BaseURL / CredEnv / UpstreamModel, it is stored on the server at
`gateway.go:1732`, and `New()` fails loud on a malformed one (`gateway.go:1841-1846`, which the
comment itself calls "the SAME class of security boundary").

That roster reaches exactly one path. `git grep -n resolveRoute -- 'internal/gateway/*.go' | grep -v _test`
returns the definition (`internal/gateway/tool_routing.go:393`) and **two callers**, both in
`tool_routing.go` (`:194`, `:369`) — the `fak_syscall` / tool-call path landed by #2528.

The chat wire ignores it. Every chat handler copies the client's model id straight into the agent
options and nothing else:

- `internal/gateway/http.go:616` — `agent.WithModel(req.Model)`
- `internal/gateway/messages.go:1388`, `messages_stream_planner.go:228`
- `internal/gateway/completions.go:128`, `responses.go:313`, `stream_proxy.go:84`, `gemini.go:188`

`agent.WithModel` overrides `HTTPPlanner.ModelID` — the request **body** — and never the single
fixed `BaseURL` or credential chosen at boot by `selectChatPlanner`
(`internal/gateway/gateway.go:2049-2125`, four exhaustive modes: dual / proxy-only /
in-kernel-only / mock). The one per-request model decision on the chat path is
`DualPlanner.RoutesLocal(reqModel)` (`internal/gateway/dual_planner.go`), a **binary** local-alias
test whose local id is settable only by `fak guard --alongside`.

**Sharper than "the chat wire ignores the roster."** The roster *is* read on the chat path —
exactly once, and not to route. `Server.proxiedLocality` (`internal/gateway/metrics_locality.go:102-118`)
calls `s.roster.BoundZone(reqModel)` to book the turn self-hosted vs vendor for `/metrics`. So today
`/metrics` attributes a chat turn's locality from a binding that **did not decide where the turn
went** — the dial was fixed at `New()`. That makes this issue a correctness fix for the locality
number as well as a capability addition.

**And the tool wire's binding is not a transport either.** `resolveRoute` returns
`Target.EngineRoute()` — a string like `"openai:acct/gpt-5.5"` written to `abi.ToolCall.Engine` so
the residency PDP can adjudicate before `Submit`. It carries no BaseURL and no credential, and all
13 non-test `RegisterEngine` call sites use literal engine ids, so no roster-derived id is ever
registered. The roster's `Target.BaseURL` / `Target.CredEnv` are dead fields outside printers
(`cmd/fak/route.go`) and observability meta (`internal/gateway/tool_routing.go:463`).
`internal/modelroute/account.go:48-50` names the missing piece directly: building an
`agent.HTTPPlanner` from a `Target` is *"the additive dispatch wiring above this seam"* — and
`docs/model-accounts.md:678` still records it as **deferred**.

**Net effect:** a roster declaring three models on three accounts changes nothing about which
upstream answers `/v1/messages` or `/v1/chat/completions`. "N models on one serve" today means
"N ids the one configured upstream happens to accept", not fak routing.

## Why this is next

This is the smallest change that makes one `fak serve` a genuinely multi-model front door, and it
adds no new configuration surface — the roster, the flag (`--route-accounts`), the resolver and its
refusal vocabulary all already exist and are already validated at boot. Everything else in the
gateway epic (a real `/v1/models` catalog, per-model placement, heterogeneous workers) is
downstream of the chat wire being able to answer "which upstream owns this model id".

## Working spine

On each chat request, before planner selection: if `s.roster != nil`, run `req.Model` through
`s.resolveRoute(req.Model, principal)`. A **hit** binds that request to the roster Target's
BaseURL / credential / UpstreamModel. A **miss** keeps today's behavior exactly — pass the id
through to the boot-configured upstream — so an unrostered id is never newly refused.

## In scope

- A per-request planner binding on the chat path, derived from the existing `resolveRoute`.
- Reuse of the existing principal plumbing (`internal/gateway/keyset.go:26`) so a per-principal
  roster binding behaves the same on chat as it already does on tool calls.
- A refusal/passthrough decision written down as a closed rule, and a metric or debug counter
  distinguishing *bound-by-roster* from *passed-through*.

## Out of scope

- The `--native` in-loop tool path. `agent.WithRouteAccounts`
  (`internal/agent/loop_session.go:271`) has **zero non-test callers** —
  `internal/gateway/native_serve.go` and `cmd/fak/main.go` pass `WithRouteManifest` only — so a
  native served turn's tool calls skip the roster entirely. Real, verified, and a separate leaf.

- Changing `GET /v1/models` (its own child).
- Any latency/cost/health-based *choice* among candidates — this is a **binding**, not a policy.
  `gateway.Router` stays off the path.
- The tool-call path, which already works.
- New CLI flags. `--route-accounts` is the surface.

## Done condition

With a roster declaring two models on two distinct upstream base URLs, `POST /v1/messages` naming
model A reaches upstream A and model B reaches upstream B from one `fak serve` process; an id in no
roster reaches the boot-configured upstream exactly as it does at HEAD.

## Witness

`go test ./internal/gateway -run 'TestChatWireResolvesRosterRoute'` — an httptest pair of upstreams
plus a two-target roster, asserting per-request upstream attribution and the unchanged
pass-through arm.

## Acceptance gate

The new test passes; `go test ./internal/gateway` stays green; a request naming an unrostered model
is byte-for-byte unchanged from HEAD behavior (asserted, not assumed).

## Dependencies

None blocking. Independent of #4013 and #3967 (those are about *replica* health, not *model*
binding).

## Confusion risks

- **The roster is already read here, for a different purpose.** A change that adds a *second*
  roster lookup beside `proxiedLocality`'s, instead of making the routing decision the thing
  locality is derived from, leaves `/metrics` attributing off a binding that still routes nothing.
- **`Target.EngineRoute()` is an adjudication token, not a dial.** Reusing it as the transport key
  will not work: `kernel.Reap` looks engines up in an exact map whose keys are all literals.

- **`agent.WithModel` looks like it routes.** It sets the request body's model id only; the
  transport is fixed at boot. Reading it as routing is the exact misread this issue exists to fix.
- **`DualPlanner` is not the general case.** It caps at two fak-hosted identities and its
  `RoutesLocal("")` returns false — an empty model must keep going to the proxy.
- **Do not reach for `gateway.Router`.** It is a tiered *policy* with health and 403-cooldown
  demotion, inert on the request path (`cmd/fak/computeauto.go:216` is its only non-test caller).
  Pulling it in here converts a small binding into a routing-policy change.

## Likely files

`internal/gateway/tool_routing.go`, `internal/gateway/http.go`, `internal/gateway/messages.go`,
`internal/gateway/completions.go`, `internal/gateway/responses.go`,
`internal/gateway/stream_proxy.go`, `internal/gateway/gemini.go`, `internal/modelroute/account.go`

```routing
lane: gateway
paths: internal/gateway/**
expected_steps: resolve req.Model through s.resolveRoute on the chat path; bind BaseURL/cred/UpstreamModel on hit; pass through on miss; test both arms
```

## Parent context

**#5632** — the gateway-as-fleet-front-door epic. This leaf is one of its eleven children and is dispatchable on its own.

## Work unit

leaf

## Work scale

S1

## Expected steps

5

## Trigger

Filed from the #5632 research pass (2026-08-05), which measured this gap first-hand at HEAD; the grounding lines in **Current state** are the evidence.

## Batch policy

One leaf per gap, one gap per lane. No further issues are expected from this trigger; a follow-on rung, if any, is named in **Out of scope**.

## Closure binding

Closes on a commit stamped `(fak gateway)` whose diff adds the chat-path roster resolution and whose CI run shows `TestChatWireResolvesRosterRoute` green.

- **Required model tier:** T2
- **Optimal model tier:** T2

### Related

#2528 (closed — the tool-call half this extends), #595, #5416, #2902, #2861, #4588

records.title: feat(gateway): advertise the roster-bound model catalog on GET /v1/models
records.body:
_Parent epic: #5632 — the gateway as the fleet's front door._

## Current state

`GET /v1/models` is the one model-discovery surface fak serves, and it can return at most two ids.
`handleModels` (`internal/gateway/http.go:1092-1099`) seeds `data` with a single row from `s.model`
and appends exactly one more when the planner type-asserts to `*DualPlanner`:

```go
data := []map[string]any{{"id": s.model, "object": "model", "owned_by": "fak"}}
if d, ok := s.planner.(*DualPlanner); ok {
    data = append(data, map[string]any{"id": d.LocalModelID(), ...})
}
```

There is **no reference to `s.roster`** in the handler. So a gateway launched with
`--route-accounts` declaring three models on three accounts advertises one id, and a client has no
way to tell an id this gateway is *bound* to from one it will blindly forward upstream. The Codex
projection built below it (`http.go:1100-1130`) inherits the same one-or-two-row `data`.

## Why this is next

Discovery is the cheap half of multi-model hosting and the half a client actually consumes: an
OpenAI-wire client that cannot enumerate the catalog needs out-of-band knowledge for every id. The
handler is small, the roster is already on the `Server`, and this is the natural companion to the
chat-wire roster binding — the catalog should describe exactly what that binding will honor.

## Working spine

`handleModels` folds three sources into a deduplicated, deterministically ordered list: the
boot-configured `s.model`, the `*DualPlanner` local alias when present, and every model declared in
`s.roster`. Ids collapse on exact match; ordering is stable so the drift gate and clients see a
fixed sequence.

## In scope

- Reading `s.roster` in `handleModels` and folding declared models into `data`.
- Dedup + stable ordering, and carrying the fold through to the Codex projection so both shapes
  agree.
- Updating `docs/fak/openapi.yaml` / `docs/fak/api-reference.md` if the response shape changes at
  all (the route table is drift-gated by `internal/gateway/openapi_spec_test.go`).

## Out of scope

- Any change to which upstream serves a model (that is the chat-wire roster child).
- Leaking account, credential-env, or base-URL details into the response. The catalog names
  **models**, never seats or secrets.
- Health/availability fields. A declared model is advertised whether or not its upstream is up;
  liveness is the serving-report child's job.

## Done condition

A `fak serve` started with a roster declaring models A, B, C returns all three from
`GET /v1/models` in a stable order, with no duplicate when a declared model equals `s.model` or the
dual local alias; a serve with no roster returns exactly what HEAD returns.

## Witness

records.title: feat(gateway): carry the served model on WorkerSpec so the fleet registry can describe a heterogeneous worker set
records.body:
_Parent epic: #5632 — the gateway as the fleet's front door._

## Current state

`gateway.WorkerSpec` — the record the live worker registry keys everything on — has no model field:

```go
// internal/gateway/fleet_membership.go:67-72
type WorkerSpec struct {
	ID       string
	Role     WorkerRole
	Engine   EngineKind
	Endpoint string
}
```

The replica set is homogeneous **by construction**, not merely by current configuration.
`newProxyPlanner` (`internal/gateway/gateway.go:2358-2383`) hands the *same* `model` string to
`newConfiguredHTTPPlanner` for every configured base URL and then builds
`NewReplicaRouter(model, replicas)` — one model string for the whole set
(`internal/gateway/replica_router.go`). There is no model→worker map anywhere in the tree.

The consequence is a one-directional registry: `FleetMembership` can route **around** a worker
(unhealthy, draining) but can never route **to** a worker *because of which model it holds*. Every
downstream consumer inherits the blindness — `Snapshot()`
(`internal/gateway/fleet_membership.go:261`) is read by `replica_router.go:264`,
`serving_autoscaler.go:479,524` and `fleet_membership_metrics.go:99`, and none of them can express
"this worker serves GLM, that one serves Qwen".

## Why this is next

The moment a fleet holds more than one model — which is the whole premise of `--route-accounts`,
of `internal/polymodel`, and of the placement ladder's fleet rung — an unlabeled worker registry
stops being merely incomplete and starts being *wrong*: it will happily hand a request for model A
to a worker holding model B, and report the resulting upstream error as a health problem. Adding
the field is small; adding it *after* several consumers have hardened around a homogeneous set is
not.

## Working spine

`WorkerSpec` grows an optional `Models []string` (empty = "unconstrained", today's behavior), and
the placement path gains a model-aware filter that runs **before** the health filter, so
"no worker holds this model" is a distinct, typed outcome from `ErrNoHealthyWorker`. The proxy
replica construction learns to attach per-replica model ids rather than one shared string.

## In scope

- The `Models` field on `WorkerSpec`, threaded through `Add` and `Snapshot`.
- A model-aware candidate filter in the pick path, with a typed `ErrNoWorkerForModel` distinct from
  `ErrNoHealthyWorker`.
- Per-replica model ids at the `newProxyPlanner`/`NewReplicaRouter` seam so a heterogeneous set is
  *representable*; the configuration surface that populates them may follow separately.
- The fleet metrics family gaining a model label, if it can be done without unbounded cardinality.

## Out of scope

- Constructing or attaching `FleetMembership` on a live process — that is **#4013** and is a
  dependency, not part of this.
- Live add/drain/remove of replicas — that is **#3967**.
- Any placement *policy* over the model dimension (cost, tier, cache affinity). This issue makes
  heterogeneity **expressible**; choosing among candidates is a later rung.
- Prefill/decode phase splitting across machine classes (#4302) — a different axis of heterogeneity.

## Done condition

A `FleetMembership` holding workers `{A: [m1], B: [m2]}` returns only A as a candidate for `m1` and
only B for `m2`; a worker with an empty `Models` remains a candidate for every model (exactly
today's behavior); a request for a model no worker holds returns `ErrNoWorkerForModel`, not
`ErrNoHealthyWorker` and not a dial to a wrong upstream.

## Witness

`go test ./internal/gateway -run 'TestFleetMembershipFiltersByModel'` — covers the two-model
partition, the empty-`Models` compatibility arm, and the distinct typed error.

## Acceptance gate

New test passes; `go test ./internal/gateway` green including the existing fleet-membership,
replica-router and autoscaler suites; `go test -race ./internal/gateway` green (the registry is
read concurrently by the health loop and the pick path).

## Dependencies

#4013 (nothing constructs `FleetMembership` in production) — this issue is still worth landing
first, because #4013's constructor should populate the model field on the way in rather than be
retrofitted.

## Confusion risks

- **Empty must mean "unconstrained", not "serves nothing".** A fail-closed reading here silently
  empties every existing configuration.
- **Two typed errors, not one.** Folding "no worker holds this model" into `ErrNoHealthyWorker`
  makes a configuration mistake look like an outage — the single most expensive confusion in this
  area.
- **`WorkerSpec` is not the only fleet record.** `fleetbus.Instance` and `fleetspine.Heartbeat`
  have the same missing field and are separate leaves; do not try to unify the three rosters here.
- **Metric cardinality.** A model label on a per-worker gauge multiplies series; bound it.

`internal/gateway/fleet_membership.go`, `internal/gateway/replica_router.go`,
`internal/gateway/gateway.go`, `internal/gateway/fleet_membership_metrics.go`,
`internal/gateway/serving_autoscaler.go`

```routing
paths: internal/gateway/**
expected_steps: add Models to WorkerSpec; model filter before health filter; typed ErrNoWorkerForModel; per-replica model ids at newProxyPlanner; tests
```

records.title: feat(modelroute): produce fak.modelroute.serving.v1 from a live gateway so the placement ladder's fleet rung stops being a hand-written file
records.body:
_Parent epic: #5632 — the gateway as the fleet's front door._

## Current state

`internal/modelroute` has a serving-liveness record and nothing in fak produces it.
`internal/modelroute/serving.go:76` declares:

```go
const ServingReportSchema = "fak.modelroute.serving.v1"
```

Grepping the whole tree for that string returns **only** `_test.go` fixtures
(`cmd/fak/route_place_serving_test.go`, eight occurrences) and one doc sample
(`docs/model-accounts.md:516`). The single ingestion point is `loadServingReport`
(`cmd/fak/route_place_serving.go:121-137`), which reads a path an operator passes with
`--serving <path>`.

So the **fleet rung of the placement ladder is gated by a hand-written JSON file.**
`modelroute.PlaceWithServing` walks device → fleet → vendor with a closed reason vocabulary
(`internal/modelroute/placement.go`, `zone.go`), and whether a fleet zone is admissible depends
entirely on a file a human remembered to refresh. Meanwhile a real prober sits one package away:
`internal/gateway/fleet_membership.go` runs a health loop with hysteresis and drain and exposes
`Snapshot() []WorkerStatus` (`:261`). The two never meet — `Place`/`PlaceWithServing` has **zero
callers in `internal/gateway`** (only `cmd/fak/dispatch_rung_escalate.go:392`,
`cmd/fak/dispatch_rung_resolve.go:310`, `cmd/fak/route_place.go:172`).

`internal/modelroute/serving.go` is explicit that it does not intend to probe — *"Probing is
somebody else's job, above this tier."* This issue is that job.

## Why this is next

A placement decision that consults a stale operator file is worse than one that consults nothing:
it reports a **zone** verdict with the ladder's closed reason vocabulary, which reads as measured
when it is asserted. The producer is the smallest change that turns the ladder's fleet rung from a
convention into an observation, and every downstream multi-model decision (which zone, which
worker, which account) inherits its honesty.

## Working spine

A serve process that maintains a `FleetMembership` emits a `fak.modelroute.serving.v1` document
from its own `Snapshot()` — one entry per worker with its observed state and observation timestamp
— to a well-known path under the fleet state dir. `loadServingReport` gains a
freshness/staleness rule so a report nobody refreshed degrades to *unknown*, not to *healthy*.
`--serving <path>` keeps working unchanged as the operator override.

## In scope

- A producer that folds `FleetMembership.Snapshot()` into `modelroute.ServingReport` and writes it
  atomically (temp-then-rename, per the `fleetbus.Announce` precedent at
  `internal/fleetbus/dirbus.go:142-176`).
- A staleness rule on the consumer side: an entry older than a stated TTL is `unknown`, and the
  ladder's reason vocabulary gains (or reuses) the token for "fleet liveness not observed".
- The default location, derived from the existing fleet state dir rather than a new flag.

## Out of scope

- Cross-host aggregation of reports from several machines. A file per instance is the v1; folding
  them is a follow-on.
- Calling `PlaceWithServing` from `internal/gateway` — the *consumer* join is separate work; this
  issue lands the **producer** so that join has something true to read.
- Latency/throughput/goodput signals. This is **liveness**, not performance. (fak does measure
  TTFT and goodput in `internal/gateway` — `debug.go:92 TTFTTurns`, `MeanTTFTSeconds`,
  `fak_serving_goodput_requests_per_second`; feeding *those* into placement is a different issue
  and is not claimed here.)

## Done condition

With a `FleetMembership` probing two endpoints, one up and one down, a `fak.modelroute.serving.v1`
document appears at the default path whose entries match the observed states; `fak route place`
without `--serving` consumes it and reaches the same verdict it reaches today when handed an
equivalent file by hand; a report older than the TTL yields *unknown* rather than a stale positive.

## Witness

`go test ./internal/modelroute -run 'TestServingReportStaleness'` and
`go test ./cmd/fak -run 'TestRoutePlaceReadsProducedServingReport'` — the second builds a
membership over two httptest endpoints, produces the report, and places against it with no
`--serving` flag.

## Acceptance gate

Both tests pass; `go test ./internal/modelroute ./cmd/fak` green; passing `--serving <path>`
explicitly still takes precedence over the produced file (asserted); no placement verdict changes
for an operator who has not opted in.

## Dependencies

#4013 — nothing constructs `FleetMembership` in a live process today, so the producer has no
source until that lands. The staleness rule and the schema fold can be built and tested against an
injected snapshot before then.

## Confusion risks

- **A produced report must not be more trusted than a hand-written one.** Both are claims with a
  timestamp; the TTL applies to both.
- **Do not let "no report" mean "fleet is down".** The ladder already has a closed reason
  vocabulary — pick the token that means *unobserved*, and if none fits, add one rather than
  overloading a health token.
- **The gateway must not import a placement decision to write this file.** Producing a report is
  an *emission*; consuming it is the other direction and is deliberately not in scope, so the two
  packages stay acyclic.

`internal/gateway/fleet_membership.go`, `cmd/fak/route_place_serving.go`,
`cmd/fak/serve.go`, `docs/model-accounts.md`

records.title: feat(fleetbus): carry served-model capability on the Instance presence record so the fleet roster can answer which model is served where
records.body:
_Parent epic: #5632 — the gateway as the fleet's front door._

## Current state

The fleet control bus's presence record cannot say what an instance serves.
`internal/fleetbus/fleetbus.go:292-309`:

```go
type Instance struct {
	Schema  string
	ID      string
	Machine string
	Role    string   // e.g. "serve"
	PID     int
	Addr    string   // control address, informational
	Ops     []Op     // what it SAYS it can apply — display/diagnostic only
	SeenUTC string
}
```

`Role` is a coarse kind ("serve"), and `Ops` is explicitly documented as a claim that nothing
routes on. There is no model, no engine, no placement zone.

The same hole exists in every other presence record in the tree:
`fleetspine.Heartbeat` (`internal/fleetspine/spine.go:31-39`) carries Schema / ID / Host / State /
AppVersion / Sessions / GeneratedUTC and not even an address; `gateway.WorkerSpec`
(`internal/gateway/fleet_membership.go:67`) carries ID / Role / Engine / Endpoint. Three rosters,
zero model fields — and they are code-level disjoint (no tracked Go file imports both
`internal/fleetbus` and `internal/gateway`, or both `fleetbus` and `fleetspine`).

**So no fleet surface in fak can answer "which model is served where."** The bus roster is also the
ack fold's denominator (`internal/fleetbus/fold.go:51-55`), which means a selector can address "all
serve instances" but never "every instance serving model X".

## Why this is next

The bus already has the two hard parts — a denominator that survives instance death
(`RowOutstanding`, `fold.go:16-20`) and an at-most-once apply claim
(`dirbus.go:268-284`). What it lacks is the one field that makes a *fleet of different models*
addressable. Without it, every model-scoped operator action ("drain everything serving the old
checkpoint", "reload the route manifest on the GLM hosts") degrades to fan-to-all plus per-host
refusal, which is exactly the accepted-but-not-applied shape the package doc warns about.

## Working spine

`Instance` grows optional capability fields — the models this instance serves and, when known, its
placement zone — and the selector grammar grows a matching axis. Both are additive: an instance
that declares nothing keeps matching exactly the selectors it matches today, and the field stays a
**claim**, not a witness, consistent with the `Ops` precedent.

## In scope

- Optional `Models []string` (and, if it costs nothing, `Zone string`) on `fleetbus.Instance`,
  populated by the announcer on a serve instance from whatever the process actually fronts.
- A selector axis matching on it, with the same fail-closed rule the package already documents for
  untagged records.
- `fak fleet` roster output showing the field so an operator can read the catalog.
- Schema-version handling: an older record without the field must still parse and still count in the
  denominator.

## Out of scope

- Making the field authoritative for routing. It stays a display/selection claim; the **ack is the
  witness** (`internal/fleetbus` package doc invariant).
- Unifying `fleetbus.Instance`, `fleetspine.Heartbeat` and `gateway.WorkerSpec` into one record.
  That is a much larger design question; this issue adds the field where the control plane needs it.
- The `WorkerSpec` model field — a separate leaf in the `gateway` lane.

## Done condition

A serve instance fronting models A and B announces both; `fleetbus.PublishTargets` with a
model-scoped selector addresses exactly the instances declaring that model; an instance announced
by an older binary (no field) parses, stays in the roster, and is still counted in `Targeted` by
`Fold`.

## Witness

`go test ./internal/fleetbus -run 'TestInstanceModelSelector'` — covers the positive match, the
non-match, and the old-record compatibility arm through `Fold`.

## Acceptance gate

New test passes; `go test ./internal/fleetbus` green including the fold and roster suites; a
directive published against a model selector into a fleet where nobody declares that model is
refused `FLEETBUS_NO_TARGET` rather than accepted and left outstanding (the existing edge rule at
`internal/fleetbus/dirbus.go` / `PublishTargets`).

## Dependencies

None blocking. Pairs naturally with the gateway-scoped applier child, which is the first consumer
of a model-scoped selector.

## Confusion risks

- **A roster claim is not a witness.** The package doc is explicit; this field must not become a
  routing input on the bus.
- **The denominator must not shrink.** An instance that predates the field, or declares nothing,
  still belongs in `Targeted` for any selector that matched it before — `fold.go:89-102` explains
  precisely why a shrinking denominator is how this report learns to lie.
- **`Role` is not a model.** "serve" describes the process kind; overloading it would break the
  existing selector semantics.

`internal/fleetbus/fleetbus.go`, `internal/fleetbus/fold.go`, `internal/fleetbus/dirbus.go`,
`cmd/fak/fleet_control.go`, `cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus.go`

records.title: feat(serve): a gateway-scoped fleetbus applier so control-plane ops fan to N gateways instead of N POSTs
records.body:
_Parent epic: #5632 — the gateway as the fleet's front door._

## Current state

The fleet control bus and the gateway's control routes both shipped, and they do not touch. **No
file in `internal/gateway` imports `internal/fleetbus`**, and the tree's only applier is
session-scoped by type:

```go
// cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus.go:51-59
type fleetBusApplier struct {
	tbl    *session.Table
	native bool
	ctx    context.Context
}
```

Its first gate refuses anything outside the session vocabulary —
`if _, known := sessionctl.Spec(op); !known { ... }` (`serve_fleetbus.go:63`), documented at
`:12-15` as *"pause/resume/cancel/terminate/throttle → the same `Table.Transition` write … anything
else → `FLEETBUS_UNKNOWN_OP`, acked, never dropped"*. Construction is
`&fleetBusApplier{tbl: tbl, native: native, ctx: ctx}` (`:287`) — it is handed the session table,
never the `gateway.Server`.

Meanwhile every gateway-scoped posture change is a **per-process HTTP POST**: the policy reload,
the admission and cache-posture routes, and the rest of the 23 `/v1/fak/*` control verbs in
`Server.routeTable()` (`internal/gateway/http.go:51-167`). Changing cache posture or reloading the
route manifest across N gateways is N POSTs, N addresses, and no fold that says who actually
applied it.

## Why this is next

Epic #5599's premise — *"tell the fleet `go`, and show me who heard"* — is only half-delivered
while the bus reaches sessions and not the processes fronting them. The expensive half is already
built and tested: the roster denominator, the honest `RowOutstanding` fold
(`internal/fleetbus/fold.go`), the at-most-once apply claim
(`internal/fleetbus/dirbus.go:268-284`), and the ack contract. What is missing is a second applier
that speaks the gateway's vocabulary.

## Working spine

A second applier, constructed with the `gateway.Server` rather than the session table, registers a
**disjoint, closed** op vocabulary for gateway-scoped posture: reload the route manifest, change
cache posture, change the admission/backpressure posture. It reuses the same drain loop, the same
`ClaimApply`, and the same `Ack` shape, so the existing fold reports it unchanged. Ops outside its
vocabulary keep returning `FLEETBUS_UNKNOWN_OP`; the two appliers never share an op token.

## In scope

- A gateway-scoped applier in `cmd/fak` holding the serve `*gateway.Server`, wired into the same
  drain loop that `serve_fleetbus.go:287` already runs.
- A closed op vocabulary, disjoint from `sessionctl.Spec`, with a per-op capability / boundary /
  witness triple in the style `internal/sessionctl` already uses.
- Each op's ack carrying a real `Witness` string and `Affected` count — what changed, not that a
  message arrived.
- Dispatch: one op token routes to exactly one applier; ambiguity is a startup error, not a
  runtime coin flip.

## Out of scope

- New gateway *capabilities*. Every op must map onto a control the gateway already exposes over
  HTTP; this is a second **transport**, not new authority.
- Session ops. `serve_fleetbus.go` keeps them.
- The per-process HTTP routes, which stay exactly as they are (and remain the way #3967's live
  replica ops are driven).
- A network transport for the bus. `DirBus` and its stated shared-directory limitation are
  unchanged.

## Done condition

`fak fleet control send --op <gateway-op> --all` reaches two `fak serve` processes on one bus, both
apply, both ack with a witness naming what changed, and the fold reports `applied=2 outstanding=0`;
an instance that cannot apply the op refuses with a closed reason and is counted `refused`, never
silently `applied`.

## Witness

`go test ./cmd/fak -run 'TestFleetBusGatewayApplier'` — two in-process appliers over one temp
`DirBus`, asserting apply, the witness string, the refusal arm, and that a session op still routes
to the session applier.

## Acceptance gate

New test passes; `go test ./cmd/fak ./internal/fleetbus ./internal/sessionctl` green; publishing an
op token belonging to neither vocabulary still yields `FLEETBUS_UNKNOWN_OP` acked (not dropped);
the two op vocabularies are asserted disjoint by a test, not by convention.

## Dependencies

#5599 (epic parent). Independent of the session-applier durability fix, though both touch
`cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus.go` — coordinate on the lane lease.

## Confusion risks

- **A directive is never its own witness** (`internal/fleetbus` package doc). An ack that says
  "received" is the phantom this package exists to prevent; each op must report what it changed.
- **`STEER_NO_OWNED_LOOP` is the cautionary precedent.** `Server.ownsSessionLoop()` returns
  `s.native`, so a non-native serve refuses steer rather than returning a false `202`. A gateway op
  a process cannot honor must refuse the same way.
- **Do not fan `/v1/fak/*` blindly.** Twenty-three routes are not twenty-three fleet ops; pick the
  posture-shaped ones and leave read/debug routes alone.

`internal/fleetbus/fleetbus.go`, `internal/gateway/http.go`
