A fleet-bus lifecycle apply writes the in-memory session table and stops there.
`cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus.go` contains **no reference** to the durable path, the session registry, or
`leaseref` (verified: `git grep -n 'applySessionControlDurable\|leaseref\|Registry' -- cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus.go`
returns nothing). Its lifecycle arm calls `a.tbl.Transition(st.TraceID, run, reason)` directly
(`:171`) and its fan-out goes through `sessionctl.Broadcast(a.tbl, ...)` (`:149`).

The durable mirror — the thing that republishes `leaseref.SessionDescriptor` so a cross-host reader
sees the new state — fires only from `applySessionControlDurable`
(`cmd/fak/session_durable.go:233`), whose only caller is `cmd/fak/main_session_control.go:194`, the
**HTTP** session-control path.

So the same logical operation takes two different paths with two different durability outcomes:

| Path | In-memory table | Durable mirror / leaseref |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /v1/fak/session/...` → `applySessionControlDurable` | written | written |
| fleet bus directive → `fleetBusApplier` | written | **not written** |

After `fak fleet control send --op pause --all`, the bus's ack fold reports `applied` while
`GET /v1/sessions` and every `leaseref` reader still report the old state — and a serve restart
restores from the durable record, silently undoing the pause.

## Why this is next

This is the failure mode `internal/fleetbus` was built to prevent, arriving through the back door.
The package doc's invariant is *"a directive is never its own witness"* — the ack from the applier
is the proof. Here the ack is **truthful about the in-memory write and wrong about the outcome an
operator will observe**, which is worse than an unanswered directive: the fold shows a green
`applied=N outstanding=0` over state that any other reader contradicts.

## Working spine

The fleet-bus lifecycle arm routes through the same durable apply the HTTP path uses, so one
operation has one implementation. Where the applier currently calls `Transition` directly it calls
the durable helper; where it broadcasts, it broadcasts over the durable apply per matched session.
The ack's `Affected` count then reflects durably-applied sessions, not table writes.

## In scope

- Routing `fleetBusApplier`'s lifecycle path through `applySessionControlDurable` (or a shared
  helper factored out of it), including the broadcast/selector arm.
- Threading the durability mirror into the applier at construction (`serve_fleetbus.go:287`).
- Making the ack's `Affected` / `Witness` describe the durable outcome.
- A refusal for the case where durability is configured-off, so the ack says *applied in memory
  only* rather than plain `applied`.

## Out of scope

- Changing the durable format or the `leaseref` descriptor.
- The gateway-scoped op vocabulary (separate leaf).
- Making durability mandatory. `guardDurabilityWanted` stays opt-in; this issue makes the two paths
  agree under whatever it is set to.

## Done condition

With durability enabled, a `pause` delivered over the bus and a `pause` delivered over
`POST /v1/fak/session/...` leave identical observable state: same `session.Table` state, same
`GET /v1/sessions` response, same `leaseref` descriptor; and a serve restart after the bus pause
restores paused, not running.

## Witness

`go test ./cmd/fak -run 'TestFleetBusApplyReachesDurableMirror'` — applies one lifecycle op by each
path against the same durability mirror and asserts the two resulting states are equal, plus the
restart-restores-paused arm.

## Acceptance gate

New test passes; `go test ./cmd/fak` green including the existing fleetbus-applier and
session-control suites; with durability off, the ack explicitly reports the weaker outcome rather
than a bare `applied`.

## Dependencies

#5599 (epic parent). Touches the same file as the gateway-scoped-applier leaf — serialize on the
`cmd` lane lease.

## Confusion risks

- **The green fold is the bug.** Reading `applied=N outstanding=0` as evidence the fleet paused is
  exactly the mistake this fixes; the fold is faithfully reporting a write that did not reach the
  state everyone else reads.
- **Two apply paths must become one, not two-that-agree.** A parallel durable write bolted onto the
  applier will drift the moment either side changes.
- **`sessionctl.Broadcast` refuses a zero-session selector by design** (`serve_fleetbus.go:137-139`)
  — preserve that refusal when moving the arm to the durable path.

## Likely files

`cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus.go`, `cmd/fak/session_durable.go`, `cmd/fak/main_session_control.go`,
`internal/sessionctl/broadcast.go`, `internal/leaseref/`

```routing
lane: cmd
paths: cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus.go, cmd/fak/session_durable.go, cmd/fak/main_session_control.go
expected_steps: route the bus lifecycle arm through applySessionControlDurable; thread the mirror at construction; report the durable outcome in the ack; equality test across both paths
```

records.title: fix(sessionctl): nothing calls TagSession, so every lane/wave/label fleet selector matches zero sessions
records.body:
_Parent epic: #5632 — the gateway as the fleet's front door._

## Current state

`sessionctl` owns a process-global tag registry that broadcast selection resolves against, and
**nothing ever writes to it.** `git grep -n TagSession -- '*.go'` returns three lines, all in
`internal/sessionctl/broadcast.go`, and none of them is a call:

```
internal/sessionctl/broadcast.go:24:  // a process-global tag registry keyed by trace (TagSession / SessionTag / ...
internal/sessionctl/broadcast.go:73:  // TagSession records trace's routing metadata for broadcast selection. The spawn ...
internal/sessionctl/broadcast.go:77:  func TagSession(trace string, meta BroadcastMeta) {
```

Two comments and the definition. The package documents the fail-closed rule — an untagged session
matches no selector — and names the intended taggers (the dispatch worker launcher, the wave
driver). **Those callers do not exist.**

The consequence lands on the live control plane: `cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus.go:148` builds
`sessionctl.BroadcastSelector{Lane: d.Selector.Lane, Wave: d.Selector.Wave, Label: d.Selector.Label}`
straight from the fleet directive, so `--lane` / `--wave` / `--label` on a fleet directive resolve
against an always-empty registry and always match **zero** sessions. To an operator that is
indistinguishable from an empty fleet.

## Why this is next

Half the documented fleetbus selector grammar is inert. The instance axes (machine, role) work
because `fleetbus.Instance` carries those fields; the session axes silently do not, and they fail
in the most expensive direction — a `--lane` scoped `pause` reports success over zero sessions
while every targeted session keeps running. Fixing it is a call at the spawn site, not a design.

## Working spine

Every session admitted on a serve process is tagged at admission with whatever routing metadata is
already known at that point (lane, wave, label), so `BroadcastSelector` resolves against a
populated registry. The registry is also cleaned up when a session ends, so a long-lived process
does not accumulate tags for dead traces.

## In scope

- Calling `sessionctl.TagSession` at the session admission/spawn site with the metadata available
  there.
- Untagging (or expiring) on session end so the registry tracks live sessions.
- Making an all-zero-match scoped broadcast **visibly** distinct from a successful one — the
  operator must be able to tell "no session carried that lane" from "every session was steered".
- A test that fails if the tagger is removed again.

## Out of scope

- Extending the selector grammar with new axes.
- Tagging sessions created outside a serve process.
- The dispatch worker launcher / wave driver as *separate* taggers, if the admission site already
  covers the sessions a fleet directive can reach; note explicitly which spawn sites remain
  untagged rather than silently leaving them out.

## Done condition

A serve process holding sessions tagged `lane=alpha` and `lane=beta` applies a `--lane alpha`
scoped fleet directive to exactly the alpha sessions; the ack's `Affected` is non-zero and matches;
a directive naming a lane nobody carries reports a distinguishable zero-match outcome rather than
an indistinguishable `applied`.

## Witness

`go test ./internal/sessionctl -run 'TestBroadcastSelectorMatchesTaggedSessions'` plus
`go test ./cmd/fak -run 'TestFleetDirectiveLaneSelectorAffectsSessions'` — the second drives the
selector through the real applier path.

## Acceptance gate

Both tests pass; `go test ./internal/sessionctl ./cmd/fak` green; the fail-closed rule is preserved
(an untagged session still matches no selector) and asserted; the registry does not grow unbounded
across session churn (asserted by count after N create/destroy cycles).

## Dependencies

#5599 (epic parent). Independent of the durable-mirror fix, though both make fleet directives
actually do something — landing this one first makes that one's failure visible.

## Confusion risks

- **This is not a missing feature, it is a missing call.** The registry, the selector resolver and
  the fail-closed rule are all built and tested; only the producer is absent.
- **Zero-match must not read as success.** That is the whole operator-facing harm; changing the
  matcher without changing the reporting leaves the confusion in place.
- **Tag lifetime is part of the fix.** Tagging without untagging turns a correctness bug into a
  leak, and stale tags make a selector match a dead trace.

## Likely files

`internal/sessionctl/broadcast.go`, `cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus.go`, `cmd/fak/serve_stages.go`,
`internal/session/`

```routing
lane: sessionctl
paths: internal/sessionctl/**
expected_steps: call TagSession at admission; untag on end; make zero-match distinguishable; tests at both layers
```

records.title: feat(serve): publish the live gateway URL and read-scoped bearer into the guardsessions discovery index
records.body:
_Parent epic: #5632 — the gateway as the fleet's front door._

## Current state

fak has a gateway-URL discovery index (#5400) and the long-lived, network-facing front door does
not publish into it. `publishGuardSessionGateway(url, bearer)` —
`cmd/fak/guard_sessions.go:106`, described at `:95` as *"the PRODUCER half of gateway discovery
(#5400)"* — has exactly one caller:

```
cmd/fak/guard.go:1038:  if _, perrs := publishGuardSessionGateway(gwURL, guardReadBearer); ...
```

**No serve file references the `guardsessions` package at all**
(`git grep -ln guardsessions -- 'cmd/fak/serve*.go'` returns nothing).

So `fak guard` — a session-scoped process — leaves a discoverable address, and `fak serve` — the
process whose entire purpose is to be dialed — leaves none. Its address must be handed out of band
every time, by a human, into every client and every dashboard.

The credential machinery this needs already exists on the guard path: a read-scoped bearer of 128
bits from `crypto/rand`, minted per launch and accepted only on `/healthz`, `/debug/vars` and
`/metrics`.

## Why this is next

Everything else in the fleet epic assumes a control point can *reach* a gateway. The fleet-status
aggregate (#4231), any external dashboard, and the fleet bus's `Instance.Addr` all presuppose an
address that arrived from somewhere. Today that somewhere is a person. The producer, the index and
the read-scoped bearer are all built; this is the call site.

## Working spine

At serve startup, once the listener has a concrete address, mint a read-scoped bearer with the same
generator the guard path uses and publish `(url, bearer)` through the existing
`publishGuardSessionGateway` producer. On shutdown, retract or let the record expire, so a stale
address does not outlive the process.

## In scope

- Publishing the live gateway URL + read-scoped bearer from `fak serve`, reusing the guard path's
  producer and bearer minting rather than duplicating either.
- Resolving the URL from the **bound listener** (including an ephemeral `:0` port), not from the
  requested flag value.
- Retraction or expiry on shutdown, and a non-fatal failure mode: a publish error must warn, never
  prevent the gateway from serving.
- Honoring whatever opt-out the guard path already honors, at the same granularity.

## Out of scope

- Any new authorization scope. The read-scoped bearer keeps exactly its current three-route
  allowance.
- A new discovery mechanism, registry or protocol. This uses #5400's index as-is.
- The A2A agent card's endpoint (a separate leaf) — different surface, same underlying
  "we do not know our own address" problem.
- Cross-host propagation of the index.

## Done condition

A `fak serve` bound to an ephemeral port publishes a record whose URL dials **that** listener and
whose bearer is accepted on `/healthz`; the record disappears (or is marked expired) after the
process exits; a publish failure logs a warning and the gateway still serves.

## Witness

`go test ./cmd/fak -run 'TestServePublishesGatewayDiscovery'` — starts a serve on `:0`, reads the
published record, dials the URL, and asserts the bearer is accepted on `/healthz` and rejected on a
non-exempt route.

## Acceptance gate

New test passes; `go test ./cmd/fak` green; the published URL is derived from the bound address
(asserted with `:0`, which is where a flag-derived URL fails); no write-scoped credential is
published (asserted by inspecting the record).

## Dependencies

#5400 (the discovery seam and its producer) — already landed; this is its second producer.

## Confusion risks

- **`/healthz` is always auth-exempt** (`internal/gateway/http.go:403-411`), so a test that only
  checks `/healthz` proves nothing about the bearer. Assert the rejection arm too.
- **Do not publish the flag value.** `--addr :0`, `--addr 0.0.0.0:8080` and a hostname all need the
  resolved, dialable form; publishing the request is how the record becomes confidently wrong.
- **A stale record is worse than none.** Retraction or expiry is part of this issue, not a
  follow-on.

## Likely files

`cmd/fak/serve.go`, `cmd/fak/serve_stages.go`, `cmd/fak/guard_sessions.go`,
`internal/guardsessions/`

```routing
lane: cmd
paths: cmd/fak/serve.go, cmd/fak/serve_stages.go, cmd/fak/guard_sessions.go
expected_steps: mint read-scoped bearer at serve boot; resolve URL from the bound listener; publish via publishGuardSessionGateway; retract on shutdown; test with :0
```

records.title: fix(gateway): serve the A2A agent card with this process's real endpoint instead of the hardcoded fleet.example.com
records.body:
_Parent epic: #5632 — the gateway as the fleet's front door._

## Current state

The A2A agent card — the one card-shaped discovery surface fak serves — is a literal that points
peers at `example.com`:

```
internal/gateway/a2a.go:370:  AgentCardURL: "https://fleet.example.com/a2a/agent-card"
internal/gateway/a2a.go:726:  ID:          "fleet-fak"
internal/gateway/a2a.go:730:  Endpoint:    "https://fleet.example.com/a2a"
```

Nothing in `a2a.go` reads the listener address. The card is served on a live route
(`/a2a/v1/agent-card`, one of the four A2A patterns in `Server.routeTable()`,
`internal/gateway/http.go:51-167`), so a peer that fetches it and dials what it says never reaches
the gateway that served it — and the identity fields are a fixed `fleet-fak` / `Fleet fak Agent`
regardless of which process answered.

This is worse than an absent surface: a schema demo served on a production route looks like a
working descriptor, and the failure appears at the peer as a DNS or connection error attributed to
the peer's own configuration.

## Why this is next

A card is a *contract about where to send the next request*. Fixing it is small and bounded, and it
is a precondition for the card ever carrying anything else worth declaring — skills, supported
wires, or (once the roster reaches the wire) the models this gateway actually fronts. Declaring
capabilities from an endpoint nobody can dial is not worth building.

## Working spine

The card is constructed per request from the serving process: the endpoint and card URL are derived
from the bound listener and the incoming request's host, and the identity fields reflect the
configured engine/instance rather than a fixed literal. No `example.com` string survives in a
served response.

## In scope

- Deriving `Endpoint` and `AgentCardURL` from the actual listener/request rather than literals,
  including the ephemeral-port case.
- Identity fields (`ID`, `Name`) reflecting the configured engine id / instance identity, with the
  current values as the fallback when nothing is configured.
- A test that fails if a placeholder host reappears in any served response.

## Out of scope

- Extending the card's declared skills or capabilities.
- Advertising models on the card — that depends on the roster reaching the chat wire and is a
  separate leaf.
- Any change to the A2A task/message routes themselves.
- TLS scheme inference beyond what the request already tells us; a reverse-proxy override may be
  needed and, if so, should be a stated follow-on rather than guessed at here.

## Done condition

A gateway bound to an ephemeral port serves an agent card whose `Endpoint` resolves to that same
listener — verified by dialing it from the test and receiving the A2A route, not a DNS failure —
whose `ID`/`Name` reflect the configured engine/instance, and in which no `example.com` string
appears.

## Witness

`go test ./internal/gateway -run 'TestA2AAgentCardEndpointIsLive'` — serves on `:0`, fetches the
card, dials the advertised endpoint, and scans the full serialized response for placeholder hosts.

## Acceptance gate

New test passes; `go test ./internal/gateway` green; `TestOpenAPISpecDocumentsEveryServedRoute`
still green; a repo-wide grep shows no `fleet.example.com` reachable from a served response path
(fixtures and docs may keep it).

## Dependencies

None. Shares a root cause with the serve-discovery leaf (the process does not know its own dialable
address) and the two can share a helper.

## Confusion risks

- **Behind a reverse proxy the bound address is not the public one.** Prefer the request's
  `Host`/forwarded headers where available and say in the code which source wins; do not silently
  advertise an internal address.
- **`example.com` is reserved for documentation** — it will always resolve to something and never
  to fak, which is why this fails as a confusing timeout rather than a clean error.
- **The card is served, not just defined.** A fix that only changes the struct default while a
  handler rebuilds the literal leaves the bug live.

## Likely files

`internal/gateway/a2a.go`, `internal/gateway/http.go`, `internal/gateway/gateway.go`

```routing
lane: gateway
paths: internal/gateway/a2a.go
expected_steps: derive Endpoint/AgentCardURL from listener+request; identity from configured engine/instance; assert no placeholder host in any served response
```

records.title: feat(polymodel): put the poly-model lane on the live serve path — construct a Pool so one process hosts many models and decodes one
records.body:
_Parent epic: #5632 — the gateway as the fleet's front door._

## Current state

fak's answer to "host many models on one kernel" is built, proven and unreachable from the serving
front door. `internal/polymodel` documents itself as *"hosting many models on one kernel and
serializing decode to one lane — the 'host 10s of models, share the prefill, decode one'
design"*. `internal/residency` binds a `polymodel.Pool` to real weight handles, and its own header
says it reaches a live request path *"only when a future rung"* lands.
`modelroute.Plan.BridgeToPolymodel(pool *polymodel.Pool)` (`internal/modelroute/polybridge.go`)
exists with `BridgeToPolymodelEnabled` and `PickPolyDrafter`.

The serve path never meets any of it:

- **No file under `internal/gateway` imports `internal/polymodel`** (only a testdata JSON mentions
  the name). Importers are `internal/model/*`, `internal/residency`,
  `internal/modelroute/polybridge.go` and `cmd/polymodelbench`.
- **Nothing constructs a `polymodel.Pool` on a serve process.** `polymodel.Enabled()` reads
  `FlagEnv = "FAK_POLYMODEL"`, defaults **off**, and is deliberately kept out of defconfig.
- `gateway.selectChatPlanner` (`internal/gateway/gateway.go:2049-2125`) has exactly four boot-time
  modes — dual / proxy-only / in-kernel-only / mock — so one process fronts **one** in-kernel model,
  plus at most one more via `DualPlanner`'s binary local-alias test.

The plan doc agrees this rung is open: `docs/serving/polymodel-prefill-share-plan.md:218` still
marks **"Multi-model weight residency / whole-model eviction ON a backend — [GAP]"**, while epic
**#529 and its children #530–#535 are all CLOSED** — the epic closed on the proven, offline layer,
not on the live path.

## Why this is next

The gateway epic's other children make one process able to *front* several models by routing to
several upstreams. This is the other half: making one process able to *host* several models
locally. It is the difference between fak-as-a-proxy and fak-as-a-multi-model-server, and every
piece except the constructor and the request-path hook is landed and unit-tested.

## Working spine

Behind the existing `FAK_POLYMODEL` flag (default off, unchanged), a serve process configured with
more than one local model constructs a `polymodel.Pool`, registers each model's weights through
`internal/residency`, and resolves the request's model id to a pool member — decoding on the single
serialized lane the design specifies. With the flag off, `selectChatPlanner`'s four modes behave
exactly as they do at HEAD.

## In scope

- A `polymodel.Pool` constructed on the serve path when the flag is on and more than one local
  model is configured.
- A fifth planner arm in `selectChatPlanner` (or an equivalent seam) that resolves `req.Model` to a
  pool member, using the existing bridge (`Plan.BridgeToPolymodel`) rather than a new resolver.
- The configuration surface for declaring more than one local model to `fak serve`.
- Refusal for a request naming a model the pool does not hold, with a closed reason — never a
  silent fallback to a different model's weights.

## Out of scope

- **MoE expert residency (#5606 and its rungs).** That is residency *within* one model's expert
  set; this is whole-model residency across several models. The two must not be conflated — cite
  the distinction in the code comment.
- Whole-model eviction policy under memory pressure. This rung lands hosting; eviction is the
  follow-on the plan doc's `[GAP]` row also names.
- Turning `FAK_POLYMODEL` on by default, or adding it to defconfig.
- Prefill/decode disaggregation across machines (#4302).

## Done condition

With `FAK_POLYMODEL=1` and two local models configured, one `fak serve` process answers requests
naming either model from one pool, with decode serialized as the design specifies; a request naming
an unheld model is refused with a closed reason; with the flag unset, every existing serve
configuration behaves byte-for-byte as at HEAD.

## Witness

`go test ./internal/gateway -run 'TestServePolymodelPoolRoutesByModelID'` — two small local models,
asserting per-request member selection, the serialized decode lane, the typed refusal for an unheld
id, and the flag-off compatibility arm.

## Acceptance gate

New test passes; `go test ./internal/gateway ./internal/polymodel ./internal/residency` green;
with the flag unset, `selectChatPlanner`'s existing four modes are asserted unchanged; no new
default-on behavior.

## Dependencies

None blocking — the pool, the residency binding and the bridge are all landed. Pairs with the
`GET /v1/models` catalog leaf, which is how a client would discover a locally hosted set.

## Confusion risks

- **#529 is closed and this is not a re-file.** The epic closed on the proven layer; the plan doc's
  line 218 `[GAP]` row is the open part, and no open issue covers it.
- **"Multi-model" means two different things in this tree.** Fronting N upstreams (the roster
  children) and hosting N local models (this) are separate mechanisms with separate failure modes.
- **`polymodel` is deliberately out of defconfig.** Landing this must not change that; the flag
  stays the gate.
- **Decode is serialized on purpose.** A change that parallelizes decode to make a benchmark look
  better is a different design, not this one.

## Likely files

`internal/gateway/gateway.go`, `internal/polymodel/polymodel.go`, `internal/residency/`,
`internal/modelroute/polybridge.go`, `cmd/fak/serve.go`,
`docs/serving/polymodel-prefill-share-plan.md`

```routing
lane: polymodel
paths: internal/polymodel/**, internal/residency/**
expected_steps: construct a Pool on serve behind FAK_POLYMODEL; resolve req.Model to a pool member via BridgeToPolymodel; typed refusal for an unheld id; flag-off compatibility test
```

records.title: fix(gateway): a --native served turn's in-loop tool calls skip the account roster — WithRouteAccounts has zero non-test callers
records.body:
_Parent epic: #5632 — the gateway as the fleet's front door._

## Current state

`internal/agent` has a run option for wiring the model-account roster into an agent loop, and
nothing in production passes it. `git grep -n WithRouteAccounts -- '*.go' | grep -v _test` returns
three lines, all in `internal/agent/loop_session.go` — the doc comment (`:259`), the definition
(`:271`), and a second comment (`:319`) — and **no call site**.

The option's own documentation (`loop_session.go:319-336`) says it resolves a plan member through
the roster to the account-bound `Target.EngineRoute()` and that it *"mirrors the gateway's
`resolveRoute` exactly"*. The mirror is never hung: `internal/gateway/native_serve.go` and
`cmd/fak/main.go` build their agent loops with `WithRouteManifest` only.

**Consequence:** under `fak serve --native`, the served turn runs an in-process agent loop, and that
loop's tool calls resolve their engine through the manifest while the proxying path resolves the
same call through the roster (`internal/gateway/tool_routing.go:194,369` → `resolveRoute` →
`Target.EngineRoute()`). Two serving modes, two different route resolutions for the same tool call,
and the divergence is silent — the native path simply never sees the account binding, so a
residency PDP adjudicating a native turn sees a manifest route where the proxy path would have
shown it an account-resolved one.

## Why this is next

`--native` is the mode that owns its agent loop (`Server.ownsSessionLoop()` returns `s.native`, the
same bit that decides whether a steer is honored), so it is the mode where a roster binding matters
most and is absent. The fix is one option passed at loop construction; the cost of leaving it is a
route-resolution divergence between two modes of the same binary that no test currently forbids.

## Working spine

Every place that builds an agent loop inside a serve process passes `WithRouteAccounts(s.roster)`
alongside the existing `WithRouteManifest`, so the in-loop resolution order matches the proxy
path's. A test asserts the two paths agree on the resolved route for the same tool call and roster.

## In scope

- Passing `WithRouteAccounts` at the native-serve and `cmd/fak/main.go` loop-construction sites.
- A divergence test: one roster, one tool call, resolved through both the proxy path and the native
  loop, asserting the same engine route.
- Reconciling precedence when both a manifest and a roster are wired, and writing that precedence
  down where both options are documented.

## Out of scope

- Chat-path model routing through the roster — that is #5633, a different resolution and a
  different wire.
- Registering roster-derived engine ids so `EngineRoute()` reaches a driver. That is a real
  follow-on (all 13 non-test `RegisterEngine` sites use literal ids) and its own leaf.
- Any change to the manifest path's behavior when no roster is configured.

## Done condition

With a roster configured, a tool call served through `fak serve --native` resolves to the same
engine route the proxying path resolves it to; with no roster configured, both paths behave exactly
as they do at HEAD.

## Witness

`go test ./internal/gateway -run 'TestNativeLoopResolvesRouteLikeProxyPath'` — one roster, one tool
call, both paths, asserting equal resolved routes plus the no-roster compatibility arm.

## Acceptance gate

New test passes; `go test ./internal/gateway ./internal/agent ./cmd/fak` green; the precedence rule
between manifest and roster is asserted by a test rather than only documented.

## Dependencies

None blocking. Independent of #5633, though both make the roster load-bearing and should agree on
precedence.

## Confusion risks

- **`WithRouteManifest` and `WithRouteAccounts` are not alternatives.** The manifest routes to
  declared engines; the roster binds a model id to an account. Passing one is not passing the other,
  which is precisely how this went unnoticed.
- **The divergence is silent.** Nothing errors today — the native loop just resolves differently.
  A fix without the equality test leaves the next caller free to drop the option again.
- **`EngineRoute()` is an adjudication token, not a dial.** Landing this makes the native path's
  adjudication honest; it does not make either path dial the roster's `BaseURL`.

## Parent context

**#5632** — the gateway-as-fleet-front-door epic. Sibling of #5633 (the chat-wire half); this is
the native-loop tool-call half.

## Work unit

leaf

## Work scale

S1

## Expected steps

4

## Trigger

Filed from the #5632 research pass (2026-08-05); surfaced while verifying #5633's roster claims and
confirmed first-hand — `WithRouteAccounts` has zero non-test callers at HEAD.

## Batch policy

One leaf per gap. The `RegisterEngine` follow-on named in **Out of scope** is the only expected
successor and is not filed yet.

## Closure binding

Closes on a commit stamped `(fak gateway)` passing `WithRouteAccounts` at the serve loop-construction
sites, with `TestNativeLoopResolvesRouteLikeProxyPath` green.

- **Required model tier:** T1
- **Optimal model tier:** T2

## Likely files

`internal/gateway/native_serve.go`, `cmd/fak/main.go`, `internal/agent/loop_session.go`,
`internal/gateway/tool_routing.go`

```routing
lane: gateway
paths: internal/gateway/native_serve.go, internal/agent/loop_session.go
expected_steps: pass WithRouteAccounts at both loop-construction sites; settle manifest-vs-roster precedence; equality test across proxy and native paths
```

records.body:
## Parent context
#4636

## Summary

Add a repository closeout verifier that derives secondary obligations from a commit range and the current candidate paths instead of trusting an agent checklist.

fak already has specialized checks for documentation placement, generated indexes, release state, and witnessed completion. The missing layer is one bounded report that maps the actual change set to the follow-up artifacts it owes and returns repairable machine states.

## Scope

- Accept a commit range and, optionally, selected dirty paths.
- Drive obligation discovery from a declarative change-kind-to-artifact map.
- Emit one row per obligation with a closed state such as `paid`, `unpaid`, `unproven`, `no_candidates`, or `inherited`.
- Include candidate and checked counts so an empty range or empty selector cannot look clean.
- Render bounded repair missions without letting worker narration set the final verdict.
- Keep any lifecycle-hook adapter advisory and bounded; the verifier must be rerun after repairs.

## Done conditions

- Invalid or unreadable ranges return a typed could-not-run result.
- Generated-index, documentation, release, and tracker obligations can be registered without hard-coding them into the renderer.
- JSON and human output describe the same obligation rows and counts.
- A repair run cannot mark itself complete; only a fresh readback of the repository range can close the row.
- Synthetic fixtures cover paid, unpaid, inherited, empty-domain, and checker-unavailable cases.

## Proof requirement

Land a failing-first fixture where a primary change omits one declared secondary artifact, show the verifier naming the exact unpaid row, apply the repair, and independently rerun the verifier to a paid result. Include a second fixture proving an empty or invalid range cannot return an ordinary pass.

## Non-goals

This issue does not prescribe a release process or require every repository to enable the same obligation classes.

records.body:
## Parent context
#2503

## Summary

Make repeat-alert suppression conditional on a successfully persisted deduplication receipt. A best-effort write must not be followed by a suppression decision that assumes the receipt exists.

One current operator-page path updates its dedup store best-effort and ignores the write result before deciding whether a standing condition should be re-notified. A storage failure can therefore create a split state: the current process suppresses repeats even though no durable receipt proves the notification state.

## Scope

- Return a typed persistence result from the alert/page dedup store.
- Suppress a repeat only when the prior receipt was read successfully and the refreshed receipt was durably written.
- On persistence failure, emit a visible degraded state and choose a bounded retry or re-notification policy.
- Preserve occurrence count, first seen, last seen, signature, and delivery outcome separately.
- Apply the contract to at least one existing page or alert path.

- A planted write failure cannot return an ordinary `suppressed` result.
- A successfully persisted first notification suppresses later repeats for the same signature.
- A corrupt or unreadable dedup store produces a typed degraded result rather than an empty clean store.
- Concurrent refreshes do not lose the occurrence count or create duplicate first notifications.
- Delivery failure and receipt-persistence failure remain distinct.

records.title: feat(analytics): make fleet comparisons cluster-aware and declare the analysis unit
records.body:
## Parent context

Part of #2822.

## Problem

When operational observations are nested inside waves whose sizes differ substantially, a pooled worker statistic and an equally weighted statistic over waves answer different questions. Treating every worker as independent understates shared wave-level variation; giving every wave equal influence can overrepresent very small cohorts. Any claimed orchestration effect should therefore declare its analysis unit and expose sensitivity to cluster weighting.

Fak’s fleet, trajectory, evaluation, and self-improvement analytics may compare repeated batches of agent runs. Without cluster-aware inference, the same evidence can produce different conclusions depending on whether it is reduced by worker, wave, or spend. It can also acquire false confidence by treating workers exposed to the same wave conditions as independent repetitions.

## Proposed contract

Make this distinction explicit at the project boundary, preserve the inputs needed to audit it, and fail closed when the distinction cannot be established.

## Done when

1. Every comparative fleet report declares the observational unit, clustering key, treatment-assignment unit, and weighting rule.
2. Reports retain each cluster’s eligible population and metric denominator.
3. When cluster sizes are unequal, emit both a cluster-weighted estimate and an exposure-weighted estimate.
4. Return a typed `AGGREGATION_SENSITIVE` or equivalent verdict when the estimates differ enough to change the conclusion.
5. Confidence or uncertainty calculations resample or model whole clusters rather than assuming all nested workers are independent.
6. Predeclare minimum eligible cluster count and minimum within-cluster support; undersupported comparisons remain unmeasured.
7. Add a synthetic fixture with unequal cluster sizes where a naive pooled result, an unweighted cluster result, and a cluster-aware result disagree.
8. Add a control with balanced clusters where the supported reductions reconcile.

- A committed known-positive fixture proves the signal can succeed.

## Parent context

Part of #1063.

## Problem

Before interpreting a score as system quality, establish that the measurement instrument could resolve the required threshold for the evaluated population. A population may be measurable, wholly below the instrument ceiling, mixed across that ceiling, or unmeasured; those states must not collapse into one scalar. records.title: fix(effects): bind preflight, mutation, and rollback to one subject-set receipt
records.body:
## Parent context

Part of #4509.

## Problem

A state-changing operation must apply to exactly the resources whose prior state it observed. Forward actions and compensating rollback must consume the same immutable subject-set receipt; otherwise a scoped observation can authorize an unscoped change to resources the operation never examined. Benchmark harnesses that temporarily alter environmental or runtime state should behave transactionally: capture the initial state, apply the requested changes, and restore and verify the original state after every outcome. A benchmark is not complete when measurements finish; failed restoration must produce an explicit non-success verdict. A temporary mutation is not safely complete when the primary operation succeeds. Its receipt should separately prove the precondition, requested change, observed effective state, compensation attempt, and observed restored state. Restoration should use a semantic equivalence rule because dynamic fields need not return byte-for-byte to their earlier values.

Fak coordinates scoped workers, leases, worktrees, file sets, and cleanup actions. Scope widening between preflight and effect could mutate or restore unrelated subjects using assumptions derived from the selected subject alone. Sequential benchmark and self-improvement arms can contaminate one another when run-scoped settings leak. A restoration receipt would make later comparisons depend on verified clean state rather than cleanup convention. Tool and agent workflows can temporarily acquire leases, alter execution settings, or stage reversible configuration. Primary success must not conceal an ineffective mutation or failed cleanup.

## Proposed contract

Make this distinction explicit at the project boundary, preserve the inputs needed to audit it, and fail closed when the distinction cannot be established.

## Done when

1. - Represent pre-state capture, mutation, measurement, restoration, and post-state verification as distinct managed stages.
2. - Attempt restoration after success, measurement failure, and cancellation.
3. - Emit a typed restoration receipt without sensitive environmental values.
4. - Return a non-success result when restoration or its verification fails.
5. - Refuse a subsequent arm when the preceding arm left relevant state unknown or changed.
6. - Add a synthetic adapter proving successful restoration, benchmark-failure restoration, cancellation restoration, cleanup failure, and preservation of unrelated ambient state.
7. - Define typed stages for `BEFORE`, `REQUESTED`, `EFFECTIVE`, `RESTORE_ATTEMPTED`, and `RESTORED`.
8. - Bind all stages to the same opaque subject receipt without publishing its identity.
9. - Distinguish request acceptance from independently observed effect.
10. - Declare which fields require exact restoration and which use semantic equivalence.
11. - Run compensation after success, refusal, error, and cancellation.
12. - Make ineffective application, failed restoration, and unreadable post-state first-class outcomes that cannot be hidden by primary success.
13. - Add fixtures that fail immediately after application and during restoration.
14. - Require an independent post-action readback before emitting `RESTORED`.

records.title: feat(eval): distinguish uncalibrated, sample-bound, and signal-limited evidence
records.body:
## Parent context

Part of #1063.

## Problem

Evaluation should use an evidence-state machine rather than treating a raw success rate as sufficient. An apparently perfect result without counterexamples is still uncalibrated. Adding counterexamples may lower the rate while improving the validity of the evidence. Once calibrated, an equivalent decline can legitimately be treated as regression. The ruling should also distinguish cases where more samples could establish the target from cases where the current signal cannot reach it regardless of sample count.

Judge, selector, guard, and self-improvement evaluations can otherwise reward blind calibration sets or repeatedly spend evaluation budget on a mechanism whose observed rate cannot meet its required bar.

## Proposed contract

Make this distinction explicit at the project boundary, preserve the inputs needed to audit it, and fail closed when the distinction cannot be established.

## Done when

1. - Represent not-measured, no-counterexample, finite-sample-limited, signal-limited, and certified states explicitly.
2. - Bind each ruling to its calibration coverage, observed counts, target, and confidence support.
3. - Produce a finite additional-sample requirement only when certification remains mathematically reachable; otherwise return an explicit mechanism-change action.
4. - Treat acquisition of the first counterexamples as evidence progress even if the raw metric falls.
5. - Continue to name the metric decline, but gate it only when the baseline was already calibrated.
6. - Gate loss of counterexample coverage rather than allowing a return to an apparently perfect but blind state.

records.body:
## Parent context

Part of #4509.

## Problem

A subprocess can exit successfully while reporting that inputs were only partially applied, state was initialized unexpectedly, or a requested behavior was disabled. Those messages are evidence about result validity, not incidental console decoration.

Fak wraps tools and evaluates their outputs. Treating exit success as semantic success can admit a degraded or non-comparable result while the only contrary evidence remains buried in a private log.

## Proposed contract

Make this distinction explicit at the project boundary, preserve the inputs needed to audit it, and fail closed when the distinction cannot be established.

## Done when

1. - Define versioned diagnostic classes such as advisory, compatibility drift, partial application, validity-blocking, and unknown.
2. - Each adapter records diagnostic class, source stage, count, policy version, and a digest of the retained raw transcript.
3. - A validity-blocking diagnostic prevents a clean result even when the child exits successfully.

Part of #4509.

## Problem

A managed runner should not hand an existing evidence directory to a child that may clear or replace prior outputs at startup. Fresh execution, same-run resume, and deliberate replacement are different operations and require different authority.

records.title: fix(dgxbridge): every lab GPU control session accepts verbs but completes no command (hub-side wedge)
records.body:
## Problem

Every control session on the lab GPU box accepts control verbs but **completes no command**. The box is up and the hub is answering — this is not a credential or connectivity failure, and it is not the "no session running" case the doctor's hint describes.

Reproduced 2026-08-06, from a Windows dev host, with a `dgxbridge` binary built from the current private source.

### What works

| Rung | Result |
|---|---|
| `slack_token` | resolved |
| `control_channel` | resolved |
| `channel_live` | reachable |
| `sessions` | answers — 4 live, 6 total |
| `status` | answers, returns the box banner |
| `new persistent` / `new shell` | both create a session that registers `RUNNING` |
| `!tail <id>` | answers with a real transcript |

The transcript shows the box at a live root shell prompt, timestamped minutes before the probe. The machine is healthy.

### What fails

```
$ dgxbridge -session-id persistent-5 run 'nvidia-smi --query-gpu=... --format=csv,noheader'
dgxbridge: run(to-file): exec(tail): dgxbridge: completion sentinel not found in this
thread's transcript (read 4 tail replies for this session; none carried the sentinel)

$ dgxbridge -session-id persistent-5 -transcript run 'nvidia-smi -L'
dgxbridge: dgxbridge: HUB_UNRESPONSIVE: hub_timeout: exec(tail): context deadline exceeded

$ dgxbridge -session-id persistent-5 selftest
readback BROKEN: sentinel_missing — the shell isn't echoing commands
```

### What rules out the documented causes

`selftest` attributes `sentinel_missing` to "usually a stale dgxbridge client or a shell parked at a `>` continuation prompt, NOT a dead hub". Neither holds here:

- **Not a stale client** — the binary was built fresh from the current private `cmd/` + `internal/` sources during this session.
- **Not a continuation prompt** — the transcript shows a normal `#` prompt, not `>`.
- **Not tmux redraw noise** — it reproduces identically on a freshly created `shell` profile session (mode=pty), not just `persistent`/tmux.
- **Not a stale session** — it reproduces on sessions created seconds earlier, as well as on three pre-existing ones (two of which have been `running` for ~1d21h).
- **Not cleared by the recovery ladder** — `!interrupt <id>` then `!reset <id>` restarted the pane process (`process_restart`, new pid appears in the transcript) and the shell still did not echo. After the reset the transcript stops advancing entirely: commands posted afterwards via `!send` never appear in it.

So the fault is between the hub's stdin injection / transcript capture and the shell, and it affects **every** session including brand-new ones in both profiles.

## Impact

The GPU box is unusable through the only path that reaches it (there is no inbound SSH). Every hardware-gated deliverable is blocked behind this — for example #4952's remaining definition-of-done (CUDA+NCCL build, 8-rank `LOAD_READY`, per-rank resident memory, streaming + non-streaming capture) and the real-hardware half of #5627's async-upload overlap measurement.

## What is needed

The documented last resort is a **hub restart**, which I deliberately did not attempt: it is an operator action on the lab box, and there are 4 live sessions on it belonging to other users. That call is not mine to make unilaterally.

Suggested next steps for whoever owns the box:

1. Inspect the hub process (`slack-control`) and its per-session bridges on the box directly.
2. Check whether the session transcript writer (`/var/lib/slack-control/sessions/<id>/transcript.jsonl`) is still being appended after a `!send` — it stopped advancing here immediately after a `!reset`.
3. Restart the hub if nothing lighter clears it, then confirm with `dgxbridge -probe doctor` and `dgxbridge selftest` (which should print `readback OK`).

## Worth fixing separately

`fak nightrun caps` reports `creds=none` on this host, which is wrong and actively misleading — it sent me down a credential-hunting path when the credentials resolve fine. The Slack bot token is already in the environment; the control channel id simply is not in any `.env`, and the bridge needs `FAK_SLACK_CHANNEL` set for `doctor` to reach READY. A capability probe that reports `creds=none` when the real state is "credentials resolve, control session wedged" points at the wrong fix.

Happy to file that as its own leaf if it is not folded in here.

records.title: fix(gateway): a --native turn's manifest routing ignores Subject.Labels, so a label-matching rule diverges from the proxy path
records.body:
_Parent epic: #5632 — the gateway as the fleet's front door. Sibling of #5644._

## Current state

#5644 closed the ROSTER half of the native/proxy route divergence: a `serve --native` turn now
resolves a tool call's engine through the same manifest→roster→principal chain the proxying path
uses. A second, independent divergence in the same resolution survives it — the **manifest
classification** itself.

The gateway classifies a tool call with labels:

```go
// internal/gateway/tool_routing.go: routeDecision
s.route.Route(modelroute.Subject{
    Aspect: modelroute.AspectToolCall,
    Tool:   tool,
    Labels: routeLabels(readOnly, meta),   // read_only, sensitivity, tenant
})
```

The in-process agent loop classifies the same call with **no labels at all**:

```go
// internal/agent/loop_session.go: routeToolEngine
d := c.route.Route(modelroute.Subject{Aspect: modelroute.AspectToolCall, Tool: tool})
```

**Consequence:** a manifest whose `Match` keys on `read_only`, `sensitivity`, or `tenant` routes
one way on the proxy path and another way in the owned loop, for the same tool call. A rule like
"route sensitive payloads to the local account" is honored when proxying and silently ignored
under `--native`. As with #5644 the divergence is silent — nothing errors, the loop just picks a
different plan.

## Why this is next

It is the remaining half of the same defect class #5644 fixed, on the same seam, and it is the
half that touches the residency floor most directly: `sensitivity` is exactly the label an
operator would route on to keep a tenant payload off a remote account.

`internal/gateway/native_route_parity_test.go` (landed with #5644) states this exclusion in its
header and deliberately uses tool-only manifests so its witness does not over-claim.

## Working spine

The agent loop grows the same label surface the gateway already computes, and the #5644 parity
test is extended with a label-matching manifest arm that fails before the change.

## In scope

- Carrying the call's `read_only` / `sensitivity` / `tenant` signals into the agent loop's
  routing `Subject.Labels`.
- Extending `internal/gateway/native_route_parity_test.go` with a label-matching manifest arm
  asserting both paths pick the same plan.

## Out of scope

- Any change to the roster/principal resolution #5644 landed.
- New label KINDS beyond the three `routeLabels` already lowers (that is #599 signal enrichment).

## Done condition

With a manifest whose rules match on `read_only` / `sensitivity` / `tenant`, a tool call served
through `fak serve --native` selects the same plan the proxying path selects; a tool-only
manifest behaves exactly as it does at HEAD.

## Witness

`go test ./internal/gateway -run TestNativeLoopRouteParityLabelMatchedManifest` — one
label-matching manifest, one tool call, both paths, same plan; plus the existing tool-only arms
staying green.

## Acceptance gate

New label arm passes; `go test ./internal/gateway ./internal/agent` green (modulo failures
already red on the trunk); the tool-only arms of the #5644 parity test unchanged.

## Dependencies

None blocking. #5644 has landed (14e5095ad447).

## Confusion risks

- **This is NOT the roster divergence.** #5644 fixed which ACCOUNT a routed id binds to. This is
  which ROUTED ID the manifest picks in the first place — an earlier stage of the same chain.
- **The loop does not have `meta` the way the gateway does.** The gateway derives labels from the
  ToolCall meta it built; the loop classifies before building one, so the signals have to be
  derived at the loop's own call site rather than read off an existing map.

## Parent context

**#5632** — the gateway-as-fleet-front-door epic. Direct successor of #5644, which closed the
roster half of this divergence and named this half as out of frame.

## Work unit

leaf

## Work scale

S1

## Expected steps

3

## Trigger

Found while landing #5644 (2026-08-06): writing the native/proxy parity test required pinning the
manifests to tool-only matching, because a label-matching manifest diverges for a reason #5644
does not fix.

## Batch policy

One leaf per gap.

## Closure binding

Closes on a commit stamped `(fak gateway)` carrying the call's routing labels into the agent
loop's Subject, with a label-matched parity arm green.

- **Required model tier:** T1
- **Optimal model tier:** T2

## Likely files

`internal/agent/loop_session.go`, `internal/gateway/native_route_parity_test.go`,
`internal/gateway/tool_routing.go`

```routing
lane: gateway
paths: internal/agent/loop_session.go, internal/gateway/native_route_parity_test.go
expected_steps: lower the call's read_only/sensitivity/tenant signals into the loop's routing Subject; extend the parity test with a label-matching arm; keep the tool-only arms byte-identical
```

### Related

#5632, #5644, #599, #5332

records.title: fix(gateway): a --native turn's in-loop tool calls are not vDSO principal-scoped, so one tenant can be served another's cached read
records.body:
_Parent epic: #5632 — the gateway as the fleet's front door. Found while landing #5644._

## Current state

The gateway's proxy path lowers the request's tenant ISOLATION principal onto every tool call, so
the vDSO scopes its tier-2 cache entry PER PRINCIPAL:

```go
// internal/gateway/tool_routing.go: buildCall
if p := principalFromContext(ctx); p != "" {
    meta[vdso.MetaPrincipal] = p
}
```

The comment there names exactly what that closes: "a different principal can neither be served nor
fill the same (tool,args) entry, closing the cross-tenant cache leak + the hit/miss timing oracle."

The in-process agent loop that `fak serve --native` drives does **not** do this. `internal/agent`
has no principal on its tool calls at all — after #5644 the loop carries a principal for ROUTE
resolution (`WithRoutePrincipal`), but that principal is never lowered onto
`abi.ToolCall.Meta[vdso.MetaPrincipal]`.

**Consequence:** under `fak serve --native`, two different principals' read-shaped tool calls with
identical args share ONE vDSO tier-2 entry. Tenant B can be served bytes filled by tenant A, and
the hit/miss timing difference is observable — the same cross-tenant leak the proxy path closed,
still open on the mode that owns its loop.

## Evidence this is real, not theoretical

Observed first-hand while writing `internal/gateway/native_route_parity_test.go` (#5644): two
tests drove the owned loop under **different** `WithPrincipal` contexts, and the second test's
read-shaped `get_user_details` call was served from the first test's fill — it never reached the
adjudicator chain at all. The test had to be re-pointed at a WRITE-shaped tool (`book_flight`),
which the vDSO never dedups, and the file's `routedTool` comment records why. That is the leak
reproducing inside our own test binary.

## Why this is next

`--native` is the mode fak is steering serving toward, and the keyset residency work (#5332) plus
#5644 both assume the principal is load-bearing end to end. A principal that gates ROUTING but not
CACHING is a half-closed boundary, and the cache half is the one that moves bytes across tenants.

## Working spine

The owned loop lowers its configured principal onto each tool call's meta under the same
`vdso.MetaPrincipal` key the gateway uses, so one identity scopes both the route and the cache. A
test proves two principals cannot share a tier-2 entry through the native loop.

## In scope

- Lowering the loop's principal (already wired by `WithRoutePrincipal`, #5644) onto
  `abi.ToolCall.Meta[vdso.MetaPrincipal]` at the loop's call-construction site.
- A test: same tool, same args, two principals, through the owned loop — no shared fill.

## Out of scope

- Any change to the vDSO's own keying or to the proxy path's principal handling.
- Route resolution, which #5644 already closed.

## Done condition

Under `fak serve --native`, a read-shaped tool call made by one principal is never served from, and
never fills, a vDSO entry readable by a different principal. With no principal configured the loop
behaves exactly as it does at HEAD (single-tenant: every caller shares).

## Witness

`go test ./internal/gateway -run TestNativeLoopScopesVdsoPerPrincipal` — one tool, one arg set, two
principals driven through the owned loop, asserting the second call reaches the kernel rather than
being served from the first's fill.

## Acceptance gate

New test passes; `go test ./internal/gateway ./internal/agent ./internal/vdso` green (modulo
failures already red on the trunk); the no-principal arm byte-identical to HEAD.

## Dependencies

None blocking. Builds on #5644 (landed, 14e5095ad447), which put the principal on the loop.

## Confusion risks

- **`WithRoutePrincipal` did not already fix this.** It gates which ACCOUNT a routed id may bind
  to. The vDSO reads a different thing — `Meta[vdso.MetaPrincipal]` — which nothing sets on the
  loop's calls.
- **The empty principal is not a bug.** A single-tenant deployment presents "" and every caller
  legitimately shares one scope; that is the documented v0.1 behavior and must stay.

## Parent context

**#5632** — the gateway-as-fleet-front-door epic. Surfaced by #5644's parity test; the cache half
of the same principal boundary #5332 opened and #5644 extended to routing.

## Work unit

leaf

## Work scale

S1

## Expected steps

records.title: add(cmd): give fak agent a --route-accounts flag so its loop can pass WithRouteAccounts
records.body:
_Parent epic: #5632 — the gateway as the fleet's front door. Residual of #5644._

## Current state

#5644's "In scope" named two loop-construction sites that should pass `WithRouteAccounts`: the
native-serve site and `cmd/fak/main.go`. Only the first was landable, and #5644 landed it
(14e5095ad447).

The `cmd/fak/main.go` site is the `fak agent` CLI verb:

```go
// cmd/fak/main.go:1074
func loadAgentRouteOptions(path string) (*modelroute.Manifest, []agent.RunOption, error) {
    ...
    return &manifest, []agent.RunOption{agent.WithRouteManifest(&manifest)}, nil
}
```

`fak agent` has a `--route-manifest` flag and **no roster flag at all** — there is no
`*modelroute.Roster` in scope to pass. `fak serve` has `--route-accounts` (serve.go:134, resolved
at serve.go:415-439); `fak agent` does not. So closing this half is not "one option passed at loop
construction" as #5644 framed it — it needs a new operator surface: a flag, its config-bail text,
a `servewiring`-style entry, and docs. That is why #5644 stopped at the serve path, whose
done-condition it fully met.

## Why this is next

`fak agent` is the one-shot local arm operators reach for first, and it is the surface where a
bring-your-own-account roster is most visible (`fak route --accounts` already ships the pure
resolver and the no-spend probes). Leaving it manifest-only means the same routed id dispatches to
a different account depending on whether you ran `fak agent` or `fak serve --native`.

## Working spine

`fak agent` grows `--route-accounts <path>` mirroring `fak serve`'s: load + validate via
`modelroute.LoadRoster`, fail loud on a malformed roster, and pass `agent.WithRouteAccounts` (and
`agent.WithRoutePrincipal` where a principal is knowable) alongside the existing manifest option.

## In scope

- A `--route-accounts` flag on `fak agent`, loaded and validated exactly as `fak serve` does.
- Passing `WithRouteAccounts` from `loadAgentRouteOptions`.
- A test that `fak agent` with a roster resolves a routed id to its account-bound `EngineRoute()`.

## Out of scope

- The serve/native path (#5644, landed).
- Registering roster-derived engine ids so `EngineRoute()` reaches a driver — still the open
  follow-on #5644 named, and still unfiled as its own leaf.
- A principal model for `fak agent`, which has no keyset and no request boundary; the empty
  principal (unrestricted accounts only) is the honest default here.

## Done condition

`fak agent --route-manifest M --route-accounts R` binds a routed tool call to the account-resolved
`Target.EngineRoute()`, the same value `fak serve --native` binds for the same manifest+roster;
without `--route-accounts` the verb behaves exactly as it does at HEAD.

## Witness

`go test ./cmd/fak -run TestAgentVerbBindsRouteAccounts` — one manifest, one roster, asserting the
account-resolved route is what the run options resolve to, plus a no-flag arm unchanged.

## Acceptance gate

New test passes; `go test ./cmd/fak` green (modulo failures already red on the trunk); a malformed
roster fails loud at startup rather than mis-binding.

## Dependencies

None blocking. #5644 landed the shared loop-side plumbing this consumes.

## Confusion risks

- **This is not a one-line change, despite #5644's framing.** The blocker is the missing flag, not
  the missing option; #5644's "one option at loop construction" was true only of the serve site.
- **A roster carries env-var NAMES, never secrets.** The `fak serve` loader is the pattern to copy
  verbatim, including its `writeConfigBail` refusal.

## Parent context

**#5632** — the gateway-as-fleet-front-door epic. Residual half of #5644, which closed the
`--native` serve path and could not close this one without adding an operator surface.

## Work unit

leaf

## Work scale

S1

## Expected steps

4

## Trigger

Filed while landing #5644 (2026-08-06): its In-scope list named `cmd/fak/main.go`, and the site
turned out to have no roster available to pass.

## Batch policy

One leaf per gap.

## Closure binding

Closes on a commit stamped `(fak cmd)` adding `fak agent --route-accounts` and passing
`WithRouteAccounts` from `loadAgentRouteOptions`, with the account-binding test green.

- **Required model tier:** T1
- **Optimal model tier:** T2

`cmd/fak/main.go`, `cmd/fak/serve.go` (pattern reference), `cmd/fak/route_accounts_test.go`

```routing

paths: cmd/fak/main.go
expected_steps: add --route-accounts to fak agent; load+validate via modelroute.LoadRoster with a fail-loud config bail; pass WithRouteAccounts from loadAgentRouteOptions; test the account-resolved binding and the no-flag arm
```

records.title: feat(trajctl): quote a capability-conditioned trajectory denominator
records.body:
## Problem

Users cannot know before dispatch whether an agentic request is likely to be answered at the required quality within a reasonable cost envelope. Today `trajctl` observes budgets and scored progress after declaration, while capability, tool-policy, and index state live on separate surfaces. No immutable quote joins them, corrects itself online, or can be calibrated against witnessed outcomes.

## Working spine

For the `repo_question` request class, add a replayable quote ledger that records a versioned capability/index snapshot, quality contract, route template, and p50/p80/p95 cost envelope before execution; appends revisions without overwriting the initial quote; and binds completion to witnessed quality and raw realized cost.

## In scope

- Define the quote and capability-snapshot schemas, including readiness/auth/freshness rather than enabled-tool count.
- Join existing `capindex`, `toolcoverage`, index revision, and `trajctl` observations for one request class.
- Implement hierarchical historical lookup with a typed `cold-start` abstention when support is insufficient.
- Append immutable online revisions after capability failures or phase observations.
- Backtest chronological held-out quantile coverage, including censored runs.
- Meter quote compute, readiness probes, passive telemetry, and offline calibration separately; enforce the documented synchronous overhead budget.
- Render the initial quote, material revisions, and terminal reconciliation to users by default, with a stable JSON event schema and bounded-cardinality operator metrics.
- Self-check fixtures: fresh index, stale index, disappearing MCP tool, cheapest route failing quality, censored run, and cold start.

## Out of scope

- A universal learned predictor across all request/effect classes.
- Collapsing coverage and efficiency into one score.
- Claiming an oracle optimum when alternative routes were not replayed.
- Making per-query counterfactual replay or a generative-model call part of the online fast path.

## Done condition

A first-class `fak` verb emits the initial `repo_question` quote, immutable material revisions, and terminal reconciliation in human and stable JSON forms. Each event exposes estimator overhead and confidence/calibration support. The cached fast path makes no network or model call, and an observer-effect witness measures it against the documented latency/percentage budget. A held-out backtest reports p50/p80/p95 empirical coverage and refuses an unsupported cold-start quote. A captured fixture demonstrates the denominator widening after a capability failure while preserving the original quote.

## Witness

Unit tests for all six fixtures plus a chronological held-out calibration report from the fixture corpus. Golden human/JSON outputs prove the before/during/after user contract, including cold-start and capability-failure revisions. An off/passive/full observer-effect benchmark reports quote compute, probe latency/calls, model tokens, and provider cost. The completion record must bind the declared quality contract to an independently checkable outcome rather than the agent narrative.

## Acceptance gate

`fak validate --mine` for every changed path is green; the focused package tests pass under WSL/CI; human and JSON golden outputs are committed; the estimator overhead benchmark reports off/passive/full deltas; metrics use bounded-cardinality labels; and the captured quote/revision/backtest artifacts are committed.

## Research basis

`docs/notes/AGENTIC-TRAJECTORY-DENOMINATOR-2026-08-06.md` defines the denominator as a quality-constrained, capability-conditioned counterfactual cost distribution and details the minimal spine, calibration, coverage boundaries, and failure modes.

## Likely files

- `internal/trajctl/`
- `cmd/fak/`
- a fixture corpus under the owning package
- CLI/reference documentation

## Coordination

This crosses existing `trajctl`, `capindex`, and tool-coverage read surfaces. Consume their exported snapshots; do not rewrite peer-owned implementations. One coherent leaf commit should own the schema, verb, fixture proof, and docs.

## Work estimate

8 points: schema/snapshot join (2), quote/revision ledger (2), historical estimator and abstention (1.5), six-fixture proof (1.5), held-out calibration and docs (1).

## Parent context

Part of trajectory control epic #2533.

## Overall completion contribution

8/40 points toward calibrated trajectory pricing across request classes; this spine contributes 20% by establishing the first end-to-end request class and ledger contract.

## Target envelope

Production target: repo questions under versioned repository, MCP, policy, and index snapshots, with calibrated cost envelopes and explicit abstention.

## Witnessed envelope

Initial witness: deterministic fixture corpus and chronological held-out backtest for the `repo_question` class; no live cross-repository generalization claim.

## Completion standard
prototype

records.title: Token-profile spine: classify request economics before admission
records.body:
## Problem
A scalar total-token count collapses token classes with different API cost and server-load profiles. Guard admission cannot distinguish uncached prefill, cached-input reads, and reserved decode before spend.

## Done condition
- Add a versioned preflight token-class contract separating uncached input, cached input, and reserved output.
- Price API cost and scheduler load on separate axes.
- Expose a keyless captured halo example showing that economic and load dominance can differ.
- Document forecast-vs-observed boundaries and the follow-on integration direction.

## Witness
`fak token-profile --halo` emits all three classes, separate cost/load dominance, a shift-left action, and an explicit reconciliation boundary; package and captured-output tests cover the contract.

records.title: Preserve provider-native token usage and map it into canonical classes
records.body:
## Context
Follow-up to #5771. OpenAI-, Anthropic-, Gemini-, and local-engine usage payloads expose different details; flattening them into prompt/completion totals loses cache reads/writes, reasoning, and modality provenance.

## Done condition
- Define lossless provider adapters that retain raw usage fields and map known fields into versioned canonical token classes.
- Keep unknown provider fields available for replay/audit.
- Add fixtures for at least OpenAI cached input, Anthropic cache read/creation, and one local engine.
- Prove totals reconcile without double-counting.

## Witness
Fixture tests show native payload -> canonical classes -> reconciled totals, while raw provenance remains queryable.

records.title: Reconcile token forecasts, reservations, and observed usage by request ID
records.body:
## Context
#5771 creates a preflight forecast but explicitly does not claim it equals billed or hardware-observed usage.

## Done condition
- Carry one request/profile ID through guard admission, server execution, and provider response.
- Record forecast, reserved, observed, and released counts per token class.
- Compute forecast error and cache-expectation accuracy without treating missing provider detail as zero.
- Cover success, streaming, cancellation, retry, and provider-error paths.

## Witness
An end-to-end test admits a request, completes it with synthetic provider usage, and reads back one reconciled record with conservation assertions.

records.title: Admit and route requests on separate prefill, cache, and decode envelopes
records.body:
## Context
Equal total tokens can impose different server load. #5771 supplies a typed vector before execution; admission should consume it instead of one scalar.

## Done condition
- Add configurable envelopes for uncached prefill, cached-input/KV transfer, and reserved decode.
- Return typed refusal reasons naming the exhausted class and recovery.
- Route profiles to compatible capacity while preserving existing default behavior when class policy is absent.
- Avoid head-of-line blocking where a decode-heavy request exhausts only the decode envelope.

## Witness
Deterministic scheduler tests submit equal-total profiles with different mixes and prove different admit/route decisions for the intended class.

records.title: Forecast cache-hit probability and provenance before token admission
records.body:
## Context
`input.cached` at preflight is an expectation, not an observed fact (#5771). Admission needs confidence and evidence rather than a boolean cache claim.

## Done condition
- Represent expected cached span, confidence, predictor provenance, cache namespace/affinity, and freshness.
- Derive the forecast from available prefix/cache metadata without provider spend.
- Define fail-open/fail-closed behavior for stale or unavailable predictors.
- Score predictions against reconciled provider observations.

## Witness
Table tests cover certain hit, certain miss, partial/stale/unknown predictions, and a ledger fold reports calibration error.

records.title: Expose token-class profiles in debug vars, usage ledger, traces, and query
records.body:
## Context
A shift-left decision is useful only if operators can see why it happened and compare it to observed usage (#5771).

## Done condition
- Publish bounded-cardinality per-class forecast/reserved/observed/released counters.
- Attach request/profile IDs and class decisions to traces and the gateway usage ledger.
- Add an operator query that explains cost dominance, load dominance, refusal/route action, and reconciliation status.
- Define redaction and cardinality rules for tenant/model/cache identifiers.

## Witness
One synthetic request is visible with consistent values across debug vars, ledger, trace fixture, and query output.

records.title: Extend token classes for reasoning, multimodal, cache-write, and prediction tokens
records.body:
## Context
The #5771 spine intentionally starts with three text classes. Provider APIs additionally distinguish reasoning, audio/image input/output, cache creation tiers, and accepted/rejected prediction tokens.

## Done condition
- Specify an additive class/version policy and parent-child rollups.
- Add classes only where economic or scheduling duties differ.
- Map representative provider fields without forcing unsupported providers to fabricate zeros.
- Preserve backward-compatible three-class rollups.

## Witness
Cross-provider fixtures demonstrate additive decoding and stable v1 consumers while new classes retain distinct cost/load semantics.

records.title: Calibrate scheduler token weights against measured hardware service time
records.body:
## Context
The weights in #5771 are explicit illustrative policy inputs, not hardware truth. Production scheduling needs model/engine/device calibration.

## Done condition
- Measure prefill, cache-read/transfer, and decode service time over controlled token shapes on a sanctioned compute node.
- Fit and version weights with model, engine, hardware, batch, and confidence provenance.
- Compare against the tuned scalar-total baseline under held workloads.
- Refuse a net-true gain claim unless the measured alternative and overhead are included.

## Witness
A reproducible benchmark ledger and calibration artifact predict held-out service time within a declared error bound and report net scheduling value.

records.title: Enforce tenant token-class budgets and release unused output reservations
records.body:
## Context
Dollar budgets and capacity reservations differ by class. Output must be reserved before generation but unused decode should not remain charged to capacity (#5771).

## Done condition
- Add per-tenant/model policy limits by canonical class and optional USD ceiling.
- Atomically reserve before execution and release unused output on completion/cancel/error.
- Make retries/idempotency unable to double-reserve or double-charge.
- Emit typed budget refusals and reconciliation records.

## Witness
Concurrent tests prove no oversubscription, conservation of reservations, and correct release across streaming cancellation and retry.

records.title: Build token-class halo demo comparing equal totals with unequal cost and load
records.body:
## Context
The best halo for #5771 is not a dense dashboard: it is two requests with the same total tokens whose class mixes force different decisions.

## Done condition
- Add a runnable keyless demo with two equal-total profiles: cache-heavy/prefill-heavy versus decode-heavy.
- Show scalar admission making the same decision and token-class admission making different explainable decisions.
- Render cost and scheduler-load bars plus the shift-left action.
- Include `-selfcheck` and a captured render witness; document the one-command run.

## Witness
The captured render pins equal totals, unequal cost/load vectors, and different admission/route outcomes; `-selfcheck` passes from a fresh clone.
