records.title: Epic: micro-context fabric for 100-10,000 parallel agents
records.body: ## Goal Establish micro-context/context-splitting as a dedicated high-priority fak research and delivery focus: one immutable cached agent base serving 100, 1,000, then 10,000 independently scheduled logical contexts, with bounded physical model slots.  ## Why now Single-session hardware has hard latency, KV, and decode limits; software-side independent work is much wider. The program targets both (1) turning usable single-stream inference into high aggregate performance and (2) turning a slow single stream into useful aggregate service or multi-user throughput without hiding critical-path latency.  ## Shipped spine `go run ./cmd/microcontextdemo -selfcheck -contexts 10000 -workers 64` is the S0 harness witness. It proves bounded 10k logical-context execution and one shared base installation. It is explicitly synthetic and makes no model-throughput claim.  Research contract: `docs/research/micro-context-fabrics.md`.  ## Done condition - S0 through S7 in the research contract have captured witnesses. - Controlled-kernel and API-only paths both run end to end. - 100, 1k, and 10k scale points report model provenance, physical slots, TTFT/tail latency, prefill/decode throughput, cache evidence, RAM/KV, errors, verifier pass rate, and useful completions/time. - Tuned sequential and provider-native batching baselines are included. - Tool-capable contexts preserve capability isolation, leases/idempotency, and independent effect verification. - Single-critical-path usability and aggregate throughput remain separate headline axes.  ## Child tracks Real-endpoint spine; prefix-cache A/B; hibernation/backpressure; harness assumptions/lightweight descriptor; compatibility scheduler; tool/effect safety; 10k controlled-kernel soak; API-only adapter; quality/observability ledger; multi-user fairness/economics.  ## Non-claims 10k logical contexts do not mean 10k OS processes or resident KV slots. Synthetic contexts/sec is not tokens/sec. Orchestration concurrency is not an inference speedup.  ## Delivery checklist - [x] #5786 — S1 real-endpoint 100-context spine - [x] #5787 — S2 shared-prefix A/B - [x] #5788 — S3 1,000-context hibernation/restart - [x] #5789 — harness inventory and lightweight descriptor - [x] #5790 — compatibility scheduler - [x] #5791 — tool/effect safety - [x] #5792 — S5 controlled-kernel 10k soak - [x] #5793 — S6 API-only adapter - [x] #5794 — quality/observability ledger - [x] #5795 — S7 multi-user fairness/economics         - [x] #5817 — S2b kernel cache-observable shared-prefix A/B (supersedes the S2 cache verdict) - [x] #5820 — S5a 1,000 real-model-turn contexts (small-first ramp to #5792) - [x] #5818 — multi-turn descriptor continuation budgets - [x] #5819 — in-kernel compatibility-batch execution - [x] #5821 — cache-value Track-1 fold of witnessed shared-base reuse  ## Fan-out and contract repair (2026-08-06) - Hardening fan-out filed off spine `28846558d0` (markers `fanout-microcontextdemo-*`): #5830–#5844 (qa ×3, dogfood ×2, product ×3, observability ×2, integration ×3, docs, release). - #5792–#5795 repaired to dispatch-ready contract bodies (research completion standard, routed, `research` label removed); round-trip: 9/9 dispatchable via `fak issue contract -from-issues`.

records.title: Micro-context S1: run 100 delta contexts on one real endpoint
records.body:
Parent: #5785

## Problem
The shipped S0 proves harness fan-out only. It does not cross a real model/provider seam.

## Done condition
- Add a runnable spine using the existing fak OpenAI-compatible gateway with one immutable base and 100 task deltas.
- Bound physical concurrency and preserve per-context cancellation/error identity.
- Capture model/provider/hardware provenance, base/delta tokens, TTFT p50/p95, prefill/decode throughput, failures, and wall time.
- Keep full-harness bring-up out of the hot path.

## Witness
A checked-in command and captured artifact complete exactly 100 contexts against a real endpoint; a verifier checks counts and explicitly distinguishes single-stream latency from aggregate throughput.

records.title: Micro-context S2: measure shared-prefix A/B against tuned batching
records.body:
Parent: #5785

## Problem
A shared base is valuable only if it produces observed cache/prefill savings against real alternatives.

## Done condition
- Compare tuned sequential, provider-native batch, unique full prompts, and byte-identical base-plus-delta requests.
- Canonicalize tool/schema ordering and record the base fingerprint plus cache miss reasons.
- Report billed cached tokens where available, TTFT, prefill/decode tokens/sec, queue tax, and net useful completions/time.
- Label every value measured, observed, or modeled.

## Witness
A reproducible A/B artifact on one real endpoint demonstrates or falsifies prefix reuse; `fak claim-check` accepts any reported gain against the tuned baseline.

records.title: Micro-context S3: hibernate and resume 1,000 bounded contexts
records.body:
Parent: #5785

## Problem
One thousand logical contexts cannot require one thousand resident KV allocations or full transcripts.

## Done condition
- Integrate existing microagent hibernation/warm-band/session seams into the research spine.
- Define warm, parked, and hibernated states with bounded RAM/KV and admission backpressure.
- Resume after process restart without duplicating completed effects.
- Measure restore latency, recompute cost, queue age, memory, and eviction behavior.

## Witness
A captured 1,000-context run crosses a forced restart, retires every context exactly once, stays under a declared memory envelope, and reports resident versus hibernated counts.

records.title: Inventory harness assumptions and define a lightweight micro-context descriptor
records.body:
Parent: #5785

## Problem
Current agent harnesses often assume one process, terminal, cwd, transcript, credentials, and approval channel per agent; replicating that shell dominates tiny tasks.

## Done condition
- Measure fixed bring-up cost for full fak, Claude/Ultracode-style, and available API-only paths.
- Classify which assumptions are semantic requirements versus UI/session conveniences.
- Define a versioned descriptor: base_id, task_delta, capability_set, budget, continuation, output_contract.
- Build an adapter from the descriptor into existing microagent/gateway seams without a second fleet runtime.

## Witness
A checked-in benchmark and contract test show the descriptor running the same fixed task corpus as a full harness and quantify startup/RAM/token differences with limitations stated.

records.title: Schedule micro-contexts by model and batch compatibility class
records.body:
Parent: #5785

## Problem
Model, sampling, tool, deadline, prefix, and sequence-length differences fragment batches and can erase parallel gains.

## Done condition
- Define compatibility keys and bounded queues for prefill and decode work.
- Include priority/deadline fairness, starvation prevention, cancellation, and head-of-line avoidance while tools run.
- Expose padding tax, batch fill, queue delay, and slot utilization.
- Fail open to existing routing when classification is unavailable.

## Witness
Deterministic scheduler tests plus a captured mixed-workload run show compatible coalescing, incompatible isolation, bounded latency, and no starvation.

records.title: Make tool-capable micro-contexts effect-safe under parallel execution
records.body:
Parent: #5785

## Problem
Parallel model turns become unsafe when contexts collide on files, rows, messages, approvals, or other effects.

## Done condition
- Bind each context to a least-privilege capability set and resource/lane lease.
- Journal tool intents/results with idempotency keys and separate model slots from tool waits.
- Require independent effect read-back before folding actionable results.
- Quarantine conflicts and retries without poisoning unrelated contexts.

## Witness
An end-to-end adversarial test runs conflicting and disjoint tool tasks concurrently; disjoint effects complete, conflicts are serialized/refused, and no duplicate effect survives retry/restart.

records.title: Micro-context S5: soak 10,000 contexts on a controlled kernel
records.body:
## Parent context
Epic #5785 — micro-context fabric for 100–10,000 parallel agents. Research contract: `docs/research/micro-context-fabrics.md`. Rungs S0–S4 shipped with captured witnesses (#5786–#5791).

records.title: epic(agent): tool-call WIDTH as a governed default — measure, encourage, enforce, monitor calls-per-turn
records.body:
## Summary

Tool-call **width** — how many tool calls one assistant turn issues — is the axis that
buys latency and accuracy at once, and fak currently has no governed position on it: no
live meter, no default posture, no enforcement seam, and (worse) a wire-shaping bug that
structurally pushes models *away* from batching.

This epic groups the measure / encourage / enforce / monitor rungs for tool-call width.

## The load-bearing distinction: WIDTH, not VOLUME

The naive framing ("better models make more tool calls, so make more tool calls") is
half right, and the wrong half is expensive. The literature separates cleanly:

- **Width (calls per assistant turn) is a real win.** [Wide & Deep](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.07359v1)
  jointly scales depth (more iterations) against width (parallel tool calling within a
  single reasoning step) and finds that scaling width *both* increases accuracy *and
  reduces the number of turns needed* — 62.2% with GPT-5-Medium on BrowseComp, above the
  54.9% originally reported for GPT-5-High, with no context-management tricks.
- **Width is controllable at the runtime, not just the model.** The
  [LLM-Tool Compiler](https://arxiv.org/html/2405.17438v1) fuses similar tool operations
  into one function at runtime and reports **up to 4x more parallel calls**, with token
  cost down ~40% and latency down ~12% — and up to **5x** more parallel calls when
  combined with prompting schemes. Width responds to harness design.
- **Volume (total calls per task) is confounded with failure.** A 1,440-run MCP benchmark
  found retry rate inflating cost **1.4-2.8x**, with models at 75% first-attempt pass
  finishing at 96-98% only after up to 3 retries. Raw call count rises when the agent is
  *failing*, so a KPI that rewards volume rewards thrash.

So the metric to govern is `tool_calls_per_assistant_turn` and a batched-turn rate —
exactly what [#5019](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/5019) named — **not**
calls-per-task. fak's own prior art agrees the pressure only relocates:
`docs/notes/SCALING-LAWS-OF-AGENTS-2026-06-19.md` §10 argues batching moves the reread
tax from forked prefixes into one fat working set rather than deleting it, which is
another reason the meter has to exist before the nudge does.

## Where fak stands today (measured, not assumed)

| Rung | State |
|---|---|
| Measure | `internal/agent/turnbatch.go` folds `tool_calls_per_assistant_turn` + `batched_turn_rate` — and is an **orphan**: no consumer anywhere in the tree. |
| Encourage | Nothing. No launch-time posture, no SessionStart rule, no setting. |
| Enforce | Nothing on the request path. The gateway *advertises* `supports_parallel_tool_calls: true` in its `/v1/models` descriptor (`internal/gateway/http.go:1127`) — a discovery field, not a request-path capability — while nothing in the tree ever reads `tool_choice.disable_parallel_tool_use` (zero hits repo-wide). On the anthropic→anthropic passthrough the raw body is relayed verbatim, so the field does reach upstream *there*; what is missing everywhere is any fak-side handling. |
| Monitor | Nothing fleet-side. No ratchet, no dashboard row, no regression alarm. |
| Actively harmful | The gateway re-emits N parallel tool results as **N stacked single-block user turns** — the documented anti-pattern for sustaining parallel tool use. Witnessed; see the child bug. |

[#5019](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/5019) is CLOSED with **none of its
three acceptance criteria met**. Only the *measurement primitive* landed — the pure fold in
`internal/agent/turnbatch.go` (`0329bf9806`, the sole commit in history referencing #5019,
which adds nothing else). Criterion (b) asks for the KPI to be "emitted per session and
aggregated in the dispatch/witness metrics", and no tracked caller of `ParseTranscriptTurns`
/ `FoldTurnBatch` / `ScanTranscriptBatch` exists (prose mentions only, at
`internal/sessionaudit/delegated.go:16`, `cmd/fak/model_acceptance_run.go:242`,
`internal/modelaccept/modelaccept.go:71`); criterion (a), the launch-time batching nudge,
was never wired (`ultracodeSettingsArg` at `cmd/fak/accounts_launch.go:59` still injects only
`{"ultracode":true}`); criterion (c), the before/after cadence note, was never written.

This epic picks up that unmet remainder and adds the enforcement + monitoring rungs #5019
did not scope.

## The control surface, honestly

There is **no API knob that forces width**. The Anthropic
[parallel tool use](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/parallel-tool-use)
surface only exposes the *suppression* direction — `tool_choice.disable_parallel_tool_use`
caps the model at one tool per response. Encouraging width is therefore a three-lever
harness job:

1. **Message-history shape** — the docs are explicit that splitting parallel tool results
   across separate user turns *degrades* subsequent parallelism. This is the lever fak is
   currently pulling backwards.
2. **System-prompt posture** — a standing instruction to batch independent calls.
3. **Tool schema design** — batch-capable tools (the LLM-Tool Compiler's fusion result),
   so width is expressible without the model having to plan a DAG.

## Children

- Fix the tool-result re-encode that suppresses batching (the harmful rung — do first) — #5797
- Honor and forward `disable_parallel_tool_use`; stop advertising an unbacked capability — #5798
- Wire the orphan `turnbatch` KPI into a real consumer (#5019 remainder) — #5799
- Fleet width monitor + a `batched_turn_rate` regression ratchet — #5800
- Launch-time batching nudge, shadow-first, graded against the KPI — #5801
- Give `fak_read` and the per-item MCP verbs a batch axis so width is expressible — #5816
- Harden the width corpus: it grades instruction-following, not the model's own decision to
  batch — #5845
- ~~Grade tool-call width per turn in model acceptance~~ — **LANDED independently** as
  #5802 (`f4d84c8eae`), which shipped hours before this epic was written.
  `Task.MinParallelToolCalls` + `Run.ToolTurns` grade WIDTH separately from volume
  (`internal/modelaccept/modelaccept.go:40,191`), `ModelDecision.tool_calls_per_tool_turn`
  reports it per model (`:119,:241`) on turnbatch's exact denominator, and
  `examples/model-acceptance-agentic-v1.json`'s `parallel-lookup` task distinguishes a
  batched run from a serialized one. #5807 duplicated it and is closed; the one genuine
  remainder it surfaced is #5845.

## Ordering rationale

Fix-then-measure-then-nudge, deliberately. Shipping the nudge first would grade a prompt
change against a wire path that suppresses the behaviour being asked for, and the nudge
would be scored as ineffective for the wrong reason.

The acceptance-grade rung is already in (#5802): the corpus can now tell a batched turn from
a serialized one, so the wire fix (#5797) and the nudge (#5801) have a grader waiting.
Fix-then-measure-then-nudge still holds for the remaining rungs — the fleet meter
(#5799/#5800) is the part that is still missing.

## Acceptance

- A live `tool_calls_per_assistant_turn` / `batched_turn_rate` reading exists per session
  and is aggregated fleet-side.
- The gateway neither suppresses width structurally nor advertises a knob it ignores.
- Any width-raising posture is graded against the meter, shadow-first, with a before/after
  on one lane.

_Framing note: the goal is width per turn, never volume per task. A child that raises
total call count without raising calls-per-turn has probably found a retry loop, not a win._

records.title: fix(gateway): parallel tool_results are re-emitted as N stacked user turns, structurally suppressing batching
records.body:
## Summary

fak's gateway decodes an inbound Anthropic user turn carrying N parallel `tool_result`
blocks into N separate canonical `RoleTool` messages. The Anthropic and Gemini adapters
then **always** re-emit those as N separate single-block `user` messages, and the
OpenAI-compatible adapter does so whenever the `FAK_OPENAI_TOOL_MESSAGES_AS_TEXT` lowering
is on (default off, but on by default in the shipped `gemini-gcp` and `mac` presets). One
batched turn goes in; a stack of serialized turns goes out.

Anthropic's [parallel tool use docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/parallel-tool-use)
call this out directly: if parallel tool results are split across separate user turns
instead of batched into one `user` message with multiple `tool_result` blocks, parallelism
**degrades**. So fak is currently shaping the wire in the direction that trains the model
out of the behaviour we want more of.

## Witness

Throwaway test against `internal/agent`, inbound = 3 messages where the last is ONE user
turn holding 2 `tool_result` blocks:

```
INBOUND wire: 3 messages (last = ONE user turn, 2 tool_result blocks)
decoded to 4 canonical messages:
  [0] role=user      toolcalls=0 toolCallID=""
  [1] role=assistant toolcalls=2 toolCallID=""
  [2] role=tool      toolcalls=0 toolCallID="toolu_1"
  [3] role=tool      toolcalls=0 toolCallID="toolu_2"
RE-ENCODED to anthropic upstream: 4 messages
  [0] role=user      blocks=1
  [1] role=assistant blocks=2
  [2] role=user      blocks=1     <-- was one batched turn
  [3] role=user      blocks=1     <-- now two stacked user turns
```

Three messages in, four out; the single batched tool-result turn became two stacked
single-block user turns.

## Where

- Fan-out (correct, and documented as intentional): `internal/agent/anthropic_server.go:169-173`
  — "A user turn carrying tool_result blocks fans them out into RoleTool messages (one per
  result, in order)".
- The un-collapsed re-encode, all four adapters:
  - Anthropic: `internal/agent/adapters.go:876-880` — one `anthropicMessage{Role:"user"}` per `RoleTool`.
  - Gemini: `internal/agent/adapters.go:1129-1138` — one `geminiContent{Role:"user"}` per `RoleTool`.
  - Qwen/OpenAI-compatible: `internal/agent/adapters.go:244-255` — `msg.Role = RoleUser`
    plus a `<tool_response>` text block per result, but **only** under the opt-in
    `OpenAIToolMessagesAsText` lowering (sole call site `adapters.go:191-193`; set from
    `FAK_OPENAI_TOOL_MESSAGES_AS_TEXT` for the `openai`/`xai` providers at
    `chat.go:655-656`, default false). With the flag off — the default OpenAI/vLLM/SGLang
    chat wire — tool results stay native `role=tool` messages and this adapter does not
    stack user turns at all (`adapters.go:82-83`). The mode is not exotic, which is why the
    fix still covers it: `scripts/dogfood-claude.ps1:227,257` turn it on by default for the
    `gemini-gcp` and `mac` presets (`docs/fak/claude-gemini-gcp.md:63`).
  - OpenAI Responses: `internal/agent/adapters.go:634-640` — flat item list; this one is
    fine, the Responses wire has no user-turn stacking to begin with.

The fan-out itself is not the bug. The missing **re-collapse** on the way out is.

All line numbers are against `1a1151dc07`; on a hot trunk prefer the symbol names as the
durable anchors.

## Why it slipped through

`internal/gateway/role_alternation.go:126-129` exempts a run of `RoleTool` messages from
`FlawSameRoleStacked` — `CheckRoleAlternation`'s `agent.RoleTool` arm only decrements
`pending` and never raises the stacked-role flaw, which is raised solely on the
`RoleAssistant` arm (`:122-124`) and the `RoleUser` arm (`:136-138`). The exemption is
*documented* at `:52-58` and `:31-35`, on the correct reasoning that such a run "is the
several results of one assistant turn's parallel tool calls, which is a single logical
turn". That exemption is right for the *canonical* array — but nothing re-imposes the
single-logical-turn shape at the adapter boundary, so the stack is reconstituted on the
wire where the provider does see it as stacked user turns.

## Cost

- **Width suppression** — the documented degradation of subsequent parallel tool use,
  i.e. directly against the epic's goal.
- **Cache prefix churn** — stacked same-role turns are the shape `role_alternation.go:8-10`
  already names as bursting the provider's prompt cache.
- **Wire-shape risk** — consecutive `user` messages are the violation fak's own
  adjudicator refuses for non-tool roles; some providers reject or silently renormalize it.

## Proposed fix

Re-collapse at marshal time: in each adapter, fold a maximal run of adjacent `RoleTool`
messages into ONE provider turn carrying all their blocks —

- Anthropic: one `{"role":"user","content":[tool_result, tool_result, ...]}`.
- Gemini: one `user` `geminiContent` with several `functionResponse` parts.
- Qwen/OpenAI-compatible: one user message concatenating the `<tool_response>` blocks.

Order within the run must be preserved (results are id-keyed but order is load-bearing for
cache prefix stability). Everything here is a pure function of the message array, so it is
table-testable with no network.

## Acceptance criteria

- A round-trip test: one inbound user turn with N `tool_result` blocks re-encodes to
  exactly ONE upstream user turn with N blocks, for Anthropic, Gemini, and the
  OpenAI-compatible path under `OpenAIToolMessagesAsText: true`.
- A no-change arm for the default OpenAI wire (`OpenAIToolMessagesAsText: false`), asserting
  it still emits one native `role=tool` message per result.
- Message count is preserved across decode -> marshal for the batched-tool-result shape
  (the witness above goes from 3-in/4-out to 3-in/3-out).
- `CheckRoleAlternation` still passes on the canonical array (the `RoleTool` exemption is
  unchanged — the fix is at the adapter boundary, not in the adjudicator).
- No behaviour change for the single-tool-result case.

## Related

Part of the tool-call-width epic. Sibling of the `disable_parallel_tool_use` passthrough
gap. This is the "stop actively suppressing it" rung and should land before any
width-raising nudge is graded, or the nudge will be measured against a wire that fights it.

_Best-effort report from a code read plus the runtime witness above; I have not measured
the downstream accuracy delta, only established the shape and cited the vendor guidance
that the shape degrades parallelism._

Parent: #5796

records.title: feat(gateway): honor and forward tool_choice.disable_parallel_tool_use (capability advertised but unbacked)
records.body:
## Summary

The gateway's model-listing endpoint advertises `"supports_parallel_tool_calls": true`
(`internal/gateway/http.go:1127`, in the per-model descriptor `handleModels` returns from
`/v1/models`), but **nothing on the request path** reads, honors, or maps
`tool_choice.disable_parallel_tool_use` — zero hits repo-wide.

One nuance that narrows the bug without dissolving it: on the anthropic→anthropic
passthrough the client's raw body is relayed verbatim (`messages_stream_passthrough.go:426`
→ `StreamAnthropicRaw`; buffered twin `messages.go:1419-1420` `WithRawRequestBody(req.Raw)`),
so on **that one route** the field does reach the upstream and the upstream enforces it. fak
still has no seam that observes or sets it, and on every route that reconstructs the request
rather than byte-passing it — notably the OpenAI chat wire, whose `ChatRequest` carries no
`tool_choice` field at all — it is dropped entirely.

That is the one direction of width control the vendor API actually exposes — see the
[parallel tool use docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/parallel-tool-use):
with `tool_choice: auto`, `disable_parallel_tool_use: true` means at most one tool call per
response; paired with `any` or `tool` it pins exactly one. There is no counterpart knob
that *forces* width, which makes correctly handling the suppression knob the whole of the
API-level surface.

## Current state

`tool_choice` is only partially modeled today:

- `internal/gateway/messages.go:1140-1157` — `toolChoicePinnedName` parses `tool_choice`
  solely to extract `{"type":"tool","name":...}` for a soundness check. The check
  **preserves** rather than refuses: the caller does `delete(drop, pinned)` to exempt that
  tool from the floor-deny prune set, so fak never forwards a body whose `tool_choice` names
  a tool absent from `tools[]`. (The model may still propose the pinned call, and the kernel
  `DEFAULT_DENY`s it at adjudication — witness `TestInboundToolsKeepsToolChoicePinnedDef`.)
  Its decode struct declares only `Type` and `Name`, so every other sub-field — including
  `disable_parallel_tool_use` — is discarded by the unmarshal. That is this ticket's point.
- `internal/gateway/wire.go:313-315` — the OpenAI `/v1/chat/completions` wire doc states
  that "tool_choice and other unknown OpenAI fields are still accepted and ignored (drop-in
  compatibility)". `ChatRequest` (`wire.go:319-362`) declares no `ToolChoice` field, and
  `handleChatCompletions` (`http.go:498`) decodes into that struct rather than byte-passing,
  so the whole `tool_choice` object is dropped on decode.
- `internal/agent/adapters.go:155` and `:445` declare `ToolChoice` as a bare `string`, on
  `openAIRequest` and `openAIResponsesRequest`. (`:199` and `:554` are not declarations but
  struct-literal assignments of a locally synthesized value — `toolChoice := ""`, then
  `"auto"` if any tools are present, at `:187-190` and `:538-541`.) The gap is wider than a
  type mismatch: **`adapterRequest` (`:51-85`) has no `ToolChoice` field at all**, so no
  client-supplied `tool_choice` — string or object — ever reaches these adapters, and
  `reservedExtraBodyKey` (`internal/agent/chat.go:787-796`) fences `tool_choice` out of the
  `ExtraBody` escape hatch. The Anthropic adapter, the one upstream with a native
  `disable_parallel_tool_use`, models no `tool_choice` field whatsoever (`anthropicRequest`,
  `:786-796`).

Net: the flag is dropped on every path that reconstructs the request, survives only by
accident on the raw anthropic passthrough, and the capability endpoint claims support
regardless of route.

All line numbers are against `1a1151dc07`; `messages.go` in particular renumbers on nearly
every gateway commit, so treat the symbol names as the durable anchors.

## Why it matters for the width epic

1. **Truthfulness.** Advertising a capability the request path ignores is the kind of
   unbacked claim the repo's own standards exist to prevent.
2. **It is the enforcement seam.** Once fak parses the flag it also owns a *place* to
   express policy about width — including the shadow-mode observability the monitoring
   child needs (how often do clients ask to suppress parallelism, and on which lanes?).
3. **Correctness for sequential workflows.** The `any` + `disable_parallel_tool_use`
   combination is the documented pattern for enforcing step ordering. A client relying on
   it through fak currently gets un-ordered parallel execution.

## Proposal

- Extend the `tool_choice` decode to the full object: `type` (`auto` / `any` / `tool` /
  `none`), `name`, and `disable_parallel_tool_use`.
- Forward it faithfully on the Anthropic upstream path; map it to the nearest native
  construct where one exists (e.g. `parallel_tool_calls: false` on OpenAI-compatible
  upstreams) and record a typed note where no equivalent exists rather than silently
  dropping it.
- Where fak cannot honor it, either refuse with a structured reason or stop advertising
  the capability for that route — not both-and-neither.
- Emit the observed `disable_parallel_tool_use` rate as a counter, so the width monitor can
  distinguish "the model chose not to batch" from "the client forbade batching". Without
  that split, the batched-turn-rate KPI is uninterpretable on any lane where a client sets
  the flag.

## Acceptance criteria

- A request with `tool_choice: {"type":"auto","disable_parallel_tool_use":true}` reaches an
  Anthropic upstream with that field intact on the **reconstructing** path (wire test). The
  raw passthrough already satisfies this by relaying the body verbatim; a regression test
  should pin that too, so a future refactor away from byte-passing cannot silently drop it.
- The same request against an OpenAI-compatible upstream carries the native equivalent, or
  is refused with a structured reason — never silently dropped.
- `supports_parallel_tool_calls` in the models payload is backed by a test that exercises
  the flag end to end, or the advertisement is removed for unsupported routes.
- A counter distinguishes client-suppressed turns from model-chosen single-call turns.

## Related

Part of the tool-call-width epic. The monitoring child depends on the suppression counter
landing here, otherwise its denominator is contaminated.

Parent: #5796

records.title: feat(agent): wire the orphan turnbatch KPI into a real consumer (#5019 remainder)
records.body:
## Summary

[#5019](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/5019) shipped the measurement
primitive and closed, but two of its three acceptance criteria are unmet. The KPI it built
is an **orphan**: `internal/agent/turnbatch.go` has no consumer anywhere in the tree.

## Evidence

`internal/agent/turnbatch.go` exports a complete, tested fold —
`ParseTranscriptTurns`, `FoldTurnBatch`, `ScanTranscriptBatch`, and a
`TurnBatchStats` carrying `tool_calls_per_assistant_turn` and `batched_turn_rate` under
schema `fak.turnbatch.v1`. A tree-wide search for any of those symbols outside
`internal/agent/turnbatch{,_test}.go` returns nothing in tracked code (the only other hits
are copies under scratch/overlay directories).

Against #5019's stated criteria:

| Criterion | State |
|---|---|
| KPI primitive exists | **Met** — `turnbatch.go`, with tests. |
| `tool_calls_per_assistant_turn` emitted per session and aggregated in dispatch/witness metrics | **Not met** — nothing calls it. |
| Opus autonomous-lane launches carry a batching instruction | **Not met** — no launch-time posture exists (tracked separately as the nudge child). |
| Before/after cadence note on one grind lane | **Not met** — no data to compare. |

The prose in `turnbatch.go:5-8` names the gap precisely: the KPI exists so that "a
launch-time 'batch independent calls' nudge had no metric to be measured against" is no
longer true. That is still true, because the metric is never read.

## Why this is the first thing to fix after the wire bug

The other rungs all depend on it. The nudge child cannot be graded, the monitoring child
has no series to ratchet, and the model-acceptance child has no shared definition of width
to reuse. Wiring one consumer unblocks three.

## Proposal

Give `turnbatch` exactly one real consumer, and prefer the cheapest one that produces a
durable series:

- A `fak` verb that folds a session transcript (or a directory of them) and emits the
  `fak.turnbatch.v1` payload — the same shape `internal/codexlifecycle`'s
  `ToolCallsPerTurn` report already takes for codex rollouts
  (`internal/codexlifecycle/health.go:322,418`), so the two engines become comparable
  rather than two bespoke numbers.
- Emit onto the witness sidecar / dispatch metrics so the value persists per session
  instead of being recomputed by hand.
- Keep the evidence-minimal contract the package already holds: structural counts only, no
  prompt / argument / result / model text (`turnbatch.go:15-18`).

Two design points worth deciding explicitly rather than inheriting:

1. **Denominator.** `BatchedTurnRate` excludes text-only turns (correct — they had nothing
   to batch), while `ToolCallsPerAssistantTurn` divides by *all* turns including text-only
   ones. Those two answer different questions and a dashboard that shows them side by side
   without saying so will mislead. Consider also emitting calls-per-*tool*-turn.
2. **Sampling.** If this ever moves onto a hot path rather than a post-hoc transcript fold,
   it must go behind `internal/turntaxmeter`'s 1-in-N `Sampler` — that package exists
   precisely as the observer-effect fence for per-turn meters.

## Acceptance criteria

- At least one tracked, non-test caller of `ScanTranscriptBatch` / `FoldTurnBatch` exists.
- A session produces a persisted `fak.turnbatch.v1` reading without a bespoke scan.
- The reading is comparable to the codex-side `tool_calls_per_turn` (same denominator
  convention, or an explicit documented difference).
- Rounding and zero-denominator behaviour are unchanged (the fold stays pure).

## Related

Part of the tool-call-width epic; picks up the unmet remainder of #5019. Blocks the
monitoring and nudge children.

Parent: #5796

records.title: feat(observability): fleet tool-call-width monitor + a batched_turn_rate regression ratchet
records.body:
## Summary

Once `tool_calls_per_assistant_turn` is emitted per session, nothing yet watches it across
the fleet. This is the monitoring rung: aggregate width per lane / engine / model, and
ratchet it so a regression is visible rather than inferred months later from a latency
complaint.

## Why a ratchet and not a target

Width is the axis where a naive target does real damage. The distinction the epic rests on:

- **Width per turn** — parallel calls in one assistant response — is the good direction.
  [Wide & Deep](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.07359v1) shows scaling it raises accuracy *and*
  cuts turn count.
- **Volume per task** — total calls to finish — is largely a **failure signal**. A 1,440-run
  MCP benchmark found retries inflating cost 1.4-2.8x; models at 75% first-attempt pass
  reach 96-98% only after up to 3 retries. A dashboard that rewards total calls rewards
  thrash.

So the monitored series must be width, and it must be reported next to a success/outcome
series, or the fleet will optimize toward a metric that goes up when things go wrong.

## Proposal

Series to aggregate, per lane and per engine/model:

- `tool_calls_per_assistant_turn` (mean; p50/p90 if the sample supports it)
- `batched_turn_rate` — fraction of tool-calling turns issuing >= 2 calls
  (`BatchedTurnMinCalls`, `internal/agent/turnbatch.go:36`)
- tool-turn share — tool-calling turns / all assistant turns; this is the "narrates between
  single calls" number #5019 measured by hand (2,609 text-only vs 1,960 tool actions in a
  ~40-session sample)
- **client-suppressed rate** — turns where the request carried
  `disable_parallel_tool_use`, from the `tool_choice` child. Without this split the
  batched-turn rate cannot distinguish "model didn't batch" from "client forbade batching".
- an outcome co-series (task success / lane closure rate) so width is never read alone

Ratchet, not target:

- Record a per-lane baseline once the KPI has a stable sample.
- Alarm on a **downward** step change in `batched_turn_rate` — a regression in harness or
  prompt shape that suppresses batching (exactly the class the tool-result re-encode bug
  belongs to) should be caught automatically next time.
- Do **not** alarm on width being merely low; low width can be correct for a genuinely
  sequential task. The signal is the step change against that lane's own history.

`internal/turnbench/changepoint.go` already exists in-tree for step-change detection and is
the natural fit rather than a fresh threshold rule.

## Cost fence

If any part of this samples on a hot path rather than folding transcripts after the fact,
it goes behind `internal/turntaxmeter`'s 1-in-N `Sampler` — that package is the declared
observer-effect fence for per-turn meters, and its own doc notes the per-sample cost cap
must stay witnessed by a green test.

## Acceptance criteria

- A fleet-level view shows `batched_turn_rate` and `tool_calls_per_assistant_turn` per lane
  and per engine, with the outcome co-series alongside.
- Codex and Claude lanes are comparable on one axis (shared denominator convention with
  `internal/codexlifecycle`'s `ToolCallsPerTurn`, or a documented difference).
- A synthetic downward step in `batched_turn_rate` trips the ratchet in a test.
- The client-suppressed rate is excluded from the batching denominator.
- No hot-path meter without a sampler and a witnessed cost cap.

## Related

Part of the tool-call-width epic. Depends on the orphan-KPI child (needs a series to watch)
and on the `tool_choice` child (needs the suppression counter to keep its denominator
clean).

Parent: #5796

records.title: feat(guard): launch-time batching posture via sessionsteer, shadow-first, graded against batched_turn_rate
records.body:
## Summary

The "encourage" rung, and the last unmet acceptance criterion of
[#5019](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/5019): inject a standing
batch-independent-calls posture at launch, behind a settings knob, shadow-first, and grade
it against the `batched_turn_rate` meter rather than against a vibe.

## Why prompting is the lever

There is no API parameter that raises width. The
[parallel tool use docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/parallel-tool-use)
expose only the suppression direction (`disable_parallel_tool_use`), and note that while
Claude 4-family models have strong parallel tool use by default, the way to *increase* the
likelihood is a system-prompt instruction to invoke independent tools simultaneously in a
single block. The
[LLM-Tool Compiler](https://arxiv.org/html/2405.17438v1) result is consistent: runtime
fusion alone gives up to 4x more parallel calls, and up to **5x when combined with
prompting schemes** — prompting is additive with structural changes, not a substitute.

## Where it wires

[`cmd/fak/guard.go:1256-1273`](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/1a1151dc07/cmd/fak/guard.go#L1256-L1273)
already installs a SessionStart hook (`installGuardSessionStartHook`, `:1270`) and computes
a `sessionStartManaged` posture (`guardSessionStartManaged`, `:1267`);
`internal/sessionsteer` is the pure decision core that turns
a content-free session snapshot into a typed directive the guard hooks render as an
injected RULE. A width posture is a new directive field on that existing seam, not a new
mechanism. #5019's own open question was whether the nudge belongs in the launch preamble
or a persisted setting — `sessionsteer` answers it: put the *decision* in the pure core and
let the hook render it, so the posture is table-testable and shadow-loggable.

## Proposal

- Add a width posture to the `sessionsteer` directive: off / advisory / standing.
- Render it as a short SessionStart RULE for autonomous and grind lanes only, gated by the
  same per-launch settings path as the other launch postures.
- **Shadow first.** Emit the directive and log it without injecting, for a soak, so the
  baseline `batched_turn_rate` is measured on the same lanes that will later receive the
  nudge. A before/after where "before" is a different lane is not a comparison.
- Then enable on one grind lane and report the paired delta: `batched_turn_rate`,
  `tool_calls_per_assistant_turn`, p50 action cadence, and an outcome series.

## Wording constraints (the part that can go wrong)

#5019 flagged the real risk: a nudge strong enough to move the number can push the model to
batch calls that have genuine **data dependencies**, turning a latency win into a
correctness bug. Guard rails:

- Instruct batching of *independent* calls explicitly, and say so — not "make more tool
  calls".
- Never phrase it as a count or a quota. A model told to hit a number will pad.
- Keep it short. This text rides every turn's prefix; a long rule is a permanent token tax
  on every lane it is enabled for, which is the cost side the epic's own scaling-laws note
  (`docs/notes/SCALING-LAWS-OF-AGENTS-2026-06-19.md` §10) warns about.

## Ordering

This should land **after** the tool-result re-encode fix. Grading a prompt nudge against a
wire path that splits parallel tool results into stacked user turns — the shape the vendor
docs say degrades parallelism — would score the nudge as ineffective for a reason that has
nothing to do with the nudge.

## Acceptance criteria

- The posture is a typed field on the `sessionsteer` directive with golden-table coverage.
- Shadow mode logs the directive without injecting, and a baseline is recorded per lane.
- Enabling it is a per-launch setting, off by default, never a global.
- A paired before/after on one grind lane reports `batched_turn_rate`,
  `tool_calls_per_assistant_turn`, p50 action cadence, and an outcome series.
- A dependency-ordering check: no measured increase in tool-call retries or errors
  attributable to batching dependent calls.

## Related

Part of the tool-call-width epic; closes the last open acceptance criterion of #5019.
Depends on the orphan-KPI child (nothing to grade against otherwise) and should follow the
re-encode fix.

Parent: #5796

records.title: feat(modelaccept): grade tool-call WIDTH per turn, not just MinToolCalls per task
records.body:
## Summary

`internal/modelaccept` can already require a **total** number of tool calls for a task
(`MinToolCalls`, `internal/modelaccept/modelaccept.go:28`, gated at `:162` and validated at
`:308`). It cannot express or grade **width** — how many of those calls the model issued in
a single turn. That makes the acceptance corpus blind to the one tool-use axis the
literature says separates models on long-horizon work, and it grades the axis that is
confounded with retries.

## The gap, concretely

`examples/model-acceptance-agentic-v1.json` has tasks like:

- `multi-step-tool` — "Use the provided read-only lookup tool at least twice", `min_tool_calls: 2`
- `retry-recovery` — "Call the provided flaky read-only tool ... retry once", `min_tool_calls: 2`

Both are satisfied identically by a model that issues two calls in two serialized turns and
by a model that issues two independent calls in one turn. Those are very different
capabilities. Worse, `retry-recovery` reaching `min_tool_calls: 2` is *by construction* a
retry — so the same field is being used to encode "the model batched" and "the model
failed once and recovered", which are opposite signals.

`examples/model-acceptance-prospective-v3-report.json` makes the conflation explicit — its
`production-multi-record` task asks for both records "in **separate** tool calls" while
still grading only the count.

## Why width belongs in acceptance

- [Wide & Deep](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.07359v1) scales width (parallel calls per
  reasoning step) against depth and finds width raises accuracy *and* lowers turn count —
  62.2% with GPT-5-Medium on BrowseComp vs the 54.9% originally reported for GPT-5-High.
  Width is a capability, and it is the capability that pays.
- Provider support is genuinely uneven, so it is a real acceptance question rather than a
  formality: some model families reject `parallel_tool_calls` outright while their
  successors support it, meaning "can this model batch at all" is a routing-relevant fact
  fak should know before it pins a model to a lane.
- Volume alone misleads. A 1,440-run MCP benchmark found retry rate inflating cost 1.4-2.8x;
  models at 75% first-attempt pass reach 96-98% only with up to 3 retries. A corpus that
  rewards call count rewards the failing model.

## Proposal

Add a width axis to the task schema and the fold, kept strictly separate from the existing
volume field:

- `min_parallel_tool_calls` (or a `max_tool_turns` sibling) — a task can require that N
  independent calls arrive in ONE assistant turn, not merely N calls overall.
- Record per-run `tool_turns` alongside the existing `ToolCalls`, so the fold can derive
  calls-per-turn using the **same denominator convention** as
  `internal/agent/turnbatch.go` rather than inventing a third definition of the same ratio.
- Report width per model in the acceptance report as a first-class dimension, so
  "better models batch more" becomes a graded, reproducible claim about *this* corpus
  instead of an inherited assumption.
- Add at least one genuinely parallel-friendly task: two independent lookups with **no**
  data dependency, where a one-turn solution is strictly better and the corpus can tell.

Keep `MinToolCalls` as-is for the retry/recovery tasks where total count is the right
question. The point is to stop one field carrying two meanings.

## Acceptance criteria

- A task can declare a per-turn width requirement, validated the way `MinToolCalls` is
  (`:308` rejects a width requirement without `tool_required`).
- The report carries a per-model width figure using `turnbatch`'s denominator convention.
- A corpus task exists whose independent-calls-in-one-turn solution is distinguishable from
  the serialized solution, and the fold distinguishes them (table test with both run shapes).
- Existing corpora keep their current verdicts (the new field is additive and optional).

## Related

Part of the tool-call-width epic. Shares the width definition with the orphan-KPI child —
those two should agree on the denominator, or the fleet meter and the acceptance grade will
disagree about the same model.

Parent: #5796

records.title: fix(cmd): print the freshness/supersession rung in the feature-query text render (residual of #3163)
records.body:
## The gap

`FeatureCard.Freshness` ships (#3163) and is emitted on `--json` / `fak_feature_query`, but the **default human table never prints it**. `cmd/fak/feature.go:93` renders five columns — `Name`, `Kind`, `Effect`, `Source`, `Summary` — and drops `c.Freshness` entirely.

So #3163's own *"First checkable step"* (**"compute *and print* `SUPERSEDED_BY`"**) is met on the machine surfaces and unmet on the operator surface.

## Witness (same query, two surfaces)

```console
$ fak feature query "field borrow query quality" --limit 40 --json
"name":      "doc:Borrow scout: lmnr (Laminar) -> fak (2026-07-09)",
"freshness": "SUPERSEDED_BY:doc:Borrow scout: lmnr (Laminar) -> fak - deep re-study (2026-07-10)",

$ fak feature query "field borrow query quality" --limit 40
doc:Borrow scout: lmnr (Laminar) -> fak (2026-07-09)
   dev-doc   read   devindex   a `field-borrow` pass over Laminar's ...
```

The rung is present in one and absent in the other.

## Scope

- Surface `Freshness` in the text render — a sixth column, or a suffix/marker on superseded and stale rows (the rung string can be long, so a compact marker plus the full value in `--json` is acceptable).
- One exact-output render test pinning a `SUPERSEDED_BY` row and a `STALE` row.

## Non-goals

- No ranking change. The rung stays advisory: never re-order, never drop a card (#3163's fence).
- No new freshness computation — `freshnessByKey` / `stalenessByKey` already produce the value; this is render-only.
- Not the push/INVALIDATE half (#3326), not the `supersedes:` front-matter edge, not `Resolved by <sha>`.

## Routing

- Lane: **cmd** (`cmd/fak/feature.go`). Filed separately from #3163 because #3163 routed to the `docs` lane, and a render fix under a `(fak docs)` stamp would not diff-witness.
- Parent: #3163 (rung), epic #1494 (self-use of the query + memory surface).
- Background: `docs/notes/SELFQUERY-CARD-FRESHNESS-3163-TRIAGE-2026-08-06.md` (what shipped, what remains, the two-freshness-axis disambiguation).

records.title: Micro-context cache observability: controlled warm/cold prefix rerun
records.body:
## Parent context
#5785; follow-up to #5787 and input to #5792.

## Problem
The first real endpoint reported `cached_prompt_tokens=0`, exposed no prefix lookup/fill counters, and had no provider-native chat batch endpoint. Near parity therefore cannot distinguish no cache from an unobservable cache path.

## Done condition
- Add a controlled endpoint mode with explicit prefix lookup, fill, eviction, and miss-reason counters.
- Provide deterministic cold reset and warm-preserve controls and record the base fingerprint.
- Attribute cached tokens to endpoint-native evidence rather than prompt similarity.
- Rerun unique, shared-cold, shared-warm, concurrent, and tuned-sequential arms under one declared model/hardware/config.
- Report TTFT, prefill/decode, queue tax, useful completions/time, RAM/KV, and every cache event without blending orchestration concurrency into cache benefit.

## Witness
A scrubbed artifact plus verifier reconciles request-level cached-token provenance with endpoint cache counters and `fak claim-check` grades any cache gain against the tuned baseline. A null result is acceptable and must remain `not-yet` rather than a gain claim.

## Work estimate
Estimate: 5 points. Uncertainty: operator-supplied estimate; revise through the parent denominator when evidence changes.

## Overall completion contribution
Contribution: 5/50 points.

## Completion standard
research

  62.2% with GPT-5-Medium on BrowseComp vs the 54.9% originally reported for GPT-5-High.
  Width is a capability, and it is the capability that pays.
- Provider support is genuinely uneven, so it is a real acceptance question rather than a
  formality: some model families reject `parallel_tool_calls` outright while their
  successors support it, meaning "can this model batch at all" is a routing-relevant fact
  fak should know before it pins a model to a lane.
- Volume alone misleads. A 1,440-run MCP benchmark found retry rate inflating cost 1.4-2.8x;
  models at 75% first-attempt pass reach 96-98% only with up to 3 retries. A corpus that
  rewards call count rewards the failing model.

## Proposal

Add a width axis to the task schema and the fold, kept strictly separate from the existing
volume field:

- `min_parallel_tool_calls` (or a `max_tool_turns` sibling) — a task can require that N
  independent calls arrive in ONE assistant turn, not merely N calls overall.
- Record per-run `tool_turns` alongside the existing `ToolCalls`, so the fold can derive
  calls-per-turn using the **same denominator convention** as
  `internal/agent/turnbatch.go` rather than inventing a third definition of the same ratio.
- Report width per model in the acceptance report as a first-class dimension, so
  "better models batch more" becomes a graded, reproducible claim about *this* corpus
  instead of an inherited assumption.
- Add at least one genuinely parallel-friendly task: two independent lookups with **no**
  data dependency, where a one-turn solution is strictly better and the corpus can tell.

Keep `MinToolCalls` as-is for the retry/recovery tasks where total count is the right
question. The point is to stop one field carrying two meanings.

## Acceptance criteria

- A task can declare a per-turn width requirement, validated the way `MinToolCalls` is
  (`:308` rejects a width requirement without `tool_required`).
- The report carries a per-model width figure using `turnbatch`'s denominator convention.
- A corpus task exists whose independent-calls-in-one-turn solution is distinguishable from
  the serialized solution, and the fold distinguishes them (table test with both run shapes).
- Existing corpora keep their current verdicts (the new field is additive and optional).

## Related

Part of the tool-call-width epic. Shares the width definition with the orphan-KPI child —
those two should agree on the denominator, or the fleet meter and the acceptance grade will
disagree about the same model.

## Purpose
Productize the zero-adoption launch spine shipped in `cmd/fak@43a1c0ec03a0`: users keep typing `claude`/`codex`, or bare `fak`, while retaining a reliable and obvious direct escape.

## Scope
Track the remaining platform activation, provider extensibility, diagnostics, upgrade durability, telemetry, and acceptance work. The first-class TUI toggle is already tracked separately in #5784.

## Done
- Every child issue has an executable done condition and independent witness.
- Claude and Codex shims are installable, diagnosable, bypassable, and removable on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
- Install/update/uninstall cannot lose the recorded underlying provider command or create shim recursion.
- Adoption and bypass behavior are documented and measured without recording prompts or provider arguments.

## Spine witness
`fak launch install|uninstall|default|enable|disable|status`, bare-`fak` dispatch, and direct escapes shipped at `cmd/fak@43a1c0ec03a0`.

## Leak check
Public product behavior only; no credentials, private infrastructure, prompts, or local user paths belong in issue evidence.

## Follow-on tickets

records.title: launchshim: activate shim PATH automatically and reversibly
records.body:
## Parent
#5808 — zero-adoption provider launch productization.

## Problem
`fak launch install` writes safe shims but currently tells users to prepend the shim directory to `PATH`. That remaining manual step defeats the zero-adoption promise and differs across PowerShell, cmd.exe, bash, zsh, and fish.

## Done
- Install offers an idempotent automatic activation path for supported shells/OSes, preserving user-owned startup-file content byte-for-byte outside a clearly delimited fak block.
- The current process receives a copy/paste command when automatic mutation cannot affect it immediately.
- Uninstall removes only fak-owned activation and is a no-op when already absent.
- Repeated install/uninstall/install converges without duplicate PATH entries.
- Captured Windows PowerShell plus macOS/Linux POSIX-shell witnesses prove a fresh shell resolves `claude` and `codex` to the fak shim and direct bypass still reaches the recorded provider.
- `--no-path` retains the current managed/manual-install behavior.

## Failure witness
Tests cover read-only startup files, paths containing spaces, absent startup files, and pre-existing user edits around the managed block.

## Leak check
Fixtures use synthetic homes and paths; no real usernames or provider credentials.

records.title: launchshim: harden cross-platform install and recursion refusal
records.body:
## Parent
#5808 — zero-adoption provider launch productization.

## Problem
The shim installer relies on `exec.LookPath` and a same-directory check. PATH aliases, symlinks, `.cmd`/`.exe` resolution, stale recorded paths, and repeated installs can still produce an indirect shim-to-shim loop or platform-specific breakage.

## Done
- Resolve and persist a canonical underlying provider identity on Windows, macOS, and Linux, including symlink and PATHEXT cases.
- Refuse install when the only discovered provider transitively resolves back to the fak shim, with a named recovery action.
- Atomic config writes preserve the last known-good config under process races and injected write/rename failures.
- Status identifies missing, moved, non-executable, and recursive underlying commands without launching them.
- An install→guarded launch→direct launch→uninstall acceptance matrix runs for Claude and Codex on all three OS families in CI or sanctioned nodes.
- Race and adversarial tests fail before the hardening and pass after it.

## Leak check
Diagnostics may show scrubbed/basename paths by default; JSON evidence must not publish home-directory PII.

## Parent

The shipped spine hardcodes `claude` and `codex`. Users also need another shortcut/default provider without waiting for a new binary release, while preserving safe argument boundaries and direct pass-through.

records.title: launchshim: preserve shims and provider bindings across fak upgrades
records.body:
## Parent
#5808 — zero-adoption provider launch productization.

## Problem
A fak self-update or package-manager replacement can move/replace the binary while generated shims contain an absolute fak path. Provider upgrades can likewise move the recorded underlying executable. Zero adoption must survive routine upgrades without silent bypass or breakage.

## Done
- Define and implement an upgrade-safe shim target strategy for installer, `go install`, archive installs, and `fak self-update`.
- After fak moves or is replaced, doctor repairs or offers one deterministic repair command without rediscovering the shim as the provider.
- Provider-path movement is detected and can be rebound only to a non-shim executable with explicit evidence.
- Config schema carries a version and has forward/backward migration tests from the shipped v1 shape.
- Acceptance tests simulate fak binary replacement and provider replacement, then prove guarded and direct launches still reach the intended executables.
- Rollback to the previous fak binary preserves a usable direct escape.

## Leak check
Migration logs and tests use synthetic paths and never serialize provider arguments or credentials.

records.title: launchshim: measure guarded/direct adoption with privacy-safe counters
records.body:
## Parent
#5808 — zero-adoption provider launch productization.

## Problem
The feature promises zero-adoption use, but there is no evidence showing shim launches, bare-fak launches, guarded launches, direct escapes, failures, or disable duration. Raw argv must not enter telemetry.

A dedicated leak test scans the complete emitted ledger and rendered JSON for prompt, secret, path, and argument canaries.

records.title: feat(gateway): give fak_read and the per-item MCP verbs a batch axis so width is expressible
records.body:
## Summary

The epic names three levers for raising tool-call width. Two have children (message-history
shape #5797, system-prompt posture #5801). The third — **batch-capable tool schemas** — has
none, and it is the lever with the largest measured effect in the literature.

fak's own MCP surface currently makes width *inexpressible* for its most-used verb: every
per-item tool takes exactly one item.

## Current state

Across the ~22 tools the gateway advertises (`internal/gateway/mcp.go:600-760`), exactly one
declares an array parameter — `fak_session_reset.messages`, which is a transcript payload,
not a batch axis. Every per-item verb is strictly singular:

- `fak_read` — `{"file_path": {"type":"string"}}`, `"required": ["file_path"]`
  (`internal/gateway/mcp.go:612-621`; engine at `internal/agent/readengine.go:77`)
- `fak_admit` — `"required": ["tool"]`, one tool per call
- `fak_revoke` — `"required": ["witness"]`, one witness per call

So an agent that wants to read five files through the kernel must issue five separate
`fak_read` calls. It can only express that as *width* if the harness happens to batch them
into one assistant turn — and per #5797 the wire path then splits the results back apart
anyway.

## Why this is the highest-leverage of the three levers

The [LLM-Tool Compiler](https://arxiv.org/html/2405.17438v1) fuses similar tool operations
into a single function at runtime and presents them to the model as one unified task. On a
large-scale Copilot deployment that yielded **up to 4x more parallel calls**, with token
cost down ~40% and latency down ~12% — and **up to 5x** more parallel calls when combined
with prompting schemes. The mechanism is exactly the gap above: the model cannot batch what
the schema cannot express, and a fused schema lets it batch without having to plan a DAG.

There is a second, fak-specific reason this verb in particular. `fak_read` exists to serve
verified-fresh cache hits without touching disk (`internal/agent/readengine.go:13-24`) —
which means the multi-file read is precisely the case where the kernel's cache advantage
compounds, and precisely the case the current schema forces into N round trips. The tool
whose value is highest at batch size N is the one capped at N=1.

## Proposal

- Add a batch axis to the per-item verbs, starting with `fak_read`: accept `file_paths`
  (array) alongside `file_path` (string), returning results in request order with per-item
  errors rather than failing the whole call. Keep the singular form working — this is
  additive, and an existing single-path caller must not change behaviour.
- Do the same for `fak_admit` where the kernel already has a batch decision path
  (`BatchDecide` is referenced by `internal/fusedturn` as the real default-deny floor), so
  the tool surface stops being narrower than the kernel underneath it.
- Preserve adjudication semantics **per item**: a batch call is N adjudications, not one.
  A batch must never become a way to smuggle an un-adjudicated item past the floor, and a
  single refused item must not silently drop the rest. This is the load-bearing safety
  property of the change and deserves its own test.
- Update the tool descriptions to say the batch form is preferred for independent items —
  the description text is itself part of the width nudge, and it is the one place a nudge
  costs no per-turn prefix tokens on lanes that never call the tool.

## Interaction with the other children

- Complements #5801 rather than duplicating it. The LLM-Tool Compiler result is that
  schema fusion and prompting are **additive** (4x alone, 5x combined), so both should land
  and be measured separately or neither delta is attributable.
- Changes what #5799/#5800 are measuring, and they should know: a batched `fak_read`
  *lowers* raw tool-call count while *raising* useful work per call. That is the one case
  where the width KPI and the goal genuinely diverge, so the monitor needs an items-per-call
  notion or a fused call will read as a regression.

## Acceptance criteria

- `fak_read` accepts an array of paths and returns per-item results in request order, with
  per-item errors; the single-path form is unchanged.
- Each item in a batch is adjudicated independently; a test proves a batch containing one
  refused item refuses exactly that item and still serves the rest.
- Cache semantics hold per item (a batch of 5 where 3 are verified-fresh does 2 disk reads).
- The monitor in #5800 can distinguish "one call doing 5 items" from "one call doing 1 item"
  so fusion does not read as a width regression.

## Related

Part of the tool-call-width epic (#5796) — the third lever, previously unticketed.

records.title: Micro-context S2b: witness shared-prefix cache benefit on a cache-observable controlled kernel
records.body:
## Parent context
Epic #5785 — micro-context fabric for 100–10,000 parallel agents. Research contract: `docs/research/micro-context-fabrics.md`. Direct follow-on to S2 (#5787).

## Current state
- S2's shared-prefix A/B on the first real endpoint observed **zero cache benefit**: 0 billed cached tokens, no cache metric exposed, `/v1/batches` 404; `claim_verdict: not-yet` (`docs/research/micro-context-s2-prefix-ab.md`). The 1.36× concurrency gain was retained as a separate, honest claim.
- The program's central agentic-cache-benefit claim is therefore unwitnessed anywhere, in either direction.
- fak controls cache-observable serving seams that were never connected to this spine: `internal/radixkv` prefix-reuse counters (exercised by `cmd/radixbench`), the vLLM V1 adapter's exact-span KV governance (`docs/serving/vllm-v1-adapter.md`), and the in-kernel engine (`docs/fak/in-kernel-model.md`).

## Why this is next
The epic's premise is that one immutable cached base amortizes prefill across many delta contexts. Until an endpoint that can *see* its prefix cache runs the A/B, the premise has no witness. This is the highest-leverage missing measurement in the program.

## Working spine
The shipped S2 A/B harness (`cmd/microcontextdemo` prefix A/B mode, commit 09e20bc3f2) and `go run ./cmd/microcontextdemo -selfcheck` (passing 2026-08-06).

## In scope
- Run the same unique-full-prompts vs one-base-plus-deltas A/B against a fak-controlled, cache-observable endpoint (in-kernel engine with `radixkv` counters, or the vLLM V1 adapter with KV events).
- Capture kernel-side cache hit/miss counts, prefill tokens saved, TTFT and throughput deltas, alongside the usage-derived view.
- Include tuned-sequential and provider-native batching baselines per the measurement contract.
- Publish the verdict either way — a witnessed negative is a valid result.

## Out of scope
- API-only providers (#5793); folding results into the cache-value P&L (separate issue); scheduler changes.

## Done condition
A captured A/B witness doc `docs/research/micro-context-s2b-kernel-cache-ab.md` reports kernel-observed prefix-cache evidence for the shared-base path, with baselines, and the S2 `not-yet` cache verdict is superseded by a witnessed verdict.

## Witness

## Acceptance gate
- `go run ./cmd/microcontextdemo -selfcheck -contexts 1000 -workers 16` exits 0 (regression floor).
- The captured A/B ledger passes its verify counterpart (ships with this issue).

- The resolving commit cites this issue and ends its subject with `(fak microcontextdemo)`.

- `internal/radixkv/`
- `docs/research/`

leaf

4. Ship the verify counterpart and witness doc; supersede the S2 verdict.

records.title: Fold witnessed micro-context shared-base reuse into the cache-value Track-1 P&L
records.body:
## Parent context
Epic #5785 — micro-context fabric. Research contract: `docs/research/micro-context-fabrics.md`. Consumes the S2b kernel cache witness (filed alongside this issue).

## Current state
- `internal/cachevaluereport` maintains the two-track cache P&L (Track 1 WITNESSED kernel reuse vs Track 2 OBSERVED provider $) with a provenance fence; `fak cachevalue feed|weekly|savings|status` render it.
- The micro-context program produces cache-relevant evidence (one shared base install, per-context delta reuse, `base_fingerprint` in the S0 witness JSON) but nothing feeds the P&L; the fabric's cache benefit is invisible to the fleet report.
