records.title: fix(serve): a fleetbus lifecycle no-op is counted as Affected, so a resume over an already-running fleet acks "11/11 took it"
records.body:
_Parent epic: #5599 — the fleet control bus. Spine: #5600 (closed, landed `bb2401e7a5`)._

## Current state

`Outcome.Affected` on a fanned lifecycle op counts sessions the selector **matched and did not
refuse** — not sessions whose run state actually changed. A no-op write (resume a Running session,
pause a Paused one) is counted as an apply and reported with the word "took it".

The applier loop, `cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus.go:216-229`:

```go
applied := 0
for _, traceID := range matched {
	st, took := a.tbl.Transition(traceID, run, reason)
	if !took {
		continue
	}
	...
	applied++
}
```

`took` is not a changed-flag. `internal/session/table.go:233-268` returns `false` for exactly one
case — a terminal session:

```go
func (t *Table) Transition(trace string, to RunState, reason string) (State, bool) {
	t.mu.Lock()
	cur := t.getLocked(trace)
	if cur.Run.terminal() {
		t.mu.Unlock()
		return cur, false // a stopped session is terminal; refuse to revive it
	}
	from := cur.Run
	cur.Run = to
	...
	return out, true
}
```

`from == to` runs the whole body and returns `true`. Nothing downstream distinguishes the two: the
table's own observer already does, at `internal/session/observe.go:293-302` —
`notableTransition` returns `false` when `from == to`, and `Running` is not in the notable set at
all — so a fanned `resume` over an already-Running fleet fires **zero** transition events while the
ack claims every session took it.

That `applied` becomes both the wording and the count,
`cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus.go:234-245`:

```go
out := fleetbus.OutcomeApplied(
	fmt.Sprintf("%s: %d/%d session(s) took it and reached the durable mirror", op, applied, len(matched)),
	applied)
```

and surfaces verbatim to the operator at `cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:337` (`affected=%d`) and
`:350-351` (`affected=%d` total). Live witness: `fak fleet control send --op resume --all` on an
instance whose 11 sessions were all already `Running` printed
`affected=11 resume: 11/11 session(s) took it` and exited 0, with no `-> running` transition in the
serve log — because there were none to log.

The bus's own contract says this field means something stronger.
`internal/fleetbus/fleetbus.go:648-654`: *"Witness is what the instance actually observed change"*
and *"Affected is how many local subjects the op landed on."* The package doc at
`cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus.go:19-23` is blunter: *"The ack reports what was OBSERVED, never what was
enqueued … Affected counts the sessions it landed on."*

## Why this is next

This is the same failure the spine was built to refuse, one level in. #5600's commit message names
a fleet-wide *"4 of 4 applied, 0 affected"* as "the accepted-but-never-applied phantom wearing a
success token", and the file's own doc calls that shape out by name. The overcount is that phantom
with the numbers inverted: instead of a hollow apply with an honest zero, it is a hollow apply
wearing a **full** count. It is strictly worse, because a zero invites a second look and an
`11/11` closes the question.

Downstream consumers read `AffectedTotal` as a fleet-wide effect measure
(`cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:350-351`), so a control loop that gates on "did the fleet move" gets a
confident yes from a fleet that did not move. Every other #5599 child (durability #5639, tagging
#5640, gateway routing #5638) makes the apply path *reach further*; none of them makes the count
*true*, and each one that lands widens the blast radius of a count that is not.

## Working spine

The applier already loops per session and already has both states in hand — `a.tbl.Transition`
returns the resulting `State`, and the pre-write run state is readable from the same snapshot
`matchedSessions` walked. Splitting `applied` into *changed* vs *already-in-state* is a local
change inside `applyLifecycle`; the ack schema already has the two fields needed (`Affected` for
the count, `Witness`/`Detail` for the wording).

## In scope

- `applyLifecycle` (`cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus.go:203-246`) distinguishes a run-state **change** from
  a no-op write, and sets `Affected` to the change count only.
- The detail string stops asserting "took it" for sessions that were already in the target state;
  it reports both numbers (e.g. changed vs already-there) so a no-op fan is legible rather than
  silent.
- The all-no-op case stays `applied` (the instance heard it and it is already true) — it must not
  become a refusal, and its `Affected` must be `0`, which
  `internal/fleetbus/fleetbus.go:651-654` already documents as a legal outcome.
- Regression test covering: all-no-op, all-changed, and a mixed batch.

## Out of scope

- Changing `session.Table.Transition`'s signature or its `(State, bool)` contract. Other callers
  read `bool` as "not terminal" and that meaning is correct for them; the fix belongs at the
  counting site.
- The `steer` path (`cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus.go:148-195`). Its count is per-send and already
  reflects delivery, not state.
- The stale doc comment at `cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus.go:197-202` claiming lifecycle "goes through
  `sessionctl.Broadcast`" when the code fans directly — a separate cleanup leaf.
- `applyGwBus` (`cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus.go:102-117`), which already reports `changed` correctly:
  `0` for `gateway-route-unchanged`, `1` for `gateway-route-reloaded`. It is the shape to copy.

## Done condition

Fanning a lifecycle op at a set of sessions already in the target run state yields
`Outcome.Status == applied` with `Outcome.Affected == 0`, and a detail string that does not claim
those sessions "took it"; fanning at a mixed set yields `Affected` equal to the number whose
`session.State.Run` differed before the write, strictly less than `len(matched)`.

## Witness

`go test ./cmd/fak -run 'TestFleetBusLifecycleNoOpNotAffected' -count=1` — a new test seeding a
`session.Table` with N `Running` traces, applying
`fleetbus.Directive{Op: "resume", Selector: fleetbus.Selector{All: true}}` through
`fleetBusApplier.Apply`, and asserting `out.Status == fleetbus.AckApplied && out.Affected == 0`
plus `!strings.Contains(out.Detail, "took it")`. A second arm pauses one of the N first and asserts
`out.Affected == 1` against `matched == N`.

Today that test fails with `affected=N`.

## Acceptance gate

The new test passes; `go test ./cmd/fak -run 'FleetBus' -count=1` and
`go test ./internal/fleetbus ./internal/session ./internal/sessionctl -count=1` stay green,
including the durability arms added by #5639 (`cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus_durable_test.go`) and the
gateway arms from #5638 (`cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus_gateway_test.go`). The existing assertions at
`cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus_test.go:223` and `:244` (applied/2 and applied/1 over sessions that do
change state) must keep their current counts unchanged — the fix must narrow only the no-op case.
An all-no-op fan must remain `applied`, never `FLEETBUS_APPLY_REFUSED`.

## Dependencies

None blocking. Lands on top of #5638 / #5639 / #5640, all closed. Touches the same function #5639
made durable, so it should land after that commit (`df6b27a38d`) — it already has.

## Confusion risks

- **`took` is not `changed`.** `internal/session/table.go:236-239` shows the only `false` is
  terminal. Reading that bool as "the write mattered" is the whole bug.
- **Zero-affected is not a failure.** `internal/fleetbus/fleetbus.go:651-654` explicitly blesses a
  zero-affected applied ack. Converting the all-no-op case into a refusal would trade an overcount
  for a false alarm, and `Fold`'s refused tally would then red on a fleet that is exactly where the
  operator asked it to be.
- **Do not fix this by re-reading the table after the write.** A concurrent turn can move the state
  between the write and the read; the pre-write run state must come from the same read the
  transition made, or from a snapshot captured before the loop.
- **`Terminating` and `Draining` are not no-ops when re-applied** in the same sense as `Running` —
  check the actual `from`/`to` pair rather than special-casing `resume`.

## Likely files

`cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus.go`, `cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus_test.go`, `internal/session/table.go` (read
only — the observer precedent at `internal/session/observe.go:293-302`), `cmd/fak/fleet_control.go`
(operator-facing rendering)

```routing
lane: cmd
paths: cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus*.go
expected_steps: read pre-write run state in applyLifecycle; count changes not writes; reword the detail; add the no-op/mixed test; keep the all-no-op case applied
```

## Parent context

**#5599** — the fleet control bus epic; the spine is **#5600** (closed, landed `bb2401e7a5`). This
leaf is a correctness fix to the ack that spine defined and is dispatchable on its own.

## Work unit

leaf

## Work scale

S1

## Expected steps

4

## Assumptions

The pre-write run state is readable from the same snapshot `matchedSessions` already walks, so
counting changes needs no second read of the table (if it is not, the loop must capture `from`
before the write rather than re-reading after it — the concurrency hazard named in
**Confusion risks**).

No consumer depends on `Affected` meaning "matched". Checked at HEAD: the only readers are the two
renderers at `cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:337` and `:350-351`. If a later control loop starts gating on
the field, it wants the narrowed meaning, not the current one.

## Coordination notes

Lane `cmd`. `cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus.go` is the same file #5638, #5639 and #5640 each landed in, so
take the lane lease before editing and re-read HEAD first — those three are closed but the file is
active. `internal/session/table.go` is read-only for this leaf; do not change `Transition`'s
signature, since other callers read its bool correctly.

This leaf and #5825 both touch the fleetbus applier's blast radius from different sides (what it
counts vs which sessions it reaches). They do not overlap in code and can land in either order.

## Trigger

Filed from a live operator run at HEAD (2026-08-05): `fak fleet control send --op resume --all`
reported `affected=11 resume: 11/11 session(s) took it` and exit 0 against a fleet whose sessions
were all already `Running`, with zero transitions recorded in the serve log. The grounding lines in
**Current state** were re-confirmed at HEAD after #5637-#5640 landed.

## Batch policy

One issue per defect — this is not part of a batch. A duplicate scan of the existing open backlog
found no issue covering the `Affected` count; the dedupe marker is `Outcome.Affected` +
`serve_fleetbus.go`. If a related fix lands first, update this issue rather than filing a second
one.

## Closure binding

Closes on a commit stamped `(fak cmd)` making `Outcome.Affected` count run-state changes rather
than non-terminal writes, with `TestFleetBusLifecycleNoOpNotAffected` green and the existing
`cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus_test.go` counts unchanged.

- **Required model tier:** T2
- **Optimal model tier:** T2

### Related

#5599 (epic parent), #5600 (spine), #5639, #5638, #5640

records.title: fix(fleetbus): a retained directive still applies to instances that boot after the operator's exit 0, so terminate/pause keeps acting on a report already closed
records.body:
_Parent epic: #5599 — centralized fleet control, one control point / N instances._

## Current state

`fleetbus.Drain` decides what to apply with exactly one filter — the selector —
`internal/fleetbus/drain.go:101-108`:

```go
for _, d := range directives {
	rep.Seen++
	if !d.Selector.MatchesInstance(self) {
		continue
	}
	rep.Matched++

	fresh, err := b.ClaimApply(self.ID, d.ID)
```

`grep -c Targets internal/fleetbus/drain.go` is **0**. The publish-time target set
(`Directive.Targets`, `internal/fleetbus/fleetbus.go:494`) is stamped by the control point
(`cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:150`) and is read only by the fold as a denominator floor
(`internal/fleetbus/fold.go:104-106`). The drain side never consults it, and nothing compares the
instance's boot instant against `d.IssuedUTC` — `Instance` carries no start-time field at all
(`internal/fleetbus/fleetbus.go:336-369`; `SeenUTC` is re-stamped on every announce,
`cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus.go:394`).

Meanwhile the control point exits **0** the moment the publish-time set has all acked applied
(`cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:313-316`) and prints
`applied — all N addressed instance(s) witnessed it` (`cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:369`). The
directive stays in the log until its TTL, which defaults to **5 minutes** and is `0 = never
expires` (`cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:89`).

So a process that boots *after* that exit 0 still matches `--all` / `--machine` / `--role`, still
gets a `fresh` claim (a restarted serve is a **new** bus id — host+pid,
`cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus.go:437-439`), and applies. With a lifecycle op and no session axis,
`applyLifecycle` fans over **every live session on the instance**
(`cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus.go:197-201`) — sessions that did not exist when the operator issued the
command.

Measured at HEAD with a scratch probe against `internal/fleetbus` (`ApplierFunc` counting calls):

```
targets stamped at publish = [serve-box-1000]
operator fold: complete=true applied=1 targeted=1 -> exit0=true
late boot drain: seen=1 matched=1 applied=1 refused=0 expired=0; applier calls total=2
late boot is in publish-time Targets? false
72h-later boot, ttl=0 directive: matched=2 applied=1 expired=1
```

The second applier call happened 60s after the operator's exit 0, on an instance the selector had
never resolved to. With `--ttl 0` the same thing happens 72 hours later.

## Why this is next

This is the package's own stated failure mode arriving through the back door.
`internal/fleetbus/fleetbus.go:516-519` refuses a negative TTL precisely because it would produce
"an unbounded directive that **every instance joining the bus for the rest of the log's life**
still applies… the exact 'stale `go` applied an hour later' the TTL exists to prevent." That fence
holds for `-5m`; it does not hold for the ordinary `--ttl 5m` publish, where the same
join-late-and-apply path is open for the whole window, and it does not hold at all for the
documented `--ttl 0`.

The consequence is asymmetric with the rest of the design. Everywhere else the bus refuses to let a
report be more confident than the evidence (`RowOutstanding`, `fold.go:16-20`; the denominator floor,
`fold.go:89-102`; `FLEETBUS_NO_TARGET` at the edge, `fleet_control.go:141-145`). Here the report is
*complete and correct* — and the fleet keeps changing state behind it. `terminate` and `pause` are
in the fannable set (`serve_fleetbus.go:134-136`), so the concrete outcome is a serve that comes up,
re-attaches its sessions, and immediately kills or parks them for a command whose report the
operator closed.

## Working spine

`Drain` gains a second admission test alongside the selector: a directive that recorded a
publish-time target set is applyable only by an instance that was in it. Instances that were not
addressed at publish either skip silently (the same silence the package already documents for a
non-matching directive, `drain.go:78-81`) or ack a closed refusal — whichever keeps the fold's
arithmetic honest. Directives with no `Targets` (published before the field existed) keep today's
selector-only behaviour, matching the fold's own back-compat rule at `fold.go:100-102`.

## In scope

- The admission test in `fleetbus.Drain`, driven by `Directive.Targets`.
- Reconciling this with the fold's deliberate "a fleet grows mid-fan-out" rule
  (`internal/fleetbus/fold.go:108-110`, `cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:160-163`), which today adds any
  newly-announced matching instance to the denominator. Both halves must agree on one answer for
  "is a process that announced after the publish addressed?" — today drain says yes and the
  operator's exit code says the question is closed.
- If the chosen answer needs a time comparison rather than the target list, the presence record
  needs a real start instant (`SeenUTC` cannot serve: it is re-stamped every announce).
- Back-compat arm: an empty `Targets` must not stop old directives from draining.
- A `fak fleet control` doc/help note stating exactly how long after a send a late boot can still be
  reached, since `--ttl` is the only control today.

## Out of scope

- Changing the default `--ttl` or removing `--ttl 0`. The window is a symptom; the missing
  admission test is the defect.
- Directive revocation / cancel-after-send. That is a separate capability, not a fix to this one.
- Pruning the directive log. `Directives()` deliberately returns expired records so a drainer can
  ack them expired (`internal/fleetbus/dirbus.go:36-38`).
- The cross-host transports and the capability floor — named children of #5599.

## Done condition

An instance whose id is absent from a directive's non-empty `Directive.Targets` completes a drain
pass over that directive with `Applied == 0` and the applier never invoked, while an instance named
in `Targets` still applies it; a directive carrying an empty `Targets` still applies to every
selector match, and `Fold` over the resulting acks still partitions `Targeted` exactly
(`Applied + Refused + Expired + Outstanding == Targeted`).

## Witness

`go test ./internal/fleetbus -run 'TestDrainLateBoot'` — a new test that publishes an `--all`
directive with `WithTargets` naming one live instance, drains it there, folds to
`Complete && Applied == Targeted` (the exit-0 condition at `cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:313`), then
announces a second instance and drains as it: the assertion is that the applier call count does not
increase. A second arm publishes with `Targets` empty and asserts the late instance DOES apply
(back-compat).

## Acceptance gate

`go test ./internal/fleetbus` green, including the existing `drain_test.go`, `fold_test.go` and
`e2e_process_test.go` suites; `go test ./cmd/fak -run 'TestFleetControl|TestServeFleetBus'` green;
and the fold arithmetic invariant `Applied+Refused+Expired+Outstanding == Targeted` still holds for
every arm of the new test.

## Dependencies

None blocking. Sits on the spine landed in `bb2401e7a5` (#5600) and on the `Targets` field that
spine already ships. Touches the same drain path as #5639, which is closed.

## Confusion risks

- **The TTL is not this fence.** A short TTL narrows the window; it never closes it, and `--ttl 0`
  is documented as legal. Fixing this by shortening the default would be the appearance of a fix.
- **`Targets` is currently fold-only.** `fold.go:89-102` explains why it exists as a *denominator
  floor*; using it as an *admission list* is a new meaning for the same field and must be documented
  as such, or a future reader will assume the fold semantics apply.
- **The "fleet grows mid-fan-out" rule is deliberate**, not an oversight — see
  `cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:160-163`. This issue is not a claim that rule is wrong; it is a claim
  that the rule and the exit-0 contract currently disagree, and only one of them can be right.
- **A restart is a new bus identity.** `defaultFleetBusInstanceID` is host+pid
  (`cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus.go:437-439`), so the at-most-once claim in
  `internal/fleetbus/dirbus.go:268-284` does not dedupe across a restart — by design, and that is
  what makes this reachable.
- **Explicit `--instance` selectors are already safe.** Only `--all` / `--machine` / `--role` (and
  the `--model` / `--zone` axes from #5637) leak, so a repro must use one of those.

## Likely files

`internal/fleetbus/drain.go`, `internal/fleetbus/fleetbus.go`, `internal/fleetbus/fold.go`,
`internal/fleetbus/drain_test.go`, `cmd/fak/fleet_control.go`, `cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus.go`

```routing
lane: fleetbus
paths: internal/fleetbus/drain.go, internal/fleetbus/fleetbus.go, internal/fleetbus/drain_test.go
expected_steps: add the Targets admission test to Drain; reconcile with the fold's late-announce rule; back-compat arm for empty Targets; new TestDrainLateBoot; doc the reachable window in fleet control help
```

## Parent context

**#5599** — the centralized fleet control epic. The spine (#5600) landed `bb2401e7a5` and shipped
both `Drain` and `Directive.Targets`; this leaf closes the gap between them and is dispatchable on
its own.

## Work unit

leaf

## Work scale

S1

## Expected steps

5

## Assumptions

A directive is meant to address the roster that is live at PUBLISH time. That is what the stamped
`Targets` field exists for (`internal/fleetbus/fleetbus.go:494`, stamped at
`cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:150`) and what the operator's exit-0 verdict claims. If the intended
semantic is instead "anyone who sees it before the TTL expires", then the code is right and the
verdict wording plus the `--ttl` help are what must change — decide which before writing the fix.

Retention itself is still wanted: a live instance that is briefly unreachable must still get the
directive. This leaf narrows WHO a retained directive applies to, not whether retention exists.

## Coordination notes

Lane `fleetbus`. `internal/fleetbus/drain.go` and the `Directive`/`Instance` records in
`internal/fleetbus/fleetbus.go`. Coordinates with #5824: both concern which instances a directive
legitimately reaches, and #5824 changes the instance identity this leaf's filter would key on. If
both are in flight, land #5824 first so the boot-time comparison is written against the final
identity.

## Trigger

Filed from a HEAD verification pass (2026-08-06) over the post-#5600 fleetbus code, after #5637 /
#5638 / #5639 / #5640 landed. The probe output in **Current state** was measured against
`internal/fleetbus` at `3a1b7320f0`; the scratch test file was removed after running.

## Batch policy

One issue per defect — not batched. A duplicate scan of the existing open backlog found no issue
covering late-boot application; the dedupe marker is `drain.go` + `MatchesInstance`. Related work on
the same file should update this issue rather than open a duplicate.

## Closure binding

Closes on a commit stamped `(fak fleetbus)` that adds the publish-time-targets admission test to
`fleetbus.Drain` (with the empty-`Targets` back-compat arm) and lands `TestDrainLateBoot` green,
with `go test ./internal/fleetbus` and `go test ./cmd/fak -run 'TestFleetControl|TestServeFleetBus'`
passing.

- **Required model tier:** T2
- **Optimal model tier:** T2

### Related

#5599 (epic parent) · #5600 (the spine that shipped both `Drain` and `Targets`, closed
`bb2401e7a5`) · #5637 (the `--model` / `--zone` selector axes, which widen the leaking surface) ·
#5639 (the durable-mirror fix on the same apply path) · #2753 (the per-session control vocabulary
this bus carries)

records.title: fix(fleetbus): the default serve bus identity is neither restart-stable nor collision-proof, so the exactly-once apply claim breaks both ways
records.body:
_Parent epic: #5599 — centralized fleet control. Spine: #5600 (closed, landed as `bb2401e7a5`)._

## Current state

The fleet control bus's exactly-once apply claim is keyed on the instance id, and `fak serve`'s
default instance id is derived from the **pid** — so it changes on every restart.

`cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus.go:427-439`:

```go
func resolveFleetBusID(sf *serveFlags) string {
	if sf.fleetBusID != nil && strings.TrimSpace(*sf.fleetBusID) != "" {
		return sanitizeBusToken(strings.TrimSpace(*sf.fleetBusID))
	}
	return defaultFleetBusInstanceID()
}

// defaultFleetBusInstanceID names this process on the bus. Host+pid is stable for the
// process lifetime and unique across a box, which is exactly the scope of an instance
// record; an operator who wants a stable name across restarts passes --fleet-bus-id.
func defaultFleetBusInstanceID() string {
	return sanitizeBusToken(fmt.Sprintf("serve-%s-%d", fleetBusMachine(), os.Getpid()))
}
```

The claim is a filesystem marker at `<root>/applied/<instance>/<directive>`
(`internal/fleetbus/dirbus.go:58`), taken with `O_CREATE|O_EXCL`
(`internal/fleetbus/dirbus.go:276`) and gating the apply in `Drain`
(`internal/fleetbus/drain.go:108-116`). It is documented as "partitioned per instance (no
cross-instance contention at all) and **never expires**" (`internal/fleetbus/dirbus.go:259-260`).

A new pid therefore means a new instance id, a new `applied/` partition, and a **fresh claim on a
directive this box already applied**. The directive is still there to re-read: the log is retained
(`Directives()` returns expired ones too, `internal/fleetbus/dirbus.go` / `drain.go:87-88`), the
CLI's default TTL is 5 minutes and `0` is offered as "never expires"
(`cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:89`), and `TTLSec: 0` really is unbounded
(`internal/fleetbus/fleetbus.go:477-478`, `ExpiresAt` at `fleetbus.go:601-609`).

**HEAD states the opposite of what it does.** The `--fleet-bus` help promises restart safety
outright (`cmd/fak/serve.go:240`):

> "Exactly-once under at-least-once redelivery: a per-(instance,directive) O_EXCL claim means **a
> directive re-read after a restart is recognised, never re-applied**."

while the `--fleet-bus-id` help two lines down contradicts it (`cmd/fak/serve.go:242`):

> "Pass a name to **keep one identity across restarts** — the id is what the exactly-once apply
> claim is keyed on."

Measured at HEAD against `internal/fleetbus` (temp probe, since deleted): one `--all --ttl 0`
directive, boot #1 as `serve-box-1000` → `applied=1`; a second drain under the **same** id →
`alreadyDone=1, applied=0` (the dedup works); a restart six hours later as `serve-box-2000` →
`seen=1 matched=1 alreadyDone=0 applied=1 expired=0`. Total applier invocations for one directive
on one box: **2**, and the ack log carries two `applied` acks (`serve-box-1000`,
`serve-box-2000`), so the fold reads the double-apply as ordinary success.

The re-apply is not a harmless no-op. `applyLifecycle` resolves targets from the **current** table
at drain time (`cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus.go:208`, `matchedSessions` at
`cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus.go:248-265`), so a `terminate`/`cancel` re-applied after a restart lands on
whatever sessions cold resume just re-attached — different sessions than the operator addressed.

Secondary consequence of the same root: `<root>/applied/` gains one never-pruned subdirectory per
pid, forever.

**The other horn — the documented workaround collides.** `cmd/fak/serve.go:242` tells the operator
to pass `--fleet-bus-id` "to keep one identity across restarts", which is the only remedy HEAD
offers for the above. But the apply claim is partitioned *per instance id*: the marker is
`<root>/applied/<instance>/<directive>`, taken with one `O_EXCL` create
(`internal/fleetbus/dirbus.go:58`, `:259-260`, `:276`), and the roster record is the single file
`<root>/instances/<id>.json`, written last-writer-wins by an atomic rename
(`internal/fleetbus/dirbus.go:154,170`). Two serves that take the advice and share one id therefore
collapse into **one** roster entry, and exactly one of them wins the `O_EXCL` claim — the operator
reads `targeted=1 applied=1 complete=true` and exits 0 while the second serve's sessions were never
touched. `Selector.MatchesInstance` (`internal/fleetbus/fleetbus.go:251-266`) matches on the record,
so it cannot see the difference either.

The two horns are one defect: the fix must deliver both properties at once — stable across a restart
*and* unique among concurrent serves — which is why the working spine below is keyed on the listen
address rather than on any operator-supplied string.

## Why this is next

Exactly-once application is the one property `internal/fleetbus` exists to provide — it is the
stated reason `ClaimApply` sits on the `Bus` interface rather than being left to callers
(`internal/fleetbus/dirbus.go:22-25`), and it is the spine's headline in #5600. The bus half holds
it correctly; the identity that keys it does not survive the exact event a restart-oriented control
plane is aimed at. A destructive lifecycle op re-applied to the wrong sessions, acked `applied`,
is worse than the "honest gap" the at-most-once design deliberately chose
(`internal/fleetbus/dirbus.go:262-267`). Fixing the identity is cheap now, while `--fleet-bus` is
still off by default and the only consumer is `fak serve`.

## Working spine

The default instance identity becomes something that is **both** stable across restarts of the same
serve and unique among serves running concurrently on one box — the two properties the pid default
gets only half of. The listen address is the natural candidate: `*sf.addr` is already in scope at
the arming site (`cmd/fak/serve_stages.go:564`, addr read at `cmd/fak/serve_stages.go:596`), two
concurrent serves on one box cannot bind one port, and a restarted serve rebinds the same one.
Cases with no stable address (`--stdio`, `--addr :0`) fall back to a durable identity claimed under
the bus dir, or, failing that, keep the pid form — but then the help must stop promising restart
safety for that case. `--fleet-bus-id` stays the explicit override.

`Instance.Addr` already exists on the record for exactly this kind of information and is currently
passed empty (`cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus.go:355-358`), so the announce gains a real value on the way
past.

## In scope

- A restart-stable, concurrently-unique default for `defaultFleetBusInstanceID`
  (`cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus.go:437-439`), with a named, documented fallback for the transports that
  have no stable address.
- Populate `Instance.Addr` on announce (`cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus.go:357`) instead of `""`.
- Reconcile the two contradictory flag helps (`cmd/fak/serve.go:240` and `cmd/fak/serve.go:242`) so
  the restart claim in `--fleet-bus` matches what the default identity actually guarantees.
- A regression test that fails on today's tree: two successive identity resolutions across a
  simulated restart must produce the same id and therefore one apply.
- A second regression arm for the collision horn: two serves armed concurrently on one box must
  resolve **different** ids, so the roster denominator counts both and each takes its own claim.

## Out of scope

- Changing `ClaimApply`'s semantics, the marker layout, or the deliberate at-most-once ordering
  (claim before apply, `internal/fleetbus/dirbus.go:262-267`). The bus half is correct; only the
  identity feeding it is wrong.
- Pruning `<root>/applied/<instance>/` for retired instances. Real, caused by the same root, but a
  GC policy is its own leaf — worth filing once the identity stops churning per restart.
- Cross-host identity collision (two boxes with the same hostname). Unchanged by this leaf.
- Retry / escalation of the outstanding set, still owned by epic #5599.

## Done condition

With `--fleet-bus` armed and no `--fleet-bus-id`, a serve that is stopped and relaunched on the same
box with the same transport resolves the **same** instance id, so a still-unexpired directive it
already applied is counted `already_done` on the first post-restart drain (`DrainReport.AlreadyDone`
increments, `Applied` does not) and no second `applied` ack is appended for that directive. Two
serves launched concurrently on one box with distinct addresses still resolve **distinct** ids and
each apply an `--all` directive exactly once.

## Witness

`go test ./cmd/fak -run 'TestFleetBusIdentitySurvivesRestart'` — a new test that resolves
`resolveFleetBusID` twice against the same `serveFlags` shape while varying only the pid source,
asserts the ids are equal, then drives `fleetbus.Drain` over a temp bus dir twice under those ids
and asserts `rep2.AlreadyDone == 1 && rep2.Applied == 0` and `len(acks) == 1`. A sibling arm with
two distinct addresses asserts distinct ids and `rep.Applied == 1` on each.

Reference counter-run on today's tree (the probe above): the second drain reports
`alreadyDone=0 applied=1` and the ack log holds two `applied` rows.

## Acceptance gate

`fak buildcheck --vet ./cmd/fak ./internal/fleetbus`, then
`go test ./internal/fleetbus/... ./cmd/fak -run 'FleetBus|FleetControl'` green, including the new
restart arm and the existing `resolveFleetBusID` token check at
`cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus_test.go:340`. The `--fleet-bus` and `--fleet-bus-id` help strings must not
both be present in their current contradictory form: `fak serve --help` may claim restart-safe
exactly-once only for the identity shape the code actually delivers.

## Dependencies

None blocking. Independent of the gateway-scoped applier (#5638) and the capability field (#5637),
both of which are already landed on top of this code.

## Confusion risks

- **Stability and uniqueness pull opposite ways.** The pid default is unique among concurrent
  processes and unstable across restarts; a bare `serve-<host>` would be the reverse, and would
  silently make two concurrent serves share one claim so only one of them ever applies a directive
  — the failure `cmd/fak/serve.go:242` already describes for a shared `--fleet-bus-id`. Any fix must
  hold both, and the test must cover both arms.
- **A shrinking or churning roster corrupts the fold.** The instance id is also the roster key and
  the ack fold's denominator (`internal/fleetbus/fold.go:51-55`); changing its derivation changes
  what `Outstanding` counts. Old-shaped records must still parse and still count.
- **The claim never expires by design.** Do not "fix" this by giving the marker a TTL — the package
  doc rejects time-windowed dedup explicitly (`internal/fleetbus/dirbus.go:253-260`): a stale `go`
  re-firing tomorrow is the failure the package exists to prevent.
- **Expiry is not the fence.** The default TTL is 5 minutes (`cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:89`), which
  is squarely inside a supervised restart, and `--ttl 0` removes the bound entirely.

## Likely files

`cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus.go`, `cmd/fak/serve.go`, `cmd/fak/serve_stages.go`,
`cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus_test.go`, `internal/fleetbus/dirbus.go`

```routing
lane: fleetbus
paths: cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus.go, cmd/fak/serve.go, cmd/fak/serve_stages.go, cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus_test.go
expected_steps: pick a restart-stable+unique identity source; rewrite defaultFleetBusInstanceID with a named fallback; populate Instance.Addr; reconcile the two flag helps; add the restart + concurrent-serve test arms
```

## Parent context

**#5599** — the centralized fleet control epic. The spine (#5600, closed, landed as `bb2401e7a5`)
shipped the exactly-once apply claim; this leaf repairs the identity that keys it, and is
dispatchable on its own.

## Work unit

## Work scale

S1

5

## Assumptions

The listen address is available and stable at the arming site (`*sf.addr`, in scope at
`cmd/fak/serve_stages.go:564`) for the deployments that matter. Transports with no stable address
(`--stdio`, `--addr :0`) are assumed to be the minority and are handled by the named fallback — if
they turn out to be the common case, the fallback becomes the primary design and the help must stop
promising restart safety for it.

Assumes no operator currently depends on a per-pid identity to distinguish successive runs of one
serve in the roster. Nothing at HEAD reads the id that way.

## Coordination notes

Lane `fleetbus`, but the edit lands in `cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus.go` and `cmd/fak/serve.go` — take
the `cmd` lane lease too if the split is enforced. Coordinates with #5823, which filters by instance
at drain time and should be written against the identity this leaf settles; land this one first if

only the identity feeding it is wrong.

## Trigger

Filed from a HEAD verification pass (2026-08-06) over the fleetbus children landed after the spine
(#5637, #5638, #5639, #5640). The double-apply was reproduced against `internal/fleetbus` with a

One issue per defect — not batched, though it covers both horns of a single identity defect

`defaultFleetBusInstanceID`. The `<root>/applied/` GC named in **Out of scope** should be filed only
after this lands.

records.title: fix(serve): --fleet-bus-dir scopes only the bus, so a fanned lifecycle op mutates every session in the host's shared registry
records.body:
_Parent epic: #5599 — the fleet control bus. Spine: #5600 (closed, landed `bb2401e7a5`)._

## Current state

`--fleet-bus-dir` scopes the **bus** and nothing else. The sessions a drained directive is applied
to come from a completely different root, and no flag on `fak serve` scopes that one.

The applier resolves its targets from the process's session table:

- `matchedSessions` walks `a.tbl.Snapshot()` (`cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus.go:252`) and
  `applyLifecycle` writes through `a.tbl.Transition` (`cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus.go:218`).
- That table is `serveSessions`, passed at the arming site
  (`cmd/fak/serve_stages.go:564-565`) and declared `var serveSessions = session.NewTable()`
  (`cmd/fak/main_session_control.go:34`).

`serveSessions` is described as "process-local" (`cmd/fak/main_session_control.go:27`) and in
memory it is — but it is **hydrated at startup from the host's shared on-disk session registry**.
`runServe` calls `configureServeSessionDurability(serveSessions, "", os.Stderr)`
(`cmd/fak/serve_stages.go:407`) with an empty path, so the path always falls through to
`defaultSessionRegistryPath()` (`cmd/fak/session_durable.go:142-150`) — `FAK_SESSION_REGISTRY` if
set, else `<UserConfigDir>/fak/session-registry.json`, a single per-user file every serve on the box
shares. The restore then re-attaches every descriptor in it into the live table
(`mirror.restore(tbl)`, `cmd/fak/session_durable.go:122`; `tbl.Restore(...)` at `:265` and `:327`).

So a brand-new `fak serve --fleet-bus --fleet-bus-dir <a private temp dir>` starts life owning
**every live session on the machine**, including sessions belonging to unrelated agents, and
`--op pause --all` writes to all of them. The only knob that narrows this is the
`FAK_SESSION_REGISTRY` environment variable (`cmd/fak/session_durable.go:24`): there is no
`--session-registry` flag, `cmd/fak/serve.go` never mentions it, and neither does the
`--fleet-bus-dir` help, which instead frames the bus directory as *the* thing that decides reach —
"On one machine a directory IS a real cross-process control plane" (`cmd/fak/serve.go:241`).

The selector layer is careful in exactly the place this is careless. `--all` on `send` is documented
as something that "must be STATED, never implied by an absent filter"
(`cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:82`) — a deliberate guard rail on the fan across *instances*. The fan
from one instance across *sessions* has no equivalent statement, no dry-run, and no count shown
before the write.

**Live witness (2026-08-05, this box).** A demo serve armed with a private `--fleet-bus-dir`, run
solely to produce an end-to-end directive→ack transcript for #5600, was sent
`--op pause --all`. It reported `affected=12  pause: 12/12 session(s) took it` and exit 0. The 12
were real sessions belonging to other workers on the host — overnight job runners and peer
Claude/Codex sessions (`contract-repair-claude-74832-c6861445`, `tools-claude-54364-d9ee6a53`,
`docs-claude-74832-a042b24f`, `cmd-claude-22716-167c4f84`, and eight `win-*` sessions). They were
restored with `--op resume --all`, verified by a third resume logging zero `-> running` transitions.
Nothing in the invocation, the flag help, or the output indicated the blast radius before the write.

## Why this is next

The spine's contract is that an ack states what actually changed. It does — accurately — for a fan
whose *extent* the operator never chose. A control plane that is honest about its effect and silent
about its reach is still a control plane you cannot safely rehearse, and rehearsal is the normal way
anyone will first meet `--fleet-bus`: arm a throwaway serve, point it at a scratch directory, send
one directive. That path currently ends in a fleet-wide `pause` of other people's work.

This also blocks the epic's own testing story. Every remaining #5599 child (retry/escalation,
routing #5638, durability #5639, tagging #5640) wants a live fan exercised against a real serve;
today that cannot be done on a shared host without hitting peers, so the arms that most need a live
witness are the ones that will get a test double instead.

## Working spine

Two independent, cheap moves, either of which removes the trap; both together are the fix:

1. **Make the scope reachable from the CLI.** Add a `--session-registry` flag threaded into the
   `path` argument `cmd/fak/serve_stages.go:407` currently hard-codes to `""`. The plumbing already
   exists — `configureServeSessionDurability` takes the path and honours `"off"` for a pure
   in-memory table (`cmd/fak/session_durable.go:73-81`) — so this is flag wiring, not new mechanism.
2. **State the reach at arm time.** When `--fleet-bus` is armed, log once how many sessions were
   hydrated and from which registry path, so the operator sees `12 sessions from
   C:\...\session-registry.json` before any directive lands rather than `12/12 took it` after.

## In scope

- A `--session-registry` flag on `fak serve` (path, or `off` for in-memory), wired to the existing
  `path` parameter at `cmd/fak/serve_stages.go:407`, documented alongside `--fleet-bus-dir`.
- A one-line arm-time notice naming the hydrated session count and the resolved registry path when
  `--fleet-bus` is on.
- `--fleet-bus-dir`'s help (`cmd/fak/serve.go:241`) stops implying the bus directory bounds reach,
  and names what actually does.
- A test asserting a serve started with an isolated registry does not adopt sessions from another
  registry, so the isolation is a property and not a convention.

## Out of scope

- Changing the default registry path or the durability/restore design
  (`cmd/fak/session_durable.go`). The shared registry is deliberate and correct for the real fleet;
  only the inability to opt out of it from the CLI is the defect.
- A confirmation prompt or `--dry-run` on `fleet control send`. Worth considering, but it is an
  operator-UX leaf on the control point, not the serve-side scoping fixed here.
- The `affected` overcount in the same transcript — filed separately as its own leaf.
- Per-session ACLs or multi-tenant ownership on the registry. A much larger design; this leaf only
  restores the ability to run an isolated serve.

## Done condition

`fak serve --fleet-bus --fleet-bus-dir <tmp> --session-registry <tmp>/sessions.json` hydrates zero
sessions from the user's shared registry, and a subsequent `fleet control send --op pause --all`
against that bus reports `affected=0` while every session in the shared registry keeps its run
state. With `--fleet-bus` armed and no `--session-registry`, the serve emits one line naming the
resolved registry path and the number of sessions adopted from it.

## Witness

`go test ./cmd/fak -run 'TestServeSessionRegistryScoped' -count=1` — a new test calling
`configureServeSessionDurability` against registry A seeded with N descriptors, then against
registry B seeded with none, asserting the second table's `Snapshot()` is empty; and an arm of
`fleetBusApplier.Apply` over the empty table asserting `Outcome.Affected == 0` and
`Status == applied`.

Today the flag does not exist, so the test does not compile — that is the starting failure.

## Acceptance gate

The new test passes. `go test ./cmd/fak -run 'FleetBus|SessionDurab' -count=1` and
`go test ./internal/session ./internal/fleetbus -count=1` stay green, including the durability arms
from #5639. A serve started with **no** `--session-registry` must keep hydrating from
`defaultSessionRegistryPath()` exactly as today — this leaf adds an opt-out, it must not change the
default fleet's behaviour, and `cmd/fak/session_durable_test.go`'s existing expectations must hold
unchanged.

## Dependencies

None blocking. Independent of the other #5599 children; lands on top of #5637-#5640, all closed.

## Confusion risks

- **"Process-local" is about the Go value, not the data.** `cmd/fak/main_session_control.go:27`
  says process-local and is correct about the `*session.Table`; the *contents* come from a shared
  file. Reading that comment as isolation is the whole trap.
- **`--fleet-bus-dir` is not a sandbox.** It scopes announcements, directives, claims and acks —
  every path under `<root>/` in `internal/fleetbus/dirbus.go` — and nothing about which sessions get
  written. A private bus with a shared registry is the dangerous combination, and it is the one a
  cautious operator will reach for first.
- **`off` is a real option and must stay one.** `configureServeSessionDurability` already accepts
  `"off"` (`cmd/fak/session_durable.go:77-81`); the flag should expose it rather than invent a
  second spelling.
- **Do not "fix" this by defaulting `--fleet-bus` to an isolated registry.** That would make the
  armed control plane unable to see the fleet it exists to control — the reach is correct for the
  real deployment; only the absence of an opt-out is wrong.

## Likely files

`cmd/fak/serve.go` (flag + help), `cmd/fak/serve_stages.go` (the `""` at `:407`, arm-time notice),
`cmd/fak/session_durable.go` (read only — path resolution), `cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus.go` (read only —
`a.tbl` consumers), `cmd/fak/session_durable_test.go`, `docs/cli-reference.md`

```routing
lane: cmd
paths: cmd/fak/serve.go, cmd/fak/serve_stages.go, cmd/fak/session_durable*.go
expected_steps: add --session-registry and thread it into configureServeSessionDurability; log the hydrated count and path when --fleet-bus arms; correct the --fleet-bus-dir help; add the isolation test; document the flag
```

## Parent context

**#5599** — the centralized fleet control epic; the spine is **#5600** (closed, landed
`bb2401e7a5`). This leaf makes the spine safe to rehearse on a shared host and is dispatchable on
its own.

## Work unit

## Work scale

S1

## Expected steps

5

## Assumptions

The shared session registry default is correct for a real fleet — a control plane that could not
see the host's sessions would be useless — so only the missing opt-out is the defect. If the project
instead decides an armed `--fleet-bus` should default to isolation, this leaf's shape changes
completely and **Out of scope** has to be revisited.

Assumes `configureServeSessionDurability`'s existing `path`/`"off"` handling
(`cmd/fak/session_durable.go:73-81`) is sufficient to express the scoped case, so no new mechanism
is needed — only flag wiring.

## Coordination notes

Lane `cmd`. `cmd/fak/serve.go` and `cmd/fak/serve_stages.go` are high-traffic shared files; take
the lane lease and re-read HEAD before editing. `cmd/fak/session_durable.go` is read-only for this

Anyone rehearsing #5599's remaining children on a shared host is blocked by this issue, so it is

records.title: fix(fleetbus): stop foldFleetControl from reporting an unreadable roster as an empty fleet
records.body:
_Parent epic: #5599 — centralized fleet control, one control point / N instances, command out / ack back._

## Current state

`foldFleetControl` is the only place `fak fleet control` turns bus state into a report, and it
discards both read errors. `cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:181-186` at HEAD (`3a1b7320f0`):

```go
func foldFleetControl(bus *fleetbus.DirBus, d fleetbus.Directive) fleetbus.Report {
	now := fleetControlNow()
	roster, _ := bus.Instances(now, fleetbus.DefaultInstanceTTL)
	acks, _ := bus.Acks(d.ID)
	return fleetbus.Fold(d, roster, acks, now)
}
```

The `send` path *does* check the same read — `cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:133-137` refuses with
`read roster: %v` and exit 2 — and `instances` checks it at `cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:250-254`.
The fold, which is what both `await` (`fleet_control.go:168`) and `status`
(`fleet_control.go:220`) call, does not. A failed `bus.Instances` (its only error path is
`os.ReadDir` on `<root>/instances` failing with something other than `ErrNotExist` —
`internal/fleetbus/dirbus.go:182-189`) is indistinguishable from an empty fleet.

The roster is a denominator input, not decoration. `fleetbus.Fold` seeds rows from
`d.Targets`, then **adds** every roster instance the selector matches
(`internal/fleetbus/fold.go:108-121`), then decides
`rep.Complete = rep.Targeted > 0 && rep.Outstanding == 0` (`fold.go:165`). `emitFleetControl`
maps `rep.Complete && rep.Applied == rep.Targeted` to **exit 0**
(`cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:313-316`). So an unreadable roster silently drops targets from the
denominator and can manufacture the exit code that the package doc reserves for
WITNESSED APPLIED (`cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:19-21`).

Measured at HEAD with a scratch probe in `package main` (bus in a temp dir, `inst-a` and
`inst-b` announced, directive stamped `Targets=[inst-a]`, `inst-a` acks applied, `inst-b`
silent):

- healthy roster → `targeted=2 applied=1 outstanding=1 complete=false`, exit **1** —
  `inst-b` correctly shows `outstanding`.
- `<root>/instances` replaced by a regular file (the shape a torn directory, a permission
  change, or a hostile mount takes) → `bus.Instances` returns a non-nil error, the fold
  swallows it, `targeted=1 applied=1 outstanding=0 complete=true`, exit **0**, verdict
  `applied — all 1 addressed instance(s) witnessed it`.

Two further consequences of the same swallow, present even when `d.Targets` holds the whole
denominator:

- Every row renders `(left the roster)` (`cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:342-345`), because
  `Row.InRoster` is only set from the roster loop. The report actively asserts that live
  instances have died.
- A directive carrying no `Targets` — the compatibility case the fold documents at
  `internal/fleetbus/fold.go:101-102` ("folds back to the roster-only denominator … for old
  records only"), reachable from a peer on an older binary or a replayed log — loses its
  denominator entirely and reports only the instances that happened to answer.

The `acks` half of the same line is much weaker and should be said plainly: `bus.Acks` errors
only on a non-token directive id (`internal/fleetbus/dirbus.go:308-311`), and every directive
reaching the fold has already passed `Validate`, so that error is effectively unreachable.
Per-file read failures inside `Acks` are swallowed one level down (`dirbus.go:314-318`) and are
a separate concern.

## Why this is next

The whole justification for this package is that the enqueue is not the witness
(`cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:19-25`), and `fold.go:16-20` states the invariant directly: "a report
that cannot say 'one instance never answered' is indistinguishable from one where everybody
did." `fold.go:89-102` then spends thirteen lines explaining that deriving the denominator from
the roster is "the subtle way this report learns to lie" — and the caller hands that same fold a
silently empty roster whenever the read fails. The infrastructure to be honest already exists;
one discarded error is what routes around it. This is a one-function fix against a fold that is
already pure and already tested.

## Working spine

`foldFleetControl` returns an error alongside the report. `awaitFleetControl` stops polling on a
read failure and `runFleetControlStatus` reports it, both exiting non-zero with the underlying
error text — the same treatment `send` already gives the identical call at
`cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:133-137`. A read that cannot be completed is reported as a read
failure, never rendered as a fleet fact.

## In scope

- `foldFleetControl` (`cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:181-186`) propagates the `bus.Instances` error.
- `awaitFleetControl` (`cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:164-179`) surfaces it rather than looping on a
  report built from a failed read.
- `runFleetControlStatus` (`cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:220`) prints it to stderr and exits
  non-zero, matching the `send` and `instances` wording.
- Propagate the `bus.Acks` error too, for symmetry and to keep the next reader from
  re-introducing the discard — noted as belt-and-braces, not as the defect.

## Out of scope

- Changing `fleetbus.Fold`. It is pure and correct given its inputs; the defect is entirely in
  what the caller feeds it.
- Changing `bus.Instances`'s own per-file tolerance (`internal/fleetbus/dirbus.go:191-207`),
  where an unparsable or stale record is deliberately skipped. That leniency is documented and
  wanted; only the whole-directory failure is at issue.
- Retry/backoff on a transient bus read. Report it; do not paper over it.

## Done condition

With `<bus>/instances` made unreadable (replaced by a regular file, so `os.ReadDir` fails with
something other than `ErrNotExist`), `fak fleet control status --directive <id>` exits non-zero
and prints the underlying read error on stderr, instead of exiting 0 with a verdict of
`applied — all N addressed instance(s) witnessed it`; and an instance that announced after the
publish is never dropped from `Targeted` because the roster read failed.

## Witness

`go test ./cmd/fak -run 'TestFleetControlFoldReportsRosterReadError'` — a new test that builds a
`DirBus` in `t.TempDir()`, announces `inst-a` and `inst-b`, publishes a directive stamped
`WithTargets([inst-a])`, records an `AckApplied` from `inst-a` only, asserts the healthy fold
gives `Targeted=2 / Outstanding=1` and a non-zero exit, then replaces `<root>/instances` with a
regular file and asserts the second fold returns an error and a non-zero exit rather than
`Complete=true` at exit 0.

## Acceptance gate

The new test passes; `go test ./cmd/fak -run 'TestFleetControl'` and `go test ./internal/fleetbus`
stay green; `cmd/fak/fleet_control.go` contains no `bus.Instances(` or `bus.Acks(` call whose
error is assigned to `_`; and the failure message matches the shape already used at
`cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:135` so the three verbs report one bus read failure one way.

## Dependencies

None blocking. Sits on top of the spine landed in `bb2401e7a5` (#5600) and is independent of the
capability-field work in #5637.

## Confusion risks

- **The `send` path already checks this — twice is not redundant.** The check at
  `fleet_control.go:133` happens once, before publish; the fold runs repeatedly during the wait
  and again on every `status`, and holds no error path of its own.
- **`d.Targets` is a floor, not a ceiling.** It bounds how far the denominator can shrink for
  a directive published by a current binary, but `fold.go:108-121` adds roster instances on top
  — a fleet that grows mid-fan-out, and every pre-`Targets` record, still depends on the roster
  read succeeding.
- **The acks discard is not the same defect.** `bus.Acks` cannot realistically error here
  (`dirbus.go:308-311`); do not write the issue up as two equal halves.
- **A missing bus directory is not a failure.** `bus.Instances` maps `ErrNotExist` to
  `(nil, nil)` (`dirbus.go:185-187`); an empty fleet must stay a fact, and the `instances` verb
  already says so at `cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:263-268`.

## Likely files

`cmd/fak/fleet_control.go`, `cmd/fak/fleet_control_test.go`

```routing

paths: cmd/fak/fleet_control.go, cmd/fak/fleet_control_test.go
expected_steps: propagate the Instances error out of foldFleetControl; thread it through awaitFleetControl and status; match send's message shape; add the unreadable-roster test
```

`bb2401e7a5`); this is a correctness leaf on the operator-facing half of that spine and is
dispatchable on its own.

records.title: fix(fleetbus): fleet control send/status hard-code the 90s roster TTL only `instances --ttl` can change
records.body:
_Parent epic: #5599 — centralized fleet control. Spine landed as `bb2401e7a5` (#5600)._

## Current state

`fak fleet control` has three verbs that all resolve the same roster, and only one of them
lets the operator say what "live" means.

`instances` takes the liveness window as a flag — `cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:235,250`:

```go
ttl := fs.Duration("ttl", fleetbus.DefaultInstanceTTL, "how recent an announcement must be to count as live")
...
roster, err := bus.Instances(fleetControlNow(), *ttl)
```

`send` computes the addressee set from a hard-coded constant — `cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:133`:

```go
roster, err := bus.Instances(now, fleetbus.DefaultInstanceTTL)
```

and so does the fold that both `send`'s ack wait and `status` read —
`cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:183`:

```go
roster, _ := bus.Instances(now, fleetbus.DefaultInstanceTTL)
```

`DefaultInstanceTTL` is 90s (`internal/fleetbus/fleetbus.go:78`). That roster is not
cosmetic in `send`: it is the input to `PublishTargets` (`cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:140`,
`internal/fleetbus/fold.go:189-197`), which decides both the `FLEETBUS_NO_TARGET` refusal at
`fleet_control.go:141-145` and the `Targets` stamped onto the directive at
`fleet_control.go:150` — the denominator `Fold` then treats as the floor
(`internal/fleetbus/fold.go:89-106`).

Two consequences at HEAD:

1. **The roster an operator inspects is not the roster `send` addresses.** `instances --ttl 5m`
   can list six instances; the very next `send --all` addresses only those fresh within 90s,
   and reports exit 0 ("all addressed instances witnessed it") over the smaller set.
   `instances --ttl 30s` is the mirror image: it hides instances `send` will still command.
2. **`--ttl` means two different things across sibling verbs.** On `send` it is directive
   expiry — `cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:89`: `"how long the directive stays applyable (0 = never
   expires)"` — so an operator who reaches for `send --ttl 5m` to widen the roster silently gets
   a longer-lived directive fanned to the same 90s set.

`status` has the split in its weaker form: it has no `--ttl` flag at all
(`cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:191-195` declares only `--directive`, `--bus`, `--json`), yet it
folds through the same hard-coded 90s at `fleet_control.go:183`, so the roster half of its
denominator cannot be adjusted at all — including for a re-read of a directive published
minutes ago.

Nothing in the tree covers the divergence: `cmd/fak/fleet_control_test.go` exercises staleness
only at the default (`TestFleetControlInstancesTreatsAStaleAnnouncementAsGone:286-307`), where
the flag and the constant happen to agree.

## Why this is next

This is the one knob on the control point that changes *who gets commanded*, and it is wired
to the verb that commands nobody. It matters most exactly when an operator is already
debugging a flaky fleet: the announce cadence is operator-settable
(`--fleet-bus-interval`, `cmd/fak/serve.go:243`) and `startFleetBusLoop` only replaces a
non-positive value (`cmd/fak/serve_fleetbus.go:343-345`) — nothing enforces the flag help's
"must stay well under 90s". On such a fleet `instances --ttl 5m` is precisely the diagnostic
reach, and it produces a roster `send` then contradicts without saying so. The bus's own
doctrine is that the denominator must never quietly shrink (`internal/fleetbus/fold.go:89-102`);
a hard-coded window that disagrees with the operator's stated one shrinks it in a way no output
line names.

## Working spine

The roster liveness window becomes one operator-visible value shared by all three verbs, passed
into `bus.Instances` instead of read from the package constant at two call sites, and echoed in
the output so the addressee set is checkable against the roster the operator inspected. The
constant stays the default, so unflagged behaviour is byte-identical.

## In scope

- A roster-liveness flag on `send` and `status` under a name that does **not** collide with
  `send --ttl`'s existing directive-expiry meaning (e.g. `--roster-ttl`), plumbed to both
  `bus.Instances` call sites (`cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:133,183`), including through
  `foldFleetControl` / `awaitFleetControl` so the wait loop re-reads under the same window.
- The same spelling accepted by `instances`, with today's `--ttl` kept working there.
- The resolved window echoed in `send`/`status` output (JSON `fleetControlJSON`,
  `cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:319-327`, and the rendered footer) so a roster reading and an
  addressee set can be compared after the fact.
- A test pinning that `instances` and `send` agree on membership for the same window.

## Out of scope

- Changing `DefaultInstanceTTL` (90s) or the announce cadence defaults.
- Refusing `--fleet-bus-interval >= DefaultInstanceTTL` on `fak serve`. Real, adjacent, and a
  separate leaf in the serve lane.
- Any change to `Fold`'s denominator floor semantics: an addressed instance that dies still
  stays `RowOutstanding` (`internal/fleetbus/fold.go:89-106`).
- Corroborating bus membership against `leaseref` — that is the epic's roster-join child.

## Done condition

For one bus containing an instance whose last announce is older than 90s but younger than the
stated window: `instances` and `send` return the same membership decision for that instance
under the same flag value — `send` publishes to it (exit 1 under `--wait 0`, no
`FLEETBUS_NO_TARGET`) when the window covers it, and refuses `FLEETBUS_NO_TARGET` when the
window does not, matching whether `instances` printed it. With no flag stated, every verb still
resolves the roster at `fleetbus.DefaultInstanceTTL` and the existing suite is unchanged.

## Witness

`go test ./cmd/fak -run 'TestFleetControlSendHonorsTheStatedRosterWindow'` — new test in
`cmd/fak/fleet_control_test.go`, announcing an instance at `now-3m` via the existing
`controlBus` / `fleetbus.NewInstance` helpers, then asserting three arms: (a) default window —
`instances` omits it and `send --all --wait 0` exits 2 with `FLEETBUS_NO_TARGET` (today's
behaviour, unchanged); (b) widened window — `instances` lists it and `send` publishes, exit 1;
(c) `status --directive <id>` under the widened window counts it in `targeted`.

## Acceptance gate

The new test passes; `go test ./cmd/fak -run TestFleetControl` and `go test ./internal/fleetbus`
stay green, including `TestFleetControlInstancesTreatsAStaleAnnouncementAsGone`; `send --ttl`
retains its directive-expiry meaning (`NewDirective`'s `TTLSec`, `cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:89,123`)
and is not repurposed; `go vet ./...` clean.

## Dependencies

None blocking. Sits on the spine landed in `bb2401e7a5` (#5600) and does not conflict with
#5637's `Instance` capability fields.

## Confusion risks

- **`--ttl` already means directive expiry on `send`.** Reusing the name there would silently
  change the lifetime of every fanned directive. Pick a distinct spelling.
- **A wider window is not a promise of liveness.** It only widens who gets *addressed*; the ack
  is still the only witness (`internal/fleetbus` package doc), and a wider window makes
  `RowOutstanding` more likely, not less.
- **Do not "fix" this by making the roster the denominator.** `fold.go:89-106` explains why the
  publish-time `Targets` floor exists; the window must not become a way to drop an addressed
  instance from `Targeted`.
- **`awaitFleetControl` re-reads the roster each pass** (`cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:160-179`) — the
  new value has to reach `foldFleetControl`, not just the pre-publish read, or the wait loop and
  the publish disagree with each other.

## Likely files

`cmd/fak/fleet_control.go`, `cmd/fak/fleet_control_test.go`, `docs/cli-reference.md:216`

```routing
lane: fleetbus
paths: cmd/fak/fleet_control*.go
expected_steps: add the roster-window flag to send/status; thread it through foldFleetControl and awaitFleetControl; echo it in JSON and the rendered footer; test the three arms; update the CLI reference line
```

## Parent context

**#5599** — the centralized fleet control epic, whose spine (#5600) landed the three verbs this
leaf makes agree with each other. Dispatchable on its own; not a prerequisite for any other
child.

## Work unit

## Work scale

S1

4

## Assumptions

One roster-freshness meaning should hold across `send`, `status` and `instances`. Assumes the
right fix is to make the existing `--ttl` reach all three rather than to add a second flag per verb.

Assumes the name collision is real and must be resolved by spelling: `send --ttl` today means
DIRECTIVE EXPIRY (`cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:89`), not roster freshness. Reusing `--ttl` for both on
one verb would be worse than the current gap, so the roster knob needs its own name
(e.g. `--instance-ttl`) wherever both apply.

## Coordination notes

Lane `cmd`, file `cmd/fak/fleet_control.go`, touching all three verb bodies plus
`foldFleetControl`. Overlaps textually with #5826 (same function) and #5828 (same wait loop); take
the lane lease and re-read HEAD, and prefer landing after those two so the flag threading is written
once against their final shape.

One issue per defect — not batched. A duplicate scan of the existing open backlog found no issue
covering the roster-TTL split; the dedupe marker is `DefaultInstanceTTL` + `fleet_control.go`. The
three verbs are fixed together in one commit because a partial fix leaves exactly the inconsistency
being removed.

Closes on a commit stamped `(fak fleetbus)` that threads an operator-stated roster window through

arm proving unflagged behaviour is unchanged.

records.title: test(fleetbus): awaitFleetControl sleeps on the wall clock inside a seam-measured budget, so the wait-expiry path has no test
records.body:
_Parent epic: #5599 — the fleet control plane. Spine: #5600 (closed, landed as `bb2401e7a5`)._

## Current state

`cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:164-179` measures the wait budget through the injectable clock but
sleeps on the real one:

```go
func awaitFleetControl(bus *fleetbus.DirBus, d fleetbus.Directive, wait time.Duration) (fleetbus.Report, time.Duration) {
	const poll = 250 * time.Millisecond
	start := fleetControlNow()
	for {
		rep := foldFleetControl(bus, d)
		waited := fleetControlNow().Sub(start)
		if wait <= 0 || rep.Complete || waited >= wait {
			return rep, waited
		}
		remaining := wait - waited
		if remaining > poll {
			remaining = poll
		}
		time.Sleep(remaining)
	}
}
```

`fleetControlNow` is declared as the package's clock seam at `cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:56-57`
("the clock seam, matching fleetNow's role in the sibling verbs"), and every other read of time in
this file goes through it (`:121`, `:169`, `:182`, `:250`). The loop's *blocking* step does not:
`time.Sleep` at `:177` is wall-clock and unmockable.

The two halves therefore disagree, and the disagreement is load-bearing:

- **Frozen clock ⇒ unbounded spin.** A test that pins `fleetControlNow` to a constant makes
  `waited` permanently `0`, so `waited >= wait` is never true. With `wait > 0` and no ack, the loop
  never exits — it sleeps 250 ms per pass forever. The seam that exists to make time cheap is the
  thing that hangs the test.
- **Real clock ⇒ real seconds.** The only way to reach the expiry return at `:171` today is to burn
  the whole budget in wall time.

The test file shows the cost already paid. Every timeout-shaped case in
`cmd/fak/fleet_control_test.go` dodges the loop entirely with `--wait 0`, which short-circuits at
the `wait <= 0` arm before any sleep — `:89`, `:112`, `:223`, `:393`. The one test that does enter
the loop, `TestFleetControlSendWaitsForALateAck` (`:181-213`), drives it with a real wall-clock
helper goroutine (`time.Sleep(10 * time.Millisecond)` at `:197`, an 8 s deadline at `:188`, a 9 s
budget at `:202`) and asserts on `time.Since(start)` at `:207`.

**So the budget-expiry path — `--wait 5s`, nobody acks, exit 1 after the deadline — has no test at
all.** It is the path an operator hits whenever a directive goes unapplied, and it is the one arm of
`awaitFleetControl` that no test can reach without either spinning forever or spending the budget.

## Why this is next

The control plane's whole claim is that exit 0 means *witnessed applied* (`fleet_control_test.go:5-8`).
The complement of that claim — exit 1 after a real wait — is the branch nobody exercises. A future
change to the poll arithmetic (an off-by-one on `remaining`, a `waited > wait` instead of `>=`, a
poll that outruns the budget) lands green today.

The fix is small and local: honour the seam in the delay too, so a fake clock can advance the loop
without wall time.

## Working spine

Introduce a package-level sleep seam beside `fleetControlNow` — e.g. `fleetControlSleep = time.Sleep`
— and call it at `cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:177`. A test then installs a paired fake: the sleep hook
advances the same fake `now` it was handed, so the loop makes progress in zero wall time and the
existing return conditions at `:170` are reached exactly as in production. Default behaviour is
byte-identical: unset seams are `time.Now` and `time.Sleep`.

## In scope

- A sleep seam in `cmd/fak/fleet_control.go` used by `awaitFleetControl`, documented as the twin of
  the existing `fleetControlNow` seam at `:56-57`.
- A test that drives the budget-expiry return (`waited >= wait`, `rep.Complete == false`) on a fake
  clock with no real sleeping, asserting the reported `waited` and the exit-1 verdict from
  `emitFleetControl`.
- A test that drives the early-return-on-ack path on the same fake clock, so the completion arm is
  covered without the wall-clock helper goroutine.

## Out of scope

- Replacing the poll loop with a watcher / `fsnotify` / channel notification. That is a different
  design with its own failure modes; this issue only makes the existing loop testable.
- Changing the 250 ms poll constant, the default `--wait 10s` (`:92`), or any observable output.
- Retiring `TestFleetControlSendWaitsForALateAck`. It is an end-to-end wall-clock witness and stays;
  the new tests sit beneath it at the unit level.
- The sibling `fleetNow` seams in the other `fak fleet` verbs.

## Done condition

A test pins `fleetControlNow` to a fake clock, advances it only from the injected sleep hook, and
`awaitFleetControl(bus, d, 5*time.Second)` on an unacked directive returns a report with
`Complete == false` and `waited >= 5s` while the test's own real elapsed time stays under 100 ms.
The same test file also proves the loop returns early when an ack lands, on the same fake clock.
With the seam left unset, `awaitFleetControl` sleeps on `time.Sleep` exactly as it does at
`bb2401e7a5`.

## Witness

`go test ./cmd/fak -run 'TestFleetControlAwait' -timeout 30s` — the new cases must pass, and the
whole `-run` selection must finish in well under a second of wall time (contrast: reaching the
expiry arm today requires spending the budget). Guard against regression to the hang: the frozen
clock arm must terminate, not time out.

## Acceptance gate

`go test ./cmd/fak -run 'TestFleetControl' -timeout 120s` green, including the pre-existing
`TestFleetControlSendWaitsForALateAck` end-to-end arm. The new expiry test completes without real
sleeping. No change to `fak fleet control send` output, exit codes, or default flag values —
`--wait 0` still short-circuits at `cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:170` and still exits 1 unwitnessed
(`fleet_control_test.go:89-98`).

## Dependencies

None blocking. Sits on top of the #5600 spine (`bb2401e7a5`), which introduced both the seam and
the loop.

## Confusion risks

- **This is not a production bug.** With the real `time.Now`, `awaitFleetControl` behaves correctly;
  the defect is that the seam is half-installed, so the behaviour is untestable. Do not "fix" the
  timing arithmetic — it is right.
- **Do not make the fake clock advance itself inside `foldFleetControl`.** The advance belongs to
  the sleep hook, otherwise the number of folds per simulated second becomes an accident of the
  fold implementation.
- **The `wait <= 0` arm is not the timeout arm.** `--wait 0` returns before any sleep (`:170`) and
  is already covered four times over; covering it again does not close this issue.
- **`waited` is a reported value, not just a loop variable.** It is returned and rendered by
  `emitFleetControl` (`cmd/fak/fleet_control.go:156-157`), so a fake-clock test must assert on it,
  not merely on the exit code.

## Likely files

`cmd/fak/fleet_control.go`, `cmd/fak/fleet_control_test.go`

```routing
lane: fleetbus
paths: cmd/fak/fleet_control*.go
expected_steps: add a sleep seam beside fleetControlNow; use it in awaitFleetControl; add fake-clock tests for the expiry and early-ack arms; keep the wall-clock end-to-end test green
```

## Parent context

**#5599** — the fleet control plane epic. The loop was introduced by its spine child #5600 (closed,
landed as `bb2401e7a5`); this leaf closes the test hole that spine left in its own wait path, and is
dispatchable on its own.

## Work unit

## Work scale

## Assumptions

The `fleetControlNow` seam is meant to be fully injectable, matching the sibling verbs it was
modelled on — so the sleep belongs behind a seam too, rather than the budget being moved back onto
the wall clock. Assumes adding a `fleetControlSleep` seam (or an injectable ticker) is acceptable
package style; if the project prefers a single injected clock object, that is a larger refactor than
this leaf and should be said before starting.

Assumes the 250 ms poll constant itself is fine and only its blocking call needs the seam.

`cmd/fak/fleet_control_test.go`. Directly adjacent to #5826, which changes `foldFleetControl` — the
function this loop calls each pass — and to #5827, which threads a flag through the same loop. Take

between.

**Current state** were read at `3a1b7320f0`, where `cmd/fak/fleet_control.go` is unmodified since
