records.title: fix(conceptcatalog): CONCEPT_FRESHNESS scores a git tree but prints a worktree remedy, so the cure it names cannot clear it
records.body:
_Repo tooling, not fleetbus. No epic parent — this is a pre-commit gate ergonomics defect in the
`conceptcatalog` lane. Sibling defect on the neighbouring gate: **#5534**._

## Current state

`CONCEPT_FRESHNESS` scores a **git tree**. The remedy it prints regenerates from the **worktree**.
On this shared multi-session checkout those are never the same tree, so the printed cure cannot
clear the refusal.

The gate, `internal/hooks/gate_conceptfreshness.go:23`:

```go
res, err := conceptcatalog.CheckGitTree(d.Root, "")
```

`CheckGitTree` with an empty treeish resolves the **index** (`internal/conceptcatalog/freshness.go:109`,
`git write-tree`), `git archive`s it into a temp dir (`:120`), and regenerates *inside the
extraction* (`:166`, `return CheckFresh(tmp)` → `:175`, `--workspace <tmp>`). Under a pathspec
commit — the mandated `git commit -s -m … -- <paths>` shape — git hands the hook its temporary
partial-commit index, so the scored tree is HEAD plus your pathspec and nothing else.

The refusal it emits, `gate_conceptfreshness.go:37`:

```go
Detail: fmt.Sprintf("generated concept artifacts are stale: %v; run `%s` and stage the result", res.StalePaths, res.Regenerate)
```

`res.Regenerate` is the constant at `internal/conceptcatalog/freshness.go:28`:

```go
RegenerateCommand = "python tools/concept_disambiguation_scorecard.py --markdown-dir docs/concept-disambiguation-scorecard"
```

**No `--workspace`.** The generator defaults to the repo root
(`tools/concept_disambiguation_scorecard.py:2357-2378`), and it derives its numbers by walking the
whole workspace for `.go`/`.md` files (`:1544-1597`, `_walk_files` / `rglob`) — not just the
concept corpus. So the remedy scores every peer's uncommitted edit anywhere in the checkout.

The two operator-facing verbs read the worktree too:

- `cmd/fak/concept.go:51` — `fak concept freshness` → `conceptcatalog.CheckFresh(root)`
- `cmd/fak/concept.go:74` — `fak concept generate` → `--workspace root`

There is no `--staged` (or any tree-scoped) option on either; `cmd/fak/concept.go:35-90` has
exactly `position | classify | freshness | generate | validate`.

**Measured at HEAD `3a1b7320f0` today**, regenerating the same artifact against three trees:

| tree regenerated from | disambiguation-debt | covered / discovered | legacy score |
|---|---|---|---|
| committed `README.md` at HEAD | 74 (clarity 4 + coverage 70) | 2299 / 2369 | 96.1 |
| HEAD's own tree (`git archive HEAD` → regen) | 74 (clarity **2** + coverage **72**) | 2301 / **2373** | **97.2** |
| the worktree (what the printed remedy does) | **95** (clarity 2 + coverage **93**) | 2303 / **2396** | **96.6** |

All three disagree. `INDEX.md` diverges by 67 diff lines between the worktree regen and the
HEAD-tree regen. Two consequences fall straight out:

1. **The committed artifact is not reproducible from the tree it was committed with.** HEAD's
   `README.md` does not match a regen of HEAD, because it was generated from somebody's dirty
   worktree. Every honest regeneration therefore moves the headline numbers by an amount unrelated
   to the committer's diff.
2. **`fak concept freshness` says "fresh" while the gate keeps refusing** — it compares the
   worktree artifact against a worktree regen, which is self-consistent by construction and says
   nothing about the tree the gate scores.

The only way through today is to hand-build the gate's tree: `GIT_INDEX_FILE=<tmp> git read-tree
HEAD` + `git add -- <paths>` + `git write-tree`, `git archive` it, extract, regenerate *inside the
extraction*, and copy the two artifacts back. That is the body of `CheckGitTree` re-implemented by
hand at the shell, once per refused commit. Cost measured today: ~1 hour across ~6 refused commits.

## Why this is next

Every other gate in `hooks.PreCommitGates()` prints a remedy that, run verbatim, clears it. This
one prints a remedy that produces a *different wrong answer*, and it fires on the exact paths a
concept-corpus change must touch — so it blocks the work it exists to police. #5534 documents the
identical index-vs-worktree split on the neighbouring `CONCEPT_ADMISSION` gate, but its fix
("stage the corpus file") does **not** help here: staging is necessary and not sufficient, because
the artifact is a function of the *whole* scanned tree, not of the corpus files alone. The two
gates need the same principle applied twice; this is the half that needs new code rather than a
longer sentence.

## Working spine

Give the operator a verb that regenerates against **the same tree the gate scores**, and make the
refusal print that verb. `CheckGitTree` already contains the whole mechanism — resolve treeish,
archive, extract, regenerate in the extraction. Today it throws the regenerated bytes away after
comparing. The fix is to let a caller keep them.

## In scope

- A tree-scoped regeneration path in `internal/conceptcatalog` — e.g. `RegenerateFromGitTree(root,
  treeish, dest)` factored out of the existing archive/extract/generate body at `freshness.go:107-167`
  so freshness-checking and regeneration share one extraction, and the artifacts land in the
  worktree at `GeneratedReadme` / `GeneratedIndex`.
- A CLI surface for it: `fak concept generate --staged` (and the matching `fak concept freshness
  --staged`), defaulting to the same empty-treeish → `git write-tree` resolution the gate uses, so
  it works unchanged inside a pre-commit hook.
- Make `FreshnessResult.Regenerate` carry that command when the result came from `CheckGitTree`, so
  `gate_conceptfreshness.go:37` prints a remedy that actually clears the gate. `RegenerateCommand`
  stays as the worktree-mode string for `CheckFresh` callers.
- A note in the refusal that the gate scores the staged tree, not the worktree — the same sentence
  #5534 asks for on its gate.

## Out of scope

- Making HEAD's committed scorecard reproducible from HEAD (a one-shot corpus regeneration commit;
  it will happen naturally the first time someone regenerates correctly, and the numbers will jump).
- Changing what the generator scans, or the debt/coverage arithmetic.
- The `CONCEPT_ADMISSION` half — that is #5534.
- Auto-staging the regenerated artifacts. Writing them is enough; the operator names their own
  pathspec (shared trunk).

## Done condition

With a dirty peer edit present in the worktree that shifts the token counts, running the command
the `CONCEPT_FRESHNESS` refusal prints, then re-running the gate against the same pathspec, yields
**no** `CONCEPT_FRESHNESS` finding — and the artifacts written match, byte for byte after newline
normalization, what `CheckGitTree` regenerated when it refused.

## Witness

`go test ./internal/conceptcatalog -run 'TestRegenerateFromGitTreeClearsTheFreshnessGate'` — a
hermetic repo where (a) the tracked artifacts are stale for the index tree, (b) an *unstaged*
worktree file is present that changes the generator's discovered-token count, (c) the new
tree-scoped regeneration runs, (d) `CheckGitTree(root, "")` afterwards reports `Fresh: true` while
`CheckFresh(root)` (worktree mode) does **not** — pinning that the two modes are genuinely
different and that the gate's mode is the one the remedy satisfies.

Plus `go test ./internal/hooks -run TestConceptFreshness` asserting the emitted `Detail` names the
tree-scoped command rather than bare `conceptcatalog.RegenerateCommand`.

## Acceptance gate

Both witness tests pass; `go test ./internal/conceptcatalog ./internal/hooks ./cmd/fak -run
'Concept'` green; `scripts/ci.ps1` green. The existing freshness suite
(`internal/conceptcatalog/freshness_test.go:16,49,63,88`) must stay green unmodified — in
particular `TestGeneratedReadmeRoundTripsThroughGitStaging`, which pins the CRLF/LF normalization
from #5136 that the new write path must not re-break. `fak concept generate --staged` in a clean
checkout must produce artifacts identical to `fak concept generate`, so the new mode is provably a
strict refinement rather than a second answer.

## Dependencies

None blocking. Shares a root cause with #5534 (`CONCEPT_ADMISSION`, open) and should land after or
alongside it so both refusals get the same "this gate reads the staged tree" sentence. #5136 and
#5002 (both closed) constrain the byte-comparison path this touches.

## Confusion risks

- **`CheckFresh` and `CheckGitTree` are not interchangeable.** `CheckGitTree` calls `CheckFresh` on
  an *extraction* (`freshness.go:166`); the argument is a tree root, never the repo. Refactoring
  them together is how the peer-dirty bug the git-tree mode exists to avoid gets reintroduced.
- **The artifact is a whole-tree function, not a corpus function.** Staging the corpus files (the
  #5534 remedy) does not make the worktree regen match — a peer's uncommitted `.go` file anywhere
  under `cmd/` or `internal/` moves the counts, measured above.
- **The generator exits 1 on an ACTION verdict.** `freshness.go:182-191` and `cmd/fak/concept.go:80-88`
  both treat non-zero exit as success if every artifact exists. A new write path must keep that
  rule or it will read an honest ACTION snapshot as a generator crash.
- **Do not make the gate read the worktree** to close the gap. That inverts it into the peer-dirty
  failure `CheckGitTree`'s doc comment at `freshness.go:105` was written to prevent, and would make
  one session's refusal depend on another session's unsaved work.

## Likely files

`internal/conceptcatalog/freshness.go`, `internal/hooks/gate_conceptfreshness.go`,
`cmd/fak/concept.go`, `internal/conceptcatalog/freshness_test.go`,
`internal/hooks/gate_conceptfreshness_test.go`

```routing
lane: conceptcatalog
paths: internal/conceptcatalog/**
expected_steps: factor tree-scoped regen out of CheckGitTree; add fak concept generate/freshness --staged; carry the tree-scoped command in FreshnessResult.Regenerate; tests
```

## Parent context

**No epic parent.** This is repo tooling — a pre-commit gate ergonomics defect in the
`conceptcatalog` lane, not fleetbus work, so it is deliberately not filed under #5599/#5600. Its
nearest relative is **#5534**, the same index-vs-worktree split on the sibling `CONCEPT_ADMISSION`
gate; the two are independently dispatchable and neither blocks the other.

## Work unit

leaf

## Work scale

S1

## Expected steps

4

## Assumptions

The gate's tree-scoring is CORRECT — scoring HEAD+pathspec is the only reproducible corpus on a
shared multi-session checkout — and the printed remedy is what is wrong. If the project instead
decides the gate should score the worktree, this leaf inverts and the fix is in
`gate_conceptfreshness.go`, not in the remedy string.

Assumes a contributor hitting this gate is willing to run one extra command, so a correct remedy
(a `--staged`-style regeneration against the same tree the gate scores) is a sufficient fix and
auto-regeneration inside the gate is not required.

## Coordination notes

Lane `conceptcatalog`. `internal/conceptcatalog/freshness.go` and `cmd/fak/concept.go`; the gate
itself (`internal/hooks/gate_conceptfreshness.go`) only needs to keep printing `res.Regenerate`.
This is repo tooling on the shared checkout — every session's commit path runs this gate, so land it
in one commit and do not leave the remedy string half-updated between pushes.

## Trigger

Measured first-hand at HEAD `3a1b7320f0` on 2026-08-06 while trying to land concept-corpus edits:
~6 commits refused by `CONCEPT_FRESHNESS`, ~1 hour lost, cleared only by hand-building the gate's
tree with `GIT_INDEX_FILE` + `read-tree` + `write-tree` + `git archive`. The three-tree table in
**Current state** is that measurement, reproduced from the tree.

## Batch policy

One issue per defect — not batched. A duplicate scan of the existing open backlog found no issue
covering the remedy/scoring mismatch; the dedupe marker is `RegenerateCommand` + `CheckGitTree`.
Contributors who hit this gate repeatedly should update this issue with their case rather than
filing duplicates of the same friction.

## Closure binding

Closes on a commit stamped `(fak conceptcatalog)` that adds the tree-scoped regeneration path and
the `--staged` CLI surface, makes `CONCEPT_FRESHNESS` print it, and lands
`TestRegenerateFromGitTreeClearsTheFreshnessGate` green alongside the unmodified existing freshness
suite.

- **Required model tier:** T2
- **Optimal model tier:** T2

### Related

#5534 (sibling gate, same root cause), #5136, #5002, #5359, #4760

records.title: test(modelaccept): the width corpus grades instruction-following, not the model's own decision to batch
records.body:
## Summary

**Re-scoped.** This issue was originally filed asking for per-turn tool-call WIDTH grading in
`internal/modelaccept`. That work had already landed in #5802 (`f4d84c8eae`), hours before
this was written — see the supersession comment below. Every original acceptance criterion is
met at HEAD.

One genuine remainder survives, and it is a grading-validity problem rather than a missing
feature: **the width task in the acceptance corpus measures instruction-following, not the
model's own decision to batch.**

## Current state

`examples/model-acceptance-agentic-v1.json`, task `parallel-lookup`:

```json
{
  "id": "parallel-lookup",
  "prompt": "Two records must be fetched with the provided read-only lookup tool. Neither
             lookup depends on the other's result, so issue BOTH of them in a single
             assistant turn rather than one after the other. ...",
  "tool_required": true, "min_tool_calls": 2, "min_parallel_tool_calls": 2
}
```

The grading machinery around it is sound — `ToolCallWidth`'s pigeonhole lower bound
(`internal/modelaccept/modelaccept.go:426`) genuinely separates a batched run from a
serialized one, and `TestAgenticCorpusGradesToolCallWidthPerTurn` pins both shapes. The
*task* is what under-specifies the capability:

1. **The prompt tells the model to batch.** "issue BOTH of them in a single assistant turn
   rather than one after the other" converts the task into instruction-following. A model
   that batches only when explicitly told scores identically to one that batches natively —
   but those two models behave very differently on the fleet's real traffic, where nothing
   tells them.
2. **Only one tool is supplied.** That makes it a BFCL *Parallel Function* case at best, and
   never exercises discrimination.

## Why that gap matters (BFCL's categories)

The [Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard](https://openreview.net/pdf?id=2GmDdhBdDk) splits
function calling into **single / multiple / parallel / parallel multiple**. Two are width:

- **Parallel Function** (200 AST / 50 executable) — one user query requiring several calls in
  parallel; **the model must determine how many calls to make**. The determination is the
  graded capability, which a prompt saying "issue both" removes.
- **Parallel Multiple** (200 AST / 40 executable) — several function docs supplied, each
  invoked zero or more times; built adversarially with more docs than queries and some
  functions deliberately unused, so the model must batch **and** filter.

Without the unused-tool arm, the corpus grades batching without grading the discrimination
that makes batching safe — and a model that fires every available tool at once scores well.
That failure mode is the mirror image of the data-dependency risk noted in #5801.

## Proposal

- Add a sibling task that states the goal without prescribing the shape (e.g. "return both
  records"), so width is inferred rather than instructed. Keep `parallel-lookup` as-is: the
  instructed and un-instructed pair is more informative than either alone, and their *delta*
  is precisely "does this model need the nudge #5801 proposes?" — which makes this corpus the
  natural grader for that child.
- Add a **parallel-multiple** arm: supply several tool docs, at least one of which must go
  unused, and fail a run that calls the decoy.
- Record which calling mode the run used. BFCL reports prompt-based function calling as
  generally more flexible than native FC mode in complex scenarios, with the same trend in
  parallel-multiple — so a model grading poorly on width in native mode may be mis-driven
  rather than incapable, and the readout will be misread as a model property if the mode is
  not recorded.
- Keep naming aligned with BFCL's categories so a fak verdict is legible next to a public
  number for the same model, rather than being a third private definition of "parallel call"
  alongside `turnbatch`'s and the fleet monitor's.

**Sampling caveat for anyone citing BFCL here:** the V2 *Live* parallel splits are tiny — 16
parallel and 24 parallel-multiple against 258 simple and 1,037 multiple. Quote the 200-sample
non-live splits.

## Acceptance criteria

- A width task exists whose prompt does **not** instruct batching, and the corpus reports it
  separately from the instructed one.
- A parallel-multiple task supplies at least one tool that must go unused; a run that invokes
  the decoy does not pass.
- The report records the calling mode (native FC vs prompt-based) per run.
- No verdict change for existing corpora — the additions are new tasks, not new gates on old
  ones.

## Related

Part of the tool-call-width epic (#5796). Grading rung landed in #5802; this is the corpus
validity remainder. The instructed/un-instructed delta is the natural grader for #5801.

Parent: #5796

records.title: fix(modver): cmd/fak test binary has not compiled on trunk since 4f564f6fe4 — a committed witness depends on an unlanded trend.go
records.body:
`cmd/fak/version_trend_test.go` landed at `4f564f6fe4` (2026-08-05 22:06 -0700) but the
`internal/modver` change it compiles against never landed. Since then **`go vet ./cmd/fak/`
and `go test ./cmd/fak/` fail to build for every session in the shared checkout**:

```
cmd\fak\version_trend_test.go:98:11: mover.Dormant undefined (type modver.ModuleTrend has no field or method Dormant)
cmd\fak\version_trend_test.go:107:14: dormant.Dormant undefined
```

Reproduced on a **pristine trunk-HEAD worktree** (no local diff), so this is trunk, not a
dirty working tree.

### Why this is P1

`go test ./cmd/fak/` is the acceptance gate named by a large share of open issues. While it
does not build, no `cmd/fak` issue can be closed on a green gate, and any agent that runs it
sees a red that has nothing to do with its own change.

### What is missing

The dependency exists only as **uncommitted working-tree content** in the shared checkout:

| path | state | needed for |
|---|---|---|
| `internal/modver/trend.go` | ` M` (uncommitted, +228/-41) | adds `ModuleTrend.Dormant`, `RevsPerWeek`, `Series` — makes `cmd/fak` **compile** |
| `cmd/fak/version_trend.go` | ` M` (uncommitted, +84) | per-section `--top` cap — makes the committed test **pass** |

### Measured, not assumed

On a detached worktree pinned at trunk HEAD, copying in **only** those two files:

- `go test ./internal/modver/` → `ok` (HEAD's own modver tests pass against the new `trend.go`)
- `go vet ./cmd/fak/ ./internal/modver/` → clean
- `go test ./cmd/fak/ -run 'VersionTrend|Trend'` → `ok` (the committed witness passes)

With `internal/modver/trend.go` alone, `cmd/fak` compiles but
`TestRunVersionTrendJSONTopCapsEachSection` still fails — the two files are **coupled** and
must land together.

### Not simply committable as-is

1. The same author's `internal/modver/regression.go` + `regression_test.go` (both untracked)
   currently **fail**: `TestScoreDropsWarnsOnFixtureRegression` compares a float `Delta` for
   exact equality and gets `-0.30000000000000004` vs `-0.3`. That file is genuinely mid-work
   and must NOT be swept in.
2. Landing `cmd/fak/version_trend.go` trips `CONCEPT_ADMISSION` on its new symbol
   `renderTrendSeries` (family `render-materialize`), and `fak concept classify` currently
   dies in this checkout with `decode planned snapshot: unexpected end of JSON input` — the
   generator renders the *current* corpus fine (valid 5.8 MB JSON, `_meta.json` has its
   `meta:{as_of,fak_version}` block), so the crash is on the *planned* corpus. That is a
   second, separable defect blocking the fix.

### Definition of Done

- `internal/modver/trend.go` and `cmd/fak/version_trend.go` land **together** on trunk.
- `renderTrendSeries` is positioned or classified in the concept corpus, staged in the SAME
  commit (`--path tools/concept_disambiguation_scorecard.data/_meta.json --path .../rows-*.json`).
- `go vet ./cmd/fak/` clean and `go test ./cmd/fak/ -run 'VersionTrend|Trend'` green from a
  clean trunk-HEAD worktree.
- `internal/modver/regression.go` is explicitly **out of scope** — do not land it here.

### Acceptance gate

`go vet ./cmd/fak/ && go test ./cmd/fak/ -run 'VersionTrend|Trend' -count=1 && go test ./internal/modver/ -count=1`

### Parent context

Follow-on to `4f564f6fe4` (`test(cmd): add a --top per-section cap witness over the trend JSON
surface`), which landed the witness without its dependency. Lane: `modver`.

### Closure binding

Closes when a commit stamped `(fak modver)` (or `(fak cmd)`) lands both paths and the
acceptance gate above is green on trunk HEAD.

records.title: fix(pythongate): port-or-delete tools/fleet_regdir*.py — TestNoNewPythonTools is red on main and blocks every tools-lane commit
records.body:
## Problem

`go test ./internal/pythongate -run TestNoNewPythonTools` is **red on `main`** and has been since
5 Aug 2026. Two tracked Python tools are not in the grandfathered baseline:

```
--- FAIL: TestNoNewPythonTools (0.04s)
    2 NEW python tool(s) not in the grandfathered baseline:
      tools/fleet_regdir.py is a NEW python tool; port it to Go instead (NEW_PYTHON_TOOL)
      tools/fleet_regdir_test.py is a NEW python tool; port it to Go instead (NEW_PYTHON_TOOL)
FAIL	github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/internal/pythongate	0.192s
```

## Why it matters

The `tools` lane's refusal mode is "the pre-commit hook refuses the commit until the package is
green." So this does not just fail a test — it **blocks every `tools`-lane commit on trunk**. It was
found while working #5624, whose commit path it blocks independently of that issue's own blockers.

## Evidence

| fact | value |
|---|---|
| introducing commit | `6f98eb4106` `fix(tools): converge the Python fleet registry resolvers on the host ladder (fak tools)` |
| date | Wed 5 Aug 2026 |
| ancestor of `HEAD` | yes |
| `git status --porcelain` on both paths | clean — tracked and committed, not in-flight |
| `internal/pythongate/baseline.go` entries | 593 |
| `git ls-files 'tools/*.py'` | 595 |

The 2-entry gap is exactly these two files. `6f98eb4106` added them without the ratchet ever going
green.

## The fix is NOT to grow the baseline

`internal/pythongate/doc.go` is explicit: the allowlist "can never grow", and `baseline.go` is
regenerated "only to TIGHTEN it after a port-and-delete — never to re-admit a new tool." Appending
these two paths would silently loosen the ratchet and defeat the de-Python policy it exists to
enforce.

So the correct resolutions are, in preference order:

1. Port `fleet_regdir.py` to Go (house pattern: `internal/<name>/` package + `cmd/fak/` shell),
   `git rm` both Python files, then regenerate `baseline.go` by the recipe in `doc.go` (which will
   shrink it, as intended).
2. If the logic already exists in Go and these are dead, delete them and regenerate.

## Non-goals

- Not a change to the pythongate ratchet's policy or its allow/refuse semantics.
- Not a fix for #5624's own blockers (pythongate-vs-spec, and the AF_UNIX transport gap).
- Not a sweep of other Python tooling.

## Witness

`go test ./internal/pythongate -count=1` green on `main`, with `baseline.go` entry count strictly
**lower** than 593 (never higher), and `git ls-files 'tools/*.py'` matching it.

## Routing

Lane: `tools` (tree `tools/**`, `scripts/**`) — currently held exclusive by live holder `w4591`
(pid 80596, acquired 2026-07-18), which is why this is filed rather than fixed. The `internal/pythongate`
half is a separate tree if the port lands there.

records.title: bug(livecodebench): the raw arm cannot distinguish a max_tokens-truncated generation from a complete one
records.body:
## What

`cmd/livecodebench`'s raw arm cannot tell a completed generation from one the sampler
truncated at `--max-tokens`. It records both identically, so a truncated generation is
graded as a wrong answer and pass@1 silently absorbs a harness artifact as if it were
model capability.

## Evidence

`chatCompletionsResponse` (`cmd/livecodebench/raw.go:232`) decodes exactly two things:

```go
type chatCompletionsResponse struct {
	Choices []struct {
		Message agent.Message `json:"message"`
	} `json:"choices"`
	Usage agent.Usage `json:"usage"`
}
```

There is no `finish_reason` field, so the value never reaches the harness, and
`gatewaySampler` returns only `out.Choices[0].Message.Content` (`raw.go:207`).

Witnessed on a live datacenter-GPU serve of Qwen3.6-27B through fak's own in-kernel CUDA
forward. Every real LiveCodeBench problem came back at exactly the cap:

```
{"completion_tokens":2048, ...}   # every request, never a natural stop
{"event":"gateway_http_request","path":"/v1/chat/completions","duration_ms":312952.549}
```

`completion_tokens` equal to `--max-tokens` on every single request is the signature of
universal truncation, and the report carries no field that would say so.

## Why it matters

This is a benchmark honesty defect, not a cosmetic one. A reasoning-style model spends
its budget thinking before it emits the fenced answer, so at a small `--max-tokens` the
run can score ~0 while the model is never actually asked to finish. Read off the current
report, that is indistinguishable from "the model cannot solve these problems". The
report is the artifact the evidence-class rules are supposed to make trustworthy, so it
must not be able to hide the difference.

There is a second, related drop in the same struct: models that split output into
`reasoning_content` + `content` have their answer discarded entirely when the budget is
spent mid-thought, because only `content` is read. That is the same root cause — the
decoder keeps content and throws away every other signal about how the generation ended.

## Proposed fix

1. Decode `finish_reason` per choice; thread it into the per-sample record.
2. Count truncated samples in the report and surface the tally in the summary line.
3. Refuse `result_claim_allowed: true` when any sample was truncated — a run that hit the
   cap has not measured the model, and should say so rather than publish a number.
4. Fall back to `reasoning_content` when `content` is empty, and mark such a sample as
   reasoning-only so it is never silently graded as an attempted answer.

## Acceptance

`go test ./cmd/livecodebench/...` covering: a `finish_reason: "length"` response is
recorded as truncated; a report containing a truncated sample cannot carry
`result_claim_allowed: true`; an empty `content` with non-empty `reasoning_content` is
retained and flagged rather than dropped.

records.title: fix(quality): the god-file ratchet is red on committed trunk — 4 offenses at HEAD (serve.go, dispatch_tick_preflight.go, anthropic_compact.go, main.go:main)
records.body:
## Problem

The god-file/god-function growth ratchet is RED on **committed trunk**, not just in the
peer-dirty worktree. Measured in a clean room built from `git archive HEAD`
(HEAD = `bdd7e1ab62e746fc4627df023d345fb88ebc45d8`), four offenses are real at HEAD:

|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cmd/fak/dispatch_tick_preflight.go` | 1559 lines | 1559 | 1500 (no baseline entry) | YES — NEW god-file |
| `cmd/fak/serve.go` | 1563 lines | 1565 | 1500 (no baseline entry) | YES — NEW god-file |
| `internal/agent/anthropic_compact.go` | 1507 lines | 1507 | 1500 (no baseline entry) | YES — NEW god-file |
| `cmd/fak/main.go:main` | span 582 | span 582 | frozen 482, +20% slack = 578 | YES — grandfathered GREW |
| `cmd/fak/dispatch_tick.go:evaluateDispatchTick` | span 388 | span 406 | frozen 304, +20% slack = 364 | no — uncommitted peer growth only |
| `internal/gateway/messages.go` (sibling gate) | 1740 lines | 1771 | 1739 pin (`internal/godfileceiling`) | YES — grew past pin by 1 |

Both ratchets are red:

- `go test ./internal/hooks/ -run TestGodfileGate_LiveTreeClean` — 5 offenses over the live tree, 4 of them present at HEAD.
- `go test ./internal/godfileceiling/` — 4 files over cap, including `internal/gateway/messages.go` 1740 > 1739 at HEAD.
- `fak hygiene --gates GOD_FILE_GROWTH` exits 1.

`fak hooks pre-push` still exits 0, so pushes are not wedged — this is a CI/hygiene red, not a fleet push wedge.

## Which commit crossed each line

All four are ancestors of HEAD:

- `dispatch_tick_preflight.go` 1478 -> 1559 at `5491894c2a` (2026-08-05, stallscan lane).
- `serve.go` 1489 -> 1501 at `e8e869073f` (2026-08-05), then 1503 -> 1563 at `ce82ee62cc` (2026-08-06).
- `anthropic_compact.go` 1491 -> 1507, and `internal/gateway/messages.go` 1733 -> 1740, both at `79e72951ee` (2026-08-05).
- `main.go:main` span 578 -> 582 at `3f985b6c97` (2026-08-06).

`evaluateDispatchTick` is clean at HEAD only because `longFuncs` collects a function
solely when its span exceeds `godFuncMaxLines` (400). Its frozen+slack ceiling is 364, so
between 365 and 400 lines it is shielded from its own stated ceiling. At HEAD it sits at
388 — inside that shielded band. A peer's uncommitted +18 lines push it to 406, past the
400 collection floor, at which point it is compared against 364 and reds.

is under its ceiling, then regenerate `internal/hooks/godfile_baseline.go` with
`FAK_GODFILE_BASELINE_REGEN=1` and re-pin `internal/godfileceiling`. Do NOT raise a ceiling
or regenerate the baseline upward to clear the red — the baseline's contract is that entries
may only shrink or disappear, never grow.

records.title: fix(hooks): the god-file gate's fast-path skip is keyed to godFuncMaxLines alone, so raising FAK_GODFUNC_MAX_LINES silently disables the FILE ceiling
records.body:
## Problem

`godfileScanTree` in `internal/hooks/gate_godfile.go` uses a single fast-path skip keyed to
the FUNCTION ceiling alone:

```go
lines := countLines(body)
if lines <= godFuncMaxLines {
    continue
}
```

The comment justifies it as "Files at or under godFuncMaxLines lines are skipped whole —
they can hold neither a god-file nor a god-function." That reasoning only holds while
`godFuncMaxLines <= godFileMaxLines`. Both are operator-tunable:

```go
godFileMaxLines = gateEnvInt("FAK_GODFILE_MAX_LINES", 1500)
godFuncMaxLines = gateEnvInt("FAK_GODFUNC_MAX_LINES", 400)
```

Set `FAK_GODFUNC_MAX_LINES=2000` and every file under 2000 lines is skipped before the FILE
ceiling is ever evaluated — so the 1500-line god-file rule silently stops firing for exactly
the band it exists to police. Loosening the FUNCTION dimension silently disables the FILE
dimension.

This is reachable by an operator following the gate's own advice: `godfileFixHint`, printed
on every finding, says "widen the growth slack or raise the ceiling for the run
(FAK_GODFILE_GROWTH_SLACK_PCT / FAK_GODFILE_MAX_LINES / FAK_GODFUNC_MAX_LINES)".

## Fix

The correct fast-path threshold is the lower of the two ceilings:

```go
if lines <= min(godFileMaxLines, godFuncMaxLines) {
    continue
}
```

Under the shipped defaults (1500 / 400) `min` is 400, so this is a **no-op on the current
tree** — it cannot change any verdict today and cannot launder an existing red. It only
closes the tunable-coupling hole.

## Secondary observation (not part of this fix)

`longFuncs` collects a function only when `span > godFuncMaxLines` (400). A grandfathered
function whose frozen+slack ceiling is below 400 is therefore shielded from its own stated
ceiling in the band between that ceiling and 400. Concrete live case:
`cmd/fak/dispatch_tick.go:evaluateDispatchTick` is frozen at 304, slack ceiling 364, and
sits at 388 lines on committed HEAD — over its stated ceiling but under the 400 collection
floor, so it does not red. The finding text ("past its frozen ceiling 304 (+20% growth
slack = 364)") therefore overstates how tightly the gate actually binds a grandfathered
function. Tightening that would red additional existing code, so it wants its own decision
and its own issue; recorded here only so the next reader does not mistake it for a bug in
the fix above.

## Parent context

Parent epic #2653 (pre-push the live-tree governance ratchets) and #2936 (god-file
containment gate). Found while attributing the live ratchet red tracked in #5849.

## Acceptance gate

A test in `internal/hooks/gate_godfile_test.go` that sets `FAK_GODFUNC_MAX_LINES` above
`FAK_GODFILE_MAX_LINES` over a synthetic file between the two ceilings, and asserts the
FILE-dimension finding still fires. It fails before the one-line change and passes after.
`go test ./internal/hooks/` verdicts over the live tree are unchanged by the fix.

## Closure binding

Closed by the witnessed commit landing the one-line fix plus its regression test, bound via
`dos commit-audit`.

## Witness

The new regression test above, failing before and passing after — the repro is the proof.

Estimate: 1 points. Uncertainty: operator-supplied estimate; revise through the parent denominator when evidence changes.

Contribution: 1/100 points.

records.title: feat(experiments): route #3546's steerability A/B through the #3568 negframe_reframe lever instead of hand-authored arm fixtures
records.body:
Carved out of #3568 (its last unmet DoD refinement) so #3568 can close on the evidence it actually has.

## The gap

#3568 shipped the lever and the per-turn signal: `FAK_ABLATE=negframe_reframe` (or a sweep child's `FAK_ABLATE_NEGFRAME_REFRAME=0`) routes fak-authored SessionStart prose UNREFRAMED, an unset env REFRAMES it, and `fak guard`'s exit summary folds one line naming the active arm.

Its final refinement said the consumer should follow:

> #3546's A/B consumes this lever: its control arm runs `FAK_ABLATE=negframe_reframe` over a measured stream (cross-linked on #3546), replacing hand-swapped strings with one env toggle.

That never happened. `experiments/negframe-steerability-ab/` (dated 2026-07-09, **before** the lever landed) contains ZERO references to `FAK_ABLATE`, `negframe_reframe`, or `guardNegframeReframe`:

```
git grep -n "FAK_ABLATE\|negframe_reframe\|ReframeFakOnly\|guardNegframeReframe" -- experiments/negframe-steerability-ab/*
(no output)
```

It scores a **hand-authored** paired corpus (`fx.ArmA` negative-framed / `fx.ArmB` reframed, `fixtures.go`) through `negframe.Classify`, and reports a *modeled* compliance delta — exactly the hand-swapped-strings shape #3568 was written to retire. #3546 is CLOSED, so this consumer wiring currently has no home.

## Non-goals

- Re-opening #3546 or re-litigating its modeled-compliance result.
- Any change to the lever, the journal row, or the exit-summary line (all shipped and gated under #3568).

## Definition of Done

- [ ] The experiment's control arm is produced by running the measured path under `FAK_ABLATE=negframe_reframe` rather than by reading `fx.ArmA`, with the treatment arm being the same path with the env unset.
- [ ] The experiment reads the per-turn journal rows (`.fak/negframe/journal.jsonl`, `arm`/`applied`/`residual`/`verbatim_fallback`) as its measured signal, so the arm label in the report comes from the run rather than from fixture construction.
- [ ] `go test ./experiments/negframe-steerability-ab -count=1` green, with a test asserting the two arms are produced by the env toggle (a fixture-only corpus reds it).
- [ ] The report distinguishes MEASURED from MODELED compliance, or states plainly that it remains modeled.

## Witness

`go test ./experiments/negframe-steerability-ab -count=1`; the emitted report JSON showing an arm label sourced from the journal.

records.title: fix(accounts): `fak accounts headroom` is cooldown-blind — prints a cooled seat as OFFERABLE while `fak accounts cooldown` reports it walled
records.body:
## Symptom

At a single instant, the two account verbs disagreed about the same bucket:

- `fak accounts headroom` reported the bucket at `+2` (OFFERABLE band).
- `fak accounts cooldown` reported that same bucket walled by a genuine active
  `usage-limit` cooldown.

## Root cause

`cmd/fak/accounts_headroom.go` had **two** producers of the headroom signal and only one of
them applied the durable cooldown override:

- `rotationHeadroom` (the rotation planner's producer) called `headroomFromRoster(...)` and
  then folded in `applyCooldownToHeadroom(...)` from the fleet-shared cooldown store.
- `runAccountsHeadroom` (the `headroom` display verb) called `headroomFromRoster(...)`
  **directly**, skipping the override entirely.

So the verb printed the live roster's offerability read, which lags or misses a cap that fired
seconds ago, while the cooldown store held the certain, fresher walled signal.

## Why it matters

Display-path only today — nothing in the tree consumes the `headroom` verb's JSON
(`fak.accounts-headroom.v1`); the only dispatch site is `cmd/fak/accounts.go`'s subcommand
switch, and the rotation planner uses the *other*, correct producer. But it is exactly the
misleading signal that tempts an operator (or an agent) into `fak accounts cooldown --clear`
on an account that is really rate-limited, burning spawn attempts against a walled seat.

## Fix

Route both producers through one fold, `rosterHeadroom(rows, now)` = roster tiering +
cooldown override, so the two paths cannot drift apart again.

Regression tests in `cmd/fak/accounts_headroom_test.go`:
`TestAccountsHeadroomVerbHonorsCooldown` (end-to-end on the verb's JSON) and
`TestRosterHeadroomWallsCooledOfferableBucket` (the exact offerable-row-plus-active-cooldown
misread).

records.title: dispatch wave: scraped directory tokens make issues universal colliders; pricer-only narrowing yields phantom concurrency
records.body:
## The bug (real, reproduced)

`dispatchtick.ExtractIssueRepoPaths` (`internal/dispatchtick/router.go:625`, regex `:49`) scrapes repo
paths out of issue prose and routinely yields a bare **directory** token (`cmd/fak`, `internal/recall`)
alongside real file paths. `fak dispatch wave` feeds that raw set straight into the pairwise
tree-collision pricer, and collision is literal directory-prefix containment
(`internal/dispatchorder/dispatchorder.go:1154-1162 treeOverlap`, after `normalizeTree` `:1165` strips
`/**`). So a bare `cmd/fak` **contains every `cmd/fak/*.go`**, making that issue a universal collider
that serializes its whole lane.

Amplifier: `dispatchWaveOrderStamp` (`cmd/fak/dispatch_wave.go:665`) gives core-source trees a `+1e6`
boost, so the universal collider sorts **first** in `greedySafeSet` and is admitted ahead of everyone
it blocks.

Measured on the cached backlog (`.fak/dispatch/backlog.json`, 1110 issues, `IssueLimit: 1000` matching
`dispatchRoutedBeforePrereqHold`) → 157 routed / 153 scoped candidates. **99 of 156 scoped issues carry
a redundant directory token.**

## Why the obvious fix does NOT work — this is the load-bearing part

The tempting fix is to decouple the two uses of the path set: let the **pricer** see a narrowed
(file-level) set while `--lease-tree` (`cmd/fak/dispatch_wave.go:833`) keeps the **coarse**
(directory) set, so a worker never loses the lease coverage it needs to edit an unnamed sibling file.

That is exactly what a prototype did. **It produces phantom concurrency and must not ship.**

The wave prices on the narrow set, but it still launches each worker with the coarse `--lease-tree`,
and *two runtime gates re-impose the coarse geometry*:

1. `cmd/fak/dispatch_tick.go:946` — `treeCollisionFromScopes(liveScopes, pick.Tree)`, where
   `live.Tree` is read from the coarse `.lease-tree.json` sidecar.
2. `cmd/fak/dispatch_tick.go:1119` — `acquireDispatchLaneLease(..., pick.Tree, ...)` →
   `internal/regionadmit/regionadmit.go:287`, which refuses with `RungTreeOverlap` using the **same**
   `dispatchorder.TreesOverlap`.

So issue A (`cmd/fak` + `cmd/fak/foo.go`) and issue B (`cmd/fak/bar.go`) price as disjoint, both get
launched, and B is then refused at lease acquire because A holds a live lease over `cmd/fak`.

### Measured: priced safe set vs. concurrency actually reached

Offline over the cached backlog. "priced" = `len(dispatchorder.Plan(...).Keep)`. "effective" = walking
that safe set in dispatch order and admitting only while the **coarse** trees stay pairwise disjoint,
i.e. simulating the runtime lease gate.

| scope | priced before | priced after | **effective before** | **effective after** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| whole backlog (153 cands) | 22 | 42 | **22** | **21** |
| lane `cmd` (36) | 9 | 13 | **9** | **9** |
| lane `docs` (23) | 12 | 13 | **12** | **12** |
| lane `gateway` (16) | 3 | 8 | **3** | **1** |

The priced safe set nearly doubles (22 → 42) and collision edges halve (2676 → 1272), but real
concurrency is **flat or worse**. `gateway` drops 3 → 1 because narrowing reorders the greedy pick, so
a candidate admitted early on narrow geometry blocks more successors on its coarse tree than the
pre-change pick did.

Net effect if shipped: the fleet spawns ~2x workers that immediately take a `COLLISION_RISK` hold or a
`RungTreeOverlap` lease refusal — burning account seats and marking cooldown attempts — for zero
throughput. A prior projection of "cmd-lane safe set 11 → 93" does **not** reproduce; I measure 9 → 13
priced and 9 → 9 effective.

## What would actually fix it

The lease record currently conflates two different geometries:

- **admission** geometry — "may these two workers run at once?" (`regionadmit.Decide`,
  `treeCollisionFromScopes`, the wave pricer). Wants the **narrow**, file-level set.
- **authorization** geometry — "which files is this worker allowed to write?"
  (`dispatchPathInLeaseTree` at `cmd/fak/dispatch_tick_witness.go:706`, `internal/gitgate` via
  `cleanLeaseTree` at `gitgate.go:390`). Must stay **coarse**, or workers get blocked committing an
  unnamed sibling file.

Narrowing only the pricer splits the first use in one place and leaves it coarse in two others, which
is why it fails. The fix is to carry **both** trees end to end: lease record + `.lease-tree.json`
sidecar gain an admission tree distinct from the authorization tree; `regionadmit.Decide` and
`treeCollisionFromScopes` adjudicate on the admission tree; `gitgate` / `dispatchPathInLeaseTree` keep
using the authorization tree. Touches `internal/leaseref`, `internal/regionadmit`, `internal/gitgate`,
`cmd/fak/dispatch_tick.go`, `cmd/fak/dispatch_wave.go`.

Because that is a schema change on the live lease path with a standing dispatch cron running, it is
deliberately **not** being shipped as a drive-by.

## Next checkable step

1. Add the second tree to the lease record + sidecar behind a reader that defaults it to the
   authorization tree (so old sidecars keep today's exact behavior).
2. Switch `regionadmit.Decide` and `treeCollisionFromScopes` to the admission tree.
3. Re-run the effective-concurrency measurement above; the acceptance bar is **effective** (not
   priced) concurrency rising on `gateway` and `cmd`, with `gateway` never regressing below 3.

Not `#4320` — that one is closed and targeted the lease *fallback*, a different surface.

records.title: fix(dispatch): teach worker fuel that a kernel refusal is a PAUSE, and to checkpoint-commit
records.body:
## Problem

Forensics over 111 failed `FleetIssueDispatch` worker sessions: ~80% produce NO
COMMIT. Two of the measured root causes are prompt-shaped, and both worker fuels
carry them.

1. **Capability-floor stop (18/111, 16%).** The worker's turn is refused by the
   kernel and the session simply ENDS (`end_turn`). This is a misread: a
   `REQUIRE_WITNESS` / preview-confirm refusal is a **PAUSE**, not a denial. Its
   own `dos.toml` entry says so ("A pause, not a terminal denial") and names two
   sanctioned resolutions: the compiled sidestep (e.g. `fak sync push` for a
   gated `git push`), or re-proposing the identical call with the `_fak_confirm`
   key. Neither fuel mentioned `REQUIRE_WITNESS`, `_fak_confirm`, or the sidestep
   at all; the only refusal guidance they carried was "honor a REFUSE (pick
   nothing and stop)", which actively teaches quitting.

2. **No checkpoint-commit (~5/111 directly, amplifies every other mode).** Commit
   was step 4-5, gated behind a full green `make ci`, with no instruction to
   commit incrementally. The median session is killed at 8-10 minutes and 27 of
   37 killed workers already held edits, so edits reliably die uncommitted. This
   is why ~130 files sit stranded in the shared tree from dead workers.

3. **Early sanctioned bail.** The rendered dispatch prompt's FIRST sentence
   offers "— OR end with a final report naming the exact gate you could not reach
   and why", inviting a give-up before any attempt.

## Done

`.claude/goal-prompts/resolve-top-issue-witnessed.md` (the `super-loop` /
`/goal` fuel) now carries all three fixes, still under the 4000-char `/goal` cap:

- a new "A refusal is a PAUSE, not the end of your run" section with the two
  sanctioned `REQUIRE_WITNESS` resolutions, the terminal-vs-pause test, and an
  explicit "never end a session by reporting a refusal as your result";
- a checkpoint-commit step whose honest bar is *compiles* (`fak commit`'s
  `COMMITTED_RED` gate) + *its own targeted test passes*, explicitly lower than
  the ship bar but never licensing broken or unverified work, with `Fixes #N`
  held back for the real fix;
- the bail moved out of the opening and conditioned on having attempted the
  sanctioned adaptation first (the honest escape hatch is preserved).

## Remaining

The **standing dispatcher does not use that `.md`.** It renders its own prompt
from `tools/issue_worker_prompt.py` (imported by `tools/issue_resolve_dispatch.py`;
see any `.dispatch-runs/resolve-*.prompt.txt`). A Go twin renders the same packet
from `internal/dispatchtick/prompt.go` + `promptrules.go`.

Both still need the same three fixes. This half is **blocked on the `tools` lane
lease**, which is held by a live loop (`dos arbitrate` REFUSED it; the lane
journal shows the same refusal to a peer). Note also that
`internal/dispatchtick/prompt.go` currently has ~20h-stale uncommitted edits from
a dead worker and depends on an untracked `promptrules.go`, so the two renderers
are one atomic unit spanning the busy lane — landing only the Go half would red
the build and trip the Go/Python rule-parity test.

## Acceptance

- `tools/issue_worker_prompt.py` and `internal/dispatchtick/prompt.go` carry the
  refusal-taxonomy and checkpoint-commit guidance, and the first-sentence bail is
  conditioned rather than offered up front.
- Any refusal token added to the packet is one the live registry declares
  (`internal/promptlint` lints the rendered prompt; `TRUST_VIOLATION` and
  `SECRET_EXFIL` are NOT declared here and would red the freshness gate).
- Rule-table changes stay mirrored across the Go spec and the Python renderer
  (`TestPythonRendererMirrorsTheGoRuleSpec` requires equal rule-ID sets).
- Capability-floor `end_turn` sessions drop from their 16% baseline.

records.title: fix(dispatch): worker guard resolves an unrefreshed in-repo fak.exe ahead of PATH — fleet ran a 34-commit-stale, dirty binary
records.body:
## Summary

`FakSelfUpdate` keeps **one** `fak.exe` fresh — the one on `PATH`. But the two
dispatch code paths that actually front workers resolve to **build artifacts that
nothing ever refreshes**, so the fleet runs `fak guard` from a binary that can be
tens of commits and hours behind trunk, built from a peer-dirty tree.

Witnessed tonight: the worker guard binary was **34 commits behind HEAD** and
stamped `+dirty`.

## The three binaries on this host

| Path | Stamp (`fak version --json`) | Built | Behind HEAD | Refreshed by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `C:\Users\USER\bin\fak.exe` (PATH) | `b225bb1ca2`, clean | 21:07 | 1 (doc-only) | **`FakSelfUpdate`, every 20 min** |
| `C:\work\fak\tools\.bin\fak.exe` | `394f65f0a4`, **+dirty** | 17:20 | **34** | *nothing* |
| `C:\work\fak\fak.exe` | `84bd6ac27f`, **+dirty** | 19:08 | 16 | *nothing* |
| `C:\Users\USER\go\bin\fak.exe` | **unstamped** | Jul 16 | ~3 weeks | *nothing* (used by `FleetSlackBeat`) |

## Mechanism

Two resolvers prefer an in-repo artifact **ahead of** `PATH`:

- `tools/dispatch_worker.py:887` `resolve_fak_bin()` — precedence
  `$FAK_BIN` → `tools/.bin/fak.exe` → `PATH`. Used at `dispatch_worker.py:1099`
  to wrap **every dispatched worker** in `fak guard`. `$FAK_BIN` is unset on this
  host and `tools/.bin/fak.exe` exists, so every worker got the 34-commit-old dirty build.
- `tools/issue_resolve_dispatch.py:664` `_fak_command_prefix()` — precedence
  `$FAK_BIN` → `<root>/fak.exe` → `go run ./cmd/fak`. Used at
  `issue_resolve_dispatch.py:806` for `fak issue contract --live`.

Meanwhile `_fak_bin()` (`issue_resolve_dispatch.py:3169`, the lease gate) uses
`shutil.which("fak")` → the **fresh** PATH binary. So a single dispatcher tick
mixes two different `fak` builds.

`cmd/fak/selfupdate.go:144-184` is correct and does the right thing — it builds
from a **pristine detached `origin/main` worktree**, never the peer-dirty tree,
which is why the PATH binary is clean. Its `--target` is just a single path, so
the other copies are outside its reach.

## Behavioral witness

`1edb247cd2` (20:57) made `fak accounts headroom` cooldown-aware (#5853). With
`aug5-netra` genuinely cooled, the two binaries disagree **right now**:

```
OLD tools/.bin (394f65f0a4): "uuid:55860c22-...":2    <- OFFERABLE, the #5853 misread
NEW              (b225bb1ca2): "uuid:55860c22-...":-1  <- walled, correct
```

Symbol-table confirmation: `go tool nm` finds `main.rosterHeadroom` (introduced by
`1edb247cd2`) in the PATH binary and **not** in `tools/.bin/fak.exe`.

## Can `fak version` answer the staleness question?

**Yes — this part already works, and is not the bug.** `cmd/fak/version.go:33`
`cmdVersion` prints `appversion.Current()` on line 1 (which reads the *tree's*
VERSION file and therefore *can* mislead — documented at `version.go:15-32`), then
`debug.ReadBuildInfo()` → `buildProvenanceLine` (`version.go:159`) reads
`vcs.revision` / `vcs.time` / `vcs.modified`. That is a genuine embedded stamp that
travels with the binary. `fak version --json` (`version.go:65`) exposes it as
`{commit, dirty, stamped}` and is the right probe.

The gap is **not** that we cannot tell. It is that **nobody asks** at dispatch time.

## Proposed fix

1. **Resolution precedence** — in `resolve_fak_bin()` and `_fak_command_prefix()`,
   prefer the freshest stamped binary rather than a fixed path order: keep `$FAK_BIN`
   first (explicit operator intent), then compare `fak version --json`'s `commit`
   against `git rev-parse HEAD` and pick a clean, current one; treat `dirty:true` or
   `stamped:false` as disqualifying when a clean alternative exists.
2. **Assert at tick time** — have `issue_resolve_dispatch.py` emit a
   `binary_freshness` field in its `--json` tick output (chosen path, commit, dirty,
   commits-behind-HEAD) so `dispatch_status.py` surfaces drift instead of hiding it.
   `internal/binstamp` already models exactly this (`Freshness`/`Cause`, consumed by
   `cmd/fak/doctor.go:406` `runningStampFreshness`) — reuse it rather than add a
   second notion of fresh.
3. **Widen the refresh** — either point `FakSelfUpdate` at every known install path,
   or delete `tools/.bin/fak.exe` and `./fak.exe` after use so resolution falls
   through to the one binary that *is* maintained.

Related but distinct: #3764 (Defender scans all 3 copies), #3668 (stallscan's
deployed binary stale).

## Mitigation already applied

`tools/.bin/fak.exe` and `./fak.exe` were refreshed in place from the clean
`b225bb1ca2` PATH binary (rename-then-place; live workers finish on the old copy).
That is a **one-shot manual patch that will re-rot** the next time anything rebuilds
those artifacts from a dirty tree — the precedence fix above is the durable one.

records.title: fix(guard): lane-scoped, account-blind goal park disables a whole lane for every account (33% of no-commit worker sessions)
records.body:
`fak guard`'s long-`Retry-After` goal park (#4805) is **lane-scoped and account-blind**, so ONE
account's 1-hour 429 disables an entire lane for **every** account until the park's timestamp
elapses — while the dispatcher keeps dispatching into that lane and `fak guard` kills each child
mid-`tool_use`: no report, no commit, median ~8 minutes in, most already holding uncommitted edits.

Measured across 111 failed worker sessions: **37 of 111 no-commit sessions (33%)**. `quality`
lane shipped 1/18; `gateway` shipped 0/10. This is the fleet's single largest throughput leak.

## Three defects

1. **The park check is account-blind.** `cmd/fak/guard_child_supervision.go:guardGoalParked`
   returned `parked` from `rec.ClaimedAt == 0 && rec.ParkedUntil > now`, never consulting
   `rec.Account`. All three call sites in the supervision loop consult it **before**
   `rotation.rotateAfterExit`, so a positive verdict short-circuits account rotation entirely —
   the one mechanism that could have moved the run to a healthy seat.

2. **`DISPATCH_ACCOUNT` was never wired into the child env.** `cmd/fak/dispatch_tick_worker.go:dispatchWorkerEnv`
   receives `account dispatchtick.Account` and sets `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` / `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` / `CODEX_HOME`
   from it, but never `DISPATCH_ACCOUNT`. `cmd/fak/guard.go`'s park template reads
   `os.Getenv("DISPATCH_ACCOUNT")`, so **every one of the 27 live records carries a blank account** —
   which, combined with (1), is why a park walls everyone.

3. **A park never retires.** Nothing in the product ever called `goalpark.Store.ClaimDue` — only the
   `fak goal-park claim` CLI, which no automation invokes — so `claimed_at` is `0` in all 27 records
   and the resume every record's own `next_legal_action` promises ("wait until parked_until; then
   supervisor atomically claims and resumes the same command") never happens. `Retry-After` is also
   unclamped, so an oversized or mis-scaled value parks for months.

## Fix

- `goalpark.Record.Blocks(account, now)` — the ONE predicate every reader uses. A blank
  `Record.Account` blocks **nobody** (a record that cannot name whose wall it is has no one to stop);
  a foreign account blocks nobody; only the walled account waits, and only until `parked_until`.
- `goalpark.Store.Resolve(goal, account, supervisor, now)` — the single supervisor seam. It applies
  `Blocks`, and when the wait HAS elapsed it claims the record on the spot (the guard asking the
  question *is* the supervisor resuming that goal), so a due park retires exactly once instead of
  accumulating. Fails open on any load error: over-parking is the failure this seam exists to prevent.
- `goalpark.MaxWait` (24h) clamps `parked_until` at write time.
- `dispatchWorkerEnv` sets `DISPATCH_ACCOUNT` from the chosen seat (tag, else config-dir base), and
  **deletes** it for an anonymous seat so a child never inherits the tick's stale identity.
- `parkGoalIdentity()` in `cmd/fak` is the single source the park writer and the park reader both use,
  so the two can never disagree about whose wall a record is.

Related: #4805 introduced the park. #3523 is adjacent (park-and-retry on `REFUSE_NO_ACCOUNT`) but different.

records.title: fix(dispatch): ACTIVE_COMPACT_RUNAWAY latches after recovery and holds the whole fleet for one lane's worker
records.body:
## Symptom (observed 2026-08-06 ~21:36 PDT)

```
planner   : claude #4334 lane=tools held ACTIVE_COMPACT_RUNAWAY age=3.3m next=wait-for-loop-worker-to-exit-or-fix-compact-control
use       : HEADROOM_HELD slots=4/24 free=20 next=wait-for-loop-worker-to-exit-or-fix-compact-control
limiter   : configured_max (cap=24 live=4 headroom=20 max=24 seats=24 free=14 leased=4 lane_leases=0/3)
```

**20 of 24 slots idle behind one worker.** Two independent defects combine to produce it.

### Read the status line correctly first
`#4334` is **not** the runaway worker — it is `target_issue`, the issue the tick *wanted to
launch* and refused (`dispatch_status.py:4078-4087`). The runaway was **#4568 on lane
`quality`**. The reported number is the victim, not the culprit; this misdirects diagnosis
and is worth a separate status-line clarification.

## Defect 1 — the hold latches; it never clears on recovery

`_compact_runaway_from_log` (`tools/issue_resolve_dispatch.py:539-603`) scans the worker log
and counts **all-time** turns >= `ACTIVE_COMPACT_RUNAWAY_MIN_PAST_K` (20k) past compact,
firing at `MIN_COUNT` (3). It has no recency window, so once a worker has *ever* overshot 3
times, the hold is latched for the rest of that worker's life.

Its own docstring claims "several **consecutive** tool turns" — consecutiveness was never
implemented.

#4568's real trajectory (58 tool turns):

| turns | ctx | state |
|---|---|---|
| 52-58 | 98.0 -> 109.3 / 96 | drifts past budget |
| 61 | **109.3 -> 70.6** | **compaction FIRED, shed 39k** |
| 71-79 | 126.3 -> 134.1 / 96 | overshoots again (9 hits >= 20k -> latch) |
| 86 | **134.1 -> 68.1** | **compaction FIRED AGAIN, shed 66k** |
| 86-96 | 68.1 -> 93.3 / 96 | healthy, under budget, still progressing |

**Compact control was working.** It shed twice and recovered the worker both times. The
worker took 17 more tool turns and was still writing its log. The hold nonetheless still
reported `active` — it was describing an overshoot that had been cured ~17 turns earlier.

Same shape as the lane goal-park that outlived the 429 that caused it: *a hold that
outlives the condition it was raised for, with no expiry and no clearing verb.*

## Defect 2 — a lane-local fault taking a fleet-wide hold

`active_compact_runaway_hold` (`:606-653`) never records **which lane** a runaway burns, and
the call site (`:5662-5676`) returns before reaching any lane logic. So a runaway on
`quality` blocked dispatch to `tools`, `session`, `gateway` — every disjoint lane.

A compact runaway is *one worker's local context state*. It justifies not stacking a second
worker on the **same** lane. It is no reason to idle 20 slots on unrelated lanes.

Third instance tonight of one recurring shape: **one unit's local condition escalates into a
fleet-wide block, and the fleet waits instead of routing around it** (cf. the goal-park with
no expiry, and a lane lease held by a worker dead since 2026-07-18). The common root
assumption is that a worker-scoped fault is a fleet-scoped fact.

## Fix

1. **Recency**: a compaction *shed* (ctx dropping >= `ACTIVE_COMPACT_RUNAWAY_SHED_K` = 5k
   below the previous turn) is positive proof compact control just worked — clear the
   accumulated hits. Context only grows within a compaction cycle, so a drop that large has
   no other cause. The hold now describes compact control failing **now**, not once.
2. **Lane scope**: stamp each candidate with its lane (`_spawn_header_lane`, already used by
   the lane-lease gate) and hold only when the runaway's lane collides with the tick's
   chosen lane. **Fails closed** when any lane is unknown (unreadable spawn header) — an
   unparseable header cannot prove disjointness.
3. Report `scoped_lane` / `collides` / `sheds` in the payload so a scoped-past runaway is
   never a silent drop.

## Verification

Against the live tree, the hold went `active: true` -> `active: false` — #4568 shows
`sheds: 2` with only 2 post-shed hits (below the count floor). No worker was killed; #4568
was healthy and progressing throughout, and killing it would have destroyed uncommitted work.

## Follow-ons (not in this change)

- `ACTIVE_GUARD_LIVELOCK` (`:490-536`) has the **identical** lane-blind shape — its
  candidates carry no lane and its call site (`:5647-5661`) holds fleet-wide. Same fix applies.
- The `planner` status line should name the runaway worker, not just the held target issue.
- There is still no operator verb to clear a genuine runaway; the only exit is worker exit.

records.title: A dead worker's lane lease blocks its lane forever: acquire never applies the kernel's own dead-lease filter, and no reap verb is exposed
records.body:
## Symptom

The `tools` lane was held by worker `w4591` from **2026-07-18** until tonight (**2026-08-06**) — 19 days. Every peer that asked for the lane was refused:

```
$ dos lease-lane acquire --lane tools --owner <peer>
reason = lane 'tools' is already held by a live loop - pick a different --lane or wait.
```

Lane-journal seq 2294 shows the same refusal issued to an unrelated peer (`harvest-recovery`), so this was chronic, not a race. `w4591` had been dead the whole time.

## The holder was provably dead, and the kernel can already prove it

```
$ python -c "from dos import proc_delta; print(proc_delta.probe(80596, host_id='DESKTOP-BB3FMHP', this_host='DESKTOP-BB3FMHP', recorded_starttime=134288779379632999))"
ProcLiveness(alive=False, detail='pid 80596 is gone (win32 INVALID_PARAMETER)')
```

Same host, so the local pid+`proc_starttime` probe is authoritative (no cross-host TTL overlay needed). Both arms of the kernel's own `_lease_is_dead` predicate (`lane_lease.py:224`) were satisfied: heartbeat-stale far past TTL **and** confirmed-dead holder pid.

## Root cause

`lane_lease.live_leases(config, *, expire_dead: bool = False)` — the dead-lease filter is **opt-in and defaults OFF**. `acquire()` (`lane_lease.py:389`) deliberately passes the structural fold:

```python
live = live_leases(config) + extra   # expire_dead=False, by design
```

The in-code rationale is sound for its own case: `expire_dead=True` would probe the pid of a *fresh* lease whose short-lived journaling subprocess has already exited, report `alive=False`, and let a racing acquirer double-book (the TOCTOU the lease exists to prevent; it previously regressed `test_coord_demo_k4_serializes_writes`).

But the consequence is that **the authority path never self-heals**. A lease whose holder died has no expiry on the only call that grants lanes. Only two callers pass `expire_dead=True` (`cli.py:6330`, `cli.py:8377`) and neither grants a lane.

## No reap verb is exposed

`dos lease-lane` offers exactly `{acquire, release, heartbeat, spawn, live}`. The two functions that *are* meant to clear an orphan have **no CLI surface at all**:

- `lane_lease.adopt()` (`lane_lease.py:559`) — no `add_parser("adopt")`, no caller in `cli.py`.
- `SCAVENGE` — recognised as a journal op (`cli.py:8590` `_QUEUE_DRAIN_OPS`) but nothing emits it from the CLI.

`live_leases`' own docstring says the dead orphan is kept visible "precisely so [`adopt()` and the orphan-reclaim sweep] can transfer/scavenge it" — but neither is reachable by an operator.

## The workaround I used (undocumented, and too blunt)

`release()` matches on `holder == owner`, so naming the dead holder works:

```
$ dos lease-lane release --lane tools --owner w4591
{"lane": "tools", "owner": "w4591", "released": true}
```

This is append-only and auditable, but it is indistinguishable from a legitimate self-release: it asserts no liveness check, so it will just as happily evict a **live** holder. It is a footgun, not a reap.

## Why this is worth fixing

This is the same defect class as the goal-park bug fixed tonight: **state that outlives the condition that created it, with no sanctioned way to clear it.** A single crashed worker permanently removes a lane from the fleet, and the blast radius grows monotonically — `dos lease-lane live` currently shows leases still held from 2026-07-16 by `fable-superloop-23874`, `ultracode-5025`, `goal-4876`, and others, all with the same shape.

## Suggested fix

Expose a reap verb that applies the liveness predicate the kernel already has, rather than trusting the caller:

```
dos lease-lane reap --lane <name> [--owner <holder>]
```

refusing unless `_lease_is_dead(lease, now, this_host)` holds, and journaling a `SCAVENGE` (already in `_QUEUE_DRAIN_OPS`). That keeps `acquire()`'s TOCTOU-safe structural fold untouched — the self-heal becomes an explicit, evidence-gated operator action instead of an implicit read-time elision.

records.title: fix(dispatchtick): restore the #1699 branch-role prompt witness — TestDispatchPromptCarriesDevelopmentBranchRole is red on trunk
records.body:
## What is red

`go test ./cmd/fak -run TestDispatchPromptCarriesDevelopmentBranchRole -count=1` fails on the
committed trunk in 0.02s:

```
--- FAIL: TestDispatchPromptCarriesDevelopmentBranchRole (0.00s)
    dispatch_tick_test.go:168: prompt missing "Just commit on `dev`.":
```

This is the acceptance witness of **#1699** (`branch-regime: teach dispatch and agent prompts
to ship on dev`), which is CLOSED. Its witness no longer holds.

## Why it is a real trunk red, not peer WIP

All three inputs are byte-identical to HEAD (`git status --porcelain` clean for each):

- `cmd/fak/dispatch_tick_test.go` — the assertion
- `cmd/fak/dispatch_tick_route.go` — `dispatchPrompt`, the call under test
- `internal/dispatchtick/` — the prompt generator (whole tree clean)

So the failure reproduces from committed sources alone; nothing in the shared dirty tree
causes it.

## Root cause — a one-token wording drift

The generator emits lowercase, no trailing period:

`internal/dispatchtick/promptrules.go:165`
```go
"checkout-of-tracked-files - just commit on `%s`", branch),
```

The test asserts capitalised, with a trailing period:

`cmd/fak/dispatch_tick_test.go:166`
```go
for _, want := range []string{"configured development branch `dev`", "Just commit on `dev`."} {
```

`want[0]` ("configured development branch `dev`") matches — the branch role plumbing itself is
working, and `got["development_branch"] == "dev"` passes the check above it. Only the second
string mismatches, on case and punctuation.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Decide which side is canonical — align the assertion to the emitted wording, or change
      the emitted wording and update `internal/dispatchtick/prompt_test.go` (which pins the
      sibling string `"Just commit on main"` at line 449) in the same commit.
- [ ] `go test ./cmd/fak -run TestDispatchPromptCarriesDevelopmentBranchRole -count=1` green.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/dispatchtick -count=1` green.

## Routing note

The prompt string lives in `internal/dispatchtick`, whose lane was held by a live lease when
this was filed — coordinate with that holder rather than editing across it. Found incidentally
while running the `cmd` lane gate for #5254; unrelated to that issue.

records.title: fix(dispatch): ACTIVE_GUARD_LIVELOCK is a lifetime tally that latches, and holds the whole fleet for one lane's worker
records.body:
Follow-on to #5858, which fixed the identical two defects in the sibling hold
`ACTIVE_COMPACT_RUNAWAY`. The agent that shipped #5858 filed this rather than widening
its own scope. Both properties were re-verified independently here against the module as
it stands after `2c61d84ef979` — this is not an assumption of symmetry.

## Defect 1 — the hold is a LIFETIME tally, so it latches and never clears on recovery

`_guard_result_livelock` (`tools/issue_resolve_dispatch.py:464-506` pre-fix) folds a worker's
guard-audit journal into `counts[(tool, reason, digest)] += 1` over **every row in the file**,
and fires at `ACTIVE_GUARD_LIVELOCK_MIN_COUNT = 10`. Guard journals are **append-only**, so
that tally can never decrease. Once a worker crosses 10, the hold is latched for the life of
the journal, however long ago the livelock ended.

Probed against the unmodified module (journal: 10 identical `QUARANTINE`/`tool_result` rows,
then **400 consecutive clean `DECIDE` rows**):

```
  hold['active'] = True
  hit            = {'livelock': True, 'tool': 'tool_result', 'reason': 'SECRET_EXFIL',
                    'digest': 'abc123', 'count': 10}
  VERDICT: LATCHES
```

The worker demonstrably broke out 400 decisions ago and is still shipping work. The hold is
describing a livelock that is over.

### Docstring vs. code

The docstring calls this "the result-side analogue of the status-card livelock fold". The
status-card fold it names — `tools/dispatch_status.py:_guard_livelock_candidates:2571-2627` —
tracks `longest_run`, a **consecutive** run that is reset to 0 by any non-matching row, and
admits a candidate on `count >= 10 **or** longest_run >= 3`. The dispatcher's version
implements only the lifetime count and never the run. It is not the analogue it claims to be.

Consequence, probed against the unmodified module: ten quarantines scattered singly across
2000 rows of productive work — **never two adjacent**, a livelock by no reading —

```
  hold['active'] = True
```

Exactly the shape #5858 found in the compact-runaway docstring, whose "consecutive" claim was
likewise never implemented.

## Defect 2 — a lane-local fault taking a fleet-wide hold

`active_guard_livelock_hold` (`:509-546` pre-fix) stamps each candidate with
`{"log", "issue"}` and **no lane**, and the call site (`:5682-5696` pre-fix) returns
`ACTIVE_GUARD_LIVELOCK` before any lane logic is reached. A livelock on `quality` therefore
blocked dispatch to `tools`, `session`, `gateway` — every disjoint lane.

The lane is not merely absent, it is *available*: the scan already opens the worker's resolve
log, and `_spawn_header_lane` parses `lane=` from that log's first line. Probed:

```
  hold keys      = ['active', 'candidates', 'reason']
  candidate keys = ['count', 'digest', 'issue', 'livelock', 'log', 'path', 'reason', 'tool']
  candidate lane = None
  spawn header lane parses as: quality      <- available, just never read
  VERDICT: LANE-BLIND
```

A guard result livelock is *one worker's local tool loop*. It justifies not stacking a second
worker on the **same** lane. It is no reason to idle every unrelated lane.

## Fix (same template as #5858)

- **Recency window** (`ACTIVE_GUARD_LIVELOCK_ESCAPE_ROWS = 50`): every parsed journal row
  advances a clock; a key not reproduced for a full window is forgotten, both mid-scan (a
  later repeat starts a *new* burst that must reach `min_count` on its own) and at the tail
  (a burst already a window behind the journal head is a worker that recovered). This is the
  role the compaction shed plays in #5858. It cures the latch *and* the scattered-singles
  false positive with one mechanism. `escapes` / `rows` / `rows_since` are reported so the
  clear is legible.
- **Lane stamping + lane-scoped collision**: candidates carry `lane`; the hold returns
  `lanes` / `lane_unknown`; the call site computes `collides` and only blocks on a collision.
- **Fail closed**: `lane_unknown` defaults to `True`, so an unreadable spawn header keeps the
  old fleet-wide behaviour rather than guessing disjointness.
- **Never a silent drop**: `payload["active_guard_livelock"]` is set with `scoped_lane` and
  `collides` on *both* arms, so a scoped-past hold is visible in the tick payload.

Window sizing rationale: the status-card fold's own tight signal is 3 consecutive repeats; 50
intervening rows with no recurrence is over an order of magnitude past that.

## Scope check

`active_guard_livelock_hold` and `active_compact_runaway_hold` are the only two
`active_*_hold` functions in the dispatcher. The remaining early holds in `evaluate`
(`WEEKLY_CAPPED`, `SEAT_COOLED`, `GATEWAY_DOWN`, `BACKEND_HEALTH_SKIP`,
`BACKEND_UNHEALTHY`) are genuinely fleet-scoped conditions — account budget, gateway and
backend health — not one worker's local state, so a fleet-wide hold is correct for them.
`NO_LANE` / `LANE_BUSY` / `DIRTY_PATH_COLLISION` are already scoped to the chosen lane or
target. With this fix, no hold in `evaluate` retains the shape.

## Tests

`tools/issue_resolve_dispatch_test.py`: 8 new tests, each verified to **fail** against an
unmodified snapshot of the module and pass after. The 3 pre-existing guard-livelock tests
pass on both sides (no-regression guards). Full file: 374 passed, 1 pre-existing unrelated
failure (`test_opencode_backend_routes_product_and_stamps_payload`, non-hermetic, fails on
HEAD too).

records.title: fix(dispatch): explain the 50 empty guard sessions - 10% of spawns journal zero decisions
records.body:
## Parent context

#4954 — epic(operator): generic loop-fleet operator, keep every loop doing REAL work, not just
running. An empty guard session is the purest instance of that epic's failure: a loop that ran
and did nothing.

## What

10% of guarded worker sessions boot, create a guard-audit journal, and emit **zero** decision
rows. Measured over `.dispatch-runs/guard-audit/*.jsonl`, window 2026-07-27 14:00 →
2026-08-06 22:32 local (10.4 days):

- **513** guarded sessions on record
- **463** non-empty
- **50 empty (9.7%)** — booted under guard, never made a single tool call

`tools/dispatch_status.py` already surfaces this as `empty=50` in the guard card, but nothing
acts on it and nothing explains it.

## Why it matters

This is the largest single measured loss in the guard journal, by an order of magnitude. For
scale, over the same window and the same corpus:

| Loss mode | Sessions |
|---|---|
| **empty (0 decisions)** | **50** |
| terminated on a kernel refusal | 22 |
| terminated on `CHILD_CRASH` | 12 |
| terminated on a delete-command refusal, work lost | 5 |

An empty session consumed a spawn, an account rotation, and a dispatch slot and returned
nothing. At the dispatcher's currently-reported service rate of 1.292/h, 50 dead spawns over
10.4 days is ~4.8/day of pure spawn waste.

## What is not yet known

The journal cannot distinguish these hypotheses, because an empty journal is by construction
evidence-free:

1. the child never launched (spawn failed, binary/PATH/account problem);
2. the child launched but died before its first tool call (auth wall, rate-limit wall, model
   refusal at turn 0);
3. the guard wired the journal but the child ran unguarded and journaled elsewhere;
4. the session was a legitimate no-op (nothing to do, exited clean).

(4) would be benign; (1)-(3) are not. They are currently indistinguishable.

## Done condition

- An empty guard session records **why** it was empty — at minimum a terminal row carrying the
  child's exit status and stderr tail, written by the guard wrapper at teardown rather than by
  the child.
- `tools/dispatch_status.py`'s guard card breaks `empty=N` down by that cause instead of
  reporting one opaque count.
- A witness: a test that boots a guard session whose child exits immediately and asserts the
  journal carries the cause row, not zero rows.

## Evidence

- Corpus: `.dispatch-runs/guard-audit/*.jsonl`, 513 files, window above.
- Producer: the dispatch worker's `guard_wrap` (`tools/dispatch_worker.py` / `cmd/dispatchworker`).
- Consumer: `tools/dispatch_status.py` `_GUARD_*` folds (`empty_sessions`).

Estimate: 3 points. Uncertainty: operator-supplied estimate; revise through the parent denominator when evidence changes.

Contribution: 3/100 points.

records.title: fix(journal): make a DENY row decodable - args_label truncates to 2 tokens, hiding a 9-death worker cluster
records.body:
## Parent context

#4954 — epic(operator): generic loop-fleet operator, keep every loop doing REAL work, not just
running. This is the observability gap that stops a measured worker-death cluster from becoming
a fix.

## What

The guard-audit journal's `args_label` field records only the **first two whitespace tokens** of
a refused command. That is enough to classify a refusal, but not enough to fix the fuel that
caused it — so a measured, repeating worker-death cluster cannot be turned into a targeted
prompt rule.

## The concrete blocker

Measured over `.dispatch-runs/guard-audit/*.jsonl`, window 2026-07-27 → 2026-08-06 (10.4 days),
**22 dispatched worker sessions ended on a kernel refusal** — the journal's last row is a `DENY`
and the worker never called another tool. Broken down by the refused command's `args_label`:

| `args_label` | terminal deaths | decodable? |
|---|---|---|
| delete commands (`rm …`, `Remove-Item …`, `git clean`) | 6 | yes — fuel rule `no-delete` shipped in c9d8d8f |
| `command=cd fak` | 5 | **no** |
| `command=git config` | 4 | **no** |
| everything else | 7 | partly |

The `cd fak` + `git config` cluster is **9 deaths — more than the delete cluster's 6** — and it
is the one class that already has a shipped fix. But `cd fak` and `git config` are prefixes, not
commands. Nothing in the journal says what the worker actually tried, so there is no way to know
whether the right fix is a fuel rule, a policy carve-out, or a genuine bug.

Two of the five `cd fak` refusals came back `SELF_MODIFY` rather than `POLICY_BLOCK`, which
suggests at least some of them are compound commands (`cd fak && <something that writes fak's
own files>`) rather than a bare `cd`. That is a hypothesis the current field cannot confirm.

## Why the field is short (and why that is right by default)

`args_label` is deliberately lossy: the journal is a shared, committed-adjacent artifact and the
full argv of an arbitrary worker command is an exfiltration surface. The existing `args_digest`
(a full sha256 over the args) preserves integrity without disclosure. So the ask is **not** "log
the whole command".

## Done condition

Any one of these closes it, in preference order:

1. A refusal row carries a **structured decision context** from the refusing policy rung — the
   matched rule id and the specific offending token — rather than a raw command prefix. This is
   disclosure-free: the policy already knows which pattern matched.
2. `args_label` widens **only on a DENY row** (a refusal is already an anomaly worth explaining)
   to a redacted-but-decodable form, with paths/values scrubbed and the verb chain kept.
3. A local-only sidecar (gitignored, not the committed journal) retains full argv for the recent
   window so a fleet operator can decode a cluster without the disclosure landing in the artifact.

Plus: re-run the terminal-refusal breakdown above and confirm the `cd fak` / `git config` cluster
resolves into a nameable cause.

## Evidence

- Corpus: `.dispatch-runs/guard-audit/*.jsonl`, 513 sessions, 463 non-empty, 302 refusal rows.
- Row schema: `internal/journal.Row` (`args_label`, `args_digest`).
- Prior art in the same seam: the `no-delete` worker-fuel rule (`internal/dispatchtick/promptrules.go`,
  mirrored in `tools/issue_worker_prompt.py`, witness `SPURIOUS_STAGED_DELETION`) — that fix was
  only targetable because `rm`/`Remove-Item` survives a two-token truncation. `cd`/`git` does not.

## Work estimate
Estimate: 3 points. Uncertainty: operator-supplied estimate; revise through the parent denominator when evidence changes.

## Overall completion contribution
Contribution: 3/100 points.

## Completion standard
development

records.title: fix(dos): the lane-lease heartbeat rung has no writer — 0 HEARTBEAT ops in 18096 WAL entries, so liveness degenerates to TTL age and cannot discriminate live from dead holders
records.body:
## Parent context

Child of epic #750 (*witnessed two-heartbeat liveness — alive-and-progressing read from an
oracle, not the agent's self-report*). This is the concrete, measured instance of that epic's
premise on the lane-lease seam: the "second heartbeat" it wants read is never written.

## Summary

The lane-lease **heartbeat rung has no writer on this fleet**. `dos.lane_lease._lease_is_dead`
treats a quiet heartbeat as its primary liveness evidence and the holder PID as a mere
corroborator — but nothing ever appends a `HEARTBEAT` op, so `heartbeat_at` is absent for
**100% of live lease records**. "The heartbeat went quiet" therefore degenerates into "older
than the 5-minute grace since ACQUIRE" for every lease, the corroborating dead-PID rung fires
universally, and a mechanism built to distinguish a live holder from a dead one **cannot
