discriminate at all**. The live/dead split is carried entirely by TTL age; the heartbeat rung
contributes nothing.

Surfaced while landing #5859 (`fix(tools): invert lane-lease liveness evidence so WAL freshness
outranks the PID probe`, 31b9a667c86e).

## Reproduced counts (re-measured 2026-08-06 on this host)

Every `C:\work\*\.dos\lane-journal.jsonl`, counted by `op`:

| WAL | entries | ACQUIRE | RELEASE | ENFORCE | REFUSE | other | **HEARTBEAT** | recs w/ `heartbeat_at` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fak` | 2992 | 111 | 84 | 2732 | 65 | — | **0** | **0** |
| `dos-kernel-public` | 1291 | 11 | 9 | 1243 | — | ATTEMPT 28 | **0** | **0** |
| `fleet` | 12741 | 242 | 238 | 12195 | 25 | HONEST_STOP 24, SCAVENGE 3, STOP 3 | 10 | 10 |
| `fak-ci` | 270 | 13 | 8 | 242 | 5 | — | 2 | 2 |
| `dos-old-archive` | 661 | 3 | 3 | 654 | — | — | 1 | 1 |
| `Benchmark` | 39 | 18 | 16 | — | 5 | — | 0 | 0 |
| `fleet-public` | 96 | 1 | — | 95 | — | — | 0 | 0 |
| `dos-fix` | 4 | — | — | 4 | — | — | 0 | 0 |
| `dos-live-rehome` | 2 | — | — | 2 | — | — | 0 | 0 |
| **total** | **18096** | 399 | 358 | 17167 | 100 | — | **13 (0.07%)** | **13** |

Zero `HEARTBEAT` ops in the two WALs that actually matter — the active `fak` dispatch tree and
`dos-kernel-public`. The 13 fleet-wide beats are historical residue in `fleet`/`fak-ci`/
`dos-old-archive`, not a running cadence.

*Correction to the original report:* the figures it cited (2871 entries — 107 ACQUIRE / 81
RELEASE / 2619 ENFORCE / 64 REFUSE / 0 HEARTBEAT) are `C:\work\fak\.dos\lane-journal.jsonl`,
**not** `dos-kernel-public`'s WAL. Same shape, +121 entries of live growth since. The
zero-HEARTBEAT conclusion reproduces in both, and fleet-wide, so the finding stands — only the
file attribution was off.

## Where the evidence ordering lives

`dos-kernel` checkout, `src/dos/lane_lease.py`:

- `:220-221` — `_DEFAULT_LIVE_TTL_MINUTES = 50.0`, `_LIVE_TTL_GRACE_MINUTES = 5.0`
- `:224` — `def _lease_is_dead(...)`; the ordering contract is spelled out at `:233-260`
  ("(a) TTL/heartbeat staleness … (b) Dead PID on THIS host … only as a FASTER reclaim of a
  lease that is ALSO already heartbeat-stale, NEVER as an outright eviction of a still-FRESH
  lease")
- `:275` — `stamp = lease.get("heartbeat_at", "") or lease.get("acquired_at", "")` ← the
  fallback that silently becomes the *only* path
- `:286` — `if age_min is not None and age_min <= _LIVE_TTL_GRACE_MINUTES: return False`
- `:308` — `if probe.alive is False and age_min is not None: return True` ← the corroborator
  rung that fires universally
- `:314` — `return age_min > (ttl + _LIVE_TTL_GRACE_MINUTES)`

The writer and its (absent) callers:

- `src/dos/lane_lease.py:603` — `def heartbeat(...)`, whose own docstring concedes the gap:
  *"The HEARTBEAT op, its `replay` fold, and the `journal_delta._HEARTBEAT_OPS` fold all
  already existed — but NOTHING in the package ever wrote one … A held worker calling
  `dos lease-lane heartbeat` on a cadence is what makes it reachable."*
- `src/dos/cli.py:5446,5449` — the **only** caller of `lane_lease.heartbeat()` anywhere in the
  kernel: the `dos lease-lane heartbeat` CLI verb handler itself. Nothing calls that verb on a
  cadence; the references outside `cli.py` are all skill/docs prose telling an agent it *should*.

## Consequence

The recorded lane-lease `pid` is the **ephemeral `dos lease-lane acquire` subprocess** that
journals its ACQUIRE and exits immediately (`lane_lease.py:453`, `:466-492`) — the reservation
is designed to outlive it. So once a lease passes the 5-minute grace:

1. `probe.alive is False` is true for essentially every lease (the acquirer is gone by design),
2. `heartbeat_at` is absent for every lease (no writer),

and the `:308` rung — intended as a rare fast-path for a holder that is *dead **and** silent* —
becomes the universal path. A lease held by a live, working agent and a lease abandoned by a
crashed one are byte-identical after five minutes.

Measured against the live tree with `python tools/dispatch_status.py --fast` (post-#5859):

```
lane lease: 27 held — live=0 dead-holder=18 unknown=9
```

All 9 `unknown` are leases inside their TTL whose ephemeral acquirer has exited — including
`guard` (8.4m) and `hooks` (12.5m), which at that instant were held by **live** resolver workers
(pids 23180 / 83504, corroborated by the same card's `worker/lease cross-check: clean=2`). The
classifier cannot call them `live` because there is no beat to read; the only reason it does not
call them `dead` is the deliberate fail-safe added in #5859. `live=0` with two provably-live
holders is the whole defect in one line.

## Wanted

Either of:

- **Wire the cadence beat.** The dispatch/resolver loops that hold a lane lease call
  `dos lease-lane heartbeat` per iteration — the kernel already ships `--coalesce-within-s` for
  exactly this write-amplification concern.
- **Or retire the rung honestly.** Declare lane leases TTL-only and drop the heartbeat evidence
  path (and the verb), so `_lease_is_dead` stops implying evidence it never has.

Silently keeping a primary-evidence rung that is never populated is the worst of the three.

## Notes

- **The fix likely belongs in dos-kernel** (`https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/dos-kernel`),
  which is a separate, read-only checkout on this host. Filing here because fak's
  dispatch/resolver loops are the would-be beat callers, and fak's WAL is where the gap was
  measured.
- Related but distinct: `anthony-chaudhary/dos-kernel#246` (*MCP `dos_arbitrate` reports a HELD
  lane FREE: it never reads the lane-journal*) — another lane-lease liveness read that is wrong,
  on a different seam.
- Also adjacent: #5085 (admission honors a 4h-stalled lease; no reap path) and #750 (epic:
  witnessed two-heartbeat liveness). Neither states this writer gap.

## Repro

```bash
# op-kind census across every lane-journal WAL on the host
python - <<'PY'
import json, collections, pathlib, glob
for p in sorted(glob.glob(r"C:\work\*\.dos\lane-journal.jsonl")):
    ops=collections.Counter(); hb=0; n=0
    for line in pathlib.Path(p).read_text(encoding="utf-8",errors="replace").splitlines():
        if not line.strip(): continue
        n+=1; rec=json.loads(line); ops[str(rec.get("op"))]+=1
        if rec.get("heartbeat_at"): hb+=1
    print(f"{p} n={n} hb_field={hb} {dict(ops.most_common())}")
PY

# the only caller of the writer
grep -rn "lane_lease\.heartbeat(" <dos-kernel>/src   # -> src/dos/cli.py:5449 only
```

Refs #5859.

## Work estimate
Estimate: 3 points. Uncertainty: operator-supplied estimate; revise through the parent denominator when evidence changes.

## Overall completion contribution
Contribution: 3/100 points.

## Completion standard
production

## Target operating envelope
- heartbeat coverage: n/a (correctness repair; the deliverable is a written beat or an honestly retired rung, not a numeric operating envelope)

## Witnessed operating envelope
- heartbeat coverage: n/a (measured absence - 0 HEARTBEAT ops in 18096 WAL entries; there is nothing to witness until a writer exists)

records.title: fix(dispatch): the close-resolved arm closes an issue whose own witness commit says "The issue stays open"
records.body:
## Current state

`tools/issue_resolve_witnessed.py` is the dispatch loop's auto-close arm. A standing cron
runs it; it closed #2444/#2419/#2403 unattended at 05:41-05:42Z on 2026-08-06.

Reproduced today (dry-run, `--issue-limit 8000 --max-commits 600`):

```
would_close |#2694 | 2726d19 | doc | docs(claude-mac): capture a shareable visual of the preflight panel...
```

The commit it cites, `2726d19`, says in its own body:

> The capture itself is still blocked and **this commit does not claim it**. [...]
> No artifact is claimed under `visuals/` and no README link is added, because neither
> would be true yet. **The issue stays open.**

So the arm plans to close an issue on a commit whose author explicitly wrote that it does
not resolve it.

## Why it gets through

Two gates should have caught it and neither can:

- `claim_binds_resolution` (#2998) has a **docs-rung carve-out**: any issue whose title
  starts with `docs(` accepts a `doc`-kind claim. #2694 is titled `docs(claude-mac): ...`,
  so a docs-only commit binds by title shape alone -- the carve-out never asks whether the
  diff contains the artifact the issue asks for (#2694's Done condition is "one artifact
  committed under `visuals/`"; `2726d19` adds none).
- The #3870 coverage gate keys on an `epic` label / an unchecked `- [ ]` task box /
  a spine-first marker. #2694's body has none of those, so it binds.

## The failure class

Every gate in the arm reasons over the issue (labels, body, timeline) or over the commit's
*diff shape* (claim kind, touched paths). **Nothing reads the commit message body**, which is
where an author states scope. The counter the arm inherits grades "is there a witnessed
commit citing #N", which is strictly weaker than "is #N done".

A second live instance: `3dbe6bf2` (`feat(agent): add the agent-runtime spine endpoint as a
standalone tested unit (#3258)`) writes "this does NOT wire the route onto the served gateway
mux. Nothing in the shipped serving path changes [...] claiming it as a served endpoint now
would be claiming an integration that has no witness." That commit is `code_effect` over real
source paths, so the docs carve-out is not even needed -- the class is broader than the
carve-out.

Measured cost of the weaker question: an audit today found `closable-now=46` over-reports by
~6.5x -- of 46 candidates the arm would close 10, and independent verification cut that to 7.

## Done condition

A commit whose body explicitly disclaims resolution never satisfies the claim, at any rung.
The arm emits a typed hold instead of `would_close`.

## Witness

`#2694` / `2726d19` is refused with a typed hold in a dry-run plan, and the 7 issues the arm
correctly closed today (#2762, #2444, #2425, #2419, #2403, #2299, #3282) are unaffected.

## Precision budget

Measured over the last 1500 commits, a high-precision disclaimer marker set matches 7 commits
(0.47%), and every one is a genuine "I did not finish this" note. Notably a bare `follow-on`
marker matches 56/1500 (3.7%) and would falsely refuse `fec8da6f76`, one of the #2299
witnesses -- so the marker set must not use it.

## Out of scope

Widening the arm's `--issue-limit` (#2694 sits outside the default newest-1000 window, so the
cron does not reach it *today* -- but the gate defect is real and fires the moment the window
moves or an operator passes a wider `--audit-json`).

## Related

- #3870 -- the coverage gate for the sibling partial-close class.
- #2998 -- the claim-kind gate that owns the docs-rung carve-out.

Hold-evidence comments are already posted on #2694 and #3258, so a wrong close is pre-refuted
and reversible.

records.title: fix(dispatchconservation): no-commit vocabulary misses the Python sweep's classes, folding restart_exhausted into unknown
records.body:
## What

`internal/dispatchconservation`'s closed `noCommitReasons` vocabulary
(conservation.go:71) only copied the Go half of the no-commit class list
(`internal/dispatchtick/witness.go:76-84`). But the `.witness` sidecars this package
reads are written by the **Python** sweep, `tools/issue_resolve_dispatch.py`
(`classify_no_commit_reason`, NO_COMMIT_* consts at :3939-3947), whose vocabulary is
wider. Three classes it stamps were absent:

- `restart_exhausted`  (:3946)
- `preview_confirm_feedback` (:3944)
- `missing_log_artifact` (:3945)

Anything outside the set hits `if !noCommitReasons[reason] { reason = "unknown" }`
(conservation.go:203) and is booked as **unknown** — so the conservation ledger, whose
entire purpose is "we spent K units this window, where did each go?", relabelled a
named, actionable guard terminal as "we could not tell".

## Measured impact

78h window ending 2026-08-07T06:19:45Z, this repo's own `.dispatch-runs`
(276 spent worker-units, 225 no-commit):

| source | unknown | restart_exhausted |
|---|---|---|
| `.witness` sidecars (ground truth, 225 rows) | 143 | 26 |
| `fak dispatch-conservation --window-h 78` (before) | **169** | **absent** |

26 of 225 no-commit units (11.6%) — 15% of the reported `unknown` bucket — were
misattributed. `restart_exhausted` is the guard's equivalent-restart reap
(`cmd/fak/guard_child.go:1323` `guardEquivalentRestartStatus`, stamped with
`dominant_cause=BUDGET_CONTEXT_EXHAUSTED`); it is the single most actionable no-commit
terminal the fleet produces, and it was invisible in the ledger.

Over the full 21.6d of retained sidecars (2381 records) `restart_exhausted` is 897
units — 37.7% of all finished workers — so any historical read of this ledger
understated it by the same mechanism.

## Fix

Widen `noCommitReasons` to the union of both producers, and document that it must
stay a superset. Regression test: `TestPythonSweepReasonsAccountedNotFolded`
(mirrors the existing `TestModelSwitchableReasonsAccountedNotFolded`).

After: `no-commit reasons: auth_wall=16, policy_block=35, restart_exhausted=26,
self_modify=5, unknown=143` — matches the sidecars exactly.

## Follow-on (not in this fix)

The residual `unknown=143` is still the largest bucket (52.8% of runs / 54% of
seat-hours in the clean window). It is the classifier's explicit fall-through, so it
is not one thing. Filed separately.

records.title: fix(dispatch): split the NO_COMMIT unknown fall-through — 52.8% of runs / 54% of seat-hours, and 75% of it is a clean session exit
records.body:
## The largest disposition bucket in the fleet is the classifier's fall-through

`classify_no_commit_reason` (`tools/issue_resolve_dispatch.py:3985`) returns
`NO_COMMIT_UNKNOWN` when no signature matches (`:4019`). That residual bucket is now
the fleet's **single largest terminal disposition, by both runs and seat-hours**.

Measured over the clean current-fleet window (2026-08-04 00:00Z .. 08-07 06:15Z,
**282 finished-worker `.witness` records**, 102.3h of wall-to-witness time):

| disposition | runs | % | hours | % |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **NO_COMMIT / unknown** | **149** | **52.8%** | **55.2** | **54.0%** |
| WITNESSED | 48 | 17.0% | 20.4 | 20.0% |
| NO_COMMIT / policy_block | 35 | 12.4% | 11.6 | 11.3% |
| NO_COMMIT / restart_exhausted | 26 | 9.2% | 12.1 | 11.9% |
| NO_COMMIT / auth_wall | 16 | 5.7% | 0.2 | 0.2% |
| NO_COMMIT / self_modify | 5 | 1.8% | 1.3 | 1.3% |
| CLAIM_UNWITNESSED | 3 | 1.1% | 1.4 | 1.4% |

52% of `unknown` runs are a repeat of `unknown` on the **same issue** — and because the
reason is the fall-through, the anti-churn picker has nothing to route on.

## It is not opaque — it is two distinguishable things, and one of them is nameable

Reading the log tails directly (n=149):

- **112/149 (75.2%) carry the COMPLETE guard exit summary**, through the final
  `guard · cache window` section emitted at
  `cmd/fak/guard_child_supervision.go:483`. These sessions ended **normally**: no
  crash, no wall, no refusal — the worker just finished and landed nothing.
- **37/149 (24.8%) have no epilogue at all** — died before the guard could write it.
  A genuinely different failure, currently indistinguishable from the first.

The marker is inside the existing default tail window: with `_CAP_TAIL_BYTES = 4096`
(`tools/issue_resolve_dispatch.py:2781`) the section is found in **112/112** of the
cases a 24 KiB tail finds. No widening needed — this is a ~5-line classifier addition.

## What the clean-exit half actually looks like

Same window, comparing the two groups (turn counts read from the guard epilogue):

| | UNKNOWN (no commit) | WITNESSED |
|---|---|---|
| n (with epilogue) | 112 | 39 |
| turns: p25 / med / p75 | 20 / **25** / 28 | 43 / **53** / 64 |
| tool calls (median) | 114 | 309 |
| wall-clock (median) | **26.0 min** | **26.8 min** |
| at/over the 29m wall | 48% | 35% |

Both groups burn the **same wall-clock**. The losing group gets **~half the turns**
(25 vs 53) and ~a third of the tool calls in that same time — i.e. these workers are
not running out of *clock*, they are running out of *throughput per minute* and dying
mid-task with the work unlanded. Worth noting the 29m wall is NOT the discriminator:
more of the losers hit it, but the winners hit it too and still land.

## Ask

Split `NO_COMMIT_UNKNOWN` into two typed classes so the biggest bucket becomes
routable and the next measurement is possible:

- `clean_exit_no_commit` — complete guard epilogue present, no resolving commit.
- keep `unknown` for the residual (no epilogue): a genuinely unclassified death.

This is measurement, not behavior change: it makes the 54%-of-seat-hours bucket
attributable, and it is the prerequisite for grading whether c9d8d8f71a (#3220,
`checkpoint-commit` / `refusal-taxonomy` worker fuel, cut over at 2026-08-07 04:47Z)
actually moves the clean-exit half. At the time of writing that renderer has only
~11 runs of data — far too few to grade.

Note the ledger side of this was just fixed separately in #5866 (the Go conservation
vocabulary was folding `restart_exhausted` into `unknown` on top of everything above).

## Evidence

All numbers from `C:\work\fak\.dispatch-runs\resolve-*.{witness,log,prompt.txt}`
(2381 witness records retained, 2026-07-16..08-07; 282 in the clean window).

records.title: feat(dispatch): detect DOA spawns — a stale-binary argv mismatch burned 350 worker-units (91.6% of 7 days) with zero detection
records.body:
## A stale-binary flag mismatch burned 350 worker-units over 7 days, undetected

Between **2026-07-28 and 2026-08-03** the dispatcher spawned workers with
`--compact-solvency-floor` (passed at `tools/dispatch_worker.py:610` and
`cmd/dispatchworker/guard.go:396`) against a `fak.exe` that did not define the flag.
Every such worker died instantly at flag parse:

```
# fak-spawn <sha>-N issue=N lane=compute backend=claude argv0=fak.exe
flag provided but not defined: -compact-solvency-floor
usage: fak guard [flags] -- <agent command...>
```

The agent never started. Not one turn was served.

## Scale, with denominators

Per-day, from the retained `.dispatch-runs/resolve-*.log` set (2381 runs, 2026-07-16..08-07):

| date | runs | DOA at flag parse | % |
|---|---|---|---|
| 07-16 .. 07-27 | 1717 | 0 | 0.0% |
| 2026-07-28 | 34 | 30 | 88.2% |
| 2026-07-29 | 55 | 55 | **100%** |
| 2026-07-30 | 43 | 43 | **100%** |
| 2026-07-31 | 53 | 53 | **100%** |
| 2026-08-01 | 61 | 61 | **100%** |
| 2026-08-02 | 56 | 56 | **100%** |
| 2026-08-03 | 80 | 52 | 65.0% |
| 2026-08-04 .. 08-07 | 282 | 0 | 0.0% |

**350 worker-units** — 91.6% of every worker dispatched in that 7-day window. For six
consecutive days the fleet's *entire* resolve throughput was zero-by-construction.

The condition is already resolved (no occurrence since 08-03), so this is **not a live
outage**. The gap is that nothing detected it.

## Why nothing caught it

Each DOA run still produced a `.witness` with `claim: CLAIM_NO_COMMIT`, and
`classify_no_commit_reason` (`tools/issue_resolve_dispatch.py:3985`) has no signature
for a flag-parse death, so all 350 landed in `reason: unknown` — the same bucket as
every other unexplained failure. Nothing in the dispatch path distinguishes "the agent
ran and chose not to commit" from "the agent binary rejected its own argv".

The tell is unambiguous, single-line, and appears in a <2 KiB log: Go's `flag` package
prints the literal `flag provided but not defined: -<name>` then the usage block. A
worker log under 2 KiB containing that string cannot be anything else.

## Ask

Two cheap, independent additions:

1. **Classify it.** Add a `spawn_argv_rejected` (or similar) class to
   `classify_no_commit_reason`, matched on `flag provided but not defined` in a
   stub-sized log. One regex, alongside the existing `_NOOP_BANNER_RE` banner-noop
   check at `:4016`. Any recurrence then names itself in
   `fak dispatch-conservation`'s breakdown instead of hiding in `unknown`.
2. **Fail loudly on the first one.** A DOA spawn rate above a small threshold within
   one tick is never normal — it means dispatcher and binary have drifted. This is the
   `check_backend_health` DEAD-streak shape already used for `banner_noop`, applied to
   argv rejection.

Prevention is separately worth considering: the dispatcher could probe
`fak guard --help` once per binary build-id and refuse to spawn on an argv the binary
will reject, rather than discovering it 350 units later.

## Evidence

`C:\work\fak\.dispatch-runs\resolve-*.log` (per-day counts above are exact, from all
2381 retained records). Flag definition today: `cmd/fak/guard.go:167`.
Note `guardAuditRetentionCount = 512` in `cmd/fak/guard.go` caps the guard-audit file
count — the per-day numbers above come from the `resolve-*` run logs, which are not
subject to that cap.

records.title: fix(dispatch): re-blockable terminals draw 53 re-dispatches / 18.0h, but 13% still land — needs a consecutive-identical hold, not a reason-class cooldown
records.body:
## Re-blockable terminals are re-dispatched anyway, but a hard hold would be wrong

`classify_no_commit_reason`'s docstring (`tools/issue_resolve_dispatch.py:3922-3928`)
states the intent plainly:

> a SELF_MODIFY / POLICY_BLOCK guard refusal is a worker that TRIED and was
> STRUCTURALLY blocked (re-dispatching it re-blocks identically — an anti-churn
> cooldown should hold it, not re-storm it)

Measured over the clean current-fleet window (2026-08-04 .. 08-07, 282 finished-worker
`.witness` records across 115 distinct issues):

- **24 issues** hit a re-blockable terminal (`policy_block` or `self_modify`).
- After that terminal they drew **53 further worker-units, costing 18.0h** (17.6% of
  the window's 102.3h).
- Of those 53 re-dispatches: **16 (30%) re-blocked identically** — pure waste, exactly
  what the docstring predicts.
- But **7 (13%) went on to land a witnessed commit.**

That last number is the important one: a hard cooldown on `policy_block` would have
suppressed 7 real closes to save 16 wasted runs. **The docstring's premise is only 30%
true, not 100% true** — "re-dispatching it re-blocks identically" is not what the data
shows. So this should not be fixed by simply holding these issues.

Worst offenders (issue, first re-blockable reason, re-dispatches after it,
re-blocked-again, eventual wins, hours):

```
#5103  policy_block  n=12  reblocked= 1  wins=2   4.1h
#3267  policy_block  n= 7  reblocked= 4  wins=1   1.2h
#4568  policy_block  n= 7  reblocked= 5  wins=0   2.0h
#5586  self_modify   n= 5  reblocked= 2  wins=1   2.3h
#5587  policy_block  n= 4  reblocked= 2  wins=0   1.0h
```

`#4568` is the clean case for a hold: 7 re-dispatches, 5 re-blocked, 0 wins, 2.0h burned.
`#5103` is the clean case against one: 12 re-dispatches, only 1 re-blocked, 2 wins.

## Wider churn context

Same window: **48 issues burned 2+ worker-units** (`fak dispatch-conservation
--window-h 78` reports `#3267x16, #5103x14, #5587x13, #4568x9, #3152x8`), and
**70 of 115 issues (61%) never landed a commit at all**, consuming 146 runs and 49.3h
— **48% of all seat-time in the window**.

## Ask

Not a blanket cooldown. What the data supports is a **per-issue, escalating** hold keyed
on *consecutive identical* re-blocks rather than on the reason class alone: hold after
the 2nd consecutive identical block on the same issue (which catches #4568) while
leaving an issue whose block did not recur free to retry (which preserves #5103's wins).

The discriminator already exists in the sidecar — `reason` is recorded per run, so
"consecutive identical reason on the same issue" is computable from
`.dispatch-runs/resolve-*.witness` with no new instrumentation.

## Evidence

`C:\work\fak\.dispatch-runs\resolve-*.witness` (282 records in window, 2381 retained
overall). Related: #5866 (ledger vocabulary fix, landed), #5867 (the `unknown`
fall-through, which is a larger bucket than this one and should be split first — its
52% same-issue repeat rate is invisible to any reason-keyed hold while it stays
untyped).

records.title: fix(dispatch): clean_exit_no_commit is 89% a provider 429 / wall-clock terminal, not a throughput gap — the classifier's 4 KiB tail is shorter than the guard epilogue
records.body:
`clean_exit_no_commit` was named an hour ago by #5867 and immediately became the fleet's
largest single loss: **118 of 291 graded resolve units** over the clean current-fleet
window (2026-08-04T00:00Z .. 08-07T07:00Z), ~41% of spent seat-time. It has been read as
a **throughput** problem — same ~26 minutes as a winning run, roughly half the turns — and
the natural lever for that reading is worker-prompt fuel.

**That reading is wrong. 105 of the 118 (89.0%) end on a typed guard terminal that the
ledger had no class for.** The guard names the cause in the log every time; the classifier
was not looking for it.

## Distribution (n=118, disjoint)

| class | n | % | what actually happened |
|---|---|---|---|
| provider quota wall | 67 | 56.8% | HTTP 429 |
| wall-clock envelope | 38 | 32.2% | `TIME_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` at the dispatch `--max-duration` (1740s) |
| residual (genuine) | 13 | 11.0% | session really did end quietly with nothing |

The quota class carries two independent witnesses, either sufficient:

* `internal/goalpark.RecordLongRetry` parks the goal with `Reason=LONG_RETRY_AFTER` **only**
  for a 429 whose `Retry-After` clears `LongWaitFloor` (1h). The two teardown branches in
  `cmd/fak/guard_child_supervision.go` print it: `goal parked outside active context budget`
  when the child exited on its own (25 units), and `context budget signal ignored as
  terminal` when the guard **suppressed the restart that would have continued the work**
  (40 units).
* `cmd/fak/accounts_cooldown.go` drops the account from the servable pool on the same wall
  (34 units, 32 overlapping the above).

The turn stream corroborates verbatim:

```
fak-turn trace=win-611ca8 FAILED reason=rate_limited wire=anthropic_messages after=1s \
  kind=weekly_limit announced_wait=1h13m40s ceiling=1m30s relayed=true
API Error: Request rejected (429) - upstream is rate-limited/overloaded (HTTP 429) and fak
already retried: the provider-named wait (~1h13m40s) is LONGER than this client can hold a
request open
```

`kind=weekly_limit` — these are subscription **weekly** caps, not transient overload.

## Root cause: the classifier's tail window is smaller than the guard's epilogue

`tools/issue_resolve_dispatch.py::classify_no_commit_reason` reads a **4 KiB** tail. The
guard prints its exit summary *after* the terminal that caused the exit, and that epilogue
runs a **median 7199 bytes** (112 of 118 exceed 4096). So every terminal line is scrolled
out of the window:

| marker | median dist. from EOF | within 4 KiB | within 16 KiB |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TIME_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` | 7671 B | **0 / 38** | 38 / 38 |
| `LONG_RETRY_AFTER` park | 7564 B | 4 / 65 | 65 / 65 |
| usage-cap cooldown | 8620 B | **0 / 34** | 34 / 34 |
| `Request rejected (429)` | 8293 B | **0 / 24** | 24 / 24 |

This is not a regex-quality problem — at 4 KiB the evidence is **not in the window**, for
100% of the affected units. It is also a known-and-already-solved problem in the same file:
`_RESTART_EXHAUSTED_TAIL_BYTES = 16 * 1024` exists for exactly this reason ("the live
epilogue can exceed the generic 4 KiB quota-banner tail"). That fix was applied to one
signature and never to the others.

## Why it matters beyond the label

Neither named class is an agent behaviour a worker prompt can move — one is purchased
capacity, one is a configured envelope. Worse, the bucket is being used as the **endpoint
for grading prompt changes** (#3220's `checkpoint-commit` fuel). Over 08-04..08-07 the
composition of the bucket swings hard with provider quota weather (08-06 00h: 11/11 quota;
08-07 00h: 4/11), so a V1-vs-V2 comparison on the un-split bucket is measuring the
provider's rate limiter, not the prompt. **The 13-unit residual is the number a prompt
change is entitled to claim credit for.**

## Fix (this issue)

Split `clean_exit_no_commit` in `internal/dispatchconservation` into
`provider_quota_wall` / `wall_clock_exhausted` / residual, reading the terminal through a
16 KiB tail (matching the producer's own existing window, so the ledger still never claims
to see something the producer could not have seen). The first-stage 4 KiB window that
decides "epilogue present" is deliberately left alone — #5867 verified its stability there.

Live corpus, before -> after: `clean_exit_no_commit` **118 -> 13**, `provider_quota_wall`
70, `wall_clock_exhausted` 38.

## Follow-ons NOT fixed here (need a decision, filed for visibility)

1. **The producer should stamp these too.** `tools/issue_resolve_dispatch.py` is currently
   being edited by another worker (uncommitted, mirroring #5867's three classes into its
   own `NO_COMMIT_*` vocabulary), so this change stays reader-side and is written to work
   from **either** entry point. But the sweep is what downstream routing/cooldown reads, and
   a quota wall should route very differently from a re-blockable refusal: it is not the
   issue's fault and must not feed a per-issue re-block streak.
2. **The 40 restart-suppressed units are a recoverable loss, not a wall.** Those workers had
   context-budget headroom and were mid-work; the guard declined the restart *only* because
   the goal was parked. If dispatch held the unit and resumed after `parked_until` instead of
   burning it, that is ~14% of the window's resolve units back.
3. **The 13 genuine residuals are three different things**, from a session-by-session read:
   **6/13 were killed by the guard's own capability floor** — one turn in which *every*
   proposed call was gated is reported upstream as a synthetic `end_turn`, and the deny-all
   auto-continue that exists to resume past exactly this produced no further turn in 6 of 7
   occurrences (5x a destructive-op preview-confirm gate, 1x a `TRUST_VIOLATION` WebFetch).
   One died at **2.5 minutes with 60% of its context unused**. This is invisible in `finish=`
   telemetry because the synthetic `end_turn` is indistinguishable from a real one.
   **1/13 was context overflow** (compactor bailed `burst_unprofitable` at 177.8k/96.0k, no
   solvency floor to override; the two runs that *did* get solvency-forced sheds survived).
   **6/13 ended correctly** — the agent finished, refused to fabricate a commit, and wrote a
   substantive report (lane held by a live sibling, issue already implemented, triplicate).
   Those are legitimate no-ops with no terminal to record them as anything but a loss.

records.title: CORE_SELF_MODIFY clearance is satisfiable by any agent for any edit: the resolver only proves a path is tracked
records.body:
## Claim

The hard-self core lock (`internal/abi/**`, `internal/adjudicator/**`) refuses commits with `CORE_SELF_MODIFY` and has no env escape — it demands a maintenance witness claim that a resolver confirms. **In practice that clearance is satisfiable by any agent, for any edit, with a claim that corroborates nothing about the change.**

This was reported by the agent that landed 8af92fbdc3. I verified it against the resolver source and the on-disk decision notes before filing; the report is accurate, and the mechanism is weaker than described.

## Verified: the resolver is an existence check

`internal/witness/witness.go:211-222`, the `committed:` arm:

```go
case "committed":
	_, code, err := r.run(ctx, r.dir, "ls-files", "--error-unmatch", "--", ":/"+arg)
	if err != nil { return abi.WitnessAbstain }
	if code == 0 { return abi.WitnessConfirmed }
	return abi.WitnessRefuted
```

`git ls-files --error-unmatch` proves exactly one thing: *a path is tracked in git*. It says nothing about the edit being committed, who reviewed it, or whether it is safe.

The `path:` arm (`witness.go:224-233`) is weaker still — a bare `os.Stat`.

## Weaker than reported: the resolver cannot see the edit at all

`internal/corelockgate/corelockgate.go:155`:

```go
outcome := resolver.Resolve(ctx, nil, claim)
if outcome == abi.WitnessConfirmed { return "", false }  // gate cleared
```

The `*abi.ToolCall` argument is **`nil`**. So even a resolver that wanted to correlate the claim against the changed pathset structurally cannot — it receives only the claim string. There is no code path on which the claim and the diff are compared.

## Empirical: what the fleet actually claims

All `corelock-maintenance` decisions recorded in `refs/notes/fak/decisions` (27 clearances):

| count | witness claim |
|---|---|
| 10 | `committed:internal/adjudicator/decide.go` |
| 7 | `committed:internal/adjudicator/reversibility.go` |
| 3 | `path:internal/adjudicator/setpolicy_benchmark_test.go` |
| 2 | `committed:internal/adjudicator/decide_egress_test.go` |
| 1 each | `path:` on five other adjudicator test files |
| 1 | `path:C:\...\Temp\fak-5146-adjudicator-witness.txt` |

Two observations:

1. **The claim is routinely unrelated to the edit.** `525a596cd2` changed `internal/adjudicator/oot_mention.go`, `oot_mention_test.go`, and `outoftree.go`, and cleared the lock with `committed:internal/adjudicator/decide.go` — a file the commit never touched. `8af92fbdc3` changed `internal/abi/denyrules.go` and cleared with the same string. It is a constant, effectively a password.

2. **One clearance used a file the agent had just created itself** (`path:` on a `fak-<pid>-adjudicator-witness.txt` under the host temp dir). That is self-report with an extra step, which is precisely what the gate's stated contract forbids.

## Why this matters

The gate's own remedy text says the witness is required "after independent read-back confirms the edit" (`corelockgate.CoreLockRemedyCommit`). Nothing in the mechanism checks that read-back happened. The gate imposes real friction — it stops an *accidental* core edit — but provides no assurance against a deliberate one, while reading in the audit trail as though it did. A `hard-self-maintenance-witness-confirmed` note on a commit currently means "some tracked path exists".

## Not proposing a fix

Changing a core-lock clearance is a human policy decision, so this is filed for triage rather than patched. Directions a maintainer might weigh: bind the claim to the changed pathset (pass the real pathspec instead of `nil` and require the claim to name it); require a claim kind that carries independent evidence (`ancestor:`/`notests:`/`symptom:` already exist and are strictly stronger than `committed:`/`path:`); or accept the gate as friction-only and downgrade its language and its audit note so the trail stops overstating what was verified.

## Reproduction

```
git notes --ref=refs/notes/fak/decisions list | awk '{print $1}' | git cat-file --batch \
  | grep -o '"op":"corelock-maintenance"[^}]*"witness":"[^"]*"'
git log -1 --stat 525a596cd2   # compare the touched paths against its recorded claim
```

records.title: perf(compaction): 52.4% of the repeated tool-result duplication is cross-fire and unreachable by any within-wire dedup (#5254 residual)
records.body:
## Parent context

[#5254](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/5254) — repeated shell tool-result spans
are the dominant post-compaction regrowth class. Its mechanism (the cross-turn verbatim-span fold
`dedupMessagesCrossTurn`, ported in `2ab350829c` from #3345) is shipped, correct, and lossless.
This issue is **not** a defect report against it.

## What

`42d0047be7ad` landed a counterfactual replay that bounds that fold over the whole existing
corpus. Alongside the headline win it established a **refutation that currently has no tracking
issue**: just over half of the duplication #5254 is named after is structurally out of reach of
the mechanism #5254 shipped — and out of reach of *any* within-wire mechanism.

Witness: `internal/session/testdata/compactaudit/replay-bound-witness-2026-08-07.md`, "REACH"
section. Denominator: 3,288 native-Codex rollouts (0 unreadable), 1,591 compaction fires, **1,544
post-fire windows** carrying ≥1 tool result, 277,684 tool-result rows / 1,195,667,003 bytes.

| split | rows | dup bytes | share |
|---|---|---|---|
| **in-window** — the earlier copy is inside the same post-fire wire | 812 | 6,027,548 | **47.6%** |
| **cross-fire** — the earlier copy precedes the fire | 798 | 6,645,892 | **52.4%** |

## Why cross-fire is unreachable within the wire

The regrowth audit's duplicate table is **session-wide and spans compaction fires**, so it
correctly types a row as a duplicate of something that was *compacted out of the wire*. By the
time a gateway-side fold sees the later copy, the earlier copy no longer exists on the wire — so
there is nothing left to match it against.

That is a property of the *wire*, not of the fold's implementation. Widening the fold's window,
lowering its 8-line minimum-run floor, or making it smarter cannot recover these bytes: the
referent is gone by construction. #5254's own framing — "the same output re-entering the window it
was just compacted out of" — names precisely the case its fix cannot address.

## What class of mechanism could address it

Anything that reaches cross-fire duplication must hold **state that outlives the wire it is
compacting**. Three candidate families, roughly in increasing cost, all with existing in-repo
surfaces to build on:

1. **Suppress at the source — never let the duplicate become bytes.** The root cause is the agent
   re-issuing a read-only tool call (`git status`, a re-`Read`) after its memory of the earlier
   result was compacted away. `internal/vdso` tier 2 is already exactly this shape: a content
   cache keyed on `(tool, args-sha256, world-version)`, filled from `EvComplete` events and
   invalidated by a write-shaped completion. It lives outside the wire, so a compaction fire does
   not evict it. **The checkable question is whether a vDSO hit currently survives and is
   consulted across a fire**, and what share of the 798 cross-fire rows carry
   `Speculatable`-eligible tool calls. That measurement is the natural first step and does not
   require building anything.
2. **An eviction ledger in the compactor.** Retain digests of the spans compaction evicted, and
   replace a re-entering body with a reference/stub plus a retrieval handle. This buys back the
   referent explicitly, at the cost of durable per-session state the current fold deliberately
   does not keep.
3. **Compaction policy rather than a new mechanism.** Pin high-recurrence tool-result spans across
   the fire so the earlier copy stays in-window — which converts cross-fire duplication into
   in-window duplication that the *already-shipped* fold reaches. Cheapest to try, but it spends
   exactly the context budget compaction exists to reclaim, so it needs its own bound.

## Scope, and what this is not

- **Scoping finding, not a bug.** The shipped fold is measured lossless: 0 lines destroyed of
  2,903,131 removed-and-relocated, and the same detector reports 1,196,294 destroyed lines for the
  full pass (dedup + the pre-existing lossy head+tail elision), so the zero is not vacuous.
- **Not a reason to hold #5254.** The in-window half is real: 158 of 300 `REPEATED_TOOL_RESULT`
  windows collapse (52.7%), dup bytes −55.2%, 165,366,011 bytes shed. This issue exists so the
  52.4% residual is *tracked* rather than assumed closed when #5254 closes.
- **The load-bearing number is the share, not the absolute.** The same witness shows the audit's
  `dup_bytes` instrument undercounts the fold by ~13× (it keys duplicates at whole-row granularity
  — `{content hash, ROW length}` — while 96.9% of folds are span-level partials), so 12,673,440 is
  itself a lower bound. Treat 52.4% as the reliable quantity and the byte totals as floors.
- The replay is a **counterfactual** over a corpus ~96% of which never crossed fak's wire — "what
  would this have collapsed here", not a claim about bytes saved in the field.

## Evidence

- Witness: `internal/session/testdata/compactaudit/replay-bound-witness-2026-08-07.md`
- Design note (corrections section): `docs/notes/COMPACTION-REPEATED-TOOL-RESULT-DEDUP-2026-07-19.md`
- Mechanism: `internal/agent/message_elide.go` (`dedupMessagesCrossTurn`)
- Scorer: `internal/session/compactregrowth_replay.go` (`ScanCompactRolloutReplay`)
- Harness: `internal/agent/message_elide_corpus_replay_test.go`
- Candidate surface for (1): `internal/vdso` (package doc, tier 2), `internal/abi/speculate.go`
- Landed by: `42d0047be7ad` (#5254)

## Done condition

- The cross-fire share is re-measured against a mechanism proposal, not just restated — at
  minimum: what fraction of the 798 cross-fire duplicate rows are `vdso.Speculatable`-eligible
  tool calls, which bounds family (1) before any code is written.
- A decision recorded for each of the three families above: pursued, or declined with the reason.
- If any is pursued, its own bound measured the same way this one was (counterfactual replay over
  the same 1,544-window corpus, so the numbers compose with the existing witness).

records.title: Dispatched workers run a fak binary no updater refreshes; FakSelfUpdate reports success for a different path
records.body:
## Summary

`FakSelfUpdate` converges exactly one binary (`--target C:\Users\USER\bin\fak.exe`) and reports
success, while **every worker the dispatcher launches runs a different `fak` binary that nothing
on the host ever refreshes**. Trunk fixes therefore do not reach dispatched workers until someone
hand-builds that file.

This is the same defect shape as #5868 (DOA spawns read as an idle fleet): **state whose lifetime
is decoupled from the condition it describes** — here a success exit code decoupled from whether
the binary the fleet actually loads moved.

## Measured (2026-08-07 ~01:10 PDT)

| Path | build | vs `origin/main` | refreshed by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `C:\Users\USER\bin\fak.exe` | `2c52df490c53` | **trunk tip** | `FakSelfUpdate` every 20 min |
| `C:\work\fak\tools\.bin\fak.exe` | `b225bb1ca20f` | **58 commits behind** (built 2026-08-06 21:07) | **nothing** |
| `C:\Users\USER\go\bin\fak.exe` | `b225bb1ca20f` | 58 commits behind | **nothing** |
| `C:\work\fak\fak.exe` (repo root) | `8af92fbdc366 +uncommitted` | a 4th, dirty hand-build | **nothing** |

`FakSelfUpdate` is **healthy**: LastRunTime 01:07:01, target rewritten 01:07:48, now at the trunk
tip. The updater is not broken — its blast radius is one path.

## Root cause

`tools/dispatch_worker.py` `resolve_fak_bin` (L887-905) resolves
`$FAK_BIN -> <workspace>/tools/.bin/fak.exe -> PATH`. `FAK_BIN` is unset host-wide, and
`tools/.bin/fak.exe` exists, so **PATH is never consulted**. Every dispatched worker argv is

```
C:\work\fak\tools\.bin\fak.exe guard --provider anthropic --audit ... -- claude ...
```

Durable proof — `.dispatch-runs/guard-probe.json` records
`"bin": "C:\work\fak\tools\.bin\fak.exe"` under build-id key `70103040-...`, and `70103040`
is that file's exact byte size.

Nothing writes `tools/.bin/fak.exe` on this host: the only writers are `make` targets and CI
workflows, and they write the **extensionless** `tools/.bin/fak` (hence that file being newer,
23:32, and a different size — a red herring, not the updater).

Three different binaries are used inside a single dispatcher tick:
- worker/guard argv -> `tools\.bin\fak.exe` (stale, 58 behind)
- `issue contract` gate (`_fak_command_prefix`, L837-845, repo-root-first) -> `C:\work\fak\fak.exe` (unmaintained dirty build)
- lease gate (`_fak_bin`, L3395-3406, `shutil.which`) -> `C:\Users\USER\bin\fak.exe` (fresh)

## Why it was invisible

`fak self-update` writes no log, no ledger, no JSON line, no status file — stdout only, and the
registered action is `conhost --headless cmd.exe /c ... ` with **no redirection**, so every line is
discarded. The only observable is the scheduler's `LastTaskResult`, one overwritten integer that is
`0` for "installed", "already current", "busy" and "--check" alike. Windows'
`Microsoft-Windows-TaskScheduler/Operational` log is also disabled, so there is no OS-level history
either.

Second-order: because the scheduled task's invoker is `tools\.bin\fak.exe` — an absolute path
captured at registration time (2026-06-28) — **the updater that runs is itself frozen 58 commits
back**. Any fix shipped to `cmd/fak/selfupdate.go` is dead code on this host until that file is
refreshed once.

## Blast radius

~20 fixes landed on trunk overnight. Dispatcher-launched workers ran guard code from
`b225bb1ca20f` (2026-08-06 21:01) for the whole window. Note the 42 `fak.exe` processes alive on
the box are all `C:\Users\USER\bin\fak.exe` (fresh) — they come from `fak accounts launch` /
interactive paths, **not** from `issue_resolve_dispatch.py`. So the running fleet and the
dispatcher's fleet are on different builds.

## Fix

- `cmd/fak/selfupdate.go`: after a fleet-mode install, also converge the invoker and
  `<root>/tools/.bin/fak[.exe]` through the same build->vet->smoke gate; exit non-zero with
  `outcome=sibling-stale` when `--target` lands but a sibling does not.
- Closed outcome vocabulary (`installed`, `target-current`, `busy`, `check-only`, `gate-failed`,
  `sibling-stale`, `self-*`) emitted as one timestamped `self-update: at=... outcome=...` line on
  every exit path.
- `tools/install_self_update_schedule.ps1`: append tick output to
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Fleet\watchdog\self_update.log` so the outcome line survives.

## Follow-ups not covered here

1. **A one-time refresh of `C:\work\fak\tools\.bin\fak.exe` is required** before the fix can take
   effect (the frozen-invoker bootstrap). `go build -o tools/.bin/fak.exe ./cmd/fak` from a green
   tree, or re-run `tools/install_self_update_schedule.ps1`.
2. `tools/issue_resolve_dispatch.py` `_fak_command_prefix` / `tools/dispatch_preflight.py`
   `_fak_command` resolve the unmaintained repo-root `C:\work\fak\fak.exe`. Owned by another agent
   tonight; not touched.
3. A stale-binary lag line on the dispatch status card (`tools/dispatch_status.py`) would make this
   class visible without reading logs.
4. **Disk**: `C:\Users\USER\bin\` holds ~462 MB of `fak.exe.old.*` swap-asides (7 files) plus ~20
   older `.bak`/`.old` binaries. Left in place deliberately as evidence.

records.title: CORE_SELF_MODIFY clears on a witness that need only be tracked, not related: 13/50 recorded clearances name a file the commit never touched
records.body:
## The defect

`CORE_SELF_MODIFY` is the hard-self lock over `internal/abi/**`, `internal/adjudicator/**`
and `internal/corelocks/**` — the one gate in the system with **no environment escape**.
An edit there clears only by supplying a *maintenance witness* claim that
`corelockgate.CheckCoreLockHardSelf` resolves against independent evidence.

The resolver answers a question about the **claim alone**. `internal/witness/witness.go`,
`case "committed":`

```
git ls-files --error-unmatch -- :/<arg>   ->  exit 0 => WitnessConfirmed
```

That asks *"is this path tracked anywhere in this repository?"* — never *"is this path part
of the change being cleared?"*. **Any tracked path in the tree therefore opens the gate.**
Verified directly on this checkout:

```
$ git ls-files --error-unmatch -- :/README.md ; echo $?
0                      # committed:README.md would clear CORE_SELF_MODIFY
$ git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD HEAD ; echo $?
0                      # ancestor:HEAD is constant-true: a commit is its own ancestor
```

`corelockgate.go` made it structural rather than accidental: it resolved with
`resolver.Resolve(ctx, nil, claim)` — a **nil `*abi.ToolCall`** — so the resolver was handed
no description of the change and *could not* correlate even in principle.

## Measured, with the denominator

`refs/notes/fak/decisions` carries **4,822 notes**. Of those, **50** contain a
`corelock-maintenance` record; all 50 are `"verdict":"allow"`. For each I compared the
`witness` claim against the commit's real `git show --name-only` set (the note already
records that set in its own `tree` field, in the same JSON object — so the mismatch was
computable from the record all along and had simply never been computed):

| reading | count | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| **correlated** | **23 / 50** | the claim names a path the commit actually changed — and all 23 name a *locked* path. The honest case. |
| **uncorrelated** | **13 / 50** | the claim names a path the commit never touched |
| **indeterminate** | **14 / 50** | `ancestor:` (13) and `grep:` (1) — structurally incapable of naming the change (see below) |

The canonical instance, `525a596cd2`:

```json
{"op":"corelock-maintenance","verdict":"allow","reason_class":"CORE_SELF_MODIFY",
 "tree":["internal/adjudicator/oot_mention.go","internal/adjudicator/oot_mention_test.go",
         "internal/adjudicator/outoftree.go"],
 "witness":"committed:internal/adjudicator/decide.go"}
```

`decide.go` is not in that commit. It is merely tracked, so the resolver said CONFIRMED.

Concentration is stark: `committed:internal/adjudicator/decide.go` appears **10x** and
`committed:internal/adjudicator/reversibility.go` **7x** — 17 of 50 clearances lean on two
files. **4** clearances used `path:` on an **absolute temp file outside the repo** that the
clearing agent had just written itself (e.g. a `...\Temp\fak-5146-adjudicator-witness.txt`),
which is precisely the self-report the witness package's own doc comment says it refuses.

### Was there a legitimate reason to name a different file? Partly — and it matters

Yes, for **2 of the 13**. The gate runs **before any `git add`** (`safecommit.go` step 4,
ahead of the STALE_UNTRACKED step that is explicitly "before any `git add`"), so
`committed:<path>` is evaluated against the *pre-commit* index. For a **newly added** file
`git ls-files --error-unmatch` exits 1 => REFUTED. So a maintainer whose change consists
only of new files **cannot** name their own work with `committed:` at all:

* `58a8924131` — sole file `A internal/adjudicator/codereview_agent_test.go`
* `e24c78a028` — sole file `A internal/adjudicator/reversibility_confirm_supervision_test.go`

Those two had no in-change `committed:`-satisfiable option and reached for a neighbouring
tracked file. That is a **grammar gap, not misconduct**, and any enforcement rung must not
punish it.

For the **other 11**, an in-change tracked (`M`) file was available and was not used —
including `525a596cd2`, which could have named its own modified `outoftree.go`, and
`d4ba1629d4`, whose single changed file `setpolicy_benchmark_test.go` was modified and
directly nameable yet was cleared with a self-authored temp file. (Three *other* clearances
used `path:` on that same file correctly.)

The 13 `ancestor:` claims are a separate structural point: the gate runs pre-commit, so the
change **is not a commit yet** and no history-shaped claim can name it — `ancestor:HEAD` and
`ancestor:origin/main` are constant-true. That is a weakness of the *claim grammar offered
to this gate*, not a mismatch that can be measured per-record, so it is reported as
`indeterminate` rather than accused.

## What shipped: observation, not enforcement

New `corelockgate.CorrelateWitness(claim, changed)` — pure, no git, no filesystem —
returns tri-state `correlated` / `uncorrelated` / `indeterminate` plus a reason sentence,
computed from `CoreLockCheck.Changed`, which the gate already holds. It is reported through
a new optional `CoreLockCheck.Observe` hook and recorded on the append-only maintenance
decision note as `witness_correlation`, alongside the `witness` and `tree` it reconciles.

Deliberate constraints:

* **The shared `committed:` rung is untouched.** It is raised by the file-admission hook,
  the dispatch-tick witness, the agent turn journal and the workflow journal — contexts with
  no "changed pathset" at all, where a correlation constraint is meaningless. The gate that
  owns a changed set asks the extra question.
* **Abstain over refute.** Only a claim positively shown to name something outside the
  change is `uncorrelated`. Matching is generous about separators, `./`, git's `:/` magic
  prefix, case, and containing directories, so an honest maintainer cannot be accused by a
  spelling difference.
* **The verdict is unchanged.** A CONFIRMED-but-uncorrelated witness still clears the lock
  today. Making the mismatch blocking in the same change that first measures it would refuse
  live fleet work mid-run, and on a surface with no env escape a rule even slightly too tight
  locks every maintainer out of `internal/adjudicator/**` permanently.

The shipped logic was replayed over the real 50-record corpus and reproduces the table above
exactly (23 / 13 / 14), misjudging none of the 23 honest cases.

## `not yet` — the enforcement step this issue carries

1. Let the recorded distribution accumulate on new `corelock-maintenance` notes, then turn
   `uncorrelated` into a refusal at the single consult point in `CheckCoreLockHardSelf`
   (one `if`). Checkable: a new clearance whose witness names an untouched file is refused,
   while one naming a changed file still passes.
2. **Close the grammar gap first, or step 1 will refuse the 2 honest cases above.** A
   maintainer whose change is purely additions needs a claim that can name a not-yet-tracked
   file. Options: let the corelock route accept `path:<changed file>` as the additive-change
   form, or add a rung resolved against the *staged/changed* set rather than the index.
3. Bound the self-authored-artifact affordance. `path:` on an absolute out-of-repo temp file
   is a self-report; the remedy sentence ("after independent read-back confirms the edit")
   invites exactly that shape without requiring the read-back to be independent.
4. Surface the reading to the operator on the `fak commit` path (not done — `cmd/fak` did not
   build in this checkout due to an unrelated peer refactor in `internal/gateway`).

Bounded: `internal/corelockgate/`, `internal/witness/decision.go`, `internal/safecommit/`.
No core-locked tree was touched.

records.title: lintwrites: the MALFORMED deny detail can echo file bytes, contradicting its own "never the file content" bound
records.body:
Two related false-safety findings in `internal/adjudicator/lintwrites.go`. Both are
**inside the hard-self core lock** (`CORE_SELF_MODIFY`, no environment escape), so this
issue reports rather than fixes them. Found while auditing the core-lock maintenance
witness (see the companion issue on `CORE_SELF_MODIFY` witness correlation).

## 1. `findingLine`'s comment claims a bound the code does not have

`internal/adjudicator/lintwrites.go:119-121`:

```go
// findingLine renders the bounded file:line:col witness the MALFORMED deny
// carries. The detail is the checker's message (never the file content); a
// zero line/col (the checker did not locate it) collapses to "<path>: <msg>".
```

The package header repeats it at lines 16-17: *"Bounded disclosure. The deny carries one
finding (file:line:col), never the file body: the deny channel is not a content oracle."*

The `never the file content` half is false. `goParseWitness` passes `el[0].Msg` from
`go/parser` straight into `findingLine`, and go/scanner's messages **embed the offending
source token verbatim** — including a whole string literal. Reproduced against the stdlib
(all literals below are synthetic placeholders, not credentials):

| written content (the whole-file write being linted) | resulting `e.Msg` |
|---|---|
| `var x = 1 "SYNTHETIC_NOT_A_SECRET_line_one_of_the_file"` | `expected ';', found "SYNTHETIC_NOT_A_SECRET_line_one_of_the_file"` |
| `var x = SYNTHETIC_NOT_A_SECRET_value$` | `expected ';', found 'ILLEGAL'` |
| `const tok = "..." bad` | `expected ';', found bad` |

The JSON half leaks a single character rather than a token
(`invalid character 'S' looking for beginning of value`), so it is materially tighter — but
the Go path is not bounded to a *location*, it is bounded to *one finding*, and one finding
can carry an arbitrarily long identifier or string literal out of the file being written.

The distinction matters because a MALFORMED deny is **attacker-influenced**: the content is
supplied by the agent under adjudication, so an agent that wants a byte out of its own
proposed write can choose a syntax error that puts that byte in the parser's message. The
comment tells a reader the channel is closed when it is not, which is the part that makes
this worth a ticket rather than a note.

## 2. `lintwrites.go` is the one witness producer that can echo file bytes, and has no producer-side bound

Every other witness/deny detail in this area is derived from evidence the agent did not
author (git ancestry, tracked paths, object existence). `lintwrites.go` is the exception:
its detail is a function of the **written content itself**. That asymmetry deserves an
explicit bound at the producer rather than a comment asserting one:

* truncate `detail` to a small fixed budget (the location is the load-bearing part; the
  token is not), and/or
* strip the `found <tok>` tail from `scanner.Error.Msg` before it reaches `findingLine`,
  and/or
* replace the token with its `token.Token` class, keeping the diagnostic useful
  (`expected ';', found STRING`) while carrying no file bytes.

## Exposure: latent, but shipped on in a load-bearing preset

`LintWrites` is opt-in and **off by default** (`internal/adjudicator/decide.go:73`;
`TestLintWritesOffByDefaultDoesNotDeny` pins it), and the rung is additionally scoped to
whole-file writes of `.go`/`.json`. So this is latent for a default deployment.

It is **not** latent for `examples/presets/coding-agent-safe.json:181`, which ships
`"lint_writes": true`, and which `docs/notes/CODING-USE-CASE-SCORECARD-2026-06-26.md`
describes as *"the hardened, round-trip-gated floor ... Load-bearing for Claude-Code-type
agents."* That preset also lists `SECRET_EXFIL` among the things it defends, which is the
same class of concern this deny channel quietly reopens.

## Suggested resolution

Whether or not the bound in (2) is adopted, the comments in (1) should stop asserting
"never the file content" while the code can emit it — either tighten the code to match the
comment (preferred, since the comment describes the intended contract) or correct the
comment to describe what is actually guaranteed. Both files are core-locked, so this needs
the maintenance-witness route.

Verified on `internal/adjudicator/lintwrites.go` at
`bec7eccccc`. No files were modified for this report.

records.title: fix(journal): concurrent writers on one journal path fork the hash chain, and the linear verifier calls the result tampered
records.body:
## Summary

`internal/journal.Open` recovers the chain head (`seq` + `lastHash`) into **process-local** state and
`appendLocked` allocates `Seq` from that private counter. Nothing prevents two processes from holding
the same journal path open, and nothing warns when they do. Each then appends from its own stale
snapshot of the head, so the file stops being a hash **chain** and becomes a hash **tree**: rows fork
off a shared prefix and the same `Seq` is reissued down more than one branch.

`journal.VerifyRows` — the linear verifier behind `fak audit verify` — reports that as
`sequence gap` / `broken chain`, i.e. as **tampering**, on a file nobody edited.

This is the same defect class as #5524 (closed), which hit the `fak guard replay` temp path. That one
was cured by disambiguating the **path** so each writer got its own file. This issue is the residual:
the writer still has no interlock, and a legacy shared file is still resolved by readers.

## Measured, on the reference host's captured `<config>/fak/guard-audit.jsonl`

Denominator: **60,514 chained rows**, spanning 2026-06-25 15:32:37 to 2026-07-01 16:17:33.

| property | result |
|---|---|
| rows whose own `chainHash(prev_hash,row)` recomputes to `hash` | **60,514 / 60,514 (100%)** |
| rows with a duplicate hash | **0** |
| non-genesis rows whose parent hash is absent (orphans) | **0** |
| genesis rows (`prev_hash==""`) | **1** |
| rows with `seq==1` | **1** |
| adjacent links where `row[i].prev_hash == row[i-1].hash` | 29,127 / 60,513 — **31,386 breaks (51.87%)** |
| rows at their linear position (`seq == i+1`) | 14 / 60,514 — **60,500 off (99.98%)** |
| adjacent seq deltas | `+1`: 29,288 · forward jump: 15,338 · repeat: 186 · **backward (rewind): 15,701** |
| timestamps going backward in file order | **0 / 60,513** |
| reconstructed root-to-tip branches | **342**, of which **342 pass the unmodified `journal.VerifyRows`**, 0 broken |
| branch points (a row named as parent by >1 row) | **335** |

Control group, same host, same resolver: the **462** non-empty per-session
`.dispatch-runs/guard-audit/*.jsonl` files hold **77,318** rows and pass the strict linear
`VerifyRows` with **zero** seq breaks, zero link breaks and zero hash mismatches.

`fak audit diagnose` on the same shared file independently returns
`verdict=INTERLEAVED, orphan_rows=0, intact_chains=342, broken_chains=0, branch_points=335`, exit 0.

## What the numbers actually say

- **Nothing was tampered with.** Every row is individually authentic and every parent resolves.
- **The damage is a fork, not an interleave of independent counters.** One genesis, one `seq==1`;
  every writer continues the *shared* numbering from whatever head it read at `Open`.
- **"Sequence gap" is a misnomer for the majority of it.** 15,701 adjacent pairs go *backward*;
  only 15,338 jump forward.
- **The disk writes are fine.** Timestamps are perfectly monotone in file order, so `O_APPEND` is
  serializing correctly. The defect is purely in the process-local seq/head allocation.
- **The hash chain fails too, not just the sequence.** 51.87% of adjacent links are broken.
  `verifyStep` checks `Seq` before `PrevHash`, so the seq error is reported first and masks it.

## Residual security exposure, stated plainly

On a forked file the surviving guarantee is a hash **tree**: an edited or deleted *interior* row
still orphans its children and is detected. What is lost is total order, and a **tip** row (one no
other row names as parent) can be truncated leaving no hole. A linear chain has exactly one such
point; this file has **342**. So concurrent writers buy a materially weaker guarantee than a single
writer — the cure is one writer per file, not a wider verifier.

## Fallout this caused

`internal/vcacheqa`'s `TestDogfood_RealGuardAuditJournalVerifies` ran the linear `VerifyRows` over
every path `guardrsi.JournalPaths` resolves, which includes the legacy shared
`<config>/fak/guard-audit.jsonl` (`internal/guardrsi/guardrsi.go:124-129`). It has been **red since
the commit that introduced it** — the test landed in `add97ec106` on 2026-06-30 19:31, and the first
fork in that capture is at 2026-06-26 08:58:29, four days earlier. Multiple agents have since hit it
and set it aside as "not mine", which is exactly how a suite loses its authority.

(For the record: `cfebe7244a` (`boundWitness`) is **not** implicated. `Witness` is not in the hash
pre-image, and the failing file's last write is 2026-07-01, five weeks before that commit.)

## Done in the same breath as this report

- `internal/journal/forest.go` — exports `journal.VerifyForest`, which applies the **same unmodified
  `VerifyRows`** once per root-to-tip branch instead of once per file, and **adds** a requirement the
  linear read never makes: every non-genesis row's parent must be present. A forked-but-intact file
  passes; a dropped, replayed, edited or renumbered row still fails.
- `internal/vcacheqa/dogfood_test.go` — holds every single-writer file to the strict linear
  `VerifyRows` with no allowance, and only falls back to `VerifyForest` where the linear read already
  failed. It also now refuses to pass if *no* single-writer file was exercised, so the strict
  contract can never quietly go uncovered.

## Still open — what this issue is asking for

1. **The writer has no interlock.** `journal.Open` should refuse, or at minimum warn, when the path
   is already held by a live writer (advisory lock / `O_EXCL` sidecar / PID+start-time stamp). Today
   an operator who sets `FAK_AUDIT_JOURNAL` to the same path in two shells, or passes the same
   `--audit PATH` twice, silently forks the trail with no diagnostic until a much later
   `fak audit verify` calls it tampered.
2. **`guardrsi.JournalPaths` still resolves the legacy shared `<config>/fak/guard-audit.jsonl`** and
   hands it to strict linear verifiers. Decide whether that path is retired, or marked as
   multi-writer at the resolver so consumers pick the right verifier without guessing.
3. **Dedupe.** `cmd/fak/audit_diagnose.go`'s `diagnoseRows`/`reconstructChain` now duplicates
   `journal.VerifyForest`. It should be refactored onto the exported function so the two cannot
   drift. Deliberately not done in this pass: `go build ./cmd/fak` is currently broken by an
   unrelated in-flight `internal/gateway` refactor, so the change could not be compile-verified.

records.title: gitdaily: delete the untracked internal/gitdaily/score.go duplicate of the shipped #5587 health card
records.body:
`internal/gitdaily/score.go` + `score_test.go` are **untracked, consumer-less, and superseded**. They are a second, independently-written implementation of the #5587 git-daily health card that lost the race to the one that shipped. This issue is the durable verdict so the next worker dispatched near #5587 does not re-derive it a 14th time.

**Recommended action: delete both files.** Nothing imports them; deleting them cannot break the build.

```
?? internal/gitdaily/score.go        (384 lines)
?? internal/gitdaily/score_test.go   (247 lines)
```

## What actually shipped

#5587 is closed. The canonical card is `internal/metrics.GradeGitDailyHealth`
(`internal/metrics/git_daily_health.go`), surfaced as `fak git-daily --score`
(`cmd/fak/git_daily.go:124`) and gated in `make ci` via `make gitdaily-score`
(added by d195e75627). Its debt key `git_daily_debt` and schema
`fak-git-daily-health/1` are a documented concept in
`docs/fak/concept-glossary.md`.

## Why the untracked pair is not a candidate

1. **Zero consumers.** Nothing in the tree references `ComposeHealth`,
   `RenderHealth`, `FoldHealth`, schema `fak-git-daily-health-scorecard/1`, or
   corpus key `git_daily_missed_days`. The 631 lines only ever run their own test file.
2. **It collides with the documented concept.** It re-defines
   `HealthDebtKey = "git_daily_debt"` — the same corpus headline the glossary binds to
   `internal/metrics`, `GitDailyDebtKey`, schema `fak-git-daily-health/1` — but emits it
   under a *different* schema. Two cards claiming one debt key in one control pane.
3. **It is missing the axis the card exists for.** The shipped `fold_drift` KPI grades the
   trailing non-ok streak — the literal #4602 signature (a wedged lock pinning the tier while
   the job keeps reporting daily success). The untracked card has no streak rule at all; its
   "drift" lens is just staleness, which duplicates the shipped `adoption` recency gate.
4. **Weaker grading elsewhere.** The shipped card caps `outcome_health` at 50 on any incident
   (an incident does not self-heal), carries three `Soft` advisories, and renders a one-line
   operator fragment. The untracked card has none of these; its health lens is a flat
   `OK/Runs` ratio.
5. **Weaker witness discipline** — which matters, because "score from witnesses, never from
   self-report" is #5587's named confusion risk. Both fold from `fak-git-daily/1` rows, so both
   clear the basic bar. But only the shipped side has
   `TestRealLedgerCaptureIsDerivedFromTheRawRows`, an explicit anti-self-report check that the
   pinned tally equals what the raw rows fold to. The untracked
   `TestHealthCardOverTheLiveLedger` asserts structure only and deliberately never asserts a
   floor — so it cannot catch a regression, and in fact does not catch item 6.
6. **It reds a healthy clone.** Graded against this clone's live ledger on 2026-08-07 it
   returns `ok=false, debt=1`:

   ```
   SHIPPED   => grade=A debt=0 ok=true
   UNTRACKED => grade=A debt=1 ok=false  usage=0.750 (covered 3/4 days, 1 "missed")
     !! git_daily_usage 0.750  recorded a tick on 3/4 graded days (2026-08-04..2026-08-07, 1 missed)
   ```

   The "missed" day is **today**, whose 03:00 tick has not fired yet. Its `DriftFraction`
   has that grace (`dark := h.StaleDays - 1`); its `UsageFraction` does not — today is always
   in the denominator. On a young ledger that one not-yet-fired day is 25% of the window and
   blows straight through the 0.8 pass line. Since `--score` exits 1 on debt, wiring this
   would fail a healthy clone every morning until the ledger is ~5 days old. That is exactly
   the failure `score.go`'s own file header warns against ("train an operator to ignore the
   card"), and exactly what `DefaultGitDailyStaleDays = 2` in the shipped card was written to
   avoid.

## The one idea worth keeping (do NOT fold it in here — it needs its own ticket)

The untracked card grades one dimension the shipped card genuinely does not: **calendar-day
coverage of a trailing window** (`DaysCovered / WindowDays`, headline `git_daily_missed_days`).
The shipped `adoption` KPI only asks "has it ever run?" and "how stale is the *newest* row?",
so an intermittent job whose newest tick is fresh grades clean:

```
job ran 4 of the last 11 days, newest tick TODAY, every tick ok:
  SHIPPED   => grade=A debt=0 ok=true    <-- green
  UNTRACKED => grade=C debt=1 missed_days=7

job fired every OTHER day for two weeks, newest tick today:
  SHIPPED   => grade=A debt=0 ok=true    <-- green
  UNTRACKED => grade=B debt=1 missed_days=6
```

That is a real blind spot. But it is **not** a copy-paste port, for two reasons, which is why
it belongs in a separate scoped issue rather than as a rider on closed #5587:

- The untracked implementation of it is the buggy one (item 6). A correct version needs a
  today-grace rule in the coverage denominator, matching the grace `adoption` already grants.
- The signal is **confounded**: a day with no row is ambiguous between "the trigger broke" and
  "the host was powered off". The shipped card names this explicitly in its adoption defect
  text ("a powered-down host reads the same way because a skipped tick writes no row"), so
  excluding coverage may have been a deliberate call, not an oversight. Whoever picks this up
  should settle that question first.

## Reproduction

The comparison above was produced with `go test -overlay` against both packages, injecting a
probe into `internal/gitdaily` (tier 2) that imports `internal/metrics` (tier 1) and rebuilds
`GitDailyHealthInput` exactly as `cmd/fak/git_daily.go:gitDailyHealthInput` does. No files were
added to the tree. Both suites are green as they stand: `go test ./internal/gitdaily/` ok 2.5s,
`go test ./internal/metrics/ -run 'GitDaily|RealLedger'` ok 0.4s.

records.title: dispatch: four fak-binary resolvers disagree, and an admission gate runs a +uncommitted build
records.body:
## What

Three independent resolvers pick a `fak` binary on ONE dispatch tick, under three
different rules, and on this host they pick **three different builds** — one of
which is a `+uncommitted` working-tree hand-build that decides an admission gate.

Measured on the live fleet host, 2026-08-07:

| resolver | rule | resolved path | build |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tools/dispatch_preflight.py:_fak_command` | `$FAK_BIN` → `<root>/fak[.exe]` → PATH | `C:\work\fak\fak.exe` | `8af92fbdc366` **+uncommitted** (16 behind trunk) |
| `tools/issue_resolve_dispatch.py:_fak_command_prefix` | `$FAK_BIN` → `<root>/fak[.exe]` → `go run` | `C:\work\fak\fak.exe` | same dirty build |
| `tools/dispatch_worker.py:resolve_fak_bin` | `$FAK_BIN` → `<ws>/tools/.bin/fak[.exe]` → PATH | `C:\work\fak\tools\.bin\fak.exe` | `b225bb1ca20f` (66 behind trunk) |
| `tools/issue_resolve_dispatch.py:_fak_bin` | `$FAK_BIN` → PATH | `C:\Users\USER\bin\fak.exe` | `a0637364f28f` (4 behind) |

`FAK_BIN` is unset host-wide, so every rule falls through to its own second
candidate and **PATH is never reached** for the first three. They agree only by
accident.

Two distinct problems fall out:

1. **The `fak issue contract` admission gate and the `fleet-accounts resolve`
   account router both execute a `+uncommitted` hand-build.** A gate whose verdict
   comes from a working-tree compile that no commit pins is not reviewable and not
   reproducible. Whatever `C:\work\fak\fak.exe` was built from at 00:39 is what has
   been admitting/holding issues since.
2. **Every dispatched worker is fronted by `tools/.bin/fak.exe`, 66 commits behind
   trunk.** (Separate from #5873's self-update path fix, which converges
   `~/bin/fak.exe` — a path no resolver above ever reaches on this host.)

## Already landed

`tools/dispatch_preflight.py` now measures this every tick: a `fak_bin` block in
the preflight payload, `DIRTY_FAK_BIN` / `FAK_BIN_DISAGREEMENT` warnings on stderr
and on the status card, and a durable
`.dispatch-runs/fak-bin-provenance.json` keyed on the resolver→build fingerprint
(so a 03:00 disagreement is still answerable at 09:00). That is measurement only —
it deliberately does not touch resolution order, because `resolve_fak_bin` returns
`None` to fail OPEN on a host with no fak built.

## Still open

- Decide the intended single source of truth for "the fleet's fak" and converge the
  four resolvers on it, preserving fail-open. Not done here: changing resolution
  order is a live-fleet risk and a human call.
- Nothing today stops a `+uncommitted` build from deciding an admission gate. The
  warning is loud but advisory.

## Repro

```
python -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'tools');from pathlib import Path;import dispatch_preflight as dp,json;print(json.dumps(dp.fak_bin_provenance(Path('.')),indent=1))"
```

records.title: dispatch_preflight_test is not hermetic: ambient FAK_HOST_*/FAK_SESSIONS_PER_ACCOUNT turn a green module 13-red
records.body:
## What

`tools/dispatch_preflight_test.py` reads the operator's ambient environment. On the
live fleet host, which exports fleet-tuning knobs, **13 of 128 tests fail** — and
they pass cleanly the moment those knobs are unset. The module is green on trunk;
it is the *host* that turns it red, so any agent running it here reads a false red
and may "fix" code that is correct.

Measured on this host, 2026-08-07 (trunk `b776d3035c`):

```
$ python -m pytest tools/dispatch_preflight_test.py -q
13 failed, 115 passed

$ env -u FAK_HOST_CORES_PER_WORKER -u FAK_HOST_THREADS_PER_CORE \
      -u FAK_SESSIONS_PER_ACCOUNT python -m pytest tools/dispatch_preflight_test.py -q
128 passed
```

## The three leaking knobs

| env var (set on this host) | captured at import by | tests it breaks |
|---|---|---|
| `FAK_HOST_CORES_PER_WORKER=1` | `dispatch_preflight.HOST_CORES_PER_WORKER` (default 2) | `HostCapacityPureTest` x2, `HostCapFoldTest`, `RenderTest::test_render_shows_host_cap` — assert `host_cap=32` for a 64-core box, get 64 |
| `FAK_HOST_THREADS_PER_CORE=1000` | `dispatch_preflight.HOST_THREADS_PER_CORE` (default 400) | same family |
| `FAK_SESSIONS_PER_ACCOUNT=6` | `fleet_accounts` via `SESSIONS_PER_ACCOUNT_ENV` (default 4) | `SeatPoolTest` x8, `LiveSeatLeasesTest` — assert `total_seats == 4`, get 6 |

## Why a per-test `mock.patch.dict` will not fix it

All three are folded into **module-level constants at import time**
(`HOST_CORES_PER_WORKER = _env_pos_int("FAK_HOST_CORES_PER_WORKER", 2)` at
`tools/dispatch_preflight.py:1479`). By the time a test body runs, the env has
already been read. The fix has to be either:

- the test module pins the knobs before importing (clear the three keys in
  `load()` / `load_fleet_accounts()`, or `setUpModule`), **or**
- the constants become lazy reads so a test can patch the env at all.

Pinning in the test loader is the smaller change and matches how `patch_checks`
already stubs every other ambient input for hermeticity.

## Why it matters here

This is the same class of defect as a stale binary: the check reports on something
other than the thing under test, and reports it confidently. An agent that runs
this module on the fleet host today sees 13 red and no signal that its own diff is
not the cause.

records.title: fix(toolproc): session-qualify the brokered background call id — bg:<n> collides across sessions in the shared journal
records.body:
## Symptom

`fak toolproc ps --events .fak/toolproc/journal.jsonl` — the reader named in the
`--toolproc-hooks` flag help and in `cmd/fak/toolproc.go` — refuses this
workspace's live journal with:

```
toolproc: duplicate spawn for call bg:8
```

`Fold` refuses the WHOLE table on a duplicate spawn identity, so one collision
blinds every session's rows, not just the colliding one.

## Cause — a per-session key used as a global key in a shared file

`internal/toolproc/hookpulse.go` builds the background-job identity from the
harness's background-shell id alone:

```go
if id := hookBackgroundID(p.ToolResponse); id != "" {
    callID := "bg:" + id
```

That id is a small integer the harness allocates **per session** and restarts at
1 for each new session. But `.fak/toolproc/journal.jsonl` is ONE SHARED FILE for
the whole workspace by design (`cmd/fak/guard_toolproc_hooks.go`: "One shared
journal per workspace: events carry the harness session id, so concurrent
guarded sessions interleave without colliding"). Every other identity on the
journal honours that — spawns key on the harness's globally unique `tool_use_id`,
and the fallback identity in `hook.go` is explicitly session-qualified
(`fmt.Sprintf("hk:%s:%s:%s", p.SessionID, p.ToolName, digest)`). The bg bridge is
the one path that drops the session qualifier.

## Measurement (live journal, 29,525 rows, 2,344 sessions, 2026-07-16..2026-08-07)

- 18,200 distinct spawned `call_id`s; **11 are spawned more than once**.
- **All 11 are `bg:` ids**, and **all 11 span more than one session**
  (`bg:8` x3 in 3 sessions, `bg:10` x3 in 3, `bg:11` x3 in 3, `bg:1..5` x2 each).
- 0 non-`bg:` duplicated identities. The collision set is exactly the unqualified
  key space.
- 14 duplicate spawn rows in total — enough to refuse the entire table.

## This is the same defect class as #5524 / #5876

A key that is unique per writer, used as the key in a file with many writers.
#5524 settled the cure: one writer per file, or a globally unique key — never a
looser verifier. `hookCallState` and the poll bridge resolve against the same
unqualified id, so a poll can also correlate onto ANOTHER session's job.

## Ask

Session-qualify the brokered-background identity at the producer, e.g.
`callID := "bg:" + p.SessionID + ":" + id`, matching `hook.go`'s existing
fallback. `Fold`'s duplicate-spawn refusal is correct and should not be relaxed.

## Not a duplicate of #3152

#3152's lifetime split (`session_end` written for a hook firing rather than for
the session's lifetime) is fixed by 74bffd4d4964. Replaying the live journal in
layers shows they are independent and stacked:

| layer | result |
|---|---|
| as-is | refuses at row **100 of 29,525** (0.34% in) — the `session_end` defect |
| + #3152 fix (74bffd4d4964) | +126 `session_resume` rows; clears the boundary defect, then refuses on `duplicate spawn for call bg:8` |
| + session-qualified bg id (this issue, probe only) | **folds clean: 18,214 procs, 8,420 running, 9,794 done, 4,964 orphaned, 105 sessions resumed** |

So this is the last thing standing between the operator and a working tool-process table.

records.title: feat(model): wire load-provenance to an operator surface and a run-manifest producer (#4746 remainder)
records.body:
## Why

[#4746](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/4746) ("expose loader-transform provenance in run evidence") is the backlog's most-retried open issue — **28 dispatch attempts**.
