records.title: feat(index): add set-based token containment as the near-duplicate test for paraphrased text
records.body:
## Axis

**Set-based token *containment* over an existing full-text index, as the near-duplicate test for LLM-paraphrased text — measured to beat both string normalisation and sentence embeddings, with no model, no vector column, and no new dependency.**

## Prior art (INSPIRE only — see licence note)

`agnt-gg/agnt`, `backend/src/utils/memorySimilarity.js:1-30` @ `66208c56`. Measured on their live store of 97,504 rows:

| approach | result |
|---|---|
| exact byte match | caught **0.002%** (exactly two rows were byte-identical) |
| normalised shape key | collapsed 1.56x |
| bag-of-words hashing | **worse than a dumb prefix** (1.02x) |
| MiniLM embeddings, 250-row probe | 43.2% lower bound |
| **token containment over the existing FTS index** | **51.6% blocked / 72.8% had a near-duplicate at all** |

Their conclusion: *"The redundancy is semantic, so the comparison has to be set-based rather than string-based"* — and containment beat embeddings while needing no model download, no vector column, and no new dependency.

**Their worldview:** a local-first desktop app cannot ask a user to download an embedding model to deduplicate their own notes. That constraint pushed them to find the cheap method that actually works — and the honest reporting of the negative results (bag-of-words losing to a prefix) is what makes the measurement worth trusting.

## fak seam

fak's own capability lookup, `fak_feature_query`, is a lexical ranker with a documented false-ABSENT problem — the reason the `field-borrow` and `study-repo` skills both instruct agents to *"guard the lexical ranker's false-ABSENT by varying the phrasing and a raw `Grep`"*, and to witness a high-value ABSENT twice before trusting it.

**This is not a theoretical concern.** During the study pass that produced this ticket, three `fak_feature_query` calls phrased at three different axes each returned the entire index (~1.0–1.2M characters, exceeding the response limit), so the entire capability witness for this study had to be re-done with raw `Grep`. A ranker that cannot discriminate is the same defect as a ranker that cannot recall.

fak already has the substrate this borrow needs: `internal/gateway/mcp_defer.go:68` documents `rankToolNamesByIntent`, a **hybrid ranker** over the tool catalog that *"fails OPEN"* and replaced a substring matcher precisely because substring matching lacked ranked recall (#3235). The technique exists in fak — on the tool catalog, not on the feature/capability index.

**Witness:** PARTIAL. `Grep` over `internal/` for `containment|jaccard|near.?dup|shingle|minhash|simhash` returns only path-containment checks in the adjudicator and process-tree containment in accounts — no set-based text similarity anywhere.

## First checkable step

A pure scoring function in `internal/` — `Containment(a, b []string) float64`, the fraction of the smaller token set present in the larger — plus a fixture test over a handful of hand-built paraphrase pairs and non-pairs, asserting the paraphrases score above a declared threshold and the non-pairs below it.

Pure function, no index wiring, no I/O. Pointing it at the feature index (and deciding the threshold from fak's own corpus rather than AGNT's) is the follow-on.

## Licence

**INSPIRE, not INTEGRATE.** Source-available under the "AGNT Community Core License" — study permitted, redistribution/forking forbidden. Clean-room reimplementation in Go; citation for provenance only.

Study trail: `docs/notes/CONCEPT-STUDY-AGNT-2026-08-08.md`

records.title: feat(dojocal): gate repeat extraction on a structural outcome signature that excludes durations
records.body:
## Axis

**Gate repeat expensive work on a hash of the outcome's *structural shape* — so the repetitive case degrades to silence without ever suppressing the anomalous one, and there is no threshold to tune.**

## Prior art (INSPIRE only — see licence note)

`agnt-gg/agnt`, `backend/src/services/evolution/ExtractionGate.js:1-84` @ `66208c56`.

The problem, measured: *"May 2026 alone wrote 50,194 memory rows, and the largest single cluster is 4,859 copies of 'Duplicate timer trigger execution'."* An LLM insight-extraction step was re-running on structurally identical outcomes and writing the same conclusion thousands of times.

The signature (`workflowSignature`) hashes:
- the run status,
- the **sorted** multiset of `node_id:status`,
- an `anyError` flag,

and **deliberately excludes durations** — *"including them would make every run novel"*, which is the whole design in one clause. Same shape within `EXTRACTION_COOLDOWN_MS` (24h) means skip; a new shape always runs. Result: 288 extractions/day to 1 (99.7% reduction).

Two properties worth taking beyond the idea itself:
- it **fails open** — a gate error runs the extraction rather than dropping it;
- it records `occurrence_count` on *both* paths, so the suppressed runs still produce a census. Suppression yields data instead of destroying it.

**Their worldview:** AGNT's evolution loop spends LLM calls to mine its own execution history, on a single user's machine where that spend is visible and personal. They needed the repetitive tail to cost nothing while the rare anomaly still got full attention — hence a structural equality test rather than a similarity threshold nobody can tune.

## fak seam

`Grep` over `internal/` for `novelt|outcome.?signature|structural.?signature|cooldown.*extract` finds novelty only as a **ranking weight**, not a gate:

- `internal/dojocal/select.go:28` — `selectWNovelty = 0.45`, one term in a weighted score
- `internal/dojocal/select.go:417` — `Novelty == 1` marks a cell with no journal touch at all

That is "prefer the novel candidate when ordering a list". It is not "skip this work because its outcome shape has been seen". Nothing in fak hashes an outcome's structure to suppress a repeat.

**Witness:** PARTIAL. fak has a novelty *concept* in the dojo/RSI selector; it has no structural-signature gate upstream of any expensive repeat step.

fak has candidate consumers: the RSI/dojo loop re-derives from repeated runs, and the guard-complaint intake (`internal/guardaccuracy/complaints.go:42`) already carries an `Occurrences` recurrence weight — the census half of this design, without the gate half.

## First checkable step

A pure signature function in `internal/`:
- `Signature(status string, nodes []NodeOutcome, anyError bool) string`, hashing the sorted `id:status` multiset;
- a test that two runs differing **only in duration** produce the **same** signature (the excluded-durations property, pinned);
- a test that a single changed node status produces a **different** signature.

Pure function, no store, no caller. Choosing which fak lane consumes it, and its cooldown, is the follow-on.

## Licence

**INSPIRE, not INTEGRATE.** Source-available under the "AGNT Community Core License" — study permitted, redistribution/forking forbidden. Clean-room reimplementation in Go; citation for provenance only.

Study trail: `docs/notes/CONCEPT-STUDY-AGNT-2026-08-08.md`

records.title: feat(tools): reconcile line endings per file with mixed-file healing and a banned-constant guard test
records.body:
## Axis

**A file's existing line endings win over any global policy on write, mixed files heal to their dominant ending, and the whole contract is defended by a test that bans the platform-default EOL constant from every write path.**

## Prior art (INSPIRE only — see licence note)

`agnt-gg/agnt`, `backend/src/utils/lineEndings.js:1-46` @ `66208c56`.

The observed damage:

> `write_file` over an existing CRLF file rewrote the WHOLE file to LF. A one-line change to OrchestratorService.js restyled 3,654 lines.

And the subtler half, which is the part most implementations miss — **mixed** files:

> OrchestratorService.js at 3654 CRLF / 15 LF [...] A patch script that does `detectEol(file)` once then builds a multi-line anchor silently matches ZERO in the other half of the file, which is indistinguishable from a wrong anchor.

Their contract: no policy configured → fall back to policy; uniform file → **existing wins**; mixed file → **heal to dominant**; binary → untouched. Enforced structurally:

> There is deliberately no `os.EOL` anywhere in this module, and a guard test (`lineEndings.contract.test.js`) keeps it out of every write path.

**Their worldview:** AGNT is a cross-platform desktop app whose agent edits the user's own checked-out repo, so a whole-file EOL flip lands in the user's `git diff` immediately and destroys review. The test banning the platform constant is the durable part — the contract survives the next contributor who reaches for the obvious helper.

## fak seam

fak solves this **locally, in one parser**, and nowhere else:

- `internal/agentsindex/agentsindex.go:10` — *"a section's Raw is sliced verbatim from the source bytes (CRLF preserved)"*, with `:211` and a dedicated witness `agentsindex_test.go:149` (`TestCRLFSpansStayByteExact`)

That is one module defending itself. There is no repo-wide write-path contract, no mixed-file handling anywhere, and no test keeping the platform-default constant out of write paths. `Grep` over `internal/` for `gitattributes|lineEnding|os\.EOL` finds no policy layer.

The failure this prevents is already recorded operationally on this repo: an editing tool flipping a file's endings turns a one-line change into a whole-file diff, which on a shared trunk both destroys review and inflates the commit-by-explicit-path surface.

**Witness:** PARTIAL. fak has byte-exact CRLF preservation in a reader; it has no reconciliation contract on the writer side, and specifically nothing for mixed files.

## First checkable step

A pure `internal/` helper:
- `Detect(b []byte) (dominant EOL, mixed bool)`;
- `Reconcile(existing, new []byte) []byte` implementing absent→policy / uniform→existing-wins / mixed→heal-to-dominant / binary→untouched;
- a fixture test covering all four cases, with the mixed case built at a realistic ratio (overwhelmingly one ending plus a handful of the other) so the dominant-healing branch is genuinely exercised;
- an architest row asserting no write path imports the platform-default EOL constant.

## Licence

**INSPIRE, not INTEGRATE.** Source-available under the "AGNT Community Core License" — study permitted, redistribution/forking forbidden. Clean-room reimplementation in Go; citation for provenance only.

Study trail: `docs/notes/CONCEPT-STUDY-AGNT-2026-08-08.md`

records.title: epic(loopsteer): steer live tool-call repetition, not just degenerate prose
records.body:
## Thesis

fak's live loop-breaker reads **prose**, not **actions**. `degenerateStreak`
(`internal/gateway/messages_resultnotes.go:212-240`) collects the trailing run of
*text-only* assistant turns and counts `[fak]` echoes and verbatim prose repeats. Its
second statement is the load-bearing premise:

```go
if len(m.ToolCalls) > 0 {
    break // "A turn carrying a tool_use is forward progress and ends the run."
}
```

So a model that calls the same tool with the same arguments forty times in a row is,
by the live steer's own definition, making forward progress on every one of those
turns. The streak never starts and `repetitionLoopSteer` (line 291) never fires.

fak already agrees this is a real pathology — it just only notices after the session is
over. `internal/sessionaudit/behavior.go` computes `RepeatFailures` /
`MaxRepeatFailure` over `(tool, sig)` pairs with a `repeatFailureMin` floor
(`RepeatFailureRow`, line 60-65), plus `SuccessLoops` and `StallGaps`. That is exactly
the right detector, sitting in the **offline audit** lens where it cannot save the run
that is burning tokens right now.

This epic moves the action-grain repetition signal into the live path and gives it a
response that is not "end the turn".

## Source studied

`youneslaaroussi/Marionette` @ `1f058aa292cf7cf82e4db34cd1e6e7bb521da770` (MIT) —
`lib/chat-context.tsx:581-679`. A browser agent driving a 9,216-token on-device model,
where a stuck loop is unrecoverable inside the window. Their loop-breaker is
tool-signature-based, cyclic-pattern aware, non-fatal, and carries a per-verb exclusion
list. **INSPIRE** — clean-room in Go; TS/React source, nothing to vendor.

Their worldview: a weak small model loops constantly, so the harness repairs it in-band
and keeps going. Their README (line 815) is explicit that this is scaffolding — *"as the
model gets better at reasoning we can gradually remove these guardrails."* fak runs
frontier models, so the *rate* is far lower — but the fleet is autonomous and unattended,
which is precisely where an undetected action loop is expensive and nobody is watching.

## Children

- Action-grain detection in the live path (the `sessionaudit` detector, promoted)
- A non-fatal in-band correction that lets the run continue
- A per-verb exclusion list so legitimately-repeated tools do not trip it

## Companions

Study note: `docs/notes/CONCEPT-STUDY-MARIONETTE-2026-08-08.md`.
Skill: `.claude/skills/study-repo/SKILL.md`.

records.title: feat(loopsteer): detect repeated tool-call signatures in the live gateway path
feat(loopsteer): non-fatal in-band loop correction that lets the run continue
records.body:
Part of #5904.

## Axis

**A detected loop is corrected in-band and the run continues** — rather than the turn
being ended.

## fak today

`internal/gateway/messages_resultnotes.go:291-313` — `repetitionLoopSteer` has exactly
one response: a terminal assistant turn with `Stop: "end_turn"`, whose text says *"I was
repeating myself without making progress ... Stopping that loop."* The doc comment is
explicit that this is the design — *"it breaks the loop deterministically and cheaply (no
model round-trip) and Claude Code reads a normal terminal assistant turn so its agent
loop settles instead of grinding to the turn-cap."*

That is the right call for the failure it was built for (a policy-blocked tool the model
keeps retrying — the loop is genuinely unrecoverable, so ending is correct). It is the
wrong call for a recoverable loop: a model re-reading the same file because it forgot it
already had the contents does not need the run killed, it needs to be told.

There is currently no middle rung between "invisible" and "terminate".

## Source

`youneslaaroussi/Marionette` @ `1f058aa292cf7cf82e4db34cd1e6e7bb521da770` (MIT) —
`lib/chat-context.tsx:600-660`. On detection it appends a synthetic
`[TOOL RESULT]\nLOOP DETECTED: ...` observation into the transcript and **continues the
loop**. The correction arrives on the channel the model is already reading (a tool
result), so it needs no special handling, and the run proceeds. Their cyclic-pattern
branch gets the same treatment. `MAX_LOOPS = 60` remains as the outer backstop, so
non-fatal correction never means unbounded.

**INSPIRE** (MIT, TS → Go clean-room).

## First checkable step

Add a non-terminal variant beside `repetitionLoopSteer` that returns a corrective
in-band note (`prependTextBlock` at line 319 is the existing seam for putting kernel text
ahead of surviving `tool_use` blocks) instead of an `end_turn` turn — naming the repeated
call and what varied-or-not, and leaving the tool_use blocks intact so the turn proceeds.
Keep the existing terminal steer for the policy-blocked case; select between them on
whether the repeated call was *refused* (unrecoverable → terminate) or merely *repeated*
(recoverable → correct and continue).

Witness: a trace of repeated-but-allowed calls yields a turn that still carries its
tool_use blocks plus the note; a trace of repeated policy-refused calls still yields
`end_turn`.

Ship-alone: yes — it is a second response mode; the existing steer keeps its behaviour.

## Companions

Parent epic: see linked. Study note:
`docs/notes/CONCEPT-STUDY-MARIONETTE-2026-08-08.md`.

records.title: feat(loopsteer): mark legitimately-repeated verbs benign so repetition detection stops false-firing
records.body:
Part of #5904.

## Axis

**Some verbs are legitimately repeated, and a repetition detector that does not know
which ones is a false-positive generator.**

## fak today

`internal/sessionaudit/behavior.go:295-305` applies a single global `repeatFailureMin`
floor to every `(tool, sig)` pair with no per-verb notion. Any live detector built on the
same keying (see the sibling leaf) inherits the same blindness.

The failure is concrete: an agent filling twelve fields of a form, or paging through a
long file, or scrolling a buffer, emits a run of same-shaped calls that is *correct
behaviour*. Score that as a loop and the steer fires on healthy work — which is worse
than not detecting loops at all, because it trains operators to disable it.

## Source

`youneslaaroussi/Marionette` @ `1f058aa292cf7cf82e4db34cd1e6e7bb521da770` (MIT) —
`lib/chat-context.tsx:587`:

```ts
const excludedTools = ['think', 'fillInput', 'findElements', 'scrollDown', 'scrollUp']
```

A flat, explicit, reviewable allowlist of verbs whose repetition is expected — the
reasoning tool, the field-filler, the search, and the two scroll verbs. It is not
clever, and that is the point: the set of legitimately-repeatable verbs is a property of
the tool catalog, so it belongs *next to* the catalog rather than being inferred.

**INSPIRE** (MIT, TS → Go clean-room).

## First checkable step

Attach a `RepeatBenign bool` (or equivalent) to the verb-tier table in
`internal/devindex/tiers.go`, defaulting false, and have both the offline
`sessionaudit` counter and the live detector skip verbs marked benign. Seed it with
fak's own genuinely-repeated verbs — the read/search family — rather than guessing.

Witness: a trace of twelve repeated benign-verb calls scores 0; the same trace with a
non-benign verb scores twelve.

Ship-alone: yes — it lands as a table column plus two call-site filters and is testable
against the offline lens alone, before any live detector exists.

## Companions

Parent epic: see linked. Study note:
`docs/notes/CONCEPT-STUDY-MARIONETTE-2026-08-08.md`.

records.title: feat(ctxpages): derive a skill's tool-schema fault set from its declared allowed-tools
records.body:
Child of #2398 (progressive disclosure as kernel paging).

## Axis

**A procedure's declared tool set IS its fault set** — activating a skill materialises
exactly the tool schemas that skill declares, atomically, in the same fault. Not "skill
bodies are pages" and "tool schemas are pages" as two independently-ranked page classes.

## fak today

Both halves exist and are not connected.

- Every skill already declares its tools: `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` frontmatter carries
  `allowed-tools: Read, Bash, Grep, Glob` (e.g. `.claude/skills/commit-clean/SKILL.md:6`,
  `.claude/skills/issue-triage/SKILL.md:6`). That declaration is used as a **permission
  fence** — #2398's own thesis frames it as *"frontmatter-declared capability bounds
  enforced by convention become span-scoped policy enforced by the kernel."*
- Tool schemas page independently via `fak_tools_search` (`internal/gateway/mcp.go`),
  which the feature index describes as *"search and retrieve tool schemas on demand with
  progressive disclosure ... a `detail_level` (name|description|full)"* — driven by a
  **query**, not by the procedure that needs them.

So `allowed-tools` answers "may this run?" and never "load this." A skill that needs
five schemas still relies on the model issuing a well-phrased `ToolSearch` for each, and
a mis-phrased query silently under-faults — the skill runs with a tool it can't call.

#2398 chooses the resident set *"deterministically per intent"* via the `rankCards`
discipline. This leaf adds the cheaper, exact case underneath that ranking: when the
intent is *"run skill X"*, the required set is not a ranking problem, it is already
written down in X's frontmatter.

## Source

`youneslaaroussi/Marionette` @ `1f058aa292cf7cf82e4db34cd1e6e7bb521da770` (MIT).

- `lib/playbooks/types.ts:1-6` — a procedure record is
  `{ id, description, contents, requiredTools: string[] }`. The required tools are part
  of the procedure's *definition*.
- `lib/tools/getPlaybook.ts:24` — retrieving a procedure by id concatenates the body with
  the docs for exactly its declared tools, in one return value:

  ```ts
  const toolDocs = generateToolDocumentation(TOOL_REGISTRY, playbook.requiredTools)
  const fullPlaybook = `${playbook.contents}\n\n## Tools for this workflow\n\n${toolDocs}\n\n${TOOL_FORMAT}`
  ```

- `lib/playbooks/index.ts:15` — only one-liners stay resident:
  `'## Available Playbooks\n\n' + PLAYBOOKS.map(p => \`- **${p.id}**: ${p.description}\`)`.

They quantify the win in their own README (lines 466-473): 22 tools resident ≈ 2,400
tokens (74% of the window free) versus 9 core tools + playbook one-liners ≈ 850 tokens
(91% free) — ~1,550 tokens reclaimed against a **9,216-token hard ceiling**.

**INSPIRE** — MIT, so integration would be legal, but this is TS against a Chrome
extension registry; the borrow is the coupling, not the bytes.

### Their worldview, and why it still applies here

They are pinned under a 9,216-token on-device model where over-residency is fatal, so
they had no choice but to make disclosure exact. fak's window is vastly larger, so the
*byte* pressure is weaker — but the correctness argument survives the difference: the
under-fault (skill runs, tool schema absent, call fails) is a real failure mode
independent of window size, and #3229 makes the always-sent floor a first-class concern
anyway.

## A caveat worth carrying

`allowed-tools` is currently a **maximum** (a fence), and this leaf would also read it as
a **minimum** (a fault set). Those are not the same set: a skill may permit a tool it
rarely uses. Land the fault-set derivation such that the two readings stay
distinguishable — either a separate frontmatter key, or an explicit decision (recorded)
that for skills the fence and the fault set are intentionally the same list.

## First checkable step

Parse `allowed-tools` from `SKILL.md` frontmatter into a resolved tool-schema page set,
and assert the set matches the declaration exactly for every skill in `.claude/skills/`.
Witness: a table test over the checked-in skills that each one's derived fault set equals
its frontmatter list, and that a skill naming an unknown tool fails loudly at parse time
rather than at call time.

Ship-alone: yes — the derivation and its test land without changing what the gateway
actually pages.

## Companions

Parent: #2398. Related: #3229 (always-sent token floor), #1258 (syspromptmmu).
Study note: `docs/notes/CONCEPT-STUDY-MARIONETTE-2026-08-08.md`.

records.title: test(gateway): sequenced scripted-model harness with inter-step data flow over the real tool loop
records.body:
## Axis

**Deterministic multi-step E2E over the *real* agent loop and the *real* tools, where
step N+1 consumes step N's actual output** — the model is the only thing substituted.

## fak today

fak has a scripted mock, and it is deliberately a *single-shot canned reply*, not a
sequence. `internal/gateway/gateway.go:2182` and `internal/gateway/http.go:1360` both
guard it with warnings that *"scripted responses must never be mistaken for model
output"*, and the operator-facing diagnosis text describes an empty `--base-url` as
*"the offline scripted mock, hence canned replies."*

That covers "does the wire work". It does not let a test say: *call tool A, take the
index A really returned, feed it to tool B, assert the loop terminates* — which is the
shape of every real agent failure. Today those paths are exercised either by unit tests
that stub the tools (so the loop is not real) or by live model runs (so the test is
nondeterministic).

## Source

`youneslaaroussi/Marionette` @ `1f058aa292cf7cf82e4db34cd1e6e7bb521da770` (MIT) —
`lib/ui-test-runner.ts` (172 lines) with `lib/e2e-config.ts`.

The mechanism: `checkForTestTrigger()` matches a user utterance to a test case, then
`getNextTestChunk()` emits, *in place of model output*, a literal
`<function_call>{"function": "...", "arguments": ...}</function_call>`. Everything
downstream — parsing, routing, tool execution, the result loop — is the production path.

The part that makes it more than a replay script is the inter-step data flow:

- `call_tool` steps carry `saveAs`, binding the tool's **real** result into a test
  context (line 72-77)
- `extract_data` steps run a `regex` + `captureGroup` over a saved result to pull out a
  value (line 98-112)
- `resolveVariables()` (line 153-171) recursively interpolates `{varName}` into the next
  step's arguments

So the script asserts against what the tools actually returned, not against values the
test author hardcoded. `wait_for_input` terminates the sequence cleanly.

Note it ships **disabled** behind `E2E_TEST_CONFIG.ENABLE_UI_TEST_MODE` (line 30) — the
harness is inert in production by construction, which is the right default for anything
that can impersonate a model.

**INSPIRE** (MIT, TS → Go clean-room).

## First checkable step

Add a sequenced script backend beside the existing canned mock: a JSON/table-driven list
of steps (`call_tool` with optional `save_as`, `extract` with a capture group, `respond`)
that the gateway emits as successive assistant turns, with `{var}` interpolation from
prior **real** tool results. Gate it behind the same explicit-off flag discipline the
current mock uses, and keep the "never mistaken for model output" warnings.

Witness: one E2E test that scripts a two-tool sequence where the second call's argument
comes from the first call's real output, and asserts the loop terminates with the
expected final turn — passing with no model and no network.

Ship-alone: yes — new test-only backend, no production path changes.

## Companions

Study note: `docs/notes/CONCEPT-STUDY-MARIONETTE-2026-08-08.md`.

records.title: feat(capture): deny a source at ingest instead of masking its spans at read time
records.body:
## Axis

**Exclude a whole *source* at ingest, so its content never enters the store** — as
distinct from masking spans on the way out of a store that already holds them.

## fak today (PARTIAL — the capability is present, this axis is not)

fak's redaction is span-grained and read/egress-time:

- `internal/canon/pii.go:58` — `RedactPII(body []byte) (redacted []byte, masked int)`
  masks email/phone/ID/card spans inside a body that has already been produced. This
  session saw it fire live: `[fak] masked 1 PII span in a tool result (PII_REDACTED) —
  the rest of the output is intact and in context.`
- `internal/agent/transcript.go:175` — `RedactOutboundMessages` / `redactOutbound` runs a
  `wirescreen.Redactor` over messages heading outbound.
- `internal/adjudicator/decide_egresslist_test.go` — an egress list governs where data
  may go.

All three answer *"what may leave"*. None answers *"what may be taken in"*. For fak's own
capture surfaces (session journal, trajectory capture) the content is recorded first and
screened later, which means the sensitive bytes exist at rest, and the guarantee is only
as good as every downstream reader remembering to screen.

The warn-first default makes this sharper, not softer: masking is designed to let work
continue, so it is the wrong instrument for a source you never wanted recorded at all.

## Source

`youneslaaroussi/Marionette` @ `1f058aa292cf7cf82e4db34cd1e6e7bb521da770` (MIT) —
`lib/auto-capture.ts:4-45`. Their ambient page recorder consults two tables **before**
capture:

- `SKIP_DOMAINS` — mail, chat, banking-adjacent, social origins
- `SKIP_PATTERNS` — `/login/i /signin/i /signup/i /register/i /auth/i /checkout/i /cart/i
  /payment/i /settings/i /account/i /profile\/edit/i /admin/i`

plus a 24h dedup cooldown keyed on normalised `origin + pathname`. A page matching either
table is never read, never embedded, never stored. Nothing downstream has to remember
anything.

They also ship the falsification procedure for the resulting claim (`PRIVACY.md:230-238`:
open DevTools, watch the Network tab, observe zero outbound requests) — a claim paired
with the check that would refute it, which is a posture fak already holds elsewhere.

**INSPIRE** (MIT; TS → Go clean-room, and the tables themselves are domain-specific —
fak's equivalents are paths and repos, not consumer web origins).

### Their worldview, and where it diverges

They are privacy-maximalist for a consumer running an ambient recorder over their whole
browsing session — the blocklist is a product promise. fak's capture is over an
engineering workspace the operator already owns, so the *motivation* is weaker. What
carries across is the **structural** point rather than the privacy pitch: a
never-recorded source needs no downstream discipline, and the failure mode of
"screen it later" is unbounded in the number of readers.

## First checkable step

Confirm-or-refute, then build: enumerate fak's capture entry points (session journal,
trajectory capture) and check whether any consults a deny table before writing. If —
as the greps above suggest — none does, add an ingest-time source predicate consulted
*before* the write, seeded with a conservative table (credential and secret paths, the
lab-access surfaces) and expressed as a refusal reason from the existing closed
vocabulary rather than a silent drop, so a skipped source is auditable.

Witness: a test that a denied source produces zero bytes at rest (not masked bytes) and
one recorded refusal.

Ship-alone: yes — one predicate plus its table, before one write path.

## Companions

Study note: `docs/notes/CONCEPT-STUDY-MARIONETTE-2026-08-08.md`.

records.title: feat(accounts): drive the cap kind from the anthropic-ratelimit-unified headers, not four independent banner-text guesses
records.body:
## Problem

Four independent places in this repo answer the question "is this Claude wall a 5-hour rolling
cap or a weekly limit?", and **all four guess from banner text**:

| classifier | input | vocabulary |
|---|---|---|
| `tools/issue_resolve_dispatch.py` `_cap_hit_from_text` | worker `resolve-*.log` tail | `weekly` / `rolling_5h` / `session` |
| `tools/fleet_accounts.py` `active_account_cap_throttles` | the sidecar's `kind` string | `reset` leg vs `weekly` leg |
| `internal/accounts/cooldown.go` `ResolveReset` / `ResolveCooldownReset` | launch stderr | one `CooldownUsageLimit` kind |
| `internal/fleetaccounts/soonness.go` `resetTime` | a carried throttle's reset string | dated (weekly) vs bare (rolling) layouts |

Text is the **weakest available signal** and it is not the only one we have. The provider already
answers the question unambiguously, on every response, in the `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-*`
headers — and **this repo already reads them**:

- `internal/agent/retry_limit.go` `unifiedResetFor(reason, h, now)` selects the `5h` header family
  for `resume.LimitSession` and the `7d` family for `resume.LimitWeekly`.
- `internal/resume/scan.go:78-81` already defines the closed vocabulary `LimitSession` /
  `LimitWeekly` / `LimitUsage` / `LimitRate`.

So the authoritative signal and a typed vocabulary both exist. Neither reaches the cooldown store
or the dispatcher gate, which re-derive the answer from prose and disagree with each other.

A concrete consequence of deriving it from text instead: `internal/resume/scan.go:78` documents
`LimitSession` as *"the 5-hour rolling cap"*, while `tools/issue_resolve_dispatch.py` treats
`session` as a **short** window with a 90-minute ceiling. The same token means two different
window lengths in two packages, and nothing catches it because no test compares them.

## Proposed fix

1. Promote the header read to a shared, typed producer: a `CapKind` resolved from
   `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-5h-*` vs `-7d-*` (plus its `-reset` epoch), not from prose.
2. Carry that kind and reset through the seams that currently re-derive it — the account-cap
   sidecar `.dispatch-runs/account-cap-<product>[-<account>].json`, `CooldownEntry`, and the
   `throttle["weekly"]` leg `DisambiguateCap` reads.
3. Demote banner-text classification to an explicit **fallback**, used only when no headers were
   captured (a bounced child process, a log tail with no wire record), and mark the sidecar with
   which source decided so an operator can tell a measured hold from a guessed one.
4. Rename or split `LimitSession` so "session" stops meaning both "the 5-hour rolling cap"
   (`internal/resume`) and "a short sub-hour window" (the dispatcher). One parity test asserts the
   two packages agree on every fixture.

## Acceptance criteria

- A captured 429 carrying `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-7d-*` produces a `weekly` hold whose reset
  equals the header epoch, with **no** banner text present in the fixture at all.
- The same for `5h` → a rolling hold, again with no banner text.
- A fixture with headers AND a *contradicting* banner resolves to the header's answer, and the
  sidecar records `source=header`.
- A fixture with no headers still resolves via text and records `source=banner`.
- One parity test pins `internal/resume`'s vocabulary and the dispatcher's kind strings to the same
  window lengths, so `session` cannot mean 5 hours in one package and 90 minutes in another.

## Relationship

- Blocks-on / follows #5890, which fixes the **text** classifier (banner detection, the missing
  `rolling_5h` kind, per-kind hold ceilings, the weekly floor). That is the fallback path this
  issue makes secondary. #5890 is worth landing first and independently, because the fallback runs
  whenever headers are unavailable.
- #1352 (durable sessions / 429 taxonomy) is the umbrella this typing belongs to.
- #2610 fixed the gateway `announced_wait` path, which is the one existing case where a
  machine-emitted window already beats prose — this generalizes that principle to the provider's
  own headers.

## Work estimate
Estimate: 5 points. Uncertainty: the header capture point (`internal/agent`) and the cooldown
writer (`cmd/fak` / `internal/accounts`) are on different call paths; plumbing may need a carrier
struct rather than a field.

## Overall completion contribution
Contribution: 5/5 points.

## Completion standard
production

## Target operating envelope
- header_sourced_share: >= 90% of holds written from headers rather than banner text
- cap_kind_disagreements: 0 fixtures where the header source and the text fallback disagree unresolved
- vocabulary_parity: 1 test pinning resume/dispatcher window lengths equal

## Witnessed operating envelope
- header_sourced_share: n/a (no header-sourced path reaches the cooldown store yet; measured today is 0%)
- cap_kind_disagreements: n/a (no header source exists to disagree with)
- vocabulary_parity: n/a (no test compares the two vocabularies today)

## Notes

The header reader already exists and is unit-tested — `internal/agent/retry_limit.go`
`unifiedResetFor` — so this is a plumbing and typing change, not new provider integration.

records.title: fix(dispatch): launch_goal_detached.ps1 hands guard a flat 200k cumulative budget and restart-limit 3, killing every detached worker at ~15% of runway
records.body:
## What

`tools/launch_goal_detached.ps1` hands `fak guard` a **flat** `--context-budget-tokens
200000` and `--restart-limit 3`. Both Go and Python launch paths were fixed long ago to
*derive* these (#2972, #4253); the PowerShell launcher was pinned to neither sibling and
silently kept the pre-fix shape. It is the launcher `/fleet-wave` and `/super-loop` drive,
so every attended wave in this repo inherits the starved budget.

`--context-budget-tokens` is a **CUMULATIVE** allowance, not a per-turn ceiling
(`internal/session/usage.go` `DebitUsage`): each turn subtracts that turn's *entire*
resident window, so `turns_funded ≈ budget / resident_per_turn`. The launcher's comment
justified 200000 as "~3x headroom over the ~62K turn-1 floor" — that is the per-turn vs
cumulative dimensional error `cmd/dispatchworker/guard.go` already documents as
`FIXED(turn-starvation)`. Under a cumulative meter the headroom factor **is** the turn
count.

## Witness — wave fw08081943, 2026-08-08

Nine detached guarded workers. **All nine** died `API Error: 409 ... request refused:
BUDGET_CONTEXT_EXHAUSTED`, child exit 1, between 19:49:43Z and 19:51:45Z — 6-8 minutes
into a 45-minute `--max-duration` runway (~15%), the exact signature both siblings'
comments record for the starved regime.

The compactor was **not** at fault, and the durable witness proves it. From
`.fak/nightrun/compaction-health.jsonl`, the nine sessions:

| fired | bailed | shed (tok) | budget | cache_read_at_fire |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 9 | 34,132 | 96000 | 88,638 |
| 6 | 5 | 207,124 | 96000 | 174,807 |
| 0 | 12 | 0 | 96000 | — |
| 3 | 9 | 107,674 | 96000 | 126,094 |
| 5 | 7 | 70,367 | 96000 | 213,925 |
| 3 | 8 | 130,894 | 96000 | 73,524 |
| 6 | 5 | 203,763 | 96000 | 199,115 |
| 6 | 5 | 201,984 | 96000 | 294,606 |
| 6 | 5 | 252,028 | 96000 | 248,161 |

Wave-wide: 37 fires, **1,207,966 tokens shed**, `anchor_starved=0`, `solvency_forced=0`,
and all 65 bails are correct-by-design reasons (`under_budget` 54, `too_few_msgs` 10,
`burst_unprofitable` 1). Compaction did its job and the session died anyway, because
residents of 73k-294k against a 200,000 cumulative allowance fund **~2 turns**, and
`--restart-limit 3` spends the three hops in minutes.

The shed-line itself is correct — `--expose-profile headless` gives 96000, matching every
row. Only the drain ceiling and the restart cap are wrong.

## Arithmetic

| | Go / Python | PowerShell (this bug) |
|---|---|---|
| context budget | `max(200000-32000, 62000) × 12` = **2,016,000** | flat **200,000** (10× low) |
| restart limit | **16** | **3** |
| turns funded at the 96000 shed-line | 21 (≥ 12 ✓) | **2** (≥ 12 ✗) |

## Why it stayed hidden

`tools/launch_goal_detached.ps1` has **no test coverage anywhere in the tracked tree** —
every apparent hit is a gitignored scratch mirror. `TestClaudeGuardCompactHistoryBudget`
and friends pin Go↔Python to each other; the third sibling was never added, so it could
drift indefinitely without reddening anything.

## Done condition

1. The launcher's `-ContextBudgetTokens` default equals `claudeGuardContextBudgetTokens`.
2. Its `--restart-limit` equals `claudeGuardRestartLimit`.
3. A drift pin asserts both against the **derivation** (not literals), so a future envelope
   change moves all three launch paths together.
4. The pin also asserts the end-to-end property that actually failed: a worker sitting at
   the shed-line resident still has a full epoch funded.
5. Regression witness: the pin must fail against the pre-fix launcher.

## Notes

Found while running a real wave; the wave itself produced no closes because of this.

records.title: feat(agent): disclose an interrupted prior turn in the resumed agent's own context, not just on metrics
records.body:
## Problem

fak detects an interrupted prior turn and records it — **for the operator only**. The
resumed *agent* is never told.

`internal/agent/loop.go:463-465` reads the write-ahead checkpoint once at loop entry and
lands it on the metrics struct:

```go
if resume := cfg.resumeCheckpoint(); !resume.IsZero() {
	m.ResumedPendingTurn = resume
}
```

The comment above it (`internal/agent/loop.go:456-462`) is explicit about the intent —
"so the run is observably RESUMING that turn (attempt N) rather than starting a fresh
turn-0 that has forgotten the lost attempt" — and equally explicit that it is
"Read-only here". The write-ahead machinery itself is sound (`internal/agent/chat.go:562`,
`:864`, the symmetric clear at `:1034`).

So the *supervisor* knows the turn was interrupted. The *model* resumes with a context
that has forgotten it. Everything the lost attempt may have already done — a partially
applied commit, a lander that ran, a pushed ref, a spawned worker — is invisible to the
agent that is about to decide what to do next. On this repo's shared trunk that is
exactly the shape that produces a double-apply.

## The borrow

`PrimeIntellect-ai/prime-agent` @ `a18809e00ea30638584d87b3afea7285a9d7296c` writes the
crash notice **into the transcript itself**, as a hidden entry addressed to the model:

`packages/coding-agent/src/modes/daemon/daemon-catalog-process.ts:268-277` injects a
`custom_message` reading:

> `<prime_agent_worker_interrupted>` … uncertain model, tool, bash, or child-agent work
> was not replayed. Inspect external side effects before continuing.

Two properties worth taking, independent of their daemon:

1. **The disclosure is in-band.** It reaches the decision-maker, not just the dashboard.
   The agent can act on it (check `git log`, check the lock, check for a pushed ref)
   before doing anything with side effects.
2. **It names the uncertainty honestly** — "was not replayed", "inspect external side
   effects" — rather than silently resuming as if the gap did not exist.

They pair it with a recovery rule that refuses to replay: a mutation recorded as
`received` with no `result` is treated as uncertain and never re-issued
(`packages/coding-agent/src/modes/daemon/command-recovery-journal.ts:73-89`).

fak should **not** copy that half — fak's write-ahead checkpoint is a typed cursor into a
deterministic journal and re-entering it is the correct, audited behavior. The borrow is
narrowly the *disclosure*, not the refusal-to-replay.

## First checkable step

When `resumeCheckpoint()` is non-zero at loop entry, inject one bounded system/custom
message into the resumed turn's context stating that a prior attempt was interrupted at
attempt N and that external side effects (commits, pushes, spawned workers, held locks)
may already exist and should be verified before new side-effecting work.

Witness: a test that drives the loop with a non-zero `resumeCheckpoint()` and asserts the
provider saw the interruption notice in the outbound context — not merely that
`m.ResumedPendingTurn` was set.

## Witness

- fak seam: `internal/agent/loop.go:463-465` (metrics-only), `internal/agent/chat.go:562`
  (the write-ahead twin that produces the checkpoint).
- Dogfooded `Grep` over `internal/resume/`, `internal/sessionjournal/`,
  `internal/watchdoghealth/`: fak's crash lane (`internal/resume/crashdrive.go:47-56`)
  joins CRASHED records to identity/watchdog state for *analysis*. Nothing injects the
  fact of the crash into the resumed agent's own context. **PARTIAL on this axis** — the
  detection exists, the in-band disclosure does not.
- License: MIT source into an Apache-2.0 tree. This is **INSPIRE** — the technique only;
  no bytes copied (TypeScript → Go).

Source: `PrimeIntellect-ai/prime-agent` @ `a18809e00ea30638584d87b3afea7285a9d7296c`.
Filed from a `/study-repo` pass; see `docs/notes/CONCEPT-STUDY-PRIME-AGENT-2026-08-08.md`.

records.title: test(ci): prove the suite passes with zero provider credentials by stripping them at the entry point
records.body:
## Problem

fak manages real Anthropic seats — `accounts add`, `accounts launch`, credential refresh,
cooldowns, a live gateway. Nothing in the test entry point proves the suite cannot reach
those real credentials or spend real tokens.

`Makefile:91` is the whole contract:

```make
test: architest-gate
	go test ./...
```

Credential hygiene is currently **per-test and opt-in**: individual tests call
`os.Unsetenv` where the author remembered to
(`internal/fleetaccounts/discover_apikey_test.go:169`,
`internal/dispatchtick/main_test.go:13`, `internal/gardenbundle/gardenbundle_test.go:237`),
and `internal/accounts/credrefresh_test.go:122` documents the need explicitly — "have
`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, and `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` removed (else
`claude -p` …)". That comment is the tell: the requirement is understood, but it is
enforced one test at a time, so a newly added test inherits the developer's live
environment by default. The failure is silent and expensive — a test that quietly
authenticates against a real seat passes locally, burns tokens, and may mutate account
state.

## The borrow

`PrimeIntellect-ai/prime-agent` @ `a18809e00ea30638584d87b3afea7285a9d7296c` makes it a
property of the **entry point**, not of each test.

`test.sh:5-20` moves the credential store aside under an `EXIT` trap so it is restored
even on failure or Ctrl-C:

- stash `~/.prime/agent/auth.json`, restore via `trap … EXIT`
- set the no-local-LLM flag
- then `test.sh:26-60` `unset`s ~35 provider credential env vars before invoking the suite

Three details that make it more than a shell trick:

1. **A named single source of truth.** Both `test.sh` and their `--no-env` run wrapper
   (`prime-agent.sh:26-63`) carry a pointer to the one file that enumerates the variables
   (`packages/ai/src/env-api-keys.ts`), so the list cannot drift silently in one place.
2. **It is a stated rule, not a convention.** Their `AGENTS.md:32` — "Do not use real
   provider APIs, real API keys, or paid tokens" — and the suite is built around a faux
   provider so the rule is satisfiable rather than aspirational.
3. **The restore is trapped**, so an interrupted run does not leave the developer without
   their credentials.

## First checkable step

Add a credential-stripping wrapper in front of the `test` target (or a `test-hermetic`
target wired into `make ci`) that clears the provider env vars from one enumerated list,
and a test asserting that list matches fak's own credential-env registry so the two cannot
drift.

Witness: a test that exports a bogus `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`,
runs the wrapper, and asserts the child process saw neither.

fak already has the registry half — `internal/envconfiglint` enumerates credential-shaped
env names (`internal/envconfiglint/envconfiglint_test.go:15` covers `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`,
`GITHUB_TOKEN`, `DB_PASSWORD`, `CLIENT_SECRET`, …), so the source of truth exists and is
already tested. This is wiring it to the test entry point, not building it.

## Witness

- fak seam: `Makefile:91` (`test:` target — no credential fence),
  `internal/envconfiglint/` (the existing enumeration to reuse).
- Dogfooded `Grep` over `internal/`, `cmd/`, `Makefile` for `unsetenv|ANTHROPIC_API_KEY|
  hermetic`: hits are per-test `os.Unsetenv` calls and hermetic *fixture* helpers, never a
  suite-wide fence. **PARTIAL on this axis** — the enumeration exists, the entry-point
  enforcement does not.
- License: MIT source into an Apache-2.0 tree. **INSPIRE** — technique only (their
  `test.sh` is bash around an npm suite; fak's is a Makefile around `go test`).

Source: `PrimeIntellect-ai/prime-agent` @ `a18809e00ea30638584d87b3afea7285a9d7296c`.
Filed from a `/study-repo` pass; see `docs/notes/CONCEPT-STUDY-PRIME-AGENT-2026-08-08.md`.

records.title: feat(a2achan): bound send RATE per sender-target pair, not just queue depth
records.body:
## Problem

`a2achan` bounds a mailbox's **depth** but not a sender's **rate**. One agent can occupy
a peer's entire attention budget as fast as that peer drains.

`internal/a2achan/a2achan.go:96` sets `DefaultQueueCap = 1024`, and
`queueFullVerdict` (`internal/a2achan/a2achan.go:159-161`) refuses an enqueue past the cap:

```go
return abi.Verdict{Kind: abi.VerdictDeny, Reason: abi.ReasonRateLimited, By: "a2achan/cap"}
```

The reason token is `ReasonRateLimited`, and the doc comment at
`internal/a2achan/a2achan.go:155-158` is candid that this is an "honest in-set mapping"
onto the closed vocabulary rather than a real rate limit. It is a **memory** bound: it
closes the #3480 unbounded-growth leak for an abandoned mailbox, which it does correctly.

What it does not bound is throughput against a *live* peer. A receiver that drains
promptly never reaches 1024, so a chatty or looping sender can enqueue without limit,
indefinitely, and consume the target's turns. The cap only engages once the target has
already stopped coping.

## The borrow

`PrimeIntellect-ai/prime-agent` @ `a18809e00ea30638584d87b3afea7285a9d7296c` runs **three
independent layers** on the same channel
(`packages/coding-agent/src/core/agent-messages.ts:12-15`, `:334-365`, `:463-506`):

1. a per-message size cap (16 KiB),
2. a per-session pending-queue depth cap (20) — fak's existing layer, and
3. a **token bucket keyed on the `sender → target` pair** (3 per 1000 ms).

The third is the one fak lacks, and the pair-keying is the load-bearing part: a global
rate limit would let one loud sender starve every other sender's access to the same
target, while a per-pair bucket bounds each *relationship* independently.

The detail worth taking with it: **the bucket is refunded when delivery fails**
(`packages/coding-agent/src/modes/daemon/daemon-mode.ts:5435`). Without a refund, a sender
that hits a full queue or a paused bus permanently burns quota for a message that was
never delivered — the limiter would punish the sender for the receiver's state.

Their worldview for this: a shallow star topology (`RLM_MAX_DEPTH` defaults to 1) of
long-lived unattended agents where a confused child looping on `agent_message.send` is a
realistic failure, and no human is watching. fak's dispatch fleet has the same shape and
the same absence of a human, which is why the borrow transfers.

## First checkable step

Add a per-`(from, to)` token bucket to `Bus.Send`/`Publish` alongside the existing depth
cap, refunding the token when the enqueue is refused for any reason other than the rate
limit itself. Keep the closed-vocabulary `abi.ReasonRateLimited` — it becomes literally
true — but distinguish the `By:` tag (`a2achan/rate` vs the existing `a2achan/cap`) so the
two backpressure causes stay separable in the audit trail.

Witness: a test that sends N messages faster than the bucket refills to a target that is
draining normally (queue never near 1024) and asserts the refusals carry `By:
"a2achan/rate"`; plus a test that a `cap`-refused send does not consume a rate token.

## Witness

- fak seam: `internal/a2achan/a2achan.go:96` (`DefaultQueueCap`), `:159-161`
  (`queueFullVerdict`), `:165-175` (`Send`'s deny-as-value contract).
- Dogfooded `Grep` over `internal/a2achan/` for `rate|quota|bucket|per.?sender|refund|
  window`: every hit is either the `ReasonRateLimited` token or the depth cap's own
  documentation. There is no time-based limiter and no quota to refund.
  **PARTIAL on this axis** — depth-backpressure is PRESENT and correct; rate-backpressure
  is ABSENT.
- License: MIT source into an Apache-2.0 tree. **INSPIRE** — technique only.

Source: `PrimeIntellect-ai/prime-agent` @ `a18809e00ea30638584d87b3afea7285a9d7296c`.
Filed from a `/study-repo` pass; see `docs/notes/CONCEPT-STUDY-PRIME-AGENT-2026-08-08.md`.

records.title: fix(fleetaccounts): weekday-named weekly resets ('reset on Monday at 9am') are unparseable in Go and wall the seat indefinitely
records.body:
## Problem

Claude names a weekly reset by **weekday** far more often than by date ("your limit will reset on
Monday at 9am"). The Go reset parser cannot resolve that form, and it fails in the *opposite*
direction from the Python one — so the same banner produces two different, both-wrong holds
depending on which side of the fleet reads it.

`internal/fleetaccounts/soonness.go:15`:

```go
var weekdayPrefixRE = regexp.MustCompile(`^(mon|tue|wed|thu|fri|sat|sun)\s+`)
```

It strips a **three-letter** weekday followed by whitespace — the `"Mon Jun 25 at 1pm"` shape its
own comment names. Two adjacent real shapes fall through:

1. **Full weekday name.** `"monday at 9am"` — `^mon` is not followed by `\s`, so nothing is
   stripped, `raw` stays `"monday at 9am"`, and none of `resetTime`'s six layouts parse it.
   `resetTime` returns `ok=false` → `resetIsFuture` nil (unknown) → and per the regex's own
   comment, `throttleIsActive` then **fails closed and treats it as a still-active weekly cap,
   walling a healthy seat indefinitely.**
2. **Weekday with no date.** `"mon 9am"` — the prefix IS stripped, leaving `"9am"`, which the
   bare-time layout anchors to **today**. A Monday reset read on a Thursday resolves to a few
   hours out instead of four days.

The Python side has the mirror-image bug, now fixed by #5890: `_parse_reset_to_utc` ignored the
weekday word entirely and its bare time-of-day branch resolved `"Wednesday at 3pm"` read on a
Thursday to **today 3pm — a 1.6-hour hold on a cap with six days left to run.** #5890 added a
weekday branch to the Python parser; the Go parser still has neither behavior.

So today: Go over-holds a weekday-named reset forever (fail-closed unknown), Python under-held it
to a few hours. Neither is the real reset, and the two disagree — which is exactly the divergence
`resetTime`'s doc comment claims to prevent ("Mirrors fleet_accounts._reset_is_future's
anchoring").

## Proposed fix

1. Widen the weekday scrub to full names and make it a *resolving* branch, not just a strip:
   a weekday token plus a time-of-day resolves to the **next** such weekday (rolling a full week
   when the named day/time is at or before now), matching the branch #5890 added to
   `_parse_reset_to_utc`.
2. Keep an explicit date winning over a weekday token, so `"Mon Jun 3 at 9am"` still resolves to
   Jun 3 even when Jun 3 is a Wednesday.
3. Keep the horizon clamp so a garbled clause can never wall a seat indefinitely — the current
   fail-closed-on-unparseable path is the indefinite wall this issue is about.
4. Add a cross-language fixture list so the Go and Python parsers are pinned to the same answer
   for the same string.

## Acceptance criteria

- `resetTime("Monday at 9am", <a Thursday>)` returns the following Monday 09:00, `ok=true` — today
  it returns `ok=false`.
- `resetTime("mon 9am", <a Thursday>)` returns the following Monday, not today.
- `resetTime("Mon Jun 3 at 9am", ...)` still returns Jun 3 (date beats weekday).
- A fixture table of weekday-named resets produces the same instant from the Go parser and from
  `tools/issue_resolve_dispatch.py:_parse_reset_to_utc`.
- A behavioral test asserts a weekday-named weekly throttle is neither re-admitted before its
  reset nor held past it.

## Relationship

- Follows #5890, which fixed the Python half and added the weekday branch this mirrors.
- #5911 (header-authoritative cap kind) makes text parsing the fallback rather than the source;
  this issue hardens that fallback, so the two are complementary, not alternatives.

## Work estimate
Estimate: 2 points. Uncertainty: low — `resetTime` is pure and already time-injected; the risk is
the fail-closed callers that currently depend on `ok=false` for these strings.

## Overall completion contribution
Contribution: 2/2 points.

## Completion standard
production

## Target operating envelope
- weekday_reset_parse_rate: >= 6/6 weekday fixture forms resolved (today 0/6 in Go)
- go_python_reset_disagreements: 0 across the shared fixture table
- indefinite_walls_from_unparseable_weekday: 0

## Witnessed operating envelope
- weekday_reset_parse_rate: n/a (no weekday branch exists in Go yet; measured today is 0/6)
- go_python_reset_disagreements: n/a (no shared fixture table exists to compare against)
- indefinite_walls_from_unparseable_weekday: n/a (fail-closed by construction today; the count is
  unmeasured because the wall is silent, not logged)

## Notes

The Go failure mode is documented in `weekdayPrefixRE`'s own comment — "without this strip the
weekday makes the whole string unparseable, which resetIsFuture reports as nil (unknown) and
throttleIsActive then treats fail-closed as a still-active weekly cap — walling a healthy seat
indefinitely". That is precisely what a full weekday name still does.

records.title: epic(ohmypi-study): mine can1357/oh-my-pi @896bf5f (CoW worker isolation, mid-stream tool-call steering, compaction arithmetic, reversible credentials) for fak — witnessed borrows
records.body:
Umbrella for the witnessed borrows mined from **can1357/oh-my-pi** (`omp`), an MIT
TypeScript/Bun + Rust coding-agent harness, forked from `badlogic/pi-mono`.

**Source:** <https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi>
**Pinned:** `896bf5f33e0b67bdd0cf951c82739a28e75d0823`
**License:** MIT. fak is Apache-2.0, so MIT→Apache vendoring would be permitted with
attribution — but **every child is routed INSPIRE (clean-room)**, because the source is
TypeScript/Rust and the value is the technique, not the bytes. Each child cites its
source `path:line@896bf5f`.

## Same upstream as #4040's sibling study

`prime-agent` (studied 2026-08-08, `docs/notes/CONCEPT-STUDY-PRIME-AGENT-2026-08-08.md`,
filed #5892/#5893) is a **hard fork of the same `pi-mono` ancestor**. The two studies
therefore cover sibling descendants of one codebase, and the borrows are disjoint by
construction — that note's rows are lock identity, no-progress oracles, and the memory
cluster; this epic's are isolation cost, the tool-call stream, compaction arithmetic,
credentials, and retry safety. Where they touch, this epic defers to the earlier filing.

## Their worldview (reconstructed, with evidence)

- **A full harness for one developer on a laptop**, where fak is a management plane wrapped
  around someone else's agent. This asymmetry eliminated a whole class of otherwise
  attractive borrows (structural-summary reads, hashline anchors, the fs scan cache): fak
  does not own the read/edit tools, so there is nothing to borrow them into.
- **Fan-out is normal and disk is scarce** — hence one isolation PAL with eight
  copy-on-write backends (`crates/pi-iso/src/lib.rs`) rather than one copy strategy.
- **The model is treated as steerable mid-generation**, not only at tool boundaries — hence
  stream rules that abort a tool call while its arguments are still being written.
- **Credentials are substituted, not removed**, so the model can still operate on a value
  it must never see.

## Children

Each is independently shippable and sized to a first checkable step. No monolith.

**Worker isolation cost** (also under #3165; deliberately distinct from #3572's warm pool
and #3242's shared GOCACHE — those amortize *creation* and *build*, this attacks *bytes*):
- #5918 — CoW isolation-backend seam, default = today's behavior
- #5919 — Windows block-clone backend behind that seam (depends on #5918)

**The tool-call stream** (fak's guard decides at the `PreToolUse` boundary; these move the
observation earlier):
- #5920 — stream-rule matching over tool-argument deltas, detection only
- #5921 — affordance-first mid-stream substitution — **inverts the source's policy** (see
  below); depends on #5920
- #5922 — anti-nag injection ledger, counted in completed turns and restored on resume
  (ships independently of #5920)

**Context arithmetic** (`internal/compactcohere` already models cache TTL; these add the
missing per-decision economics):
- #5924 — tool-declared useless results
- #5925 — minimum-prune floor + structural cut-point validation

**Credentials & retry:**
- #5923 — reversible per-install HMAC secret placeholders (`internal/secretgate` removes;
  this substitutes-and-restores)
- #5926 — remaining-quota preflight (`internal/accounts/cooldown.go:97` parses the 429
  *after* the loss)
- #5927 — replay-safety gate on auto-retry

Only two dependency edges exist (#5919→#5918, #5921→#5920); the other eight are
independently dispatchable today.

## The one deliberate inversion

The source's mid-stream injection is a prohibition frame — literally
`<system-interrupt reason="rule_violation" …>`. fak has a shipped, scored position that
this is the weaker construction: `internal/negframe` backs `fak score negframe`, whose law
is that steer prose leads with the affordance, and which hands back a positive rewrite
**only where the reframe is mechanically unambiguous**
(`cmd/fak/negframescore.go:76-78`; `experiments/negframe-steerability-ab/README.md:44-49`).

Applied to interception, that gives fak's rule: **interrupt only when you can substitute
the action to take; when there is no unambiguous substitute, do not interrupt.** Ship the
source's lifecycle and race discipline; refuse its frame.

## Explicitly NOT borrowed (witnessed, not assumed)

- **Content-addressed artifacts** — `internal/blobfs` is already a durable CAS implementing
  `abi.Resolver` / `abi.CASPinner` / `abi.PageOutBackend`; strictly stronger than the
  source's session-local `artifact://` integers. PRESENT-on-axis.
- **Approval tiers (read/write/exec)** — `internal/adjudicator`'s capability-floor rungs
  plus `internal/laneadmit`'s lane/tree/lease collision model are a richer admission
  system. PRESENT-on-axis.
- **Read/edit tooling** (structural summaries, hashline anchors, selector grammar, fs scan
  cache) — N/A: fak does not own these tools.
- **`snapcompact`** (history rendered to per-model-tuned PNG frames priced against vision
  billing geometry) — genuinely novel, and a watch item rather than a borrow: it depends on
  owning the transcript renderer.

## Method note

Read serially, not via the skill's parallel fan-out: a standing session instruction bars
spawning subagents unless the operator asks. Depth was met by reading 18 subsystem design
docs end-to-end plus `crates/pi-iso/src/lib.rs`, and every fak-side seam cited in a child
was verified against the working tree before filing.

Study note: `docs/notes/CONCEPT-STUDY-OH-MY-PI-2026-08-08.md`.

records.title: feat(workerworktree): add a copy-on-write isolation-backend seam — make a worker tree cost O(delta), not ~450MB (epic #5917, #3165)
records.body:
Give `internal/workerworktree` a pluggable **isolation backend** seam so a worker's
private writable tree can be materialized copy-on-write instead of by a full
`git worktree add`, and land the seam with today's behavior as the default backend
(zero behavior change on the first commit).

## The axis

**Per-worker tree materialization cost** — the bytes and wall-clock it takes to hand one
worker a writable private view of the trunk.

This is deliberately *not* the axes fak already owns:

- **Worktree isolation exists** (#1334, shipped `17ba17f`) — not this.
- **Creation-frequency amortization exists** — the warm pool shipped at
  `internal/workerworktree/pool.go:24-36` (#3572) leases/returns pre-prepared members.
  A pool makes you create *less often*; it never makes one tree *cheaper*.
- **Build-cache sharing exists** (#3242, warm read-only base GOCACHE) — that attacks the
  cold-build tax, not the tree bytes.

The axis here is the copy itself: `Prepare` is O(tree) on every filesystem. On a
copy-on-write filesystem the same operation is O(delta) — the worker's tree costs only
what the worker actually writes.

## Source (INSPIRE — clean-room)

`crates/pi-iso/src/lib.rs` @ `896bf5f` — one isolation PAL behind a single
`IsolationBackend` trait, with a per-target `native()` default and a universal fallback:

- APFS `clonefile(2)`, btrfs subvolume snapshot, ZFS clone, Linux `FICLONE` reflink
- kernel `overlayfs` (degrading to `fuse-overlayfs` when the syscall is denied)
- Windows `FSCTL_DUPLICATE_EXTENTS_TO_FILE` block clone (NTFS/ReFS), ProjFS
- `Rcopy` — `git worktree` when the lower tree is a git repo, else recursive copy

The load-bearing design decision to copy: **`IsolationBackend::diff` delegates to
`git diff` whenever the merged tree is a git repo**, so the produced patch is
byte-identical to what `git apply` consumes. That is what lets the backend vary
underneath while the land path stays exactly the same.

**License:** oh-my-pi is MIT (`LICENSE:1`); fak is Apache-2.0, so vendoring would be
permitted with attribution. Routed **INSPIRE** anyway — the source is Rust, the value is
the technique, and fak's Go idiom + `GitRunner` seam differ enough that a clean-room
implementation is smaller than an FFI boundary.

## Witness — PARTIAL (on-axis)

fak is in the neighborhood but not on this axis. Every materialization path funnels
through `internal/workerworktree/workerworktree.go:359` (`Prepare`), which shells a
detached `git worktree add`. Cost is O(tree) whether or not the pool is warm. The
cold-worktree leak accounting prices it directly:

> `internal/workerworktree/coldreap.go:11-12` — "Prepare CREATES a ~450MB detached
> worktree per worker; Reap collects exactly ONE…"

At the fleet cap this epic targets, ~450MB × N is the disk budget. A CoW backend turns
that into ~450MB once plus each worker's actual delta.

Searched for prior art before filing: no open issue covers reflink/clonefile/block-clone.
#3572 (pool) and #3242 (GOCACHE) are adjacent and intentionally not duplicated.

## Scope of THIS leaf (ship-alone)

Seam only. No new syscall backend ships here.

1. Define `IsolationBackend` in `internal/workerworktree` with `Materialize` and
   `Release`, mirroring the `GitRunner` injection style already used by `Prepare` /
   `Land` / `Reap`.
2. Implement exactly one backend — `gitWorktree` — that calls today's code path verbatim.
3. Route `Prepare`/`Reap` through the seam with `gitWorktree` as the hard default.
4. Preserve the invariant that `git diff <baseSHA>` run with cwd = `Result.Path` yields
   exactly today's patch — `Land` computes the diff itself and feeds it to the lane ledger
   and the core-lock gate.

**Correction (see the implementation-plan comment):** this originally specified a `Diff`
method on the interface. Reading `Land` says do **not** add one — it already calls
`git diff` inside the worker tree at `workerworktree.go:493` and `:507`, and a
backend-supplied differ would create a second way to compute the core-lock gate's input.
Backends preserve the diff by keeping git's linkage, not by overriding the differ.

Follow-on backends are separate leaves and are explicitly out of scope here.

## First checkable step

`go test ./internal/workerworktree/` stays green with the seam in place and
`gitWorktree` selected — including `concurrent_land_soak_test.go` and
`land_refusal_retry_test.go`, which are the land-path regression witnesses.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] `IsolationBackend` interface exists in `internal/workerworktree` with a documented
      contract for `Materialize` / `Release`.
- [ ] `gitWorktree` backend implements it by calling the existing `Prepare`/`Reap` path
      with no observable change (same dir name, same detached HEAD, same env).
- [ ] `Prepare` and `Reap` select the backend through the seam; the default is
      `gitWorktree` and requires no config to stay on today's behavior.
- [ ] A backend-conformance test asserts the invariant directly, against every registered
      backend: materialize → write a known change → `git diff <baseSHA>` inside the produced
      path returns the expected patch, and `git diff --name-only` the matching name list.
      This is what makes #5919 safe to write; land it here even with one backend to run it
      against. The failure mode it guards is a **silent empty diff** that reads as "the
      worker landed nothing" — no error line, work lost.
- [ ] A table test proves backend selection is injectable (a fake backend can be
      substituted without touching `Prepare`'s callers).
- [ ] `go test ./internal/workerworktree/` green, including the concurrent land soak.
- [ ] `make ci` green; no new leaf/tier row needed (the package already exists), and no
      new `exec.Command` site added outside the existing `GitRunner`.
- [ ] The package header documents the seam and names the ~450MB-per-worker cost it
      exists to attack, cross-referencing #3165.

## Non-goals

- Any real CoW syscall (separate leaves).
- Changing `Land`'s serialization, lease, or core-lock semantics.
- Touching the pool (#3572) or GOCACHE (#3242) paths.

---

**Epic:** #5917 (oh-my-pi study). **Source pinned at** `896bf5f`. **Route:** INSPIRE (clean-room; MIT source, Apache-2.0 target).

records.title: feat(workerworktree): add the Windows block-clone isolation backend behind the CoW seam (epic #5917, #3165)
records.body:
Add a **Windows block-clone** isolation backend behind the seam from the parent leaf, so
a worker tree on NTFS/ReFS is materialized copy-on-write instead of byte-copied.

Depends on the `IsolationBackend` seam leaf. Do not start this before that lands.

## The axis

Same axis as the seam leaf — **per-worker tree materialization cost** — narrowed to the
platform the maintainers' fleet actually runs on. This is the leaf that converts the seam
from a refactor into a measured disk win, which is why it ships first among the backends.

## Source (INSPIRE — clean-room)

`crates/pi-iso/src/lib.rs` @ `896bf5f` names the Windows path
(`FSCTL_DUPLICATE_EXTENTS_TO_FILE` block clone, NTFS/ReFS) as one of eight backends
selected by a per-target `native()` default, with `Rcopy` as the universal fallback when
the filesystem refuses.

The transferable discipline is the **fallback ladder**, not the ioctl: probe the
capability, and degrade to the previous backend rather than failing the worker. A worker
that cannot start is strictly worse than a worker that starts with a full copy.

**License:** MIT source, Apache-2.0 target — vendoring permitted with attribution, but
routed **INSPIRE** (Rust → Go, and the Win32 call is `golang.org/x/sys/windows` here).

## Witness — ABSENT (on-axis)

No block-clone / reflink / `clonefile` call site exists anywhere in the tree; searched by
symbol and by concept before filing. Every worker tree is a full `git worktree add`
(`internal/workerworktree/workerworktree.go:359`), priced at ~450MB each
(`internal/workerworktree/coldreap.go:11-12`).

## Scope of THIS leaf (ship-alone)

1. A capability probe: does the target volume support block cloning? (ReFS yes; NTFS
   depends on the Windows build. Probe, never assume from the drive letter.)
2. A `blockClone` backend implementing `IsolationBackend`, gated behind that probe.
3. Fallback ladder: `blockClone` → `gitWorktree`, chosen at `Prepare` time and recorded
   on the `Result` so an operator can see which backend served a given worker.
4. The materialized path must still satisfy the seam's invariant: `git diff <baseSHA>` run
   with cwd = `Result.Path` yields exactly today's patch. A block clone copies the
   *checkout* bytes; git's linkage (the `.git` file pointing at `root`'s
   `worktrees/<id>` admin dir) must then be attached/repaired — `git worktree repair` is
   the supported route. **Budget real time for this step: it, not the syscall, is the hard
   part of this ticket.** See the implementation-plan comment on #5918.

## First checkable step

On a ReFS or block-clone-capable NTFS volume, `Prepare` a worker tree and show the
allocated size is a small fraction of the logical size, while
`go test ./internal/workerworktree/` stays green and `Land` produces the same patch.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] `blockClone` backend implements `IsolationBackend`; selected only when the probe
      says the volume supports it.
- [ ] The probe is a real runtime check against the target volume, not an OS-version or
      drive-letter guess, and is unit-tested with both outcomes.
- [ ] Fallback to `gitWorktree` is automatic and silent-but-recorded: no worker fails to
      start because the filesystem declined the clone.
- [ ] The selected backend name is exposed on the `Prepare` result so it is visible in
      dispatch telemetry.
- [ ] A witness test proves `Land`'s emitted patch is byte-identical under `blockClone`
      and under `gitWorktree` for the same fixture change.
- [ ] The concurrent land soak (`concurrent_land_soak_test.go`) is green under the new
      backend, not just the default one.
- [ ] Tests skip cleanly (never fail) on a volume without block-clone support, so CI on
      any runner stays green.
- [ ] A measured before/after disk number for one prepared worker tree is recorded in the
      issue — this leaf's value claim is a measurement, not an assertion.
- [ ] Any new Win32 call site is registered per the repo's `exec`/syscall gate rules;
      `make ci` green.

## Non-goals

- The APFS / btrfs / ZFS / `FICLONE` backends (separate leaf, lab hardware).
- ProjFS or overlayfs projection — different semantics, not a copy replacement.
- Changing pool (#3572) or GOCACHE (#3242) behavior.

records.title: feat(streamrules): match guard rules against streaming tool-argument deltas — the detection primitive (epic #5917)
records.body:
Match guard rules against **streaming tool-argument deltas** as they arrive, rather than
only against a completed tool call at the `PreToolUse` boundary. Detection primitive
only — this leaf does not abort, inject, or change any decision.

## The axis

**How early a rule can observe a tool call.** Not "does fak have a guard" (it has a strong
one) — the axis is the *observation point*. fak's rules fire when the arguments are
complete; a streaming matcher sees them being written.

Why the axis matters: everything downstream — cancelling a doomed call before it costs a
full generation, substituting the right action while the model is still mid-thought —
depends on having seen the argument early. This leaf buys the observation; later leaves
spend it.

## Source (INSPIRE — clean-room)

`docs/ttsr-injection-lifecycle.md` @ `896bf5f` (Time-Traveling Stream Rules), §2
"Streaming monitor lifecycle":

- Buffers are isolated **per tool-call stream key**, so sibling calls in one assistant
  turn never contaminate each other's match state.
- Where a tool exposes a reconstructed per-file digest, the matcher runs on the
  reconstructed snapshot; otherwise it appends the raw delta. Identical consecutive
  snapshots for a stream key are skipped — the cheap guard against re-matching an
  unchanged buffer on every token.
- Scope tokens gate which streams a rule watches (assistant text, thinking, any tool, a
  named tool, plus per-tool path globs). **Default scope excludes thinking** — a
  deliberate choice worth copying: rules should not police reasoning.

**License:** MIT → Apache-2.0, compatible; routed **INSPIRE** (TypeScript → Go).

## Witness — ABSENT (on-axis)

fak's rule surface is boundary-triggered. `internal/sessionsteer` injects at SessionStart
and persists at Stop; `internal/adjudicator` decides at admission time; the guard's
`PreToolUse` path sees a complete call. Searched for a streaming/partial-argument matcher
by symbol and concept — none exists, and no open issue covers it.

This is an ABSENT that was witnessed twice (varied phrasing + raw symbol grep) before
filing, per the borrow discipline for a high-value gap.

## Scope of THIS leaf (ship-alone)

A pure, side-effect-free matcher package. No wiring into a decision path.

1. A `StreamKey`-isolated buffer set: append deltas, keyed by tool-call id, reset per turn.
2. Rule scope parsing: text / thinking / any-tool / named-tool, plus optional path globs.
   Thinking is **off** unless a rule opts in.
3. `CheckDelta` / `CheckSnapshot` returning all matching rules for a scoped buffer.
4. Consecutive-identical-snapshot suppression.
5. Invalid rule handling: a rule whose pattern fails to compile is dropped with a
   diagnostic and never wedges the session — startup continues.

Value on its own even before anything consumes it: it makes "which rule would have fired,
and how early?" answerable offline against a recorded stream.

## First checkable step

A table test that replays a recorded tool-argument delta sequence for two sibling tool
calls and asserts each rule matches on the correct stream key, at the delta index where
the pattern first completes — and that a repeated identical snapshot does not re-match.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] New package with no dependency on the guard/adjudicator decision path (import-free
      enough to be a low tier); scope, buffers, and matching are all pure functions.
- [ ] Per-tool-call-id buffer isolation is proven by a test with ≥2 sibling calls where a
      rule matches exactly one.
- [ ] Default scope excludes thinking; a test pins that a thinking-only match is NOT
      returned unless the rule opts in.
- [ ] Consecutive identical snapshots do not re-match (test).
- [ ] An uncompilable rule pattern is dropped with a diagnostic and the remaining rules
      still register (test) — no startup wedge.
- [ ] Rule scope supports named-tool and path-glob gating, each with a test.
- [ ] Zero behavior change to any existing guard decision — this leaf wires nothing.
      A reviewer can confirm by grep: no call site outside the new package + its tests.
- [ ] New leaf carries its architest tier row; `make ci` green.

## Non-goals

- Aborting, injecting, or altering any tool call (next leaf).
- AST-based conditions — the source supports them; defer until the regex path is proven.
- Replacing `PreToolUse`. This is an *earlier* observation point, not a replacement
  decision point.

---

**Epic:** #5917 (oh-my-pi study). **Source pinned at** `896bf5f`. **Route:** INSPIRE (clean-room; MIT source, Apache-2.0 target).

records.title: feat(streamrules): interrupt mid-stream only to substitute the action to take — affordance-first, never a violation frame (epic #5917)
records.body:
Spend the streaming match from the detection leaf: when a rule matches mid-stream and
**carries an unambiguous substitute action**, abort that tool call, discard the partial,
and re-prompt with the action to take. When no substitute exists, do **not** interrupt.

This is the leaf where fak deliberately diverges from the source, and the divergence is
the point.

## The axis

**What the model is told when a rule fires** — and, downstream of that, *whether firing is
even permitted*.

## The divergence — lead with the affordance, and only interrupt when you can substitute

The source injects a prohibition frame. Its interrupt template is literally:

```
<system-interrupt reason="rule_violation" rule="..." path="...">
```

fak already has a shipped, scored position that this is the weaker construction.
`internal/negframe` backs `fak score negframe`, whose stated law is:

> "steer prose leads with the affordance. A directive framed as a prohibition makes the
> reader invert a negative to find the action; where that inversion is mechanical, the
> card names the positive rewrite and counts it as debt until applied."
> — `cmd/fak/negframescore.go:76-78`

And the design of that package is the exact rule this leaf must inherit: negframe hands
back a positive rewrite **only where the reframe is mechanically unambiguous**, and
deliberately does *not* auto-rewrite judgement-tier negations
(`experiments/negframe-steerability-ab/README.md:44-49`).

Transplanted to the interception channel, that yields the gating rule for this leaf:

- **A rule with a substitute** ("write via the commit lane" for a raw-`git commit` match)
  → interrupt, discard the partial, inject the **action to take**. The message names what
  to do; it does not name a violation.
- **A rule with no substitute** (judgement-tier: "this is probably unwise") → **must not
  interrupt**. Interrupting with a scolding frame costs a full generation and hands back
  nothing actionable. It degrades to the non-interrupting reminder path or stays silent.

So the borrowed *mechanism* is the source's; the borrowed *policy* is inverted. Ship the
lifecycle, refuse the frame.

## Source (INSPIRE — clean-room)

`docs/ttsr-injection-lifecycle.md` @ `896bf5f`, §3–4. The mechanically valuable parts,
all worth copying verbatim in shape:

- Abort is **synchronous** from the handler; extension/notification work is explicitly not
  awaited before it.
- The abort reason is **scoped to the matched tool-call id**, so sibling calls get a
  distinct reason instead of a blanket turn kill.
- `contextMode: discard` drops the targeted partial assistant output before retry, so the
  model never re-reads its own aborted attempt.
- The retry is deferred ~50ms and guarded by **four** independent staleness checks — retry
  token, prompt generation, abort-pending state, and target-message identity. Any failure
