Answers one question about the parked-work surface: which parked refs still hold content that is not on `main`, and how much. It exists because that question was answered **wrong twice in one session, in two different directions, and both wrong answers were the KIND that reads as good news.** The salvage index was written from the first, and its documented landing recipe *deletes newer work from main* as a result.

**TRAP A — an orphan bag reads as EMPTY.** Every salvage bag is built through a temp index as a **parentless** commit, so it shares no history with `main`. `git diff --name-only main...<tag>` then exits **128 with empty stdout**, and a caller that only reads stdout takes that as "nothing is parked here". Measured: **66 of 162 tags were orphans**, and one reported **0 files while holding 686 lines**. The failure is silent and points at "safe to prune", which is why it survived a whole sweep. So: resolve the merge base first, and take an orphan's payload from `git ls-tree` instead. **Never infer emptiness from empty stdout.**

**TRAP B — "the blob differs from main" is NOT "unlanded".** The obvious per-file test compares the bag's blob to main's and calls any difference unlanded work. That is how you recommend `git checkout <tag> -- <paths>` for a bag whose files main already has in a **larger, later** form: the checkout reverts the difference. One bag scored as fully unlanded under blob identity, and landing it that way would have dropped **239 lines of newer code**. **Diverged is its own outcome** and the tool must say so, because the correct action on it is a three-way diff and nothing else.

Hence three states per payload file, from a **two-dot** `git diff --name-status` (two-dot compares trees directly and needs no merge base, so one code path serves orphan and descendant alike):

```
A   absent from main   — the only true at-risk salvage
M   present, differs   — DIVERGED; needs a human three-way diff
-   byte-identical     — landed
```

## The generalizable kernel

- **An empty stdout from a git plumbing call that also exited non-zero is not a measurement.** Check the exit code; orphan history is the common cause.
- **Landed / unlanded is a false dichotomy.** DIVERGED is a third state, and it is the one where the naive remedy destroys work.
- Classify **per payload file**, not per ref — a ref that is 90% landed and 10% novel reads as all-or-nothing otherwise.

## Why fak needs it

- fak has exactly this surface: `refs/fak/wip/*` checkpoint refs, `internal/wipref` (`fak wip reap --census`, #5340), `internal/wiprecon` (reconciliation and the RECLAIM worklist, #5480), `internal/orphanscan`, `internal/goalpark`, `internal/seatpark`.
- `internal/wipref/census.go` classifies **per ref** into `OwnerLanded` / `OwnerUnknown` / `CensusClosedCleanEstimate` / `CensusClosedDirtyRecoverable`. There is no per-payload-file `A/M/-`, so a partially-landed checkpoint has no accurate class — and `CensusClosedCleanEstimate` is *the headline number a future collector will size itself against*.
- `internal/wiprecon`'s RECLAIM verdict is `git apply --check` against the moving working tree. That is the right conservative test for *applying*, but it does not distinguish "does not apply because it is already landed" from "does not apply because trunk moved past it" — which is Trap B in a different coat.
- fak's own lore already records the consequence class: a sweeper committing your dirty files, and `fak sweep --apply` taking the whole lane including live peers.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Per-payload-file classification for every `refs/fak/wip/*` checkpoint: `A` (absent from HEAD), `M` (present, differs — **DIVERGED**), `-` (byte-identical, landed), computed from a **two-dot** `git diff --name-status` so one code path serves orphan and descendant refs alike.
- [ ] A **measurement first**: how many current fak checkpoint refs are parentless, published in the ticket. If none are, the DoD records that and Trap A is closed by evidence rather than by code.
- [ ] Every git plumbing invocation in the census path checks its **exit code**; a test proves that a parentless ref does not report zero payload files.
- [ ] `DIVERGED` becomes a first-class census class in `internal/wipref`, distinct from both landed and recoverable, and `CensusClosedCleanEstimate` excludes it.
- [ ] Any reclaim/collect path that would `checkout`/`apply` a `DIVERGED` file refuses and emits the three-way-diff instruction instead.
- [ ] A regression fixture: a ref whose file HEAD already carries in a strictly larger later form is classified `DIVERGED`, and the naive blob-identity classifier is shown (in the test) to call it unlanded.
- [ ] Rerun of the `--census` headline number before and after, with the delta explained.

## Non-goals

- Changing the reap delete policy. This sharpens the classification the policy reads.

records.title: feat(memory): keep the agent auto-memory index true — a Go reconciler under the green gate
records.body:
## Source

`tb/tensor-build-main/tools/memoryindex/` — `main.go`, `scan.go` (their HOOKS-03 / #339).

## What it does there

Keeps the Claude Code auto-memory index (`MEMORY.md`) true: the index is one line per memory file, and it drifts the moment a memory is written, renamed or deleted by hand. The tool scans the memory directory and reconciles the index against it.

The transferable argument is about **where the logic lives**: their production path is a shell hook wired into `PostToolUse` and `Stop`, self-contained, carrying its own copy of the logic. *"Logic in shell is logic `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...` never sees, so the repo's own green gate cannot catch a regression in it."* The Go port exists so the checker is covered by the same gate as everything else.

(That port is itself still unwired in their tree — the honesty machinery around that fact is the subject of the sibling `unwiredscore` ticket, and should not be conflated with this one.)

## The generalizable kernel

An agent-memory index is a **derived artefact with no gate**, maintained by the same agent whose memory it indexes — which is the worst possible custodian, because the agent reads the index to decide what it already knows. Drift is self-concealing: a memory missing from the index is a memory the next session will not recall, and nothing reports it.

Two properties worth copying: (1) the reconciler is **Go, under the green gate**, not a shell hook; (2) it is a **checker first, writer second** — check mode diffs and exits non-zero, so the drift is visible in CI even when nothing is allowed to rewrite the file.

## Why fak needs it

- fak already treats agent memory as first-class: `internal/fleetmemory`, `internal/memoryread`, `internal/memq` (epic #2395 — "capped, write-and-read verified memory as the default recall path"), `internal/memorystability`, `internal/memview`, `internal/memvaluescore`, `internal/codexmemory`, and the `memory-compact` skill.
- **#2618 / #2619** (the `[[wikilink]]` graph and a materialized backlink index) are the graph half of the same problem — an index over memory files with no mechanical proof it is complete. This ticket is the *completeness reconciler* those two want underneath them: a backlink index over an incomplete file census is confidently wrong.
- The failure mode is concrete: a memory written with no index line is unreachable by recall; an index line pointing at a deleted memory is a dangling recall target; a memory whose `name:` slug disagrees with its filename breaks every `[[wikilink]]` to it.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] `internal/<name>`: a pure reconciler over `{memory files, index lines}` returning `{missing_from_index, index_line_with_no_file, slug_filename_mismatch, duplicate_slug}` — no filesystem or git I/O in the pure core, so it unit-tests without fixtures on disk.
- [ ] Frontmatter parsing validates the required fields (`name`, `description`, `metadata.type`) and reports a closed `type` vocabulary violation as its own finding.
- [ ] **Check mode is the default**: diff and exit non-zero on drift, touching nothing. A `-write` mode reconciles.
- [ ] `[[wikilink]]` targets are resolved against the file census, and unresolvable links are reported **separately** from missing index lines — a dangling link is a different defect from a missing row, and #2619 needs both distinguished.
- [ ] Wired to a real trigger (a `fak memory` sub-verb, and/or the existing memory driver path) rather than landing as an unwired port. If it must ship unwired, it carries the fires-on-success pin from the sibling `unwiredscore` ticket.
- [ ] A measured run over a real memory directory publishing the four counts, so the drift rate is known rather than assumed.
- [ ] Cross-linked from #2618 / #2619 as their completeness precondition.

## Non-goals

- Deciding what belongs in memory, or compacting it — that is the `memory-compact` skill.
- Changing the memory file format.

records.title: feat(unwiredscore): a fires-on-success pin — a doc claiming NOT WIRED must fail the day it becomes false
records.body:
## Source

`tb/tensor-build-main/tools/precommit/binroster_test.go` plus the `⛔ NOT WIRED` header convention in `tools/memoryindex/main.go` and `tools/indexgraph/main.go`.

## What it does there

Several tools in that tree are honest ports that **nothing calls yet**. The header says so in as many words — *"⛔ NOT WIRED. It has no verb and no caller"* — and then does something unusual: it makes the claim **checkable, and fires on success**.

`binRosterPins["tools/memoryindex"]` is a pin whose test *"fails the day anything outside this directory carries a run line for it."* From the header:

> It **FIRES ON SUCCESS** — the cutover HOOKS-03/#339 asks for is the outcome, and it must not be possible to land it without being told this paragraph, and the parity test's "delete me with the shell" instruction, have both gone false. The tie is bidirectional: `binRosterAdmissions` pins the words above, so the pin cannot be cleared while this text still claims to be unwired.

And the same file carries the correction that makes the point: the doc *"said 'exactly one hit' until this measurement"*. A comment recording a number needs the measurement attached, or it is only true on the day it was written.

The other half of the convention: the doc used to say the logic had been *"moved here"*. It was **copied**, and the difference is the entire point — two implementations of one checker, and the green gate covers the one nobody runs.

## The generalizable kernel

Three tied ideas:

1. **A prose claim of the form "X is not wired" is a testable proposition.** Pin it, and let the pin fail when it becomes false — so the person who finally wires it is *forced* to read and delete the paragraph that is now a lie.
2. **Bidirectional tie**: the pin also pins the words, so the pin cannot be quietly deleted while the stale prose survives. Neither side can drift alone.
3. **Fires on success, not on failure.** The normal gate fires when something breaks. This one fires when the work *completes*, because completion is exactly when the documentation goes stale and nobody is looking for a gate.

## Why fak needs it

- `internal/unwiredscore` already exists and already measures unwired surface — this gives it teeth: a score says "N unwired", a pin says "and this specific one's own description will refuse to stay wrong."
- fak's lore is dense with this exact decay: *green tests never validate a header comment*; *verify lane PROSE claims, not just tests*; *ledger negatives go stale — a triage agent's STILL_OPEN is a snapshot*; *comments recording a number need the measurement attached*.
- fak ships ports and prototypes constantly (`internal/trunkbuildprobe` is itself "a Go port of the retired `tools/trunk_build_probe.py`"), and the copied-not-moved hazard — two implementations, gate covering the unused one — is live wherever a Python tool has a Go successor. `internal/pythongate` is the register of that whole migration.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] A pin mechanism in `internal/unwiredscore` (or adjacent) taking `{package, claim text, predicate}` and **failing when the predicate goes true** — with a failure message that names the prose to delete.
- [ ] The **bidirectional tie**: the pin also asserts the claim text is still present verbatim, so deleting the paragraph without clearing the pin also fails. Tested in both directions.
- [ ] At least one predicate implemented for the common case: "no call site outside this package" — computed from the AST/import graph, not from `grep`, so a string in a test fixture does not count as a caller.
- [ ] A **numbers-need-a-measurement** variant: a pin that ties a count stated in prose to the value the tool computes, so a stale number in a doc comment fails rather than merely misleads.
- [ ] Applied to ≥3 real fak sites, chosen from the copied-not-moved population (a Go port whose Python original still runs, per `internal/pythongate`), with the pins landing green and their claims true at a named SHA.
- [ ] Documented in `AGENTS.md` or the contributor docs as the convention for landing an intentionally-unwired port, so the next one does not ship a bare comment.

## Non-goals

- Wiring anything. This ticket makes "not wired yet" an honest, self-correcting state, not a permanent one.

records.title: feat(preflight): probe controls — every probe needs a positive control, and no fail-open range verdicts
records.body:
## Source

Three tb tools that are domain-specific in their subject and identical in their epistemology:

- `tools/logcal/mcapcal` — re-derives camera intrinsics from log files.
- `tools/logcal/mcaprate` — the **negative control** for that decoder.
- `tools/logcal/crosscheck` — cross-channel agreement between two independent derivations.
- `tools/r13optical` — measures inter-frame rotation from pixels alone.

The measurements themselves do not port. The four rules they encode do, and every one of them is a rule about **probes that lie quietly**.

## What they do there

**1. A probe that reports nothing is blind until a positive control proves otherwise.** `mcapcal` decodes a message using field numbers derived from the descriptor the file itself carries. `mcaprate` decodes *the same bytes* using the canonical upstream field numbering instead, and reports what that produces and whether the three structural checks fire. Without that negative half, "the checks did not fire" and "the checks cannot fire" are the same output. The named trap: a decoder written from a schema's *visual order* silently reads the wrong field and returns **plausible garbage with no error**.

**2. Two channels that share no code path make agreement into evidence.** `crosscheck` compares a log-derived value against an independently published census. Disagreement then localises the fault to one side, which a single-source measurement can never do.

**3. A range test fails open, and a table of greens reads as agreement.** From `crosscheck`'s own correction: the `in [min,max]?` column — the only verdict the table used to print — was **TRUE for all six rows, including both outliers**, because the admissible ranges span 2.08x to 5.26x. *"It is a threshold that fails open, and a reader scanning that column sees six greens and concludes the channels agree."* The ratio column is where the disagreement lives. Also flagged: one row agreed at **exactly 0.000%** because both channels carry the same nominal constant — *a tautology rather than a cross-check*, and it is labelled `NOMINAL-LOOKING` for that reason.

**4. An argmin always returns a number, and the argmin of noise looks like a measurement.** `r13optical` therefore ships **two controls per measurement**: `explained = 1 - madBest/madZero` (how much of the observed change the answer accounts for; ~0 means the answer explains nothing) and a far-pair control (if the best fit is no better than the deliberately-decorrelated pair, no model applies at all).

The header on `crosscheck` also notes its own summary of the evidence was **wrong until corrected, in the direction that overstates it** — five rows "agreeing" when only three could, and two disagreeing rather than one.

## The generalizable kernel

Four checkable rules for any fak probe or scorer:

1. Every probe ships a **positive control** (a case that must fire) and, where a decode or parse is involved, a **negative control** (the wrong-but-plausible interpretation, run on the same input).
2. A verdict derived from a **single** channel is labelled as such; agreement between independent channels is the only thing reported as corroboration.
3. **No fail-open threshold as the headline column.** If the admissible band admits nearly everything, report the *magnitude* (ratio, delta, residual), not the boolean.
4. A fit or search that always returns an answer must report **how much of the signal that answer explains**, plus a control that would look the same under pure noise. A tautological agreement (both sides read the same constant) is flagged, never counted.

## Why fak needs it

- fak is dense with probes and scorers whose failure mode is exactly this: `internal/trunkbuildprobe`, `internal/accountprobe`, `internal/apihostprobe`, `internal/xprobe`, `internal/preflight`, `internal/guardaccuracy`, plus dozens of `*score` packages and the whole scorecard family.
- fak's operating lore is a catalogue of rule-1 failures: *a vacuous green-gate behind `//go:build ignore`*; *`go test -overlay` reporting a false `ok`*; *green tests never validate a header comment*; *`git grep` alternation is BRE, so `A|B` silently returns a false negative*. Every one is "the check could not fire and the output was indistinguishable from clean".
- Rule 3 is live in fak's scorecards, where a pass/fail band is the printed column and the magnitude is not.
- Rule 4 is live wherever fak ranks or selects — `internal/dispatchorder`, `internal/simhash`/`trigram` similarity, `internal/issuededup`. A dedup that always returns a nearest neighbour needs to report how near.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] A written probe contract in the contributor docs stating the four rules, with the tb evidence as the rationale.
- [ ] A small shared helper for reporting a measurement as `{value, explained_fraction, control_value, single_channel: bool}` so the controls are a type, not a convention.
- [ ] **Positive control coverage audit**: every `internal/*probe*` package and the `preflight` ladder is listed with whether it has a test that *must fail* if the probe goes blind. Gaps are enumerated, not silently skipped.
- [ ] ≥3 probes retrofitted with a positive control, at least one of which is shown (in the test) to have been silently blind before.
- [ ] ≥1 negative control landed for a parse/decode path — the wrong-but-plausible interpretation run on the same bytes, asserting the structural checks fire.
- [ ] A scan of scorecard/probe output for **fail-open boolean headlines** (a band so wide it admits nearly everything): each found instance either gains a magnitude column or records why the boolean is sufficient.
- [ ] Tautological agreement detection: where two "independent" channels resolve to the same constant, the output labels it rather than counting it as corroboration.

## Non-goals

- Porting any of the four tools. Their subject matter (camera intrinsics, log rates, pixel registration) has no fak analogue; only the epistemology does.

records.title: feat(ci): a structural checker for .github/workflows with one comment-aware line source and needs-edge resolution
records.body:
## Source

`tb/tensor-build-main/tools/ciyaml/` — `structural.go`, `pipeline_test.go`, `sameindent_test.go` (their P5-12 / #76). 282 LOC of tool, 694 of test.

## What it does there

A small, **dependency-free** structural checker for CI pipeline YAML. Their module pins zero dependencies and no YAML package is vendored anywhere, so this is deliberately **not** a general YAML parser: it enforces the specific invariants that catch the overwhelming majority of hand-edit breakage — tab indentation, missing colon-space, unbalanced quotes and brackets — plus two that matter more than generic parseability for a DAG-shaped CI definition: **every step `key:` is unique**, and **every `depends_on` reference resolves to a real key**.

Two structural lessons, both from real drift in that tree:

**1. The file list went stale, invisibly.** The check used to name its inputs as a literal. `.github/workflows/` grew two new workflows while the literal still named one, so **two of the three workflows in the repo were checked by nothing.** The fix: **walk the directory**, never enumerate.

**2. "Comment- and block-scalar-aware" was a claim about all four scanners, and for a while it was true of only one.** The key-uniqueness and DAG-edge scanners read every raw line, so a `command: |` body — a multi-line shell script — could declare a step key or a DAG edge, and a trailing `# comment` on a real `key:` line could erase one. The fix is `eachStructuralLine`: **a single line source that all four scanners consume**, which is what makes the sentence in the doc true rather than merely intended.

They also shell out to `actionlint` when it is on PATH — best-effort, skips cleanly, never a hard dependency of `go test ./...`.

## The generalizable kernel

- **Walk, never enumerate.** A checker with a hard-coded input list silently stops covering whatever is added next, and the gap is invisible from the green result.
- **One line source, many scanners.** If several scanners need the same "which lines are real content?" predicate, sharing it is the only way the claim stays true for all of them. Duplicated tokenisation drifts one scanner at a time.
- **A DAG-shaped config deserves DAG checks** (unique node ids, every edge resolves) more than it deserves generic schema validation.
- An external linter can be **best-effort on PATH** without becoming a dependency.

## Why fak needs it

- `internal/workflowlint` is *not* this — it lints ultracode **Workflow scripts** for fak-nativeness (self-index, memory, shared-path leasing), which is a different artefact entirely. There is no structural checker for `.github/workflows/*.yml` in fak.
- fak's CI is large and load-bearing: `ci.yml`'s masked gate stack halts at the first failing step of ~48, and `ci-fast.yml` is the release green-window gate. A malformed or mis-wired workflow is expensive to discover from a run.
- The DAG check has a direct fak analogue — GitHub Actions `needs:` between jobs. A `needs:` naming a job that no longer exists is a class of breakage that only surfaces on push.
- **Push-lane relevance**: fak already has a recurring, expensive failure where a `.github/workflows/` change is refused **server-side** for a missing `workflow` OAuth scope while `--dry-run` exits 0 and the pre-push check says `ok:true`. A local structural + reference check on workflow files is the natural place to also assert "this push touches workflow files, so check your token scopes first" — turning a ~30-minute rediscovery into a line of output.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] `internal/<name>`: a stdlib-only structural checker over `.github/workflows/**` that **walks** the directory rather than naming files; a test asserts the walk finds every workflow currently in the tree.
- [ ] A **single line source** (the `eachStructuralLine` shape) consumed by every scanner, so comment-awareness and block-scalar-awareness are properties of one function, not four. A test proves a `run: |` body cannot declare a job id or a `needs:` edge, and that a trailing comment cannot erase a real one.
- [ ] Structural checks: tab indentation, missing colon-space, unbalanced quotes/brackets, inconsistent sibling indent.
- [ ] DAG checks: **job ids are unique**, and every `needs:` reference resolves to a job id in the same workflow.
- [ ] `actionlint` invoked best-effort when on PATH, skipped cleanly otherwise; never a hard dependency of `go test ./...`.
- [ ] Zero new module dependencies — fak's entire external set is two `golang.org/x` modules and must stay that way.
- [ ] Wired as a pre-push/CI gate on the workflow path lane, and it **also** emits the token-scope warning when the push range touches `.github/workflows/` (cross-reference the `workflow`-scope push failure).
- [ ] Run at a named SHA over fak's current workflows with findings published, seeded into a ratchet if non-zero.

## Non-goals

- Writing a general YAML parser or a schema validator. `actionlint` does schema; this does structure and references.

records.title: feat(tools): a render-determinism lock — hash the INPUT, because the generator output is never byte-identical twice
records.body:
## Source

`tb/tensor-build-main/tools/docpack/lock.go`.

## What it does there

A render lock for generated PDFs. The measurement that forced it:

> Chrome does not print a byte-identical PDF twice. Two runs over one unchanged document produced **three different files at three different sizes** (653153, 663847, 663903 bytes) — the renderer stamps a wall-clock creation date and its object numbering drifts. So **"did the output change?" cannot be asked of the output.**

Without an answer to that question, every run rewrites every PDF: *"~9 MB of binary diff that says nothing, on a repo where a fleet shares one checkout."*

The fix: hash the **input** — the exact HTML that produced each PDF — and store `{pdf → sha256(html)}`. A run recomputes the input hash; unchanged input means skip the write entirely.

The lock file's **location** carries its own lesson. It went under `docs/` first, which was wrong twice: `docs/` holds documents and this is build state; and mechanically, every lane in their path-lease config names a kind directory, so a loose file there matched no lane and **fell through to the exclusive global catch-all, which serializes the entire fleet on one lock.** It lives beside the tool instead.

And it is **committed**, wherever it lives, because its whole job is to answer a question about the committed artefacts — "were these built from the documents currently in the tree?" — which a gitignored file could not answer for anyone but the person who last ran it.

## The generalizable kernel

Three rules for any nondeterministic generator in a shared checkout:

1. **When the output is not reproducible byte-for-byte, key the freshness check on a hash of the INPUT.** Comparing outputs is not merely inefficient, it is undefined.
2. **Build state is not a document.** Where you put a state file determines which path lease it falls under, and a file that matches no lane can serialise the whole fleet on the catch-all.
3. **A freshness record must be committed** if the question it answers is about committed artefacts. A gitignored lock answers only for the last person who ran the tool.

## Why fak needs it

- The churn cost is real here: a shared checkout with ~20–30 concurrent sessions, where `fak commit` holds a fleet-wide lock for 60–126s and `fak sweep`/`git add -A`-shaped paths can pick up files nobody meant to commit. A generator that rewrites unchanged bytes on every run manufactures exactly the dirty-file noise that makes peer WIP classification hard.
- fak has several generated-artefact gates already — `CONCEPT_FRESHNESS`, `INDEX_SYNC`, the `llms-full` mirror. The lore records the pathology: *the llms-full mirror treadmill — regen once, don't chase*; and *concept-freshness regen is a no-op yet the gate still refuses*. Both are "the freshness question was asked of the wrong artefact".
- Rule 2 maps directly onto fak's `dos.toml` path lanes and the `global` catch-all: a new state file in the wrong directory is a fleet-wide serialisation hazard, and that hazard is currently learned by hitting it.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] `internal/<name>`: a generic `{artifact path → sha256(canonical input)}` lock with load/save/check, pure and unit-testable, usable by any fak generator.
- [ ] Skip semantics: unchanged input hash ⇒ **no write at all** (not a write of identical bytes), proven by a test asserting the file mtime and content are untouched.
- [ ] Applied to ≥1 real fak generator whose output is not byte-reproducible, or — if fak has none today — applied to the generators whose *inputs* are cheap to hash and whose regen currently rewrites unconditionally (`llms-full` mirror, concept artefacts), with the before/after diff-bytes-per-run measured and published.
- [ ] Lock file placement is chosen against the **path-lane map** and the choice is justified in the package doc; a test asserts the chosen path matches a named lane and not the `global` catch-all.
- [ ] The lock is **committed**, and a gate can answer "were these artefacts built from the tree as it stands?" for any checkout, not just the author's.
- [ ] A test that proves the naive check is wrong for at least one real generator: same input, two runs, non-identical output bytes.

## Non-goals

- Making any renderer deterministic. This ticket assumes it is not and routes around it.

records.title: feat(docs): zero-dep Markdown to print-ready HTML/PDF behind a managed verb
records.body:
## Source

`tb/tensor-build-main/tools/deckpdf/` (751 LOC + 627 test) and `tools/mdpdf/` (1164 + 853) — the same capability at two maturities, plus `tools/docpack/` as the driver.

## What they do there

Render Markdown to a print-ready HTML page and then to PDF via headless Chrome, inlining each figure. `deckpdf` is slide-shaped; `mdpdf` generalises it with a `Layout` abstraction and a document/deck split.

Four design decisions are the transferable part:

**1. Zero dependencies, hand-rolled subset.** *"No Python, no Node, no pandoc. The Markdown subset below is hand-rolled against exactly the constructs the deck uses, and the module stays dependency-free."*

**2. The vendor binary is wrapped, never handed to a human.** *"The operator runs one command and gets a PDF. The headless-Chrome invocation is wrapped here, exactly the way `tb build` wraps trtexec — a vendor binary is the reality we wrap from Go, never a command handed to a human."*

**3. Layout detection: the author's marker wins, then a corpus rule — never content inference.** From `DetectLayout`: *"Guessing from the content (say, 'mostly short sections') was tried on paper and rejected — an explainer with terse sections would silently become a 40-page deck, and the failure looks like a rendering bug rather than a classification one."*

**4. It lives in `tools/`, not behind a product verb**, with the boundary argued explicitly: rendering a document is not an engine capability.

## The generalizable kernel

- A **hand-rolled subset parser is the correct answer** when the corpus is yours and the dependency budget is zero. The subset is bounded by the constructs actually used, and a test enumerates them.
- **Wrap the vendor binary.** A README step that says "now run Chrome with these flags" is an unmanaged surface; the same call from Go is testable, discoverable and can fail with a sentence.
- **Never infer a document's class from its content.** An explicit marker, then a corpus-wide default. Misclassification that presents as a rendering bug is the expensive kind.

## Why fak needs it

- fak's external dependency set is **two `golang.org/x` modules pinned by a 4-line go.sum**, and the repo is document-heavy (`docs/`, `INDEX.md`, `llms.txt`, benchmark galleries, scorecards, release notes). Producing a shareable artefact from any of it currently has no in-repo path.
- There is demand in the tree already: the workspace carries `dos-concept-video` and `ui-walkthrough-video` siblings, `internal/marketing`, `internal/operatorbrief`, `internal/programreport`, `internal/milestonereport`, `internal/executive-reporting`-shaped surfaces, and #2694 ("capture a shareable visual of the preflight panel"). Every one of those wants "turn this Markdown into something you can send someone".
- Decision 3 is a fak-relevant hazard independently: fak has many document *kinds* (notes, audits, scorecards, explainers) discriminated today by directory convention.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] `internal/<name>`: Markdown → print-ready HTML with a **hand-rolled, bounded** subset parser; the supported construct list is enumerated in the package doc and each construct has a test.
- [ ] **Zero new module dependencies.** A test or gate asserts `go.mod`'s require set is unchanged.
- [ ] Any construct outside the subset is a **loud error naming the construct and the line**, never silent passthrough — an unsupported construct rendering as literal text is the failure that reads as a typo.
- [ ] Headless-Chrome (or equivalent) invocation wrapped behind a fak verb with a timeout, a clear "binary not found" message naming what to install, and a `--html-only` mode that needs no browser at all — so the parser is testable and useful in CI without the vendor binary.
- [ ] **Layout/kind selection**: explicit marker first, then a corpus default keyed on path. Content-based inference is explicitly rejected in the package doc with the reason.
- [ ] `-print` / `--stdout` mode that touches nothing on disk.
- [ ] Integrates with the sibling **render-determinism lock** ticket, so a PDF is not rewritten when its input HTML is unchanged.
- [ ] One real fak document rendered end to end and attached to the ticket as proof.

## Non-goals

- Full CommonMark. The subset is deliberately bounded by the corpus.
- A slide *authoring* experience.

records.title: build(tools): nested-module dependency quarantine — keep the root at two deps while a heavy tool gets its own go.mod
records.body:
## Source

`tb/tensor-build-main/tools/videogen/main.go` (2896 LOC across 49 files, of which the root runner is small).

## What it does there

The tree's explainer-video renderer needs `golang.org/x/image` for its bitmap and antialiased font paths. The root module deliberately has **zero external dependencies**. Rather than take the dependency at the root or drop the capability, the heavy code lives in a **nested module** (`tools/videogen/terminal`) with its own `go.mod`, and a *small stdlib-only runner* at `tools/videogen` preserves the repo-root `go run ./tools/videogen ...` interface and **hides the module boundary from the caller**.

## The generalizable kernel

Dependency budgets are usually enforced by refusal — "we don't take deps, so we don't build that." The nested-module pattern is the third option: **quarantine the dependency behind a module boundary and a stdlib-only façade**, so the root module's `go.mod`, `go.sum`, supply-chain surface and `go install` story are unchanged, and the caller's interface is identical.

The properties that make it work, all of which need asserting or they rot:

- The root's require set and `go.sum` are **provably** unchanged — the whole point is defeated silently if a later edit pulls the dep up.
- `go build ./...` / `go test ./...` from the root **do not traverse** the nested module, so the nested code needs its own CI invocation or it is untested and nobody notices.
- The façade is stdlib-only, and that is checkable.
- The boundary is invisible at the call site.

## Why fak needs it

- fak's dependency posture is explicit and strict, and it is a stated product property: *"The entire external dependency set is two `golang.org/x` extended-standard-library modules … pinned by a 4-line go.sum"*, and *"The Go module is the repository root, so it installs directly: `go install github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/cmd/fak@latest`."* Both are load-bearing claims, and both are exactly what a nested module protects.
- fak keeps hitting the wall from the other side: a large `tools/` Python surface exists **because** the Go root cannot take dependencies, and that surface has its own gate (`internal/pythongate`) and its own recurring pain — CI runs `tools/*_test.py` without pytest, a new `tools/*_test.py` cannot land, the py-debt KPI fights the pythongate ratchet. A sanctioned Go-with-quarantined-deps lane is the missing third option between "stdlib only" and "write it in Python".
- Concrete near-term consumers: the sibling Markdown→PDF ticket (if a rendering dep ever proves unavoidable), image/chart generation for scorecards and `internal/marketing`, and the `dos-concept-video` / `ui-walkthrough-video` work already living outside the repo.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] A documented, sanctioned pattern for a nested `tools/<name>/<dep-heavy>/go.mod` with a stdlib-only root runner, written up in `AGENTS.md` / `CONTRIBUTING.md` alongside the existing dependency rule — so the next contributor finds the third option instead of reaching for Python.
- [ ] A **gate asserting the root `go.mod` require set and `go.sum` are unchanged** (or changed only with an explicit, reviewed allowlist bump) — the claim in the module doc becomes checkable rather than aspirational.
- [ ] A **gate asserting every façade runner is stdlib-only** (no non-stdlib imports in the root-side package), so the quarantine cannot leak by accident.
- [ ] A **gate asserting every nested module is actually built and tested** by CI — the root `./...` does not reach it, and an untested nested module is the predictable failure. Enumerate nested `go.mod` files by walk, not by list.
- [ ] `go install github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/cmd/fak@latest` is verified working after the pattern lands (it must be unaffected), with the check in the release gate.
- [ ] The pattern is exercised by ≥1 real nested module, or — if nothing needs it yet — landed as gates plus documentation only, with the ticket explicitly recording that no nested module exists yet so the gates are vacuously green (and pinned per the sibling `unwiredscore` fires-on-success ticket).

## Non-goals

- Relaxing the root dependency budget.
- Migrating existing `tools/*.py` in this ticket. This makes the Go alternative available; migrations are separate.

records.title: feat(ingest): two-signal admission with a first-class ABSTAIN — a retrieval query is a weak label, not a label
records.body:
## Source

`tb/tensor-build-main/tools/classmint/main.go` (their NC-02 / #992).

## What it does there

Acquires public exemplar imagery for a new class from the class **name alone**, so minting a new class costs no human labeling and no per-class code. The subject matter (a computer-vision taxonomy, Wikimedia Commons retrieval) has no fak analogue. Two properties do.

**1. Provenance is the product, not a side effect.** *"Every downloaded file is recorded with the query that retrieved it and the page that carries its licence, so a reviewer can re-derive the exemplar set rather than take it on faith."* Also: a real contact string in the User-Agent, because the upstream API rejects anonymous bulk clients — the identification is policy, not politeness.

**2. Retrieval is a WEAK signal, and one weak signal is not a label.** *"The retrieval query is ALSO the first of two class signals: an image returned for 'sailing yacht' is weak evidence that it depicts one. The mint stage must require a second, independent signal and **abstain when they disagree**. Retrieval alone is not a label."*

The API base is a `var`, not a `const`, for exactly one reason: the tests point it at a local test server, because a test that reached the real service would be a flake and a policy violation.

## The generalizable kernel

- **Ingestion must record the query, not just the result.** An artefact you cannot re-derive is an artefact you must take on faith, and a corpus of those is unauditable.
- **Two independent signals, or ABSTAIN.** A single retrieval/heuristic hit is evidence, not a label. Disagreement between two signals is a *third outcome* and must be representable — collapsing it into either answer is how a corpus silently acquires wrong labels at scale.
- **Every network base URL is a `var`**, so the test suite never reaches the real service.

## Why fak needs it

- fak ingests and classifies constantly, and mostly from one signal: `internal/benchingest`, `internal/benchcatalog`, `internal/issuestriage`, `internal/issuededup`, `internal/issuecatalog`, `internal/conceptcatalog`, `internal/ideascout`, `internal/harvest`, `internal/sotacoverage`, `internal/wiki`. Each turns a retrieval or a heuristic into a class.
- The abstain discipline already has partial homes and no shared rule: `dos_refuse_reasons` / `dos_check_reason` give a closed refusal vocabulary; the commit-audit path already **ABSTAINs** on a vague subject rather than guessing. **#3949** (evidence-tiered VERIFIED gate + machine-witnessed reproducibility floor) and **#3947** (committed decision-ledger + skip-audit closure for `idea_scout`) are both asking for this from different directions.
- The failure this prevents is one fak has hit: a triage agent's `STILL_OPEN` is a *snapshot*, not a fact, and acting on it without re-verifying against HEAD cost real worker-hours twice. That is single-signal classification with no abstain state.
- Provenance-on-ingest is also the honest answer to fak's citation problem — citation lanes cannot verify links, so the in-repo evidence rule has to be recorded at ingest time or not at all.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] A shared **provenance record** for any ingested item: `{query or rule that produced it, source identity/URL, licence or terms where applicable, retrieved-at, tool version}`, stored with the item, sufficient to re-derive it.
- [ ] A shared **two-signal admission** helper: `{signal_a, signal_b} → ADMIT | REJECT | ABSTAIN`, where disagreement is `ABSTAIN` and `ABSTAIN` is a **first-class stored outcome**, not a drop. Pure and unit-testable.
- [ ] The abstain vocabulary is closed and reuses the existing refusal-reason vocabulary rather than inventing free text.
- [ ] Applied to ≥1 real fak ingest path (`benchingest`, `issuestriage` or `ideascout`), with a measured before/after: how many items were admitted on one signal, and how many of those become `ABSTAIN`.
- [ ] An audit query answering "which admitted items rest on a single signal?" — so existing single-signal admissions are visible rather than indistinguishable from corroborated ones.
- [ ] **Every network base URL in the touched paths is a `var`**, and a test asserts no test in the package reaches a real external host.
- [ ] Cross-linked to #3949 and #3947 as the shared substrate both need.

## Non-goals

- Porting image acquisition or anything Commons-specific.
- Re-adjudicating already-admitted corpus items in this ticket; the audit query makes them visible, backfill is separate.

records.title: epic(borrow): generalize the tb tensor-build tools folder into fak — 18 tools surveyed, 18 tickets
records.body:
Survey of every tool under `tb/tensor-build-main/tools/` (18 tools, ~25k LOC + ~26k test LOC), asking one question per tool: **what here is a general mechanism rather than a domain artefact, and does fak already have it?**

The tb repo is a TensorRT engine-lifecycle repo with a very different subject matter, but it runs the same *topology* fak does — one shared checkout, ~20–30 concurrent agent sessions, a trunk-only commit policy, path leases, and a content pre-commit gate. That means its scar tissue transfers even where its code does not. Most of what follows is a measured failure in that tree that fak either has, or is one commit away from having.

## Filed

| # | Tool | The transferable kernel |
|---|---|---|
| #5931 | `precommit` | **Deny only what THIS commit introduces.** Judge `HEAD ⊕ staged`, not the shared dirty disk. Their version of this bug denied every doc-touching commit fleet-wide for hours, citing a path in nobody's diff. fak's `hooks/filesource.go` reads the working tree today; #5128 is already this class. |
| #5932 | `trunkverdict` | A **commit-keyed** trunk-green record. Their `main` was red for 262 commits over ~28h with no gate noticing. fak has `trunkbuildprobe` (why it is red) and no ledger (whether it is). Notify, don't refuse. |
| #5933 | `lanescan` | **An empty lease census must be distinguishable from "I read the wrong journal."** A positional walk found shadow state roots *inside* the repo; three cwds returned byte-identical "every lane is free" while 22 leases were held. Fails open into the referee. |
| #5934 | `verbsdoc` | Generate the verb surface **from source, never from `--help`**, with a **REFUSES** column and a precondition enum whose **zero value is UNVERIFIED** and whose gap count is printed on the page. |
| #5935 | `enumlint` | **Closed-enum exhaustiveness** over the Go AST. fak's dominant modelling idiom, hand-checked in exactly one package (`wipref`'s `TestClassifyVocabulary`). Shares a discovery pass with #5649. |
| #5936 | `testq` | The **ratchet contract**: keys stable under editing, counts not line numbers, hard-fail on an unparseable baseline row, and only ever claim "not growing". fak runs one of these (`pythongate`) and has no Go equivalent. |
| #5937 | `indexgraph` | Reachability under **named** resolver semantics, each with its own denominator, read from **HEAD not the worktree**. Their audit's headline was unreproducible the day it published. |
| #5938 | `doclint` (coverage family) | **Publish the gate's denominator.** A checker that cannot enumerate its own blind spots reads as complete coverage. fak has already been burned by an ignore pattern silently swallowing source. |
| #5939 | `doclint` (`breath`) | Gate the **countable half** of a prose contract and refuse the judgement half in writing — an entailment check scores the best plain-language writing as the least faithful. Feeds #3229 / #3535. |
| #5940 | `holdcensus` | **DIVERGED is a third state.** "Landed vs unlanded" recommends a checkout that reverts newer work; and an orphan ref's empty stdout is not a measurement. fak's `wipref` census is per-ref, not per-payload-file. |
| #5941 | `memoryindex` | The agent-memory index is a **derived artefact with no gate**, maintained by the agent that reads it. Check-first reconciler in Go, under the green gate. Completeness precondition for #2618 / #2619. |
| #5942 | `precommit/binroster` | A **fires-on-success pin**: a doc claiming NOT WIRED fails the day it becomes false, and the tie is bidirectional so the pin cannot be cleared while the stale prose survives. Gives `unwiredscore` teeth. |
| #5943 | `logcal` ×3 + `r13optical` | **Probe controls.** Positive control or the probe is blind; two channels or it is not corroboration; no fail-open boolean as the headline; a search that always returns an argmin must report how much it explains. |
| #5944 | `ciyaml` | **Walk, never enumerate** the input set, and give every scanner **one** comment-and-block-scalar-aware line source. Plus DAG checks (`needs:` resolution) that schema validation does not do. `workflowlint` is a different artefact. |
| #5945 | `docpack` | **Hash the input, not the output**, when the generator is not byte-reproducible. Also: build state is not a document, and its directory decides which path lease it falls under. |
| #5946 | `deckpdf` + `mdpdf` | Zero-dep Markdown → print-ready output; wrap the vendor binary rather than handing a human a command; **never infer a document's class from its content**. |
| #5947 | `videogen` | **Nested-module dependency quarantine** — the third option between "stdlib only" and "write it in Python". fak's two-dep `go.mod` and direct `go install` are stated product claims; make them checkable. |
| #5948 | `classmint` | **Two signals or ABSTAIN**, with abstain as a stored outcome, and provenance recorded at ingest so an artefact can be re-derived rather than taken on faith. Substrate for #3949 / #3947. |

## Folded rather than filed separately

- **`r13optical`** — its subject (inter-frame rotation from pixels) has no fak analogue. Its transferable content is the two-controls-per-measurement discipline, which is the same rule `logcal` teaches, so both are in #5943 rather than duplicated.
- **`deckpdf` and `mdpdf`** are the same capability at two maturities and are one ticket (#5946); `docpack` is split out (#5945) because the determinism lock is independently useful to generators that have nothing to do with documents.

## Nothing pulled

No tool was surveyed and skipped entirely — but three (`classmint`, `logcal`, `r13optical`) contributed **only** an epistemic rule, not code. Their tickets say so, and their non-goals sections explicitly refuse the port.

## Adjacent existing work

#5128 (a peer's staged file wedging a tree-wide gate) is a single instance of #5931's seam. #5649 (closed-vocabulary drift) shares a discovery pass with #5935. #2618 / #2619 (the wikilink graph) sit on top of #5941. #3949 / #3947 want #5948's substrate. #3229 / #3535 are #5939's consumer.

records.title: epic(rubricrefine-study): mine RubricRefine (arXiv 2605.09730, pre-execution contract verification) for fak — witnessed borrows
records.body:
## What this is

A `/study-repo` pass over **RubricRefine** (arXiv:2605.09730v3, cs.LG, 15 May 2026 — *"Improving Tool-Use Agent Reliability with Training-Free Pre-Execution Refinement"*), read through its released prompt artifact **`anonymousrubricauthor/RubricRefinePrompts`**, pinned at `2c082addf5197a078827727e9412975e82ea7f10` (`2c082ad`), cloned read-only to scratch.

The paper's thesis: the dominant failures in code-mode tool use are **inter-tool contract violations** — wrong output shape, incorrect tool routing, broken argument provenance — that *run to completion without raising an error*, which makes runtime feedback insufficient. Their answer is a training-free **pre-execution** layer: generate a task- and registry-conditioned rubric, score the candidate against it **without executing**, and repair before dispatch.

## License gate

The checkout carries **no LICENSE file** → treat as **all-rights-reserved**. Every candidate is therefore **`inspire`-ONLY**: clean-room Go reimplementation from the described *pattern*, source-cited, **no bytes vendored, no prompt text copied**.

## What was read

All 6 files at the pin (the repo is prompts-only; there is no implementation code released): `README.md`, `prompt_1_rubric_design_system.txt`, `prompt_2_rubric_generation.txt`, `prompt_3_rubric_scoring_system.txt`, `prompt_4_evaluation.txt`, `prompt_5_generator_system.txt`. Completeness critic: no subdirectories, no unopened files, nothing material left unread on the source side.

Their three phases (`README.md:18-26`): **A** rubric generation (conditioned on `{instructions}` + `{tool_docs}`), **B** iterative scoring (per-item PASS/FAIL + a 1–10 scalar, no execution), **C** iterative repair, looping until the score hits the early-stop threshold of 10.

## Their user world (reconstructed, falsifiable)

They optimize for a **benchmark researcher chasing a number on M3ToolEval**, not an ops user maintaining a rule corpus. Evidence: `prompt_1:65` scopes output checks to "the benchmark-required contract"; `prompt_3:8` reasons about "the benchmark interaction"; `README.md:4` says the prompts were "released in response to reviewer requests for reproducibility" — released for *review*, not for reuse. This matters for what fak should take: the **architecture** is borrowable, the **rule corpus is not** (see the worldview finding below).

## Witness summary (on-axis, against fak's code)

| Candidate (source anchor @2c082ad) | Axis | fak seam witnessed | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Scalar score welded to its own itemization — "evaluate all items first, then score"; all-PASS + empty `critical_failures` ⇒ score **exactly** 10 (`prompt_3:46-49`); forced-FAIL coupling (`prompt_4:40-42`) | reference-free internal consistency between a model's scalar and its own item list | `internal/trajctl/judgescorer.go:180` — default fold is `clamp01(verdict.Progress)`, the model's free scalar; per-criterion findings (`:160-173`) are evidence refs only and never constrain it | **PARTIAL — filed** |
| Checks derived from the declared tool registry — rubric conditioned on `{tool_docs}` (`prompt_2:7-9`); "verify keyword names against those signatures literally and fail invented keyword names" (`prompt_4:46`) | whether the pre-dispatch arg floor is *derived from the tool's declared schema* vs hand-written per rule | `internal/adjudicator/decide.go:197-216` — `ArgPredicate` is operator-authored manifest text (Tool/Arg/Glob/Re/N); no `inputSchema` read anywhere in the package | **PARTIAL — filed** |
| Verifier forbidden from failing on unverifiability (`prompt_4:64-65`, `prompt_3:43-44`) | does "couldn't check it" become a refusal? | `internal/witness/settle.go:57` — "unverifiable => ABSTAIN"; `:203` "Only unverifiable abstains" | **PRESENT — fak's is a typed state in the settle machine, stronger than a prompt instruction** |
| Budget-matched arms (equal pre-execution reasoning opportunities) | arm comparability in A/B | `internal/ablate/ablate.go:348` *refuses* to compare arms with different workload hashes; `:287,319` declared baseline + `TokenDelta` | **PRESENT — structurally enforced, vs their prose protocol** |
| Early-stop on score==10 (`README.md:24`) | loop-termination predicate | `internal/attemptbudget/attemptbudget.go:191-235` — terminates on typed failure classes (`DISTINCT_ERRORS`, `TRANSIENT_EXHAUSTED`) | **PRESENT — typed classes beat a scalar threshold** |
| Per-criterion attribution | which criteria moved the score | `internal/trajctl/rubric.go:56-59` + `judgescorer.go:160-173` (#2544) | **PRESENT** |
| Conjunctive hard-AND rubric | pass/fail objectives without partial credit | `internal/trajctl/rubric.go:67-70` (#3926) | **PRESENT** |

Note on prior art: **#3922** (apexagents-study) dismissed the rubric-judge neighborhood as PRESENT. That was correct at the *capability* level and remains so — but the score↔itemization **binding** axis was not witnessed there, and it is open on the default soft fold. That is the filed borrow.

## Worldview finding (recorded, not filed — fak is ahead)

Their five prompt files (356 lines total) carry substantial **rule-corpus accretion with no dedup gate**: `prompt_3:38` and `:39` are near-verbatim duplicates, as are `prompt_1:49`/`:50`, `prompt_2:27`/`:28`, and `prompt_5:11`/`:12`; the `min`/`max`/`sum` variadic-tool rule family is restated across all five files. This is the visible residue of iterative prompt-patching against benchmark failures — consistent with the researcher user-world above. fak already has the decay/dedup machinery this implies a need for (`skill-overlap`, `clean-skill`, `memory-compact`, the `kpi_duplication` card), so there is no borrow here — it is recorded as the observation it is, and as the reason **not** to port their rule text.

## Not witnessed this pass (parked honestly)

- **Per-check-category value attribution** (their rubric-category ablation, which measures *which* check categories carry the win). fak's nearest surface, `dos helped`, lives in the DOS binary rather than this tree, so no on-axis witness was possible here. Not dismissed — unwitnessed.
- **Generator rejecting bad verifier advice** (`prompt_5:38`: ignore a repair instruction that would produce a syntax-invalid call). No crisp mis-behaving fak seam located; held per the "no file:line seam, no issue" rule.

## Honest limits

- The clone is `--depth 1` and the repo has a **single squashed commit** ("Add files via upload"), so there is no history to read — the accretion evidence above is *internal* (near-duplicate rules within files), not from a log.
- No implementation code was ever released, only prompts; every claim here is anchored in prompt text or the paper abstract, never in an unreleased implementation.

## Filed

- **This epic** — the study umbrella.
- Children below.

Provenance: `docs/notes/CONCEPT-STUDY-RUBRICREFINE-2026-08-08.md`.

records.title: feat(trajctl): bind a judge verdict's scalar to its own per-criterion findings (soft fold has no consistency check)
records.body:
Borrow from the **RubricRefine** study (epic filed alongside; `docs/notes/CONCEPT-STUDY-RUBRICREFINE-2026-08-08.md`).

## The gap

`internal/trajctl/judgescorer.go:180` folds a judge verdict into its W1 row as:

```go
value := clamp01(verdict.Progress)
```

In the **default** (non-conjunctive) path that is the model's **free scalar**, clamped and nothing else. The per-criterion findings are marshalled into evidence refs immediately above (`:160-173`, per-criterion attribution from #2544) but they **never constrain `value`**.

So a judge call can return `Progress: 1.0` while its `Criteria` list carries findings at `Progress: 0.0`, and fak records `Value: 1.0` with the contradicting findings sitting right beside it in the same evidence bundle. Nothing in the fold notices. The only existing binding is the **opt-in** conjunctive mode (`rubric.go:67-70`, #3926), which is all-or-nothing and applies only to pass/fail objectives — the soft-progress default, which is what most objectives use, has no consistency check at all.

## The borrow (axis)

**Reference-free internal consistency between a model-emitted scalar and the model's own itemization.**

RubricRefine welds the two in its scoring prompt (`prompt_3_rubric_scoring_system.txt:46-49` @`2c082ad`):

- "Evaluate all rubric items first, then assign the final score after reviewing the full PASS/FAIL results."
- "Score must be monotonic with correctness: more PASS items and fewer FAIL items should produce a higher score."
- "If all required rubric items are PASS and `critical_failures` is empty, the score must be exactly 10."

and couples it in the other direction in `prompt_4_evaluation.txt:40-42` @`2c082ad`: for each named violation class, *at least one specific category item must be FAIL* **and** the score must be < 10.

The key property is that this needs **no ground truth**. It is not calibration-against-a-reference — fak already has that in `internal/quality/calibration.go`, which requires a `ref.Text` carrying ground-truth support flags. This constrains the scalar against the *same call's own* item list, which is available for free on every judge verdict fak already collects.

## Why they built it that way

Their repair loop early-stops on `score == 10` with **no ground truth at inference time** (`README.md:24` @`2c082ad`). The scalar is the loop's termination signal, so an uncoupled score would let the loop stop on a hallucinated 10. They had to make the number mean something. fak's judge rows feed objective-progress tracking rather than a repair loop, so the pressure was lower — but an inflated `Value` is still a false progress signal in the ledger.

fak already knows this failure class exists in a neighbouring lane: `tools/check_commit_msg.py:79` names "the preview/mutation grade divergence of #3912", where an artifact scored 100/A that should not have.

## First checkable step

A pure consistency predicate over `JudgeVerdict` — same shape as the existing `conjunctiveValue` helper — asserting the scalar does not contradict the criteria, e.g.:

- `verdict.Progress` at or near 1.0 while any criterion finding is below the pass threshold ⇒ inconsistent;
- monotonicity: the scalar must not exceed what the per-criterion findings support.

On violation, fail closed the way the rest of `Score` already does (`:129-150` return **no row** on a closed objective, nil client, over-cap spend, or marshal error) rather than crediting the unsupported value — and attach an evidence ref naming the contradiction, mirroring the `rubric-conjunctive` ref at `:184-193`.

Scoped to the existing fold; extends the #2544/#3926 rung, no new subsystem.

## License

Source is **all-rights-reserved** (no LICENSE file at the pin) ⇒ **`inspire` only**: clean-room Go, no prompt text or bytes copied. The three rules quoted above are cited as evidence of the pattern, not as text to port.

records.title: feat(adjudicator): derive argument-conformance checks from a tool's declared input schema (ArgPredicates are all hand-written)
records.body:
Borrow from the **RubricRefine** study (epic filed alongside; `docs/notes/CONCEPT-STUDY-RUBRICREFINE-2026-08-08.md`).

## The gap

The adjudicator's argument-level floor is `Policy.ArgPredicates` (`internal/adjudicator/decide.go:197-216`). Every field is **operator-authored manifest text**:

```go
type ArgPredicate struct {
    Tool   string         // exact tool name
    Arg    string         // the argument key inspected
    Kind   ArgKind        // matcher selector
    Glob   string         // containment glob
    Re     *regexp.Regexp // deny regex
    N      int            // byte cap
    ...
}
```

These are genuinely load-bearing — they turn the floor "from *which tool* into *which tool with which arguments*" (`decide.go:60`) and they are RESTRICT-ONLY and evaluated before the affirmative allow, so an allow-listed tool with a malicious argument is refused **at the floor**.

But every rule has to be **written by hand, per tool, per arg key**. A grep for `inputSchema` / `InputSchema` / `toolSchema` across `internal/adjudicator` returns nothing: the tool's own **declared input schema is never consulted**. So a whole class of contract violation is invisible to the floor unless somebody anticipated it in the manifest:

- an argument key that appears in **no** declared parameter of the tool's schema (an invented kwarg),
- a **required** parameter that is absent,
- a value whose **type** contradicts the declared type.

This is precisely the failure family the paper is about — violations that "run to completion without raising errors".

## The borrow (axis)

**Derive the argument-conformance checks from the tool's declared signature, instead of hand-writing one rule per (tool, arg) pair.**

RubricRefine conditions its whole check set on the registry: the rubric-generation prompt is templated on `<available_tools>{tool_docs}</available_tools>` (`prompt_2_rubric_generation.txt:7-9` @`2c082ad`), and scoring is instructed to "verify keyword names against those signatures **literally** and fail invented keyword names" (`prompt_4_evaluation.txt:46` @`2c082ad`), with the generator side told "Each keyword must exactly match a documented parameter name" (`prompt_5_generator_system.txt:32` @`2c082ad`).

Note this is a **deterministic, schema-mechanical** check — not a model judgement. It reads a declared JSON Schema and compares argument keys against it. That distinction matters for where it can live (see below).

## Why they built it that way, and why fak's situation now rhymes

Their registry is **handed to them fresh per task instance**, so hand-written per-arg rules were never an option — deriving from `{tool_docs}` was forced. fak's tool surface was historically stable and operator-curated, which is exactly why hand-written `ArgPredicate` rules were affordable. That premise is weakening: MCP tools arrive from **third-party servers whose schemas fak never wrote**, and nobody hand-writes a manifest rule for each one.

## Scope boundary — do NOT put a model-judged verifier in the floor

fak's decide path is deliberately deterministic, in-process, and non-executing. `Policy.LintWrites` (`decide.go`, the `LintWrites` field comment) already draws this line explicitly: it refuses *unparseable* Go/JSON, but for languages whose only checkers shell out it **DEFERS** — "fail open, never denying over a quality signal the decide path cannot produce."

That is a real, stated tradeoff and it still holds. The borrow here is therefore **only** the schema-mechanical conformance check (a JSON Schema comparison is pure, in-process, no exec — it fits the floor's constraints). RubricRefine's *model-judged* semantic verifier is **DIVERGENT for the adjudicator** and must not be ported into it.

## First checkable step

A schema-conformance rung that, given a tool's declared input schema, refuses a call carrying an argument key absent from that schema — with the existing floor discipline:

- **RESTRICT-ONLY**, like `ArgPredicates`: a conforming call is never *granted* an allow by conformance alone.
- **Fail open when the schema is unavailable or unparseable** — an absent schema must DEFER, never deny, exactly as `LintWrites` defers rather than denying on a signal it cannot produce.
- A generated check that cannot be grounded in a declared schema is **dropped, not enforced**. This is the safety property RubricRefine had to add once its checks became generated: its scorer is told that if a rubric item demands something absent from the documented tools, "do not enforce the invented tool requirement" (`prompt_3_rubric_scoring_system.txt:32` @`2c082ad`). Hand-written rules are reviewed; derived rules are not, so the derivation must defend against itself.

Related but distinct: **#4220** (reach-delta gate) concerns deltas on a *policy change*; this is per-call conformance against a *tool schema*.

records.title: feat(guard): guards should join the fleet bus AND apply steer by default — the Stop-hook seam already injects text at the turn boundary
records.body:
_Parent epic: #5599 — centralized fleet control. Sibling of #5638 (the gateway-scoped applier)._

## The operator case that exposed this

An operator enrolled a new account seat (`fak accounts enroll-current --name aug8-netra`) and then
tried to do the exact thing #5599 opens with — *"tell the fleet `go`, and show me who heard"*:

```
$ fak dev fleet control send --op steer --text "go" --all --wait 5s
fak fleet control send: FLEETBUS_NO_TARGET: selector "all" addresses none of the
  0 live instance(s) in C:\Users\USER\AppData\Local\Fleet\bus
```

Zero targets — while **16 guard gateways were live and answering `/debug/vars` on that same box**
(47 live handles / 30 unique gateways in `fak session ls`, 16 reachable). Falling back to the
single-session path on one of them:

```
$ fak signal steer g660e5fdb --text "go" --addr http://127.0.0.1:62013
fak signal steer: steer not applied (STEER_NO_OWNED_LOOP): this serve process forwards
  proxy turns and owns no agent loop to drain the steer …
```

So the fleet was fully populated and entirely uncommandable, by two independent defaults.

## Root cause — two defaults, both individually correct

**1. A guard-launched gateway never joins the bus.** `--fleet-bus` defaults to `false`
(`cmd/fak/serve.go:241`, *"Off by default (arming a control plane must be stated)"*), and **no
`cmd/fak/guard*.go` file imports `internal/fleetbus` at all** — so a guard gateway does not
announce an Instance record even when a bus directory exists. No announcement ⇒ no roster row ⇒
the denominator #5599 calls load-bearing is 0 ⇒ `FLEETBUS_NO_TARGET`.

**2. Even reachable, it cannot apply a steer.** `Server.ownsSessionLoop()` returns `s.native`
(`internal/gateway/http.go:1179-1181`), and the guard path fronts an external harness
(Claude Code) that owns its own turn loop. `serve_fleetbus.go:152` and `http.go:1290` both refuse
with `STEER_NO_OWNED_LOOP`.

Neither refusal is a bug — both are the anti-phantom discipline #3528 established, and I would not
weaken either. The bug is that **the default posture of the fleet's most common process makes the
control plane structurally unreachable**, so the plane #5600/#5638 built has, in practice, no
members. The refusals are honest about a fleet nobody can steer; they do not make it steerable.

## Why "just pass the flags" is not the answer

`--fleet-bus` is opt-in per process, and guard sessions are launched by dispatch loops, the
relaunch broker, and humans in terminals — there is no single place an operator can add a flag and
have tomorrow's guards inherit it. A control plane whose membership depends on every launcher
remembering a flag has a roster that silently under-reports, which is precisely the unfalsifiable
"everyone acked" #5599 fences out. Membership has to be the default for the plane to mean anything.

## Proposed shape (open to alternatives)

- **`fak guard` announces on the bus by default.** Presence is not a capability grant: an Instance
  record is a read-only *"I exist, here is what I can apply"* announcement. Arming *authority* can
  stay stated; arming *visibility* should not be. Keep an opt-out (`--fleet-bus=false`) for
  isolated/test guards.
- **Declare capability in the Instance record.** A guard that owns no loop should announce
  `steer: unsupported` rather than accept-then-refuse. Then `--all` addresses it, the fold reports
  `refused STEER_NO_OWNED_LOOP` against a real denominator, and the operator sees *"16 instances,
  0 can steer"* — the honest answer — instead of `FLEETBUS_NO_TARGET`, which reads as "no fleet."
- **Give the guard path a real applier for what it CAN do.** Even without an owned loop, a guard
  can act on the ops that matter after an account event: re-read the seat roster, drop a parked
  worker's `STALE_CRED` hold, pause/resume. The motivating case — *"a seat was added, everyone
  parked on exhaustion should now go"* — needs a seat-refresh op far more than it needs `steer`.
- **Optionally, a harness-input seam** so `steer` can reach a wrapped harness that owns its own
  loop. Larger, and probably its own child issue; the three above already close the reported gap.

## Acceptance

- A guard started with no fleet flags appears in `fak dev fleet control instances` within one TTL.
- `fak dev fleet control send --op <seat-refresh> --all` reports N addressed / N acked against
  those guards, with a per-instance outcome.
- `--op steer --all` against loop-less guards reports **refused with the closed reason and a real
  denominator**, never `FLEETBUS_NO_TARGET` and never a false applied.
- An explicit `--fleet-bus=false` guard still announces nothing (the opt-out is honored).
- The 12 workers currently sitting in `fak dev fleet monitor` as `auth-or-rate-blocked`
  ("current blocker: auth/login required", oldest 70h) can be released by one control-point
  command after a seat is enrolled — the #5599 motivating case, end to end.

## Evidence (measured at HEAD, 2026-08-08)

| Claim | Witness |
|---|---|
| Bus roster empty while fleet is live | `fleet control instances` → `0 live`; `fak session ls` → 47 live handles, 16 reachable gateways |
| Guard never announces | no `cmd/fak/guard*.go` imports `internal/fleetbus` |
| Bus membership is opt-in | `cmd/fak/serve.go:241` — `fs.Bool("fleet-bus", false, …)` |
| Steer needs a native loop | `internal/gateway/http.go:1179-1181` (`ownsSessionLoop → s.native`) |
| Refusal is by design | `serve_fleetbus.go:152`, `http.go:1284-1290`, #3528 |
| Fleet is starved on exactly this | `fak dev fleet monitor` → 243 workers, 12 `auth-or-rate-blocked` |

Filed from an operator session that hit this while enrolling a seat.

records.title: fix(accounts): `refresh --force` silently logs out the operator's own live session — warn, print the repair, or hand off
records.body:
## What happened

An operator enrolled the seat they were currently signed in as, then completed the deliberate
token-family divorce that `enroll-current` defers when `--no-divorce` is passed:

```
PS C:\work> fak accounts refresh --name aug8-netra
aug8-netra    backup   snapshotted 2 blob(s) before refresh
aug8-netra    fresh    not due yet (expires 2026-08-09 05:13Z, in 7h30m0s); pass --force to prove it can rotate
summary: 1 seat(s): ok=0 fresh=1 stale=0 hollow=0 skipped=0

PS C:\work> fak accounts refresh --name aug8-netra --force
aug8-netra    ok       rotated onto family a190cbe5 (was 442fd283)
summary: 1 seat(s): ok=1 fresh=0 stale=0 hollow=0 skipped=0
```

The rotation succeeded exactly as designed. It also **killed the operator's own live interactive
session**, which was running out of the source dir (`~/.claude`, no `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`). That dir's
`.credentials.json` went hollow (`accessToken: ""`, `refreshToken: ""`, `expiresAt: 0`) and every
subsequent turn bounced:

```
Login expired · Please run /login
❯ go
Login expired · Please run /login
❯ go
Login expired · Please run /login
❯ /login
  ⎿  Login successful
```

Four dead turns and a manual re-login, mid-task. Recovery worked — post-`/login` both dirs probe
HTTP 200 on `api/oauth/profile` and sit on separate families (`~/.claude` → `f00b3d90`,
`aug8-netra` → `a190cbe5`) — so nothing was lost. But the operator had to discover the cause and
the fix themselves, from a message that names neither.

## This is not the copy-a-login bug — that part worked

`internal/accounts/credfamily.go` documents this precisely: *"an adopt is not really a COPY of a
login, it is a MOVE of one — and the only honest thing a tool can do is perform that move at a
moment the operator chose (and is watching), rather than let it detonate later."* That reasoning is
right, and the divorce did what it promised.

The gap is narrower and entirely on the **source** side: fak knows, at the moment it rotates, that
it is about to invalidate a specific config dir — and it does nothing for the live session sitting
on it. The cost lands at a chosen moment, which is the win; it just lands as an unexplained hard
logout instead of a handled one.

## Three concrete defects

**1. No warning that the source dir is THIS session.** `refresh --force` is happy to rotate a family
whose twin is `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` (or `~/.claude` when unset — i.e. the shell you are typing in).
It knows both sides: `DetectSharedRefreshFamily(src, dir)` already computes the sharing, and
`enroll-current` records the source. A refresh that is about to hollow the caller's own session
should say so before it does it, and require a confirmation or an explicit
`--yes-log-me-out`-style flag. Note the *first* (unforced) run's hint — *"pass `--force` to prove it
can rotate"* — actively invites the destructive path while describing it as a proof.

**2. The invalidated dir is left hollow with no repair.** After the rotation, `~/.claude` held a
hollow credential — the exact shape `CredentialHollow` exists to recognise as *"a seat that was
working and now needs a human /login."* fak detects this state by name and still leaves the operator
to notice it from a harness error message. At minimum, print the recovery command
(`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<src> claude /login`) at the moment of hollowing; the divorce path in
`accounts_add_divorce.go:72` already does exactly this — the standalone `refresh` path does not.

**3. The live session has no graceful reaction to credential rotation.** The harness discovers the
dead credential only by failing a turn, and each retry re-fails identically with no diagnosis. A
session whose credential was rotated out from under it should either (a) re-read
`.credentials.json` and pick up a valid successor, or (b) fail once with a message naming the cause
("this dir's OAuth family was rotated by `fak accounts refresh --name aug8-netra`") and the fix —
rather than N identical `Login expired` bounces.

## Proposed shape

- `fak accounts refresh` resolves whether the seat shares a family with the **caller's own** config
  dir; if so, refuse without an explicit acknowledgement flag, naming the session it will end.
- Whenever a rotation hollows a sibling dir, print what died and the one command that fixes it
  (reuse `divorceAdoptedFamily`'s wording — the divorce path already gets this right).
- Consider a `--handoff` mode: rotate the seat **and** re-point the source dir at a still-valid
  credential (or re-login it) so the operator's session survives the split. This is the outcome the
  operator expected here and the one that makes the whole flow safe to run mid-task.
- Harness side: on a 401 whose local credential is hollow, surface the cause once instead of
  repeating `Login expired`.

## Acceptance

- `fak accounts refresh --name <seat> --force`, where `<seat>` shares a family with the caller's
  config dir, refuses without an explicit acknowledgement and names the session at risk.
- With the acknowledgement, it prints the hollowed dir and its exact recovery command.
- A test covers the source-dir-is-the-caller case (pure fingerprint compare — no network needed;
  `credfamily.go`'s primitives are already unit-testable by design).

## Evidence (2026-08-08)

| Claim | Witness |
|---|---|
| Rotation succeeded | `rotated onto family a190cbe5 (was 442fd283)` |
| Source dir hollowed | `~/.claude/.credentials.json` → `accessToken:""`, `refreshToken:""`, `expiresAt:0` |
| Live session broke | 4× `Login expired · Please run /login`, manual `/login` required |
| Both dirs healthy after re-login | `api/oauth/profile` HTTP 200 for both; families `f00b3d90` / `a190cbe5` |
| fak can already detect the state | `accounts.CredentialHollow`, `accounts.DetectSharedRefreshFamily`, `accounts.RefreshFamilyID` |
| Divorce path already prints recovery; refresh path does not | `cmd/fak/accounts_add_divorce.go:72` |

Related: #5953 (guard fleet-bus default), #2260 (STALE_CRED park), #3580 (recoverable-seat worklist).
Background: `internal/accounts/credfamily.go`.

records.title: refactor(dos): re-partition OPERATOR_GATE — 76 of 91 refusal reasons share one category, so per-category attribution is impossible
records.body:
Borrow from the **RubricRefine** study (epic filed alongside; `docs/notes/CONCEPT-STUDY-RUBRICREFINE-2026-08-08.md`).

## The gap, in one number

`dos refuse-reasons` returns **91 reasons across 4 categories**, and the distribution is:

| category | reasons |
|---|---|
| `OPERATOR_GATE` | **76** |
| `STALE_CLAIM` | 7 |
| `MISROUTE` | 6 |
| `TRUE_DRAIN` | 2 |

**84% of every refusal fak can emit lands in a single category.**

The machinery around it is good and is not the complaint: every one of the 91 carries a `token`, `summary`, and a `fix` (91/91), and 89/91 carry `see_also`. The *taxonomy* is the problem, not the record shape.

## Why one bucket at 84% is a real defect, not cosmetics

`OPERATOR_GATE` is not a coherent class. A sample of its members:

- **lane / lease contention** — `LANE_LEASE_HELD_BY_LIVE_DISPATCH_LOOP`, `COLLISION_RISK`, `LANE_BLOCKED_ON_SOAK_GATED_PHASES`
- **agent pathology** — `DOOM_LOOP`, `CRASH_RESTART_EXHAUSTED`, `HOST_CHURN_BACKOFF`
- **commit hygiene** — `BARE_COMMIT_SWEEP`, `NEVER_AMEND_SHARED`, `OFF_TRUNK`, `MESSAGE_RACE`
- **architecture violation** — `ARCH_LAYER_VIOLATION`, `CORE_SELF_MODIFY`, `FORBIDDEN_CALL_SHAPE`
- **cost / budget ceilings** — `RESUME_COST_EXCEEDED`, `GATE_LATENCY_REGRESSION`
- **known-bad ledger states** — `KNOWN_BAD_ALREADY_CLAIMED`, `KNOWN_BAD_NOT_WITNESSED`, `KNOWN_BAD_EXPIRED_OR_REVOKED`, `BLOCKED_BY_KNOWN_BAD`
- **inventory debt** — `UNTIERED_LEAF`, `REQUIRE_WITNESS`, `BLOCKED_BY_OPEN_PREREQ`

These share nothing except "something stopped you." A category that means *stopped* carries no information beyond `refusal: true`, which is already its own field.

The consequence is measurement, not aesthetics: **you cannot ask which class of refusal earns its keep.** Any per-category rollup — which gates fire most, which are pure friction, which prevent real damage, which to soften — returns "OPERATOR_GATE, 84%" and tells you nothing. The taxonomy cannot support attribution, so the refusal surface cannot be tuned by evidence.

## The borrow (axis)

**A check/refusal taxonomy whose categories are roughly co-equal and independently ablatable, so per-category value attribution is possible.**

RubricRefine partitions every check into 7 co-equal sections with stable label prefixes — Intent (`A`, `B`), Ordering/dataflow (`D1`), Argument/format (`a`, `b`, `z`), Type/shape contract (`S1`), Execution-critical (`E1`), Final-answer (`F1`–`F4`), Tool-choice (`T1`) — declared as the required output format at `prompt_2_rubric_generation.txt:69-104` and mirrored exactly in the scorer's response schema keys at `prompt_4_evaluation.txt:68` (`intent`, `ordering_dataflow`, `argument_format`, `type_shape_contract`, `execution_critical`, `final_answer`, `tool_choice`) @`2c082ad`.
