## Parent

Part of #6042. This is the minimal working spine; every live adapter and policy must depend on this contract rather than coupling layers directly.

## Deliverable

Add a small versioned coordination package and an offline `fak coordinate plan` surface with four neutral objects: `Snapshot` (typed cache/compute/harness/serve observations), `Constraints` (operator/security/budget invariants), `Plan` (ordered typed actions and fallbacks), and `DecisionRecord` (alternatives, reasons, provenance and correlation identity).

## Definition of done

- [ ] `fak coordinate plan --snapshot <testdata case> --json` deterministically emits a schema-versioned plan without network, model, GPU, or daemon.
- [ ] One testdata case spans cache residency, two compute placements, harness fan-out intent, and serve queue pressure; changing each input changes the chosen plan in a table-tested way.
- [ ] Hard constraints and soft preferences are distinct; infeasible plans fail typed and explain why.
- [ ] Rejected alternatives and reason codes are present in JSON and human output.
- [ ] The core package imports no concrete cache, scheduler, harness, provider, or engine package.
- [ ] Unknown schema versions, stale observations, partial snapshots, and deterministic tie-breaking are tested.
- [ ] A captured offline selfcheck is committed as the end-to-end spine witness.

## Integration

Reuse #5969's workflow-plan references, #3266's task/lease identity, and #5629's trace context. Do not create a second scheduler or orchestration contract.

## Parent ref

#6042

## Current state

Cache, compute, harness, and serve each make local decisions, but there is no neutral versioned coordination object or offline planner. Cross-layer work therefore couples packages ad hoc and cannot produce one deterministic decision record.

## Why now

This is the priority/P1 `gen/now` spine for the coordination epic. Later live adapters, canaries, and global policies cannot be built or witnessed honestly until this offline contract exists.

## Working spine

Load one committed cross-layer snapshot testdata case through the coordination planner, apply typed constraints in a dependency-neutral package, and emit a deterministic JSON `Plan` plus `DecisionRecord` in a captured selfcheck.

## Work unit

One minimal end-to-end coordination leaf: core neutral types and deterministic offline planner, thin CLI registration, testdata case, table tests, and captured selfcheck in one issue commit.

## Expected steps

8

## Assumptions

- Existing workflow-plan, task/lease, and trace identities are reusable without importing their concrete runtime owners into the core package.
- This issue is offline-only; no live scheduler action is required.
- The smallest plan may use a bounded initial action taxonomy as long as schemas are versioned and unknown versions fail typed.

## Confusion risks

- Do not build a second scheduler or orchestration runtime.
- Do not import concrete cache, engine, provider, or harness packages into the neutral core.
- Do not defer the CLI selfcheck or testdata case to a follow-up; they are the spine witness.

## Coordination

Own only `internal/coordinate/**`, including package tests and testdata. Preserve peer changes; command registration is a separately leased child.

## Trigger

Dispatch when #6046 is open, #6042 exists, and the gateway/coordination tree is not leased by another worker.

## Batch policy

One issue and one commit for key `coordination-offline-plan-spine`; dedupe against #6046 and any existing `coordinate plan` registration before each rerun.

## In scope

- Versioned neutral `Snapshot`, `Constraints`, `Plan`, and `DecisionRecord` objects.
- Deterministic offline planning and typed infeasibility/schema errors.
- A package-native offline plan/selfcheck surface; thin `fak coordinate plan` registration is a separately leased cmd-lane child.
- Cross-layer testdata case, input-variation table tests, and captured offline selfcheck.

## Out of scope

- Applying actions to live cache, compute, harness, or serve systems.
- Long-running coordination daemons, global optimization, or model calls.
- Canary/default-on policy rollout, which remains in follow-on issues.

## Done condition

At committed trunk, the package-native selfcheck deterministically plans the cross-layer testdata case offline, tests prove each input and failure mode, and the core package remains free of concrete layer imports.

## Witness

A captured package-native offline selfcheck plus focused package/CLI tests that exercise deterministic output, rejected alternatives, stale/partial input, unknown schema, infeasibility, and tie-breaking.

## Acceptance gate

`fak validate --mine internal/coordinate` with focused affected tests, followed by `fak ci-preflight` on the committed tip; exact explicit paths must match the final diff.

## Closure binding

The closing commit subject contains `#6046` and `(fak coordinate)`; GitHub closure is accepted only after independent diff and CLI selfcheck read-back.

## Lane`n`ngateway

## Likely files

- `internal/coordinate/**`


- `internal/coordinate/testdata/cross-layer-snapshot.json`

## Model tier

JUDGE — additive architecture spine with deterministic behavior, import-boundary review, and an end-to-end CLI witness.




## Boundary notes

This gateway-lane issue edits only internal/coordinate/**. The thin cmd/fak registration and CLI subprocess witness must be filed and leased as a separate cmd-lane child before the parent epic is complete; this split prevents an under-scoped cross-lane lease.

records.title: fix(windowgate): suppress Windows console flashes from Go toolchain helpers

The Go toolchain is a console executable on Windows, so helper invocations from windowless fak processes could allocate transient black conhost windows. records.title: feat(scorecard): pure delivery-flow fold — measure how work flows, not just how much is open
records.body:
## Current state

The fleet measures how much work is OPEN (an issue count) but nothing measures how work
FLOWS. A backlog count cannot distinguish a lane shipping steadily from a lane that has
started everything and finished nothing — both read identically as a number of open issues.

Concretely, at the time of filing this repository's own working tree showed:

- **105 untracked `.go` files**, none older than 11 days and 103 of them under 7 days —
  roughly 10 new uncommitted files per day. This is real work in flight that no dashboard
  can see, because an issue tracker structurally cannot read a working tree.
- **39 of those are scratch probe litter** (`zz_*`, `zz*probe*`, dot-prefixed `.slopdedup_*.go`)
  left behind by agent sessions rather than deliberate WIP.
- **Two independent build breaks caused by half-applied multi-file refactors** — a
  `callID` parameter added to `admissionLedger.admit` with one production call site missed,
  and an `exec.Command` → `windowgate.Command` swap that orphaned its `os/exec` import.
  Both violated AGENTS.md:359-372 ("leave the shared tree buildable"), and neither was
  visible to any instrument until `go build ./...` was run by hand.

There is no single number that would have surfaced any of this.

## Scope

### In scope

Add `pkg/scorecard/flow.go`: a PURE delivery-flow fold, in the same shape as the existing
`cachehealth.go` fold in that package (`<X>Schema` / `<X>DebtKey` / `<X>PassLine` / canonical
ordered component keys / `<X>Facts` with `*float64` "no evidence" pointers / worst-first
`<X>Row` worklist / `Compose<X>` returning a control-pane `Payload`).

Five individually-retirable families, each mapping onto a rule this repo already states:

| family | measures | retired by |
|---|---|---|
| `start_latency` | opened → first touched | pull the oldest unstarted ticket before opening a new one |
| `cycle_time` | first touched → closed | finish started work before starting more |
| `wip_headroom` | concurrent in-flight vs the WIP cap | converge before broadening (the `FOCUS_WIP_SATURATED` discipline, read as a health) |
| `wip_visibility` | in-flight work committed vs uncommitted | commit or build-tag in-flight edits |
| `commit_atomicity` | closures landing as exactly ONE commit | green the acceptance criteria before the first commit |

Plus the pure mapper helpers that convert raw signals into 0..1 healths, so the scoring core
reads no git, no `gh`, and no clock: `DurationPercentile`, `DurationHealth`,
`WIPHeadroomHealth`, `VisibilityHealth`, `AtomicityHealth`.

### Out of scope

- The CLI shell (`fak score flow`) and its registration in `cmd/fak/score.go` `scoreRoutes`.
- Registration in `internal/scorecardpane` `Cards` / `tools/scorecard_control_pane.py`
  `SCORECARDS`, and the `tools/scorecard_baseline.json` re-pin. Deliberately excluded: adding
  a portfolio card raises the total and re-pinning the shared baseline mid-flight would red
  `scorecard-ratchet` for every concurrent session.
- The gatherers that would populate `FlowFacts` from `gh` and git.

Those are follow-ons, filed separately, so this lands as one atom.

## Done condition

`pkg/scorecard` exposes `ComposeFlow(FlowFacts) Payload` and the five mapper helpers; the
headline `corpus["delivery_flow"]` equals `corpus["value"]` by construction; debt is the count
of families below the pass line and `ok == (debt == 0)`; a family with no evidence (`nil`) is
EXCLUDED from the fold rather than scored as a measured `0.0`; and the whole fold is
deterministic (no clock read anywhere in the scoring core).

## Witness

`go test ./pkg/scorecard/` green, `gofmt -l pkg/scorecard/` empty, `go vet ./pkg/scorecard/`
clean. The behavioural witnesses are named tests, not a smoke run:

- `TestFlowNumberMovesWhenAFamilyDegrades` — the headline actually discriminates.
- `TestFlowNilFamilyIsExcludedNotScoredZero` — the load-bearing nil contract.
- `TestFlowNoEvidenceFoldsToOne` — the INSUFFICIENT path reads 1.0, not a spurious 0/F.
- `TestFlowWorklistIsWorstFirst` / `TestFlowWorklistTieBreaksOnCanonicalOrder` — deterministic render order.
- `TestComposeFlowBooksOneDefectPerBelowPassLineFamily` — debt contract + per-component defect prefix.
- `TestDurationPercentileNearestRank` — nearest-rank percentile, and the input sample is not mutated.

## Likely files

- `pkg/scorecard/flow.go` (new)
- `pkg/scorecard/flow_test.go` (new)

records.title: chore(issues): dedupe the Hermes study — decomposed three times into 9 duplicate clusters
records.body:
The Hermes concept study was decomposed into child leaves **three separate times**. The
three passes overlap heavily, so a large fraction of the open Hermes backlog is the same
work filed two or three times — in the same files, under different issue numbers.

## The three passes

| pass | anchor | how its children are discoverable |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | epic **#2834** | children cite `#2834` in the body |
| 2 | epic **#2871** | children cite `#2871` in the body |
| 3 | the **`29xx` block** | ⚠️ **no `hermes-inspired` label, no epic reference** — discoverable only by grepping issue bodies for `Hermes` |

Pass 3 is the reason this went unnoticed: `label:hermes-inspired` does not select it and
neither does a `"#2834" in:body` / `"#2871" in:body` search. It is invisible to the
repo's own `*-inspired` taxonomy.

## The duplicate clusters

| cluster | one subject |
|---|---|
| #2894 ↔ #2915 | cache-safety enforced structurally — refuse/measure a mid-conversation prefix mutation |
| #2882 ↔ #2922 | the LLM approver is a PROPOSAL — structural adjudication, never an LLM in the deny path |
| #2883 ↔ #2939 | multi-surface delivery fronting the adjudicating gateway |
| #2857 ↔ #2928 | durable kanban work-board on the dispatch substrate |
| #2854 + #2855 ↔ #2927 | in-kernel cron: at-most-once fire (CAS) + catchup window + hard interrupt |
| #2862 + #2896 ↔ #2938 | config-explosion cap (Hermes' 72KB config + 23KB `.env` sprawl) |
| #2861 ↔ #2902 | declarative provider profiles — provider quirks as DATA |
| #2863 ↔ #2897 | env-var rubric — no behavioral config in env; secrets only |
| #2864 ↔ #2930 | observer + middleware contracts that adjudicate and witness |

Adjacent-but-distinct, recorded so a later pass does not over-merge them: **#2884**
(relay-connector contract — per-turn WebSocket back-channel + HMAC) and **#2929**
(scale-to-zero session hibernation of the KV-cache prefix) share the scale-to-zero
motive but are different mechanisms.

## Why this costs dispatches

A lane lease partitions **files**, not **tickets**. Two workers can hold different lanes,
both be green, and land the same change — and `fak intent claim` only dedupes an exact
target string, so `issue #2894` and `issue #2915` are two free claims on one piece of work.
This is the ticket-level analogue of the collision the lane lease was built to stop.

## Prior art that may already close several of these

Independently of the duplication, five clusters have a **closed** sibling whose commit may
already carry the done-condition (the "open issue read as unstarted" trap):

- **#2846** (2026-07-15) — structured refusal vocabulary replaces the LLM approve/deny judge → sits on #2882/#2922
- **#2886** (2026-07-16) — at-most-once cron fire witness: catchup, grace, dup-tick lock → sits on #2854/#2855/#2927
- **#4266** (2026-07-16) — `emit()` observer fan-out fail-open → sits on #2864/#2930
- **#3007** (2026-07-06) — DeepSeek V4 provider profile → sits on #2861/#2902 (residual: the declarative *registry*)
- **#2891** (2026-07-07) — subagent boundary adjudication + witness → sits on #2859

## First checkable step

1. Label the `29xx` block `hermes-inspired` and point each at epic #2871, so the family is
   selectable by the same query as the other two passes.
2. For each cluster, keep the issue with the better-written done-condition and close the
   rest as duplicates pointing at the survivor.
3. For the five with prior art, read the closing commit first and record PRESENT / PARTIAL
   with the `path:line` that was read — a residual named against a read implementation is
   worth more than a rebuild.

## Done condition

`label:hermes-inspired` selects the whole Hermes family (all three passes), and no two
open issues in it share a subject. Each closed duplicate names its survivor; each cluster
with prior art carries a PRESENT/PARTIAL verdict citing the commit that was read.

Found while scoping a fleet wave over the `*-inspired` study backlog; the pool grew from
26 to 39 leaves once pass 3 was included, and 9 of those rows turned out to be duplicates.

records.title: feat(gateway): route DeliverySender through egressfloor.AdapterSet so the transport carries the adjudicated record
records.body:
## Parent context
Follow-on from #2883 (Hermes-inspiration epic #2871), which landed the delivery **adapter seam** in `internal/egressfloor/adapter.go`.

## Current state
#2883 made an outbound delivery structurally safe at the adapter boundary: `Adapter.Deliver` takes a `DeliveryRecord`, and `DeliveryPolicy.Adjudicate` stamps an unexported provenance field so a record forged by a caller that skipped the floor is refused (`ErrNotAdjudicated`) by `EnsureSendable`, `AdapterSet.Route`, and every adapter.

The gateway send path did NOT move. `gateway.DeliveryTransport` is still:

```go
type DeliveryTransport func(platform egressfloor.Platform, destination, redactedBody string) error
```

Three raw strings. `DeliverySender.Send` adjudicates correctly and then throws the record away, passing only strings to the transport — so a transport implementation still has no way to verify the floor ran, and the guarantee #2883 established stops at the gateway edge. The two seams are correct in isolation and unwired to each other.

## Why now
`NewManifestDeliverySender` (#4392) is the live composition point and takes a `DeliveryTransport` today. Every new platform adapter written against it inherits the unverifiable string seam rather than the guarded one, so the cost of leaving this grows with each adapter added.

## In scope
- Widen `gateway.DeliveryTransport` (or add a record-carrying sibling) so the transport receives the `egressfloor.DeliveryRecord`, not three strings.
- Let `DeliverySender` hold an `egressfloor.AdapterSet` and route through `AdapterSet.Route` instead of calling a bare func.
- Keep `NewManifestDeliverySender`'s manifest-loaded allowlist and ledger witness behaviour unchanged.

## Out of scope
- Any live network client (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp/Signal) — see #2939.
- The `fak deliver` CLI command surface; that is its own leaf.
- Changing the floor's allowlist or redaction semantics.

## Done condition
`DeliverySender` dispatches through `egressfloor.AdapterSet.Route`, and a gateway test proves that a transport/adapter reached via `DeliverySender.Send` receives a record for which `egressfloor.EnsureSendable` returns nil, while a record built outside the floor cannot reach it.

## Witness
A `internal/gateway` test asserting the record-carrying dispatch, alongside the existing `TestDeliverySenderGatesOnFloor` contract.

## Lane
gateway

## Likely files
- `internal/gateway/delivery_send.go`
- `internal/gateway/delivery_manifest.go`

records.title: feat(archreport): expose the enforced architecture graph as a read-only report
records.body:
## Problem

internal/architest mechanically enforces tiers and import direction, but its useful model is trapped in _test.go and t.Log output. Operators and agents cannot ask which tier a leaf occupies, what its import-derived floor is, or whether the current committed graph has violations without reading a 200KB test file.

## Spine

Add a production internal/archreport leaf plus a thin fak architecture command. Parse the architest tier table and Go imports read-only, return a stable JSON/text report with per-tier counts, per-leaf declared tier and import floor, and named upward violations. No duplicated hard-coded package taxonomy: the report reads the same declaration source the gate enforces.

## Done

- fak architecture --json emits a stable schema over the workspace.
- fak architecture --leaf NAME scopes to one leaf and names declared tier, floor, and dependencies.
- A synthetic fixture proves a primitive->foundation-composite edge is reported while the reverse edge is legal.
- No network, exec, or mutation.

## Witness

go test ./internal/archreport ./cmd/fak -run Architecture

## Work estimate

3 points.

## Completion standard

Production.

records.title: feat(config): account for every declared fak.toml opinion at runtime
records.body:
## Parent context
Follow-on to shipped customization spine #6041 and part of epic #3256.

## Current state
`fak serve --config fak.toml` now applies four exact runtime counterparts and reports their provenance. The typed manifest also declares runtimes, inline policy, audit, tenants, agent templates, and observability enablement, but serve does not apply those orchestration-level fields. A user can write them without receiving a clear applied/deferred accounting.

## Why now
Flexible user control stays trustworthy only when every declared opinion is either applied or explicitly reported as unsupported. Silent no-ops would recreate the same hidden-opinion problem the customization surface is meant to solve.

## Working spine
Extend effective-config into a complete manifest coverage report: each declared key is `applied`, `reserved`, or `refused`, with a next action; add the next direct mappings only where a real runtime seam exists.

## In scope
- Enumerate every declared key from `deploymanifest` presence metadata.
- Report applied/reserved status and rationale in effective config.
- Refuse any key that would otherwise misleadingly look active but is unsafe to ignore.
- Add tests covering every known manifest key.

## Out of scope
A full process supervisor and adding new configuration keys.

## Done condition
Every known `fak.toml` key has an asserted runtime disposition, and no declared key can disappear silently.

## Witness
A table-driven test over the complete closed key vocabulary plus captured effective-config JSON.

records.title: feat(config): add intent-level customization guide over excellent defaults
records.body:
## Parent context
Follow-on to shipped customization spine #6041 and part of epic #3256.

## Current state
The reviewable file and truthful precedence now exist, but customization still requires knowing field names and editing TOML. fak has strong built-in defaults but no guided way to express a user's operational opinions such as local-only, team gateway, hardened ingress, or long-session budget posture without exposing a sprawling knob catalog.

## Why now
The product goal is flexible across user opinions while retaining excellent out-of-box defaults. Named, inspectable postures can encode coherent deltas and keep individual knob discovery bounded.

A `fak config guide` command asks or accepts a small set of intent-level choices, renders the minimal fak.toml delta from defaults, and explains every changed value; presets are data over the same typed manifest, never a parallel config system.

- Render only deltas from built-ins.

records.title: fix(compute): cuda_acceptance_scripts_test.go declares package cudaacceptance_test, making internal/compute unloadable
records.body:
## Symptom

Every package that (transitively) imports `internal/compute` fails to build:

```
internal/cachemeta/quantized_demote.go:3:8: found packages compute (anchorwarm.go)
    and cudaacceptance (cuda_acceptance_scripts_test.go) in internal/compute
```

Reproduce from the clone root:

```
go build ./internal/compute/ ./internal/cachemeta/ ./internal/gateway/
```

## Cause

`internal/compute/cuda_acceptance_scripts_test.go:1` declares:

```go
package cudaacceptance_test
```

Go permits exactly two package names in a directory: the package itself
(`compute`) and its external test package (`compute_test`). `cudaacceptance_test`
is neither, so the toolchain reports two packages in one directory and refuses to
load `internal/compute` at all — including for consumers that never run its tests.

Introduced by `f37e4ef914` — *fix(cuda): preserve toolkit fallback without HOME
(#6063) (fak compute)*. The other 167 files in the directory declare `package
compute` and one declares `package compute_test`; this file is the only outlier.

## Blast radius

This is not test-only. A bad package clause makes the directory unloadable, so it
takes out the ordinary build of every importer, not just `go test`. Confirmed dead:
`internal/compute`, `internal/cachemeta`, `internal/gateway`. Anything gated on a
green tree — `make ci`, and therefore every concurrent worker's ship gate — is
blocked behind it.

## Fix

Rename the clause to `compute_test` (keeps the file's external-test intent and its
current location), **or** move the file into its own directory
`internal/compute/cudaacceptance/` if the separate package name is deliberate.
Prefer the rename unless the file genuinely needs its own package boundary.

## First checkable step

`go build ./internal/compute/ ./internal/cachemeta/ ./internal/gateway/` exits 0,
then `go vet ./internal/compute/` is clean.

## Done condition

- `go build ./...` no longer reports "found packages compute and cudaacceptance".
- `go test ./internal/compute/` runs (the acceptance test still compiles and is
  still skipped/run under the same conditions it was before).
- A guard so the class cannot recur: the directory contains at most the `compute`
  and `compute_test` package clauses.

## Note

`f37e4ef914` is **not on `origin/main`** as of filing — the break is local to the
shared checkout, so it is cheap to correct before it is published.

records.title: fix(fleet-wave): default wave fuel says "token cost is not a constraint" and starves every worker of its cumulative guard budget
records.body:
`.claude/skills/fleet-wave/fuel-ultracode-wave.md` is the canonical fuel template the
`fleet-wave` skill renders for every wave worker. Its first three lines are:

```
ultracode — use the Workflow tool for exhaustive, adversarially-verified multi-agent
orchestration on the ONE leaf you take. Optimize for the most correct result; token
cost is not a constraint. Breadth across leaves is the wave's job, not yours.
```

`token cost is not a constraint` is false for a guarded wave worker, and the template
states it as the worker's **first** instruction. A worker launched by
`tools/launch_goal_detached.ps1` gets `-ContextBudgetTokens 2016000` handed to
`fak guard --context-budget-tokens`. Per `internal/session/usage.go` `DebitUsage`, that
allowance is **cumulative** and every turn debits its ENTIRE resident window. So the
budget buys roughly `2.0M / <resident window>` turns — at a ~100k window, ~20 turns.
Telling the worker cost is unconstrained, and to run adversarial multi-agent
orchestration, is a direct instruction to spend that allowance as fast as possible.

## Witness (wave `iw08091930`, 2026-08-09)

Seven workers launched against a 39-leaf pool, all on the stock template's first line.
**All seven died `BUDGET_CONTEXT_EXHAUSTED`. Zero commits landed.** They did take lanes
and claim tickets first, so the dispatches were consumed, not refused.

Per-turn trace from one worker's `err.log`:

```
fak-turn … prov=96.1k tok (87% of prompt) … compact=none-past-budget budget=spent:110.0k ctx:109.8k/96.0k
fak-turn … prov=98.7k tok (90% of prompt) … compact=none-past-budget budget=spent:110.7k ctx:110.3k/96.0k
fak guard: restart #1 … seed=972tok handback=continue
fak guard: restart #2 … seed=839tok handback=continue
fak guard: managed-context status restart_exhausted count=3 dominant_cause=BUDGET_CONTEXT_EXHAUSTED
fak guard: claude exited abnormally (code 1)
```

Two compounding effects:

1. **~100k resident per turn**, sustained, sitting past the 96k compaction shed-line with
   `compact=none-past-budget`.
2. **Restart hands back ~900 tokens.** On drain the guard restarts the child with a seed
   under 1k, so the worker wakes nearly blank, re-does the same expensive discovery, and
   drains again. Three cycles, then exit 1. Discovery is repaid every restart and never
   amortized into a commit.

This is the `SKILL.md:232` budget-starvation row (distinct `session <id>` +
`BUDGET_CONTEXT_EXHAUSTED`) reached from the skill's **own** template rather than from
operator misconfiguration — which is why it is worth a fix rather than a triage entry.

## Not the same bug as #2972

#2972 was a *birth* wall (flat 48000 budget below the ~62K baseline; fixed by the derived
budget, now `max(168000, 62000) × 12 = 2016000`). This is a *burn-rate* problem at the
correct budget: the derivation is right, and the prompt spends it.

## Suggested fix

Replace the unconditional first line with budget-aware framing. What worked in the
rewritten `iw08091930` fuel:

- state the allowance is cumulative and every turn debits the whole resident window;
- state that a restart returns ~900 tokens of seed, so exhaustion loses the work;
- forbid `Workflow`/ultracode and whole-file reads for a single-leaf worker; grep to the line;
- require the first commit inside ~10 turns, smallest correct change first;
- warn that the per-turn `ctx:<n>/96.0k` nudge is the COMPACTION shed-line, NOT the
  session budget — the note in `docs/notes/dispatch-worker-context-budget-trap-2026-07-08.md`
  already records that these two "budgets" are on different scales and that confusing them
  cost real debugging time.

If an ultracode variant is still wanted for genuinely deep single-leaf work, it should be
an opt-in template (`fuel-deep-leaf.md`) chosen deliberately, not the default every wave
inherits.

## Done condition

The default rendered wave fuel contains no "token cost is not a constraint" clause and no
unconditional `Workflow`/ultracode instruction; it states the cumulative-budget semantics
and a ship-early rule. Witness: a wave of ≥4 workers on the new default where no worker
exits `BUDGET_CONTEXT_EXHAUSTED` before its first commit.

records.title: feat(dev-ex): one closed rollout-ladder vocabulary — three leaves spell the same off/shadow/on ladder three incompatible ways
records.body:
## Parent context
Sibling of #2863 (CONFIG_NOT_ENV ratchet, shipped) and #2862 / #2896 (config-surface budget). Those bound how WIDE the front door gets; this one is about the door's INTERIOR being inconsistent.

## Current state
Three packages independently invented a staged-rollout ladder for "land it now, expose it later". All three mean the same three-or-four rungs. None of them share a type, a spelling, or a default:

| package | vocabulary | default | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `internal/dispatchtick/rollout.go` | `off` / `shadow` / `canary` / `default` | **`off`** | fully articulated; guard REFUSES `default` — promotion past canary needs a separate witness |
| `internal/promptmmu/config.go` | `on` / `shadow` / `off` | **`on`** | `ParseMode("")` resolves to on; unrecognized value also resolves to on with `ok=false` |
| `internal/memorycotravel/memorycotravel.go` | `shadow` / `live` / `off` | **`shadow`** | third spelling of the applied rung |

The applied rung is spelled `default`, `on`, and `live` in the three files. The safe rung is the default in two and not in the third. Only `dispatchtick` has a canary rung, and only it treats promotion-to-default as needing separate evidence.

The prose convention behind this is not niche: **142 non-test `.go` files** carry default-off / opt-in gating language (`git grep -liE 'default[- ]off|off by default|opt-in'` over non-test Go). The ladder is fak's dominant way of landing work in progress. It just has no shared noun.

## Why now
`dispatchtick/rollout.go` already contains the correct semantics, written out at length — including the two things the other two ladders lack: (a) `off` is the default *so that "default behavior is unchanged" is provable*, and (b) the ladder REFUSES to self-promote to default-on. Generalizing the type it already owns is cheaper than three leaves drifting further, and every new gated feature currently picks a fourth spelling.

## Working spine
The `RolloutMode` closed vocabulary in `internal/dispatchtick/rollout.go` — the only one of the three that already has the refuse-to-self-promote property worth keeping.

## In scope
- One shared package (e.g. `internal/rolloutmode`) owning the closed vocabulary, its parse, and its fail-closed rule for an unrecognized value.
- Pick ONE spelling per rung and state why (`off` / `shadow` / `canary` / `on`). The applied rung needs a single name.
- Migrate the three call sites. Each keeps its own *default* — `promptmmu` is legitimately default-on (epic #751 posture) and this issue does not change any live behavior.
- A test that the vocabulary is closed and an unknown string fails closed, not open.

## Out of scope
- Changing any leaf's current default posture or live behavior. This is a vocabulary unification, not a rollout decision.
- A registry of which features are at which rung — that is the sibling issue.
- The env-var/config-surface question (#2862, #2863).

## Confusion risks
- `promptmmu.ParseMode` resolves an UNRECOGNIZED value to default-on with `ok=false`. That is fail-OPEN and deliberate for that leaf (the epic's on-by-default posture). The shared parser must let a caller choose its fallback rather than hardcoding either direction, or this migration silently flips `promptmmu` closed / `dispatchtick` open.
- `dispatchtick`'s `default` rung is a REFUSED terminal state, not an implemented one. Renaming it to `on` must not make it look reachable.

## Done condition
The three files import one vocabulary; no leaf spells the applied rung differently; unknown-value behavior is per-caller and tested.

## Witness
`go test ./internal/rolloutmode ./internal/dispatchtick ./internal/promptmmu ./internal/memorycotravel` green, and a grep showing no remaining private `shadow`/`canary` mode enum in non-test Go.

records.title: feat(dev-ex): a feature-gate registry — give default-off WIP a declared home, a promotion witness, and an expiry
records.body:
## Parent context
The unfilled destination named by #2863 and adjacent to #2862 / #2896. Pairs with the vocabulary unification filed alongside this one.

## Current state
Landing work in progress behind a gate is fak's normal practice — **142 non-test `.go` files** carry default-off / opt-in gating language. But the gate itself is, in every case, a private convention:

- **The compile-time path works and is well-tooled.** `//go:build wip_<slug>` + `fak wip fence|unfence` + `internal/buildwitness` keep the shared trunk green. `git grep -l '^//go:build wip_'` over tracked files returns **0** — the fence is used constantly and always resolves to zero, which is the healthy outcome. Nothing here needs fixing.
- **The runtime path has no machinery at all.** "Landed but not exposed" is expressed as a prose comment plus whatever knob the author reached for. There is no way to ask the repo *which features are currently gated off, why, since when, and what evidence would promote them*.
- **The knob authors used to reach for is now banned.** #2863's CONFIG_NOT_ENV ratchet refuses NEW non-secret `os.Getenv` reads. That is correct — there are already **780 distinct `FAK_*` names** read in non-test Go — but the ratchet's own `admittedPostFreeze` (`internal/envconfiglint/admitted.go`) says it plainly: each admitted entry "genuinely belongs on a config surface; none can move there yet **because that surface does not exist** — it is #2862's deliverable." So the refusal currently has no named destination.
- **The generation model already assumes a gate exists.** `internal/devindex/generation.go` defines `gen/next` demotion evidence as "a **feature gate** proves the work is not ready for default exposure" and promotion as a "**default-exposure proof**". Nothing binds a real gate to a generation row, so that promotion evidence cannot be checked.

## Why now
#2863 shipped the refusal before the destination existed. Every gated feature landing now either burns an `admittedPostFreeze` exception, hides behind a helper the scanner cannot see (the SCANNER VISIBILITY note in `admitted.go` records four reads that went ungated exactly this way), or invents a private mode enum. The debt ledger is designed to only shrink and currently cannot.

## Working spine
`internal/policy/orgprecedence.go` — the precedence lattice that already exists and should NOT be reinvented. It resolves `compiled-in FROZEN floor > central org overlay > operator overlay > agent-self` with three knob kinds (`FROZEN`, `RATCHET`, `GATED_WIDEN`) and is enumerated row-by-row in `org_precedence_test.go`. It governs capability floors today; a feature gate is the same shape of question ("three channels have an opinion about one knob — which value runs, and who do I ask to change it?").

## In scope
A registry where one gated feature is one declared row carrying:
- **name + owner leaf** (the `(fak <leaf>)` lane that owns promotion).
- **declared default**, and the rung from the vocabulary issue. A default is a decision with a name on it, not an accident of which branch of a `switch` came first.
- **promotion evidence** — the specific witness that would move it up a rung, in the shape `gen/next` already asks for. `dispatchtick/rollout.go`'s refuse-to-self-promote rule generalizes here.
- **expiry / review-by**. A gate with no expiry becomes permanent configuration, which is precisely the Hermes sprawl #2862 is defending against. This is the mechanism that keeps the registry from BECOMING the 72KB config file.
- **resolution order** delegated to the `orgprecedence` lattice rather than a fresh override chain.

Plus: `fak feature query` (`cmd/fak/feature.go`, `internal/selfquery`) already answers "what can fak do" from cards. Gated features should be answerable there, so "what is currently landed-but-off" is a query, not a grep.

## Out of scope
- **The budget/ceiling — that is #2862 and #2896, not this.** This issue provides the surface; those two bound its size. They compose: a registry with declared expiry is what makes a ceiling enforceable, because retiring a knob becomes a dated event rather than a cleanup nobody owns.
- The `//go:build wip_` compile-time path. It works; leave it alone.
- Relocating the 780 existing env reads. The ratchet's job is that the count only goes down; this issue gives the next relocation somewhere to land.
- Any change to a live default.

## Confusion risks
- **A feature-gate registry is a config surface, and this repo's stated fear is config surfaces.** The distinguishing property must be that a gate row is TEMPORARY BY CONSTRUCTION (it has an expiry and a promotion witness) whereas a config knob is permanent. If rows can live forever, this issue has built the thing #2862 exists to prevent, and should be closed rather than shipped.
- `internal/ablate`'s `Concept` / `FeatureCard` registry (`registry.go`, `catalog.go`) is a real feature registry with owner/plane/fidelity classification — but it is scoped to sweepable cache levers for benchmark ablation arms, and its tokens are A/B selectors, not exposure gates. Decide deliberately whether to extend it or sit beside it; do not assume either.
- `internal/experiments` is an ML experiment ledger (models × backends), unrelated despite the name.

## Done condition
One gated feature is declared in the registry, resolves through the `orgprecedence` lattice, is answerable via `fak feature query`, and its row is refused by a test if it lacks a promotion witness or an expiry.

## Witness
A test that reds on a registry row with no expiry or no promotion evidence, plus `fak feature query` returning the gated feature with its rung and default.

records.title: perf(dispatch): a no-delta tick still rewrites the whole 3.2MB backlog snapshot (fak dispatch)
records.body:
## Summary

`dispatchFetchBacklogIncremental` takes the trouble to fetch only a *delta* from
GitHub, then throws that saving away on the write side: it calls `WriteBacklog`
**unconditionally**, re-marshalling and rewriting all 1024 issues even when the
delta contained zero changed and zero closed issues.

A tick that learns nothing costs a full 3.2MB disk write.

## Evidence (live tree C:\work\fak, 2026-08-09)

`cmd/fak/dispatch_tick_route.go:549-571` — cache-hit path:

```go
if snap, ok := dispatchcache.ReadBacklog(path, key); ok {
    delta, err := dispatchFetchBacklogDeltaIssues(root, snap.Watermark, limit)
    if err == nil {
        merged := dispatchcache.MergeBacklog(snap.Issues, dispatchIssueRows(delta.Issues), delta.Closed)
        watermark := delta.Watermark
        if watermark.IsZero() { watermark = now }
        if err = dispatchcache.WriteBacklog(path, key, watermark, merged); err == nil {   // <-- unconditional
            return dispatchRowsIssues(merged)
        }
    }
}
```

There is no `len(delta.Issues) == 0 && len(delta.Closed) == 0` guard. `merged` is
byte-identical to `snap.Issues` on a quiet tick; the only field that genuinely
changed is the 28-byte watermark.

`internal/dispatchcache/backlog.go:49-75` `WriteBacklog` always marshals the full
`BacklogSnapshot` and writes the entire file (temp + rename — the atomicity is
correct and should stay).

Measured: `.fak/dispatch/backlog.json` = 3,226,321 bytes / 1024 issues, and it was
observed being rewritten repeatedly during a single audit window (3,198,219 ->
3,226,321 bytes between two samples ~12 minutes apart).

## Why this is worth fixing

This is the one hot-loop write amplifier found in a broader disk-write audit where
almost everything else turned out to be expected, self-collecting churn. Cost is
~3.2MB per tick and it scales with backlog size, so it gets worse as the repo grows.

## Fix shape

Skip the write when the delta is empty, or write only an advanced watermark:

- cheapest: `if len(delta.Issues) == 0 && len(delta.Closed) == 0 { return dispatchRowsIssues(snap.Issues) }`
  before the merge/write (still refresh the watermark if that matters — see below);
- if the watermark must advance on a quiet tick, split it into its own tiny sidecar
  file so the 3.2MB issue array is rewritten only when an issue actually changed.

Keep the temp+rename atomicity either way.

Blast radius: LOW — confined to the backlog cache write path; `ReadBacklog`
already validates schema/key/watermark, so a stale-but-valid snapshot is the
existing behaviour on the read side.

## Likely files

- cmd/fak/dispatch_tick_route.go
- internal/dispatchcache/backlog.go

## Target operating envelope

- bytes written by a dispatch tick with an empty delta: 0 bytes to backlog.json
  (currently ~3.2MB)
- backlog.json mtime unchanged across two consecutive no-delta ticks
- full rewrite still occurs when >= 1 issue changed or closed

## Completion standard
production

records.title: perf(guard): origin evidence re-materializes the 34KB embedded policy per trace when its siblings use a 0-byte file (fak guard)
records.body:
## Summary

`writeGuardPolicyOriginEvidence` writes the **compile-time-constant** embedded
capability floor (`guardDefaultPolicyJSON`, 34,702 bytes) into a fresh
`.fak/guard-origin/<trace-id>-policy.json` on every `fak guard` launch.

Every copy is byte-identical, nothing ever reads the content back, and the three
sibling evidence candidates satisfy the exact same contract with a **zero-byte**
file.

## Evidence (live tree C:\work\fak, 2026-08-09)

Write site — `cmd/fak/guard_task_origin.go:73-92`, called from `cmd/fak/guard.go:1408`:

```go
path := filepath.Join(root, ".fak", "guard-origin", strings.TrimSpace(traceID)+"-policy.json")
if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil { return "" }
if err := os.WriteFile(path, guardDefaultPolicyJSON, 0o600); err != nil { return "" }
```

`guardDefaultPolicyJSON` is `//go:embed guard-default-policy.json`
(`cmd/fak/guard_policy_embed.go:97`) — a constant already inside the binary.
`wc -c cmd/fak/guard-default-policy.json` = 34,702.

The returned path is consumed only as a location contract — `registerGuardChildOriginTask`
turns it into `taskmgr.EvidenceRef{Kind: taskmgr.PathRefKind, Ref: path}`. A grep
for readers of `.fak/guard-origin/*-policy.json` finds none: no code parses the
content back.

The asymmetry is explicit in the sibling path, `guardChildOriginEvidence`
(`cmd/fak/guard_task_origin.go:56-63`), which handles `transcript`,
`budget_envelope` and `stop_hook_ledger`:

```go
// Origin evidence is a durable location contract. Create an empty evidence
// file when the producer has not appended its first row yet, so PathWitness
// verifies the location rather than marking a valid pre-launch task refused.
if _, err := os.Stat(path); os.IsNotExist(err) {
    if os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755) != nil || os.WriteFile(path, nil, 0o600) != nil {
```

So three of the four candidates prove the location with 0 bytes; only `policy`
materializes 34KB of a constant.

Measured on the live tree:

- peak sample: 66 `*-policy.json`, **61 byte-identical** (md5 `3cf485765b424071d3e56d4feaec12ab`), 2.18MB
- later sample: 18 `*-policy.json`, **all 18 byte-identical**, same md5, 686KB
- creation rate ~3.5/hour over an 18.7h window

(The directory *does* get collected — this is not a retention leak. The defect is
that the bytes should never be written in the first place.)

## Why this is worth fixing

Bytes are small (~123KB/h) but it is pure waste with a one-line fix, and it is the
only one of the four origin-evidence candidates that behaves this way — the kind of
inconsistency that quietly becomes load-bearing if left. It also creates an
unbounded number of *distinct* 34KB files keyed by trace id.

## Fix shape

Preferred: write a 0-byte file, matching the sibling contract exactly — `PathWitness`
verifies the location, which is all this ref is used for.

If a future verifier genuinely needs the floor's content, do it without N copies:
record a content hash in the file (tens of bytes), or reference the single embedded
floor / one content-addressed shared file instead of copying per trace.

Blast radius: LOW — confined to origin-evidence creation; the ref kind is
`PathRefKind` and no reader of the content exists.

## Likely files

- cmd/fak/guard_task_origin.go
- cmd/fak/guard.go

## Target operating envelope

- bytes written per guard launch for policy origin evidence: 0 (currently 34,702)
- `registerGuardChildOriginTask` still produces a `policy` evidence ref whose path exists
- no byte-identical duplicate `*-policy.json` copies accumulate under `.fak/guard-origin`

## Completion standard
production

records.title: experiment(microcontextdemo): route filter and tool stages by bounded value-of-information windows
records.body:
## Parent context

#6033, #6030, #6031, and `docs/research/micro-context-large-input-operators.md`.

## Current state

The fabric proves a bounded selector can choose one semantic filter and that admitted read tools can execute safely. It does not yet prove the more general decision problem: for each partition, whether to stop, run a deterministic filter, open a semantic micro-window, call a read tool, widen context, or escalate. Running every filter/tool is safe but can erase the economic advantage; giving the selector arbitrary execution authority erases the security boundary.

## Working spine

A bounded policy controller receives only typed partition metadata plus prior fact/receipt summaries, estimates expected decision value net of token/tool/latency cost, and chooses one allowlisted next stage. The kernel—not selector prose—enforces stage authority, budgets, dependencies, dedupe, cancellation, and terminal conditions.

## In scope

- Typed stage catalog spanning deterministic filters, semantic micro-windows, read-only tools, widen, stop, and escalate.
- Per-stage applicability, capability, estimated cost, uncertainty reduction, dependencies, and cacheability.
- Value-of-information or equivalent threshold that can skip a filter/tool whose expected decision impact is below cost.
- Bounded recursive routing with depth, spend, call, and wall-clock budgets.
- Parallel speculative *read-only* candidates with loser cancellation where net-true; no speculative effects.
- Stable cache keys over stage version, policy version, input digest, and dependency receipts.
- Confusion telemetry: wrong skips, unnecessary runs, budget exhaustion, widen/escalate, and oracle regret.
- Comparison against run-all, fixed cascade, deterministic planner, and one-shot long-context baselines at one quality target.

## Out of scope

Selector-minted capabilities, arbitrary tool names/arguments, hidden writes, cancellation-as-rollback, or a universal claim that model routing beats a static cascade.

## Done condition

A controlled mixed workload routes at least 1,000 partitions through filter/tool/window choices, proves unauthorized and dependency-invalid stages cannot dispatch, preserves an explicit quality floor, and reports net work/latency versus tuned run-all and fixed-cascade baselines. The artifact must include at least one regime where static policy wins and one where adaptive routing wins or abstain if no such boundary is observed.

## Witness

Captured decision/receipt ledger with per-partition candidate set, chosen stage, kernel admission verdict, cost, outcome, cache/replay status, cancellation disposition, and independently computed oracle regret.

## Acceptance gate

Selector authority tests, budget/dependency/cancellation tests, deterministic replay, artifact verifier, owned-path validation, and net-true claim-check evidence green.

## Work estimate

Estimate: 13 points

## Overall completion contribution

Contribution: 6/100 points

## Completion standard

experiment

## Closure binding

Close via one commit whose body carries `Closes #<n>` and an independently verified decision-ledger artifact.

## Lane

microcontextdemo

## Work unit

leaf

## Expected steps

10

## Assumptions

- Existing #6030 selector outputs, #6031 read-tool executor, and #6034 effect authority remain the sole execution seams.
- The first spine uses read-only tools; effect routing remains approval/receipt bound and non-speculative.

## Confusion risks

- Choosing a stage is not acquiring its capability.
- A cheap selector is overhead unless it avoids more work than it adds.
- Cancellation before dispatch, during read execution, and after an effect dispatch have different semantics.
- Filter order can change both quality and cache hit rate, so compare against a tuned cascade rather than an intentionally weak run-all baseline.

## Likely files

- `cmd/microcontextdemo/`
- `internal/microagent/`
- `docs/research/`
- `experiments/microcontext/`

## Parent context

## Current state

Existing S1/S6 endpoint witnesses establish bounded micro-context execution and API provenance, but do not run the #6033 alternatives on one corpus with actual tokens, dollars, TTFT/tail, retries, scheduler overhead, and tool costs.

## Scope

- Run the tuned alternatives and micro-context pipeline on sanctioned live compute/endpoints.
- Keep API-only evidence separate from controlled-kernel evidence.
- Capture provider/model/hardware, endpoint capabilities, native caching/batching, pricing snapshot, tokens, cached tokens, dollars, TTFT, p50/p95/tail, retries, queue/scheduler overhead, tool calls/cost, and quality outputs.
- Repeat enough trials for variance/sensitivity; retain raw artifacts and redacted provenance.
- Treat endpoint errors, capacity limits, and cancelled-but-billed requests explicitly.

## Done condition

A reproducible live matrix covers every eligible tuned alternative at the same held-out quality target and carries raw results, provenance, and rerun commands; missing endpoint capabilities are recorded rather than silently modeled.

records.title: research(microcontextdemo): publish net-true large-input decision boundary
records.body:
## Parent context

#6033 and closed fixture spine #6100.
## Current state

#6100 reports only a fixture-modeled hypothesis. Parent #6033 closes only after live quality/cost evidence is folded against the strongest tuned alternatives under the net-true standard.

## Scope

- Join corpus/grader, tuned configurations, and live matrix without averaging away task slices or tail latency.
- Compute Pareto eligibility at fixed quality, sensitivity/error bars, and decision regions over ambiguity, relation density, cache reuse, update locality, tool latency, and input density.
- Include all selector, scheduler, indexing, retry, tool, and invalidation costs.
- Run `fak claim-check` against the strongest tuned baseline.
- Publish where SQL/search, retrieval, long context, chunks, or micro-context wins, loses, or remains not-yet.

## Done condition

The report provides a measured, reproducible decision boundary with net-true claim-check artifacts and no headline based on a naive or quality-inferior baseline. This issue may close parent #6033 only if all of its acceptance criteria are independently witnessed.

## Witness

Final report, common result bundle, sensitivity outputs, claim-check artifacts, and origin-witnessed commit.
